lessons.title: 356. Ch 28 · Grammar A: a summary of the four speech styles
lessons.subtitle: 존댓말 · 반말 · -습니다 · -아/어요 · -다 · -아/어 · 격식체와 비격식체

explanations.title: Summary of speech styles
explanations.body: Recall the four speech styles you have learned in the past chapters: (1) Formal Polite Speech Style; (2) Informal Polite Speech Style; (3) Informal Blunt Speech Style; and (4) Formal Blunt Speech Style. These four styles can be summarized as follows: formal polite –습니다 (from Chapter 1); informal polite –아/어요 (from Chapter 2); formal blunt –다 (from Chapter 15); informal blunt –아/어 (from Chapter 5).

explanations.title: The verb endings by sentence type
explanations.body: The verb endings of the speech styles can change according to the sentence type.

explanations.title: 1. Formal polite speech style: -습니다 / -ㅂ니다
explanations.body: This speech style is perceived as formal and polite because it is often used in formal situations and for formal purposes such as radio or television news broadcasting, presentations, and sermons. It is also used when addressing a supervisor or making new acquaintances. The book’s example is a weather forecast (the English is mine):

examples.text: 오늘의 날씨를 말씀 드리겠습니다.
examples.translation: oneurui nalssireul malsseum deurigetseumnida. — I will tell you today’s weather.

examples.text: 오늘은 날씨가 맑습니다.
examples.translation: oneureun nalssiga makseumnida. — Today the weather is clear.

examples.text: 그러나 중부지방에는 오후에 잠깐 비가 오는 곳이 있겠습니다.
examples.translation: geureona jungbujibangeneun ohue jamkkan biga oneun gosi itgetseumnida. — However, in the central region there will be some places with a brief rain in the afternoon.

examples.text: 외출하시려면 우산을 준비해 주시기 바랍니다.
examples.translation: oechulhasiryeomyeon usaneul junbihae jusigi baramnida. — If you are going out, please prepare an umbrella.

explanations.title: 2. Informal polite speech style: -아/어요
explanations.body: This speech style is perceived as informal and polite because it is often used in situations where the speaker is in casual yet polite relationship with the addressee. You can use –아/어요 for a statement, a question, a command or request, or even a suggestion, without changing its form. The book’s example (5시 is spelled out; the English is mine):

examples.text: 선우 씨는 누나가 있어요?
examples.translation: seonu ssineun nunaga isseoyo? — Sunwoo, do you have an older sister?

examples.text: 누나는 없어요. 저는 형만 있어요.
examples.translation: nunaneun eopseoyo. jeoneun hyeongman isseoyo. — I have no older sister. I only have an older brother.

examples.text: 그렇군요. 참 오늘 저녁에 학교에서 재즈 콘서트가 있는데 같이 갈래요?
examples.translation: geureokunyo. cham oneul jeonyeoge hakgyoeseo jaejeu konseoteuga inneunde gachi gallaeyo? — I see. Oh, there is a jazz concert at school this evening; would you like to go together?

examples.text: 좋아요. 그럼 몇 시에 볼까요?
examples.translation: joayo. geureom myeot sie bolkkayo? — Good. Then what time shall we meet?

examples.text: 도서관 앞에서 다섯 시에 봐요.
examples.translation: doseogwan apeseo daseot sie bwayo. — Let’s meet in front of the library at five.

explanations.title: 3. Formal blunt speech style: -다
explanations.body: This speech style is perceived as formal and blunt because it is used in newspapers, journals, textbooks, etc. In spoken language, this speech style is used among friends or by those of higher status in age or rank. As you learned in Chapter 24, this style is also used as a command form in the military. The book’s example (the English is mine):

examples.text: 자, 내일은 유격훈련이 있다.
examples.translation: ja, naeireun yugyeokullyeoni itda. — Now, tomorrow there is ranger training.

examples.text: 오늘 모두 소총을 닦고 훈련을 준비한다.
examples.translation: oneul modu sochongeul dakgo hullyeoneul junbihanda. — Today everyone cleans their rifles and prepares for the training.

explanations.title: 4. Informal blunt speech style (반말): -아/어
explanations.body: This speech style is perceived as informal and blunt because it is typically used in settings where social distance between speakers need not be maintained (e.g., between friends or siblings). This style is also used by older people when they address younger people with whom they have a close relationship. The conversation presented in the informal polite speech style example can be rewritten in informal blunt speech style as follows (the English is mine):

examples.text: 선우야, 넌 누나가 있어?
examples.translation: seonuya, neon nunaga isseo? — Sunwoo, do you have an older sister?

examples.text: 누나는 없어. 난 형만 있어.
examples.translation: nunaneun eopseo. nan hyeongman isseo. — I have no older sister. I only have an older brother.

examples.text: 그렇구나. 참 오늘 저녁에 학교에서 재즈 콘서트가 있는데 같이 갈래?
examples.translation: geureokuna. cham oneul jeonyeoge hakgyoeseo jaejeu konseoteuga inneunde gachi gallae? — I see. Oh, there is a jazz concert at school this evening; do you want to go together?

examples.text: 좋아. 그럼 몇 시에 볼까?
examples.translation: joa. geureom myeot sie bolkka? — Good. Then what time shall we meet?

examples.text: 도서관 앞에서 다섯 시에 보자.
examples.translation: doseogwan apeseo daseot sie boja. — Let’s meet in front of the library at five.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: The formal polite, informal polite, formal blunt (plain) and informal blunt statement forms of a few verbs, made by the book’s rules.

lessons.subtitle: 공연소식 · 내일 일정 · 회식 · 반말 · 할아버지 · 일어나십니다 · 드십니다 · 주무십니다

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): identify the speech style and the relationship
explanations.body: The book asks you to read four scripts, circle the verb endings, tick the speech style (formal polite, informal polite, formal blunt, informal blunt) and write in English the relationship between the speaker and the listener. The scripts are the book’s (digits and “2번” are spelled out in Hangul; the book’s Script 2 repeats “이번 훈련은 특히” before “이번 훈련에는”, which is written once here); the English is mine.

examples.text: 오늘의 공연소식입니다.
examples.translation: oneurui gongyeonsosigimnida. — This is today’s performance news.

examples.text: 오늘 대학로에서는 봄 음악 축제가 있습니다.
examples.translation: oneul daehangnoeseoneun bom eumak chukjega itseumnida. — Today there is a spring music festival at Daehangno.

examples.text: 세계적으로 유명한 바이올리니스트 카라 김이 베토벤 바이올린 협주곡 이 번을 연주합니다.
examples.translation: segyejeogeuro yumyeonghan baiolliniseuteu kara gimi betoben baiollin hyeopjugok i beoneul yeonjuhamnida. — The world-famous violinist Kara Kim will play Beethoven’s Violin Concerto No. 2.

examples.text: 또한 러시아 국립 발레단이 발레 호두까기 인형을 공연합니다.
examples.translation: ttohan reosia gungnip balledani balle hodukkagi inhyeongeul gongyeonhamnida. — Also, the Russian national ballet company will perform the ballet The Nutcracker.

examples.text: 내일 일정을 말해 주겠다.
examples.translation: naeil iljeongeul malhae jugetda. — I will tell you tomorrow’s schedule.

examples.text: 아침 여섯 시에 집합한다.
examples.translation: achim yeoseot sie jipapanda. — We assemble at six in the morning.

examples.text: 집합 후에, 아침 식사를 하고 일곱 시부터 훈련장까지 행군한다.
examples.translation: jipap hue, achim siksareul hago ilgop sibuteo hullyeonjangkkaji haenggunhanda. — After assembly, we have breakfast and march to the training area from seven.

examples.text: 오후에는 유격훈련과 화생방 훈련이 있다.
examples.translation: ohueneun yugyeokullyeongwa hwasaengbang hullyeoni itda. — In the afternoon there is ranger training and CBR training.

examples.text: 이번 훈련에는 특히 따뜻한 옷을 준비하기 바란다.
examples.translation: ibeon hullyeoneneun teuki ttatteutan oseul junbihagi baranda. — For this training, in particular, prepare warm clothes.

examples.text: 가: 김 과장님, 오늘 저녁에 회식이 있다는데 어디에서 하는지 알아요?
examples.translation: ga: gim gwajangnim, oneul jeonyeoge hoesigi itdaneunde eodieseo haneunji arayo? — Manager Kim, I heard there is a company dinner this evening; do you know where it is?

examples.text: 나: 아, 회사 앞 서울 갈비에서 여섯 시에 있어요.
examples.translation: na: a, hoesa ap seoul galbieseo yeoseot sie isseoyo. — Oh, it is at Seoul Galbi in front of the company at six.

examples.text: 가: 그래요? 전 오늘 친구 결혼식이 있어서 못 갈 것 같아요.
examples.translation: ga: geuraeyo? jeon oneul chingu gyeolhonsigi isseoseo mot gal geot gatayo. — Is that so? I have a friend’s wedding today, so I don’t think I can go.

examples.text: 나: 아, 그럼 영업과 송 과장님께 연락하세요.
examples.translation: na: a, geureom yeongeopgwa song gwajangnimkke yeollakaseyo. — Oh, then contact Manager Song of the sales section.

examples.text: 가: 네, 알았어요. 고마워요.
examples.translation: ga: ne, arasseoyo. gomawoyo. — Yes, I understand. Thank you.

examples.text: 가: 너 이번 주 토요일에 뭐해?
examples.translation: ga: neo ibeon ju toyoire mwohae? — What are you doing this Saturday?

examples.text: 나: 응, 나 도서관에 가.
examples.translation: na: eung, na doseogwane ga. — Yeah, I’m going to the library.

examples.text: 가: 토요일인데 도서관에서 공부해?
examples.translation: ga: toyoirinde doseogwaneseo gongbuhae? — It’s Saturday and you’re studying at the library?

examples.text: 나: 어, 다음 주에 시험이 있어.
examples.translation: na: eo, daeum jue siheomi isseo. — Yeah, I have an exam next week.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading and writing): Youngmi’s essay about her grandfather
explanations.body: The book asks you to read Youngmi’s essay about her grandfather and, using 존댓말, to rewrite the underlined words between the lines; the first correction is made for you (일어납니다 → 일어나십니다). The book’s underlines do not survive in the text, so I treat the verbs as the underlined words; the corrections are mine (the digits are spelled out; TV is written 티브이).

examples.text: 우리 할아버지는 아침 다섯 시쯤 일어납니다.
examples.translation: uri harabeojineun achim daseot sijjeum ireonamnida. — My grandfather gets up at around five in the morning.

examples.text: 그리고 매일 아침마다 동네 뒷산을 등산합니다.
examples.translation: geurigo maeil achimmada dongne dwitsaneul deungsanhamnida. — And every morning he hikes the hill behind the neighborhood.

examples.text: 그 후에 일곱 시쯤 아침을 먹습니다.
examples.translation: geu hue ilgop sijjeum achimeul meokseumnida. — After that he eats breakfast at around seven.

examples.text: 그리고 꼭 신문을 읽습니다.
examples.translation: geurigo kkok sinmuneul ikseumnida. — And he always reads the newspaper.

examples.text: 오전에는 노인대학에서 강연을 듣습니다.
examples.translation: ojeoneneun noindaehageseo gangyeoneul deutseumnida. — In the morning he listens to lectures at the senior citizens’ college.

examples.text: 오후에는 보통 동네를 청소하거나 집에서 책을 읽습니다.
examples.translation: ohueneun botong dongnereul cheongsohageona jibeseo chaegeul ikseumnida. — In the afternoon he usually cleans the neighborhood or reads a book at home.

examples.text: 저녁에는 식구들과 같이 밥을 먹고 티브이를 봅니다.
examples.translation: jeonyeogeneun sikgudeulgwa gachi babeul meokgo tibeuireul bomnida. — In the evening he eats with the family and watches television.

examples.text: 그리고 보통 열 시쯤 잡니다.
examples.translation: geurigo botong yeol sijjeum jamnida. — And he usually sleeps at around ten.

explanations.title: The verbs rewritten in 존댓말 (mine)
explanations.body: The honorific forms: –(으)시– after the verb stem; 먹다 → 드시다 and 자다 → 주무시다 are special honorific verbs.

lessons.title: 358. Ch 28 · Activity 2: how foreign K-pop idols learned Korean (읽기)
lessons.subtitle: 듀오링고 · 쯔위 · 리사 · 한국어를 배우는 방법 · 반말 · 존댓말 · 실수

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): a newspaper article about foreign K-pop stars learning Korean
explanations.body: The book asks you to read the article about the Korean language learning experiences of some foreign K-pop stars and to answer in English: (1) What statistic is reported by Duolingo? (2) Fill in the table for 쯔위 and 리사: strategies in learning Korean and difficulties in learning Korean. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out in Hangul (2021 → 이천이십일 년, 76% → 칠십육 퍼센트) and the quotations set off as separate lines (the quotation marks are left out); the English is mine. The book glosses 방송에 출연하다: to appear on a show; 숙소: housing, accommodation.

examples.text: 미국의 언어학습 플랫폼 듀오링고에 따르면 한국 음악과 영화, 드라마의 세계적인 인기로 한국어를 배우려는 사람의 수가 이천이십일 년 이후 무려 칠십육 퍼센트나 늘어났다고 한다.
examples.translation: migugui eoneohakseup peullaetpom dyuoringgoe ttareumyeon hanguk eumakgwa yeonghwa, deuramaui segyejeogin ingiro hangugeoreul baeuryeoneun saramui suga icheonisibil nyeon ihu muryeo chilsimnyuk peosenteuna neureonatdago handa. — According to the American language-learning platform Duolingo, owing to the worldwide popularity of Korean music, movies and dramas, the number of people who want to learn Korean has increased by a whole 76% since 2021.

examples.text: 그렇다면 우리나라에서 활동하고 있는 외국인 아이돌들은 어떻게 한국어를 배웠을까?
examples.translation: geureotamyeon urinaraeseo hwaldonghago inneun oegugin aidoldeureun eotteoke hangugeoreul baewosseulkka? — Then how did the foreign idols who are active in our country learn Korean?

examples.text: 인기 걸그룹 트와이스 멤버 쯔위는 한국어를 배우기 위해 드라마를 자주 본다고 한다.
examples.translation: ingi geolgeurup teuwaiseu membeo jjeuwineun hangugeoreul baeugi wihae deuramareul jaju bondago handa. — Tzuyu, a member of the popular girl group Twice, is said to often watch dramas in order to learn Korean.

examples.text: 대만에서 온 쯔위는 최근에 한 인터뷰에서 이렇게 말했다.
examples.translation: daemaneseo on jjeuwineun choegeune han inteobyueseo ireoke malhaetda. — Tzuyu, who came from Taiwan, said the following in a recent interview.

examples.text: 한국어는 아직도 어려운 편이에요. 제가 아직 모르는 단어가 많아요. 특히 방송에 출연했을 때 선배 가수들이 쓰는 단어들이 어렵게 느껴질 때가 많아요.
examples.translation: hangugeoneun ajikdo eoryeoun pyeonieyo. jega ajik moreuneun daneoga manayo. teuki bangsonge churyeonhaesseul ttae seonbae gasudeuri sseuneun daneodeuri eoryeopge neukkyeojil ttaega manayo. — Korean is still on the difficult side. There are many words I don’t know yet. In particular, when I appear on a show, there are many times the words that senior singers use feel difficult.

examples.text: 쯔위는 이렇게도 말했다.
examples.translation: jjeuwineun ireokedo malhaetda. — Tzuyu also said the following.

examples.text: 주위에서 한국어를 잘 하려면 드라마와 영화를 많이 보라고 해서 자주 보려고 해요. 또 드라마에서 새로운 단어나 표현이 나오면 부지런히 외우려고 해요.
examples.translation: juwieseo hangugeoreul jal haryeomyeon deuramawa yeonghwareul mani borago haeseo jaju boryeogo haeyo. tto deuramaeseo saeroun daneona pyohyeoni naomyeon bujireonhi oeuryeogo haeyo. — People around me tell me to watch many dramas and movies if I want to be good at Korean, so I try to watch often. Also, when a new word or expression comes up in a drama, I try to memorize it diligently.

examples.text: 또 다른 걸그룹 블랙핑크의 멤버인 리사는 태국에서 왔다.
examples.translation: tto dareun geolgeurup beullaekpingkeuui membeoin risaneun taegugeseo watda. — Lisa, a member of another girl group, Blackpink, came from Thailand.

examples.text: 데뷔 전부터 매일 한국어 수업을 두 시간씩 받았던 리사는 이렇게 말했다.
examples.translation: debwi jeonbuteo maeil hangugeo sueobeul du siganssik badatdeon risaneun ireoke malhaetda. — Lisa, who had taken Korean classes for two hours every day since before her debut, said the following.

examples.text: 제가 멤버들과 같이 숙소 생활을 했어요. 그 때 다른 멤버들과 계속 한국어로 이야기하려고 많이 노력 했어요. 그래서 빨리 배운 것 같아요.
examples.translation: jega membeodeulgwa gachi sukso saenghwareul haesseoyo. geu ttae dareun membeodeulgwa gyesok hangugeoro iyagiharyeogo mani noryeok haesseoyo. geuraeseo ppalli baeun geot gatayo. — I lived in the dorm together with the members. At that time I made a lot of effort to keep talking in Korean with the other members. So I think I learned fast.

examples.text: 한국어를 배울 때 어려운 점에 대해서는 리사는 이렇게 말하며 웃었다.
examples.translation: hangugeoreul baeul ttae eoryeoun jeome daehaeseoneun risaneun ireoke malhamyeo useotda. — About the difficult points when learning Korean, Lisa laughed and said the following.

examples.text: 멤버들이랑은 반말로 이야기하니까 다른 사람들한테 존댓말을 자연스럽게 쓰기가 어려웠어요. 그래서 실수도 많이 하고 틀린 표현도 많이 썼어요.
examples.translation: membeodeurirangeun banmallo iyagihanikka dareun saramdeulhante jondaenmareul jayeonseureopge sseugiga eoryeowosseoyo. geuraeseo silsudo mani hago teullin pyohyeondo mani sseosseoyo. — Because I talk in blunt language with the members, it was hard to use honorific language naturally to other people. So I made many mistakes and used many wrong expressions.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the answers blank; these are mine.

rows: 1. What statistic is reported by Duolingo?
The number of people who want to learn Korean has increased by 76% since 2021
She often watches dramas; people around her advise watching many dramas and movies; she diligently memorizes new words and expressions from dramas
Korean is still on the difficult side; there are many words she doesn’t know; the words senior singers use on shows feel difficult
She took a two-hour Korean class every day before her debut; she lived in the dorm with the members and made an effort to keep talking to them in Korean
She speaks blunt language (반말) with the members, so it was hard to use honorific language (존댓말) naturally with others, and she made many mistakes and used wrong expressions

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (a SMART Board activity), Activity 3 (a video clip), and Activity 4 (reading, speaking and writing activities with students’ own essays and group work, whose texts are not part of the book’s text) are computer, video and group activities.

explanations.title: Topic C: In Korea we bow our heads to greet (한국에서는 고개를 숙여서 인사해요)
explanations.body: Mark and Soyeon are talking about the different ways of greeting and about etiquette in Korea and America. (The English is mine; the book gives none. The stage direction “(웃으면서)”, laughing, and the ellipsis in “얘기하는데…” are left out.)

examples.text: 마크: 한국에서는 인사하는 방법이 미국과 좀 다른 것 같아요. 그래서 제가 실수를 몇 번 했어요.
examples.translation: makeu: hangugeseoneun insahaneun bangbeobi migukgwa jom dareun geot gatayo. geuraeseo jega silsureul myeot beon haesseoyo. — The way of greeting in Korea seems a little different from America. So I made a few mistakes.

examples.text: 소연: 어떤 실수를 했어요?
examples.translation: soyeon: eotteon silsureul haesseoyo? — What kind of mistakes did you make?

examples.text: 마크: 며칠 전에 친구 집에 갔을 때 인사하면서 할머니를 포옹했어요. 그래서 옆에 있는 사람들이 웃었어요.
examples.translation: makeu: myeochil jeone chingu jibe gasseul ttae insahamyeonseo halmeonireul poonghaesseoyo. geuraeseo yeope inneun saramdeuri useosseoyo. — A few days ago when I went to a friend’s house I hugged the grandmother as I greeted her. So the people next to us laughed.

examples.text: 소연: 그랬어요? 한국에서는 보통 고개를 숙여서 인사해요. 그리고 어른한테는 허리를 굽혀서 공손히 인사하고요.
examples.translation: soyeon: geuraesseoyo? hangugeseoneun botong gogaereul sugyeoseo insahaeyo. geurigo eoreunhanteneun heorireul gupyeoseo gongsonhi insahagoyo. — Did you? In Korea we usually greet by bowing the head. And to elders we greet politely by bending at the waist.

examples.text: 마크: 그래요? 미국에서는 인사할 때 손을 흔들거나 악수를 해요. 그리고 포옹도 하고요.
examples.translation: makeu: geuraeyo? migugeseoneun insahal ttae soneul heundeulgeona aksureul haeyo. geurigo poongdo hagoyo. — Is that so? In America when we greet, we wave a hand or shake hands. And we also hug.

examples.text: 소연: 또 미국사람들은 말하면서 제스처를 많이 쓰지요?
examples.translation: soyeon: tto miguksaramdeureun malhamyeonseo jeseucheoreul mani sseujiyo? — Also, Americans use many gestures while talking, don’t they?

examples.text: 마크: 네, 그렇죠. 한국사람들은 어때요? 한국에서 대화할 때 지켜야 할 에티켓이 있나요?
examples.translation: makeu: ne, geureocho. hanguksaramdeureun eottaeyo? hangugeseo daehwahal ttae jikyeoya hal etikesi innayo? — Yes, that’s right. What about Koreans? Is there any etiquette that I should observe when talking in Korea?

examples.text: 소연: 네, 어른과 대화할 때 보통 눈을 똑바로 쳐다보지 않아요. 또 다리를 꼬거나 흔드는 것도 좋지 않아요. 그리고 제스처를 많이 쓰지 않는 편이에요.
examples.translation: soyeon: ne, eoreungwa daehwahal ttae botong nuneul ttokbaro cheodaboji anayo. tto darireul kkogeona heundeuneun geotdo jochi anayo. geurigo jeseucheoreul mani sseuji anneun pyeonieyo. — Yes, when talking with elders, we usually do not stare straight into their eyes. Also, crossing or shaking the legs is not good either. And we tend not to use many gestures.

examples.text: 마크: 그래요? 미국에서는 대체로 상대방의 눈을 보면서 얘기하는데, 참, 내일 차 교수님 댁에 저녁 초대를 받았어요. 주의해야 할 식사예절이 있어요?
examples.translation: makeu: geuraeyo? migugeseoneun daechero sangdaebangui nuneul bomyeonseo yaegihaneunde, cham, naeil cha gyosunim daege jeonyeok chodaereul badasseoyo. juuihaeya hal siksayejeori isseoyo? — Is that so? In America we generally talk looking into the other person’s eyes, and, oh, I have been invited to dinner at Professor Cha’s home tomorrow. Is there any table etiquette I should be careful about?

examples.text: 소연: 네. 식사할 때는 어른보다 먼저 수저를 들지 않는 것이 좋아요. 그리고 음식을 주시면 두 손으로 받으세요.
examples.translation: soyeon: ne. siksahal ttaeneun eoreunboda meonjeo sujeoreul deulji anneun geosi joayo. geurigo eumsigeul jusimyeon du soneuro badeuseyo. — Yes. When eating, it is good not to pick up your spoon and chopsticks before the elders. And when they give you food, please receive it with both hands.

examples.text: 마크: 네. 소연 씨, 고마워요. 그렇게 하지요.
examples.translation: makeu: ne. soyeon ssi, gomawoyo. geureoke hajiyo. — Yes. Thank you, Soyeon. I will do that.

explanations.title: Notes: the beckoning gesture
explanations.body: Gestures differ between cultures. In America, to beckon someone toward you, a slightly cupped hand is moved toward you repeatedly. In Korea, to call someone over, the hand is held up with the palm facing down and the fingers are moved back and forth. (The book’s pictures are left out.)

lessons.title: 361. Ch 28 · Grammar B: –지(요), intention or suggestion in a friendly manner
lessons.subtitle: -지요 · -죠 · 제가 청소하지요 · 제 차로 가죠 · 오늘은 한국 식당에서 먹지요

explanations.title: –지(요): intention or suggestion in a friendly manner
explanations.body:
Recall that you have learned –지요 as a tag question: 오늘 날씨가 좋지요? and 이 음식이 참 맛있지요? Now you will learn that –지요 can also be used in statements to express the speaker’s intention (“I will”) or a suggestion (“Let’s”). For example, 음식은 내가 만들지요 (cf. 만들겠어요) = I will make the food; and 오늘은 한국 식당에서 먹지요 (cf. 먹읍시다) = Let’s eat at a Korean restaurant today.

–지요 is often contracted to –죠: 음식은 제가 만들죠. 오늘은 한국 식당으로 가시죠.

examples.text: 음식은 내가 만들지요.
examples.translation: eumsigeun naega mandeuljiyo. — I will make the food. (cf. 만들겠어요)

examples.text: 오늘은 한국 식당에서 먹지요.
examples.translation: oneureun hanguk sikdangeseo meokjiyo. — Let’s eat at a Korean restaurant today. (cf. 먹읍시다)

examples.translation: eumsigeun jega mandeuljo. — I will make the food. (contracted)

examples.translation: oneureun hanguk sikdangeuro gasijo. — Let’s go to a Korean restaurant today. (contracted, honorific)

lessons.title: 362. Ch 28 · Grammar C: –나(요), the interrogative ending
lessons.subtitle: -나요 · 먹나요 · 가나요 · 읽나요 · 집합하나 · 요리했나

explanations.title: –나(요): an interrogative ending
explanations.body:
한국사람들은 매일 김치를 먹어요? can also be said 한국사람들은 매일 김치를 먹나요? There is no difference in meaning between the two. –나요 is a variation of –아/어요 and is an informal polite ending, but it is used only for questions. It softens the tone of the question and is used more by female speakers.

The 요 can be dropped in the informal blunt style. –나 is used to direct a question to oneself or to one’s subordinate in a rigid hierarchy, such as the military: 한국사람들은 매일 김치를 먹나? (to oneself); 김 일병, 몇 시에 집합하나? (to a subordinate: Private First Class Kim, what time do you have formation?).

examples.text: 민기 씨는 체육관에 자주 가나요?
examples.translation: mingi ssineun cheyukgwane jaju ganayo? — Does Mingi go to the gym often?

examples.text: 한국사람들은 매일 김치를 먹나요?
examples.translation: hanguksaramdeureun maeil gimchireul meongnayo? — Do Koreans eat kimchi every day?

examples.text: 한국사람들은 매일 김치를 먹나?
examples.translation: hanguksaramdeureun maeil gimchireul meongna? — Do Koreans eat kimchi every day? (asked to oneself)

examples.text: 김 일병, 몇 시에 집합하나?
examples.translation: gim ilbyeong, myeot sie jipapana? — Private First Class Kim, what time do you have formation? (asked to a subordinate)

explanations.body: Verb stem + 나(요)? The book’s examples (the English is mine; the book’s “MLI asking; SPC Kim” means a military language instructor asking a specialist):

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Verb stem + 나요 (a stem ending in ㄹ drops the ㄹ: 살다 → 사나요, 만들다 → 만드나요), and the past form with –았/었나요.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify different generations and talk about them; identify and use two different language registers, 존댓말 and 반말; and identify and talk about Korean manners and etiquette.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; a summary of speech styles; the verb ending –지(요); the interrogative ending –나(요); and the Sino-Korean syllables 례/예 (禮) and 음 (音).

explanations.title: What Chapter 29 teaches (병과 증상)
explanations.body:
Unit 8 is 건강, “Health”. Chapter 29, “Common Ailments and Symptoms”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and describe general health conditions, common ailments, and symptoms; identify and talk about basic medical and clinical specialties; and ask about common ailments and provide treatment suggestions.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; ㅅ irregular verbs; –도록 하다 (to make sure …; to see to it that …); –(으)ㄴ 지 ~(이/가) 되다 (It has been … since …); the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄴ/는 김에 (because; since; as); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 병원 (病院), 통증 (痛症), and 혈압 (血壓).

explanations.title: Medical specialties
explanations.body: The book’s list of medical specialties (the meanings are the book’s, from the Core Vocabulary). A doctor of a specialty is 과 + 의사, as in 치과 의사 (a dentist).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 병원 (病院)
explanations.body:
This Sino-Korean word means a hospital or medical clinic. The first syllable 병 (病) means sickness, illness, or disease, as in 병실 (a sickroom; an infirmary), 병석 (a sickbed; “sickness place”), and 병사 (a death from sickness). The second syllable 원 (院) means public building or house, as in 학원 (an educational institute; an academy; “learning house”), 양로원 (a nursing home), 법원 (a courthouse; “law house”), 상원 (the Upper House; the Senate), and 하원 (the Lower House; the House of Representatives). Thus the literal meaning of 병원 is “illness house” or “disease house”, and the word refers to a hospital or medical clinic, even a doctor’s office.

Keep in mind that 원 in the following words represents 병원: 입원 (admission into a hospital; hospitalization), 퇴원 (leaving the hospital; discharge from the hospital), and 원장 (the director [of a hospital]; “hospital chief”).

rows: an educational institute; an academy; “learning house”
the Lower House; the House of Representatives
leaving the hospital; discharge from the hospital

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 통증 (痛症)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means a (physical) pain. The first syllable 통 (痛) means ache or pain, as in 두통 (a headache), 치통 (a toothache), 복통 (a stomachache), and 신경통 (neuralgia; “nerve pain”). The second syllable 증 (症) means symptom, as in 불면증 (insomnia; “no sleeping symptom”), 우울증 (the blues; mental depression; “melancholy symptom”), and 증상 (symptoms; the condition [of a patient]; “symptom and condition”). Thus the literal meaning of 통증 is “pain symptom” and the word means a physical pain, an ache, a pang, or pricking.

rows: symptoms; the condition (of a patient); “symptom and condition”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 혈압 (血壓)
explanations.body:
This Sino-Korean word means blood pressure. The first syllable 혈 (血) means blood, as in 혈관 (a blood vessel; a vein; “blood tube”), 혈색 (a complexion; “blood color”), 혈액 (blood; “blood fluid”), and 수혈 (blood transfusion). The second syllable 압 (壓) means pressure or pressing, as in 고혈압 (hypertension; high blood pressure), 수압 (hydraulic pressure; “water pressure”), 압력 (pressure; “pressing power”), 고압 (high pressure; high tension; high voltage), and 중압감 (a feeling of oppression; “heavy pressing feeling”).

The book asks you to guess the meaning of 저혈압 and 혈액형 (my answers: low blood pressure; blood type).

rows: a blood vessel; a vein; “blood tube”

a feeling of oppression; “heavy pressing feeling”

explanations.title: Vocabulary Learning Strategy: use new words in meaningful ways
explanations.body: Many language experts agree that the best way to learn and memorize new words is to repeatedly use them in meaningful ways. Here are a few tips: read and listen to the new words in a sentence or paragraph; say the new words aloud to activate your auditory memory; relate the new words to words you already know; make up a sentence or create a story using the new words; and use the new words in an actual conversation.

explanations.title: Topic A: I had a hard time with the flu (독감에 걸려서 고생했어)
explanations.body: A woman who is suffering from allergies and her pregnant friend are discussing their physical conditions. (The English is mine; the book gives none. The book writes 나… and 식욕도 없고… with ellipses; they are left out, and 3개월 is spelled out.)

examples.text: 민아: 오랜만이야. 요즘 잘 지내?
examples.translation: mina: oraenmaniya. yojeum jal jinae? — It’s been a long time. How have you been lately?

examples.text: 주희: 발랐어. 그런데 발라도 가려우니까 계속 긁어. 이제는 긁은 데가 아프기 시작해.
examples.translation: juhui: ballasseo. geureonde ballado garyeounikka gyesok geulgeo. ijeneun geulgeun dega apeugi sijakae. — I did. But even when I apply it, it’s itchy, so I keep scratching. Now the places I scratched are starting to hurt.

examples.text: 민아: 아니, 나 임신했어.
examples.translation: mina: ani, na imsinhaesseo. — No, I’m pregnant.

examples.text: 주희: 어머! 축하해. 얼마나 됐어?
examples.translation: juhui: eomeo! chukahae. eolmana dwaesseo? — Oh my! Congratulations. How far along are you?

examples.text: 민아: 이제 삼 개월 조금 넘었어. 요즘은 어지럽고 구역질도 나서 힘들어. 식욕도 없고.
examples.translation: mina: ije sam gaewol jogeum neomeosseo. yojeumeun eojireopgo guyeokjildo naseo himdeureo. sigyokdo eopgo. — It’s just a little over three months now. These days I’m dizzy and I feel nauseated, so it’s hard. I have no appetite either.

examples.text: 주희: 그래? 그래도 임신했을 때는 잘 먹어야 해.
examples.translation: juhui: geurae? geuraedo imsinhaesseul ttaeneun jal meogeoya hae. — Is that so? Still, when you’re pregnant you have to eat well.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading): the symptoms table

The symptoms are the book’s; the ticks (my answers; the book’s check marks do not survive in the text) and the English are mine.

explanations.body: The flu (독감) and a body ache (몸살) bring a fever, a cough, a sore throat and aching; allergies (알레르기) bring itching and red, swollen eyes; pregnancy (임신) brings dizziness, nausea and loss of appetite (Topic A’s dialog).

explanations.title: Topic B: My lower back really hurts (허리 통증이 심해요)
explanations.body: Two college students, Hyunsoo and Jeongin, are talking about Jeongin’s hospital visit for her severe lower back pain. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

lessons.title: 369. Ch 29 · Grammar A: ㅅ irregular verbs (낫다, 붓다, 짓다, 젓다, 긋다, 잇다)
lessons.subtitle: ㅅ 불규칙 · 나았어요 · 부었어요 · 지었어요 · 저으세요 · 그으세요 · 이어요

explanations.title: ㅅ irregular verbs
explanations.body:
You have learned a few verbs whose stem ends in ㅅ, such as 낫다, 붓다, 벗다, and 씻다. Some of these verbs lose ㅅ when their stem is followed by a vowel. Take 낫다 (to get well): 낫 + 았어요 → 나았어요; 낫 + 아서 → 나아서; 낫 + 으면 → 나으면; 낫 + (으)ㄹ 때 → 나을 때.

Verbs that lose ㅅ when their stem is followed by a vowel are commonly known as “ㅅ irregular verbs”. However, not all verbs whose stem ends in ㅅ are ㅅ irregular verbs. For example, 벗다 is not an ㅅ irregular verb and does not lose ㅅ even when the stem is followed by a vowel, as in 운동복을 벗어서 세탁기에 넣으세요 (Take off your gym suit and put it in the washing machine). Only the following verbs, including 낫다, are ㅅ irregular verbs: 낫다 (to recover [from sickness]), 붓다 (to swell; to become swollen; to pour), 짓다 (to build; to compose), 젓다 (to stir), 긋다 (to draw [a line]) and 잇다 (to connect).

lessons.title: 370. Ch 29 · Grammar B: –도록 하다, to make sure; to see to it that
lessons.subtitle: -도록 하다 · 조심하도록 하겠습니다 · 드시도록 하세요 · 일어나도록 하세요 · 하도록 하셨어요

explanations.title: –도록 하다: make sure …; see to it that …
explanations.body: –도록 하다 is equivalent to the English phrases “to make sure …” or “to see to it that …”. When the speaker is the subject, the future tense is used with –도록 하다 to indicate the speaker’s will. –도록 하다 can also be used to offer suggestions or advice. It also expresses the idea of causing or influencing an action that has taken place. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 앞으로 조심하도록 하겠습니다.
examples.translation: apeuro josimhadorok hagetseumnida. — I will make sure to be cautious from now on.

examples.text: 전기를 아껴 쓰도록 할게요.
examples.translation: jeongireul akkyeo sseudorok halgeyo. — I will make sure to save electricity.

examples.text: 이 약을 하루에 세 번씩 드시도록 하세요.
examples.translation: i yageul harue se beonssik deusidorok haseyo. — Make sure you take this medication three times a day.

examples.text: 아침에 일찍 일어나도록 하세요.
examples.translation: achime iljjik ireonadorok haseyo. — Make sure you get up early in the morning.

explanations.title: Topic C: I had a health checkup (건강 검진을 받았어요)
explanations.body: Two colleagues are conversing about the medical checkup one of them received recently. (The English is mine; the book gives none; 3년 is spelled out.)

examples.text: 김 과장: 박 과장, 건강 검진은 잘 받았어?
examples.translation: gim gwajang: bak gwajang, geongang geomjineun jal badasseo? — Section Chief Park, did you get your health checkup well?

examples.text: 박 과장: 응. 잘 받았어.
examples.translation: bak gwajang: eung. jal badasseo. — Yes. I got it done well.

examples.text: 김 과장: 어떤 검사를 했는데?
examples.translation: gim gwajang: eotteon geomsareul haenneunde? — What tests did you do?

examples.text: 박 과장: 혈액 검사하고 소변 검사.
examples.translation: bak gwajang: hyeoraek geomsahago sobyeon geomsa. — A blood test and a urine test.

examples.text: 김 과장: 다 정상이래?
examples.translation: gim gwajang: da jeongsangirae? — They say everything is normal?

examples.text: 박 과장: 전에는 간이 좀 안 좋았었는데, 지금은 괜찮대.
examples.translation: bak gwajang: jeoneneun gani jom an joasseonneunde, jigeumeun gwaenchantae. — My liver wasn’t so good before, but they say it’s fine now.

examples.text: 김 과장: 콜레스테롤하고 혈압은 어때?
examples.translation: gim gwajang: kolleseuterolhago hyeorabeun eottae? — How about your cholesterol and blood pressure?

examples.text: 박 과장: 혈압은 정상인데 콜레스테롤 수치는 조금 높아.
examples.translation: bak gwajang: hyeorabeun jeongsanginde kolleseuterol suchineun jogeum nopa. — My blood pressure is normal, but my cholesterol level is a little high.

examples.text: 김 과장: 요즘 계속 살이 빠져서 나도 검진을 받을 생각이야.
examples.translation: gim gwajang: yojeum gyesok sari ppajeoseo nado geomjineul badeul saenggagiya. — I keep losing weight these days, so I’m planning to get a checkup, too.

examples.text: 박 과장: 최근에 검진 받지 않았어?
examples.translation: bak gwajang: choegeune geomjin batji anasseo? — Didn’t you get a checkup recently?

examples.text: 김 과장: 아니. 검진 받은 지 벌써 삼 년 됐어.
examples.translation: gim gwajang: ani. geomjin badeun ji beolsseo sam nyeon dwaesseo. — No. It has already been three years since I had a checkup.

examples.text: 박 과장: 그래? 그럼 검진 받을 때가 됐구나!
examples.translation: bak gwajang: geurae? geureom geomjin badeul ttaega dwaetguna! — Is that so? Then it’s time for you to get a checkup!

examples.text: 김 과장: 응. 이번에 검진 받는 김에 이것저것 다 받아 봐야겠어.
examples.translation: gim gwajang: eung. ibeone geomjin banneun gime igeotjeogeot da bada bwayagesseo. — Yes. Since I’m getting a checkup this time, I should try everything.

explanations.title: The book’s footnote
explanations.body: 이것저것 다 literally means “this thing, that thing, and all” and is translated as “everything”. When referring to every person or to everyone, we say 이 사람 저 사람 다.

explanations.title: Core words and phrases of Topic C
explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter); 검진(하다/받다), 대변(보다), 소변(보다) and 측정(하다) take the forms in parentheses; the two patterns are explained in the grammar.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): the question on a hospital’s health counseling page
explanations.body: The book shows a Q&A posted on the health counseling section of a hospital website (진료상담, 소화기내과): the title is 설사와 복통이 심합니다 (I have severe diarrhea and a stomachache), posted by 김진경. Read it and fill in a table in English. The text is the book’s with the form’s date and view count left out; the English is mine.

examples.text: 지난주에 돼지고기와 맥주를 마셨어요.
examples.translation: jinanjue dwaejigogiwa maekjureul masyeosseoyo. — Last week I had pork and beer.

examples.text: 그리고 잠을 잤는데 갑자기 복통이 시작되었습니다.
examples.translation: geurigo jameul janneunde gapjagi boktongi sijakdoeeotseumnida. — Then I slept, and suddenly a stomachache began.

examples.text: 약국에서 소화제를 사 먹었는데 낫지를 않습니다.
examples.translation: yakgugeseo sohwajereul sa meogeonneunde natjireul anseumnida. — I bought and took a digestive medicine at a pharmacy, but it is not getting better.

examples.text: 어젯밤에는 배가 너무 아파서 잠도 잘 못 잤어요.
examples.translation: eojetbameneun baega neomu apaseo jamdo jal mot jasseoyo. — Last night my stomach hurt so much that I could not sleep well.

examples.text: 계속 아랫배에 심한 통증이 있고 구역질이 납니다.
examples.translation: gyesok araetbaee simhan tongjeungi itgo guyeokjiri namnida. — I keep having severe pain in my lower abdomen and feel nauseated.

examples.text: 어제부터는 설사도 나기 시작했어요.
examples.translation: eojebuteoneun seolsado nagi sijakaesseoyo. — Since yesterday I have also started to have diarrhea.

examples.text: 바빠서 병원에 가지 못하고 있습니다.
examples.translation: bappaseo byeongwone gaji motago itseumnida. — I am busy and cannot go to the hospital.

examples.text: 어떻게 해야 할까요?
examples.translation: eotteoke haeya halkkayo? — What should I do?

examples.text: 환자분의 증상을 보면 단순한 소화불량이 아닌 것 같습니다.
examples.translation: hwanjabunui jeungsangeul bomyeon dansunhan sohwabullyangi anin geot gatseumnida. — Judging from your symptoms, it does not seem to be simple indigestion.

explanations.title: Topic C, Follow-up 1 (Reading): a medical checkup brochure
explanations.body: The book gives a brochure for a checkup program (영광병원 건강센터) and asks you (a) to translate the underlined parts into English and (b) to find in the brochure what patients must do on the day of the test. The book’s underlines do not survive in the text, so the whole brochure is given here with my English; the numbers are spelled out in Hangul, the headings and the numbered lists are written as sentences (the book’s “항목” = “an item”).

lessons.subtitle: -(으)ㄴ 지 되다 · 온 지 일 년이 되었어요 · 입대한 지 삼 년 · 얼마나 되었어요 · 몇 년 되었어요

explanations.title: Expressing the passage of time: –(으)ㄴ 지 ~(이/가) 되다
explanations.body:
In English, to express the passage of time since a certain event or action took place, we often use “it has been [length of time] since …” or “[length of time] have passed since …”, as in “It has been a year since I came to DLI”.

In Korean, we express a passage of time with –(으)ㄴ 지 ~(이/가) 되다, as in 몬트레이에 온 지 일 년이 되었어요 (It has been a year since I came to Monterey). 되었어요 means “became” or “has become”, and the literal translation of the phrase is “it has become a year since I came to Monterey”. The particle (이/가) after the length of time may be dropped, as in 공군에 입대한 지 삼 년(이) 되었습니다. (The book writes the numbers in digits; they are spelled out in Hangul here.)

examples.text: 몬트레이에 온 지 일 년이 되었어요.
examples.translation: monteureie on ji il nyeoni doeeosseoyo. — It has been a year since I came to Monterey.

examples.text: 공군에 입대한 지 삼 년이 되었습니다.
examples.translation: gonggune ipdaehan ji sam nyeoni doeeotseumnida. — It has been three years since I became an airman.

examples.text: 그 친구를 만난 지 오래 되었어요.
examples.translation: geu chingureul mannan ji orae doeeosseoyo. — A long time has passed since I met my friend.

examples.text: 한국말을 공부한 지 벌써 오 개월이 됐습니다.
examples.translation: hangungmareul gongbuhan ji beolsseo o gaewori dwaetseumnida. — Five months have already passed since I started to learn Korean.

explanations.title: Asking about the passage of time
explanations.body: To ask about the passage of time, we use 얼마나, which means “how long”, or 몇 ~, as in 몇 년 (how many years), 몇 시간 (how many hours), 며칠 (how many days), etc.

examples.text: 몬트레이에 온 지 얼마나 되었습니까?
examples.translation: monteureie on ji eolmana doeeotseumnikka? — How long has it been since you came to Monterey?

examples.text: 공군에 입대한 지 몇 년 되었어요?
examples.translation: gonggune ipdaehan ji myeon nyeon doeeosseoyo? — How long has it been since you joined the air force?

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: The question 지 얼마나 되었어요? is made with the verb’s past attributive form (–(으)ㄴ) + 지, for the book’s ten interview phrases of Follow-up 1.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Speaking and listening): the model
explanations.body: The book asks you to interview two classmates with these phrases and to write their answers in English. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 박 일병, 건강검진을 받은 지 얼마나 되었어요?
examples.translation: ga: bak ilbyeong, geonganggeomjineul badeun ji eolmana doeeosseoyo? — Private Park, how long has it been since you had a health checkup?

examples.text: 나: 일 년 되었어요.
examples.translation: na: il nyeon doeeosseoyo. — It has been one year.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking): a plan to see your family this holiday season
explanations.body: The book asks you to think about how long it has been since you were in your hometown and what else you want to do when you are there, then to tell three classmates, using –(으)ㄴ 지 ~(이/가) 되다 and –는 김에. The book’s model (2년 is spelled out; the English is mine):

examples.text: 고향에 안 간 지 이 년이나 되었어요.
examples.translation: gohyange an gan ji i nyeonina doeeosseoyo. — It has been as long as two years since I last went to my hometown.

examples.text: 그래서 이번 크리스마스 때 가족을 보러 고향에 갈 겁니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo ibeon keuriseumaseu ttae gajogeul boreo gohyange gal geomnida. — So this Christmas I will go to my hometown to see my family.

examples.text: 고향에 간 김에 고향 친구들을 만날 거예요.
examples.translation: gohyange gan gime gohyang chingudeureul mannal geoyeyo. — Since I will be in my hometown, I will meet my hometown friends.

examples.text: 고향 친구들을 만난 김에 친구들과 함께 영화도 볼 거예요.
examples.translation: gohyang chingudeureul mannan gime chingudeulgwa hamkke yeonghwado bol geoyeyo. — Since I will have met my hometown friends, I will also watch a movie with them.

lessons.title: 374. Ch 29 · Grammar D: the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄴ/는 김에
lessons.subtitle: -는 김에 · -ㄴ 김에 · 집청소하는 김에 빨래도 · 시장에 가는 김에 · 가는 길에

explanations.title: The conjunctive ending –(으)ㄴ/는 김에
explanations.body: While engaging in a certain intended activity, we often take advantage of the activity to do another activity that is not originally intended. The conjunctive ending –는 김에 is used in this context. In the first example the speaker’s main activity was doing house cleaning, and while doing it the speaker “took advantage” and also did laundry, an activity not originally intended. Likewise, in the second the speaker takes advantage of the opportunity of learning Korean and wants to learn Korean history as well. For this reason the ending works only with an action verb and, depending on the context, it can be translated as “because”, “since”, “as” or “while”.

examples.text: 집청소하는 김에 빨래도 했어요.
examples.translation: jipcheongsohaneun gime ppallaedo haesseoyo. — Since I was doing house cleaning, I did laundry as well.

examples.text: 한국어를 배우는 김에 한국 역사도 배우고 싶어요.
examples.translation: hangugeoreul baeuneun gime hanguk yeoksado baeugo sipeoyo. — Because I am learning Korean, I’d also like to learn Korean history.

examples.text: 시장에 가는 김에 술 좀 사다 주세요.
examples.translation: sijange ganeun gime sul jom sada juseyo. — Because you are going to the market, please get me some liquor.

examples.text: 피자를 주문하는 김에 음료수도 시킵시다.
examples.translation: pijareul jumunhaneun gime eumnyosudo sikipsida. — While we are ordering pizza, let’s order drinks as well.

explanations.title: –(으)ㄴ 김에
explanations.body: –(으)ㄴ 김에 can be used as well, but it implies that after the intended activity has been completed, the originally unintended activity is engaged in:

examples.text: 한국어를 배운 김에 한국 역사도 배우고 싶어요.
examples.translation: hangugeoreul baeun gime hanguk yeoksado baeugo sipeoyo. — Because I have learned Korean, I’d like to learn Korean history also.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Verb stem + 는 김에 (a stem ending in ㄹ drops the ㄹ: 만들다 → 만드는 김에) for the activity in progress, and –(으)ㄴ 김에 after it is completed.

explanations.title: Note: do not confuse it with –가는/오는 길에
explanations.body: This conjunctive ending should not be confused with –가는/오는 길에 (on one’s way to), as in:

examples.text: 시내에 가는 길에 반 친구를 만났어요.
examples.translation: sinaee ganeun gire ban chingureul mannasseoyo. — On my way downtown, I met my classmate.

examples.text: 학교에 오는 길에 도서관에 들렀어요.
examples.translation: hakgyoe oneun gire doseogwane deulleosseoyo. — On my way to school, I stopped at the library.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Speaking and listening): the sentence chain
explanations.body: The book’s circle game: the instructor begins with a –(으)ㄴ/는 김에 sentence, and the next student builds a new one with the last verb. The book’s example (the English is mine):

examples.text: 시내에 간 김에 친구를 만났어요.
examples.translation: sinaee gan gime chingureul mannasseoyo. — Since I went downtown, I met a friend.

examples.text: 친구를 만난 김에 점심을 같이 먹었어요.
examples.translation: chingureul mannan gime jeomsimeul gachi meogeosseoyo. — Since I met my friend, we had lunch together.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 3 (the circle game), Follow-up 4 (listening to two husband–wife conversations, to write the main and secondary activities), Activity 1 (SMART Board), Activity 2 (summarizing two checkup articles and exchanging information with a partner) and Activity 3 (listening to two checkup packages and recommending one) are audio, computer and partner activities.

The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify and describe general health conditions, common ailments, and symptoms; identify and talk about basic medical and clinical specialties; and ask about common ailments and provide treatment suggestions.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; ㅅ irregular verbs; –도록 하다; –(으)ㄴ 지 ~(이/가) 되다; the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄴ/는 김에; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 병원 (病院), 통증 (痛症), and 혈압 (血壓).

explanations.title: What Chapter 30 teaches (응급상황)
explanations.body:
Chapter 30, “Medical Emergencies”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: talk about accidents and physical conditions in a medical emergency situation; state reasons for an accident; ask for help in a medical emergency situation; and give instructions for first aid in a medical emergency situation.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; an attributive form + 경우(에) (in case; if; when); the auxiliary verb –아/어 두다 or –아/어 놓다; the causative infixes 이, 히, 리, 기, 우, 구, and 추; the conjunctive ending –는 바람에 (because); and the Sino-Korean syllables 화상 (火傷) and 교사 (敎師).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 화상 (火傷)
explanations.body:
This Sino-Korean word means a burn (on the physical body). The first syllable 화 (火) means fire, as in 화산 (a volcano; “fire mountain”), 화력 (heating power; thermal power; “fire power”), 화재 (a fire; “fire disaster”), and 화약 (gunpowder; “fire medicine”). The second syllable 상 (傷) means wound or injury, as in 중상 (a serious injury; a heavy injury), 상처 (a wound; an injury; a cut; a gash; a bruise; “wounded place”), 총상 (a gunshot wound; a firearm injury), and 치명상 (a lethal wound). Thus the literal meaning of the word is “fire injury”, and it refers to an injury produced by fire, heat, radiation, electricity, or a caustic agent.

The book asks you to guess the meaning of 휴화산, 활화산 and 동상, with the gloss 동 (凍): freezing (my answers: a dormant volcano; an active volcano; frostbite).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 교사 (敎師)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means a teacher or an instructor. The first syllable 교 (敎) means teaching, as in 교육 (education; “teaching and fostering [upbringing]”), 교실 (a classroom; “teaching room”), 교수 (a professor; “teaching and giving”), 교생 (a teacher student; “teaching student”), and 교관 (a [military] instructor; “teaching officer”). The second syllable 사 (師) means master, mentor, or teacher, as in 의사 (a medical doctor; “medical master”), 간호사 (a nurse; “nursing master”), and 약사 (a pharmacist; “medicine master”). Thus the literal meaning of 교사 is “teaching master”, and the word refers to an instructor (at an educational institute).

explanations.title: 한국어에는: names and dates go from general to specific
explanations.body: In Korean, names and dates go from general to specific. When stating the date of an event or birthday, the order is year, month, day, and time, as in 1959년 6월 25일 오전 6시. This word order also applies to addresses, as in 서울특별시 서초구 반포동 942번지. Note that the city (특별시) is followed by its district 구 (區), then the ward 동 (洞), and finally the house number (번지). (The numbers are spelled out in Hangul in the table.)

examples.text: 그런데 실수로 오븐을 만졌습니다.
examples.translation: geureonde silsuro obeuneul manjeotseumnida. — But by mistake he touched the oven.

examples.text: 오븐이 너무 뜨거웠습니다.
examples.translation: obeuni neomu tteugeowotseumnida. — The oven was very hot.

examples.text: 그래서 성진 씨는 손에 화상을 입었습니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo seongjin ssineun sone hwasangeul ibeotseumnida. — So Seongjin got a burn on his hand.

examples.text: 아주 아팠습니다.
examples.translation: aju apatseumnida. — It hurt a lot.

examples.text: 그래서 차가운 물로 상처를 씻고 병원에 갔습니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo chagaun mullo sangcheoreul ssitgo byeongwone gatseumnida. — So he washed the wound with cold water and went to the hospital.

examples.text: 성진 씨는 의사 선생님한테 뜨거운 오븐에 손을 데었다고 말했습니다.
examples.translation: seongjin ssineun uisa seonsaengnimhante tteugeoun obeune soneul deeotdago malhaetseumnida. — Seongjin told the doctor that he had burned his hand on a hot oven.

examples.text: 의사 선생님이 상처를 소독해 주고 붕대를 감아 주었습니다.
examples.translation: uisa seonsaengnimi sangcheoreul sodokae jugo bungdaereul gama jueotseumnida. — The doctor disinfected the wound and wrapped a bandage on it.

examples.text: 그리고 상처 부위를 만지지 말라고 하였습니다.
examples.translation: geurigo sangcheo buwireul manjiji mallago hayeotseumnida. — And the doctor told him not to touch the wound area.

examples.text: 이번 여름에 영수 씨 가족은 해수욕장으로 물놀이를 갔습니다.
examples.translation: ibeon yeoreume yeongsu ssi gajogeun haesuyokjangeuro mullorireul gatseumnida. — This summer Youngsu’s family went to the beach to play in the water.

examples.text: 수영을 잘 못하는 영수 씨가 물에 빠졌습니다.
examples.translation: suyeongeul jal motaneun yeongsu ssiga mure ppajeotseumnida. — Youngsu, who cannot swim well, fell into the water.

examples.text: 어떤 사람이 영수 씨를 구했고 일일구에 전화를 했습니다.
examples.translation: eotteon sarami yeongsu ssireul guhaetgo irilgue jeonhwareul haetseumnida. — Someone rescued Youngsu and called 119.

examples.text: 영수 씨는 숨을 쉬지 않았고 의식도 없었습니다.
examples.translation: yeongsu ssineun sumeul swiji anatgo uisikdo eopseotseumnida. — Youngsu was not breathing and was unconscious.

examples.text: 잠시 후에 일일구 구조대원이 왔습니다.
examples.translation: jamsi hue irilgu gujodaewoni watseumnida. — After a moment a 119 rescue worker came.

examples.text: 일일구 구조대원이 인공호흡을 했습니다.
examples.translation: irilgu gujodaewoni ingonghoheubeul haetseumnida. — The 119 rescue worker gave CPR.

examples.text: 그리고 영수 씨를 구급차에 싣고 병원으로 갔습니다.
examples.translation: geurigo yeongsu ssireul gugeupchae sitgo byeongwoneuro gatseumnida. — And they loaded Youngsu into an ambulance and went to the hospital.

explanations.title: Activity 3: the field-trip journal
explanations.body: The book gives a journal entry of an elementary school student about a field trip to a fire station and asks you to complete the paragraph with the words from the box (뜨거운, 차가운, 화상, 부위, 인공호흡, 구조대원; one word does not match). The book glosses 견학: a field trip; 응급처치: first aid. The completed entry (my answers: 구조대원, 뜨거운, 차가운, 부위, 인공호흡; 화상 is left over; the English is mine):

examples.text: 소방서 견학
examples.translation: sobangseo gyeonhak — A visit to the fire station

examples.text: 오늘 반 친구들과 함께 소방서에 견학을 갔다.
examples.translation: oneul ban chingudeulgwa hamkke sobangseoe gyeonhageul gatda. — Today I went on a visit to the fire station with my classmates.

examples.text: 일일구 구조대원 아저씨가 여러 가지 응급처치에 대한 설명을 해 주셨다.
examples.translation: irilgu gujodaewon ajeossiga yeoreo gaji eunggeupcheochie daehan seolmyeongeul hae jusyeotda. — The 119 rescue worker explained various first aid measures.

examples.text: 먼저 뜨거운 국물에 데었을 때는 빨리 차가운 물로 씻으라고 하셨다.
examples.translation: meonjeo tteugeoun gungmure deeosseul ttaeneun ppalli chagaun mullo ssiseurago hasyeotda. — First, he said that when you are scalded by hot soup you should quickly wash with cold water.

examples.text: 상처 부위는 만지면 안 된다고 하셨다.
examples.translation: sangcheo buwineun manjimyeon an doendago hasyeotda. — He said you must not touch the wound area.

examples.text: 그리고 곧바로 병원으로 가라고 하셨다.
examples.translation: geurigo gotbaro byeongwoneuro garago hasyeotda. — And he said to go to the hospital right away.

examples.text: 또 요즘 날씨가 더워서 수영장에서 물놀이 사고가 많이 생긴다고 하셨다.
examples.translation: tto yojeum nalssiga deowoseo suyeongjangeseo mullori sagoga mani saenggindago hasyeotda. — He also said that because the weather is hot these days, many water-play accidents happen at swimming pools.

examples.text: 물에 빠져서 의식이 없는 사람한테는 인공호흡을 해야 한다고 하셨다.
examples.translation: mure ppajeoseo uisigi eomneun saramhanteneun ingonghoheubeul haeya handago hasyeotda. — He said that for a person who fell into the water and is unconscious you must give CPR.

examples.text: 오늘 소방대원 아저씨한테서 많은 것을 배웠다.
examples.translation: oneul sobangdaewon ajeossihanteseo maneun geoseul baewotda. — Today I learned a lot from the firefighter.

explanations.title: Topic A: The child burned his hand (아이가 손을 데었어요)
explanations.body: In the emergency room, a doctor is talking to the mother of a two-year-old boy as he treats a burn on the boy’s hand. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 의사: 아이가 어떻게 화상을 입었습니까?
examples.translation: uisa: aiga eotteoke hwasangeul ibeotseumnikka? — How did the child get burned?

examples.text: 엄마: 뜨거운 국물에 손을 데었어요.
examples.translation: eomma: tteugeoun gungmure soneul deeosseoyo. — He scalded his hand in hot soup.

examples.text: 의사: 응급처치는 하셨습니까?
examples.translation: uisa: eunggeupcheochineun hasyeotseumnikka? — Did you give first aid?

examples.text: 엄마: 네. 상처부위를 차가운 물로 씻어 주었어요.
examples.translation: eomma: ne. sangcheobuwireul chagaun mullo ssiseo jueosseoyo. — Yes. I washed the wound area with cold water.

examples.text: 의사: 잘 하셨습니다. 그럼 상처 부위를 소독하고 약을 바르겠습니다. 그리고 아이가 상처를 만지면 안 되니까 붕대를 감겠습니다.
examples.translation: uisa: jal hasyeotseumnida. geureom sangcheo buwireul sodokago yageul bareugetseumnida. geurigo aiga sangcheoreul manjimyeon an doenikka bungdaereul gamgetseumnida. — Well done. Then I will disinfect the wound area and apply medicine. And since the child must not touch the wound, I will wrap a bandage on it.

examples.text: 엄마: 네. 감사합니다.
examples.translation: eomma: ne. gamsahamnida. — Yes. Thank you.

examples.text: 의사: 아이에게 뭐 다른 문제는 없어요?
examples.translation: uisa: aiege mwo dareun munjeneun eopseoyo? — Is there any other problem with the child?

examples.text: 엄마: 네, 요즘 우리 아이가 아무거나 입에 넣어서 걱정이에요.
examples.translation: eomma: ne, yojeum uri aiga amugeona ibe neoeoseo geokjeongieyo. — Yes, these days my child puts anything in his mouth, so I’m worried.

examples.text: 의사: 날카롭거나 작은 물건은 아이 근처에 두지 마세요. 목에 걸리면 아주 위험합니다.
examples.translation: uisa: nalkaropgeona jageun mulgeoneun ai geuncheoe duji maseyo. moge geollimyeon aju wiheomhamnida. — Don’t put sharp or small things near the child. It is very dangerous if they get stuck in his throat.

examples.text: 엄마: 혹시 아이가 무엇을 삼키면 어떻게 해야 하나요?
examples.translation: eomma: hoksi aiga mueoseul samkimyeon eotteoke haeya hanayo? — What should I do if the child swallows something?

examples.text: 의사: 그런 경우에는 삼킨 것이 나올 때까지 아이 등을 세게 두드려 주세요.
examples.translation: uisa: geureon gyeongueneun samkin geosi naol ttaekkaji ai deungeul sege dudeuryeo juseyo. — In such a case, pat the child’s back hard until what he swallowed comes out.

explanations.title: The book’s footnotes
explanations.body: 목, in this context, refers to 목구멍 (throat); this 걸리다 is translated as “to get something stuck (hooked on)” or “to choke”. 무엇 has dual meanings, “what” or “something”; here it is translated as “something” (this grammar feature will be introduced in Chapter 38). The grammar feature of 경우 is introduced in the Grammar in Focus section of this chapter.

lessons.title: 379. Ch 30 · Topic A Follow-up 1: first aid for burns, do’s and don’ts (읽기)
lessons.subtitle: 화상 응급처치 · 흐르는 찬물에 십 분 이상 · 얼음물은 사용하지 않는다 · 민간요법 · 감염의 위험

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a newspaper article on burn injuries
explanations.body: The book gives an excerpt from a newspaper article (chosun.com) and asks you to make a list of the do’s and don’ts for burn treatment; its hint: the article has unfamiliar words, so do not pay attention to every word but focus on the words you know. The book glosses 감염: infection; 민간요법: folk remedies; 제거하다: to remove. The text is the book’s with 10분 spelled out; the English is mine.

examples.text: 최근 집에서 직접 요리를 해 먹는 사람이 많다.
examples.translation: choegeun jibeseo jikjeop yorireul hae meongneun sarami manta. — Recently many people cook and eat at home themselves.

examples.text: 그런데 뜨거운 프라이팬, 냄비, 에어 프라이기 등을 사용하다 보면 화상을 입을 수 있어 주의해야 한다.
examples.translation: geureonde tteugeoun peuraipaen, naembi, eeo peuraigi deungeul sayonghada bomyeon hwasangeul ibeul su isseo juuihaeya handa. — But when using hot frying pans, pots, air fryers and the like, you can get burned, so you must be careful.

examples.text: 집에서 할 수 있는 올바른 화상 응급처치법을 알아본다.
examples.translation: jibeseo hal su inneun olbareun hwasang eunggeupcheochibeobeul arabonda. — Let us look at the correct first-aid method for burns that can be done at home.

examples.text: 화상을 입었다면 화상 부위를 흐르는 찬물에 십 분 이상 씻어내야 한다.
examples.translation: hwasangeul ibeotdamyeon hwasang buwireul heureuneun chanmure sip bun isang ssiseonaeya handa. — If you have been burned, you must rinse the burn area under running cold water for ten minutes or more.

examples.text: 이때 얼음물은 사용하지 않는다.
examples.translation: ittae eoreummureun sayonghaji anneunda. — At this time, do not use ice water.

examples.text: 화상 부위를 식힌 후 팔찌, 시계, 반지 등의 액세서리는 제거해야 한다.
examples.translation: hwasang buwireul sikin hu paljji, sigye, banji deungui aekseseorineun jegeohaeya handa. — After cooling the burn area, you must remove accessories such as bracelets, watches and rings.

examples.text: 옷 위로 뜨거운 물이나 국 등이 쏟아져 피부와 옷이 달라붙었다면 억지로 옷을 벗기려 하면 안 된다.
examples.translation: ot wiro tteugeoun murina guk deungi ssodajeo pibuwa osi dallabuteotdamyeon eokjiro oseul beotgiryeo hamyeon an doenda. — If hot water or soup was spilled on the clothes and the skin and clothes have stuck together, you must not try to take the clothes off by force.

examples.text: 먼저 찬물로 열을 식힌 후 옷을 제거하는 것이 좋다.
examples.translation: meonjeo chanmullo yeoreul sikin hu oseul jegeohaneun geosi jota. — It is good to cool the heat with cold water first and then remove the clothes.

examples.text: 통증이 가라앉으면 깨끗하고 마른 거즈로 화상 부위를 덮고 병원에 방문하는 것이 좋다.
examples.translation: tongjeungi garaanjeumyeon kkaekkeutago mareun geojeuro hwasang buwireul deopgo byeongwone bangmunhaneun geosi jota. — When the pain subsides, it is good to cover the burn area with clean, dry gauze and visit a hospital.

examples.text: 화상 부위에 민간요법으로 간장, 된장, 알로에, 소주 등을 바르는 것은 감염의 위험이 있기 때문에 절대 하면 안 된다.
examples.translation: hwasang buwie minganyobeobeuro ganjang, doenjang, alloe, soju deungeul bareuneun geoseun gamyeomui wiheomi itgi ttaemune jeoldae hamyeon an doenda. — Applying soy sauce, soybean paste, aloe, soju and the like to the burn area as a folk remedy must never be done, because there is a risk of infection.

explanations.title: The do’s and don’ts (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the table blank; these are my answers.

rows: Rinse the burn area under running cold water for ten minutes or more
After cooling, remove accessories such as bracelets, watches and rings
Don’t pull off clothes stuck to the skin by force; cool them with cold water first
When the pain subsides, cover with clean, dry gauze and go to the hospital
Don’t apply soy sauce, soybean paste, aloe or soju (risk of infection)

lessons.title: 381. Ch 30 · Grammar A: the conjunctive ending 경우(에), in case; if; when
lessons.subtitle: 경우 · -는 경우에 · -(으)ㄴ 경우에 · -(으)ㄹ 경우에 · 열이 날 경우에 · 사고가 난 경우에

explanations.title: The conjunctive ending 경우(에)
explanations.body: Recall the conjunctive ending –(으)면 (if; when) that we use to express a conditional, as in 차가 고장이 나면 버스로 출근합니다 (If my car breaks down, I go to work by bus). The conjunctive ending 경우(에) preceded by an attributive form is also used to express a conditional. 경우 in 경우(에) is a noun meaning a situation, case, or instance; thus the literal translation of the conjunctive ending is “in case” or “in a situation when”. Depending on the context, it can be translated as “in case”, “if”, or “when”. (119 is spelled out in Hangul; the English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 차가 고장이 나면 버스로 출근합니다.
examples.translation: chaga gojangi namyeon beoseuro chulgeunhamnida. — If my car breaks down, I go to work by bus.

examples.text: 차가 고장이 나는 경우에 버스로 출근합니다.

explanations.title: Any of the attributive forms can come before 경우(에)
explanations.body: Note that 경우(에) can be preceded by any of the attributive forms: the present –는, the past –(으)ㄴ and the future –(으)ㄹ.

examples.text: 한국에서는 사고가 나는 경우에 일일구에 전화합니다.
examples.translation: hangugeseoneun sagoga naneun gyeongue irilgue jeonhwahamnida. — In Korea, if an accident occurs, we call 119.

examples.text: 사고가 날 경우에 일일구에 전화하세요.
examples.translation: sagoga nal gyeongue irilgue jeonhwahaseyo. — If an accident occurs (in the future), call 119.

examples.text: 사고가 난 경우에 일일구에 전화하세요.
examples.translation: sagoga nan gyeongue irilgue jeonhwahaseyo. — If an accident has occurred, call 119.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Verb stem + attributive form + 경우에 (a stem ending in ㄹ drops the ㄹ before –는 and –(으)ㄴ: 살다 → 사는 경우에, 산 경우에).

lessons.title: 382. Ch 30 · Grammar B: the auxiliary verbs –아/어 두다 and –아/어 놓다
lessons.subtitle: -아/어 두다 · -아/어 놓다 · 열어 놓으세요 · 써 두세요 · 사 두었어요 · 켜 놓으세요

explanations.title: The auxiliary verbs –아/어 두다 and –아/어 놓다
explanations.body: The auxiliary verbs –아/어 두다 and –아/어 놓다, which are attached to the stem of an action verb, are from the verbs 두다 and 놓다. 두다 translates as “to put”, “to place”, “to store” or “to keep”, as in:

examples.text: 열쇠를 주머니에 두세요.
examples.translation: yeolsoereul jumeonie duseyo. — Please keep the key in your pocket.

explanations.title: 놓다
explanations.body: 놓다 translates as “to put”, “to place” or “to leave”, as in:

examples.text: 책을 책상 위에 놓으세요.
examples.translation: chaegeul chaeksang wie noeuseyo. — Please put the book on the desk.

explanations.title: Meanings of –아/어 두다 and –아/어 놓다
explanations.body: These auxiliary verbs are used to imply one of the following. 1. To do something and keep or leave it that way:

examples.text: 창문을 열어 놓으세요.
examples.translation: changmuneul yeoreo noeuseyo. — Please open the window (and keep it open).

examples.text: 옷을 체육관에 벗어 두었어요.
examples.translation: oseul cheyukgwane beoseo dueosseoyo. — I took off my clothes at the gym (and kept them there).

explanations.title: 2. To do something for future use, or once and for all
explanations.body: To do something for future use, or to do something once and for all (so that it won’t have to be repeated):

examples.text: 어려운 말은 공책에 써 두세요.
examples.translation: eoryeoun mareun gongchaege sseo duseyo. — Please write down difficult words in your notebook (for future use).

examples.text: 공책이 세일이어서 많이 사 두었어요.
examples.translation: gongchaegi seirieoseo mani sa dueosseoyo. — Notebooks were on sale and I bought a lot of them (for future use).

examples.text: 지금 숙제를 해 두세요.
examples.translation: jigeum sukjereul hae duseyo. — Please do your homework now (so that you won’t have to do it later).

examples.text: 고양이를 위해 문을 열어 놓았어요.
examples.translation: goyangireul wihae muneul yeoreo noasseoyo. — I opened the door (and have kept it open) for the cat.

examples.text: 컴퓨터를 켜 놓으세요.
examples.translation: keompyuteoreul kyeo noeuseyo. — Please turn on your computer (and keep it on).

explanations.title: The rule
explanations.body: Add 아 or 어 to the verb stem, then 두다 / 놓다. When the last syllable of the stem contains the vowels ㅏ or ㅗ, add 아 (자다 → 자 두다; 보다 → 봐 놓다). When the last syllable contains a vowel other than ㅏ or ㅗ, add 어 (만들다 → 만들어 두다; 벗다 → 벗어 놓다).

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Speaking and reading): complete the sentences
explanations.body: The book gives two lists and asks partners to connect a phrase from List A with a logically fitting phrase from List B, using –아/어 두다 or –아/어 놓다 (answers may vary; the book’s model: 결혼하기 위해서 집을 사 두었습니다 / 놓았습니다). My matches (the English is mine):

rows: In order to get married, I bought a house (in advance).
In order to go see a movie, I did my homework (in advance).
In order to get up early, I went to bed early (in advance).
In order to go to college, I saved money (in advance).
In order to invite friends, I prepared food (in advance).
In order to travel at the end of the year, I bought a plane ticket (in advance).

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking and listening): preparing to visit your family
explanations.body: The book asks you to think of at least five things to do before going home, share them with a partner, and present your partner’s preparations using –아/어 두다/놓다. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 김 일병은 고향에 가기 위해 미리 숙제를 다 해 둘 거예요.
examples.translation: gim ilbyeongeun gohyange gagi wihae miri sukjereul da hae dul geoyeyo. — Private First Class Kim will do all his homework in advance in order to go to his hometown.

examples.text: 그리고 동생 선물로 닌텐도를 사 놓을 거예요.
examples.translation: geurigo dongsaeng seonmullo nintendoreul sa noeul geoyeyo. — And he will buy a Nintendo in advance as a present for his younger sibling.

explanations.title: Topic C: How is the patient? (환자 상태는 어떻습니까?)
explanations.body: A woman is talking to a rescuer about her son who was pulled from a creek. (The English is mine; the book gives none; 5분 is spelled out, and the book’s stray space in “미끄러지 는 바람에” is closed.)

examples.text: 보호자: 이쪽이에요. 빨리 오세요.
examples.translation: bohoja: ijjogieyo. ppalli oseyo. — It’s over here. Please come quickly.

examples.text: 구조대원: 환자 상태를 좀 봅시다. 인공호흡은 했습니까?
examples.translation: gujodaewon: hwanja sangtaereul jom bopsida. ingonghoheubeun haetseumnikka? — Let’s take a look at the patient’s condition. Did you give CPR?

examples.text: 보호자: 네. 애 아빠가 오 분 전에 했어요. 그런데 아직도 안 깨어나고 있어요.
examples.translation: bohoja: ne. ae appaga o bun jeone haesseoyo. geureonde ajikdo an kkaeeonago isseoyo. — Yes. His father did it five minutes ago. But he still isn’t waking up.

examples.text: 구조대원: 맥박과 호흡을 확인해 보겠습니다. 상태가 심각하지는 않습니다.
examples.translation: gujodaewon: maekbakgwa hoheubeul hwaginhae bogetseumnida. sangtaega simgakajineun anseumnida. — I will check his pulse and breathing. His condition is not serious.

examples.text: 보호자: 정말 다행이네요.
examples.translation: bohoja: jeongmal dahaengineyo. — That’s a relief.

examples.text: 구조대원: 우선 환자의 체온을 유지해야 합니다. 먼저 젖은 옷을 벗기고 담요를 덮어 주겠습니다.
examples.translation: gujodaewon: useon hwanjaui cheoneul yujihaeya hamnida. meonjeo jeojeun oseul beotgigo damyoreul deopeo jugetseumnida. — First we have to maintain the patient’s body temperature. First I will take off his wet clothes and cover him with a blanket.

examples.text: 보호자: 네. 그리고 다리에서 피가 나서 지혈했어요.
examples.translation: bohoja: ne. geurigo darieseo piga naseo jihyeolhaesseoyo. — Yes. And his leg was bleeding so I stopped the bleeding.

examples.text: 구조대원: 잘하셨습니다. 상처가 깊지는 않네요. 그런데 어떻게 하다가 물에 빠졌습니까?
examples.translation: gujodaewon: jalhasyeotseumnida. sangcheoga gipjineun anneyo. geureonde eotteoke hadaga mure ppajeotseumnikka? — Well done. The wound isn’t deep. By the way, how did he fall into the water?

examples.text: 보호자: 바위에서 놀다가 갑자기 미끄러지는 바람에 물에 빠졌어요.
examples.translation: bohoja: bawieseo noldaga gapjagi mikkeureojineun barame mure ppajeosseoyo. — He was playing on a rock and suddenly slipped, so he fell into the water.

examples.text: 구조대원: 큰일 날 뻔 했군요! 자, 이제 환자를 구급차에 싣겠습니다.
examples.translation: gujodaewon: keunil nal ppeon haetgunyo! ja, ije hwanjareul gugeupchae sitgetseumnida. — That could have been a disaster! Now, we will load the patient into the ambulance.

lessons.title: 384. Ch 30 · First-aid steps: the Emergency Medical Information Center’s list and a Q&A on torn skin
lessons.subtitle: 응급조치 방법 · 안전한 장소로 환자를 옮기세요 · 맥박과 호흡을 확인하세요 · 찢어진 부위를 씻어 주세요

explanations.title: Topic C Follow-up 1 (Reading): the steps for an emergency
explanations.body: The book gives the Emergency Medical Information Center’s suggested steps (응급조치 방법) and asks you to translate the five steps into English. The steps are the book’s with 119 spelled out; the English is mine.

examples.text: 먼저 안전한 장소로 환자를 옮기세요.
examples.translation: meonjeo anjeonhan jangsoro hwanjareul omgiseyo. — First, move the patient to a safe place.

examples.text: 환자의 맥박과 호흡을 확인하세요.
examples.translation: hwanjaui maekbakgwa hoheubeul hwaginhaseyo. — Check the patient’s pulse and breathing.

examples.text: 필요하면 일일구로 전화를 걸어서 도움을 받으세요.
examples.translation: piryohamyeon irilguro jeonhwareul georeoseo doumeul badeuseyo. — If necessary, call 119 and get help.

examples.text: 환자를 병원으로 옮겨야 할 경우 구급차를 이용하세요.
examples.translation: hwanjareul byeongwoneuro omgyeoya hal gyeongu gugeupchareul iyonghaseyo. — If you need to take the patient to the hospital, use an ambulance.

examples.text: 구급차가 오면 보호자가 같이 타서 구조대원에게 필요한 정보를 알려주세요.
examples.translation: gugeupchaga omyeon bohojaga gachi taseo gujodaewonege piryohan jeongboreul allyeojuseyo. — When the ambulance comes, the guardian should ride along and give the rescue workers the necessary information.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading): a health-care professional’s advice on first aid
explanations.body: The book gives a Q&A and asks you to read it and write the first-aid measures in order in English. The question is a parent’s (the English is mine):

examples.text: 저희 아이가 밖에서 놀다가 자주 다칩니다.
examples.translation: jeohui aiga bakkeseo noldaga jaju dachimnida. — My child often gets hurt while playing outside.

examples.text: 피부가 찢어진 경우에는 어떤 응급조치를 해야 하나요?
examples.translation: pibuga jjijeojin gyeongueneun eotteon eunggeupjochireul haeya hanayo? — What first aid should I give when the skin is torn?

examples.text: 아이들은 공에 맞아 이마나 피부가 찢어지는 경우가 많습니다.
examples.translation: aideureun gonge maja imana pibuga jjijeojineun gyeonguga manseumnida. — Children are often hit by a ball and tear their forehead or skin.

examples.text: 그런 경우에는 먼저 찢어진 부위를 깨끗한 물로 씻어 주세요.
examples.translation: geureon gyeongueneun meonjeo jjijeojin buwireul kkaekkeutan mullo ssiseo juseyo. — In such a case, first wash the torn area with clean water.

examples.text: 그리고 상처 부위를 소독해 주세요.
examples.translation: geurigo sangcheo buwireul sodokae juseyo. — And disinfect the wound area.

examples.text: 그 다음에는 깨끗한 수건으로 상처 부위를 눌러서 출혈을 막아 주세요.
examples.translation: geu daeumeneun kkaekkeutan sugeoneuro sangcheo buwireul nulleoseo chulhyeoreul maga juseyo. — Next, press the wound area with a clean towel and stop the bleeding.

examples.text: 마지막으로 상처에 바르는 연고를 발라 주세요.
examples.translation: majimageuro sangcheoe bareuneun yeongoreul balla juseyo. — Finally, apply an ointment for wounds.

explanations.title: The first-aid steps in order (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the lines blank; these are my answers.

rows: Wash the torn area with clean water
Press the wound area with a clean towel to stop the bleeding

lessons.subtitle: 먹이다 · 입히다 · 눕히다 · 앉히다 · 늘리다 · 살리다 · 맡기다 · 벗기다 · 깨우다 · 달구다 · 낮추다

explanations.title: Causative infixes: 이, 히, 리, 기, 우, 구, 추
explanations.body: Look at the following two pairs of native Korean verbs and their meanings: 먹다 (to eat) → 먹이다 (to cause [someone] to eat; to feed); 입다 (to wear; to put on) → 입히다 (to cause [someone] to wear/put on [something]). The verbs on the right carry the 이 or 히 infix and translate as “to cause (someone) to do something”. As shown above, adding an extra syllable like 이, 히, 리, or 기 to the verbs in the first column changes the native Korean verbs into causatives. For this reason the syllables 이, 히, 리 and 기 are called “causative infixes”. Some of the less common causative infixes are 우, 구, and 추. However, there is no rule for predicting which infix goes with which verb; the infix/verb combination is somewhat arbitrary. The following table shows a list of common causative verbs.

lessons.title: 386. Ch 30 · Grammar D: the conjunctive ending –는 바람에, an unexpected cause
lessons.subtitle: -는 바람에 · 차가 고장 나는 바람에 늦었어요 · 문에 머리를 부딪치는 바람에 · 몸살이 나는 바람에

explanations.title: The conjunctive ending –는 바람에
explanations.body: –는 바람에 is a conjunctive ending used to express cause or reason. Its meaning is similar to the conjunctive endings you learned in earlier chapters: –아/어서, –기 때문에, and –(으)니까. However, –는 바람에 is mainly used for an uncontrollable or unexpected cause. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 차가 고장 나는 바람에 늦었어요.
examples.translation: chaga gojang naneun barame neujeosseoyo. — I was late because my car broke down.

examples.text: 비가 오는 바람에 산책을 못 했어요.
examples.translation: biga oneun barame sanchaegeul mot haesseoyo. — I couldn’t go for a walk because it was raining.

explanations.title: The rule: action verb stem + 는 바람에
explanations.body: More examples:

examples.text: 앞에 달리던 선수가 넘어지는 바람에 제가 우승했어요.
examples.translation: ape dallideon seonsuga neomeojineun barame jega useunghaesseoyo. — I won the race because the runner in front of me fell.

examples.text: 어제 바람이 많이 부는 바람에 나무가 넘어졌어요.
examples.translation: eoje barami mani buneun barame namuga neomeojeosseoyo. — Because it was very windy yesterday, the tree fell.

examples.text: 문에 머리를 부딪치는 바람에 머리를 다쳤어요.
examples.translation: mune meorireul buditchineun barame meorireul dacheosseoyo. — I hurt my head because I bumped into a door.

examples.text: 갑자기 손님이 오는 바람에 약속시간에 늦었어요.
examples.translation: gapjagi sonnimi oneun barame yaksoksigane neujeosseoyo. — I was late for the appointment because a guest came suddenly.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Action verb stem + 는 바람에 (a stem ending in ㄹ drops the ㄹ).

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Speaking): the chain model
explanations.body: The book’s circle game: the teacher says a sentence about a negative event and each student repeats the main clause with –는 바람에 and adds a different negative consequence. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 선생님: 교통사고가 났어요.
examples.translation: seonsaengnim: gyotongsagoga nasseoyo. — There was a traffic accident.

examples.text: 학생 일: 교통사고가 나는 바람에 길이 막혔어요.
examples.translation: haksaeng il: gyotongsagoga naneun barame giri makyeosseoyo. — Because there was a traffic accident, the road was blocked.

examples.text: 학생 이: 길이 막히는 바람에 약속시간에 늦게 갔어요.
examples.translation: haksaeng i: giri makineun barame yaksoksigane neutge gasseoyo. — Because the road was blocked, I went late to the appointment.

explanations.title: Follow-up 6 (Speaking): 몸살이 나는 바람에 시험공부를 못 했어요
explanations.body: The book asks you to think of three things you were supposed to do but did not, and what caused you not to do them, then to exchange the information with three classmates, using courtesy expressions and –는 바람에. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 안녕하세요, 고 일병, 요즘 어떻게 지내요?
examples.translation: ga: annyeonghaseyo, go ilbyeong, yojeum eotteoke jinaeyo? — Hello, Private First Class Ko, how have you been lately?

examples.text: 나: 잘 지내고 있어요. 박 일병은요?
examples.translation: na: jal jinaego isseoyo. bak ilbyeongeunyo? — I’m doing well. And you, Private First Class Park?

examples.text: 가: 나도 잘 지내요. 근데 지난주에 시험공부를 못 했어요.
examples.translation: ga: nado jal jinaeyo. geunde jinanjue siheomgongbureul mot haesseoyo. — I’m doing well, too. But last week I couldn’t study for the test.

examples.text: 나: 왜요?
examples.translation: na: waeyo? — Why?

examples.text: 가: 몸살이 나는 바람에 시험공부를 못 했어요.
examples.translation: ga: momsari naneun barame siheomgongbureul mot haesseoyo. — Because I came down with a body ache, I couldn’t study for the test.
