lessons.title: 387. Ch 30 · Activity 2: two NCOs who saved a woman (읽기)
lessons.subtitle: 육군 부사관 · 은행 앞에 쓰러진 여성 · 심폐소생술 · 구조요청 · 응급조치 · 시민을 구할 수 있었다

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): a newspaper article about two NCOs who helped a woman
explanations.body: The book gives a newspaper article (YNA) about two NCOs who helped a woman in a medical emergency, and asks you to read it and fill in a table in English (details about the two NCOs; how they found the patient; the patient’s medical condition; first aid treatment); its hint: the article has unfamiliar words, so focus on the words you know. The book glosses 심폐소생술을 시행하다: to perform CPR. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out in Hangul (the ages in parentheses are written as “스물일곱 살”, “스물네 살”; 8군단 → 팔 군단; 40대 → 사십 대; 119 → 일일구) and the quotation set off as separate lines; the English is mine.

examples.text: 육군 팔 군단에 따르면 특공대대 스물일곱 살 이지원 중사와 스물네 살 이승주 하사는 한 은행 앞에 의식을 잃고 쓰러져 있던 사십 대 중반의 여성을 구조했다.
examples.translation: yukgun pal gundane ttareumyeon teukgongdaedae seumullilgop sal ijiwon jungsawa seumulle sal iseungju hasaneun han eunhaeng ape uisigeul ilko sseureojeo itdeon sasip dae jungbanui yeoseongeul gujohaetda. — According to the Army’s 8th Corps, Sergeant First Class Lee Jiwon (27) and Staff Sergeant Lee Seungju (24) of a special forces battalion rescued a woman in her mid-forties who had collapsed unconscious in front of a bank.

examples.text: 이들은 퇴근 후 시내에 일을 보러 나왔다가 한 중년 남자로부터 은행 앞에 여성이 쓰러져 있다는 이야기를 듣고 곧바로 현장으로 달려갔다.
examples.translation: ideureun toegeun hu sinaee ireul boreo nawatdaga han jungnyeon namjarobuteo eunhaeng ape yeoseongi sseureojeo itdaneun iyagireul deutgo gotbaro hyeonjangeuro dallyeogatda. — After work, they had come downtown on an errand and, hearing from a middle-aged man that a woman was lying collapsed in front of the bank, ran straight to the scene.

examples.text: 부사관들이 도착한 곳에는 한 여성이 호흡이 없는 상태에서 쓰러져 있었고 머리에는 출혈이 보였다.
examples.translation: busagwandeuri dochakan goseneun han yeoseongi hoheubi eomneun sangtaeeseo sseureojeo isseotgo meorieneun chulhyeori boyeotda. — Where the NCOs arrived, a woman was lying collapsed, not breathing, and bleeding was visible on her head.

examples.text: 이들은 즉시 일일구에 구조요청을 하고 곧바로 심폐소생술을 시행했다.
examples.translation: ideureun jeuksi irilgue gujoyocheongeul hago gotbaro simpyesosaengsureul sihaenghaetda. — They immediately requested rescue from 119 and right away performed CPR.

examples.text: 이들은 호흡이 돌아온 여성이 의식을 잃지 않도록 대화를 계속했다.
examples.translation: ideureun hoheubi doraon yeoseongi uisigeul ilchi antorok daehwareul gyesokaetda. — They kept talking so that the woman, whose breathing had returned, would not lose consciousness.

examples.text: 그리고 팔다리를 주무르는 등 응급조치도 했다.
examples.translation: geurigo paldarireul jumureuneun deung eunggeupjochido haetda. — And they also gave first aid, such as massaging her arms and legs.

examples.text: 이 여성은 현장에 도착한 일일구 구조대에 의해 병원으로 옮겨진 뒤 치료를 받고 퇴원한 것으로 알려졌다.
examples.translation: i yeoseongeun hyeonjange dochakan irilgu gujodaee uihae byeongwoneuro omgyeojin dwi chiryoreul batgo toewonhan geoseuro allyeojeotda. — This woman is known to have been taken to a hospital by the 119 rescue team that arrived at the scene, received treatment and been discharged.

examples.text: 이지원 중사는 이렇게 말했다.
examples.translation: ijiwon jungsaneun ireoke malhaetda. — Sergeant First Class Lee Jiwon said the following.

examples.text: 평소 부대에서 구급법, 응급처치 훈련을 많이 한 결과 시민을 구할 수 있었다.
examples.translation: pyeongso budaeeseo gugeupbeop, eunggeupcheochi hullyeoneul mani han gyeolgwa simineul guhal su isseotda. — As a result of doing a lot of first-aid and emergency treatment training at my unit on ordinary days, I was able to save a citizen.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: talk about accidents and physical conditions in a medical emergency situation; state reasons for an accident; ask for help in a medical emergency situation; and give instructions for first aid in a medical emergency situation.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; an attributive form + 경우(에); the auxiliary verb –아/어 두다 or –아/어 놓다; the causative infixes 이, 히, 리, 기, 우, 구, and 추; the conjunctive ending –는 바람에; and the Sino-Korean syllables 화상 (火傷) and 교사 (敎師).

explanations.title: What Chapter 31 teaches (현대인의 질병과 예방)
explanations.body:
Chapter 31, “Modern Diseases and Prevention”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and discuss common chronic diseases and conditions and physical symptoms in industrialized Korea; state the causes of common chronic diseases and conditions in industrialized Korea; and discuss disease prevention.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the attributive form of a verb, –았(었)던 or –었(었)던, used to express a past event or state; expansion of a relative clause; the conjunctive ending –(으)니까 or –아/어 보니까, which leads to the discovery of a fact; the auxiliary verb –아/어 보이다 (to appear to be; to seem to be; to look); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 불면증 (不眠症), 과체중 (過體重), and 식중독 (食中毒).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 불면증 (不眠症)
explanations.body:
This Sino-Korean word means insomnia or sleeplessness. The first syllable 불/부 (不) is like the English prefix in-, im-, il-, or ir- and means “no” or “not”, as in 불친절 (unkindness; “no kindness”), 불균형 (unbalance; imbalance; “no balance”), and 부도덕 (immorality). The second syllable 면 (眠) means sleeping or resting, as in 최면 (hypnosis; “pressing sleep”), 동면 (hibernation; “winter sleep”), and 수면 (a sleep; a slumber). The last syllable 증 (症), which you learned about earlier, means syndrome or symptom, as in 증상 (a symptom) and 우울증 (the blues; depression). Thus the literal meaning of 불면증 is “no sleeping symptom”.

The book asks you to guess the meaning of 불규칙, 불법주차, 수면제 and 동면하다 (my answers: irregular; illegal parking; a sleeping pill; to hibernate).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 과체중 (過體重)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means overweight. The first syllable 과 (過) means excessive or over, as in 과속 (speeding; “excessive speed”), 과식 (overeating; “excessive eating”), and 과음 (overdrinking; “excessive drinking”). The second syllable 체 (體) means body, as in 상체 (the upper part of the body), 하체 (the lower part of the body), 체력 (physical strength), and 체육 (physical education; “body upbringing”). The last syllable 중 (重) means heaviness or weight, as in 체중 (body weight), 중력 (gravity; “heaviness power”), 중상 (a serious injury; “heavy injury”), and 중병 (a serious illness; “heavy illness”). Thus the literal meaning of 과체중 is “excessive body weight”, and it means overweight (because of excessive body fat).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 식중독 (食中毒)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means food poisoning. The first syllable 식 (食) means food or eating, as in 한식 (Korean food), 과식 (overeating; “excessive eating”), and 식품점 (a grocery store; “food item store”). The second syllable 중 (中) means center or middle, as in 중학교 (a middle school), 중국 (China; “central country”), 중심 (the center; the heart; the focus; “middle heart”), and 공사중 (under construction; “middle of construction”). The last syllable 독 (毒) means poison, as in 독가스 (poison gas), 독감 (influenza; “poisonous cold”), 독약 (a poisonous drug; poison; “poison medicine”), 방독면 (a gas mask; “poison preventing face”), 소독 (disinfection; sterilization; fumigation; “extinguishing poison”), and 독주 (strong liquor; “poisoned liquor”). Thus the word 식중독 literally means “(in the) middle (of) poison (caused by) food”. Keep in mind that 중독 itself is a word that means poisoning or addiction, as in 알코올중독 and 마약중독.

explanations.title: Topic B: What causes obesity? (비만의 원인은 무엇입니까?)
explanations.body: Mr. Kim, a television talk show host, discusses Korea’s obesity problem with Professor Lim. (The English is mine; the book gives none; 10년 is spelled out.)

examples.text: 사회자: 임 교수님, 요즘 한국에도 비만 인구가 점점 증가하고 있지요?
examples.translation: sahoeja: im gyosunim, yojeum hangugedo biman inguga jeomjeom jeunggahago itjiyo? — Professor Lim, the obese population in Korea is increasing gradually these days too, isn’t it?

examples.text: 임 교수: 네, 맞습니다. 십 년 전에 정상이었던 한국인의 체중이 이제는 과체중이 되었습니다.
examples.translation: im gyosu: ne, matseumnida. sip nyeon jeone jeongsangieotdeon hanguginui chejungi ijeneun gwachejungi doeeotseumnida. — Yes, that’s right. The weight of Koreans, which was normal ten years ago, has now become overweight.

examples.text: 사회자: 네. 그럼 비만의 가장 큰 원인은 무엇입니까?
examples.translation: sahoeja: ne. geureom bimanui gajang keun wonineun mueosimnikka? — I see. Then what is the biggest cause of obesity?

examples.text: 임 교수: 물론 유전적인 원인도 있습니다. 하지만 식생활이나 생활습관 등 환경적인 원인이 더 큽니다.
examples.translation: im gyosu: mullon yujeonjeogin wonindo itseumnida. hajiman siksaenghwarina saenghwalseupgwan deung hwangyeongjeogin wonini deo keumnida. — Of course there are also hereditary causes. But environmental causes such as diet and lifestyle habits are bigger.

examples.text: 사회자: 그렇군요. 현대인들은 스트레스 때문에 과식이나 과음을 많이 하는데요. 과식이나 과음도 비만의 원인이 될 수 있습니까?
examples.translation: sahoeja: geureokunyo. hyeondaeindeureun seuteureseu ttaemune gwasigina gwaeumeul mani haneundeyo. gwasigina gwaeumdo bimanui wonini doel su itseumnikka? — I see. Modern people overeat and overdrink a lot because of stress. Can overeating and overdrinking also be causes of obesity?

examples.text: 임 교수: 물론이죠. 특히 스트레스는 비만뿐만 아니라 모든 질병의 원인이지요. 그리고 비만은 암이나 심장병 같은 성인병의 원인도 됩니다.
examples.translation: im gyosu: mullonijo. teuki seuteureseuneun bimanppunman anira modeun jilbyeongui woninijiyo. geurigo bimaneun amina simjangbyeong gateun seonginbyeongui wonindo doemnida. — Of course. Stress in particular is the cause not only of obesity but of all diseases. And obesity is also a cause of adult diseases such as cancer and heart disease.

examples.text: 사회자: 그럼, 비만을 예방하려면 어떻게 해야 할까요?
examples.translation: sahoeja: geureom, bimaneul yebangharyeomyeon eotteoke haeya halkkayo? — Then what should we do to prevent obesity?

examples.text: 임 교수: 무엇보다 규칙적인 운동과 건강한 식습관이 필요합니다.
examples.translation: im gyosu: mueotboda gyuchikjeogin undonggwa geonganghan sikseupgwani piryohamnida. — Above all, regular exercise and healthy eating habits are necessary.

explanations.title: Core words and phrases of Topic B
explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter); 과식(하다), 과음(하다), 규칙(적), 예방(하다), 유전(되다) and 증가(하다) take the forms in parentheses; –(았/었)던 is explained in the grammar.

rows: (種類) a kind; a sort; a class; a species; a variety; a type
a disease; a sickness; a malady; a disorder

explanations.title: What the dialog says (mine)
explanations.body: The book asks you to fill in three bulleted items in English; these are my answers.

rows: The obese population is gradually increasing; the weight of Koreans, which was normal ten years ago, has become overweight
Heredity; environmental causes such as diet and lifestyle habits; overeating and overdrinking from stress
Regular exercise and healthy eating habits

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): guidelines to prevent obesity
explanations.body: The book gives five guidelines (비만 예방법) and asks you to translate them into English; the first is done for you (“Eat regularly.”). The text is the book’s with 8잔 spelled out; the English is mine except the first.

examples.text: 식사를 규칙적으로 한다.

lessons.title: 394. Ch 31 · Grammar A: the attributive form –았(었)던, a past action or condition
lessons.subtitle: -았던 · -었던 · 먹었던 · 비쌌던 · 더러웠던 · 살았었던 · 여행했던

explanations.title: The attributive form –았(었)던 / –었(었)던
explanations.body: Recall that the attributive form –(으)ㄴ indicates a present or timeless condition when it is attached to a stative verb, and the same attributive form indicates a past action when it is attached to an action verb. However, the attributive form –았(었)던/었(었)던, which can be attached to a stative verb or an action verb, indicates a past condition or action. (The book writes 비쌌(었)던 and 봤(었)던 with the optional 었 in parentheses; they are written here as 비쌌던 and 봤던.)

explanations.title: Attributive form for a past action or condition
explanations.body: Verb stem + 았(었)던 or 었(었)던. The book’s examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 이 건물에서 배웠던 외국어는 한국어입니다.
examples.translation: i geonmureseo baewotdeon oegugeoneun hangugeoimnida. — The foreign language (that) I used to learn in this building (but I no longer do) is Korean.

examples.text: 벨라스 홀은 내가 매일 점심을 먹었던 식당입니다.
examples.translation: bellaseu horeun naega maeil jeomsimeul meogeotdeon sikdangimnida. — Bellas Hall is a restaurant where I used to have lunch every day (but I no longer do).

examples.translation: yeogiga naega chaegeul billyeosseotdeon doseogwanimnida. — This is the library where I used to borrow books (but I no longer do).

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: The past stem + 던 (the double 었 in 았었던/었었던 is optional and stresses that the situation no longer holds).

lessons.title: 395. Ch 31 · Grammar B: expanding a relative clause
lessons.subtitle: 관계절 · 어제 내가 본 영화 · 한국말을 공부하는 학생 · 동사는 끝에 · 순서는 자유롭게

explanations.title: Relative clauses in Korean
explanations.body: A relative clause is a subordinate clause that modifies a noun or noun phrase (e.g., “who learn Korean at DLI” in “students who learn Korean at DLI”). The book’s two sentences contain relative clauses (어제 내가 본 and 한국말을 공부하는 are the relative clauses; 영화 and 학생 are the nouns they modify; the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 어제 내가 본 영화는 재미있었어요.
examples.translation: eoje naega bon yeonghwaneun jaemiisseosseoyo. — The movie (that) I saw yesterday was fun.

examples.text: 저는 한국말을 공부하는 학생입니다.
examples.translation: jeoneun hangungmareul gongbuhaneun haksaengimnida. — I am a student who is learning Korean.

explanations.title: Three features of the Korean relative clause
explanations.body: First, in Korean, a relative clause comes before the noun it modifies: 어제 내가 본 and 한국말을 공부하는 come before their modified nouns 영화 and 학생. Second, the verb in a relative clause has to be in the attributive form (e.g., 본 and 공부하는). Third, the verb in a relative clause is located at the end of the clause. Thus, when words or phrases are added to a Korean sentence to expand the relative clause, they are added before the verb in an attributive form:

examples.text: 친구랑 같이 어제 내가 본 영화는 재미있었어요.
examples.translation: chingurang gachi eoje naega bon yeonghwaneun jaemiisseosseoyo. — The movie (that) I watched with my friend yesterday was fun.

examples.text: 델몬티 극장에서 친구랑 같이 어제 내가 본 영화는 재미있었어요.
examples.translation: delmonti geukjangeseo chingurang gachi eoje naega bon yeonghwaneun jaemiisseosseoyo. — The movie (that) I saw with my friend at the Del Monte Theater yesterday was fun.

explanations.title: Word order is flexible, except for the verb
explanations.body: Because the word order is flexible, except for the verb, we can keep adding words in front of the verb in no particular order. Thus all of the following sentences mean the same thing: “The movie (that) I watched with my friend yesterday was fun.”

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 황사현상 (the yellow dust phenomenon)
explanations.body: 황사 (yellow sand), known as Asian dust, yellow dust, yellow sand, or yellow wind, is a seasonal meteorological phenomenon affecting much of eastern Asia during spring months. The dust originates in the deserts of Mongolia, northern China, and Kazakhstan, where high-speed surface winds and intense dust storms kick up dense clouds of fine, dry soil particles. These clouds are carried eastward by winds that pass over China, North and South Korea, and Japan, as well as parts of eastern Russia. The dust significantly decreases visibility and also causes a variety of health problems, including sore throats and asthma in otherwise healthy people. Often, people are advised to avoid or minimize outdoor activities, depending on the severity of the dust storms. (Quoted by the book from “Asian Dust,” Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia.)

lessons.title: 397. Ch 31 · Grammar C: –아/어 보이다, to look; to appear to be
lessons.subtitle: -아/어 보이다 · 맛있어 보입니다 · 젊어 보입니다 · 피곤해 보입니다 · 우울해 보여요

explanations.title: –아/어 보이다
explanations.body: When the auxiliary verb –아/어 보이다 is attached to the stem of a stative verb, it means “to appear to be”, “to seem to be”, or “to look”. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 이 김치가 맛있어 보입니다.
examples.translation: i gimchiga masisseo boimnida. — This kimchi appears to be tasty.

examples.text: 정 선생님은 나이에 비해서 젊어 보입니다.
examples.translation: jeong seonsaengnimeun naie bihaeseo jeolmeo boimnida. — Ms. Jung looks young for her age.

examples.text: 김 선생님이 피곤해 보입니다.
examples.translation: gim seonsaengnimi pigonhae boimnida. — Ms. Kim looks tired.

explanations.title: Compare: –(으)ㄴ/(으)ㄹ/는 것 같다
explanations.body: This auxiliary verb is similar in meaning and function to –(으)ㄴ/(으)ㄹ/는 것 같다, which you learned about in Chapter 17. However, –(으)ㄴ/(으)ㄹ/는 것 같다 can work with an action verb or a stative verb, whereas –아/어 보이다 works only with a stative verb.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Stative verb + –아/어 (the informal stem) + 보이다.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Writing): choose a verb for each picture
explanations.body: The book gives six pictures and the verbs 우울하다, 위험하다, 아프다, 외롭다, 행복하다 and 긴장되다, and asks you to choose the verb that best describes the person in each picture, conjugate it with –아/어 보이다 and use it in a phrase; the first one is done for you (우울해 보이다). The pictures are left out.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Listening and speaking): the model
explanations.body: The book asks you to write ten stative verbs and conjugate them with –아/어 보이다 in pairs. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 뚱뚱하다
examples.translation: ga: ttungttunghada — to be fat

examples.text: 나: 뚱뚱해 보여요.
examples.translation: na: ttungttunghae boyeoyo. — He looks fat.

examples.text: 나: 날씬하다
examples.translation: na: nalssinhada — to be slim

examples.text: 가: 날씬해 보여요.
examples.translation: ga: nalssinhae boyeoyo. — She looks slim.

lessons.title: 398. Ch 31 · Grammar D: –(으)니까 / –아/어 보니까, the discovery of a fact
lessons.subtitle: -(으)니까 · -아/어 보니까 · 일어나니까 · 가 보니까 · 살아 보니까 · 배워 보니까 · 발견

explanations.title: –(으)니까 as a reason (review)
explanations.body: In an earlier chapter, you learned about the conjunctive ending –(으)니까, which can be used to express a reason, as in the following examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 날씨가 좋으니까 바닷가에 갑시다.
examples.translation: nalssiga joeunikka badatgae gapsida. — Because the weather is good, let’s go to the beach.

examples.text: 피곤하니까 일찍 자고 싶어요.
examples.translation: pigonhanikka iljjik jago sipeoyo. — Because I am tired, I would like to go to bed early.

explanations.title: –(으)니까 for the discovery of a fact
explanations.body: The same conjunctive ending can also express the speaker’s action or experience that leads to the discovery of a fact. In this case, the conjunctive ending translates to “and” or “when”, and the main clause translates to “I discover(ed)” or “I find/found”. For example:

examples.text: 아침에 일어나니까 아무도 기숙사에 없었어요.
examples.translation: achime ireonanikka amudo gisuksae eopseosseoyo. — I woke up in the morning and (I discovered that) no one was in the dormitory. / When I woke up in the morning, (I found that) no one was in the dormitory.

examples.text: 서울에 가 보니까 너무 복잡해요.
examples.translation: seoure ga bonikka neomu bokjapaeyo. — I went to Seoul and (I found that) it was too crowded. / When I went to Seoul, (I found that) it was too crowded.

explanations.title: In a question
explanations.body: When –(으)니까 is used in a question, the speaker asks about the listener’s discovery. (3D → 삼디 is spelled out in Hangul.)

examples.text: 서울에 가 보니까 복잡해요?
examples.translation: seoure ga bonikka bokjapaeyo? — You went to Seoul, and did you find that it is crowded? / When you went to Seoul, did you find it was crowded?

examples.text: 삼디로 아바타를 보니까 어땠어요?
examples.translation: samdiro abatareul bonikka eottaesseoyo? — How did you like Avatar (since you watched it) in 3-D?

explanations.title: –(으)니까 / –아/어 보니까 with the discovery of a fact
explanations.body: The book’s examples (DLI → 디엘아이 is spelled out in Hangul):

examples.text: 디엘아이에서 한국말을 배워 보니까 한국말이 재미있습니다.
examples.translation: dieraieseo hangungmareul baewo bonikka hangungmari jaemiitseumnida. — I have learned Korean at DLI, and (I find that) Korean is fun.

examples.text: 도서관에 가니까 공사 중이었어요.
examples.translation: doseogwane ganikka gongsa jungieosseoyo. — I went to the library, and (I found that) it was under construction.

examples.text: 한국에 살아 보니까 한국이 달라 보입니다.
examples.translation: hanguge sara bonikka hangugi dalla boimnida. — I live in Korea, and (I find that) Korea looks different (than I thought).

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Verb stem + (으)니까 (a stem ending in ㄹ drops the ㄹ: 살다 → 사니까), and the experience form: informal stem (–아/어) + 보니까.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Speaking and reading): the model
explanations.body: The book gives five phrases (한국말을 배우다; 매일 운동을 하다; 몬트레이에 살다; 결혼을 하다; 오늘 뉴스를 듣다), and the groups take turns conjugating the phrase with –(으)니까 or –아/어 보니까 and adding a discovery. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 선생님: 샌프란시스코에 가다
examples.translation: seonsaengnim: saenpeuransiseukoe gada — to go to San Francisco

examples.text: 가 팀: 샌프란시스코에 가니까 날씨가 흐렸어요.
examples.translation: ga tim: saenpeuransiseukoe ganikka nalssiga heuryeosseoyo. — I went to San Francisco and the weather was cloudy.

examples.text: 나 팀: 샌프란시스코에 가 보니까 구경할 곳이 많았어요.
examples.translation: na tim: saenpeuransiseukoe ga bonikka gugyeonghal gosi manasseoyo. — I went to San Francisco and there were many places to see.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking): 한국말을 배워 보니까 어때요?
explanations.body: The book asks you to survey your classmates about their discoveries (phrases: 군대 생활을 해 보다, 몬트레이에 살아 보다, 한국말을 배워 보다, 한국음식을 먹어 보다, 기숙사에 살아 보다). The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 김 일병, 한국말을 배워 보니까 어때요?
examples.translation: ga: gim ilbyeong, hangungmareul baewo bonikka eottaeyo? — Private First Class Kim, how is it, now that you have learned Korean?

examples.text: 나: 한국말을 배워 보니까 아주 재미있어요.
examples.translation: na: hangungmareul baewo bonikka aju jaemiisseoyo. — Now that I have learned Korean, it is very fun.

explanations.title: Activities left out

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Writing and reading): a news article about heart disease and diabetes
explanations.body: The book gives a news article. (a) Read it and circle the words you know (hint: the story has unfamiliar words; do not pay attention to every word, focus on the words you know). (b) Read it again and write a title for the article in Korean. (c) List four causes of the diseases in English. (d) List the four disease-prevention measures in English. The book glosses 쌓이다: to be piled up, to be accumulated. The text is the book’s with 60–90% spelled out in Hangul; the English is mine.

examples.text: 심장 질환과 당뇨병 환자의 육십 퍼센트에서 구십 퍼센트는 과체중이고, 스트레스가 심한 직업을 가지고 있다.
examples.translation: simjang jilhwangwa dangnyobyeong hwanjaui yuksip peosenteueseo gusip peosenteuneun gwachejungigo, seuteureseuga simhan jigeobeul gajigo itda. — Sixty to ninety percent of heart disease and diabetes patients are overweight and have stressful jobs.

examples.text: 심장 질환과 당뇨병의 원인은 여러 가지가 있다.
examples.translation: simjang jilhwangwa dangnyobyeongui wonineun yeoreo gajiga itda. — There are various causes of heart disease and diabetes.

examples.text: 가장 큰 원인은 유전이고 환경적 원인도 있다.
examples.translation: gajang keun wonineun yujeonigo hwangyeongjeok wonindo itda. — The biggest cause is heredity, and there are also environmental causes.

examples.text: 환경적 원인은 식습관과 생활습관, 스트레스 등이 있다.
examples.translation: hwangyeongjeok wonineun sikseupgwangwa saenghwalseupgwan, seuteureseu deungi itda. — The environmental causes include eating habits, lifestyle habits and stress.

examples.text: 이런 질병을 예방하기 위해서는 첫째, 규칙적으로 운동을 해야 한다.
examples.translation: ireon jilbyeongeul yebanghagi wihaeseoneun cheotjjae, gyuchikjeogeuro undongeul haeya handa. — To prevent these diseases, first, you must exercise regularly.

examples.text: 가벼운 체조나 걷기, 집안일도 좋은 운동이다.
examples.translation: gabyeoun chejona geotgi, jibanildo joeun undongida. — Light gymnastics, walking and housework are also good exercise.

examples.text: 둘째, 바른 식습관을 갖는다.
examples.translation: duljjae, bareun sikseupgwaneul ganneunda. — Second, have proper eating habits.

examples.text: 짠 음식이나 단 음식은 피하도록 한다.
examples.translation: jjan eumsigina dan eumsigeun pihadorok handa. — Make sure to avoid salty or sweet food.

examples.text: 또 과식과 과음도 하지 않도록 한다.
examples.translation: tto gwasikgwa gwaeumdo haji antorok handa. — Also make sure not to overeat or overdrink.

examples.text: 셋째, 스트레스가 쌓이지 않도록 한다.
examples.translation: setjjae, seuteureseuga ssaiji antorok handa. — Third, make sure stress does not pile up.

examples.text: 스트레스를 받았을 때는 취미생활이나 운동으로 스트레스를 푸는 것이 좋다.
examples.translation: seuteureseureul badasseul ttaeneun chwimisaenghwarina undongeuro seuteureseureul puneun geosi jota. — When you are stressed, it is good to relieve stress with hobbies or exercise.

examples.text: 마지막으로 매년 정기 검진을 받도록 한다.
examples.translation: majimageuro maenyeon jeonggi geomjineul batdorok handa. — Lastly, make sure to get a regular checkup every year.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the lines blank; these are my answers.

rows: 심장 질환과 당뇨병의 원인과 예방 (The causes and prevention of heart disease and diabetes)
Heredity; eating habits; lifestyle habits; stress

1. Exercise regularly (light gymnastics, walking, housework). 2. Have proper eating habits (avoid salty and sweet food; no overeating or overdrinking). 3. Don’t let stress pile up (relieve it with hobbies or exercise). 4. Get a regular checkup every year.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (SMART Board), Activity 3 (listening to conversations about diabetes, cancer and obesity) and Activity 4 (a radio-show role-play with callers, in groups) are computer, audio and group activities.

The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The book’s related words (the synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (아침 6 시에 → 아침 여섯 시에).

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

lessons.subtitle: 건강한 생활 · 노인 · 편식 · 직접 · 간접 · 노화 · 편견

explanations.title: What Chapter 32 teaches (건강한 생활)
explanations.body:
Chapter 32, “Living a Healthy Life”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify healthy eating and lifestyle habits; discuss living a healthy, long life; and give and receive advice about health and nutrition.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the causative construction –게 하다; the informal ending –거든(요); –(으)ㄹ 만하다 (be worth ~ing); the conjunctive ending –는 데(에); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 노인 (老人), 편식 (偏食), and 직접 (直接).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 노인 (老人)
explanations.body:
This Sino-Korean word refers to an aged person, the elderly, or the aged; 로/노 (老) means old or aged and 인 (人) means a person. The character 老 reads as 노 when it is placed at the beginning of a word. When placed elsewhere, it reads as 로, as in 경로 (敬老), respect for the aged. 화 (化) means “become”.

The book asks you to guess the meaning of 노화, 노년, 남녀노소, 외국인, 부인 and 성인 (my answers are in the table).

rows: men and women, old and young

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 편식 (偏食)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means unhealthy diet, unhealthy dietary preference, or poor eating (habit). The first syllable 편 (偏) means skewed or tilted, as in 편견 (a bias; “skewed opinion”), 편두통 (migraine), and 편애 (partiality [for]; favoritism [to]; “skewed love”). The second syllable 식 (食) means food or eating, as in 식당 (a dining room; a restaurant; “eating house”) and 후식 (a dessert; “post food”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 편식 is “skewed eating” or “tilted eating”, and it refers to the unhealthy dietary habit of eating only a limited variety of food.

rows: a dining room; a restaurant; “eating house”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 직접 (直接)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means direct or firsthand. The first syllable 직 (直) means direct or straight, as in 직감 (intuition; “direct feeling”), 직선 (a straight line; a beeline), 직언 (straight talk; “direct speech”), and 직행 (going/coming straight; nonstop; “direct coming and going”). The second syllable 접 (接) means contact or treat, as in 접대 (a reception; a warm welcome; “treating and waiting”), 접지 (ground connection; grounding; “contact the ground”), and 접촉 (contact; touch; “contact and touch”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 직접 is “direct contact”, and the word means direct or firsthand. The antonym of the word is 간접 (indirect; secondhand), as in 간접흡연 (secondhand smoking) and 간접선거 (indirect election).

explanations.title: Topic A: People who live long mainly eat vegetables (장수하는 사람들은 주로 채식을 합니다)
explanations.body: A reporter on a radio show is talking about longevity. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 장수의 첫 번째 비결은 좋은 식습관입니다.
examples.translation: jangsuui cheot beonjjae bigyeoreun joeun sikseupgwanimnida. — The first secret of longevity is good eating habits.

examples.text: 장수하는 사람들은 주로 채식을 합니다.
examples.translation: jangsuhaneun saramdeureun juro chaesigeul hamnida. — People who live long mainly eat vegetables.

examples.text: 그리고 소식을 하고 식사를 거르지 않습니다.
examples.translation: geurigo sosigeul hago siksareul georeuji anseumnida. — And they eat lightly and do not skip meals.

examples.text: 또, 콩과 보리쌀을 섞은 잡곡밥을 매일 먹습니다.
examples.translation: tto, konggwa borissareul seokkeun japgokbabeul maeil meokseumnida. — Also, they eat mixed-grain rice with beans and barley every day.

examples.text: 쇠고기나 돼지고기는 별로 먹지 않고 생선을 자주 먹습니다.
examples.translation: soegogina dwaejigogineun byeollo meokji anko saengseoneul jaju meokseumnida. — They do not eat much beef or pork and often eat fish.

examples.text: 두 번째는 부지런한 생활습관입니다.
examples.translation: du beonjjaeneun bujireonhan saenghwalseupgwanimnida. — The second is a diligent lifestyle.

examples.text: 장수하는 사람들은 항상 일찍 일어나서 부지런히 몸을 움직입니다.
examples.translation: jangsuhaneun saramdeureun hangsang iljjik ireonaseo bujireonhi momeul umjigimnida. — People who live long always get up early and move their bodies diligently.

examples.text: 그리고 집안일도 하고 밖에서 일도 합니다.
examples.translation: geurigo jibanildo hago bakkeseo ildo hamnida. — And they do housework and also work outside.

examples.text: 세 번째 장수 비결은 좋은 자연환경에서 다른 사람들과 잘 지내는 것입니다.
examples.translation: se beonjjae jangsu bigyeoreun joeun jayeonhwangyeongeseo dareun saramdeulgwa jal jinaeneun geosimnida. — The third secret of longevity is to get along well with other people in a good natural environment.

examples.text: 장수마을은 주로 아름다운 자연 속에 있습니다.
examples.translation: jangsumaeureun juro areumdaun jayeon soge itseumnida. — Longevity villages are mostly in the midst of beautiful nature.

examples.text: 장수마을 사람들은 늘 아름다운 자연 속에서 살아서 성격도 낙천적입니다.
examples.translation: jangsumaeul saramdeureun neul areumdaun jayeon sogeseo saraseo seonggyeokdo nakcheonjeogimnida. — The people of longevity villages always live in beautiful nature, so their personalities are also optimistic.

examples.text: 마을 사람들과 자주 이야기도 나누고 항상 즐겁게 생활합니다.
examples.translation: maeul saramdeulgwa jaju iyagido nanugo hangsang jeulgeopge saenghwalhamnida. — They often chat with the people of the village and always live cheerfully.

explanations.title: The book’s footnotes
explanations.body: 쇠고기 can be used interchangeably with 소고기. 장수마을 literally means “a longevity village”. This term refers to a community of people whose average lifespan is significantly longer than the national average.

explanations.title: Core words and phrases of Topic A
explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter); 소식(하다), 장수(하다) and 채식(하다) take the form in parentheses.

explanations.title: Reading and writing: tips for a long, healthy life
explanations.body: The book lists eleven tips (건강한 삶을 위해서…) and asks you to sort them into three categories, writing the numbers in the first row and the key Korean words in the second; the first is done for you (sentence 1: 깨끗한 자연환경; the book glosses 적당하다: to be adequate, to be appropriate). The tips below have 6~8시간 spelled out; the English and my sorting are below.

examples.text: 깨끗한 자연환경 속에서 삽니다.
examples.translation: kkaekkeutan jayeonhwangyeong sogeseo samnida. — Live in a clean natural environment.

examples.text: 적당히 쉬고 매일 여섯 시간에서 여덟 시간 동안 잠을 잡니다.
examples.translation: jeokdanghi swigo maeil yeoseot siganeseo yeodeol sigan dongan jameul jamnida. — Rest adequately and sleep six to eight hours every day.

examples.text: 스트레스를 풀 수 있는 취미활동을 합니다.
examples.translation: seuteureseureul pul su inneun chwimihwaldongeul hamnida. — Do hobby activities that can relieve stress.

examples.text: 채식을 주로 합니다.
examples.translation: chaesigeul juro hamnida. — Mainly eat vegetables.

examples.text: 소식을 합니다.
examples.translation: sosigeul hamnida. — Eat lightly.

examples.text: 가벼운 운동을 규칙적으로 합니다.
examples.translation: gabyeoun undongeul gyuchikjeogeuro hamnida. — Exercise lightly and regularly.

examples.text: 공기 좋은 곳에 가서 맑은 공기를 마십니다.
examples.translation: gonggi joeun gose gaseo malgeun gonggireul masimnida. — Go to a place with good air and breathe clean air.

examples.text: 부지런히 일을 합니다.
examples.translation: bujireonhi ireul hamnida. — Work diligently.

examples.text: 가족들과 자주 대화합니다.
examples.translation: gajokdeulgwa jaju daehwahamnida. — Talk often with your family.

examples.text: 콩이나 보리쌀 등 잡곡을 섞은 밥을 먹습니다.
examples.translation: kongina borissal deung japgogeul seokkeun babeul meokseumnida. — Eat rice mixed with grains such as beans and barley.

examples.text: 긍정적인 생각과 낙천적인 태도를 가지고 생활합니다.
examples.translation: geungjeongjeogin saenggakgwa nakcheonjeogin taedoreul gajigo saenghwalhamnida. — Live with positive thoughts and an optimistic attitude.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): a survey report on the secrets of longevity
explanations.body: The following survey report, conducted by the 고령사회연구소 (Institute for Aging Society) at Seoul National University, is about living a long, healthy life. The book asks you to circle the words you don’t know and look them up (it glosses 연구소: a research institute; 차이: difference). The text is the book’s with the numbers and dates spelled out in Hangul; the book writes 건강·장수를 and the middle dot is read “and”, so it is written 건강과 장수를 here. The English is mine.

examples.text: 장수 마을의 장수 비결 조사
examples.translation: jangsu maeurui jangsu bigyeol josa — A survey of the secrets of longevity in longevity villages

examples.text: 서울대 고령사회연구소는 전북 순창군 등에서 장수 비결에 대한 조사를 하고 있다.
examples.translation: seouldae goryeongsahoeyeongusoneun jeonbuk sunchanggun deungeseo jangsu bigyeore daehan josareul hago itda. — The Institute for Aging Society at Seoul National University is conducting a survey on the secrets of longevity in places such as Sunchang County in North Jeolla Province.

examples.text: 이 연구소는 국내 대표적인 네 개 장수지역에서 육십오 세 이상 천여 명을 대상으로 조사하고 있다.
examples.translation: i yeongusoneun gungnae daepyojeogin ne gae jangsujiyeogeseo yuksibo se isang cheonyeo myeongeul daesangeuro josahago itda. — This institute is surveying about one thousand people aged sixty-five or older in four representative longevity regions in Korea.

examples.text: 이 연구소는 지난 십오 일부터 다음 달 일 일까지 이 지역 장수노인 가정을 직접 방문한다.
examples.translation: i yeongusoneun jinan sibo ilbuteo daeum dal il ilkkaji i jiyeok jangsunoin gajeongeul jikjeop bangmunhanda. — From the fifteenth of last month to the first of next month, this institute is visiting the homes of the longevity elderly in these regions in person.

examples.text: 그리고 장수 노인들의 식습관, 건강상태, 생활방식 등을 조사한다.
examples.translation: geurigo jangsu noindeurui sikseupgwan, geongangsangtae, saenghwalbangsik deungeul josahanda. — And it surveys the longevity elderly’s eating habits, health condition, lifestyle and so on.

examples.text: 이 연구소는 조사를 통해 건강한 노인과 건강하지 않은 노인들의 차이를 비교한다.
examples.translation: i yeongusoneun josareul tonghae geonganghan noingwa geonganghaji aneun noindeurui chaireul bigyohanda. — Through the survey, this institute compares the differences between healthy and unhealthy elderly people.

examples.text: 그리고 건강과 장수를 위한 식생활 모델을 만들 계획이다.
examples.translation: geurigo geonganggwa jangsureul wihan siksaenghwal modereul mandeul gyehoegida. — And it plans to make a dietary model for health and longevity.

examples.text: 순창군은 전국 이백삼십사 개 지역 중 백 세 이상 노인의 비율이 전국에서 가장 높다.
examples.translation: sunchangguneun jeonguk ibaeksamsipsa gae jiyeok jung baek se isang noinui biyuri jeongugeseo gajang nopda. — Among the two hundred and thirty-four regions nationwide, Sunchang County has the highest proportion of elderly people aged one hundred or older in the whole country.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the answers blank; these are mine.

rows: 1. What is the purpose of the survey?
To find the secrets of longevity (their eating habits, health and lifestyle), compare healthy and unhealthy elderly people, and make a dietary model for health and longevity
About 1,000 people aged 65 or older in four representative longevity regions in Korea (including Sunchang County, North Jeolla Province)
By visiting the homes of the longevity elderly in person, from the 15th of last month to the 1st of next month
The elderly’s eating habits, health condition and lifestyle
5. What was said about Sunchang County?
It has the highest proportion of people aged 100 or older among the 234 regions nationwide

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 3 (listening to three interviews with senior citizens) and Activity 4 (reading two news articles, Article A and Article B, in two groups and exchanging the information in pairs) need audio, articles that are not in the book’s text, and classmates.

explanations.title: Topic B: What are Jehyeon’s eating habits like? (제현이의 식습관이 어떻습니까?)
explanations.body: A health and nutrition counselor is giving advice to the mother of a teenager who has had a childhood obesity checkup. (The English is mine; the book gives none; 3번 is spelled out.)

examples.text: 엄마: 제현이 비만 검사 결과가 나왔어요?
examples.translation: eomma: jehyeoni biman geomsa gyeolgwaga nawasseoyo? — Have Jehyeon’s obesity test results come out?

examples.text: 건강관리사: 네, 체지방이 조금 높네요. 제현이의 식습관이 어떻습니까?
examples.translation: geonganggwallisa: ne, chejibangi jogeum nomneyo. jehyeoniui sikseupgwani eotteoseumnikka? — Yes, his body fat is a little high. What are Jehyeon’s eating habits like?

examples.text: 엄마: 제현이는 간식을 너무 좋아해요. 특히 과자나 사탕을 많이 먹어요. 그리고 채소와 생선은 잘 안 먹어요.
examples.translation: eomma: jehyeonineun gansigeul neomu joahaeyo. teuki gwajana satangeul mani meogeoyo. geurigo chaesowa saengseoneun jal an meogeoyo. — Jehyeon likes snacks too much. He especially eats a lot of cookies and candy. And he doesn’t eat vegetables and fish well.

examples.text: 건강관리사: 운동은 자주 합니까?
examples.translation: geonganggwallisa: undongeun jaju hamnikka? — Does he exercise often?

examples.text: 엄마: 아니요, 거의 안 해요. 운동을 아주 싫어하거든요.
examples.translation: eomma: aniyo, geoui an haeyo. undongeul aju sireohageodeunyo. — No, he hardly does. He hates exercise a lot, you see.

examples.text: 건강관리사: 건강에 안 좋은 습관을 가지고 있군요. 그럼, 비만이 되기 쉬워요.
examples.translation: geonganggwallisa: geongange an joeun seupgwaneul gajigo itgunyo. geureom, bimani doegi swiwoyo. — I see he has habits that are not good for health. Then it is easy for him to become obese.

examples.text: 엄마: 그래요? 비만을 예방하려면 어떻게 해야 하나요?
examples.translation: eomma: geuraeyo? bimaneul yebangharyeomyeon eotteoke haeya hanayo? — Is that so? What should we do to prevent obesity?

examples.text: 건강관리사: 여러 가지 영양소를 균형 있게 섭취해야 해요. 편식을 못 하게 하시고 음식을 골고루 먹이세요.
examples.translation: geonganggwallisa: yeoreo gaji yeongyangsoreul gyunhyeong itge seopchwihaeya haeyo. pyeonsigeul mot hage hasigo eumsigeul golgoru meogiseyo. — You must take in various nutrients in a balanced way. Don’t let him be a picky eater, and feed him a variety of food evenly.

examples.text: 엄마: 네, 알겠습니다.
examples.translation: eomma: ne, algetseumnida. — Yes, I understand.

examples.text: 건강관리사: 그리고 운동도 규칙적으로 하게 하세요. 운동할 때는 땀이 날 때까지 하면 더 좋습니다.
examples.translation: geonganggwallisa: geurigo undongdo gyuchikjeogeuro hage haseyo. undonghal ttaeneun ttami nal ttaekkaji hamyeon deo joseumnida. — And also make him exercise regularly. When he exercises, it is better to go on until he sweats.

examples.text: 엄마: 운동은 얼마나 하는 게 좋아요?
examples.translation: eomma: undongeun eolmana haneun ge joayo? — How much exercise is good?

examples.text: 건강관리사: 적어도 일주일에 세 번 이상 하면 비만 예방에 효과가 있습니다.
examples.translation: geonganggwallisa: jeogeodo iljuire se beon isang hamyeon biman yebange hyogwaga itseumnida. — If he does it at least three times a week, it is effective in preventing obesity.

explanations.title: The book’s footnote
explanations.body: 관리사 in 건강관리사 (health and nutrition counselor; health-care specialist) means a specialist, as in 피부관리사 (a skin-care specialist) or 보험관리사 (an insurance agent).

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 어린이 군것질 (children’s snacks)
explanations.body: On the way home from school, many Korean children stop for snacks at food stands where street foods, such as 떡볶이 (rice cake cooked in spicy sauce) or 튀김 (deep-fried assortments), are available. Children also stop to eat at fast-food restaurants. According to a survey conducted in 2009 by the Seoul City Administrations, 46% of elementary school students purchase snacks on the way home from school once or twice a week. (The book adds a pie chart of children’s favorite snacks from 데이터뉴스, which is a picture and is left out.)

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): 나의 식습관은 몇 점일까? (a self-assessment of eating habits)
explanations.body: The book gives a self-assessment (식습관 자가진단) of dietary patterns and lifestyle choices: read it, rate how healthy your eating habits are and identify areas that can be improved. The ten statements (the book’s, with the numbers spelled out; the English is mine):

lessons.title: 407. Ch 32 · Grammar A: the causative –게 하다, to have/make/let someone do
lessons.subtitle: ~에게 -게 하다 · ~한테 -게 하다 · 청소하게 했어요 · 마시게 하세요 · -도록 하다

explanations.title: Expressing a causative
explanations.body: A causative sentence is one in which the subject (or agent) causes or forces the object to perform an action or to be in a certain condition. For example, “The teacher made his students remain silent.” In English we normally express a causative using verbs like have, make, let, or get. In Korean, we express a causative using ~에게/한테 … –게 하다. Note that the object marked by 에게/한테 is followed by the verb –게 하다. Depending on the context, this translates to have, make, or let. The pattern: ~한테/에게 … verb stem + 게 하다. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 나는 동생에게 매일 방을 청소하게 했어요.
examples.translation: naneun dongsaengege maeil bangeul cheongsohage haesseoyo. — I had my younger brother clean the room every day.

examples.text: 나는 학생들에게 숙제를 하게 할 거예요.
examples.translation: naneun haksaengdeurege sukjereul hage hal geoyeyo. — I will make the students do their homework.

examples.text: 선생님이 저에게 사무실 전화를 사용하게 하셨어요.
examples.translation: seonsaengnimi jeoege samusil jeonhwareul sayonghage hasyeosseoyo. — The teacher let me use the office phone.

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: The book’s further examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 반장이 학생 한 명에게 칠판을 지우게 했어요.

examples.text: 엄마가 동생한테 아침마다 운동을 하게 했어요.
examples.translation: eommaga dongsaenghante achimmada undongeul hage haesseoyo. — My mom made my brother work out every morning.

explanations.title: Notes (참고)
explanations.body:
1. ~에게/한테 attached to the object can be replaced by the subject marker 이/가 or the object marker 을/를. However, ~에게/한테 is preferred over ~이/가 and ~을/를.

2. Recall from Chapter 29 that –도록 하다 means “make sure”. It is also used to imply “have someone do something”.

examples.translation: jega jinsuege chareul gochidorok haesseoyo. — I got Jinsoo to fix the car (with –도록 하다).

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Verb stem + 게 하다; the table uses the polite request –게 하세요 (“make/have them …”).

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Speaking and listening): who will do each duty?
explanations.body: In pairs, one partner is a section leader who must fairly distribute each assignment to everyone in the class. Partner A asks “누구에게 … –게 할까요?” and Partner B answers “~에게 … –게 합시다.” The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 누구에게 칠판을 지우게 할까요?
examples.translation: ga: nuguege chilpaneul jiuge halkkayo? — Whom shall we make erase the board?

examples.text: 나: 김 일병에게 칠판을 지우게 합시다.
examples.translation: na: gim ilbyeongege chilpaneul jiuge hapsida. — Let’s make Private First Class Kim erase the board.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): a doctor’s advice about nutrition
explanations.body: Read the doctor’s advice, circle the grammar feature –게 하다 and translate the sentences containing it into English (the four sentences with 게 하세요 are the third, fourth, sixth and ninth below; the book glosses 우유: milk). The English is mine.

examples.text: 요즘 체중에 문제가 있는 어린이들이 많습니다.
examples.translation: yojeum chejunge munjega inneun eorinideuri manseumnida. — These days there are many children with weight problems.

examples.text: 어릴 때부터 좋은 식습관을 기르는 것이 중요합니다.
examples.translation: eoril ttaebuteo joeun sikseupgwaneul gireuneun geosi jungyohamnida. — It is important to build good eating habits from childhood.

examples.text: 아이들에게 음료수 대신에 물이나 우유를 마시게 하세요.
examples.translation: aideurege eumnyosu daesine murina uyureul masige haseyo. — Make children drink water or milk instead of soft drinks.

examples.text: 또 지방이 많은 음식보다는 신선한 채소를 많이 먹게 하세요.
examples.translation: tto jibangi maneun eumsikbodaneun sinseonhan chaesoreul mani meokge haseyo. — Also make them eat a lot of fresh vegetables rather than fatty food.

examples.text: 간식은 과자나 케이크보다는 과일이 좋습니다.
examples.translation: gansigeun gwajana keikeubodaneun gwairi joseumnida. — For snacks, fruit is better than cookies or cake.

examples.text: 그리고 매일 규칙적으로 운동을 하게 하세요.
examples.translation: geurigo maeil gyuchikjeogeuro undongeul hage haseyo. — And make them exercise regularly every day.

examples.text: 그럼 체중이 크게 늘지 않을 거예요.
examples.translation: geureom chejungi keuge neulji aneul geoyeyo. — Then their weight will not increase much.

examples.text: 체중이 늘면 여러 가지 건강 문제가 생깁니다.
examples.translation: chejungi neulmyeon yeoreo gaji geongang munjega saenggimnida. — If weight increases, various health problems arise.

examples.text: 아이들에게 어릴 때부터 좋은 생활습관을 갖게 하세요.
examples.translation: aideurege eoril ttaebuteo joeun saenghwalseupgwaneul gatge haseyo. — Make children have good lifestyle habits from childhood.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 5 (a parent and a counselor role-play) needs a partner; the book’s model is: 저희 아들이 요즘 체중이 늘었거든요. 어떻게 해야 해요? — 매일 삼십 분씩 운동을 하게 하세요. 그리고 칼로리가 높은 음식은 피하게 하세요. (The parent’s problem uses –거든요, the next lesson; the counselor’s advice uses –게 하다. 30분 is spelled out.)

lessons.title: 408. Ch 32 · Grammar B: the sentence ending –거든(요), a reason or background
lessons.subtitle: -거든요 · 바쁘거든요 · 있거든요 · 시험 기간이거든요 · 이유 · 배경 정보

explanations.title: The sentence ending –거든(요)
explanations.body: Like the sentence ending –아/어(요), the sentence ending –거든(요) is used in informal settings. However, –거든(요) is mainly used for one of two situations. First, when providing a reason about the statement or question in a conversation, –거든(요) can be translated as “because” or “for”. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 요즘 왜 체육관에 안 오세요?
examples.translation: yojeum wae cheyukgwane an oseyo? — Why aren’t you coming to the gym these days?

examples.text: 제가 좀 바쁘거든요.
examples.translation: jega jom bappeugeodeunyo. — Because I am a little busy.

examples.text: 요즘 제가 체육관에 잘 안 가요.
examples.translation: yojeum jega cheyukgwane jal an gayo. — I don’t go to the gym often these days,

examples.text: 제가 좀 바쁘거든요.
examples.translation: jega jom bappeugeodeunyo. — for I am a little busy.

explanations.title: Giving background information
explanations.body: Second, when providing background information for the remark that will follow, –거든(요) translates to “you know” or “you see”. (The English is the book’s.) Because –거든(요) is used to provide a reason or background information, the ending is used only in a statement, never in a question.

examples.text: 시내에 커피숍이 하나 있거든요.
examples.translation: sinaee keopisyobi hana itgeodeunyo. — There is a coffee shop downtown, you know.

examples.text: 거기에서 만나요.
examples.translation: geogieseo mannayo. — Let’s meet over there.

examples.text: 시험 기간이거든요.
examples.translation: siheom giganigeodeunyo. — It is exam time, you know.

examples.text: 그래서 파티에 못 가요.
examples.translation: geuraeseo patie mot gayo. — So I cannot go to the party.

explanations.title: With a raised intonation (the book’s footnote)
explanations.body: –거든(요) with a raised intonation can be used to express the speaker’s annoyance or cynicism (the book marks the rising pitch with ↗).

examples.text: 저도 알거든요.
examples.translation: jeodo algeodeunyo. — I know that too (so stop lecturing).

examples.text: 저도 한국말을 잘 할 수 있거든요.
examples.translation: jeodo hangungmareul jal hal su itgeodeunyo. — I too can speak Korean well (so don’t boast).

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Verb or adjective stem (present or past) + 거든요; a noun + 이다 gives –이거든요.

explanations.title: Topic C: Are you interested in well-being cultural events? (웰빙 문화행사에 관심이 있으세요?)
explanations.body: A radio reporter is announcing events about well-being. The events are hosted by the YMCA. (The English is mine; the book gives none. YMCA is spelled out as 와이엠시에이, and the phone number 02-345-6789 is spelled out in Hangul, with the hyphens read 에.)

examples.translation: waiemsieieseoneun yeoreumbanghageul majihayeo dayanghan welbing munhwahaengsareul maryeonhaetseumnida. — For the summer vacation, the YMCA has prepared a variety of well-being cultural events.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 웰빙 (well-being)
explanations.body: 웰빙 (well-being) is a buzzword in Korea that refers to a healthy lifestyle trend. You see this term in words like 웰빙식품, 웰빙주택, 웰빙라이프, and 웰빙문화. Korea’s 웰빙 boom goes back to early 2002, when a popular television documentary series highlighted the hidden dangers of everyday foods. The current 웰빙 trend is linked to the rise of middle- and upper-class consumers who value health, personal development, and environmental protection. 웰빙 encompasses not only a change in consumption patterns, but also a change in values, indicating a mature, industrialized economy.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1a (Reading): an announcement about an expo
explanations.body: Read the announcement and, in English, identify the type of expo and three specific booths mentioned. The text is the book’s (9월 11일부터 20일까지 is spelled out; the book’s three booths are in parentheses in its sentence and are set apart here). The English is mine.

examples.text: 천안 웰빙식품엑스포가 구월 십일 일부터 이십 일까지 천안 삼거리공원에서 열립니다.
examples.translation: cheonan welbingsikpumekseupoga guwol sibil ilbuteo isip ilkkaji cheonan samgeorigongwoneseo yeollimnida. — The Cheonan Well-being Food Expo will be held at Cheonan Samgeori Park from September 11 to 20.

examples.text: 이번 엑스포에서는 우리 전통식품과 웰빙 유기농 건강식품을 전시합니다.
examples.translation: ibeon ekseupoeseoneun uri jeontongsikpumgwa welbing yuginong geongangsikpumeul jeonsihamnida. — At this expo, our traditional foods and well-being organic health foods will be displayed.

examples.text: 또한, 직접 체험할 수 있는 여러 전시관을 운영합니다.
examples.translation: ttohan, jikjeop cheheomhal su inneun yeoreo jeonsigwaneul unyeonghamnida. — Also, several exhibition halls where you can experience things firsthand will be operated.

examples.text: 웰빙 친환경 식품전시관, 웰빙 식품체험관, 웰빙 건강체험관
examples.translation: welbing chinhwangyeong sikpumjeonsigwan, welbing sikpumcheheomgwan, welbing geongangcheheomgwan — Well-being eco-friendly food exhibition hall, well-being food experience hall, well-being health experience hall.

examples.text: 관심 있으신 분들의 많은 참여 부탁드립니다.
examples.translation: gwansim isseusin bundeurui maneun chamyeo butakdeurimnida. — We ask for the participation of many interested people.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1b (Reading): descriptions of the booths
explanations.body: The book gives three booth descriptions and asks you to write the name of each booth in Korean and what it displays or presents in English. The book glosses 친환경: environmentally friendly, eco-friendly, “pro-environment”. The descriptions, in the book’s order (booth 1 is the first two sentences; the English is mine):

examples.text: 채식이나 소식 등 장수 식습관과 식품영양 정보를 소개합니다.
examples.translation: chaesigina sosik deung jangsu sikseupgwangwa sikpumyeongyang jeongboreul sogaehamnida. — It introduces longevity eating habits such as vegetarian diets and light eating, and food and nutrition information.

examples.text: 각 개인의 건강상태를 진단해 주고 그에 따른 올바른 건강식단을 추천해 줍니다.
examples.translation: gak gaeinui geongangsangtaereul jindanhae jugo geue ttareun olbareun geongangsikdaneul chucheonhae jumnida. — It diagnoses each individual’s health condition and recommends a proper healthy diet accordingly.

examples.text: 웰빙식품을 직접 보고 만들 수 있도록 전통 두부 만들기, 치즈 만들기 등 웰빙요리교실을 직접 운영합니다.
examples.translation: welbingsikpumeul jikjeop bogo mandeul su itdorok jeontong dubu mandeulgi, chijeu mandeulgi deung welbingyorigyosireul jikjeop unyeonghamnida. — So that you can see and make well-being food yourself, it directly runs well-being cooking classes such as making traditional tofu and making cheese.

examples.text: 패스트푸드나 인스턴트 식품의 문제점을 보여주고, 오염되지 않은 유기농 친환경 건강식품을 전시합니다.
examples.translation: paeseuteupudeuna inseuteonteu sikpumui munjejeomeul boyeojugo, oyeomdoeji aneun yuginong chinhwangyeong geongangsikpumeul jeonsihamnida. — It shows the problems of fast food and instant food and displays unpolluted organic eco-friendly health food.

lessons.title: 411. Ch 32 · Grammar C: –(으)ㄹ 만하다, to be worth ~ing; to deserve
lessons.subtitle: -(으)ㄹ 만하다 · 볼 만해요 · 구경할 만해요 · 먹어볼 만해요 · 될 만한 사람

explanations.title: –(으)ㄹ 만하다: worth doing
explanations.body: The grammar feature –(으)ㄹ 만하다, when attached to the stem of an action verb, literally means “to be worth doing”. This expression is used to indicate that a certain action is worth doing. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 그 영화는 볼 만해요.
examples.translation: geu yeonghwaneun bol manhaeyo. — That movie is worth watching.

examples.text: 몬트레이 수족관은 구경할 만해요.
examples.translation: monteurei sujokgwaneun gugyeonghal manhaeyo. — The Monterey Bay Aquarium is worth touring.

examples.text: 그 한국식당 김치는 먹어볼 만해요.
examples.translation: geu hanguksikdang gimchineun meogeobol manhaeyo. — The Korean restaurant’s kimchi is worth trying (eating).

explanations.title: –(으)ㄹ 만하다: qualified; deserving
explanations.body: –(으)ㄹ 만하다 can also be used when someone deserves something (position, award, result, consequence, etc.). In these instances, –(으)ㄹ 만하다 can be translated as “to be qualified to be something” or “to deserve to do something”. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 프랭크는 대통령이 될 만한 사람이에요.
examples.translation: peuraengkeuneun daetongnyeongi doel manhan saramieyo. — Frank is qualified to be the president.

examples.text: 제인은 상을 받을 만한 학생입니다.
examples.translation: jeineun sangeul badeul manhan haksaengimnida. — Jane is a student who is qualified to receive an award. / Jane is a student who deserves to receive an award.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Action verb stem + (으)ㄹ 만하다: the future attributive –(으)ㄹ plus 만하다 (만해요 in the polite style; 만한 before a noun). ㄹ-verbs keep the ㄹ (살 만한); ㄷ-irregular verbs change ㄷ to ㄹ (들을).

lessons.title: 412. Ch 32 · Grammar D: the conjunctive ending –는 데(에), for / in / at doing something
lessons.subtitle: -는 데(에) · 공부하는 데 · 묵을 데 · 해소하는 데 · 빌리는 데 · 예방하는 데에는

explanations.title: The dependent noun 데 (a place, a spot)
explanations.body: Recall that the noun 데 (a place, a spot) is a dependent noun. This means it must be accompanied by a modifier: 먹을 데 (a place to eat) or 아픈 데 (a sore spot). Thus, the literal meaning of –는 데(에) is “(at) a place for doing something” or “(at) a spot for doing something”. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 여기가 내가 공부하는 데예요.
examples.translation: yeogiga naega gongbuhaneun deyeyo. — This is (the place) where I study.

examples.text: 아직 묵을 데를 못 찾았어요.
examples.translation: ajik mugeul dereul mot chajasseoyo. — I haven’t yet found a place to stay.

explanations.title: –는 데(에) as a conjunctive ending
explanations.body: However, when –는 데(에) functions as a conjunctive ending, it is used to bring up a topic of doing something in order to seek or provide specific information about the topic. For this reason, the conjunctive ending –는 데(에) can be translated as “for”, “as for”, or “speaking of”. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 스트레스를 해소하는 데에 무슨 운동이 좋습니까?
examples.translation: seuteureseureul haesohaneun dee museun undongi joseumnikka? — For relieving stress, what sports are good?

examples.text: 한국에서 자동차를 빌리는 데에 국제면허증이 필요합니다.
examples.translation: hangugeseo jadongchareul billineun dee gukjemyeonheojeungi piryohamnida. — For renting a car in Korea, an international driver’s license is needed.

explanations.title: Seeking or providing information
explanations.body:
The first sentence is an interrogative sentence, so the speaker brings up the topic of relieving stress in order to seek specific information about it. The second sentence is a statement, so the speaker brings up the topic of renting a car in Korea in order to provide specific information about it.

Expressing a topic of doing something to seek/provide specific information: verb stem + 는 데(에). The book’s examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 차 바퀴를 바꾸는 데에 얼마예요?
examples.translation: cha bakwireul bakkuneun dee eolmayeyo? — How much is it for replacing tires?

examples.text: 요세미티까지 자동차로 가는 데에 얼마나 걸려요?
examples.translation: yosemitikkaji jadongcharo ganeun dee eolmana geollyeoyo? — [As for] going to Yosemite by car, how long does [it] take?

examples.text: 인터넷으로 비행기표를 사는 데에 신용카드가 필요해요.
examples.translation: inteoneseuro bihaenggipyoreul saneun dee sinyongkadeuga piryohaeyo. — A credit card is needed for buying a plane ticket online.

examples.text: 비만을 예방하는 데에는 야채와 생선이 좋습니다.
examples.translation: bimaneul yebanghaneun deeneun yachaewa saengseoni joseumnida. — Vegetables and fish are good for preventing obesity.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Verb stem + 는 데 (an ㄹ-final stem drops the ㄹ: 만들다 → 만드는 데); 에 can be dropped or followed by the topic particle 는 (-는 데에는).

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Speaking): the model
explanations.body: Sitting in a circle, each student thinks of a topic, writes a Korean question with –는 데(에) and asks the class; classmates answer in Korean. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 해외 여행하는 데에 무엇이 필요합니까?
examples.translation: ga: haeoe yeohaenghaneun dee mueosi piryohamnikka? — What is needed for traveling abroad?

examples.text: 나: 해외 여행하는 데에는 여권이 필요합니다.
examples.translation: na: haeoe yeohaenghaneun deeneun yeogwoni piryohamnida. — A passport is needed for traveling abroad.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking): things needed for a long trip and camping
explanations.body: You and your partner list three things necessary for each of two categories (장거리 여행을 하는 데; 캠핑을 하는 데), ask each other and report to the class. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 장거리 여행을 하는 데 뭐가 필요해요?
examples.translation: ga: janggeori yeohaengeul haneun de mwoga piryohaeyo? — What is needed for taking a long trip?

examples.text: 나: 장거리 여행을 하는 데는 지도와 돈, 옷이 필요해요.
examples.translation: na: janggeori yeohaengeul haneun deneun jidowa don, osi piryohaeyo. — A map, money and clothes are needed for taking a long trip.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): a health report on two patients
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a health report describing what two patients are doing to overcome their health problems. The book asks you to fill in a table in English (illness and symptoms; recommended lifestyle changes). The book glosses 웰빙족: well-being seekers, “well-being tribe”. The first patient is 김순정 (여, 52), a woman of fifty-two, and the second is 박형철 (남, 65), a man of sixty-five (the ages are in the book’s parentheses and are left out of the spoken text); 3년째 and 6개월간 are spelled out. The English is mine.

examples.text: 오늘은 특히 웰빙 라이프스타일로 병을 치료한 두 명의 웰빙족을 만나보겠습니다.
examples.translation: oneureun teuki welbing raipeuseutaillo byeongeul chiryohan du myeongui welbingjogeul mannabogetseumnida. — Today we will meet two well-being seekers who in particular treated their illnesses with a well-being lifestyle.

examples.translation: geogieseo dangnyobyeong jindaneul batgo dangnyobyeongeul gochigi wihae japgokbapgwa yachae deung geongang gwallisaga chucheonhaneun welbing sikdaneul sam nyeonjjae ttareugo itseumnida. — There she was diagnosed with diabetes and, in order to cure diabetes, has been following the well-being diet recommended by a health counselor, with mixed-grain rice and vegetables, for three years.

examples.text: 또한 영양소를 균형 있게 섭취하고 있으며 유기농 식품으로만 요리하고 있습니다.

examples.translation: bakyeongcheol ssineun gyesok pirohago tto sohwaga an dwaeseo sohwajereul yuk gaewolgan bogyonghadaga byeongwone gatseumnida. — Mr. Park Hyeongcheol went to a hospital after taking digestive medicine for six months because he was constantly tired and also could not digest.

examples.translation: jinchareul badanneunde byeongmyeongeun wiamieotseumnida. — He had an examination and the name of the illness was stomach cancer.

examples.text: 위암 수술을 받은 후 박형철 씨는 제일 먼저 술과 담배에서 벗어나기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning, and the book’s parenthesized forms such as ~하다 and ~되다 show how a noun forms a verb. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section and the end-of-book Glossary are blank or alphabetical lists of words already given.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (80세 → 팔십 세; 200칼로리 → 이백 칼로리; YMCA → 와이엠시에이; the phone number in 문의 is spelled out and its hyphens read 에; 단백질(protein) is just 단백질).

explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify healthy eating and lifestyle habits; discuss living a healthy, long life; and give and receive advice about health and nutrition.

lessons.title: 415. Ch 33 · What the chapter teaches, 국 (國) 립 (立) · 점 (點) 수 (數)
lessons.subtitle: 한국의 교육 · 국립 · 공립 · 사립 · 점수 · 만점 · 영점

explanations.title: What Chapter 33 teaches (한국의 교육)
explanations.body:
Chapter 33, “Education in Korea”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and discuss the Korean school system, academic subjects, and a typical student’s daily routine; and talk about common concerns of students in Korea.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; –도록 (up to the point; until; in order to; so that); –느라(고) (because of; due to); repeated question words; –게 되다 (to become; to come to; to turn out); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 국립 (國立) and 점수 (點數).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 국립 (國立)
explanations.body:
This Sino-Korean word means nationally run, nationally established, or simply national. So any institution or organization run by a nation can use this word, as in 국립 도서관 (a national library), 국립 대학교 (a national university), and 국립 박물관 (a national museum). As you have seen in words like 한국, 미국, 중국, and 영국, the first syllable 국 (國) means country, nation, or kingdom. The second syllable 립 (立) means establish(ed), erect(ed), or standing, as in 도립 병원 (a provincial hospital; “province-established hospital”) and 시립 도서관 (a municipal library; “city-established library”). When 립 (立) comes at the beginning of a word, the syllable changes to 입 (立), as in 입석 (standing room; room for standing). Thus the literal meaning of the word 국립 is “nationally established” or “nationally erected”. 력 (力) means power and 공 (公) means public or official.

The book asks you to guess the meaning of 국기, 국력, 출국, 사립 중학교, 공립 고등학교 and 주립 대학교 (my answers are in the second table).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 점수 (點數)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means a grade, point, mark, or score. The first syllable 점 (點) means point or spot, as in 학점 (G.P.A.; school grades; a credit), 흑점 (a sunspot; a spot on the sun; “black spot”), 만점 (perfect score; full marks; “full mark”), 영점 (zero; zero point), and 오점 (a blot; a blotch; “dirty spot”). The second syllable 수 (數) means number, as in 다수 (many; a large number; a majority; “many numbers”), 소수 (a small number; a minority; a few; “few numbers”), 수학 (mathematics; “study of numbers”), and 수치 (numerical value). Thus the literal meaning of the word 점수 is “number of points”.

The matches (mine; the English is the book’s glosses):

explanations.title: Vocabulary Learning Strategy: use new Korean acronyms
explanations.body: An acronym is a word formed from the initial letters of a set of words, as in FAQ, NYPD, NATO and PIN. A typical Korean acronym consists of the first syllables of a set of words, as in 남고 (남자 고등학교) and 외고 (외국어 고등학교). Occasionally an acronym consists of a combination of the first syllables and the last syllable, as in 자판기 (자동 판매기). explanations.title: The book’s diagram of the system
explanations.body: The book adds a diagram, in this order from the bottom: 유치원 → 초등학교 → 중학교 → 고등학교 (인문계, 실업계) → 2년제 대학 or 4년제 대학교 → 대학원. (The picture itself is left out.)

explanations.title: 한국에서는: the school year and the high schools
explanations.body:
The Korean academic school year begins with the spring semester (1학기) in March. The second semester (2학기) starts in late August and ends in mid-February. Korean schools have a summer break (여름방학) from mid-July to late August, and a longer winter break (겨울방학) from late December to early February. A brief spring break (봄방학) falls between mid-February and the beginning of March. The academic calendar is generally standardized nationwide, but it may vary slightly from region to region.

Korea has three different types of high schools. 인문계 고등학교 (일반 고등학교 or 일반고) does not specialize in a field, and is more focused on students headed for college. 실업계 고등학교 (실업고) is vocational high school, where students specialize in fields such as technology, agriculture, or finance. 실업고 students usually look for jobs directly after graduation. The third type of school, 특수 목적 고등학교 (특목고), can be divided into specialty tracks that align with a student’s interests and career path. Science high schools (과학 고등학교 or 과고), foreign language high schools (외국어 고등학교 or 외고), and art specialty high schools (예술 고등학교 or 예고) belong to 특목고 and are known for their highly competitive entrance exams.

explanations.title: 북한에서는: education in North Korea
explanations.body: Education in North Korea is strictly controlled by the government. Mandatory education (의무교육) lasts 12 years, and encompasses one year of upper kindergarten, five years of primary education, and six years of secondary education (equivalent to middle and high school in the US). Higher education is not mandatory in North Korea, and it includes three types of institutions: universities (대학교), vocational schools (전문학교), and technical schools (기술학교). Two notable universities in North Korea are the Kim Il-Sung University and Pyongyang University of Science and Technology, both located in Pyongyang.

explanations.title: Topic B: Jeonghyeon became a middle schooler this March (정현이는 올 3월에 중학생이 되었습니다)
explanations.body: The following text is about the weekday routine of a freshman in middle school. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the times and numbers are spelled out in Hangul.)

examples.text: 정현이의 학교는 여덟 시 반에 시작합니다.
examples.translation: jeonghyeoniui hakgyoneun yeodeol si bane sijakamnida. — Jeonghyeon’s school starts at half past eight.

examples.text: 정현이는 보통 아침 일곱 시쯤에 일어나 아침을 먹고 여덟 시쯤 학교에 갑니다.
examples.translation: jeonghyeonineun botong achim ilgop sijjeume ireona achimeul meokgo yeodeol sijjeum hakgyoe gamnida. — Jeonghyeon usually gets up at around seven in the morning, eats breakfast and goes to school at around eight.

examples.text: 수업은 오전에 네 시간, 오후에 두 시간 있습니다.
examples.translation: sueobeun ojeone ne sigan, ohue du sigan itseumnida. — There are four hours of classes in the morning and two hours in the afternoon.

examples.text: 점심 시간은 사 교시 수업 후에 있습니다.
examples.translation: jeomsim siganeun sa gyosi sueop hue itseumnida. — Lunch time is after the fourth-period class.

examples.text: 정현이 학교는 급식을 하지 않기 때문에 정현이는 도시락을 먹습니다.
examples.translation: jeonghyeoni hakgyoneun geupsigeul haji anki ttaemune jeonghyeonineun dosirageul meokseumnida. — Jeonghyeon’s school does not provide school meals, so Jeonghyeon eats a lunch box.

examples.text: 정현이는 여러 가지 과목 중 영어를 제일 좋아합니다.
examples.translation: jeonghyeonineun yeoreo gaji gwamok jung yeongeoreul jeil joahamnida. — Among the various subjects, Jeonghyeon likes English best.

examples.text: 그래서 매주 금요일 육 교시 특별활동 시간에는 영어웅변반에서 활동을 합니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo maeju geumyoil yuk gyosi teukbyeolhwaldong siganeneun yeongeoungbyeonbaneseo hwaldongeul hamnida. — So during the sixth-period special activity time every Friday, he does activities in the English speech club.

examples.text: 방과 후에는 곧장 학원에 가서 수학과 한문을 더 배웁니다.
examples.translation: banggwa hueneun gotjang hagwone gaseo suhakgwa hanmuneul deo baeumnida. — After class he goes straight to a private academy and learns more math and Chinese characters.

examples.text: 그리고 저녁 여섯 시쯤 집에 돌아와 저녁을 먹습니다.
examples.translation: geurigo jeonyeok yeoseot sijjeum jibe dorawa jeonyeogeul meokseumnida. — And at around six in the evening he returns home and eats dinner.

examples.text: 저녁 식사를 한 후에는 보통 두 시간 동안 숙제를 하고 컴퓨터를 하거나 가족과 함께 텔레비전을 봅니다.
examples.translation: jeonyeok siksareul han hueneun botong du sigan dongan sukjereul hago keompyuteoreul hageona gajokgwa hamkke tellebijeoneul bomnida. — After dinner he usually does homework for two hours and uses the computer or watches television with his family.

examples.text: 그러나 다음 주에 교내 영어 웅변 대회가 있기 때문에 요즘에는 매일 저녁 웅변 대회 연습을 합니다.
examples.translation: geureona daeum jue gyonae yeongeo ungbyeon daehoega itgi ttaemune yojeumeneun maeil jeonyeok ungbyeon daehoe yeonseubeul hamnida. — But because there is an English speech contest at school next week, these days he practices for the speech contest every evening.

examples.text: 어제는 밤새도록 연습하느라 늦잠을 잤습니다.
examples.translation: eojeneun bamsaedorok yeonseupaneura neutjameul jatseumnida. — Yesterday he overslept because he practiced all night long.

examples.text: 그래서 오늘 아침에는 지각을 해서 담임선생님에게 야단을 맞았습니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo oneul achimeneun jigageul haeseo damimseonsaengnimege yadaneul majatseumnida. — So this morning he was late and was scolded by his homeroom teacher.

examples.text: 그렇지만 영어 선생님께서 실력이 많이 늘었다고 칭찬해 주셨습니다.
examples.translation: geureochiman yeongeo seonsaengnimkkeseo sillyeogi mani neureotdago chingchanhae jusyeotseumnida. — But the English teacher praised him, saying that his skills had improved a lot.

explanations.title: 정현이의 1학년 3반 시간표 (Jeonghyeon’s timetable)
explanations.body: The book gives Jeonghyeon’s weekly timetable (the periods, 월 to 토); the “-” marks the two Saturday periods that are blank in the book.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: classes and homerooms
explanations.body: In the U.S., middle school and high school students usually move to different classrooms for each subject. In Korea, students move to different classrooms only for classes like music, art, science, and physical education. Otherwise, students stay in their homeroom and the teachers move. Teachers share a big office called a 교무실. Each section (of a class) has 20 to 30 students, and the sections are usually identified by numbers. For example, if a new class has 120 students and four sections, the sections are called 1–1반 (1학년 1반), 1–2반 (1학년 2반), 1–3반 (1학년 3반), and 1–4반 (1학년 4반). Each section has a student representative called 반장, who is generally elected by fellow classmates and has high grades. Each section also has a teacher called 담임 선생님 who is assigned to the section for the entire academic year.

The graphs are pictures and are left out; the article is below, with the percentages and numbers spelled out in Hangul. The English is mine.

examples.text: 한국 케이블방송은 전국 중학생 천 명을 대상으로 방과 후 활동을 조사하여 결과를 발표했다.
examples.translation: hanguk keibeulbangsongeun jeonguk junghaksaeng cheon myeongeul daesangeuro banggwa hu hwaldongeul josahayeo gyeolgwareul balpyohaetda. — A Korean cable broadcaster surveyed one thousand middle school students nationwide on after-school activities and announced the results.

examples.text: 조사 결과를 보면, 중학생들이 방과 후에 하는 일은 고등학교 입학시험 준비를 위한 학원수업이 팔십오 퍼센트, 운동이나 악기 등 특기활동이 오십오 퍼센트, 교회 등 종교활동이 십삼 퍼센트인 것으로 나타났다.
examples.translation: josa gyeolgwareul bomyeon, junghaksaengdeuri banggwa hue haneun ireun godeunghakgyo ipaksiheom junbireul wihan hagwonsueobi palsibo peosenteu, undongina akgi deung teukgihwaldongi osibo peosenteu, gyohoe deung jonggyohwaldongi sipsam peosenteuin geoseuro natanatda. — According to the results, what middle school students do after school is: private academy classes for preparing for high school entrance exams, 85%; talent activities such as sports or musical instruments, 55%; and religious activities such as church, 13%.

examples.text: 방과 후 학원수업을 받는다고 대답한 학생들의 하루 평균 학원수업 시간은 두 시간 오십오 분으로 나타났다.
examples.translation: banggwa hu hagwonsueobeul banneundago daedapan haksaengdeurui haru pyeonggyun hagwonsueop siganeun du sigan osibo buneuro natanatda. — For the students who answered that they take academy classes after school, the average daily academy class time was two hours and fifty-five minutes.

examples.text: 학원수업 과목은 영어 구십 퍼센트, 수학 칠십오 퍼센트, 과학 육십오 퍼센트, 국어 오십 퍼센트, 사회 사십 퍼센트였고, 학생 일 인당 평균 삼 점 육 과목의 수업을 듣는 것으로 조사됐다.
examples.translation: hagwonsueop gwamogeun yeongeo gusip peosenteu, suhak chilsibo peosenteu, gwahak yuksibo peosenteu, gugeo osip peosenteu, sahoe sasip peosenteuyeotgo, haksaeng il indang pyeonggyun sam jeom yuk gwamogui sueobeul deunneun geoseuro josadwaetda. — The academy class subjects were English 90%, math 75%, science 65%, Korean 50% and social studies 40%, and it was found that each student takes an average of 3.6 subjects.
