lessons.title: 419. Ch 33 · Grammar A: the conjunctive ending –도록, up to the point; until; so that
lessons.subtitle: -도록 · 배가 터지도록 · 밤새도록 · 늦지 않도록 · 갈 수 있도록 · -도록 하다

explanations.title: –도록: “(up) to the point” or “until”
explanations.body: The conjunctive ending –도록 literally means “(up) to the point” or “until”, as in 배가 터지도록 (to the point that the stomach explodes) and 손이 아프도록 (to the point that the hands hurt). Thus, the conjunctive ending is similar to –(으)ㄹ 때까지 (until), as in 배가 터질 때까지 (until the stomach explodes) and 손이 아플 때까지 (until the hands hurt). However, –도록 is often used to exaggerate a situation or to say something figuratively. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 우리는 배가 터지도록 먹었어요.
examples.translation: urineun baega teojidorok meogeosseoyo. — We ate “to the point that our stomachs exploded.” / We ate a lot. (intended meaning)

examples.text: 밤새도록 친구와 이야기했어요.
examples.translation: bamsaedorok chinguwa iyagihaesseoyo. — I talked with my friend “up to the point that the night broke.” / I talked with my friend all night long. (intended meaning)

explanations.title: –도록: “in order to”, “so as to”, “so that”
explanations.body: The conjunctive ending –도록 can also be used to mean in order to, so as to, or so that. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 대학에 갈 수 있도록 열심히 공부하겠습니다.
examples.translation: daehage gal su itdorok yeolsimhi gongbuhagetseumnida. — I will study hard “up to the point that I can go to college” or so that I can go to college.

examples.text: 회의에 늦지 않도록 일찍 오세요.
examples.translation: hoeuie neutji antorok iljjik oseyo. — Come early “up to the point that you won’t be late for the meeting” or so as to not be late for the meeting.

explanations.title: –도록 하다: “make sure”
explanations.body: –도록 하다, in which –도록 is immediately followed by 하다, is used to mean make sure or ensure. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 교실에서는 한국말만 하도록 하세요.
examples.translation: gyosireseoneun hangungmalman hadorok haseyo. — Make sure to speak Korean only in the classroom.

examples.text: 집에 가기 전에 전화하도록 할게요.
examples.translation: jibe gagi jeone jeonhwahadorok halgeyo. — I’ll make sure to call you before going home.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Verb or adjective stem + 도록 (negative: –지 않도록).

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading, speaking and listening): the model
explanations.body: In pairs, Partner A takes a card from Set A and conjugates the verb with –도록, and Partner B reads a text from Set B that logically connects. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 밤이 늦도록
examples.translation: ga: bami neutdorok — Until late at night,

examples.text: 나: 파티하고 놀았어요.
examples.translation: na: patihago norasseoyo. — I partied and played.

explanations.body: The word cards (Sets A and B) and Follow-up 2 (listening to four dialogs and marking the meaning of –도록) need cards, audio and classmates.

lessons.title: 420. Ch 33 · Grammar B: expressing a reason, –느라(고)
lessons.subtitle: -느라(고) · 도와드리느라 · 이야기하느라 · 공부하느라 · 수고하다 · 고생하다

explanations.title: –느라(고): because (of)
explanations.body: The conjunctive ending –느라(고), which translates as “because (of)”, is used to justify or explain away a negative or unpleasant consequence caused by the speaker’s own action. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 어제 저녁에 어머니를 도와드리느라 숙제를 못 했어요.
examples.translation: eoje jeonyeoge eomeonireul dowadeurineura sukjereul mot haesseoyo. — I couldn’t do my homework because I was helping my mother last night.

explanations.title: Three grammatical restrictions
explanations.body:
However, when using –느라(고) several grammatical restrictions apply:

1. Only action verbs can be attached to –느라(고).
2. The subject of the –느라(고) clause and the main clause that follows it must be the same.
3. The verb in the main clause cannot be a command or suggestion.

For example, the following sentences are grammatically incorrect (the book marks them with *): *배가 고프느라고 밥을 먹었어요. (a stative verb); *차 일병이 샤워하느라고 신 이병이 전화 소리를 못 들었어요. (different subjects); *기침을 많이 하느라고 병원에 가 보세요. (a command; an imperative).

explanations.title: Appreciation or praise
explanations.body: –느라(고) expresses the speaker’s appreciation or praise when it is used with the verbs in the main clause 수고하다 (to give oneself trouble; to take the trouble), 고생하다 (to have difficulty), and 애쓰다 (to endeavor; to strive; to take pains). (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 밤늦게까지 공부하느라고 수고했다.
examples.translation: bamneutgekkaji gongbuhaneurago sugohaetda. — You took the trouble to study until late night. (I praise you!)

examples.text: 아버지, 그 동안 저희들을 위해 일하시느라고 고생 많이 하셨어요.
examples.translation: abeoji, geu dongan jeohuideureul wihae ilhasineurago gosaeng mani hasyeosseoyo. — Father, you have taken pains working for us so far. (We appreciate you a lot!)

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Action verb stem + 느라(고) (an ㄹ-final stem drops the ㄹ: 놀다 → 노느라고; ㅂ-irregular 돕다 keeps the ㅂ: 돕느라고).

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading, speaking and listening): reason and consequence
explanations.body: The book gives six reason clauses (친구하고 놉니다; 텔레비전을 봅니다; 샤워를 합니다; 비디오 게임을 합니다; 숙제를 합니다; 한국어 공부를 합니다) to be matched with six consequences (점심을 못 먹었어요; 다른 취미활동을 못 해요; 숙제를 못 했어요; 전화를 못 받았어요; 늦게 잤어요; 체육관에 못 가요); the first match is given in the book and the answers may vary. One set of matches (mine):

rows: 텔레비전을 보느라 다른 취미활동을 못 해요.
비디오 게임을 하느라 숙제를 못 했어요.
한국어 공부를 하느라 체육관에 못 가요.

explanations.title: Topic C: I decided to take the foreign-language high school entrance exam (외고 입시 보기로 했어)
explanations.body: Two middle school students are talking on the phone about their concerns. (The English is mine; the book gives none; 8등 is spelled out.)

examples.text: 지훈: 연아야, 나 외고 입시 보기로 했어.
examples.translation: jihun: yeonaya, na oego ipsi bogiro haesseo. — Yeona, I decided to take the foreign-language high school entrance exam.

examples.text: 연아: 그래? 부모님은 어떻게 생각하셔?
examples.translation: yeona: geurae? bumonimeun eotteoke saenggakasyeo? — Really? What do your parents think?

examples.text: 지훈: 내 의견에 찬성하셔. 그래서 다음 주부터 과외받게 될 거야.
examples.translation: jihun: nae uigyeone chanseonghasyeo. geuraeseo daeum jubuteo gwaoebatge doel geoya. — They agree with my opinion. So from next week I’ll end up getting private lessons.

examples.text: 연아: 그럼 이제 바빠지겠구나. 넌 성적이 좋아서 시험만 잘 보면 합격할 거야.
examples.translation: yeona: geureom ije bappajigetguna. neon seongjeogi joaseo siheomman jal bomyeon hapgyeokal geoya. — Then you’ll get busy now. Your grades are good, so if you just do well on the exam you’ll pass.

examples.text: 지훈: 넌 어때?
examples.translation: jihun: neon eottae? — How about you?

examples.text: 연아: 네가 부럽다. 난 기말 시험 성적 때문에 속상해.
examples.translation: yeona: nega bureopda. nan gimal siheom seongjeok ttaemune soksanghae. — I envy you. I’m upset because of my final exam grades.

examples.text: 지훈: 왜? 등수가 떨어졌어?
examples.translation: jihun: wae? deungsuga tteoreojeosseo? — Why? Did your rank drop?

examples.text: 연아: 응, 중간 시험 때보다 팔 등이나 떨어졌어. 그리고 수학 점수는 정말 나빠.
examples.translation: yeona: eung, junggan siheom ttaeboda pal deungina tteoreojeosseo. geurigo suhak jeomsuneun jeongmal nappa. — Yes, it dropped by as many as eight places from the midterm. And my math score is really bad.

examples.text: 지훈: 그럼, 학원에 다녀 봐. 학원에 다니면 성적이 좀 오를 거야.
examples.translation: jihun: geureom, hagwone danyeo bwa. hagwone danimyeon seongjeogi jom oreul geoya. — Then try going to an academy. If you go to an academy, your grades will go up a bit.

examples.text: 연아: 그래서 학원을 알아보는 중이야. 너는 학원 어디 어디를 다녔니?
examples.translation: yeona: geuraeseo hagwoneul araboneun jungiya. neoneun hagwon eodi eodireul danyeonni? — That’s why I’m looking into academies. Which academies did you go to?

examples.text: 지훈: 나는 우리 동네에 있는 대성학원하고 고려학원을 다녔어.
examples.translation: jihun: naneun uri dongnee inneun daeseonghagwonhago goryeohagwoneul danyeosseo. — I went to Daesung Academy and Goryeo Academy in our neighborhood.

explanations.title: The book’s footnote
explanations.body: 외고 입시 is an example of a Korean acronym. It stands for 외국어 고등학교 입학 시험 (an entrance examination for a foreign language high school).

explanations.title: 한국에서는: school districts (학군)
explanations.body: 학군 (school district) is very important in Korea. In most cities, students are assigned by lottery to a high school in their school district. Some school districts are ranked higher than others in student success on college entrance exams. Many parents seek out these better school districts for their children.

explanations.title: Repeated question words
explanations.body: Recall the question words you learned in earlier chapters: 누구, 언제, 어디, 무엇, 무슨, and 어떤. These question words can be repeated, as in 누구 누구를 만났어요? (Who did you meet?) and 어디 어디에서 쇼핑했어요? (Where did you do shopping?). These repeated question words elicit information specific to multiple objects (persons, things, places, times, dates, etc.).

explanations.title: A conversation between two high school friends
explanations.body: Speaker B repeats 누구 in his question to elicit the specific names of the high school friends Speaker A met. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 가: 어제 파티에서 고등학교 친구들을 만났어.

examples.text: 나: 그래? 누구 누구를 만났어?
examples.translation: na: geurae? nugu nugureul mannasseo? — “Who and who” did you see? Who are they? / Which ones did you see?

examples.text: 가: 이기덕, 최대용하고 신창민.
examples.translation: ga: igideok, choedaeyonghago sinchangmin. — (They are) Lee Kideok, Choi Daeyong, and Shin Changmin.

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: Here are more example sentences where question words repeat. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.translation: teniseu chireo eonje eonje gayo? — “When and when” do you go to play tennis?

examples.translation: baekwajeomeseo mwo mwo sasseoyo? — “What and what” / What (multiple objects) did you buy at the department store?

lessons.title: 423. Ch 33 · Grammar D: –게 되다, to come to; to get to; to turn out
lessons.subtitle: -게 되다 · 걷게 되었어요 · 유학가게 되었습니다 · 좋아하게 되었습니다 · 결혼하게 되었어요 · ~이/가 되다 · -아/어지다

explanations.title: Review: ~이/가 되다 and –아/어지다
explanations.body: In earlier chapters you learned how to express a change in state or condition by using ~이/가 되다 and –아/어지다, both of which mean “to become”. Note that ~이/가 되다 is preceded by a noun, and –아/어지다 is preceded by a stative verb. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 오바마가 미국 대통령이 되었어요.
examples.translation: obamaga miguk daetongnyeongi doeeosseoyo. — Obama became the U.S. President.

examples.text: 건강해졌어요.
examples.translation: geonganghaejeosseoyo. — I became healthier.

explanations.title: –게 되다: to come to; to get to; to turn out
explanations.body: In this lesson you will learn about another grammar feature used to express a change in state or condition: –게 되다. This grammar feature works only with an action verb and means to come to, to get to, or to turn out. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 수술 후 다시 걷게 되었어요.
examples.translation: susul hu dasi geotge doeeosseoyo. — After surgery I got to walk again.

examples.text: 다음 달에 미국으로 유학가게 되었습니다.
examples.translation: daeum dare migugeuro yuhakgage doeeotseumnida. — I get to go to the U.S. to study next month.

examples.text: 한국 음악을 좋아하게 되었습니다.
examples.translation: hanguk eumageul joahage doeeotseumnida. — I came to like Korean music.

examples.text: 민 선생님께서 이번에 상을 받게 되셨어요.
examples.translation: min seonsaengnimkkeseo ibeone sangeul batge doesyeosseoyo. — It turns out that Mr. Min will receive an award this time.

examples.text: 스무 번의 맞선 끝에 결혼하게 되었어요.
examples.translation: seumu beonui matseon kkeute gyeolhonhage doeeosseoyo. — After twenty blind dates I got married.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Action verb stem + 게 되다 (past: 게 되었어요 / 게 됐어요).

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Speaking and listening): changes since coming to DLI
explanations.body: Think about changes in your life since you came to DLI, discuss them in pairs and present two of them. The book’s models (DLI is spelled out as 디엘아이; the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 디엘아이 온 후에 뭐가 달라졌어요?
examples.translation: ga: dierai on hue mwoga dallajeosseoyo? — What has changed since you came to DLI?

examples.text: 나: 네, 아침에 일찍 일어나게 되었어요. 그리고 매일 규칙적으로 운동도 하게 되었어요.
examples.translation: na: ne, achime iljjik ireonage doeeosseoyo. geurigo maeil gyuchikjeogeuro undongdo hage doeeosseoyo. — Yes, I came to get up early in the morning. And I also came to exercise regularly every day.

examples.text: 가: 최 일병은 디엘아이 온 후에 좋은 친구들을 많이 만나게 되었어요.
examples.translation: ga: choe ilbyeongeun dierai on hue joeun chingudeureul mani mannage doeeosseoyo. — Private First Class Choi has come to meet many good friends since coming to DLI.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Reading): a question on an education consultation website
explanations.body: The following text was posted on the Q&A section of an education consultation website by 지우 엄마 (Jiwoo’s mother). The book asks you to circle –게 되다 and translate the sentences that contain it into English (the sentences with 게 되었어요 are the first and the fourth). The ellipsis is dropped; the English is mine.

examples.text: 우리 딸 지우가 이번에 외국어 고등학교에 입학하게 되었어요.
examples.translation: uri ttal jiuga ibeone oegugeo godeunghakgyoe ipakage doeeosseoyo. — My daughter Jiwoo has come to enter a foreign language high school this time.

examples.text: 주위에서 여러 가지 준비해야 할 것이 많다고 하는데 어떻게 해야 할지 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.translation: juwieseo yeoreo gaji junbihaeya hal geosi mantago haneunde eotteoke haeya halji jal moreugesseoyo. — People around me say there are many things to prepare, but I don’t know what to do.

examples.text: 사실 우리 지우는 어릴 때는 영어를 별로 안 좋아했어요.
examples.translation: sasil uri jiuneun eoril ttaeneun yeongeoreul byeollo an joahaesseoyo. — Actually, when Jiwoo was little she didn’t like English very much.

examples.text: 근데, 미국에 있는 이모 집에 갔다 온 후부터 영어를 아주 좋아하게 되었어요.
examples.translation: geunde, miguge inneun imo jibe gatda on hubuteo yeongeoreul aju joahage doeeosseoyo. — But since she went to her aunt’s house in America and came back, she has come to like English a lot.

examples.text: 중학교 때는 학교 수업을 열심히 준비하고 집에서는 영어 비디오를 많이 보여 주었어요.
examples.translation: junghakgyo ttaeneun hakgyo sueobeul yeolsimhi junbihago jibeseoneun yeongeo bidioreul mani boyeo jueosseoyo. — In middle school she prepared for school classes diligently, and at home I showed her many English videos.

examples.text: 고등학교에 가면 좀 다르게 공부를 시켜야 할 것 같은데 어떻게 하면 좋을까요?
examples.translation: godeunghakgyoe gamyeon jom dareuge gongbureul sikyeoya hal geot gateunde eotteoke hamyeon joeulkkayo? — When she goes to high school, I think I need to have her study a bit differently, but what would be good?

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking and listening): experiences with the Korean language and culture
explanations.body: You share changes related to Korean grammar, Korean food and Korean products using –게 되다. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 박 일병은 김치를 좋아합니까?

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): an article posted by a Sadang Middle School student
explanations.body: The following article was posted by a student at Sa-dang Middle School. It introduces the “special activities” (extracurricular activities) at her school. The book glosses 공예: craft; 발표하다: to present. The text is the book’s with the time spelled out in Hangul; the English is mine.

examples.text: 안녕하세요?
examples.translation: annyeonghaseyo? — Hello.

examples.text: 오늘은 사당중학교의 특별활동반특활반에 대해 소개해 드리겠습니다.
examples.translation: oneureun sadangjunghakgyoui teukbyeolhwaldongbanteukwalbane daehae sogaehae deurigetseumnida. — Today I will introduce the special activity clubs of Sadang Middle School.

examples.text: 매월 첫째, 셋째 금요일오후 한 시 이십 분부터 세 시 삼십 분까지에 학생들은 자신들이 선택한 특별활동반에서 시간을 보냅니다.
examples.translation: maewol cheotjjae, setjjae geumyoirohu han si isip bunbuteo se si samsip bunkkajie haksaengdeureun jasindeuri seontaekan teukbyeolhwaldongbaneseo siganeul bonaemnida. — On the first and third Friday of every month (from 1:20 to 3:30 p.m.), students spend time in the special activity club they have chosen.

examples.text: 특활반으로는 연극반, 무용반, 미술반, 공예반, 외국어반, 음악반이 있습니다.
examples.translation: teukwalbaneuroneun yeongeukban, muyongban, misulban, gongyeban, oegugeoban, eumakbani itseumnida. — The special activity clubs include a drama club, a dance club, an art club, a craft club, a foreign language club and a music club.

examples.text: 이 중에 가장 인기 있는 반은 영어반과 음악반입니다.
examples.translation: i junge gajang ingi inneun baneun yeongeobangwa eumakbanimnida. — Among these, the most popular clubs are the English club and the music club.

examples.text: 영어반에서는 학생들이 영어웅변을 배우거나 영어연극을 연습합니다.
examples.translation: yeongeobaneseoneun haksaengdeuri yeongeoungbyeoneul baeugeona yeongeoyeongeugeul yeonseupamnida. — In the English club, students learn English speeches or practice English plays.

examples.text: 음악반에서는 학생들이 원하는 악기를 하나씩 배울 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: eumakbaneseoneun haksaengdeuri wonhaneun akgireul hanassik baeul su itseumnida. — In the music club, students can learn one instrument each, the one they want.

examples.text: 원하면 악기 대신 노래 부르기를 배울 수도 있습니다.
examples.translation: wonhamyeon akgi daesin norae bureugireul baeul sudo itseumnida. — If they want, they can also learn singing instead of an instrument.

examples.text: 학기말에는 학생들이 특활반에서 배운 것을 발표합니다.
examples.translation: hakgimareneun haksaengdeuri teukwalbaneseo baeun geoseul balpyohamnida. — At the end of the semester, students present what they learned in the clubs.

examples.text: 이 발표회에는 부모님들도 초대됩니다.
examples.translation: i balpyohoeeneun bumonimdeuldo chodaedoemnida. — Parents are also invited to this presentation.

explanations.title: The book’s three questions, answered (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the answers blank; these are mine.

rows: 1. When are the extracurricular activities held?
On the first and third Friday of every month, from 1:20 to 3:30 p.m.
2. What can students do during the music class?
Learn one instrument each, or learn singing instead
3. What do students do at the end of a semester?
Present what they learned; parents are invited to the presentation

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): a Q&A about a college entrance exam
explanations.body: The book shows a Q&A on a website’s “worry Q&A > entrance exam counseling > college entrance exam” page. The question was posted by a third-year high school student whose user name and the date and view count are left out; 고3 is spelled out as 고삼. The book glosses 수능 (수학능력시험): the college entrance exam, Korean SAT. The question and the answer (the English is mine):

examples.text: 저는 실업계에 다니는 고삼 학생입니다.
examples.translation: jeoneun sireopgyee danineun gosam haksaengimnida. — I am a third-year student in a vocational high school.

examples.text: 실업계 학생이지만 대학에 가고 싶습니다.
examples.translation: sireopgye haksaengijiman daehage gago sipseumnida. — I’m a vocational student, but I want to go to college.

examples.text: 성적은 좋은데, 국어, 영어, 수학이 약해서 수능 점수가 잘 안 나와요.
examples.translation: seongjeogeun joeunde, gugeo, yeongeo, suhagi yakaeseo suneung jeomsuga jal an nawayo. — My grades are good, but Korean, English and math are weak, so my college entrance exam score doesn’t come out well.

examples.text: 어떻게 공부해야 할까요?
examples.translation: eotteoke gongbuhaeya halkkayo? — How should I study?

examples.text: 우선 가고 싶은 대학을 빨리 결정하세요.
examples.translation: useon gago sipeun daehageul ppalli gyeoljeonghaseyo. — First, decide quickly which college you want to go to.

examples.text: 그리고 그 대학에 맞게 입시 준비를 하세요.
examples.translation: geurigo geu daehage matge ipsi junbireul haseyo. — And prepare for the entrance exam to suit that college.

examples.text: 시험 점수보다 학교 성적을 더 중요하게 생각하는 대학도 많이 있어요.
examples.translation: siheom jeomsuboda hakgyo seongjeogeul deo jungyohage saenggakaneun daehakdo mani isseoyo. — There are many colleges that consider school grades more important than exam scores.

examples.text: 수능 점수를 올리고 싶으면 입시 학원에 다니세요.
examples.translation: suneung jeomsureul olligo sipeumyeon ipsi hagwone daniseyo. — If you want to raise your exam score, go to an entrance exam academy.

examples.text: 국, 영, 수는 혼자 공부하기 힘든 과목이니까요.
examples.translation: guk, yeong, suneun honja gongbuhagi himdeun gwamoginikkayo. — Because Korean, English and math are subjects that are hard to study alone.

examples.text: 저도 실업계 고등학교를 졸업하고 대학에 들어 왔어요.
examples.translation: jeodo sireopgye godeunghakgyoreul joreopago daehage deureo wasseoyo. — I also graduated from a vocational high school and entered college.

examples.text: 꼭 가고 싶은 대학에 합격하기 바래요.
examples.translation: kkok gago sipeun daehage hapgyeokagi baraeyo. — I hope you pass the college you really want to go to.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book asks you to identify the poster’s biographical information, the concern and the type(s) of advice (ticking boxes: focus on improving GPA; decide first which college to attend; consider attending a private coaching institute; trust yourself and study wholeheartedly until the exam). My answers:

rows: A third-year student at a vocational high school who wants to go to college
Good grades but weak Korean, English and math, so the college entrance exam score is low
Decide first which college to attend; consider attending a private coaching institute (the other two boxes are not in the answer)

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (SMART Board), Activity 2 of the listening section (a clip from the TV drama 거침없이 하이킥 and the situation chosen) and Activity 4 (a teen hotline, with two callers heard and advice written in two groups) need audio, video and classmates.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning, and the book’s parenthesized forms such as ~하다 and ~되다 show how a noun forms a verb. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (1학년 → 일 학년; 9년 → 구 년; 100점 → 백 점; 고3 → 고삼).

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify and discuss the Korean school system, academic subjects, and a typical student’s daily routine; and talk about common concerns of students in Korea.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; –도록 (up to the point; until; in order to; so that); –느라(고) (because of; due to); repeated question words; –게 되다 (to become; to come to; to turn out); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 국립 (國立) and 점수 (點數).

explanations.title: What Chapter 34 teaches (대학 생활)
explanations.body:
Chapter 34, “College Life”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and discuss academic majors and classes and other college-related activities like registration; identify and discuss aspects of college life, such as employment and common concerns; and discuss plans for after graduating from college.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; using double negatives for emphasis; ~말고/–지 말고 (do not … but); ~같이/처럼 and ~같은 (like); the conjunctive ending –(으)면 –(으)ㄹ수록; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 부전공 (副專攻), 교환 (交換), and 기간 (期間).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 부전공 (副專攻)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means a minor (academic subject). The first syllable 부 (副) literally means “come close (to the first)”, and it normally means secondary, vice-, assistant, deputy, or co- when it heads a title, as in 부학장 (an associate dean; an assistant dean), 부사장 (a vice-president [of a company]), 부사령관 (a deputy commander), 부조종사 (an assistant pilot; a co-pilot), 부팀장 (an assistant team leader), and 부반장 (an assistant class leader; an assistant section leader). The word 전공 itself means a major (academic subject) or specialty. The second syllable 전 (專) means only or exclusive(ly), as in 버스 전용차선 (bus-only lane), 전문가 (an expert; a specialist), and 전매 (monopoly; “exclusive [ownership on] sale”). The last syllable 공 (攻) means hit or attack, as in 공격 (an attack; offense), 공방전 (offensive and defensive battle), 침공 (an invasion [of another country]; “invasion and attack”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 부전공 is “secondary major”, and the word refers to a secondary focus of a bachelor’s degree.

rows: an associate dean; an assistant dean
an assistant class leader; an assistant section leader
an invasion (of another country); “invasion and attack”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 교환 (交換)
explanations.body:
This Sino-Korean word means exchange, swap, or barter. The shape of the Chinese character 交 (교) depicts a person walking (with the purpose of interacting with other people). Thus, the underlying meaning is interaction (among people), and the syllable can be translated as exchange, interchange, intersect, or interact, as in 교제 (dating; going out; “interact and meet”), 교배 (crossbreeding; “interact and mate”), 교통 (traffic; “exchange of moving”), 교우 (making friends; “interact with a friend”), and 교신 (exchange of messages; communication; correspondence). The syllable 환 (換) means exchange, as in 환기 (ventilation; “exchange of air”), 환율 (exchange rate), 환전 (money exchanging; exchange of money), and 환풍기 (a ventilation fan; “exchange-of-wind machine”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 교환 is “interact and exchange”, and the word refers to the act of giving or taking one thing in return for another.

The book asks you to guess the meaning of 교차로 and 환승역 (my answers: an intersection; a crossroads — and a transfer station).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 기간 (期間)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means the duration of time, the interval of time, or period, as in 한국에서는 겨울방학기간이 길어요 (The duration of a winter break is long in Korea). The first syllable 기 (期) means period of time or term, as in 학기 (a semester; a term; “school period”), 초기 (the early period; an early stage; “first period”), 말기 (the last period; the last stage; “last period”), and 정기 (a regular interval; a fixed time; a fixed period). The second syllable 간 (間) means gap, between, or distance, as in 부자간 (“between father and son”), 공간 (space; room; “air gap”), 시간 (time; “time gap”), and 야간 (night; nighttime; “night gap”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 기간 is “duration gap” or “interval gap”.

explanations.title: Topic A: Did you sign up for classes? (수강신청 했어?)
explanations.body: The following text is about Mijin’s plans for first-year college classes. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the numbers are spelled out in Hangul.)

examples.text: 미진 씨는 한국대학교 학생입니다.
examples.translation: mijin ssineun hangukdaehakgyo haksaengimnida. — Mijin is a student at Hanguk University.

examples.text: 일 년 동안 재수를 하고 올해 드디어 대학교에 입학했습니다.
examples.translation: il nyeon dongan jaesureul hago olhae deudieo daehakgyoe ipakaetseumnida. — After studying again for a year, she has finally entered university this year.

examples.text: 미진 씨의 전공은 영문학입니다.
examples.translation: mijin ssiui jeongongeun yeongmunhagimnida. — Mijin’s major is English literature.

examples.text: 이 학년이 되면 부전공이나 복수전공으로 신문방송학도 공부할 계획입니다.
examples.translation: i hangnyeoni doemyeon bujeongongina boksujeongongeuro sinmunbangsonghakdo gongbuhal gyehoegimnida. — When she becomes a sophomore, she plans to study journalism too as a minor or a double major.

examples.text: 이번 봄 학기에는 심리학이나 교육학 같은 교양과목을 많이 수강하려고 합니다.
examples.translation: ibeon bom hakgieneun simnihagina gyoyukak gateun gyoyanggwamogeul mani sugangharyeogo hamnida. — This spring semester, she intends to take many elective courses such as psychology or education.

examples.text: 매일 저녁 아르바이트를 해야 하기 때문에 많은 학점을 들을 수 없습니다.
examples.translation: maeil jeonyeok areubaiteureul haeya hagi ttaemune maneun hakjeomeul deureul su eopseumnida. — Because she has to work a part-time job every evening, she cannot take many credits.

examples.text: 그래서 십이 학점만 신청하려고 합니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo sibi hakjeomman sincheongharyeogo hamnida. — So she intends to sign up for only twelve credits.

examples.text: 미진 씨는 내일 신입생 환영회에 갑니다.
examples.translation: mijin ssineun naeil sinipsaeng hwanyeonghoee gamnida. — Mijin is going to the freshman welcome party tomorrow.

examples.text: 대학교 사 년 동안 강의도 열심히 듣고 동아리 활동에도 부지런히 참여할 생각입니다.
examples.translation: daehakgyo sa nyeon dongan ganguido yeolsimhi deutgo dongari hwaldongedo bujireonhi chamyeohal saenggagimnida. — For her four years of university she plans to listen to lectures diligently and take part diligently in club activities too.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 재수 (studying again)
explanations.body: In Korea, when high school graduates are not admitted to the college or university to which they applied, many of them choose to spend another year taking additional college prep courses in order to get into the college or university to which they originally applied. This process is called 재수 (再修) and literally means “studying again”; the students who do this are called 재수생 (再修生).

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): which major fits each student’s interest?
explanations.body: The book gives six statements by high school seniors and seven majors (a. 컴퓨터공학; b. 국문학; c. 경영학; d. 영문학; e. 심리학; f. 건축공학; g. 경제학) and asks you to write the letter of the best major for each; one major has no match. The statements are the book’s (the book glosses 소설: novel); the answers are mine (g, 경제학, is the one with no match).

rows: 저는 사람의 생각에 대해서 관심이 많아요. 무슨 생각으로 어떤 행동을 하는지 알고 싶어요.
저는 독서가 취미예요. 셰익스피어를 좋아해서 셰익스피어 책은 영어로 다 읽었어요. 나중에 영국으로 유학 가고 싶어요.
저는 여가시간을 주로 컴퓨터 게임을 하거나 프로그램을 만들면서 보내요.
저는 사람들이 이용하기 편한 건물을 디자인하고 싶어요. 또 세계에서 가장 아름다운 건물을 내 손으로 만들고 싶어요.
저는 나중에 큰 회사의 사장이 되고 싶습니다. 회사와 직원들을 잘 관리하는 방법에 대해 배우고 싶어요.
저는 우리나라의 문학을 좋아해요. 특히 소설에 관심이 많습니다. 우리나라의 소설에 대해 공부하고 싶어요.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): a news article on the popularity of college majors
explanations.body: The following news article is about the popularity of college majors in college entrance exams. The book asks two things: the overall trend in preferred majors (applicants for humanities; applicants for natural sciences) and a table of the first, second and third popular majors. The headline’s quotation marks and the “·” marks are dropped, and the numbers are spelled out in Hangul; the English is mine.

examples.text: 자연계열 취업 인기학과 인문계열 외국어 강세
examples.translation: jayeongyeyeol chwieop ingihakgwa inmungyeyeol oegugeo gangse — Natural sciences: popular departments for employment; humanities: foreign languages are strong

examples.text: 최근 삼 년간 주요 대학 모집에서 자연계열은 취업에 유리한 학과를, 인문계열은 외국어 관련학과를 선호하는 경향이 있다는 분석이 나왔다.
examples.translation: choegeun sam nyeongan juyo daehak mojibeseo jayeongyeyeoreun chwieobe yurihan hakgwareul, inmungyeyeoreun oegugeo gwallyeonhakgwareul seonhohaneun gyeonghyangi itdaneun bunseogi nawatda. — An analysis has come out that in admissions at major universities over the last three years, natural sciences applicants tend to prefer departments favorable for employment and humanities applicants tend to prefer foreign-language-related departments.

examples.text: 한 조사에 의하면 이천이십삼 학년도 대입 정시모집에서 서울지역 열 개 대학의 의학계열을 제외한 자연계열 선호학과를 분석한 결과, 컴퓨터 관련 학과가 일 위를 차지했다고 이십사 일 밝혔다.
examples.translation: han josae uihamyeon icheonisipsam hangnyeondo daeip jeongsimojibeseo seouljiyeok yeol gae daehagui uihakgyeyeoreul jeoehan jayeongyeyeol seonhohakgwareul bunseokan gyeolgwa, keompyuteo gwallyeon hakgwaga il wireul chajihaetdago isipsa il balkyeotda. — According to one survey, in analyzing the preferred natural sciences departments, excluding medical fields, at ten Seoul-area universities in the regular admissions for the 2023 academic year, computer-related departments took first place, it said on the 24th.

examples.text: 이어 반도체 관련 학과, 네 개, 십삼 점 삼 퍼센트, 인공지능, 세 개, 십 퍼센트 관련 학과 순이었다.
examples.translation: ieo bandoche gwallyeon hakgwa, ne gae, sipsam jeom sam peosenteu, ingongjineung, se gae, sip peosenteu gwallyeon hakgwa sunieotda. — They were followed by semiconductor-related departments (four, 13.3%) and artificial-intelligence-related departments (three, 10.0%) in that order.

examples.text: 인문계열은 최근 삼 년 연속 외국어 관련 학과가 최상위권을 차지한 것으로 나타났다.
examples.translation: inmungyeyeoreun choegeun sam nyeon yeonsok oegugeo gwallyeon hakgwaga choesangwigwoneul chajihan geoseuro natanatda. — In the humanities, foreign-language-related departments were found to have taken the top rank for three years in a row.

examples.text: 서울의 열한 개 대학의 이천이십삼 학년도 입시 경쟁률을 분석한 결과, 외국어 관련 학과가 서른네 개 인기학과 중 일곱 개, 이십 점 육 퍼센트로 일 위를 차지했고, 이어 사회과학, 여섯 개, 십칠 점 육 퍼센트, 경영, 다섯 개, 십사 점 칠 퍼센트 순이었다.
examples.translation: seourui yeolhan gae daehagui icheonisipsam hangnyeondo ipsi gyeongjaengnyureul bunseokan gyeolgwa, oegugeo gwallyeon hakgwaga seoreunne gae ingihakgwa jung ilgop gae, isip jeom yuk peosenteuro il wireul chajihaetgo, ieo sahoegwahak, yeoseot gae, sipchil jeom yuk peosenteu, gyeongyeong, daseot gae, sipsa jeom chil peosenteu sunieotda. — In analyzing the 2023 admissions competition rates of eleven universities in Seoul, foreign-language-related departments took first place with seven of the thirty-four popular departments (20.6%), followed by social sciences (six, 17.6%) and business (five, 14.7%) in that order.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the answers blank; these are mine.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading, speaking and writing): which classes shall I take this semester?
explanations.body: You work in Korea and decide to take classes at a local college near your workplace. Since you work during the day, you want to take night classes that provide nine credits. The book gives the first-semester general-education timetable (교양과목 강의시간표) and asks you to choose classes, fill in a registration form (수강신청서) with nine credits and ask three classmates about their plans. The class periods are: 9교시 18:00~18:45; 10교시 18:55~19:40; 11교시 19:50~20:35; 12교시 20:45~21:30. The timetable (course; department; credits; day and period; room):

explanations.title: Topic B: I’m coming back to school next semester (다음 학기에 복학해)
explanations.body: Two college students are discussing college life. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 소희: 어, 선배, 오랜만이에요.
examples.translation: sohui: eo, seonbae, oraenmanieyo. — Oh, senior, it’s been a while.

examples.text: 우진: 그래, 오랜만이다. 잘 지내?
examples.translation: ujin: geurae, oraenmanida. jal jinae? — Yeah, it’s been a while. How are you?

examples.text: 소희: 네. 언제 제대했어요?
examples.translation: sohui: ne. eonje jedaehaesseoyo? — Fine. When were you discharged?

examples.text: 우진: 응. 지난달에 제대해서 다음 학기에 복학해.
examples.translation: ujin: eung. jinandare jedaehaeseo daeum hakgie bokakae. — Yeah. I was discharged last month, so I’ll come back to school next semester.

examples.text: 소희: 그래요? 저는 다음 학기에 휴학해요. 아르바이트를 하면서 등록금을 벌려고요.
examples.translation: sohui: geuraeyo? jeoneun daeum hakgie hyuhakaeyo. areubaiteureul hamyeonseo deungnokgeumeul beollyeogoyo. — Is that so? I’m taking a leave of absence next semester. I’m going to earn my tuition while working part-time.

examples.text: 우진: 그래? 무슨 일을 하려고?

explanations.title: 한국에서는: college life, housing and concerns
explanations.body:
College freshmen participate in several major events in their first year. In February they usually attend a welcome meeting known as 신입생 환영회 or 신입생 오리엔테이션. At this meeting, freshmen learn about college life and meet with seniors and faculty members. Once they officially start college in March, they usually go on a school excursion called MT (membership training), which is designed to strengthen the bonds between students. They also participate in a campus festival (대학축제), either in mid-spring or autumn. Activities such as contests and concerts are offered during the campus festival.

When Korean students attend college near their parents’ home, they usually live with their parents and commute. However, when attending college away from home, students often must choose one of the following living arrangements: a boarding house (하숙집), a rented room (자취방), an on-campus dormitory (기숙사), or a home of their relatives (친척집). 하숙집 usually provides a private room and two meals, and 자취방 requires that students cook their own meals. 자취 is cheaper than 하숙. Students living at a boarding house are called 하숙생; students living in a rented room are called 자취생. Koreans refer to living at a boarding house as 하숙하다 and to living in a rented room as 자취하다.

Like most college students, Korean students have many concerns. Career path is the top concern (60.0%), followed by academic performance (25.2%), financial difficulties (9.5%), adaptation to university life (4.2%), and other (1.1%). Data in the chart reflect survey results of 28,247 respondents from 283 colleges in 2017.

explanations.body: The following Q&A about college life is posted on a website (지식 Q/A > 대학 > 대학 생활), titled 대학 신입생이 됩니다 (I’m becoming a college freshman), by user freshman12 (the date and view count are left out). lessons.title: 431. Ch 34 · Grammar A: emphasis using double negatives, ~이/가 없다
lessons.subtitle: 이중부정 · 없는 물건이 없어요 · 못 하는 운동이 없어요 · 모르는 사람이 없어요 · 안 본 학생이 없어요

explanations.title: Compare the two sentences
explanations.body: Compare the following two sentences (the English is the book’s). Although both sentences convey the same meaning, the second sentence contains double negatives (못 and 없어요) and emphasizes that Andrew can eat any Korean food. Koreans use double negatives for emphasis. In this chapter, you will practice sentences that contain double negatives and end in ~이/가 없다.

examples.text: 앤드류 짐먼은 한국음식을 다 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.translation: aendeuryu jimmeoneun hangugeumsigeul da meogeul su isseoyo. — Andrew Zimmern can eat any Korean food.

examples.text: 앤드류 짐먼은 못 먹는 한국음식이 없어요.
examples.translation: aendeuryu jimmeoneun mot meongneun hangugeumsigi eopseoyo. — There is no Korean food that Andrew Zimmern cannot eat!

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: The book’s examples, with the literal and intended meanings (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 저희 가게에는 없는 물건이 없어요.
examples.translation: jeohui gageeneun eomneun mulgeoni eopseoyo. — There are no things we do not have in our store. (literal meaning) / Our store has everything! (intended meaning)

examples.text: 제 남자 친구는 못 하는 운동이 없어요.
examples.translation: je namja chinguneun mot haneun undongi eopseoyo. — There is no sport my boyfriend cannot do. (literal meaning) / My boyfriend can do any type of sport. (intended meaning)

examples.text: 서 교수님을 모르는 사람이 없어요.
examples.translation: seo gyosunimeul moreuneun sarami eopseoyo. — There is no one who does not know Professor Seo. (literal meaning) / Everyone knows who Professor Seo is. (intended meaning)

examples.text: 한국 드라마를 안 본 학생이 없어요.
examples.translation: hanguk deuramareul an bon haksaengi eopseoyo. — There is no student who has not seen Korean drama. (literal meaning) / Every student has seen Korean drama. (intended meaning)

explanations.title: Patterns (mine)
explanations.body: negative verb in attributive form + noun + 이/가 없어요 = “there is no … that does not …”, i.e. “every …”.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a furniture department store advertisement

examples.text: 누구나 다 아는 가구 백화점

lessons.title: 432. Ch 34 · Grammar B: expressing “please do not … but”, –지 말고 / ~말고
lessons.subtitle: -지 말고 · ~말고 · 떠들지 말고 공부하세요 · 졸지 말고 일어서세요 · 금요일 말고 토요일에

explanations.title: –지 마세요 turns into –지 말고
explanations.body: Compare the following two sentences (the English is the book’s). The expression –지 마세요, which you learned in Chapter 4, is used to make a request or command to not do something, as in the first sentence. However, when the request or command is immediately followed by another request or command, –지 마세요 turns into –지 말고, as in the second sentence. Thus, –지 말고 can translate to “do not do [something] but” or “instead of doing [something]”.

examples.text: 교실에서 영어를 하지 마세요.
examples.translation: gyosireseo yeongeoreul haji maseyo. — Please do not speak English in the classroom.

examples.text: 교실에서 영어를 하지 말고 한국말을 하세요.
examples.translation: gyosireseo yeongeoreul haji malgo hangungmareul haseyo. — Please do not speak English in the classroom, but speak Korean. / Please speak Korean in the classroom instead of speaking English.

explanations.title: More examples with –지 말고
explanations.body: The book’s examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 수업시간에 떠들지 말고 공부하세요.
examples.translation: sueopsigane tteodeulji malgo gongbuhaseyo. — Please do not make noises but study in class. / Please study instead of making noise.

examples.text: 김 상병, 졸지 말고 일어서세요.
examples.translation: gim sangbyeong, jolji malgo ireoseoseyo. — Please do not doze off but stand up, PFC Kim.

explanations.title: When the same verb is used for both requests: ~말고
explanations.body: When the same verb is used for both requests, the first verb is dropped. In this case, 말고 is used. The book writes the dropped parts in parentheses: 금요일(에 만나지) 말고 토요일에 만납시다; 영어(를 하지) 말고 한국말을 하세요. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 금요일 말고 토요일에 만납시다.
examples.translation: geumyoil malgo toyoire mannapsida. — Let’s meet Saturday instead of (meeting) Friday.

examples.text: 영어 말고 한국말을 하세요.
examples.translation: yeongeo malgo hangungmareul haseyo. — Please speak Korean instead of (speaking) English.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading): a news article about a survey of college freshmen
explanations.body: The following news article is about a survey covering aspects of college freshman life. The book gives the hint to focus on the words you know; it asks you to write English titles for two pie charts (the charts are pictures and are left out) and fill in a table for each chart. The text is the book’s, with the numbers, dates and percentages spelled out in Hangul; the English is mine.

examples.text: 한국대학교 학생상담센터는 올해 신입생 삼천오백 명을 대상으로 대학생활과 관련한 설문 조사결과를 이십 일 발표했다.
examples.translation: hangukdaehakgyo haksaengsangdamsenteoneun olhae sinipsaeng samcheonobaek myeongeul daesangeuro daehaksaenghwalgwa gwallyeonhan seolmun josagyeolgwareul isip il balpyohaetda. — The Hanguk University Student Counseling Center announced on the 20th the results of a survey on college life covering 3,500 freshmen this year.

examples.text: 조사 결과, 대학 입학 후 고민을 묻는 질문에 학비문제, 삼십오 점 팔 퍼센트라고 대답한 학생이 가장 많았다.
examples.translation: josa gyeolgwa, daehak ipak hu gomineul munneun jilmune hakbimunje, samsibo jeom pal peosenteurago daedapan haksaengi gajang manatda. — In the results, the most students answered tuition problems (35.8%) to the question asking about worries after entering college.

examples.text: 다음으로 학교 전공공부, 이십오 퍼센트, 시간관리, 십사 점 육 퍼센트, 취업문제, 십삼 점 사 퍼센트, 이성교제, 삼 점 사 퍼센트, 기타, 칠 점 팔 퍼센트 등의 순으로 대답했다.
examples.translation: daeumeuro hakgyo jeongonggongbu, isibo peosenteu, sigangwalli, sipsa jeom yuk peosenteu, chwieommunje, sipsam jeom sa peosenteu, iseonggyoje, sam jeom sa peosenteu, gita, chil jeom pal peosenteu deungui suneuro daedapaetda. — Next, they answered in the order of major studies (25%), time management (14.6%), employment (13.4%), dating (3.4%), other (7.8%) and so on.

examples.text: 신입생의 대부분이 아르바이트를 원했고, 아르바이트를 하는 이유로는 용돈, 육십일 점 일 퍼센트, 학비, 이십육 점 구 퍼센트, 사회경험, 오 점 일 퍼센트, 생활비, 삼 점 구 퍼센트, 기타, 삼 퍼센트 등을 꼽았다.
examples.translation: sinipsaengui daebubuni areubaiteureul wonhaetgo, areubaiteureul haneun iyuroneun yongdon, yuksibil jeom il peosenteu, hakbi, isimnyuk jeom gu peosenteu, sahoegyeongheom, o jeom il peosenteu, saenghwalbi, sam jeom gu peosenteu, gita, sam peosenteu deungeul kkobatda. — Most freshmen wanted part-time jobs, and as reasons for working part-time they chose spending money (61.1%), tuition (26.9%), social experience (5.1%), living expenses (3.9%), other (3.0%) and so on.

explanations.title: The charts, labelled (mine)
explanations.body: The pie-chart slices 가 to 바 (Chart A) and A to E (Chart B) are labelled in the book’s table, partly (다 = time management, 마 = dating, 바 = other; A = earning personal expenses, C = social experience, E = other). The titles and the full labels, from the article (mine):

rows: 가 tuition (35.8%); 나 major studies (25%); 다 time management (14.6%); 라 employment (13.4%); 마 dating (3.4%); 바 other (7.8%)
A spending money (61.1%); B tuition (26.9%); C social experience (5.1%); D living expenses (3.9%); E other (3.0%)

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (Two-in-One Vocabulary Review, SMART Board), Activity 2 (listening to two conversations about a concern and advice), Activity 3 (a video clip from the drama “Rooftop Romance”) and Activity 5 (a role-play about concerns and advice about college life, with a table to jot down ideas) are audio, video, computer and partner activities.

explanations.title: Topic C: What will you do after you graduate? (졸업한 다음에 뭐 할 거야?)
explanations.body: Two Korean college students are talking about their plans for after graduation. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 준태: 민영아, 졸업한 다음에 뭐 할 거야?
examples.translation: juntae: minyeonga, joreopan daeume mwo hal geoya? — Minyeong, what are you going to do after graduating?

examples.text: 민영: 난 미국으로 유학 갈 거야. 석사 과정에 들어가고 싶어.
examples.translation: minyeong: nan migugeuro yuhak gal geoya. seoksa gwajeonge deureogago sipeo. — I’m going to study in America. I want to enter a master’s program.

examples.text: 준태: 그래? 미국 대학원에 들어가기가 어렵지?
examples.translation: juntae: geurae? miguk daehagwone deureogagiga eoryeopji? — Really? It’s hard to get into an American graduate school, isn’t it?

examples.text: 민영: 응. 자격 조건이 까다로워. 특히 영어를 잘 해야 해. 그래서 며칠 전에 어학원에 등록했어.
examples.translation: minyeong: eung. jagyeok jogeoni kkadarowo. teuki yeongeoreul jal haeya hae. geuraeseo myeochil jeone eohagwone deungnokaesseo. — Yes. The qualification requirements are demanding. You especially have to be good at English. So I enrolled in a language institute a few days ago.

examples.text: 준태: 그렇구나. 참, 현수도 유학 준비한대. 현수랑 같이 공부해 봐.
examples.translation: juntae: geureokuna. cham, hyeonsudo yuhak junbihandae. hyeonsurang gachi gongbuhae bwa. — I see. Oh, I hear Hyunsoo is also preparing to study abroad. Try studying together with Hyunsoo.

examples.text: 민영: 좋은 생각이야. 현수는 미국에 어학 연수도 갔다 왔지?
examples.translation: minyeong: joeun saenggagiya. hyeonsuneun miguge eohak yeonsudo gatda watji? — Good idea. Hyunsoo also went on a language study program in America, didn’t he?

examples.text: 준태: 응. 그래서 영어 회화를 아주 잘 해. 나도 현수같이 영어를 잘 하면 좋겠어. 영어는 정말 어려워.
examples.translation: juntae: eung. geuraeseo yeongeo hoehwareul aju jal hae. nado hyeonsugachi yeongeoreul jal hamyeon jokesseo. yeongeoneun jeongmal eoryeowo. — Yes. So he’s very good at conversational English. I wish I could speak English as well as Hyunsoo. English is really hard.

examples.text: 민영: 맞아. 영어는 공부할수록 어려운 것 같아. 참, 넌 진로 결정했어?
examples.translation: minyeong: maja. yeongeoneun gongbuhalsurok eoryeoun geot gata. cham, neon jillo gyeoljeonghaesseo? — Right. English seems to get harder the more you study. Oh, have you decided on your career path?

examples.text: 준태: 응. 난, 취업할 생각이야. 그런데 요즘 일자리가 별로 없어서 걱정이야.
examples.translation: juntae: eung. nan, chwieopal saenggagiya. geureonde yojeum iljariga byeollo eopseoseo geokjeongiya. — Yes. I’m thinking of getting a job. But I’m worried because there aren’t many jobs these days.

examples.text: 민영: 그래도 넌 자격증도 많고 학점도 좋잖아. 그러니까 취직이 잘 될 거야.
examples.translation: minyeong: geuraedo neon jagyeokjeungdo manko hakjeomdo jochana. geureonikka chwijigi jal doel geoya. — Still, you have many certificates and good grades. So you’ll surely get a job.

explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter); 등록(하다), 부담(하다/되다), 제공(하다/되다) and 취업/취직(하다) take the forms in parentheses; ~같이/처럼/같은 and –(으)ㄹ수록 are explained in the grammar.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a flyer for a Korea–U.S. language exchange program
explanations.body: The flyer is about a Korea–U.S. language exchange program. The book asks you to fill in a table in English: period of event; location; eligible candidates; English ability; scholarship; how to apply. The flyer is the book’s with the dates and numbers spelled out in Hangul; the e-mail address is not read out (AmericanEnglishSeoul@state.gov). The English is mine.

examples.translation: icheonisipsam hanmi yeoreum eohagyeonsu peurogeuraem chamgaja mojip — Recruiting participants for the 2023 Korea-U.S. summer language study program

examples.translation: juhanmigukdaesagwan — U.S. Embassy in Korea

examples.text: 한미 여름 어학연수 프로그램은 이천이십삼 년 칠 월 삼 일부터 사 주 동안 미국 동부에 위치한 대학 세 곳에서 진행됩니다.
examples.translation: hanmi yeoreum eohagyeonsu peurogeuraemeun icheonisipsam nyeon chil wol sam ilbuteo sa ju dongan miguk dongbue wichihan daehak se goseseo jinhaengdoemnida. — The Korea-U.S. summer language study program will be held for four weeks starting on July 3, 2023, at three universities located on the U.S. East Coast.

examples.text: 지원 자격 요건
examples.translation: jiwon jagyeok yogeon — Application eligibility requirements

examples.text: 현재 한국의 대학에 다니는 학생.
examples.translation: hyeonjae hangugui daehage danineun haksaeng. — Students currently attending a university in Korea.

examples.text: 특별 활동에 적극적으로 참여한 학생.
examples.translation: teukbyeol hwaldonge jeokgeukjeogeuro chamyeohan haksaeng. — Students who have actively participated in special activities.

examples.text: 미국 유학 경험이 거의 또는 전혀 없는 학생.
examples.translation: miguk yuhak gyeongheomi geoui ttoneun jeonhyeo eomneun haksaeng. — Students with little or no experience studying in the U.S.

examples.text: 영어 능력
examples.translation: yeongeo neungnyeok — English ability

examples.text: 현재 영어 능력에 상관없이 누구나 지원할 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: hyeonjae yeongeo neungnyeoge sanggwaneopsi nuguna jiwonhal su itseumnida. — Anyone can apply regardless of current English ability.

examples.text: 학생들은 프로그램 시작 전, 간단한 영어 능력 시험을 보고 그 결과에 따라 반을 나누게 됩니다.
examples.translation: haksaengdeureun peurogeuraem sijak jeon, gandanhan yeongeo neungnyeok siheomeul bogo geu gyeolgwae ttara baneul nanuge doemnida. — Before the program starts, students will take a simple English proficiency test and be divided into classes according to the results.

examples.text: 장학금 지원
examples.translation: janghakgeum jiwon — Scholarship support

examples.text: 이 프로그램은 전액 장학금이 지원됩니다.
examples.translation: i peurogeuraemeun jeonaek janghakgeumi jiwondoemnida. — This program is supported by a full scholarship.

examples.text: 주한미국대사관은 학비, 주거비용, 식비, 교통비 및 국제선 항공료 등 참가자의 모든 비용을 전액 지원합니다.
examples.translation: juhanmigukdaesagwaneun hakbi, jugeobiyong, sikbi, gyotongbi mit gukjeseon hanggongnyo deung chamgajaui modeun biyongeul jeonaek jiwonhamnida. — The U.S. Embassy in Korea fully covers all participants’ costs, such as tuition, housing costs, food costs, transportation costs and international airfare.

examples.text: 지원 방법
examples.translation: jiwon bangbeop — How to apply

examples.text: 이 프로그램에 관심있는 학생들은 지원서와 모든 제출 서류들을 이천이십이 년 삼 월 십삼 일 전까지 이메일 주소로 제출하시면 됩니다.
examples.translation: i peurogeuraeme gwansiminneun haksaengdeureun jiwonseowa modeun jechul seoryudeureul icheonisibi nyeon sam wol sipsam il jeonkkaji imeil jusoro jechulhasimyeon doemnida. — Students interested in this program can submit the application and all required documents to the e-mail address by March 13, 2022 (as the book prints the year).

explanations.title: The table filled in (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the table blank; these are my answers.

Anyone may apply whatever their English; a simple English test before the program places students in classes
A full scholarship covering tuition, housing, food, transportation and international airfare
E-mail the application and all required documents by March 13 (the book prints 2022)

lessons.title: 435. Ch 34 · Grammar C: expressing likeness, ~같이 / ~처럼 and ~같은
lessons.subtitle: ~같이 · ~처럼 · ~같은 · 동생같이 말합니다 · 동생 같은 친구 · 카페처럼 · 영화 같은 이야기

explanations.title: ~같이, ~처럼 and ~같은
explanations.body: In English, when we express likeness or similarity, we use “like”, as in Bill acts like John or a brother like my best friend. The Korean equivalents of this are ~같이, ~처럼, or ~같은. However, ~같이 and ~처럼, which are interchangeable, modify a verb; whereas ~같은 modifies a noun. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 준기는 제 동생같이 말합니다.
examples.translation: jungineun je dongsaenggachi malhamnida. — Junki speaks like my younger brother.

examples.text: 준기는 제 동생처럼 말합니다.
examples.translation: jungineun je dongsaengcheoreom malhamnida. — Junki speaks like my younger brother (the same with 처럼).

examples.text: 준기는 동생 같은 친구예요.
examples.translation: jungineun dongsaeng gateun chinguyeyo. — Junki is a friend of mine (who is) like my brother.

explanations.title: Note on the spacing
explanations.body: Note that in the first sentence 동생같이 or 동생처럼 modifies the verb 말합니다; in the second sentence 동생 같은 modifies the noun 친구 that immediately follows it. Keep in mind that there is a space between a noun and 같은 (e.g., 동생 같은, not 동생같은).

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: Here are more example sentences that have ~같이/처럼 or ~같은. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 제임스는 한국 사람같이 한국말을 해요.
examples.translation: jeimseuneun hanguk saramgachi hangungmareul haeyo. — James speaks Korean like (native) Korean people.

examples.text: 제임스는 한국 사람처럼 한국말을 해요.
examples.translation: jeimseuneun hanguk saramcheoreom hangungmareul haeyo. — James speaks Korean like (native) Korean people (with 처럼).

examples.text: 우리 집을 카페같이 만들었어요.
examples.translation: uri jibeul kapegachi mandeureosseoyo. — I made my house (look) like a café.

examples.text: 우리 집을 카페처럼 만들었어요.
examples.translation: uri jibeul kapecheoreom mandeureosseoyo. — I made my house (look) like a café (with 처럼).

examples.text: 우리 누나 같은 여자와 결혼하고 싶어요.
examples.translation: uri nuna gateun yeojawa gyeolhonhago sipeoyo. — I would like to marry a woman like my older sister.

examples.text: 영화 같은 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.translation: yeonghwa gateun iyagireul deureosseoyo. — I heard a story (that was) like a movie.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Listening and speaking): the models
explanations.body: In pairs, one partner asks a question with a noun and verb phrase from a list and the other answers with ~같이/처럼; then they take turns asking a question from the Question List and answering with ~같은. The book’s models (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 누가 마이클 잭슨처럼 춤을 잘 춥니까?
examples.translation: ga: nuga maikeul jaekseuncheoreom chumeul jal chumnikka? — Who dances well like Michael Jackson?

examples.text: 나: 김 일병이 마이클 잭슨같이 춤을 잘 춥니다.
examples.translation: na: gim ilbyeongi maikeul jaekseungachi chumeul jal chumnida. — Private First Class Kim dances well like Michael Jackson.

examples.text: 가: 최 상병은 어떤 곳에서 살고 싶어요?
examples.translation: ga: choe sangbyeongeun eotteon goseseo salgo sipeoyo? — Corporal Choi, what kind of place do you want to live in?

examples.text: 나: 몬트레이 같은 바닷가에서 살고 싶어요.
examples.translation: na: monteurei gateun badatgaeseo salgo sipeoyo. — I want to live by a seaside like Monterey.

explanations.title: The Question List
explanations.body: The book’s six questions (the English is mine):

examples.text: 어떤 곳에서 살고 싶어요?
examples.translation: eotteon goseseo salgo sipeoyo? — What kind of place do you want to live in?

examples.text: 어떤 음식을 먹고 싶어요?
examples.translation: eotteon eumsigeul meokgo sipeoyo? — What kind of food do you want to eat?

examples.text: 어떤 사람을 좋아합니까?
examples.translation: eotteon sarameul joahamnikka? — What kind of person do you like?

examples.text: 어떤 식당을 좋아합니까?
examples.translation: eotteon sikdangeul joahamnikka? — What kind of restaurant do you like?

examples.text: 어떤 스포츠를 잘 합니까?
examples.translation: eotteon seupocheureul jal hamnikka? — What kind of sport are you good at?

examples.text: 어떤 영화배우를 싫어합니까?
examples.translation: eotteon yeonghwabaeureul sireohamnikka? — What kind of movie actor do you dislike?

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking and listening): 우리 형같이 컴퓨터를 잘하고 싶어요
explanations.body: You think about activities your family members or friends are good at and ask your partner what they would like to be as good at. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 김 일병은 뭘 잘하고 싶어요?
examples.translation: ga: gim ilbyeongeun mwol jalhago sipeoyo? — Private First Class Kim, what do you want to be good at?

examples.text: 나: 저는 우리 형같이 컴퓨터를 잘하고 싶어요. 그리고 최 일병처럼 농구를 잘하고 싶어요.
examples.translation: na: jeoneun uri hyeonggachi keompyuteoreul jalhago sipeoyo. geurigo choe ilbyeongcheoreom nonggureul jalhago sipeoyo. — I want to be good at computers like my older brother. And I want to be good at basketball like Private First Class Choi.

lessons.title: 436. Ch 34 · Grammar D: cause and effect, –(으)면 –(으)ㄹ수록, the more … the more
lessons.subtitle: -(으)면 -(으)ㄹ수록 · 많으면 많을수록 · 먹으면 먹을수록 · 알면 알수록 · 공부할수록

explanations.title: Double comparatives
explanations.body: In English, we often express a cause-and-effect relationship by using double comparatives, as in “The more people come, the more fun the party is.” Note that the first comparative (clause) the more people come functions as a cause and the second comparative (clause) the more fun the party is functions as an effect. In Korean, we can express this cause-and-effect relationship by using the conjunctive ending –(으)면 –(으)ㄹ수록. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 사람이 많이 오면 올수록 파티가 재미있어요.
examples.translation: sarami mani omyeon olsurok patiga jaemiisseoyo. — The more people come, the more fun the party is.

examples.text: 많으면 많을수록 즐거워요.
examples.translation: maneumyeon maneulsurok jeulgeowoyo. — The more, the merrier.

explanations.title: –(으)면 is optional
explanations.body: –(으)면 in –(으)면 –(으)ㄹ수록 is optional and can be deleted. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 사람이 많이 올수록 파티가 재미있어요.
examples.translation: sarami mani olsurok patiga jaemiisseoyo. — The more people come, the more fun the party is.

examples.text: 많을수록 더 즐거워요.
examples.translation: maneulsurok deo jeulgeowoyo. — The more, the merrier.

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: Here are more example sentences with the conjunctive ending (the book writes the optional part in parentheses; both versions are given; the English is the book’s):

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Verb or adjective stem + (으)면 + the same stem + (으)ㄹ수록 (a stem ending in ㄹ drops the ㄹ: 알면 알수록; ㅂ-irregular stems change ㅂ to 우: 어려우면 어려울수록).

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Speaking and listening): the model
explanations.body: In pairs, one partner draws a card, translates the English clause into Korean with –(으)면 –(으)ㄹ수록, and the other repeats it and adds a logical effect. The book’s model (the English is mine):

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning, and the book’s parenthesized forms such as ~하다 and ~되다 show how a noun forms a verb. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (9시간 → 아홉 시간; 1학년 → 일 학년; 5월 → 오 월; 64주 → 육십사 주).

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify and discuss academic majors and classes and other college-related activities like registration; identify and discuss aspects of college life, such as employment and common concerns; and discuss plans for after graduating from college.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; using double negatives for emphasis; ~말고/–지 말고 (do not … but); ~같이/처럼 and ~같은 (like); the conjunctive ending –(으)면 –(으)ㄹ수록; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 부전공 (副專攻), 교환 (交換), and 기간 (期間).

lessons.title: 438. Ch 35 · What the chapter teaches, 자 (者) · 하 (下) 반 (半) 기 (期) · 구 (求) 직 (職) · 면 (面) 접 (接)
lessons.subtitle: 직장 구하기 · 하반기 · 구직 · 면접 · 특기자 · 지하도 · 반달 · 직업 · 면도

explanations.title: What Chapter 35 teaches (직장 구하기)
explanations.body:
Chapter 35, “Job Hunting”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: ask about and discuss information related to job hunting; state how job hunters in Korea usually prepare for employment; and answer general questions at a job interview.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the passive infixes 이, 히, 리, and 기; the passive verbs 보이다 and 들리다; an attributive form + 만큼; –다고 for a statement used as the object in a sentence; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 하반기 (下半期), 구직 (求職), and 면접 (面接).

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 자 (者) in 특기자
explanations.body: The Sino-Korean syllable 자 (者) means a person. It is often used as a suffix, as in 초보자 (a novice), 학자 (a scholar), and 보호자 (a guardian). Thus, 특기자 in Topic Presentation A literally means “a person with special ability or skill”; 특기 (特技) refers to (one’s) special ability or special skill.

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 하반기 (下半期)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means the second half of a (given) period/year. The first syllable 하 (下) means below, under, or bottom, as in 지하도 (an underground pass), 남하하다 (to move down south), 천하 (the world; the whole country; “heaven below”), and 하수도 (a sewer; “under water way”). The syllable 반 (半) means half, as in 반도 (a peninsula; “half island”), 반값 (half the price), 반달 (a half moon), and 반올림 (rounding up [of a number]; “half raising”). The last syllable 기 (期) means the duration of time, the interval of time, or period, as seen in the Sino-Korean notes of Chapter 34. Thus the literal meaning of the word 하반기 is “bottom half period”, and the word normally refers to the second half of a (given) period or year. As you may have guessed, the antonym of the word is 상반기.

rows: the world; the whole country; “heaven below”
the second half of a period or year; “bottom half period”
the first half of a period or year; “top half period”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 구직 (求職)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means seeking a job. The first syllable 구 (求) means seeking, as in 구인 광고 (a help-wanted ad; “people-seeking ad”), 구혼 (a marriage proposal; a courtship; “seeking a marriage”), and 요구 (a demand; a claim; a request; “important seeking”). The second syllable 직 (職) means job, profession, or position, as in 직업 (a job; an occupation), 교직 (teaching profession), 직장 (a workplace), and 직원 (an employee; a member of the staff; “job member”).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 면접 (面接)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means a face-to-face interview. The first syllable 면 (面) means face or surface, as in 가면 (a mask; “fake face”), 면도 (shaving; “face knife”), 세면 (washing one’s face), and 체면 (face, as in saving face; “body face”). Recall that you learned the second syllable 접 (接) from the word 직접 in Chapter 32 and that it means contact or treat, as in 접대 (a reception; a warm welcome; “treating and waiting”), 접지 (ground connection; grounding; “contact the ground”), and 접촉 (contact; touch; “contact and touch”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 면접 is “face contact”, and the word refers to a face-to-face interview.

The words (the meanings are the book’s Core Vocabulary; 서류 “documents” is the book’s gloss; the book’s 채용(하다), 접수(하다) and 참가(하다) are nouns that form verbs with 하다):

explanations.title: Vocabulary Learning Strategy: activate your prior knowledge
explanations.body:
We learn and remember new information more effectively when we are familiar with part of the information or when we can relate the new information to our prior knowledge. In other words, it is important to activate our prior knowledge in our learning process.

In this chapter you will be learning about job hunting in Korea. You will encounter questions such as: What Korean companies and products am I familiar with? How much do I know about the educational background of Korean job applicants? Do I have any direct/indirect experiences or any general/specific knowledge relevant to this topic? The book asks you to jot down in English, in a box, any prior knowledge you might use in this chapter: 1. names of Korean companies; 2. Korean products; 3. educational background of Korean job applicants; 4. other relevant information regarding the Korean job market or job hunting. Then compare your knowledge with your classmates and your teacher.

explanations.body: A female job seeker is talking to a male job consultant at a job fair. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 민정: 저, 국내 외국 기업에 지원하고 싶은데 자격조건이 어떻게 되나요?

examples.text: 상담원: 외국어를 할 줄 아세요?
examples.translation: sangdamwon: oegugeoreul hal jul aseyo? — Do you know how to speak a foreign language?

examples.text: 민정: 네, 전공이 불어여서 불어를 좀 해요. 그리고 영어도 좀 해요.
examples.translation: minjeong: ne, jeongongi bureoyeoseo bureoreul jom haeyo. geurigo yeongeodo jom haeyo. — Yes, my major is French so I speak a little French. And I speak a little English too.

examples.text: 상담원: 네, 특기가 외국어네요. 그럼 다른 특기도 있으세요?
examples.translation: sangdamwon: ne, teukgiga oegugeoneyo. geureom dareun teukgido isseuseyo? — I see, your specialty is foreign languages. Then do you have any other specialty?

examples.text: 민정: 네, 컴퓨터자격증이 있어요.
examples.translation: minjeong: ne, keompyuteojagyeokjeungi isseoyo. — Yes, I have a computer certificate.

examples.text: 상담원: 좋습니다. 외국 기업들이 보통 컴퓨터와 외국어 특기자를 우대해요.
examples.translation: sangdamwon: joseumnida. oeguk gieopdeuri botong keompyuteowa oegugeo teukgijareul udaehaeyo. — Good. Foreign companies usually give preferential treatment to people with computer and foreign-language skills.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading): key words for Activity 4
explanations.body: The book lists twenty-four key words and expressions you will use in the role-play (Activity 4) and asks you to fill in the English meanings, using a dictionary as necessary. The words that appear in the Core Vocabulary have the book’s meanings; the rest (상담, 소지자, 취업, 유학, 문의, 관리, 성적, 전공, 어학연수, 학점, 자격증) are mine.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): a classified newspaper section on job recruiting
explanations.body: This classified section shows information about job recruiting. The book asks you to fill in a table in English: opening and closing dates for application; department hiring; required qualifications; preferred candidate; contact for inquiries; and glosses 증명서: a certificate. The announcement is the book’s (SK Group first-half new-employee hiring; the e-mail address and web address are not read out); the numbers in the table below are spelled out in Hangul. The English is mine.

explanations.title: Topic B: I want to work at a large company (대기업에 취업하고 싶어요)
explanations.body: In this passage you will learn about a college student’s daily routine while looking for a job. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the numbers are spelled out in Hangul.)

examples.text: 김영호 군은 대학교 삼 학년이다.
examples.translation: gimyeongho guneun daehakgyo sam hangnyeonida. — Mr. Kim Youngho is a third-year university student.

examples.text: 대학에서 경영학을 공부하고 있다.
examples.translation: daehageseo gyeongyeonghageul gongbuhago itda. — He is studying business administration at university.

examples.text: 김 군의 희망은 내년에 대기업 인턴사원으로 뽑히는 것이다.
examples.translation: gim gunui huimangeun naenyeone daegieop inteonsawoneuro ppopineun geosida. — Mr. Kim’s hope is to be selected next year as an intern at a large company.

examples.text: 인턴으로 일하면서 경력을 쌓고 싶어한다.
examples.translation: inteoneuro ilhamyeonseo gyeongnyeogeul ssako sipeohanda. — He wants to build experience while working as an intern.

examples.text: 경력이 많으면 취업에 유리하다.
examples.translation: gyeongnyeogi maneumyeon chwieobe yurihada. — If you have a lot of experience, it is advantageous for getting a job.

examples.text: 그래서 요즘은 여자 친구와 데이트할 시간도 없이 바쁘다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo yojeumeun yeoja chinguwa deiteuhal sigando eopsi bappeuda. — So these days he is busy, without even time to date his girlfriend.

examples.text: 보통 학교에 가면 가장 먼저 취업게시판을 본다.
examples.translation: botong hakgyoe gamyeon gajang meonjeo chwieopgesipaneul bonda. — Usually when he goes to school, the first thing he looks at is the job bulletin board.

examples.text: 게시판에서 여러 회사의 유용한 구직정보를 찾을 수 있다.
examples.translation: gesipaneseo yeoreo hoesaui yuyonghan gujikjeongboreul chajeul su itda. — On the board, he can find useful job-seeking information from many companies.

examples.text: 그리고 수업이 끝나면 친구들과 그룹 스터디를 한다.
examples.translation: geurigo sueobi kkeunnamyeon chingudeulgwa geurup seuteodireul handa. — And when class is over, he does a group study with his friends.

examples.text: 그 후에 학원에 가서 영어면접에 필요한 회화를 배운다.
examples.translation: geu hue hagwone gaseo yeongeomyeonjeobe piryohan hoehwareul baeunda. — After that, he goes to a private academy and learns the conversation needed for the English interview.

examples.text: 그리고 체력 관리를 위해 체육관에 가서 한 시간 동안 운동을 한다.
examples.translation: geurigo cheryeok gwallireul wihae cheyukgwane gaseo han sigan dongan undongeul handa. — And, to manage his physical strength, he goes to the gym and exercises for an hour.

examples.text: 집에 돌아가면 인터넷으로 구인정보를 찾아보고 서류 전형에 필요한 자기소개서를 계속 업데이트한다.
examples.translation: jibe doragamyeon inteoneseuro guinjeongboreul chajabogo seoryu jeonhyeonge piryohan jagisogaeseoreul gyesok eopdeiteuhanda. — When he returns home, he looks for job-listing information on the internet and keeps updating the letter of self-introduction needed for the documents screening.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: language tests
explanations.body: Many companies in Korea require applicants to demonstrate their mastery of foreign languages like English, Chinese, and Japanese through oral interviews and a written test. Thus, college students spend a great deal of time and effort preparing for tests like the TOEIC (the Test of English for International Communication), an English language test designed specifically to measure everyday English skills on the job. Many students also spend several months to a year in a foreign country to learn the country’s language (어학 연수).

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): an announcement from the City of Seoul
explanations.body: The following announcement is from the City of Seoul’s website. The book asks you to fill in a table in English with the services provided by the Seoul Job Center for job seekers, recruiters and entrepreneurs. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out and the quotation marks and bullet symbols dropped; the English is mine.

examples.text: 서울일자리센터
examples.translation: seouriljarisenteo — Seoul Job Center

examples.text: 일자리와 함께 희망도 선물합니다.
examples.translation: iljariwa hamkke huimangdo seonmulhamnida. — We give you hope together with a job.

examples.text: 서울일자리센터는 취업을 원하는 서울시민 모두에게 다양하고 안정적인 일자리를 제공하기 위한 취업 전문기관입니다.
examples.translation: seouriljarisenteoneun chwieobeul wonhaneun seoulsimin moduege dayanghago anjeongjeogin iljarireul jegonghagi wihan chwieop jeonmungigwanimnida. — The Seoul Job Center is a job specialist institution that exists to provide diverse and stable jobs to all Seoul citizens who want employment.

examples.text: 서울특별시가 운영하는 이 기관에서는 현재 스물네 명의 전문상담사가 상담을 하고 있습니다.
examples.translation: seoulteukbyeolsiga unyeonghaneun i gigwaneseoneun hyeonjae seumulle myeongui jeonmunsangdamsaga sangdameul hago itseumnida. — At this institution run by the Seoul Metropolitan Government, twenty-four professional counselors are currently giving counseling.

examples.text: 취업을 원하는 시민들에게는 전문직업상담사가 일대일 상담을 통해 구직자 적성에 맞는 일자리를 소개해 주고 필요하면 직업교육도 도와줍니다.
examples.translation: chwieobeul wonhaneun simindeuregeneun jeonmunjigeopsangdamsaga ildaeil sangdameul tonghae gujikja jeokseonge manneun iljarireul sogaehae jugo piryohamyeon jigeopgyoyukdo dowajumnida. — For citizens who want employment, professional job counselors introduce jobs that suit the job seeker’s aptitude through one-to-one counseling and, if necessary, also help with job training.

examples.text: 구인을 원하는 기업들에게는 유능한 사람을 분야와 조건에 맞게 검색해 정보를 찾을 수 있는 환경을 마련해주며 유능한 사람의 추천과 채용도 대신해 드립니다.
examples.translation: guineul wonhaneun gieopdeuregeneun yuneunghan sarameul bunyawa jogeone matge geomsaekae jeongboreul chajeul su inneun hwangyeongeul maryeonhaejumyeo yuneunghan saramui chucheongwa chaeyongdo daesinhae deurimnida. — For companies that want to hire, it prepares an environment where they can search for capable people by field and conditions and find information, and also recommends and hires capable people on their behalf.

examples.text: 창업을 원하는 시민들에게는 창업전문상담사가 창업아이템 선정부터 재무컨설팅 등 창업에 필요한 상담을 제공해 창업에 성공할 수 있도록 도와드립니다.
examples.translation: changeobeul wonhaneun simindeuregeneun changeopjeonmunsangdamsaga changeobaitem seonjeongbuteo jaemukeonseolting deung changeobe piryohan sangdameul jegonghae changeobe seonggonghal su itdorok dowadeurimnida. — For citizens who want to start a business, start-up counselors provide the counseling needed for starting a business, from selecting a business item to financial consulting, and help them succeed in starting it.

lessons.title: 443. Ch 35 · Grammar A: the passive infixes 이, 히, 리 and 기
lessons.subtitle: 피동 · 보다-보이다 · 닫다-닫히다 · 열다-열리다 · 끊다-끊기다 · 만들어지다 · 예약되다

explanations.title: The passive voice
explanations.body:
The passive tense is a grammatical voice in which the subject receives the action of a transitive verb. In English, the passive voice is created with the auxiliary verb “to be” and the past participle of the transitive verb (e.g., is opened and was built).

In Korean, the passive voice is expressed differently. The infixes 이, 히, 리, 기, 우, 구, and 추 are used to make some native Korean verbs causative verbs: 먹이다 to feed (a person) and 살리다 to revive (a person). (For more detail, refer to the Grammar in Focus section in Chapter 30.) The same infixes, except 추, are also used to make native transitive verbs passive verbs. For example: 보다 (to see; to look at) → 보이다 (to be seen); 닫다 (to close) → 닫히다 (to be closed); 열다 (to open) → 열리다 (to be opened); 끊다 (to sever; to disconnect) → 끊기다 (to be severed; to be disconnected).

The following sentences contain some of these passive verbs (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 여기서 학교 건물이 보입니다.
examples.translation: yeogiseo hakgyo geonmuri boimnida. — The school building is seen from here.

examples.text: 교실문이 일곱 시에 닫힙니다.
examples.translation: gyosilmuni ilgop sie datimnida. — The classroom door is closed at seven.

examples.text: 오늘 아침에 물이 끊겼습니다.
examples.translation: oneul achime muri kkeunkyeotseumnida. — The water was cut off this morning.

explanations.title: There is no rule
explanations.body: As with the causative verbs in Chapter 30, there is no rule that helps predict which infix works with which verb. The following table lists the most common passive verbs, grouped by infix (the book’s table, with 듣다 → 들리다 under 리 and 끊다 → 끊기다 under 기):

rows: to be cut; to be hung up

explanations.title: 참고: two other ways to make a passive verb
explanations.body: There are two other ways to make a transitive verb a passive verb. 1. Some transitive verbs become passive verbs when –아/어지다 is added to the stem. 2. Some transitive verbs that end in 하다 become passive verbs when 되다 is added to the stem.

examples.text: 인형이 예쁘게 만들어졌어요.
examples.translation: inhyeongi yeppeuge mandeureojeosseoyo. — “A doll was made pretty.” / A pretty doll was made.

examples.text: 부산까지 비행기표가 예약되었어요.
examples.translation: busankkaji bihaenggipyoga yeyakdoeeosseoyo. — The ticket to Busan has been booked. (The book’s English says “train ticket”, but the Korean says 비행기표, plane ticket.)

explanations.body: The book gives eleven verbs (보다, 쓰이다, 섞다, 잡다, 뽑히다, 닫다, 들리다, 열다, 팔리다, 흔들다, 끊다) and asks you to write the passive or active counterpart. My answers:

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading and writing): change each sentence into a passive sentence
explanations.body: The model is 문을 닫았습니다 → 문이 닫혔습니다. The book gives six sentences to change; the 30 in the second sentence is spelled 서른. The answers are mine (the English is mine):

rows: I heard a gunshot last night. / A gunshot was heard last night.
We selected thirty new employees this time. / Thirty new employees were selected this time.
