explanations.title: 보다 and 듣다 versus 보이다 and 들리다
explanations.body: In Korean, the verb 보다 means to see, to look, or to watch, depending on the context. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 어제 김 선생님을 봤습니다.
examples.translation: eoje gim seonsaengnimeul bwatseumnida. — I saw Mr. Kim yesterday.

examples.text: 저기 저 산을 한번 보세요.
examples.translation: jeogi jeo saneul hanbeon boseyo. — Please look at the mountain over there.

examples.text: 아내가 설거지할 때 나는 아기를 봅니다.
examples.translation: anaega seolgeojihal ttae naneun agireul bomnida. — I watch the baby when my wife does the dishes.

explanations.title: 듣다
explanations.body: Likewise, the verb 듣다 means to hear or to listen:

examples.text: 어젯밤 총소리를 들었어요.
examples.translation: eojetbam chongsorireul deureosseoyo. — I heard a gunshot last night.

examples.text: 내 말을 잘 들으세요.
examples.translation: nae mareul jal deureuseyo. — Please listen to “my words.” / Please listen to me.

explanations.title: The passive versions mean only “to be seen” and “to be heard”
explanations.body: However, the passive versions of these two verbs (보이다 and 들리다) mean only to be seen (not to be looked at or to be watched) and to be heard (not to be listened to). For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 왼쪽에 강이 보였습니다.
examples.translation: oenjjoge gangi boyeotseumnida. — A river was seen on the left. / I saw a river on the left.

examples.text: 멀리서 자동차 소리가 들립니다.
examples.translation: meolliseo jadongcha soriga deullimnida. — The sound of a car is heard in the distance. / I hear a car in the distance.

explanations.title: What you can see and hear
explanations.body: For this reason, Koreans use 보이다 and 들리다 when describing what they (can) see or hear (the book writes the omitted topic in parentheses; the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 소리가 잘 들립니까?
examples.translation: soriga jal deullimnikka? — “Is (the sound) well heard?” / Do you hear the sound well? / Can you hear the sound well?

examples.text: 네, 잘 들립니다.
examples.translation: ne, jal deullimnida. — “Yes, it is well heard.” / Yes, I hear it well. / I can hear it.

examples.text: 칠판이 잘 보입니까?
examples.translation: chilpani jal boimnikka? — “Is (the chalkboard) seen well?” / Do you see (the chalkboard) well? / Can you see (the chalkboard)?

examples.text: 아니요, 잘 안 보입니다.
examples.translation: aniyo, jal an boimnida. — “No, it is not seen well.” / No, I don’t see it well. / I can’t see it well.

examples.text: 무엇이 보입니까?
examples.translation: mueosi boimnikka? — “What is (being) seen?” / What do you see? / What can you see?

examples.text: 무슨 소리가 들립니까?
examples.translation: museun soriga deullimnikka? — “What sound is being heard?” / What do you hear? / What can you hear?

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Speaking): 뭐가 보입니까?
explanations.body: In pairs, Partner A asks what Partner B sees in a picture of a room (and then a house), and B answers using ~이/가 보입니다; then Partner B makes a sentence using ~이/가 들립니다 after hearing a sound. The pictures and sounds are not included. The book’s models (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 방에 뭐가 보입니까?
examples.translation: ga: bange mwoga boimnikka? — What do you see in the room?

examples.text: 나: 방에 컴퓨터가 보입니다.
examples.translation: na: bange keompyuteoga boimnida. — I see a computer in the room.

examples.text: 가: 또 뭐가 보입니까?
examples.translation: ga: tto mwoga boimnikka? — What else do you see?

examples.text: 나: 또 시계가 보입니다.
examples.translation: na: tto sigyega boimnida. — I also see a clock.

examples.text: 가: 새 소리가 들립니다.
examples.translation: ga: sae soriga deullimnida. — I hear the sound of a bird.

examples.text: 나: 비 소리가 들립니다.
examples.translation: na: bi soriga deullimnida. — I hear the sound of rain.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Reading): a neighbor’s statement
explanations.body: Someone broke into Taejin’s house while no one was home. The book asks you to read the statement written by a neighbor who lives across the street and: 1. circle all the passive verbs; 2. identify in English what the neighbor heard; 3. identify in English what the neighbor saw; 4. change the underlined sentence into the passive voice (the underline is not in the text I have). The statement is the book’s (the time is spelled in Hangul); the English is mine.

examples.text: 어젯밤 열 시쯤에 집 앞에서 차가 갑자기 멈추는 소리가 들렸어요.
examples.translation: eojetbam yeol sijjeume jip apeseo chaga gapjagi meomchuneun soriga deullyeosseoyo. — At about ten last night, I heard the sound of a car suddenly stopping in front of the house.

examples.text: 저는 그때 거실에서 책을 읽고 있었어요.
examples.translation: jeoneun geuttae geosireseo chaegeul ilgo isseosseoyo. — I was reading a book in the living room then.

examples.text: 그런데 밖에서 이야기 소리가 들렸어요.
examples.translation: geureonde bakkeseo iyagi soriga deullyeosseoyo. — But I heard the sound of talking outside.

examples.text: 그래서 밖을 봤어요.
examples.translation: geuraeseo bakkeul bwasseoyo. — So I looked outside.

examples.text: 그때 두 남자가 이웃집에서 나오는 것이 보였어요.
examples.translation: geuttae du namjaga iutjibeseo naoneun geosi boyeosseoyo. — Then I saw two men coming out of the neighboring house.

examples.text: 그리고 차 문이 열렸어요.
examples.translation: geurigo cha muni yeollyeosseoyo. — And the car door opened.

examples.text: 그 두 사람은 빠르게 그 차 안으로 들어갔어요.
examples.translation: geu du sarameun ppareuge geu cha aneuro deureogasseoyo. — The two people quickly got into the car.

examples.text: 그리고 문이 닫혔어요.
examples.translation: geurigo muni dacheosseoyo. — And the door closed.

examples.text: 그리고 차가 출발하는 소리를 들었어요.
examples.translation: geurigo chaga chulbalhaneun sorireul deureosseoyo. — And I heard the sound of the car leaving.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the answers blank; these are mine.

rows: A car suddenly stopping in front of the house; the sound of talking outside; the car leaving
Two men coming out of the neighboring house

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): a newspaper article introducing three job hunters
explanations.body: The following newspaper article introduces three job hunters. The book asks you to fill in a table in English for each of A (27), Bae (26) and Yang (31): desired job; preparations for getting a job; means of funding their education. The book glosses 실무형 코딩 학원: practical coding academy (boot camp). The article is the book’s; the ages, money amounts, months and counts are spelled out in Hangul, quotation marks and parentheses are dropped, and the letter A is spelled 에이. The English is mine.

examples.text: 삼 년째 웹디자이너 취업을 준비하는 에이 씨, 스물일곱 살은 올 이 월부터 디자인 취업 전문학원에 다니고 있다.
examples.translation: sam nyeonjjae wepdijaineo chwieobeul junbihaneun ei ssi, seumullilgop sareun ol i wolbuteo dijain chwieop jeonmunhagwone danigo itda. — A, 27, who has been preparing for a web designer job for three years, has been attending a design job-specialty academy since February this year.

examples.text: 구직 기간이 길어지면서 전문가의 도움을 받기로 한 것이다.
examples.translation: gujik gigani gireojimyeonseo jeonmungaui doumeul batgiro han geosida. — As her job-seeking period grew longer, she decided to get an expert’s help.

examples.text: 학원만으로 부족하다고 느껴 그룹과외 수업도 듣고 있다.
examples.translation: hagwonmaneuro bujokadago neukkyeo geurupgwaoe sueopdo deutgo itda. — Feeling that the academy alone was not enough, she is also taking group tutoring classes.

examples.text: 지금까지 그가 취업 학원과 과외에 쓴 돈은 백이십만 원 남짓.
examples.translation: jigeumkkaji geuga chwieop hagwongwa gwaoee sseun doneun baegisimman won namjit. — The money spent so far on the job academy and tutoring is a little over 1,200,000 won.

examples.text: 학원비를 내려고 단기 아르바이트도 뛰고 있다.
examples.translation: hagwonbireul naeryeogo dangi areubaiteudo ttwigo itda. — She is also working short-term part-time jobs to pay the academy fees.

examples.text: 에이 씨는 대기업에 입사하려면 여전히 스펙이 압도적으로 좋아야 한다며 취업 학원 수강은 사실상 필수라고 전했다.
examples.translation: ei ssineun daegieobe ipsaharyeomyeon yeojeonhi seupegi apdojeogeuro joaya handamyeo chwieop hagwon sugangeun sasilsang pilsurago jeonhaetda. — A said that to join a large company your “specs” still have to be overwhelmingly good, and that taking a job academy course is in effect a must.

examples.text: 배 모 씨, 스물여섯 살은 서울에 있는 대기업에서 일하고 싶어한다.
examples.translation: bae mo ssi, seumullyeoseot sareun seoure inneun daegieobeseo ilhago sipeohanda. — Mr./Ms. Bae, 26, wants to work at a large company in Seoul.

examples.text: 취업 준비를 하며 학원에 다니느라 카페와 스터디룸에서 주 오 일 아르바이트를 한다며 집에서 도움을 받는 사람들은 편하게 준비를 하는데, 나만 이렇게 힘들다는 생각이 들 때도 많다고 했다.
examples.translation: chwieop junbireul hamyeo hagwone danineura kapewa seuteodirumeseo ju o il areubaiteureul handamyeo jibeseo doumeul banneun saramdeureun pyeonhage junbireul haneunde, naman ireoke himdeuldaneun saenggagi deul ttaedo mantago haetda. — Bae said, “Because I attend an academy while preparing for a job, I do a part-time job five days a week at a café and a study room; people who get help from home prepare comfortably, and there are many times when I think that only I have it this hard.”

examples.text: 지난해 팔 월 대학을 졸업한 배 씨는 취업난이 심하다 보니 지원해도 떨어질 것 같다는 이유로 아직까지 입사 서류를 넣어본 적이 없다.
examples.translation: jinanhae pal wol daehageul joreopan bae ssineun chwieomnani simhada boni jiwonhaedo tteoreojil geot gatdaneun iyuro ajikkaji ipsa seoryureul neoeobon jeogi eopda. — Bae, who graduated in August last year, has not yet submitted any job application documents, for the reason that “because the job shortage is severe, I think I would fail even if I applied.”

examples.text: 중소기업을 퇴사하고 개발자로 재취업을 준비하는 양 모 씨, 서른한 살은 올해 삼 개월 과정의 실무형 코딩 학원에 참여했다.
examples.translation: jungsogieobeul toesahago gaebaljaro jaechwieobeul junbihaneun yang mo ssi, seoreunhan sareun olhae sam gaewol gwajeongui silmuhyeong koding hagwone chamyeohaetda. — Mr./Ms. Yang, 31, who left a small or medium enterprise and is preparing to be re-employed as a developer, joined a three-month practical coding academy (boot camp) this year.

examples.text: 비용은 한 달에 이백만 원씩 총 육백만 원.
examples.translation: biyongeun han dare ibaengman wonssik chong yukbaengman won. — The cost was 2,000,000 won a month, 6,000,000 won in total.

examples.text: 양 씨는 취업을 다시 준비하려니 과거보다 훨씬 어려워졌다며 그나마 개발자가 취업에 유리할 것 같아 저축한 돈을 털어 고액 부트캠프를 다니는 중이라고 말했다.
examples.translation: yang ssineun chwieobeul dasi junbiharyeoni gwageoboda hwolssin eoryeowojeotdamyeo geunama gaebaljaga chwieobe yurihal geot gata jeochukan doneul teoreo goaek buteukaempeureul danineun jungirago malhaetda. — Yang said that preparing for a job again has become much harder than in the past, and that since developers seem to have an advantage in getting jobs, “I am attending an expensive boot camp, emptying out my savings.”

explanations.body: The book gives these words to review (use a dictionary for unknown ones) and asks you to write a short story with at least two of them in each sentence, and then to read the sentences to a partner. The meanings of the Core Vocabulary words are the book’s; the rest are mine.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Writing and speaking): writing a letter of self-introduction (자기소개서 쓰기)
explanations.body: You are looking for a job and want to write a letter introducing yourself as a potential employee. The book asks you to: a. think about your job experiences, personality (strengths and weaknesses), special skills, etc. and fill in a table in English (work experience; school experience; personality [strengths/weaknesses]; special skills; other); b. using this information, think of a job you would like to do; c. in Korean, write a cover letter that includes the reasons you are qualified for the job; d. present your letter to the class, in Korean, and decide which is the most creative.

explanations.title: Topic C: Why did you apply to our company? (저희 회사에 지원한 동기가 무엇입니까?)
explanations.body: A college graduate is being interviewed by two people for a position at a trading company. (The two interviewers are both labelled 면접관 here; the book labels them 면접관1 and 면접관2. The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 면접관: 김현민 씨, 대학에서 무엇을 공부하셨습니까?
examples.translation: myeonjeopgwan: gimhyeonmin ssi, daehageseo mueoseul gongbuhasyeotseumnikka? — Mr. Kim Hyunmin, what did you study at university?

examples.text: 현민: 무역학을 전공했습니다.
examples.translation: hyeonmin: muyeokageul jeongonghaetseumnida. — I majored in trade.

examples.text: 면접관: 어떤 외국어를 잘 하십니까?
examples.translation: myeonjeopgwan: eotteon oegugeoreul jal hasimnikka? — What foreign language are you good at?

examples.text: 현민: 제가 영어에는 자신이 있습니다. 호주에서 삼 년 동안 공부를 했습니다.
examples.translation: hyeonmin: jega yeongeoeneun jasini itseumnida. hojueseo sam nyeon dongan gongbureul haetseumnida. — I am confident in English. I studied in Australia for three years.

examples.text: 면접관: 저희 회사에 지원하신 동기가 무엇입니까?
examples.translation: myeonjeopgwan: jeohui hoesae jiwonhasin donggiga mueosimnikka? — What was your motive for applying to our company?

examples.text: 현민: 이 회사가 다국적기업이기 때문에 제 전공과 특기에 잘 맞는다고 생각했습니다.
examples.translation: hyeonmin: i hoesaga dagukjeokgieobigi ttaemune je jeongonggwa teukgie jal manneundago saenggakaetseumnida. — Because this company is a multinational corporation, I thought it suited my major and specialty well.

examples.text: 면접관: 네. 자신의 장점과 단점은 무엇이라고 생각하십니까?
examples.translation: myeonjeopgwan: ne. jasinui jangjeomgwa danjeomeun mueosirago saenggakasimnikka? — I see. What do you think your strengths and weaknesses are?

examples.text: 현민: 새로운 환경에 잘 적응하는 것이 제 장점입니다. 단점은 성격이 너무 철저하다는 점입니다.
examples.translation: hyeonmin: saeroun hwangyeonge jal jeogeunghaneun geosi je jangjeomimnida. danjeomeun seonggyeogi neomu cheoljeohadaneun jeomimnida. — Adapting well to a new environment is my strength. My weakness is that my personality is too thorough.

examples.text: 면접관: 김현민 씨, 오늘 감사합니다. 노력하신 만큼 좋은 결과 있기를 바랍니다.
examples.translation: myeonjeopgwan: gimhyeonmin ssi, oneul gamsahamnida. noryeokasin mankeum joeun gyeolgwa itgireul baramnida. — Mr. Kim Hyunmin, thank you for today. I hope you get good results to the extent that you have made an effort.

explanations.title: Core words and phrases of Topic C
explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter); 개발(하다/되다) and 적응(하다/되다) take the forms in parentheses; –고 생각하다 and an attributive form + 만큼 are explained in the grammar.

rows: (開發) development; to develop / to be developed (~하다/되다)
(短點) a weak point; shortcoming; “short point”
to be new; to be fresh; to be novel
(長點) a merit; a strength; a forte; “strong point”
(適應) adaptation; to adapt oneself to / to be adapted to (~하다/되다)
(徹底) to be thorough; to be exhaustive

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): tips for preparing for a job interview
explanations.body: The following article offers tips for preparing for a job interview. The book asks you to: 1. make an appropriate title for the article in Korean; 2. write the gist of each of four tips in English; 3. add one or two tips of your own and present them to the class. The article is the book’s (the quotation marks are dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 기업들이 면접에서 중요하게 생각하는 것은 지원자의 사회성과 업무 적응력이다.
examples.translation: gieopdeuri myeonjeobeseo jungyohage saenggakaneun geoseun jiwonjaui sahoeseonggwa eommu jeogeungnyeogida. — What companies consider important in interviews is the applicant’s sociability and ability to adapt to work.

examples.text: 인사담당자들은 면접을 잘 보면 필기시험을 좀 못 봐도 입사할 수 있지만 면접에서 떨어지면 학점이나 성적이 좋아도 채용되기 어렵다고 말한다.
examples.translation: insadamdangjadeureun myeonjeobeul jal bomyeon pilgisiheomeul jom mot bwado ipsahal su itjiman myeonjeobeseo tteoreojimyeon hakjeomina seongjeogi joado chaeyongdoegi eoryeopdago malhanda. — Personnel managers say that if you do well in the interview you can join the company even if you do a little poorly on the written test, but if you fail the interview it is hard to be hired even with good credits or grades.

examples.text: 면접관은 응시자를 봤을 때 첫인상에 크게 영향을 받는다고 한다.
examples.translation: myeonjeopgwaneun eungsijareul bwasseul ttae cheosinsange keuge yeonghyangeul banneundago handa. — It is said that interviewers are greatly influenced by the first impression when they see an applicant.

examples.text: 그렇기 때문에 면접에서 좋은 점수를 얻기 위해서는 솔직하고 적극적이어야 한다.
examples.translation: geureoki ttaemune myeonjeobeseo joeun jeomsureul eotgi wihaeseoneun soljikago jeokgeukjeogieoya handa. — Therefore, to get a good score in an interview you have to be honest and proactive.

examples.text: 적극성은 그 회사에서 열심히 일하고 싶다는 생각을 충분히 표현하면 된다.
examples.translation: jeokgeukseongeun geu hoesaeseo yeolsimhi ilhago sipdaneun saenggageul chungbunhi pyohyeonhamyeon doenda. — As for proactiveness, it is enough to express fully your wish to work hard at that company.

examples.text: 예를 들어 퇴근시간이 됐는데 상사가 일을 시키면 어떻게 하겠느냐는 질문을 했을 때 가정도 중요하니 퇴근하겠다는 답보다는 필요한 일이라면 야근을 하겠다는 답을 면접관은 더 좋아한다.

lessons.title: 447. Ch 35 · Grammar C: expansion of 만큼, an attributive form + 만큼
lessons.subtitle: 만큼 · 먹은 만큼 · 할 수 있을 만큼 · 먹고 싶은 만큼 · 기대한 만큼 · 들어갈 만큼

explanations.title: As … as: a noun or a clause before 만큼
explanations.body: Look at the English sentences to see what can follow the word as: “I eat as much as Michael (does).” and “Please eat as much as you ate yesterday.” Note that as can be followed by a noun (as in the first sentence) or by a clause (as in the second sentence). Likewise, 만큼, which is the Korean counterpart you learned about in Chapter 18, can be preceded by a noun or clause (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 나는 마이클 만큼 많이 먹어요.
examples.translation: naneun maikeul mankeum mani meogeoyo. — I eat as much as Michael (does).

examples.text: 어제 먹은 만큼 많이 먹으세요.
examples.translation: eoje meogeun mankeum mani meogeuseyo. — Please eat as much as you ate yesterday.

explanations.title: The attributive form
explanations.body: When a clause precedes 만큼, however, the verb of the clause has to be in the attributive form. The following examples show how 만큼 is preceded by a clause (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 할 수 있을 만큼 하세요.
examples.translation: hal su isseul mankeum haseyo. — Please do as much as you can.

examples.text: 이 뷔페에서는 먹고 싶은 만큼 먹어도 돼요.
examples.translation: i bwipeeseoneun meokgo sipeun mankeum meogeodo dwaeyo. — At this buffet, you can eat as much as you want (to eat).

examples.text: 성적이 기대한 만큼 안 좋아요.
examples.translation: seongjeogi gidaehan mankeum an joayo. — The grade is not as good as I expected.

examples.text: 그 경기장은 팔천 명이 들어갈 만큼 큽니다.
examples.translation: geu gyeonggijangeun palcheon myeongi deureogal mankeum keumnida. — The stadium is “as big as 8,000 can enter.” / The stadium is big enough to hold 8,000.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Past attributive (-(으)ㄴ), present attributive (-는) or future attributive (-(으)ㄹ) + 만큼; an adjective takes -(으)ㄴ or -(으)ㄹ.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Speaking and listening): the model
explanations.body: In pairs, Partner A picks an unshaded card and conjugates the verb out loud, using 만큼; Partner B picks a shaded card and combines it with what A said. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 열심히 일하는 만큼
examples.translation: ga: yeolsimhi ilhaneun mankeum — to the extent that you work hard

lessons.title: 448. Ch 35 · Grammar D: expressing a statement as an object, –다고
lessons.subtitle: -다고 · 재미있다고 생각해요 · 학생이라고 · 아니라고 · 끝났다고 알고 있어요 · 오겠다고 약속했어요

explanations.title: A statement as the object of a sentence
explanations.body: In Korean, when a statement (in contrast to a command or question) becomes the object in a sentence, it goes through some “cosmetic” changes. First, the verb ending of the statement changes to the blunt formal form –다. Then 고, which functions as an object marker, is attached to the statement. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 한국말이 재미있어요.
examples.translation: hangungmari jaemiisseoyo. — Korean is fun.

examples.text: 한국말이 재미있다.
examples.translation: hangungmari jaemiitda. — (change the verb ending to the blunt formal form)

examples.text: 한국말이 재미있다고
examples.translation: hangungmari jaemiitdago — (add the “object marker” 고)

explanations.title: The new statement as an object
explanations.body: This new statement can then be used as the object in a sentence (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 저는 한국말이 재미있다고 생각해요.
examples.translation: jeoneun hangungmari jaemiitdago saenggakaeyo. — I think [that] Korean is fun.

examples.text: 저는 한국말이 재미있다고 믿어요.
examples.translation: jeoneun hangungmari jaemiitdago mideoyo. — I believe [that] Korean is fun.

explanations.title: The note
explanations.body: Thus, when a statement ends with –다고, you can tell it is the object of the sentence. (Recall –다고 하다 from Chapter 23. –다고 in –다고 하다 is the same as what you are learning here.)

explanations.title: 이다 and 아니다
explanations.body: When a declarative sentence with the verb 이다 or 아니다 becomes an object, however, ~이다고 and ~이/가 아니다고 change to ~이라고 and ~이/가 아니라고, respectively (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 그 여자가 학생이라고 생각해요.
examples.translation: geu yeojaga haksaengirago saenggakaeyo. — I think [that] the woman is a student.

examples.text: 그 여자가 학생이 아니라고 생각해요.
examples.translation: geu yeojaga haksaengi anirago saenggakaeyo. — I think [that] the woman is not a student.

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: The following examples show more instances in which a statement is used as an object (the English is the book’s; 6시 is spelled out):

examples.text: 시험이 지난 주에 끝났다고 알고 있어요.
examples.translation: siheomi jinan jue kkeunnatdago algo isseoyo. — I know [that] the exam was over last week.

examples.text: 철호가 여섯 시까지 집에 오겠다고 약속했어요.
examples.translation: cheolhoga yeoseot sikkaji jibe ogetdago yaksokaesseoyo. — Cholho promised [that] he would come home by six.

examples.text: 서진이는 좋은 친구라고 생각해요.
examples.translation: seojinineun joeun chingurago saenggakaeyo. — I think [that] Seojin is a good friend.

explanations.title: Forms (mine)
explanations.body: Statement (polite) → blunt form + 고.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Speaking and listening): the model
explanations.body: In pairs, one partner reads a sentence from a list and the other changes it to a dependent clause with –다고/라고. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 한국말이 쉬워요.
examples.translation: ga: hangungmari swiwoyo. — Korean is easy.

examples.text: 나: 한국말이 쉽다고 생각해요.
examples.translation: na: hangungmari swipdago saenggakaeyo. — I think Korean is easy.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Writing and speaking): 한국 사람들이 친절하다고 생각해요
explanations.body: You jot down your thoughts about Korea (its people, food, language, etc.) in English, discuss them with classmates using –다고/라고 + a main verb, then report the most interesting idea to the class using –다고/라고 (말)하다. The book’s models (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 박 이병, 한국에 대해 어떻게 생각해요?
examples.translation: ga: bak ibyeong, hanguge daehae eotteoke saenggakaeyo? — Private Park, what do you think about Korea?

examples.text: 나: 저는 한국 사람들이 친절하다고 생각해요.
examples.translation: na: jeoneun hanguk saramdeuri chinjeolhadago saenggakaeyo. — I think Korean people are kind.

examples.text: 박 이병은 한국 사람들이 친절하다고 했습니다. 그리고 문 일병은 한국 드라마가 너무 재미있다고 했습니다.
examples.translation: bak ibyeongeun hanguk saramdeuri chinjeolhadago haetseumnida. geurigo mun ilbyeongeun hanguk deuramaga neomu jaemiitdago haetseumnida. — Private Park said that Korean people are kind. And Private First Class Moon said that Korean dramas are very interesting.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: ask about and discuss information related to job hunting; state how job hunters in Korea usually prepare for employment; and answer general questions at a job interview.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the passive infixes 이, 히, 리, and 기; the passive verbs 보이다 and 들리다; an attributive form + 만큼; –다고 for a statement used as the object in a sentence; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 하반기 (下半期), 구직 (求職), and 면접 (面接).

lessons.title: 451. Ch 36 · What the chapter teaches, 유 (有) 무 (無) · 능 (能) 력 (力) · 개 (開) 업 (業)
lessons.subtitle: 직장생활 · 유능 · 무능 · 무료 · 능력 · 가능 · 체력 · 개업 · 개학 · 폐업

explanations.title: What Chapter 36 teaches (직장생활)
explanations.body:
Chapter 36, “Life at Work”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify, ask about, and discuss daily routines and common concerns at work; talk about plans for starting a new business; and identify, ask about, and discuss the typical lifestyle of retirees.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; –다(가) 보니(까), used to express the speaker’s own discovery/realization of something while engaging in an activity; an attributive form + 줄 알았다 (I thought); an attributive form + 줄 몰랐다 (I did not know; I was not aware); ~(이)나 used to emphasize an amount or number; the conjunctive ending –는 대로 (as soon as; immediately after); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 능력 (能力), 유무 (有無), and 개업 (開業).

explanations.title: 오늘의 漢字語: 유/무 (有/無)
explanations.body: These two Sino-Korean syllables have opposite meanings. 유 (有) means existing or with, whereas 무 (無) means not existing, lacking, or without, and is equivalent to the English prefixes non-, in-, and un-, as in 무독성 (nontoxic) or 무경험 (inexperience). These two syllables are frequently used as prefixes. The book asks you to guess the meaning of 유능/무능, 유명/무명 and 유료/무료 (my answers):

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 능력 (能力)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means ability or capability. The first syllable 능 (能) means able or capable, as in 유능하다 (to be able; to be competent), 무능하다 (to be incompetent; “lacking ability”), 전능하다 (to be omnipotent; “to be capable of all”), 가능하다 (to be possible), and 불가능하다 (to be impossible). The second syllable 력 (力) means power(ful), strength, or strong, as in 체력 (physical strength), 수력 (waterpower; hydropower), 풍력 (wind power), and 부력 (buoyancy; “floating power”). When 력 comes at the beginning of a word, the syllable changes to 역, as in 역도 (weight lifting; “power way”), 역량 (ability; capability; “amount of power”), and 역점 (emphasis; stress; “strong point”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 능력 is “capable power” or “able strength”.

rows: to be able; to be competent
to be omnipotent; “to be capable of all”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 개업 (開業)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means opening up a business. The Chinese character of the first syllable 개 (開) depicts two saloon doors being in the same plane, implying that something is open. Thus the syllable means open, as in 개학 (starting school [after a vacation]; “open school”), 개점 (opening a store; opening a shop), 개원 (opening a clinic), 개회 (the opening of a meeting; the opening of a session), 개폐 (opening and shutting), and 개전 (the commencement of hostilities; the outbreak of war; “open war”). The second syllable 업 (業) means work or business, as in 부업 (an avocation; a second job [in addition to a regular one]; “secondary work”), 농업 (agriculture; farming; “farming business”), 공업 (the manufacturing industry; “manufacturing business”), and 업종 (type of business; category of business). Thus the literal meaning of the word 개업 is “opening a business”. Keep in mind that the antonym of the word is 폐업 (closing a business; going out of business; “close a business”).

explanations.title: 새 단어: the words in the box
explanations.body: The book gives eighteen core words: 개업, 구내식당, 능력, 답답하다, 만족하다, 분위기, 불만, 사표, 상사, 수입, 수출, 야근, 업무, 여유롭다, 유능(하다), 은퇴, 자유롭다, 노후. explanations.title: Topic A: A new employee’s day (신입사원의 하루)
explanations.body: The following description is about a new employee’s typical work day. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the times are spelled out in Hangul.)

examples.text: 김인철 씨는 하루 일과를 오전 다섯 시 반에 시작합니다.
examples.translation: gimincheol ssineun haru ilgwareul ojeon daseot si bane sijakamnida. — Mr. Kim Incheol starts his daily routine at half past five in the morning.

examples.text: 입사 초에는 이른 아침에 일어나는 것이 힘들었지만, 이제는 익숙해졌습니다.
examples.translation: ipsa choeneun ireun achime ireonaneun geosi himdeureotjiman, ijeneun iksukaejeotseumnida. — At the beginning of his employment it was hard to get up early in the morning, but now he has gotten used to it.

examples.text: 정장을 하고 여섯 시 반에 집을 나와서 지하철을 타고 출근합니다.
examples.translation: jeongjangeul hago yeoseot si bane jibeul nawaseo jihacheoreul tago chulgeunhamnida. — He dresses up, leaves home at half past six, and commutes by subway.

examples.text: 아침은 회사 근처 식당에서 간단히 먹습니다.
examples.translation: achimeun hoesa geuncheo sikdangeseo gandanhi meokseumnida. — He has breakfast simply at a restaurant near the company.

examples.text: 김인철 씨 회사는 컴퓨터 부품을 수출하는 회사입니다.
examples.translation: gimincheol ssi hoesaneun keompyuteo bupumeul suchulhaneun hoesaimnida. — Mr. Kim’s company is a company that exports computer parts.

examples.text: 외국어 실력이 업무에 아주 중요하기 때문에 출근 전에 영어학원에 갑니다.
examples.translation: oegugeo sillyeogi eommue aju jungyohagi ttaemune chulgeun jeone yeongeohagwone gamnida. — Because foreign language ability is very important for the work, he goes to an English academy before going to work.

examples.text: 회사에서는 오전에 밤새 해외 바이어들에게서 온 이메일을 확인하고 답장을 합니다.
examples.translation: hoesaeseoneun ojeone bamsae haeoe baieodeuregeseo on imeireul hwaginhago dapjangeul hamnida. — At the company, in the morning he checks the e-mails that came overnight from overseas buyers and replies.

examples.text: 점심은 보통 구내식당에서 동료들과 같이 합니다.
examples.translation: jeomsimeun botong gunaesikdangeseo dongnyodeulgwa gachi hamnida. — He usually has lunch with his colleagues in the company cafeteria.

examples.text: 오후에는 보고서를 작성하고 부서 회의에 참석합니다.
examples.translation: ohueneun bogoseoreul jakseonghago buseo hoeuie chamseokamnida. — In the afternoon he writes reports and attends a department meeting.

examples.text: 퇴근 후에는 회사에서 지원하는 사내 테니스 모임에 나갑니다.
examples.translation: toegeun hueneun hoesaeseo jiwonhaneun sanae teniseu moime nagamnida. — After work he goes to the in-company tennis club supported by the company.

examples.text: 모임에 나가서 대인관계도 넓히고 하루의 피로도 풉니다.
examples.translation: moime nagaseo daeingwangyedo neolpigo haruui pirodo pumnida. — At the club he broadens his interpersonal relationships and also relieves the day’s fatigue.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a news article about employees learning languages
explanations.body: The following news article is about a trend among company employees in Seoul. The book’s hint: if you encounter unknown words, focus on the words you know and use your dictionary as necessary. It asks you to translate an underlined part and to fill in a table in English (recent trend among company employees; ways to follow the recent trend). The article is the book’s (the book writes “김이정 (여, 수출회사 근무) 씨”; here it is “수출회사 근무 김이정 씨”; 6개월 is spelled out; the quotation marks are dropped). The English is mine.

examples.text: 요즘 출퇴근 시간을 이용해 외국어를 배우는 회사원이 많아지고 있다.
examples.translation: yojeum chultoegeun siganeul iyonghae oegugeoreul baeuneun hoesawoni manajigo itda. — These days the number of company employees who use their commuting time to learn foreign languages is increasing.

examples.text: 서울 여의도의 어학원들은 이른 새벽부터 영어회화 수업을 듣는 회사원들로 복잡하다.
examples.translation: seoul yeouidoui eohagwondeureun ireun saebyeokbuteo yeongeohoehwa sueobeul deunneun hoesawondeullo bokjapada. — Language academies in Yeouido, Seoul, are crowded from early dawn with company employees taking English conversation classes.

examples.text: 육 개월 동안 영어학원에 다니고 있는 수출회사 근무 김이정 씨는 유럽의 바이어들과 영어로 말하고 계약서도 영어로 작성해야 하기 때문에 영어 실력이 아주 중요하다고 말했다.
examples.translation: yuk gaewol dongan yeongeohagwone danigo inneun suchulhoesa geunmu gimijeong ssineun yureobui baieodeulgwa yeongeoro malhago gyeyakseodo yeongeoro jakseonghaeya hagi ttaemune yeongeo sillyeogi aju jungyohadago malhaetda. — Ms. Kim Yijeong, who works at an export company and has been attending an English academy for six months, said that English ability is very important because she has to speak with European buyers in English and write contracts in English too.

examples.text: 또 학원에 직접 가지 않고 외국어를 배울 수 있는 인터넷 사이트도 인기를 얻고 있다.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading and speaking): a survey of new employees
explanations.body: Read the survey results and complete the tasks. The book’s hint: if you encounter unknown words, focus on the words you know and use your dictionary as necessary. The task: a. fill in a table with appropriate English bar-graph labels for a bar chart of four bars (가 32.7%, 나 24.4%, 다 18.6%, 라 11.6%; one label, “Educational Background” for 다, is provided); b. read again and fill in the three survey questions in English; c. write what you think are the keys to success at work; d. in pairs, ask your partner in Korean about keys to success and present the combined ideas to the class. The article is the book’s (the percentages and the number of people are spelled out in Hangul; the quotation marks are dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 우리 회사 신입사원이 생각하는 성공의 조건은 대인관계와 영어
examples.translation: uri hoesa sinipsawoni saenggakaneun seonggongui jogeoneun daeingwangyewa yeongeo — The condition for success that our company’s new employees think of: interpersonal relationships and English

examples.text: 회사 인사부에서 작년 우리 기업 신입사원 마흔일곱 명을 대상으로 설문조사를 했다.
examples.translation: hoesa insabueseo jangnyeon uri gieop sinipsawon maheunnilgop myeongeul daesangeuro seolmunjosareul haetda. — The company’s personnel department conducted a survey last year of forty-seven new employees of our company.

examples.text: 성공하기 위한 조건이 무엇이냐는 질문에 삼십이 점 칠 퍼센트의 신입사원이 대인관계라고 답했다.
examples.translation: seonggonghagi wihan jogeoni mueosinyaneun jilmune samsibi jeom chil peosenteuui sinipsawoni daeingwangyerago dapaetda. — To the question of what the condition for success is, 32.7% of the new employees answered interpersonal relationships.

examples.text: 그리고 응답자의 이십사 점 사 퍼센트는 성공의 조건으로 영어실력이라고 대답했으며, 십팔 점 육 퍼센트는 대학원 졸업이나 박사학위와 같은 학력, 십일 점 육 퍼센트는 외국유학 경험을 꼽았다.
examples.translation: geurigo eungdapjaui isipsa jeom sa peosenteuneun seonggongui jogeoneuro yeongeosillyeogirago daedapaesseumyeo, sippal jeom yuk peosenteuneun daehagwon joreobina baksahagwiwa gateun hangnyeok, sibil jeom yuk peosenteuneun oegugyuhak gyeongheomeul kkobatda. — And 24.4% of respondents answered English ability as a condition for success, 18.6% named educational background such as a graduate school degree or a doctorate, and 11.6% named study-abroad experience.

examples.text: 우리 회사의 좋은 점은 무엇인가라는 질문에는 회사의 자기개발 지원이 일 위를 차지했고 우리회사의 나쁜 점을 묻는 질문에는 삼십오 퍼센트가 짧은 휴가라고 대답했다.
examples.translation: uri hoesaui joeun jeomeun mueosingaraneun jilmuneneun hoesaui jagigaebal jiwoni il wireul chajihaetgo urihoesaui nappeun jeomeul munneun jilmuneneun samsibo peosenteuga jjalbeun hyugarago daedapaetda. — To the question “What is good about our company?”, the company’s support for self-development took first place, and to the question asking about the bad points of our company, 35% answered a short vacation.

explanations.title: Topic B: You got promoted to assistant manager, right? (너 대리로 승진했지?)
explanations.body: Two friends meet up at a coffee shop and talk about their work at different companies. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 현태: 종석아, 오랜만이다. 요즘 회사 생활은 어때?
examples.translation: hyeontae: jongseoga, oraenmanida. yojeum hoesa saenghwareun eottae? — Jongseok, it’s been a while. How is life at the company these days?

examples.text: 종석: 힘들어 죽겠어요, 형. 요즘 매일 야근이에요.
examples.translation: jongseok: himdeureo jukgesseoyo, hyeong. yojeum maeil yageunieyo. — It’s killing me, hyung. These days it’s overtime every day.

examples.text: 현태: 그래? 참, 너 대리로 승진했지? 축하한다.
examples.translation: hyeontae: geurae? cham, neo daeriro seungjinhaetji? chukahanda. — Really? Oh, you got promoted to assistant manager, right? Congratulations.

examples.text: 종석: 네, 근데 대리로 일하다 보니 일만 더 많아요.
examples.translation: jongseok: ne, geunde daeriro ilhada boni ilman deo manayo. — Yes, but as I work as an assistant manager, I find there is just more work.

examples.text: 현태: 하지만 능력을 인정받고 다양한 일을 배우잖아?
examples.translation: hyeontae: hajiman neungnyeogeul injeongbatgo dayanghan ireul baeujana? — But you’re recognized for your ability and learn a variety of work, aren’t you?

examples.text: 종석: 그건 맞아요. 그런데 회사 규모가 작아서 일도 많아요.
examples.translation: jongseok: geugeon majayo. geureonde hoesa gyumoga jagaseo ildo manayo. — That’s true. But the company is small so there’s a lot of work too.

examples.text: 현태: 우리 회사 같은 대기업에서는 매일 같은 일을 반복하잖아. 그래서 지겨워하는 동료들도 많아.
examples.translation: hyeontae: uri hoesa gateun daegieobeseoneun maeil gateun ireul banbokajana. geuraeseo jigyeowohaneun dongnyodeuldo mana. — In a large company like mine you repeat the same work every day. So many colleagues are bored.

examples.text: 종석: 그렇구나. 대기업 직원들은 다 만족하는 줄 알았는데.
examples.translation: jongseok: geureokuna. daegieop jigwondeureun da manjokaneun jul aranneunde. — I see. I thought all large-company employees were satisfied.

examples.text: 현태: 그렇지 않아. 그래서 요즘 중소기업으로 이직하는 동료들이 많이 있어.
examples.translation: hyeontae: geureochi ana. geuraeseo yojeum jungsogieobeuro ijikaneun dongnyodeuri mani isseo. — Not so. That’s why many colleagues these days are changing jobs to small and medium companies.

examples.text: 종석: 그래도 형네 회사는 보너스도 많이 주고, 재택근무도 가능하잖아요.
examples.translation: jongseok: geuraedo hyeongne hoesaneun boneoseudo mani jugo, jaetaekgeunmudo ganeunghajanayo. — Still, your company gives big bonuses and allows working from home.

examples.text: 현태: 물론 장점도 많아. 하지만 출장도 자주 있고 상사와의 관계도 힘들어.
examples.translation: hyeontae: mullon jangjeomdo mana. hajiman chuljangdo jaju itgo sangsawaui gwangyedo himdeureo. — Of course there are many advantages. But there are frequent business trips and the relationship with my boss is hard too.

examples.text: 종석: 그래요? 우리 회사는 대기업하고 연봉 차이는 있어도 분위기는 자유로워요.
examples.translation: jongseok: geuraeyo? uri hoesaneun daegieopago yeonbong chaineun isseodo bunwigineun jayurowoyo. — Is that so? My company has a salary gap with large companies but the atmosphere is free.

explanations.title: Footnote: 이직
explanations.body: 이직 can mean job change or job quitting, depending on which Chinese character (移 or 離) is used. In this sentence, the word 이직 (移職) (job change) is used.

rows: change of occupation (移職); separation from one’s position, quitting one’s job (離職)

explanations.title: Core words and phrases of Topic B
explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter); 만족(하다/스럽다), 반복(하다/되다), 불만족(스럽다), 야근(하다), 이직(하다), 인정(하다/받다), 자유(롭다) and 출장(가다) take the forms in parentheses. –다(가) 보니(까) and –줄 알다/모르다 are explained in the grammar.

rows: (滿足) satisfaction; to be satisfied / to be satisfying (~하다/스럽다)
(反復) repetition; reiteration; to repeat; to reiterate; to do over again / to be repeated (~하다/되다)
(不滿足) dissatisfaction; discontent; to be dissatisfying; to be unsatisfactory (~스럽다)
(上司) one’s superior; a senior official
(夜勤) night duty; night work; night shift; to take night duty; to work overtime into the night (~하다)
(認定) recognition; acknowledgment; confirmation; approval; to recognize; to admit; to approve / to be recognized (~하다/받다)
(自由) freedom; liberty; to be free; to be liberal; to be unrestricted (~롭다)
(在宅勤務) telecommuting; telework; “working from home”
to be boring; to be tedious; to be wearisome; to be tiresome
(出張) a business trip; a tour of duty; to go on a business trip (~가다)
discovery or realization while doing something
I thought … / I did not know …

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a survey by Korea Recruit
explanations.body: Read the survey results and complete the tasks. The book glosses 취득: acquisition. It asks you to: a. write the three survey questions in English (the second, “What have you strived for the most at your workplace this past year?”, is given); b. check the two responses to the first question among: lack of time for self-improvement; low annual income; traffic jam during the commute hour; unfairness in promotions. The text is the book’s (the number is spelled out and the quotation marks are dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 코리아 리쿠루트가 직장인 구백칠십오 명에게 세 가지 질문을 했다.
examples.translation: koria rikuruteuga jikjangin gubaekchilsibo myeongege se gaji jilmuneul haetda. — Korea Recruit asked 975 office workers three questions.

examples.text: 첫째 질문은 직장 생활에서 무엇이 가장 힘들었나, 둘째, 한 해 동안 직장에서 노력한 것은 무엇인가, 셋째, 내년에 하고 싶은 일은 무엇인가이었다.
examples.translation: cheotjjae jilmuneun jikjang saenghwareseo mueosi gajang himdeureonna, duljjae, han hae dongan jikjangeseo noryeokan geoseun mueosinga, setjjae, naenyeone hago sipeun ireun mueosingaieotda. — The first question was “What was the hardest in work life?”, the second “What did you strive for at work during the year?”, and the third “What do you want to do next year?”

examples.text: 첫 번째 질문에 대한 대답으로 낮은 연봉이 일 위, 상사와의 문제가 이 위, 그리고 대인관계의 어려움, 반복되는 야근과 자기 개발 시간 부족 순이었다.
examples.translation: cheot beonjjae jilmune daehan daedabeuro najeun yeonbongi il wi, sangsawaui munjega i wi, geurigo daeingwangyeui eoryeoum, banbokdoeneun yageungwa jagi gaebal sigan bujok sunieotda. — As answers to the first question, low annual income was first, problems with the boss second, and then difficulty in interpersonal relationships, repeated overtime and lack of time for self-development, in that order.

examples.text: 두 번째 질문에 대한 답으로 일 위는 이직, 이 위는 자격증 취득, 그 뒤로 자기 개발, 건강 등 이었다.
examples.translation: du beonjjae jilmune daehan dabeuro il wineun ijik, i wineun jagyeokjeung chwideuk, geu dwiro jagi gaebal, geongang deung ieotda. — As answers to the second question, first was changing jobs, second was acquiring certificates, and after that self-development, health and so on.

examples.text: 마지막 질문에는 이직이라는 답이 가장 많았고, 다음으로 외국어 공부와 자기 개발 그리고 자격증 취득 순이었다.
examples.translation: majimak jilmuneneun ijigiraneun dabi gajang manatgo, daeumeuro oegugeo gongbuwa jagi gaebal geurigo jagyeokjeung chwideuk sunieotda. — To the last question, the answer “changing jobs” was the most common, followed by foreign language study and self-development, and then acquiring certificates, in that order.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the answers blank; these are mine.

rows: What was the hardest thing in your work life?
What do you want to do next year?
b. The two responses to the first question
Lack of time for self-improvement; low annual income (traffic jam and unfairness in promotions are not mentioned)

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): a survey on the workplace and mental health
explanations.body: Read the text about the survey results on the relationship between the workplace and mental health. The book asks: 1. Who responded to the survey? 2. Fill in the table in English for paragraphs (나), (다) and (라) with the topic and the result. The paragraphs (가) to (라) are the book’s; the paragraph letters, the triangle marks and the quotation marks are dropped, and the numbers are spelled out in Hangul. The English is mine.

examples.text: 직장인 육십구 퍼센트가 꼽았다 정신 건강에 영향 미치는 일 위는 이 사람
examples.translation: jikjangin yuksipgu peosenteuga kkobatda jeongsin geongange yeonghyang michineun il wineun i saram — 69% of office workers picked: the number one influence on mental health is this person

examples.text: 직장 상사가 직장인 정신 건강에 미치는 영향이 가장 높다는 설문조사 결과가 발표됐다.
examples.translation: jikjang sangsaga jikjangin jeongsin geongange michineun yeonghyangi gajang nopdaneun seolmunjosa gyeolgwaga balpyodwaetda. — The results of a survey have been announced that a boss has the highest influence on an office worker’s mental health.

examples.text: 영국의 유케이지 노동인구연구소는 열 개국의 삼천사백 명 직장인을 대상으로 업무 스트레스, 직장이 정신 건강에 미치는 영향, 일에 대한 감정 등에 대한 설문을 진행했다.
examples.translation: yeonggugui yukeiji nodonginguyeongusoneun yeol gaegugui samcheonsabaek myeong jikjangineul daesangeuro eommu seuteureseu, jikjangi jeongsin geongange michineun yeonghyang, ire daehan gamjeong deunge daehan seolmuneul jinhaenghaetda. — The UKG Workforce Institute of the UK conducted a survey of 3,400 office workers in ten countries about work stress, the effect of the workplace on mental health, feelings about work and so on.

examples.text: 그 결과, 육십구 퍼센트의 직장인이 정신 건강에 가장 큰 영향을 미치는 사람으로 직장 상사를 꼽았다.
examples.translation: geu gyeolgwa, yuksipgu peosenteuui jikjangini jeongsin geongange gajang keun yeonghyangeul michineun sarameuro jikjang sangsareul kkobatda. — As a result, 69% of office workers picked their boss as the person with the greatest influence on mental health.

examples.text: 특히 직장 상사에게 받는 압박 등 부정적인 정신 환경은 가정생활 칠십일 퍼센트, 일상 육십사 퍼센트, 인간관계 육십이 퍼센트 등의 순으로 직장인에 좋지 않은 영향을 미쳤다.
examples.translation: teuki jikjang sangsaege banneun apbak deung bujeongjeogin jeongsin hwangyeongeun gajeongsaenghwal chilsibil peosenteu, ilsang yuksipsa peosenteu, ingangwangye yuksibi peosenteu deungui suneuro jikjangine jochi aneun yeonghyangeul micheotda. — In particular, a negative mental environment such as pressure from the boss had a bad effect on office workers in the order of home life (71%), daily life (64%), human relationships (62%) and so on.

examples.text: 하지만 이 중 삼십팔 퍼센트는 거의 또는 절대 직장 상사와 관계 개선을 위한 대화를 나누지 않았다.
examples.translation: hajiman i jung samsippal peosenteuneun geoui ttoneun jeoldae jikjang sangsawa gwangye gaeseoneul wihan daehwareul nanuji anatda. — But 38% of them had almost or absolutely never had a conversation with their boss to improve the relationship.

examples.text: 그 이유는 스스로 해결할 수 있어야 해서 이십 퍼센트, 상사가 신경을 쓰지 않아서 십육 퍼센트, 상사가 너무 바빠서 십삼 퍼센트 순이었다.
examples.translation: geu iyuneun seuseuro haegyeolhal su isseoya haeseo isip peosenteu, sangsaga singyeongeul sseuji anaseo simnyuk peosenteu, sangsaga neomu bappaseo sipsam peosenteu sunieotda. — The reasons were, in order, that they should be able to solve it themselves (20%), that the boss doesn’t care (16%), and that the boss is too busy (13%).

examples.text: 직장 결정에 대한 질문에서는 응답자 팔십 퍼센트 이상이 고액의 연봉보다 정신 건강을 지킬 수 있는 직장을 선호한다고 답했다.
examples.translation: jikjang gyeoljeonge daehan jilmuneseoneun eungdapja palsip peosenteu isangi goaegui yeonbongboda jeongsin geongangeul jikil su inneun jikjangeul seonhohandago dapaetda. — In the question about choosing a workplace, more than 80% of respondents answered that they prefer a workplace that can protect their mental health over a high salary.

examples.text: 매니저 이상 직급의 직장 상사 칠십 퍼센트도 같은 답변을 했다.
examples.translation: maenijeo isang jikgeubui jikjang sangsa chilsip peosenteudo gateun dapbyeoneul haetda. — 70% of bosses at manager level or above gave the same answer.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the answers blank; these are mine.

rows: 3,400 office workers in ten countries, surveyed by the UKG Workforce Institute of the UK
Who most affects mental health: 69% picked their boss; the boss’s pressure also hurt home life (71%), daily life (64%) and human relationships (62%)
Talking with the boss to improve the relationship: 38% almost or absolutely never did; reasons: should solve it themselves (20%), boss doesn’t care (16%), boss too busy (13%)
Choosing a workplace: more than 80% prefer a job that protects mental health to a high salary; 70% of managers and above agree

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 2 (listening to three conversations in which an employee discusses his work with a junior co-worker and filling in the good and bad points), Activities 1 and 3 (a word-review sentence activity and listening to three short conversations about a man’s satisfaction with his work) and Activity 4 (listening to a new employee and an experienced employee, group exchange and a flip-chart presentation) are audio and group activities.

lessons.title: 457. Ch 36 · Grammar A: the conjunctive ending –다(가) 보니(까)
lessons.subtitle: -다(가) 보니(까) · 배우다 보니까 · 살다 보니까 · 하다 보니 · 배워 보니까 · 발견 · 깨달음

explanations.title: Having been doing something, I find …
explanations.body:
The conjunctive ending –다(가) 보니(까) literally means “because I (stop to) see (what I am doing or what I have been doing)”. It is made up of –다(가) and –보니(까), which you were introduced to in Chapters 20 and 31, respectively.

–다(가) 보니(까) is used to express the speaker’s discovery or realization while engaging in another activity or being in a certain state. Thus, it translates to “having been doing something, I find/discover”. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 한국말을 배우다가 보니까 일본말도 배우고 싶어요.
examples.translation: hangungmareul baeudaga bonikka ilbonmaldo baeugo sipeoyo. — As I have been learning Korean, (I find) I want to learn Japanese as well.

examples.text: 몬트레이에 살다가 보니까 바닷가 도시가 좋아졌어요.
examples.translation: monteureie saldaga bonikka badatga dosiga joajeosseoyo. — Having lived in Monterey, (I discovered) I like coastal cities.

explanations.title: What the examples show
explanations.body: In the first sentence, the speaker finds himself wanting to learn Japanese while learning Korean (probably because he sees a close relationship between the languages). In the second sentence, the speaker realizes he came to like coastal cities while living in Monterey (probably because of his good experience living in Monterey).

explanations.title: Expressing a discovery/realization of something while engaging in an activity
explanations.body: action verb stem + 다(가) 보니(까). More examples (the book writes 한국어를 공부하다 보니 (한국어가) 재미있어요 with an optional topic; the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 매일 컴퓨터를 하다 보니까 눈이 아파요.
examples.translation: maeil keompyuteoreul hada bonikka nuni apayo. — Having worked on the computer every day, I discover that my eyes hurt.

examples.text: 한국어를 공부하다 보니 한국어가 재미있어요.
examples.translation: hangugeoreul gongbuhada boni hangugeoga jaemiisseoyo. — Having studied Korean, I find it is fun.

examples.text: 한 달 동안 출장을 와 있다 보니 가족이 보고 싶어요.
examples.translation: han dal dongan chuljangeul wa itda boni gajogi bogo sipeoyo. — Having been on a business trip for a month, I find myself missing my family.

explanations.title: 참고: –다(가) 보니(까) and –아/어 보니(까)
explanations.body: Both conjunctive endings are used to express the speaker’s discovery or realization of something. However, –다(가) 보니(까) expresses a discovery or realization while engaging in another activity or being in a certain state. On the other hand, –아/어 보니(까) expresses a discovery or realization after engaging in another activity or being in a certain state. For example (the book’s explanation): in the first sentence the speaker discovers Korean is fun while he is learning Korean; in the second sentence the speaker discovers Korean is fun after he learned Korean. (The English is mine.)

examples.text: 한국말을 배우다 보니까 한국말이 재미있어요.
examples.translation: hangungmareul baeuda bonikka hangungmari jaemiisseoyo. — I discover Korean is fun while I am learning Korean.

examples.text: 한국말을 배워 보니까 한국말이 재미있어요.
examples.translation: hangungmareul baewo bonikka hangungmari jaemiisseoyo. — I discover Korean is fun after I learned Korean.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Listening, reading and speaking): List A and List B and the model
explanations.body: In pairs, Student A picks a phrase from List A and reads it aloud; Student B picks a phrase from List B that can be logically connected and completes the sentence with –다(가) 보니(까). The book notes the answers may vary. List A: 시험 공부를 하다; 책을 읽다; 오래 걷다; 대기업에 근무하다; 친구들과 얘기하다. List B: 피곤하다; 밤 열두 시가 다 되다 (the book writes 12시); 장점이 많다; 잠이 오다; 머리가 아프다. The book’s model, then my sample sentences (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 피자를 먹다
examples.translation: ga: pijareul meokda — to eat pizza

examples.text: 나: 피자를 먹다 보니 맛이 좀 이상해요.
examples.translation: na: pijareul meokda boni masi jom isanghaeyo. — As I ate the pizza, I found the taste a little strange.

examples.text: 시험 공부를 하다 보니 피곤해졌어요.
examples.translation: siheom gongbureul hada boni pigonhaejeosseoyo. — As I studied for the exam, I found I got tired.

examples.text: 책을 읽다 보니 밤 열두 시가 다 됐어요.
examples.translation: chaegeul ikda boni bam yeoldu siga da dwaesseoyo. — As I read the book, I found it was almost twelve at night.

examples.text: 오래 걷다 보니 머리가 아파요.
examples.translation: orae geotda boni meoriga apayo. — As I walked a long time, I found my head hurts.

examples.text: 대기업에 근무하다 보니 장점이 많아요.
examples.translation: daegieobe geunmuhada boni jangjeomi manayo. — Having worked at a large company, I find there are many advantages.

examples.text: 친구들과 얘기하다 보니 잠이 와요.
examples.translation: chingudeulgwa yaegihada boni jami wayo. — As I talked with friends, I found I feel sleepy.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 2 (listening to three short conversations in which two friends discuss their work experiences, and filling in the experience and the discovery) is an audio activity.

lessons.title: 458. Ch 36 · Grammar B: an attributive form + 줄 알았다 / 줄 몰랐다
lessons.subtitle: -줄 알았다 · -줄 몰랐다 · 미혼인 줄 알았어요 · 비가 올 줄 몰랐어요 · 결혼한 줄 몰랐어요 · -다는 얘기

explanations.title: “I thought … (but I was wrong)”
explanations.body: In English, we often use the expression “I thought” when our assumption, understanding, or prediction turns out to be wrong, as in “I thought he was American” and “I thought the Korean national team would advance to the final.” In Korean, the expression – 줄 알았다 is used when our assumption, understanding, or prediction turns out to be wrong. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 김 선생님이 미혼인 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: gim seonsaengnimi mihonin jul arasseoyo. — I thought Ms. Kim was not married (but I was wrong).

examples.text: 오늘 비가 올 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: oneul biga ol jul arasseoyo. — I thought it would rain today (but I was wrong).

explanations.title: “I wasn’t aware” / “I didn’t know”
explanations.body: On the other hand, – 줄 몰랐다 is used when we find out something we did not know or were not aware of. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 김 선생님이 미혼인 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.translation: gim seonsaengnimi mihonin jul mollasseoyo. — I didn’t know that Ms. Kim is not married.

examples.text: 오늘 비가 올 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.translation: oneul biga ol jul mollasseoyo. — I wasn’t aware that it would rain today.

explanations.title: Not the same as –(으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다
explanations.body: Keep in mind that – 줄 알았다 and – 줄 몰랐다 are quite different in meaning from –(으)ㄹ 줄 알다 (to know how to do something) and –(으)ㄹ 줄 모르다 (to not know how to do something), which you learned about in Chapter 16. In addition, – 줄 알았다 and – 줄 몰랐다 can be preceded by any attributive form (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 아침에 비가 온 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: achime biga on jul arasseoyo. — I thought that it rained this morning.

examples.text: 아침에 비가 올 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: achime biga ol jul arasseoyo. — I thought that it would rain this morning.

examples.text: 지금 비가 오는 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: jigeum biga oneun jul arasseoyo. — I thought that it was raining right now.

explanations.title: Expressing “I thought … (but I was wrong)” and “I wasn’t aware” / “I didn’t know”
explanations.body: an attributive form + 줄 알았다; an attributive form + 줄 몰랐다. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 지금 비가 오는 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: jigeum biga oneun jul arasseoyo. — I thought it was raining now (but I was wrong).

examples.text: 박 선생님이 영어를 못 하는 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: bak seonsaengnimi yeongeoreul mot haneun jul arasseoyo. — I thought Mr. Park didn’t speak English (but I was wrong).

examples.text: 김 선생님이 결혼한 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.translation: gim seonsaengnimi gyeolhonhan jul mollasseoyo. — I didn’t know that Ms. Kim is married.

examples.text: 내일까지 숙제를 내야 하는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.translation: naeilkkaji sukjereul naeya haneun jul mollasseoyo. — I didn’t know that [we] have to submit our homework by tomorrow.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Listening and speaking): time words and verbs
explanations.body: List A contains time reference words and List B contains verbs. Student A chooses one word from each list and makes a sentence using –(으)ㄴ/는/(으)ㄹ 줄 모르다; Student B repeats the process with different words, and you listen to each other’s sentences and correct any mistakes. List A: 어제, 오늘, 내일, 지금, 일주일 후, 내년, 작년, 올해, 곧. List B: 약혼하다, 떠나다, 슬프다, 결혼하다, 달리다, 기쁘다, 울다, 생일이다. The book’s model and my sample sentences (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 어제 눈이 온 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.translation: ga: eoje nuni on jul mollasseoyo. — I didn’t know it snowed yesterday.

examples.text: 나: 오늘 비가 올 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: na: oneul biga ol jul arasseoyo. — I thought it would rain today.

examples.text: 어제 영희가 약혼한 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.translation: eoje yeonghuiga yakonhan jul mollasseoyo. — I didn’t know Younghee got engaged yesterday.

examples.text: 곧 친구가 떠날 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: got chinguga tteonal jul arasseoyo. — I thought my friend would leave soon.

examples.text: 지금 아기가 우는 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: jigeum agiga uneun jul arasseoyo. — I thought the baby was crying now.

examples.text: 작년에 철수가 결혼한 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.translation: jangnyeone cheolsuga gyeolhonhan jul mollasseoyo. — I didn’t know Cheolsu got married last year.

examples.text: 올해 제 생일이 일요일인 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: olhae je saengiri iryoirin jul arasseoyo. — I thought my birthday this year was on a Sunday.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Listening and speaking): reporting information with –다는 / ~(이)라는
explanations.body: The first student chooses a sentence from Box A and a source from Box B and makes a complete sentence with –다는/~(이)라는; the second student responds using – 줄 알다/모르다. The book’s model (the English is mine; the book’s “or” between the two answers is dropped):

examples.text: 가: 김 대리가 과장으로 승진했다는 얘기 들었어요?
examples.translation: ga: gim daeriga gwajangeuro seungjinhaetdaneun yaegi deureosseoyo? — Did you hear the story that Assistant Manager Kim was promoted to section chief?

examples.text: 나: 그래요? 김 대리는 상사들한테 능력을 인정받아서 승진할 줄 알았어요.
examples.translation: na: geuraeyo? gim daerineun sangsadeulhante neungnyeogeul injeongbadaseo seungjinhal jul arasseoyo. — Is that so? I thought Assistant Manager Kim would be promoted because he was recognized for his ability by his superiors.

examples.text: 나: 아니요. 김 대리가 이렇게 빨리 승진할 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.translation: na: aniyo. gim daeriga ireoke ppalli seungjinhal jul mollasseoyo. — No. I didn’t know Assistant Manager Kim would be promoted this quickly.

explanations.title: Topic C: I plan to enjoy a leisurely retirement (여유로운 노후 생활을 즐기려고 합니다)
explanations.body: The two stories are about retirement plans. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the numbers are spelled out in Hangul: 35년 → 삼십오 년, 5월 → 오 월, 제2의 → 제이의, 15년 → 십오 년.)

examples.text: 김상현 씨는 삼십오 년 동안 우체국에서 근무했습니다.
examples.translation: gimsanghyeon ssineun samsibo nyeon dongan uchegugeseo geunmuhaetseumnida. — Mr. Kim Sanghyun worked at a post office for thirty-five years.

examples.text: 올해 오 월에 정년퇴직을 할 예정입니다.
examples.translation: olhae o wore jeongnyeontoejigeul hal yejeongimnida. — He is scheduled to retire at the normal retirement age in May this year.

examples.text: 요즘 김상현 씨는 부인과 함께 제이의 인생을 준비하고 있습니다.
examples.translation: yojeum gimsanghyeon ssineun buingwa hamkke jeiui insaengeul junbihago itseumnida. — These days Mr. Kim is preparing a second life together with his wife.

examples.text: 은퇴 후에는 답답한 도시를 떠나서 시골로 갈 계획입니다.
examples.translation: euntoe hueneun dapdapan dosireul tteonaseo sigollo gal gyehoegimnida. — After retirement he plans to leave the stuffy city and go to the countryside.

examples.text: 거기에서 여유로운 노후생활을 즐기려고 합니다.
examples.translation: geogieseo yeoyuroun nohusaenghwareul jeulgiryeogo hamnida. — There he intends to enjoy a leisurely life in his old age.

examples.text: 그동안 못했던 취미활동이나 사회봉사활동을 할 생각입니다.
examples.translation: geudongan motaetdeon chwimihwaldongina sahoebongsahwaldongeul hal saenggagimnida. — He plans to do hobbies or social volunteer activities that he couldn’t do in the meantime.

examples.text: 퇴직 후에는 연금과 퇴직금, 그리고 그동안 저축해 놓은 돈으로 생활할 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: toejik hueneun yeongeumgwa toejikgeum, geurigo geudongan jeochukae noeun doneuro saenghwalhal su itseumnida. — After retirement he can live on his pension, severance pay and the money he has saved in the meantime.

examples.text: 박종필 씨는 십오 년이나 다니던 무역회사를 지난달에 그만두었습니다.
examples.translation: bakjongpil ssineun sibo nyeonina danideon muyeokoesareul jinandare geumandueotseumnida. — Mr. Park Jongpil quit the trading company he had worked at for fifteen years last month.

examples.text: 회사에 큰 불만은 없었지만 창업을 하기 위해 사표를 냈습니다.
examples.translation: hoesae keun bulmaneun eopseotjiman changeobeul hagi wihae sapyoreul naetseumnida. — He had no big complaints about the company but handed in his resignation to start a business.

examples.text: 직장경험을 활용해서 학용품을 수출하는 회사를 차리려고 합니다.
examples.translation: jikjanggyeongheomeul hwaryonghaeseo hagyongpumeul suchulhaneun hoesareul chariryeogo hamnida. — He intends to set up a company that exports school supplies, making use of his work experience.

examples.text: 퇴직금이 나오는 대로 사무실과 직원을 구하려고 합니다.
examples.translation: toejikgeumi naoneun daero samusilgwa jigwoneul guharyeogo hamnida. — As soon as his severance pay comes out, he intends to find an office and employees.

examples.text: 그리고 준비가 다 되면 개업을 할 계획입니다.
examples.translation: geurigo junbiga da doemyeon gaeeobeul hal gyehoegimnida. — And when everything is ready, he plans to open the business.

explanations.title: Core words and phrases of Topic C
explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter); 개업(하다), 수입(하다), 여유(롭다), 은퇴(하다), 창업(하다) and 활용(하다) take the forms in parentheses; –은/는 대로 and ~(이)나 are explained in the grammar.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): a Q&A about retirement
explanations.body: Read the Q&A exchange and, in English, identify the advice for successful retirement. The Q&A is the book’s (the “Q:” and “A:” labels are dropped; 제2의 is spelled 제이의); the English is mine.

examples.text: 정년퇴직을 준비하는 사람입니다.
examples.translation: jeongnyeontoejigeul junbihaneun saramimnida. — I am a person preparing for retirement.

examples.text: 퇴직 후 노후생활을 잘하려면 무엇을 준비해야 합니까?
examples.translation: toejik hu nohusaenghwareul jalharyeomyeon mueoseul junbihaeya hamnikka? — What should I prepare to live well in my old age after retirement?

examples.text: 좀 알려 주세요.
examples.translation: jom allyeo juseyo. — Please tell me a little.

examples.text: 은퇴 후 제이의 인생을 즐겁게 사시는 분들이 많습니다.
examples.translation: euntoe hu jeiui insaengeul jeulgeopge sasineun bundeuri manseumnida. — There are many people who enjoy a second life after retirement.

examples.text: 은퇴 생활을 즐겁게 하시는 분들은 모두 은퇴 후에도 바쁘게 지내고 계십니다.
examples.translation: euntoe saenghwareul jeulgeopge hasineun bundeureun modu euntoe huedo bappeuge jinaego gyesimnida. — All of those who enjoy retirement life are keeping busy even after retirement.

examples.text: 취미활동이나 봉사활동 등을 하면서 직장에 다닐 때보다 더 즐겁게 사십니다.
examples.translation: chwimihwaldongina bongsahwaldong deungeul hamyeonseo jikjange danil ttaeboda deo jeulgeopge sasimnida. — Doing hobbies or volunteer activities and so on, they live more happily than when they went to work.

examples.text: 은퇴 후에 무엇을 할지 생각해 보세요.
examples.translation: euntoe hue mueoseul halji saenggakae boseyo. — Think about what you will do after retirement.

examples.text: 부부가 함께 할 수 있는 일이면 더 좋습니다.
examples.translation: bubuga hamkke hal su inneun irimyeon deo joseumnida. — It is even better if it is something a couple can do together.

examples.text: 그리고 노후 연금을 준비하고 저축을 해 두는 것도 중요합니다.
examples.translation: geurigo nohu yeongeumeul junbihago jeochugeul hae duneun geotdo jungyohamnida. — And it is also important to prepare an old-age pension and save money.

explanations.title: The advice, in English (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves two bullets blank; these are my answers.

rows: Keep busy after retirement, for example with hobbies and volunteer activities; think about what you will do, ideally something a couple can do together
Prepare an old-age pension and save money

lessons.title: 460. Ch 36 · Grammar C: emphasizing or exaggerating quantity using ~(이)나
lessons.subtitle: ~(이)나 · 세 번이나 · 여섯 시간이나 · 오백 명이나 · 이십 년이나 · 피자나 햄버거

explanations.title: The noun marker ~(이)나
explanations.body: Recall the noun connector ~(이)나 that indicates alternative nouns, as in 피자나 햄버거 (pizza or hamburger) and 한국이나 중국 (Korea or China). It can also be used as a noun marker attached to a noun. When ~(이)나 is attached to a noun that contains a number, it implies that the number or amount is much larger than the speaker expects. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 저는 그 책을 세 번이나 읽었어요.
examples.translation: jeoneun geu chaegeul se beonina ilgeosseoyo. — I have read the book three times!

examples.text: 여섯 시간이나 숙제를 했어요.
examples.translation: yeoseot siganina sukjereul haesseoyo. — I did homework for six (darn) hours!

explanations.title: What the examples show
explanations.body: In the first sentence, the speaker is bragging that he has read the book three times by emphasizing the number of times he has read it. In the second sentence, the speaker is complaining that he did homework for six hours by exaggerating the number of hours during which he did homework.

explanations.title: Emphasizing or exaggerating a number/amount
explanations.body: numerical expression + (이)나. More examples (the numbers are spelled out in Hangul; the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 파티에 손님을 오백 명이나 초대했어요.
examples.translation: patie sonnimeul obaek myeongina chodaehaesseoyo. — I invited 500 guests to the party!

examples.text: 운전면허시험을 열 번이나 떨어졌어요.
examples.translation: unjeonmyeonheosiheomeul yeol beonina tteoreojeosseoyo. — I flunked the driver’s license test 10 times!

examples.text: 저는 이 회사에서 이십 년이나 일했어요.
examples.translation: jeoneun i hoesaeseo isip nyeonina ilhaesseoyo. — I have worked at this company for 20 years!

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading, speaking and listening): the model
explanations.body: In pairs, each pair gets a set of cards with numerical expressions; Student A picks a card and reads the sentence aloud, and Student B changes the sentence using ~(이)나 to emphasize the number. The book’s model (the book writes LA; the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 몬트레이에서 엘에이까지 차로 다섯 시간 걸립니다.
examples.translation: ga: monteureieseo ereikkaji charo daseot sigan geollimnida. — It takes five hours by car from Monterey to LA.

examples.text: 나: 몬트레이에서 엘에이까지 차로 다섯 시간이나 걸립니다.
examples.translation: na: monteureieseo ereikkaji charo daseot siganina geollimnida. — It takes as many as five hours by car from Monterey to LA.

explanations.title: More sentences (mine)
explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

examples.translation: geu gageeseo chaegeul yeol gwonina sasseoyo. — I bought as many as ten books at that store.

examples.text: 어제 밤을 새워서 커피를 다섯 잔이나 마셨어요.
examples.translation: eoje bameul saewoseo keopireul daseot janina masyeosseoyo. — I stayed up all night yesterday and drank as many as five cups of coffee.

examples.translation: geu yeonghwareul ne beonina bwasseoyo. — I saw that movie as many as four times.

lessons.title: 461. Ch 36 · Grammar D: the conjunctive ending –는 대로
lessons.subtitle: -는 대로 · 도착하는 대로 · 끝나는 대로 · 마치는 대로 · 일어나는 대로 · -자마자

explanations.title: “As soon as” with –는 대로
explanations.body:
Recall from Chapter 20 the conjunctive ending –자마자. It translates to as soon as or immediately after, as in 일어나자마자 샤워했어요 (I took a shower as soon as I got up).

–는 대로 translates similarly and can be used to express that one action or event is immediately followed by another action or event. However, the conjunctive ending –는 대로 implies that the time of an action or event is not determined. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 일어나자마자 샤워했어요.
examples.translation: ireonajamaja syawohaesseoyo. — I took a shower as soon as I got up.

examples.text: 한국에 도착하는 대로 전화하겠습니다.
examples.translation: hanguge dochakaneun daero jeonhwahagetseumnida. — I will call you as soon as I arrive in Korea.

examples.text: 수업이 끝나는 대로 집에 와.
examples.translation: sueobi kkeunnaneun daero jibe wa. — Come home as soon as the class is over.

explanations.title: Why some sentences are ungrammatical
explanations.body: In the sentences above, the arrival time and the time the class ends are not determined. Because of this implication, the following sentences are considered ungrammatical (the book marks them with an asterisk): *7시에 일어나는 대로 샤워합니다 (I take a shower at seven as soon as I get up; a specific time) and *어제 집에 오는 대로 잤어요 (I went to sleep immediately after I came home; a past action that occurred only once).

explanations.title: Expressing “as soon as” or “immediately after”
explanations.body: action verb stem + 는 대로. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 일을 마치는 대로 가겠습니다.
examples.translation: ireul machineun daero gagetseumnida. — I will go as soon as I finish the work.

examples.text: 들어오는 대로 연락주세요.
examples.translation: deureooneun daero yeollakjuseyo. — Please contact me as soon as you come in.

examples.text: 아침에 일어나는 대로 전화할게요.
examples.translation: achime ireonaneun daero jeonhwahalgeyo. — I will call you as soon as I get up.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Listening, reading and speaking): the model
explanations.body: In pairs, each pair gets a set of verb phrase cards; Student A picks a card and conjugates the verb phrase with –는 대로 and Student B makes a complete sentence with the conjugated phrase. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 집에 도착하다.
examples.translation: ga: jibe dochakada. — to arrive home

examples.text: 가: 집에 도착하는 대로
examples.translation: ga: jibe dochakaneun daero — as soon as (you) arrive home

examples.text: 나: 집에 도착하는 대로 저한테 전화하세요.
examples.translation: na: jibe dochakaneun daero jeohante jeonhwahaseyo. — Please call me as soon as you arrive home.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking): a chain of daily routine
explanations.body: As a class, sit in a circle and think of Korean action verbs likely to be used when talking about daily routine, and then, one after another, make sentences with –는 대로 using the previous student’s action verb and another action. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 아침에 일어납니다.
examples.translation: ga: achime ireonamnida. — I get up in the morning.

examples.text: 나: 일어나는 대로 샤워를 합니다.
examples.translation: na: ireonaneun daero syaworeul hamnida. — As soon as I get up, I take a shower.

examples.text: 다: 샤워를 하는 대로 아침을 먹습니다.
examples.translation: da: syaworeul haneun daero achimeul meokseumnida. — As soon as I take a shower, I eat breakfast.

explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

examples.translation: toegeunhaneun daero jibe gaseo swigo sipeoyo. — I want to go home and rest as soon as I leave work.

examples.text: 월급을 받는 대로 저축을 하겠습니다.
examples.translation: wolgeubeul banneun daero jeochugeul hagetseumnida. — I will save money as soon as I get my pay.

examples.text: 연락이 오는 대로 알려 드리겠습니다.
examples.translation: yeollagi oneun daero allyeo deurigetseumnida. — I will let you know as soon as I hear from them.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning, and the book’s parenthesized forms such as ~하다 and ~되다 show how a noun forms a verb. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary sections are blank.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (6시 → 여섯 시; 2년 → 이 년; 100% → 백 퍼센트; 제3중대 → 제삼 중대; 2시간 → 두 시간).

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify, ask about, and discuss daily routines and common concerns at work; talk about plans for starting a new business; and identify, ask about, and discuss the typical lifestyle of retirees.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; –다(가) 보니(까), used to express the speaker’s own discovery/realization of something while engaging in an activity; an attributive form + 줄 알았다 (I thought); an attributive form + 줄 몰랐다 (I did not know; I was not aware); ~(이)나 used to emphasize an amount or number; the conjunctive ending –는 대로 (as soon as; immediately after); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 능력 (能力), 유무 (有無), and 개업 (開業).

lessons.title: 463. Ch 37 · What the chapter teaches, 인명 (人命) · 운전자 (運轉者) · 야간 (夜間)
lessons.subtitle: 사고 · 인명 · 생명 · 운전자 · 야간 · 야경 · 사망자 · 부자간

explanations.title: What Chapter 37 teaches (사고)
explanations.body:
Chapter 37, “Accidents”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and provide basic information on fire, traffic, and military-related accidents; and ask about and summarize fire, traffic, and military-related accidents.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; an attributive form + 것 (the thing that; the things that; what); the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄴ 채(로); the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ 때까지 (until; to the time that); the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ 때마다 (whenever; every time that); the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ 때부터 (since; from the time that); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 인명 (人命), 운전자 (運轉者), and 야간 (夜間).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 인명 (人命)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word, which you frequently encounter in reports about human casualties, means human life. The first syllable 인 (人) means human or person, as you have seen in words such as 한국인, 미국인, and 외국인. The meanings of the second syllable 명 (命) are interesting. Its Chinese character originally meant king’s order. The character 命 is made up of 令 (king) and 口 (mouth). Thus it originally meant an order given through the king’s mouth. Because kings had power to determine one’s life or destiny through their royal order, the syllable evolved to mean life, destiny, order, as in 수명 (life; the span of life), 생명 (life; “living life”), 구명 (lifesaving; clemency; “saving one’s life”), 운명 (destiny; fate; “operating one’s life”), and 명령 (an order).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 운전자 (運轉者)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means a driver (of a vehicle or moving object). The first syllable 운 (運) means driving or operating, as in 운동 (motion; movement; exercise; “driving and moving”), 운반 (conveyance; transfer), 운송 (shipping; transport), 운영 (operation; management), 운하 (a canal; a waterway; “operating river”), and 운행 (running [of transportation]; revolution [of a celestial body]; “operating and moving”). The second syllable 전 (轉) means rolling or turning, as in 자전거 (a bicycle; a cycle; “self-rolling vehicle”), 전업 (change of employment; “turning jobs”), 전입 (moving-in; transference; “rolling in”), and 전이 (change; transition; transfer; “rolling and moving”). The last syllable 자 (者) means person or fellow, as in 사망자 (the dead; the deceased; “dead person”), 탈북자 (a North Korean defector; “person who flees North”), 중상자 (a severely wounded person), 경상자 (a lightly wounded person), 화자 (a speaker; “speaking person”), and 시청자 (a TV viewer; the TV audience; “person who watches and listens”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 운전자 is “person who operates and turns”, and the word refers to a vehicle operator or motorist.

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 야간 (夜間)
explanations.body:
This Sino-Korean word means nighttime or night, more specifically duration or period between sunset and sunrise, as in 야간훈련 (night training), 야간비행 (night flight), and 야간수업 (a night class). The first syllable 야 (夜) means night, as in 야경 (a night view), 야시장 (a night market), and 야학 (night study; an evening class). The second syllable 간 (間) means gap, room, or space (between two objects), as in 공간 (space; room; a gap; “empty space”) and 간격 (a space; an interval). As seen in Chapter 25, however, the same syllable means (in) relationship (between two entities) or between (two entities) when following a word denoting two entities, as in 부자간 ([in] father-and-son relationship; between father and son), 모녀간 ([in] mother-and-daughter relationship; between mother and daughter), etc. Thus the literal meaning of the word 야간 is “night gap” or “night space”, and the word refers to the nighttime from dusk to dawn when no sunlight is visible. The opposite of 야간 is 주간 (daytime; day).

The book asks you to guess the meaning of 야간전투, 야간경기, 야간학교 and 야간열차 (my answers: a night battle; a night game; a night school; a night train).

explanations.title: Vocabulary Learning Strategy: understand the structure of an accident report
explanations.body:
In this chapter, you will learn about the structure of accident reports you may encounter. All accident reports share a similar structure that includes these factors in the following order: When (time); Where (place); Who did what (facts); Casualties or property damages; Cause.

When: time is presented from the general to the specific. (Refer to the Cultural Notes section in Chapter 30, Topic Presentation B, to refresh your memory.) In an accident report, ~께/쯤/경 is often attached to time and indicates the approximate time of the accident (31일 오후 6시 10분쯤).

Where: the place is also presented from the general to the specific. The house or street number is not often disclosed in an accident report (서울 강남구 역삼동 주택가에서).

Who did what: in an accident report, a person’s identity is generally not fully disclosed. 모, which is similar to John Doe in English, is used to replace part or all of a person’s identity. In addition, 김 모 씨 is used to replace a name (e.g., Mr./Ms. Kim) because 씨 indicates generic male or female. Likewise, 양 is used to indicate an unmarried young girl (e.g., 이 모 양 replaces Miss Lee) and 군 is used to indicate an unmarried young boy (e.g., 박 모 군 replaces Mr. Park). Finally, in a written report, people’s ages are usually in parentheses. For example, 장 모 (32) 씨와 김 모 (45) 씨의 차량이 충돌하였습니다.

Casualties and property damages: common key words for damages are 부상, 경상, 중상, 죽다, 다치다, 숨지다, 사망하다, 인명피해, and 재산피해 (두 차량의 운전자가 모두 중상을 입고 병원에서 치료를 받고 있습니다).

Cause: the cause of the incident is generally reported last and listed as known, unknown, or under investigation. If the cause is known, the sentence often ends with 원인은 …으로 밝혀졌습니다 or …으로 드러났습니다 (Its cause is known as …). If police are still investigating, 경찰은 사고 원인을 조사하고 있습니다 (Police are investigating the cause) is generally used.
