explanations.title: Topic A: A fire broke out in a commercial building last night (어젯밤 상가에서 화재가 났습니다)
explanations.body: The following news report is about a fire that occurred at a commercial building. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the times are spelled out in Hangul, “PC” is read 피시, and the anchor and reporter labels are 앵커 and 기자.)

examples.text: 어젯밤 아홉 시, 인천시에 있는 사 층짜리 상가에서 일어난 화재로 두 명이 숨지고 세 명이 중상을 입었습니다.
examples.translation: eojetbam ahop si, incheonsie inneun sa cheungjjari sanggaeseo ireonan hwajaero du myeongi sumjigo se myeongi jungsangeul ibeotseumnida. — A fire that broke out last night at nine o’clock in a four-story shopping building in Incheon left two dead and three seriously injured.

examples.text: 네, 저는 지금 화재 현장에 나와 있습니다.
examples.translation: ne, jeoneun jigeum hwajae hyeonjange nawa itseumnida. — Yes, I am now at the scene of the fire.

examples.text: 신고를 받고 소방차들이 긴급 출동했습니다.
examples.translation: singoreul batgo sobangchadeuri gingeup chuldonghaetseumnida. — After receiving the report, fire engines were dispatched urgently.

examples.text: 하지만 상가가 좁은 골목길에 있어 소방차들이 들어가기가 쉽지 않아 진화에 어려움을 겪었습니다.
examples.translation: hajiman sanggaga jobeun golmokgire isseo sobangchadeuri deureogagiga swipji ana jinhwae eoryeoumeul gyeokkeotseumnida. — But because the shopping building is in a narrow alley, it was not easy for the fire engines to get in, so they had difficulty putting out the fire.

examples.text: 이 화재로 두 명이 숨지고 세 명이 중상을 입는 인명피해가 발생했습니다.
examples.translation: i hwajaero du myeongi sumjigo se myeongi jungsangeul imneun inmyeongpihaega balsaenghaetseumnida. — Because of this fire, human casualties occurred: two died and three were seriously injured.

examples.text: 또 건물 전체가 다 타면서 수억 원의 재산 피해가 났습니다.
examples.translation: tto geonmul jeonchega da tamyeonseo sueok wonui jaesan pihaega natseumnida. — Also, as the whole building burned down, hundreds of millions of won in property damage occurred.

examples.text: 목격자들은 일 층 피시 방에서 큰 폭발 소리와 함께 불이 위층으로 번졌다고 말했습니다.
examples.translation: mokgyeokjadeureun il cheung pisi bangeseo keun pokbal soriwa hamkke buri wicheungeuro beonjeotdago malhaetseumnida. — Eyewitnesses said that with a loud explosion sound from the PC room on the first floor, the fire spread to the upper floors.

examples.text: 소방 당국은 전기 누전으로 불이 시작됐을 가능성이 크다고 보고 정확한 화재 원인을 조사하고 있습니다.
examples.translation: sobang danggugeun jeongi nujeoneuro buri sijakdwaesseul ganeungseongi keudago bogo jeonghwakan hwajae wonineul josahago itseumnida. — The fire authorities, seeing a high possibility that the fire started from an electrical short circuit, are investigating the exact cause of the fire.

explanations.title: Footnote: ~(으)로
explanations.body: ~(으)로 used in this context (이 화재로) means because of or due to.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): a news article about a fire and its EEIs
explanations.body: Read the following news article about a fire and identify the EEIs (Essential Elements of Information). In English, fill in the table with the EEIs (the book glosses 공장: a factory; a plant). The article is the book’s; the numbers are spelled out in Hangul; the English is mine.

examples.text: 이십육 일 오전 영 시 오십일 분경 충남 당진군 신평면 거산리에 있는 한 가구 공장에서 불이 났다.
examples.translation: isimnyuk il ojeon yeong si osibil bungyeong chungnam dangjingun sinpyeongmyeon geosallie inneun han gagu gongjangeseo buri natda. — At about 12:51 a.m. on the 26th, a fire broke out at a furniture factory in Geosan-ri, Sinpyeong-myeon, Dangjin-gun, Chungnam.

examples.text: 공장 일 층에서 시작된 불은 삼 층 직원 기숙사까지 번지면서 기숙사에서 잠자던 공장 직원 세 명이 중경상을 입었다.
examples.translation: gongjang il cheungeseo sijakdoen bureun sam cheung jigwon gisuksakkaji beonjimyeonseo gisuksaeseo jamjadeon gongjang jigwon se myeongi junggyeongsangeul ibeotda. — The fire that started on the first floor of the factory spread up to the third-floor staff dormitory, and three factory employees who were sleeping in the dormitory suffered serious and minor injuries.

examples.text: 이들은 일일구 구조대에 의해 가까운 병원으로 이송되어 치료 중이다.
examples.translation: ideureun irilgu gujodaee uihae gakkaun byeongwoneuro isongdoeeo chiryo jungida. — They were transferred to a nearby hospital by the 119 rescue team and are being treated.

examples.text: 화재 현장에는 소방차 삼십여 대, 소방관 백여 명이 출동했다.
examples.translation: hwajae hyeonjangeneun sobangcha samsibyeo dae, sobanggwan baegyeo myeongi chuldonghaetda. — About thirty fire engines and about a hundred firefighters were dispatched to the fire scene.

examples.text: 불은 여섯 시간 동안 기계와 제품 등을 태우고 오전 두 시 십 분쯤에 진화됐다.
examples.translation: bureun yeoseot sigan dongan gigyewa jepum deungeul taeugo ojeon du si sip bunjjeume jinhwadwaetda. — The fire burned machines and products for six hours and was put out at about 2:10 a.m.

examples.text: 이 불로 소방 당국 추산 삼억 오천만 원 정도의 재산 피해가 발생했다.
examples.translation: i bullo sobang dangguk chusan sameok ocheonman won jeongdoui jaesan pihaega balsaenghaetda. — Because of this fire, property damage of about 350 million won, by the fire authorities’ estimate, occurred.

examples.text: 경찰은 공장에 있던 가스통이 폭발한 것을 화재 원인으로 보고 있다.
examples.translation: gyeongchareun gongjange itdeon gaseutongi pokbalhan geoseul hwajae wonineuro bogo itda. — The police see the explosion of a gas canister that was in the factory as the cause of the fire.

examples.text: 한편, 경찰은 직원들의 말을 토대로 정확한 화재 원인을 조사 중이다.
examples.translation: hanpyeon, gyeongchareun jigwondeurui mareul todaero jeonghwakan hwajae wonineul josa jungida. — Meanwhile, the police are investigating the exact cause of the fire based on the employees’ statements.

explanations.title: The EEI table (mine)
explanations.body: The book’s table asks for time and place, the meaning of the numbers 6, 30 and 100, the consequence of the fire (casualties and/or property damage) and the cause of the fire. My answers:

rows: About 12:51 a.m. on the 26th; a furniture factory in Geosan-ri, Sinpyeong-myeon, Dangjin-gun, Chungnam
The fire burned machines and products for six hours
About thirty fire engines were dispatched
About a hundred firefighters were dispatched
Three dormitory employees seriously or lightly injured; about 350 million won of property damage
Probably the explosion of a gas canister in the factory; the police are investigating based on employees’ statements

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading and speaking): a news article about a cat and a fire
explanations.body: Read the news article about a fire and identify the EEIs; the book glosses 전원: power and 추정(하다/되다): presumption. The headline, “내가 불냈냐옹…” (a play on a cat’s meow, “Did I start the fire, meow?”), is left out here. The article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (3m² → 삼 제곱미터); the English is mine.

examples.text: 대전의 주상복합 아파트에서 고양이가 전기레인지 전원을 켜 발생한 것으로 추정되는 불이 났다.
examples.translation: daejeonui jusangbokap apateueseo goyangiga jeongireinji jeonwoneul kyeo balsaenghan geoseuro chujeongdoeneun buri natda. — A fire presumed to have started when a cat turned on the power of an electric range broke out in a residential-commercial apartment building in Daejeon.

examples.text: 이십 일 영 시 사십육 분께 대전 유성구 한 주상복합 아파트 오 층 주방에서 불이 났다.
examples.translation: isip il yeong si sasimnyuk bunkke daejeon yuseonggu han jusangbokap apateu o cheung jubangeseo buri natda. — At about 12:46 a.m. on the 20th, a fire broke out in the kitchen on the fifth floor of a residential-commercial apartment building in Yuseong-gu, Daejeon.

examples.text: 일일구 소방대원이 출동해 금방 불을 끄면서 내부 삼 제곱미터와 전기레인지 일부만 타 백이십일만 원 정도의 재산 피해가 발생했다.
examples.translation: irilgu sobangdaewoni chuldonghae geumbang bureul kkeumyeonseo naebu sam jegommiteowa jeongireinji ilbuman ta baegisibilman won jeongdoui jaesan pihaega balsaenghaetda. — The 119 firefighters were dispatched and put out the fire quickly, so only three square meters of the interior and part of the electric range burned, causing about 1,210,000 won of property damage.

examples.text: 소방 당국은 집 안에 사람이 없이 고양이 한 마리만 있었던 데다 전기레인지 주변에서 불이 시작된 것으로 보이는 점 등을 토대로 고양이가 전기레인지 스위치를 켜 불이 난 것으로 보고 있다.
examples.translation: sobang danggugeun jip ane sarami eopsi goyangi han mariman isseotdeon deda jeongireinji jubyeoneseo buri sijakdoen geoseuro boineun jeom deungeul todaero goyangiga jeongireinji seuwichireul kyeo buri nan geoseuro bogo itda. — The fire authorities see the fire as caused by the cat turning on the electric range switch, based on the fact that there was no one in the house and only one cat, and that the fire appears to have started around the electric range.

examples.text: 소방 당국 관계자는 집주인이 외출한 사이 고양이가 전기레인지에 올라가 스위치를 켠 것으로 추정하고 자세한 화재 원인을 조사하고 있다고 말했다.
examples.translation: sobang dangguk gwangyejaneun jipjuini oechulhan sai goyangiga jeongireinjie ollaga seuwichireul kyeon geoseuro chujeonghago jasehan hwajae wonineul josahago itdago malhaetda. — An official of the fire authorities said they presume that while the owner was out the cat climbed onto the electric range and turned on the switch, and that they are investigating the detailed cause of the fire.

explanations.title: The EEIs and tips (mine)
explanations.body: The book’s table has the rows time and date, place, casualties and/or property damage, probable cause of the fire and other information; and then asks you and a partner to compile two or three ways for pet owners to prevent their pets from causing house fires. My answers:

rows: A fifth-floor kitchen of a residential-commercial apartment building in Yuseong-gu, Daejeon
No casualties mentioned; three square meters of the interior and part of the electric range burned; about 1,210,000 won of damage
The cat climbed onto the electric range and switched it on while the owner was out
119 firefighters put the fire out quickly; no one was home but one cat
Cut the power or cover the switches of a stove when you go out; keep cats out of the kitchen; use a stove with a safety lock

explanations.body: Follow-up 1 (listening to three YTN audio clips about different accidents and watching the video clips; the book gives 담배꽁초: a cigarette butt and 추산: estimate), Activity 1 (Two-in-One Vocabulary Review, SMART Board), Activity 3 (a news report, a firefighter’s journal and an eyewitness testimony about one fire, in groups of three) and the Topic Presentation A study steps (SMART Board and a class notebook) are audio, video, computer and group activities.

lessons.subtitle: 올림픽대교에서 승용차가 전복됐습니다 · 음주 · 중앙선 · 정면 충돌 · 추돌사고 · 차량 종류 · 한강의 다리 · 하천에 전복된 트럭

explanations.title: Topic B: A passenger car overturned on the Olympic Bridge (올림픽대교에서 승용차가 전복됐습니다)
explanations.body: The following news report is about a traffic accident on the Olympic Bridge. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the numbers are spelled out in Hangul. The title says 승용차 but the report says 승합차, a van.)

examples.text: 교통사고 뉴스입니다.
examples.translation: gyotongsago nyuseuimnida. — This is the traffic accident news.

examples.text: 오늘 오후 두 시쯤 올림픽대교에서 승합차와 버스가 정면 충돌하는 사고가 발생했습니다.
examples.translation: oneul ohu du sijjeum ollimpikdaegyoeseo seunghapchawa beoseuga jeongmyeon chungdolhaneun sagoga balsaenghaetseumnida. — At about two o’clock this afternoon, an accident occurred on the Olympic Bridge in which a van and a bus collided head-on.

examples.text: 승합차 운전자 이 모 씨가 음주 상태에서 중앙선을 넘어 마주 오던 버스를 들이받았습니다.
examples.translation: seunghapcha unjeonja i mo ssiga eumju sangtaeeseo jungangseoneul neomeo maju odeon beoseureul deuribadatseumnida. — The van driver, a Mr. Lee, crossed the center line while drunk and rammed into a bus coming toward him.

examples.text: 또 뒤에서 오던 차들은 앞에 차량이 사고가 난 것을 보고 피하려다 추돌사고를 내기도 했습니다.
examples.translation: tto dwieseo odeon chadeureun ape charyangi sagoga nan geoseul bogo piharyeoda chudolsagoreul naegido haetseumnida. — Also, cars coming from behind saw the vehicle ahead had an accident and, trying to avoid it, caused rear-end collisions.

examples.text: 이 사고로 승합차가 전복되면서 운전자 이 씨가 중상을 입었고, 버스 운전자와 승객 등 십여 명이 중경상을 입었습니다.
examples.translation: i sagoro seunghapchaga jeonbokdoemyeonseo unjeonja i ssiga jungsangeul ibeotgo, beoseu unjeonjawa seunggaek deung sibyeo myeongi junggyeongsangeul ibeotseumnida. — In this accident the van overturned and the driver Mr. Lee was seriously injured, and about ten people, including the bus driver and passengers, suffered serious and minor injuries.

examples.text: 사고 후 올림픽대교는 약 한 시간 동안 통제되었습니다.
examples.translation: sago hu ollimpikdaegyoneun yak han sigan dongan tongjedoeeotseumnida. — After the accident the Olympic Bridge was closed for about an hour.

examples.text: 경찰은 승합차 운전자가 술을 마신 채 일 차선에서 과속으로 달리다가 사고를 낸 것으로 보고 정확한 사고 경위를 조사하고 있습니다.
examples.translation: gyeongchareun seunghapcha unjeonjaga sureul masin chae il chaseoneseo gwasogeuro dallidaga sagoreul naen geoseuro bogo jeonghwakan sago gyeongwireul josahago itseumnida. — The police see the van driver as having caused the accident by speeding in the first lane while drunk, and are investigating the exact circumstances of the accident.

explanations.title: Core words and phrases of Topic B
explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter); 과속(하다), 위반(하다), 익사(하다), 전복(되다), 접촉(하다/되다), 정지(하다), 추돌(하다), 추월(하다), 충돌(하다), 통제(하다/되다) and 파손(되다/시키다) take the forms in parentheses. The book also lists 마주 오다, ~대교, 지나(가)다 and –(으)ㄴ/는/을 것, –(으)ㄴ 채(로) (see the grammar).

rows: to run into; to bump into (physically); to ram
(乘合車) a van; a wagon; a minibus; “riding-together vehicle”
(違反) a violation; a breach; to violate; to break (~하다)
(溺死) drowning; “drowning death”; to be drowned to death (~하다)
(顚覆) overturned; flipped over; to be overturned (~되다)
(接觸) touch; contact; connection; to touch; to make contact / to be connected (~하다/되다)
(正面) the front side; the front; “correct face”
(停止) stop; halt; to stop; to halt (~하다)
(中央線) a median (i.e. on a road); “center line”
(追越) passing; “pursue and pass”; to pass (~하다)
(衝突) a collision; a clash; to collide with (~하다)
(統制) control; regulation; to control; to regulate / to be controlled; to be regulated (~하다/되다)
(破損) damage (of a thing or structure); breakage; to damage / to be damaged (~시키다/되다)

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 1. vehicle types
explanations.body: In Korea, a motorcycle is called 오토바이, which comes from auto(matic) and bi(cycle). 승합차 refers to a (mini)van or minibus. A minivan is often called 봉고차, which literally means “Bongo car”. Bongo was the brand name of the first minivan manufactured by KIA decades ago. Today 승합차 or 미니밴 is more used, and the term 봉고차 is slowly disappearing. 용달차 is a small-sized commercial truck mostly used for deliveries or moving. 화물차 is a freight truck and 유조차 is an oil tanker (i.e. truck). The vehicles you can commonly see on Korean streets:

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 2. –아/어가다 and –아/어오다
explanations.body: Recall –아/어가다 and –아/어오다 from the Chapter 8 Vocabulary Builder. These phrases are used to indicate an action with a targeted location (from one place to another). For example, to express run to (the gym), we say (체육관에) 달려가다 or (체육관에) 달려오다, which literally means “run and go (to the gym)” or “run and come (to the gym)”. The verb preceding –아가다 or –어가다 usually indicates a mode of movement or direction.

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 3. ~사 (死)
explanations.body: The Sino-Korean syllable 사 (死) means death or dying, as in 사망하다 (to die; to pass away). When the syllable is placed at the end of Sino-based words, it indicates death (caused by something); for example, 동사 (凍死) means death from extreme cold; 익사 (溺死) means death from drowning; 질식사 (窒息死) means death from suffocation; 압사 (壓死) means death from crushing; 추락사 (墜落死) means death from falling.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: bridges over the Han River
explanations.body: The Han River is a major river in Korea and runs through the city of Seoul. As of 2021 there are 31 bridges crossing the Han River. The bridges link various districts of Seoul, and usually the name of the bridge comes from the area or the district connected by the bridge. The name of a bridge ends in either ~교 or ~대교 and literally means “a bridge” and “a great bridge”, respectively. Korea’s traffic patrol broadcasting provides information about traffic over each bridge. When a traffic accident occurs on a particular bridge, you will often hear ~대교를 통제하고 있습니다 (~ bridge is restricted) and ~대교로 우회하시기 바랍니다 (Please detour to ~ bridge). 잠수교, which literally means “a bridge under the water”, was designed to sink during floods. Thus, you will often hear traffic broadcasts reporting that 잠수교 is restricted because of flooding.

lessons.title: 467. Ch 37 · Grammar A: expressing “the thing(s) that” or “what”, an attributive form + 것
lessons.subtitle: -는 것 · -(으)ㄴ 것 · -(으)ㄹ 것 · 내가 매일 먹는 것 · 어제 배운 것 · 좋아하는 것은

explanations.title: The attributive form
explanations.body: Recall that in Korean we use an attributive form of a verb to turn the verb or verb phrase into an adjective. For example (the English is the book’s):

rows: a student who will learn Korean

explanations.title: Note
explanations.body: Note that 배우는, 배운, and 배울 are the attributive forms of the verb 배우다. These attributive forms are adjectives modifying the noun (학생) that follows.

explanations.title: The thing(s) that … or what …
explanations.body: Thus, we can express the thing(s) that … or what … by using an attributive form of a verb + 것. For example (the English is the book’s):

rows: the thing (that) I eat every day / what I eat every day
the thing (that) I ate yesterday / what I ate yesterday
the thing (that) I will eat tomorrow / what I will eat tomorrow

explanations.title: As a subject, an object or a complement
explanations.body: These phrases can then be used as a subject, an object, or a complement in a sentence. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 내가 매일 먹는 것은 한국음식입니다.
examples.translation: naega maeil meongneun geoseun hangugeumsigimnida. — What I eat every day is Korean food. (subject)

examples.text: 내가 매일 먹는 것을 먹지 마세요.
examples.translation: naega maeil meongneun geoseul meokji maseyo. — Please don’t eat what I eat every day. (object)

explanations.title: Do not confuse it with the gerund
explanations.body: DO NOT confuse the attributive form + –는 것 in 내가 매일 먹는 것 (what I eat every day/the thing I eat every day) with the gerund –는 것 in 먹는 것 (eating) and 마시는 것 (drinking).

explanations.title: Expressing “the thing(s) that” or “what”
explanations.body: attributive form of a verb + 것. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 한국사람들이 좋아하는 것은 축구입니다.
examples.translation: hanguksaramdeuri joahaneun geoseun chukguimnida. — Soccer is what Koreans like.

examples.text: 내가 한국식당에서 먹은 것의 이름이 뭐죠?
examples.translation: naega hanguksikdangeseo meogeun geosui ireumi mwojo? — What is the name of what I ate at the Korean restaurant?

examples.text: 어제 배운 것을 종이에 적어 보세요.
examples.translation: eoje baeun geoseul jongie jeogeo boseyo. — Please write down what you learned yesterday.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading, speaking and listening): the model
explanations.body: In pairs, Student A studies List A and Student B studies List B; one partner reads a sentence and the other changes it to a sentence using –는/(으)ㄴ/(으)ㄹ 것. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 동생이 꽃을 좋아해요.
examples.translation: ga: dongsaengi kkocheul joahaeyo. — My younger sibling likes flowers.

examples.text: 나: 동생이 좋아하는 것은 꽃이에요.
examples.translation: na: dongsaengi joahaneun geoseun kkochieyo. — What my younger sibling likes is flowers.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Listening and speaking): twenty questions
explanations.body: Sit in a circle. The teacher picks a word from a set of cards, and students ask up to ten yes/no questions using –는/(으)ㄴ/(으)ㄹ 것 to identify the word. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 학생: 보는 것이에요?
examples.translation: haksaeng: boneun geosieyo? — Is it something you look at?

examples.text: 선생님: 아니요.
examples.translation: seonsaengnim: aniyo. — No.

examples.text: 학생: 움직이는 것이에요?
examples.translation: haksaeng: umjigineun geosieyo? — Is it something that moves?

examples.text: 선생님: 아니요.
examples.translation: seonsaengnim: aniyo. — No.

explanations.title: More sentences (mine)
explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

examples.text: 제가 어제 본 것은 영화였어요.
examples.translation: jega eoje bon geoseun yeonghwayeosseoyo. — What I saw yesterday was a movie.

examples.text: 저는 친구가 준 것을 먹었어요.
examples.translation: jeoneun chinguga jun geoseul meogeosseoyo. — I ate what my friend gave me.

examples.text: 내일 할 것을 지금 준비해요.
examples.translation: naeil hal geoseul jigeum junbihaeyo. — I’m preparing now what I will do tomorrow.

lessons.title: 468. Ch 37 · Grammar B: indicating the state of a completed action, –(으)ㄴ 채(로)
lessons.subtitle: -(으)ㄴ 채(로) · 안경을 쓴 채로 · 숨진 채 발견 · 술을 마신 채 운전 · -(으)ㄴ 상태로

explanations.title: In the state of having done (something)
explanations.body: The conjunctive ending –(으)ㄴ 채(로) literally means “in the state of having done (something)”. This conjunctive ending attached to the stem of an action verb is used to indicate that the condition or state of a completed action still remains or is maintained when the main action occurs. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 나는 안경을 쓴 채로 잡니다.
examples.translation: naneun angyeongeul sseun chaero jamnida. — I slept “in the state of having put on my glasses” or I slept with my glasses on.

examples.text: 한 남성이 차 안에서 숨진 채 발견되었다.
examples.translation: han namseongi cha aneseo sumjin chae balgyeondoeeotda. — A man was found “in the state of having died” inside a vehicle or A man was found dead inside a vehicle.

explanations.title: What the examples show
explanations.body: Note that –(으)ㄴ 채(로) is attached to the stem of the action verb 쓰다 (to put on) in the first sentence and to the stem of the action verb 숨지다 (to die; to pass away) in the second sentence. Thus, the first sentence indicates that the speaker’s state of having put on his glasses is maintained while he sleeps. Likewise, the second sentence indicates that a man’s state of death remained when he was found.

explanations.title: Indicating the condition or state of a completed action
explanations.body: action verb stem + (으)ㄴ 채(로). More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 신발을 신은 채로 방 안에 들어갔어요.
examples.translation: sinbareul sineun chaero bang ane deureogasseoyo. — He entered the room “in the state of having put on his shoes” or He entered the room with his shoes on.

examples.text: 김 모 씨는 술을 마신 채 운전하다 접촉 사고를 냈다.
examples.translation: gim mo ssineun sureul masin chae unjeonhada jeopchok sagoreul naetda. — Mr. Kim caused a collision “in the state of having consumed alcohol” or Mr. Kim caused a collision while drunk driving.

explanations.title: 참고: –(으)ㄴ 채(로) and –(으)ㄴ 상태로
explanations.body: –(으)ㄴ 채(로) is interchangeable with –(으)ㄴ 상태로, which also means in the state of having done (something).

examples.text: 한 남성이 차 안에서 숨진 채 발견되었다.
examples.translation: han namseongi cha aneseo sumjin chae balgyeondoeeotda. — A man was found dead inside a vehicle.

examples.text: 한 남성이 차 안에서 숨진 상태로 발견되었다.
examples.translation: han namseongi cha aneseo sumjin sangtaero balgyeondoeeotda. — A man was found dead inside a vehicle (with –(으)ㄴ 상태로).

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Reading): a news report about an actor
explanations.body: The following is a news report about an actor involved in an accident. The book asks you to answer in English: Under what circumstances was the actor found? (three bullets). The book’s article names the actor; here the name is left out. The article is the book’s otherwise; the time is spelled in Hangul and the quotation marks are dropped. The English is mine.

examples.text: 제주에 사는 한 영화배우가 술을 마신 채 운전하다 도로 위에서 잠든 채 발견됐다.
examples.translation: jejue saneun han yeonghwabaeuga sureul masin chae unjeonhada doro wieseo jamdeun chae balgyeondwaetda. — A movie actor living in Jeju was found asleep on a road after driving while drunk.

examples.text: 이 영화배우는 이날 오전 다섯 시께 제주시의 한 도로에 자신의 스포츠유틸리티차량을 세워 둔 채 차 안에서 잠을 자고 있었다.
examples.translation: i yeonghwabaeuneun inal ojeon daseot sikke jejusiui han doroe jasinui seupocheuyutilliticharyangeul sewo dun chae cha aneseo jameul jago isseotda. — At about 5 a.m. that day, the actor was sleeping inside his own SUV, which he had left parked on a road in Jeju City.

examples.text: 경찰은 음주운전으로 인한 다른 사고는 없었다고 말했다.
examples.translation: gyeongchareun eumjuunjeoneuro inhan dareun sagoneun eopseotdago malhaetda. — The police said there were no other accidents caused by drunk driving.

examples.text: 더 자세한 경위를 조사할 예정이라고 말했다.
examples.translation: deo jasehan gyeongwireul josahal yejeongirago malhaetda. — They said they plan to investigate the circumstances in more detail.

explanations.title: The answer (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the bullets blank; my answers:

rows: He had been driving after drinking
He was found asleep inside his SUV, which was left parked on a road, at about 5 a.m.
No other accident caused by drunk driving was reported; the police will investigate further

explanations.title: Topic C: There was an accident during firing training (사격 훈련 중에 사고가 났습니다)
explanations.body: Captain Chung is reporting to Major Kim about an accident that happened a few minutes ago. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the unit numbers are spelled out in Hangul.)

examples.text: 정 대위: 김 소령님, 조금 전 야간 사격 훈련 중 총기 오발 사고가 있었습니다.
examples.translation: jeong daewi: gim soryeongnim, jogeum jeon yagan sagyeok hullyeon jung chonggi obal sagoga isseotseumnida. — Major Kim, there was a firearm misfire accident during night firing training a little while ago.

examples.text: 김 소령: 총기 오발 사고? 어느 부대야?
examples.translation: gim soryeong: chonggi obal sago? eoneu budaeya? — A firearm misfire accident? Which unit?

examples.text: 정 대위: 오 중대 제이 소대에서 사고가 발생했습니다.
examples.translation: jeong daewi: o jungdae jei sodaeeseo sagoga balsaenghaetseumnida. — The accident occurred in the 2nd platoon of the 5th company.

examples.text: 김 소령: 그래? 사상자가 있어?
examples.translation: gim soryeong: geurae? sasangjaga isseo? — Is that so? Are there casualties?

examples.text: 정 대위: 사병 한 명이 팔에 부상을 입었습니다.
examples.translation: jeong daewi: sabyeong han myeongi pare busangeul ibeotseumnida. — One enlisted soldier was injured in the arm.

examples.text: 김 소령: 사격 훈련할 때는 실탄을 쓰니까 항상 조심해야지. 근데, 왜 사고가 났어?
examples.translation: gim soryeong: sagyeok hullyeonhal ttaeneun siltaneul sseunikka hangsang josimhaeyaji. geunde, wae sagoga nasseo? — Since we use live ammunition when training on the range, we have to be careful at all times. But why did the accident happen?

examples.text: 정 대위: 사병이 총기를 부주의하게 다루었다고 합니다.
examples.translation: jeong daewi: sabyeongi chonggireul bujuuihage darueotdago hamnida. — They say the soldier handled the firearm carelessly.

examples.text: 김 소령: 부상을 입은 사병은 지금 어디에 있어?
examples.translation: gim soryeong: busangeul ibeun sabyeongeun jigeum eodie isseo? — Where is the injured soldier now?

examples.text: 정 대위: 사고 후 즉시 육군 병원으로 후송되었습니다.
examples.translation: jeong daewi: sago hu jeuksi yukgun byeongwoneuro husongdoeeotseumnida. — Right after the accident he was evacuated to the Army hospital.

examples.text: 김 소령: 다른 사병들은 괜찮아?
examples.translation: gim soryeong: dareun sabyeongdeureun gwaenchana? — Are the other soldiers all right?

examples.text: 정 대위: 다른 사병들은 모두 무사합니다. 사병들에 의하면 사격 교관이 빠르고 침착하게 응급 조치를 잘 취했다고 합니다. 그 덕분에 부상자가 적었다고 합니다.
examples.translation: jeong daewi: dareun sabyeongdeureun modu musahamnida. sabyeongdeure uihamyeon sagyeok gyogwani ppareugo chimchakage eunggeup jochireul jal chwihaetdago hamnida. geu deokbune busangjaga jeogeotdago hamnida. — The other soldiers are all safe. According to the soldiers, the range instructor took emergency measures quickly and calmly. They say that thanks to that there were few injured.

examples.text: 김 소령: 알았어. 부상당한 사병 상태가 괜찮아질 때까지 상태를 계속 보고하도록 해.
examples.translation: gim soryeong: arasseo. busangdanghan sabyeong sangtaega gwaenchanajil ttaekkaji sangtaereul gyesok bogohadorok hae. — Understood. Keep reporting the injured soldier’s condition until he gets better.

examples.text: 정 대위: 네. 알겠습니다.
examples.translation: jeong daewi: ne. algetseumnida. — Yes, sir. Understood.

explanations.title: –(으)ㄹ 때(에): when
explanations.body: Consider the literal meaning of the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ 때(에), which translates to when. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 출근할 때에 차가 많이 막혀요.
examples.translation: chulgeunhal ttaee chaga mani makyeoyo. — The traffic is quite jammed when I leave for work.

examples.text: 숙제를 할 때 음악을 듣지 마세요.
examples.translation: sukjereul hal ttae eumageul deutji maseyo. — When you do your homework, please don’t listen to music.

explanations.title: 때 and the time marker 에
explanations.body: 때 by itself is a noun that means time or moment (e.g., 그때 [that time] and 점심 때 [lunch time or time for lunch]) and ~에 is a time marker that translates to at, on, or in (e.g., 7시에 [at seven], 월요일에 [on Monday], and 2002년에 [in 2002]). Thus, the literal meaning of –(으)ㄹ 때에 is “at the time (that)” or “at the moment (that)”.

explanations.title: Replacing 에 with other time markers
explanations.body: When 에 in –(으)ㄹ 때에 is replaced with the following time markers, we get the following English meanings:

examples.text: 전화할 때마다 통화 중이에요.
examples.translation: jeonhwahal ttaemada tonghwa jungieyo. — Whenever I call (them), the line is busy.

examples.text: 시간이 날 때마다 등산해요.
examples.translation: sigani nal ttaemada deungsanhaeyo. — Whenever I find time, I go mountain climbing.

examples.text: 출근할 때부터 배가 아팠어요.
examples.translation: chulgeunhal ttaebuteo baega apasseoyo. — I have had a stomachache since I left for work.

examples.text: 어렸을 때부터 독서가 취미예요.
examples.translation: eoryeosseul ttaebuteo dokseoga chwimiyeyo. — Reading books has been my hobby since I was young.

examples.text: 숙제를 다 할 때까지 놀지 마.
examples.translation: sukjereul da hal ttaekkaji nolji ma. — Don’t play until you complete your homework.

examples.text: 친구가 전화할 때까지 잤어요.
examples.translation: chinguga jeonhwahal ttaekkaji jasseoyo. — I slept until my friend called.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): choose 마다, 부터 or 까지
explanations.body: Choosing between 마다, 부터, and 까지, fill in the blanks with the correct marker. The sentences are the book’s (LA is read 엘에이; 40년 is spelled out); the blanks are filled in with my answers; the English is mine.

rows: 진희는 대학교에 입학할 때부터 졸업할 때까지 장학금을 받았습니다.
Jinhee received a scholarship from the time she entered university until she graduated.
저는 엘에이에 자주 갑니다. 엘에이에 갈 때마다 미용실에 가서 머리를 해요.
I often go to LA. Whenever I go to LA, I go to a hair salon and get my hair done.
오늘 아침에 집을 나올 때부터 비가 왔는데 아직도 오는군요.
It was raining from the time I left home this morning and it is still raining.
아버지는 지난 달 퇴직할 때까지 사십 년 동안 같은 곳에서 일하셨어요.
My father worked in the same place for forty years until he retired last month.
저는 요리하는 것을 좋아해서 시간이 있을 때마다 요리를 합니다.
I like cooking, so I cook whenever I have time.
성미는 피아노를 어릴 때부터 배워서 지금은 상당히 잘 칩니다.
Seongmi has learned piano since she was young, so now she plays quite well.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading): a DLI student’s journal entry
explanations.body: Read the journal entry of a DLI student and complete the partial translation by filling in the blanks in English (the book gives a partial English translation with six blanks: since I woke up; until I went for lunch; until the afternoon class started; every time I go to the clinic; until my mother called). The entry is the book’s with the numbers spelled out; the English is mine.

examples.text: 오늘 아침에 일어날 때부터 머리가 아팠다.
examples.translation: oneul achime ireonal ttaebuteo meoriga apatda. — I had a headache from the time I woke up this morning.

examples.text: 그래서 학교에 조금 늦게 열 시쯤 갔다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo hakgyoe jogeum neutge yeol sijjeum gatda. — So I went to school a little late, around ten.

examples.text: 점심식사 하러 갈 때까지 공부를 좀 하고 기숙사에 돌아와서 오후 수업 시작할 때까지 잤다.
examples.translation: jeomsimsiksa hareo gal ttaekkaji gongbureul jom hago gisuksae dorawaseo ohu sueop sijakal ttaekkaji jatda. — I studied a bit until it was time to go to lunch, came back to the dormitory and slept until the afternoon class started.

examples.text: 그래도 머리가 아파서 선생님께 전화를 하고 의무실에 갔다.
examples.translation: geuraedo meoriga apaseo seonsaengnimkke jeonhwareul hago uimusire gatda. — I still had a headache, so I called the teacher and went to the medical clinic.

examples.text: 의무실에 갈 때마다 사람이 많아서 기다려야 하는데 다행히 오늘은 사람이 별로 없었다.
examples.translation: uimusire gal ttaemada sarami manaseo gidaryeoya haneunde dahaenghi oneureun sarami byeollo eopseotda. — Every time I go to the clinic there are many people so I have to wait, but fortunately there weren’t many people today.

examples.text: 약을 받아서 먹고 돌아와서 저녁 아홉 시쯤 어머니가 전화하실 때까지 잤다.
examples.translation: yageul badaseo meokgo dorawaseo jeonyeok ahop sijjeum eomeoniga jeonhwahasil ttaekkaji jatda. — I received the medicine, took it, came back and slept until my mother called at around nine in the evening.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Listening and speaking): the interview model
explanations.body: Read the questions in the first column of the table (어릴 때부터 무엇을 했어요? 어릴 때는 어땠어요?; 고등학교에 다닐 때까지 무엇을 했어요? 어릴 때는 어땠어요?; 고향에 갈 때마다 무엇을 해요?), answer them in Korean using –(으)ㄹ 때마다, –(으)ㄹ 때부터 and –(으)ㄹ 때까지, interview a partner, and report to the class. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 어릴 때부터 무엇을 했어요? 어릴 때는 어땠어요?
examples.translation: ga: eoril ttaebuteo mueoseul haesseoyo? eoril ttaeneun eottaesseoyo? — What did you do from when you were young? What were you like when you were young?

examples.text: 나: 어릴 때부터 저는 키가 컸어요.
examples.translation: na: eoril ttaebuteo jeoneun kiga keosseoyo. — I have been tall since I was young.

examples.text: 가: 박 일병은 어릴 때부터 키가 컸어요. 고등학교에 다닐 때까지 드럼을 쳤어요. 고향에 갈 때마다 박 일병은 서핑을 해요.
examples.translation: ga: bak ilbyeongeun eoril ttaebuteo kiga keosseoyo. godeunghakgyoe danil ttaekkaji deureomeul cheosseoyo. gohyange gal ttaemada bak ilbyeongeun seopingeul haeyo. — Private First Class Park has been tall since he was young. He played drums until he went to high school. Whenever he goes to his hometown, he surfs.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 2 (listening to four conversations in which a man explains that whenever he does something, something else happens, marking it good or bad and translating the sentence) is an audio activity.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): a news article about a military accident
explanations.body: The following news article is about a military accident. The book asks you to fill in a table in English: type of accident; how the accident occurred; casualties; possible cause. The book glosses 밝혀지다: to be revealed; 민가: private home; 기수: the nose (of a plane); 탈출하다: to escape; 양호하다: good. The headline (“F-4E 전투기 ‘엔진 화재’로 서해 추락… 조종사 2명 무사”) is left out; the article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (F-4E is read 에프포이); the English is mine.

examples.text: 공군 에프포이 팬텀 전투기가 십이 일 비행 중 추락했으나 조종사 두 명은 무사한 것으로 확인됐다.
examples.translation: gonggun epeupoi paenteom jeontugiga sibi il bihaeng jung churakaesseuna jojongsa du myeongeun musahan geoseuro hwagindwaetda. — An Air Force F-4E Phantom fighter crashed during flight on the 12th, but the two pilots were confirmed to be safe.

examples.text: 공군과 해경 등에 따르면 이날 낮 열두 시 이십 분쯤 경기도 화성 일대 상공을 날던 에프포이 전투기 한 대가 전곡항 남쪽 구 킬로미터 지점 서해상에 추락했다.
examples.translation: gonggungwa haegyeong deunge ttareumyeon inal nat yeoldu si isip bunjjeum gyeonggido hwaseong ildae sanggongeul naldeon epeupoi jeontugi han daega jeongokang namjjok gu killomiteo jijeom seohaesange churakaetda. — According to the Air Force and the Coast Guard, at about 12:20 p.m. that day, one F-4E fighter flying over the Hwaseong area in Gyeonggi-do crashed into the West Sea nine kilometers south of Jeongok Port.

examples.text: 사고기 조종사들은 비행 중 엔진에서 화재가 발생하자, 민가가 없는 해안 지역으로 기수를 돌렸고, 이후 비상 탈출에 성공했다.
examples.translation: sagogi jojongsadeureun bihaeng jung enjineseo hwajaega balsaenghaja, mingaga eomneun haean jiyeogeuro gisureul dollyeotgo, ihu bisang talchure seonggonghaetda. — When a fire broke out in the engine during the flight, the pilots of the crashed plane turned its nose toward a coastal area with no private homes and then succeeded in an emergency escape.

examples.text: 사고 지점 인근 해역에서는 어선 한 척이 조업 중이었다.
examples.translation: sago jijeom ingeun haeyeogeseoneun eoseon han cheogi joeop jungieotda. — In the sea area near the crash site, one fishing boat was operating.

examples.text: 조종사 두 명은 이 어선에 구조된 후 항공우주의료원으로 이송됐다.
examples.translation: jojongsa du myeongeun i eoseone gujodoen hu hanggongujuuiryowoneuro isongdwaetda. — The two pilots were rescued by this fishing boat and then transferred to the Aerospace Medical Center.

examples.text: 공군 관계자는 조종사들의 건강 상태는 양호하다고 설명했다.
examples.translation: gonggun gwangyejaneun jojongsadeurui geongang sangtaeneun yanghohadago seolmyeonghaetda. — An Air Force official explained that the pilots’ health condition is good.

examples.text: 이번 추락사고 원인은 아직 확인되지 않았으나, 군 안팎에서는 전투기의 노후에 따른 고장일 가능성으로 보고 있다.
examples.translation: ibeon churaksago wonineun ajik hwagindoeji anasseuna, gun anpakkeseoneun jeontugiui nohue ttareun gojangil ganeungseongeuro bogo itda. — The cause of this crash has not yet been confirmed, but inside and outside the military it is seen as possibly a breakdown due to the aging of the fighter.

explanations.title: The table filled in (mine)
explanations.body: The book leaves the table blank; my answers:

rows: A military aircraft crash (an F-4E fighter)
A fire broke out in the engine; the pilots steered toward an area without houses, then escaped; the plane crashed into the sea nine kilometers south of Jeongok Port
None; both pilots were rescued by a fishing boat and are in good health
Not yet confirmed; possibly a breakdown due to the aircraft’s age

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Listening, reading, writing and speaking): reporting an accident
explanations.body: You are participating in a combined exercise with an ROK intelligence unit and receive a radio message about an accident. In two groups you listen to Message A or Message B, summarize it in English, exchange the information in Korean with a student from the other group, and then report the accident to your commander with your partner, preparing the presentation in the class notebook.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with.

Now I am able to: identify and provide basic information on fire, traffic, and military-related accidents; and ask about and summarize fire, traffic, and military-related accidents.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; an attributive form + 것 (the thing that; the things that; what); the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄴ 채(로); the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ 때까지 (until; to the time that); the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ 때마다 (whenever; every time that); the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ 때부터 (since; from the time that); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 인명 (人命), 운전자 (運轉者), and 야간 (夜間).

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 2 (listening to two audio clips from YTN and MBC about different accidents and watching the video clips; the book glosses 계곡: valley; 자세: position; 파열: damage) and the listening parts of Activity 4 are audio and video activities.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning, and the book’s parenthesized forms such as ~하다 and ~되다 show how a noun forms a verb. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (5월 → 오 월; 20명 → 이십 명; 30% → 삼십 퍼센트; 119 → 일일구; 7층짜리 → 칠 층짜리; 24시간 → 스물네 시간; 5척 → 다섯 척; NLL is dropped).

lessons.title: 473. Ch 38 · What the chapter teaches, 폭력 (暴力) · 강력 (强力) · 불법 (不法)
lessons.subtitle: 범죄 · 폭력 · 폭설 · 체력 · 강력 · 강자 · 불법 · 불규칙 · 법원

explanations.title: What Chapter 38 teaches (범죄)
explanations.body:
Chapter 38, “Crime”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and discuss serious crimes such as murder, robbery, theft, sexual assault, violence, etc.; identify and describe physical appearance; identify instances of juvenile delinquency such as bullying and drug addiction; and identify shifting trends of crimes and discuss recent crimes such as ID theft and voice phishing scams.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; –는/(으)ㄴ 대로 and ~대로 (in accordance with; as); the auxiliary verb –고 말다; the auxiliary verb –아/어 있다; expressing “as long as” using –(으)ㄴ/는 한; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 폭력 (暴力), 강력 (强力), and 불법 (不法).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 폭력 (暴力)
explanations.body:
This Sino-Korean word means violence or assault. Both syllables of the word should be familiar to you because the first syllable 폭 (暴) meaning fierce or violent, as in 폭우 (a rainstorm) and 폭등 (a sudden jump; a sharp rise), and the second syllable 력 (力), meaning power or strength, as in 인력 (manpower), 수력 (water power), and 역도 (weightlifting; “power way”), were introduced earlier. Thus the literal meaning of the word 폭력 is “fierce power” or “violent power”, and the word refers to an exertion of (physical) force so as to injure or abuse.

The book asks you to guess the meaning of 폭설, 폭음, 폭식, 체력, 화력 and 역도 (my answers are in the table).

rows: a sudden jump; a sharp rise
a loud explosion sound; heavy drinking

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 강력 (强力)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means great (physical) strength, power, or might. The first syllable 강 (强) means strong or powerful, as in 강자 (a strong man; the strong), 강대국 (a big powerful country; a powerful country), 강약 (strength and weakness; a stress [in music]), 강적 (a formidable enemy; a formidable rival; “strong enemy”), 강진 (a severe earthquake), and 강화 (strengthening). The second syllable 력 (力) means power or strength. Thus the literal meaning of the word 강력 is “strong power” or “powerful strength”.

rows: a big powerful country; a powerful country

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 불법 (不法)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means illegality or unlawfulness. The first syllable 불 (不), which is used as a prefix, means not or no, and its English equivalents are non-, im-, il-, in-, ir-, and un-, as in 불규칙 (irregularity; “no regularity”), 불완전 (imperfection), 불이익 (a disadvantage; a handicap), and 불운 (misfortune; adversity; “no luck”). Keep in mind that 불 becomes 부 when it comes before a syllable that begins with ㄷ or ㅈ, as in 부동 (immobility; “no moving”), 부자연 (unnaturalness) and 부자유 (lack of freedom). The second syllable 법 (法) means law or method, as 법원 (a court of justice; a courtroom), 법관 (a judicial officer; a judge; the judiciary), 민법 (civil law; “people law”), 형법 (criminal law), and 사법부 (the judicial branch). Thus the literal meaning of the word 불법 is “no law” or “not lawful”, and the word refers to unlawfulness, illegality, illegitimacy, lawlessness, or injustice.

explanations.title: Activity 3: a middle school student’s concern
explanations.body: The following text is about a middle school student’s concerns posted on an online Q&A section. The book asks you to complete the text by filling in the blanks with the appropriate words from the list 가출, 중독, 불량, 벗어나다, 협박, 거짓말, 괴롭히다, 빼앗다 (one word is not used). The text below is completed with my answers (불량, 빼앗다, 거짓말, 가출, 벗어나다, 괴롭히다, 협박; 중독 is not used); the ellipsis and the site’s labels are left out; the English is mine.

examples.text: 안녕하세요?
examples.translation: annyeonghaseyo? — Hello?

examples.text: 저는 중학교 삼 학년 때부터 불량 서클 친구들과 어울려서 나쁜 일을 많이 했어요.
examples.translation: jeoneun junghakgyo sam hangnyeon ttaebuteo bullyang seokeul chingudeulgwa eoullyeoseo nappeun ireul mani haesseoyo. — From the third year of middle school, I hung out with friends in a delinquent club and did many bad things.

examples.text: 반 친구들 중 저보다 약한 학생의 돈도 빼앗고 왕따도 시켰어요.
examples.translation: ban chingudeul jung jeoboda yakan haksaengui dondo ppaeatgo wangttado sikyeosseoyo. — I also took money from students in my class weaker than me and bullied them.

examples.text: 부모님께 거짓말로 학원비 낸다고 하고 돈 받아 게임비로 썼어요.
examples.translation: bumonimkke geojinmallo hagwonbi naendago hago don bada geimbiro sseosseoyo. — I told my parents with a lie that I was paying academy fees, took money and spent it on games.

examples.text: 담배를 피우고 술도 마시고 집에서 가출도 여러 번 했어요.
examples.translation: dambaereul piugo suldo masigo jibeseo gachuldo yeoreo beon haesseoyo. — I smoked, drank, and ran away from home many times.

examples.text: 그렇지만 고등학생이 되고 그런 생활에서 벗어나고 싶었어요.
examples.translation: geureochiman godeunghaksaengi doego geureon saenghwareseo beoseonago sipeosseoyo. — But after becoming a high school student I wanted to break away from that life.

examples.text: 불량 학생에서 좋은 학생, 좋은 친구가 되고 싶고, 부모님께 좋은 딸이 되고 싶었어요.
examples.translation: bullyang haksaengeseo joeun haksaeng, joeun chinguga doego sipgo, bumonimkke joeun ttari doego sipeosseoyo. — I wanted to go from a delinquent student to a good student and a good friend, and to be a good daughter to my parents.

examples.text: 그래서 서클에서 나왔어요.
examples.translation: geuraeseo seokeureseo nawasseoyo. — So I left the club.

examples.text: 그런데 서클 친구들이 저를 찾아와 매일 때리고 괴롭혔어요.
examples.translation: geureonde seokeul chingudeuri jeoreul chajawa maeil ttaerigo goeropyeosseoyo. — But the club friends came looking for me and beat and tormented me every day.

examples.text: 그리고 이 사실을 부모님이나 학교에 알리면 죽이겠다고 협박을 해요.
examples.translation: geurigo i sasireul bumonimina hakgyoe allimyeon jugigetdago hyeopbageul haeyo. — And they threaten that if I tell my parents or school about this, they will kill me.

examples.text: 어떻게 해야할 지 모르겠어요.
examples.translation: eotteoke haeyahal ji moreugesseoyo. — I don’t know what to do.

examples.text: 도와주세요.
examples.translation: dowajuseyo. — Please help me.

explanations.title: Topic A: The suspect in the convenience store robbery-murder was caught (편의점 강도살인 용의자가 붙잡혔어요)
explanations.body: The following text includes an excerpt from a newspaper article about a robbery and murder, followed by an eyewitness’s statement. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the numbers are spelled out in Hangul. This is a news report of a fatal crime.)

examples.text: 지난 팔 일 밤 인천시 계양구에 있는 편의점에서 서른두 살 권 모 씨가 종업원을 흉기로 살해하고 도주했습니다.
examples.translation: jinan pal il bam incheonsi gyeyanggue inneun pyeonuijeomeseo seoreundu sal gwon mo ssiga jongeobwoneul hyunggiro salhaehago dojuhaetseumnida. — On the night of the 8th, in a convenience store in Gyeyang-gu, Incheon, a 32-year-old Mr. Kwon killed an employee with a lethal weapon and fled.

examples.text: 권 씨는 이날 밤 열한 시쯤 편의점에 들어가 종업원을 칼로 찌른 후 현금 사십여만 원을 빼앗아 도주한 혐의를 받고 있습니다.
examples.translation: gwon ssineun inal bam yeolhan sijjeum pyeonuijeome deureoga jongeobwoneul kallo jjireun hu hyeongeum sasibyeoman woneul ppaeasa dojuhan hyeomuireul batgo itseumnida. — Mr. Kwon is suspected of entering the convenience store at about eleven o’clock that night, stabbing the employee with a knife, and fleeing with about 400,000 won in cash.

examples.text: 범행 후 그는 편의점 근처 집에서 옷을 갈아입고 택시를 타고 달아났습니다.
examples.translation: beomhaeng hu geuneun pyeonuijeom geuncheo jibeseo oseul garaipgo taeksireul tago daranatseumnida. — After the crime he changed clothes at a house near the convenience store and ran away by taxi.

examples.text: 그 후 권 씨는 경기도 부천시 한 모텔에서 숨어 있다가 모텔 주인의 신고를 받은 경찰에게 붙잡혔습니다.
examples.translation: geu hu gwon ssineun gyeonggido bucheonsi han motereseo sumeo itdaga motel juinui singoreul badeun gyeongcharege butjapyeotseumnida. — After that Mr. Kwon was hiding at a motel in Bucheon, Gyeonggi-do, and was caught by police who received a report from the motel owner.

examples.text: 권 씨가 범행을 저지른 지 이틀 만입니다.
examples.translation: gwon ssiga beomhaengeul jeojireun ji iteul manimnida. — It was two days after Mr. Kwon committed the crime.

examples.text: 경찰은 권 씨를 강도살인 혐의로 체포했습니다.
examples.translation: gyeongchareun gwon ssireul gangdosarin hyeomuiro chepohaetseumnida. — The police arrested Mr. Kwon on suspicion of robbery and murder.

examples.text: 경찰 조사 결과 권 씨는 스무 살 때부터 절도, 폭력, 성폭행 등 범죄를 저지른 전과 칠 범인 것으로 나타났습니다.
examples.translation: gyeongchal josa gyeolgwa gwon ssineun seumu sal ttaebuteo jeoldo, pongnyeok, seongpokaeng deung beomjoereul jeojireun jeongwa chil beomin geoseuro natanatseumnida. — As a result of the police investigation, it turned out that Mr. Kwon had seven previous convictions for crimes such as theft, violence and sexual assault since he was twenty.

explanations.title: The eyewitness’s statement (목격자)
explanations.body: The witness’s statement as in the book (the name is left out; “175cm” is read 백칠십오 센티미터; the English is mine).

examples.text: 어제 밤 열한 시쯤 배가 고파서 간식이나 사 먹으려고 집 근처 편의점에 갔어요.
examples.translation: eoje bam yeolhan sijjeum baega gopaseo gansigina sa meogeuryeogo jip geuncheo pyeonuijeome gasseoyo. — Yesterday at about eleven at night I was hungry and went to a convenience store near my house to buy a snack or something.

examples.text: 과자를 고르고 있는데 갑자기 흉기를 들고 복면을 한 강도가 편의점으로 들어왔어요.
examples.translation: gwajareul goreugo inneunde gapjagi hyunggireul deulgo bongmyeoneul han gangdoga pyeonuijeomeuro deureowasseoyo. — While I was picking out snacks, a robber carrying a lethal weapon and wearing a mask suddenly came into the convenience store.

examples.text: 그 강도는 들어오자마자 계산대 뒤에 있던 종업원을 위협하고 돈을 요구했어요.
examples.translation: geu gangdoneun deureoojamaja gyesandae dwie itdeon jongeobwoneul wihyeopago doneul yoguhaesseoyo. — As soon as he came in, the robber threatened the employee behind the counter and demanded money.

examples.text: 종업원이 소리를 지르자 그 사람이 종업원을 칼로 찌르고 계산대에서 현금을 털어서 나갔어요.
examples.translation: jongeobwoni sorireul jireuja geu sarami jongeobwoneul kallo jjireugo gyesandaeeseo hyeongeumeul teoreoseo nagasseoyo. — When the employee screamed, he stabbed the employee with a knife, took the cash from the register and left.

examples.text: 범인이 복면을 쓰고 있어서 얼굴을 자세히 보지는 못했지만 키는 약 백칠십오 센티미터 정도였고 좀 마른 편이었습니다.
examples.translation: beomini bongmyeoneul sseugo isseoseo eolgureul jasehi bojineun motaetjiman kineun yak baekchilsibo sentimiteo jeongdoyeotgo jom mareun pyeonieotseumnida. — Because the criminal was wearing a mask I couldn’t see his face in detail, but he was about 175 cm tall and was a little on the thin side.

examples.text: 머리는 짧았어요.
examples.translation: meorineun jjalbasseoyo. — His hair was short.

explanations.title: Core words and phrases of Topic A
explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter). The book also lists ~범 (a criminal; a person who committed [a crime]), 붙잡다/붙잡히다, 빼앗다, ~(이)나 and 자세히.

rows: (犯行) a criminal act; a crime; an offense
(殺人) a murder; homicide; “killing a person”; to kill a person; to murder (~하다)
(殺害) a murder; homicide; “killing and damaging”; to murder / to be murdered (~하다/되다; 당하다)
(性暴行) a sexual assault; to commit a sexual assault / to be sexually assaulted (~하다/당하다)
(威脅) threat; menace; intimidation; to threaten (i.e. to instill fear in the victim) (~하다)
to commit (a crime, an error, etc.)

(凶器) a deadly weapon; a lethal weapon
a criminal; a person who committed [a crime]
to catch / to be caught; to arrest / to be arrested
just; settling for less-appealing option (nonnumerical noun + (이)나)

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): a crime article
explanations.body: Read the article about a crime and fill in the table in English: perpetrator and victim; crime committed; motive; consequences. The book glosses 화분: planter; 들키다: to be caught; 도망가다: to flee. The headline (a middle school student who killed a person in their seventies over a game item) is the book’s idea; the article is the book’s with the numbers and the letters A and B spelled out; the English is mine. (This is a news report of a fatal crime.)

examples.text: 지난해 이월 중학교 이 학년이었던 에이 군은 새벽 다섯 시쯤 게임 아이템을 살 돈을 훔치기 위해 경남 거제시의 한 집으로 들어갔다.
examples.translation: jinanhae iwol junghakgyo i hangnyeonieotdeon ei guneun saebyeok daseot sijjeum geim aitemeul sal doneul humchigi wihae gyeongnam geojesiui han jibeuro deureogatda. — Last February, Mr. A, who was then in the second year of middle school, entered a house in Geoje, Gyeongnam, at about five in the morning to steal money to buy game items.

examples.text: 집 거실에서 일흔네 살 여성 비 씨에게 들킨 에이 군은 화분으로 비 씨의 머리를 때리고 흉기로 찔렀다.
examples.translation: jip geosireseo ilheunne sal yeoseong bi ssiege deulkin ei guneun hwabuneuro bi ssiui meorireul ttaerigo hyunggiro jjilleotda. — Caught in the living room by a 74-year-old woman, Ms. B, Mr. A hit Ms. B’s head with a planter and stabbed her with a lethal weapon.

examples.text: 칼에 찔린 피해자가 도둑이야 하고 소리치며 문 밖으로 도망갔으나 에이 군은 따라가서 다리를 잡아 비 씨를 쓰러뜨렸다.
examples.translation: kare jjillin pihaejaga dodugiya hago sorichimyeo mun bakkeuro domanggasseuna ei guneun ttaragaseo darireul jaba bi ssireul sseureotteuryeotda. — The stabbed victim ran out the door shouting “Thief”, but Mr. A followed, grabbed her leg and knocked her down.

examples.text: 이로 인해 비 씨는 아스팔트 바닥에 머리를 다쳤다.
examples.translation: iro inhae bi ssineun aseupalteu badage meorireul dacheotda. — Because of this Ms. B hurt her head on the asphalt.

examples.text: 에이 군은 피해자의 소리를 듣고 달려 온 이웃의 신고로 경찰에 붙잡혔다.
examples.translation: ei guneun pihaejaui sorireul deutgo dallyeo on iusui singoro gyeongchare butjapyeotda. — Mr. A was caught by the police on the report of a neighbor who ran over hearing the victim’s voice.

examples.text: 피해자는 그 후 병원에 옮겨졌지만, 범행 십여 일 뒤 끝내 숨졌다.
examples.translation: pihaejaneun geu hu byeongwone omgyeojeotjiman, beomhaeng sibyeo il dwi kkeunnae sumjeotda. — The victim was then taken to the hospital but finally died more than ten days after the crime.

examples.text: 경찰은 에이 군을 강도살인 혐의로 체포했다.
examples.translation: gyeongchareun ei guneul gangdosarin hyeomuiro chepohaetda. — The police arrested Mr. A on suspicion of robbery and murder.

explanations.title: Topic B: I am a youth counselor (저는 청소년 상담사입니다)
explanations.body: A youth counselor tells a group of high school students about his experience of school violence and drug addiction. He also shares the story of how he turned his life around and became a youth counselor. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the printed text has a blank line before 때렸어요, which is left out here; “PC” is read 피시.)

examples.text: 저는 중학교 때 이사를 가서 다른 학교로 전학을 가게 되었습니다.
examples.translation: jeoneun junghakgyo ttae isareul gaseo dareun hakgyoro jeonhageul gage doeeotseumnida. — When I was in middle school we moved, and I ended up transferring to another school.

examples.text: 그런데 전학 간 학교의 불량 학생들이 저를 놀리고 괴롭히기 시작했습니다.
examples.translation: geureonde jeonhak gan hakgyoui bullyang haksaengdeuri jeoreul nolligo goeropigi sijakaetseumnida. — But the delinquent students at the school I transferred to started to tease and torment me.

examples.text: 그 아이들은 상습적으로 제 용돈을 빼앗고 욕하고 때렸어요.
examples.translation: geu aideureun sangseupjeogeuro je yongdoneul ppaeatgo yokago ttaeryeosseoyo. — Those kids habitually took my allowance, swore at me and hit me.

examples.text: 게다가 저는 그 아이들이 시키는 대로 술도 마시고 담배도 피워야 했어요.
examples.translation: gedaga jeoneun geu aideuri sikineun daero suldo masigo dambaedo piwoya haesseoyo. — On top of that, I had to drink and smoke as those kids told me to.

examples.text: 저는 부모님께 거짓말도 자주 했고 가출도 했습니다.
examples.translation: jeoneun bumonimkke geojinmaldo jaju haetgo gachuldo haetseumnida. — I often lied to my parents, and I also ran away from home.

examples.text: 그러다가 같이 어울린 형들이 준 마약에 손을 대서 결국 중독되고 말았어요.
examples.translation: geureodaga gachi eoullin hyeongdeuri jun mayage soneul daeseo gyeolguk jungdokdoego marasseoyo. — Then I got involved with drugs given by older boys I hung out with and in the end became addicted.

examples.text: 학교에는 오랫동안 가지 않아서 퇴학 당했습니다.
examples.translation: hakgyoeneun oraetdongan gaji anaseo toehak danghaetseumnida. — I didn’t go to school for a long time, so I was expelled.

examples.text: 하루는 피시방에서 물건을 훔치다가 들켜서 경찰에 신고당했습니다.
examples.translation: haruneun pisibangeseo mulgeoneul humchidaga deulkyeoseo gyeongchare singodanghaetseumnida. — One day I was caught stealing something at a PC room and was reported to the police.

examples.text: 다행히 경찰서에서 만난 좋은 경찰관의 도움으로 저는 비행 청소년 생활에서 완전히 벗어날 수 있었습니다.
examples.translation: dahaenghi gyeongchalseoeseo mannan joeun gyeongchalgwanui doumeuro jeoneun bihaeng cheongsonyeon saenghwareseo wanjeonhi beoseonal su isseotseumnida. — Fortunately, with the help of a good police officer I met at the police station, I was able to break away completely from the life of a juvenile delinquent.

examples.text: 그 경찰관 아저씨는 제 이야기를 듣고 제가 부모님과 다시 연락해서 집으로 돌아갈 수 있게 해 주고, 재활 치료도 받을 수 있도록 도움을 주었습니다.
examples.translation: geu gyeongchalgwan ajeossineun je iyagireul deutgo jega bumonimgwa dasi yeollakaeseo jibeuro doragal su itge hae jugo, jaehwal chiryodo badeul su itdorok doumeul jueotseumnida. — The police officer listened to my story, helped me contact my parents again and go back home, and helped me receive rehabilitation treatment.

examples.text: 그로부터 이십 년이 지난 지금 저는 청소년 상담사가 되어 있습니다.
examples.translation: geurobuteo isip nyeoni jinan jigeum jeoneun cheongsonyeon sangdamsaga doeeo itseumnida. — Twenty years have passed since then, and now I have become a youth counselor.

examples.text: 우리 주변에는 학교 폭력을 당하거나 담배나 마약에 중독되어 고통받는 많은 아이들이 있습니다.
examples.translation: uri jubyeoneneun hakgyo pongnyeogeul danghageona dambaena mayage jungdokdoeeo gotongbanneun maneun aideuri itseumnida. — Around us there are many children who suffer from being victims of school violence or being addicted to cigarettes or drugs.

examples.text: 저는 제가 가장 힘들었을 때 저를 도와준 경찰관처럼 우리 사회의 청소년 문제 해결을 위해 제 인생을 살려고 합니다.
examples.translation: jeoneun jega gajang himdeureosseul ttae jeoreul dowajun gyeongchalgwancheoreom uri sahoeui cheongsonyeon munje haegyeoreul wihae je insaengeul sallyeogo hamnida. — Like the police officer who helped me when I was at my hardest, I intend to live my life for solving the youth problems of our society.

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 1. 집단 따돌림, 왕따, and 학폭
explanations.body: “집단 따돌림”, “왕따”, and “학폭” refer to different forms of school violence. 집단 따돌림 literally means “group shunning” and often involves a group of people ostracizing one person. 왕따 is a slang term that combines 왕, which literally means “king” but is often used as a superlative in Korean slang, and 따 (short for 따돌림), and can be literally understood as “super-ostracizing”. Nowadays, the term “학교 폭력”, also known as “학폭” in short, is commonly used to encompass various forms of abuse in schools, including physical, verbal, and emotional mistreatment directed towards victims.

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 2. 당하다
explanations.body: The verb 당하다 (to sustain physical or mental damage) is used to express suffering from physical or mental damage. Therefore, you will often encounter 당하다 in the context of crime, disaster, or mishap, as in 왕따를 당하다, 폭행을 당하다, 사기를 당하다, etc.

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 3. ~에 손을 대다
explanations.body: ~에 손을 대다 or ~에 손대다 literally means “to lay one’s hands on (something/someone)”. This expression is often used to mean “to start something” (unpleasant), such as drugs, alcohol, or tobacco (술에 손을 대다, 노름에 손을 대다, etc.). ~에서 손을 떼다 or ~에서 손떼다 is used to mean “quit something” unpleasant (담배에서 손을 떼다).

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a news article about drug problems
explanations.body: The following news article is about drug problems. The book glosses 퍼지다: to spread; 감시: watch, surveillance; 은어: slang. The book asks you (a) to create a headline in Korean and (b) to fill in a table in English: police statistics findings; experience shared by interviewee A; new slang word and its definition; way(s) to provide help. The article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out, the quotation marks dropped (the quoted speech is marked with “ ” in English only), and the phone numbers of the treatment centers left out; the English is mine.

examples.text: 청소년들에게도 마약이 퍼지고 있습니다.
examples.translation: cheongsonyeondeuregedo mayagi peojigo itseumnida. — Drugs are spreading even to teenagers.

examples.text: 경찰에 따르면 지난해 일 월부터 팔 월까지 마약 범죄로 붙잡힌 십구 세 이하 청소년은 삼백칠십이 명입니다.
examples.translation: gyeongchare ttareumyeon jinanhae il wolbuteo pal wolkkaji mayak beomjoero butjapin sipgu se iha cheongsonyeoneun sambaekchilsibi myeongimnida. — According to the police, from January to August of last year 372 teenagers aged 19 or under were caught for drug crimes.

examples.text: 그중 삼십팔 명은 십오 세 미만 청소년입니다.
examples.translation: geujung samsippal myeongeun sibo se miman cheongsonyeonimnida. — Of them, 38 are teenagers under 15.

examples.text: 이들은 온라인으로 마약을 구매한 뒤 감시를 피하려고 비트코인으로 값을 결제했습니다.
examples.translation: ideureun ollaineuro mayageul gumaehan dwi gamsireul piharyeogo biteukoineuro gapseul gyeoljehaetseumnida. — They bought drugs online and paid for them in bitcoin to avoid surveillance.

examples.text: 비행 청소년들만 마약에 빠지는 것이 아닙니다.
examples.translation: bihaeng cheongsonyeondeulman mayage ppajineun geosi animnida. — It is not only juvenile delinquents who fall into drugs.

examples.text: 원하지 않았는데 마약에 취하는 일도 있습니다.
examples.translation: wonhaji ananneunde mayage chwihaneun ildo itseumnida. — There are also cases of getting drugged without wanting to.

examples.text: 퐁당은 음료나 술에 몰래 마약을 타서 주는 행위를 부르는 은어입니다.
examples.translation: pongdangeun eumnyona sure mollae mayageul taseo juneun haengwireul bureuneun euneoimnida. — “Pongdang” is slang for the act of secretly putting drugs in a drink or alcohol and giving it to someone.

examples.text: 마약이 든 음료를 한 번이라도 마시면 중독에 빠지기 쉽습니다.
examples.translation: mayagi deun eumnyoreul han beonirado masimyeon jungdoge ppajigi swipseumnida. — If you drink a drink containing drugs even once, it is easy to fall into addiction.

examples.text: 마약 중독자 회복을 위한 모임에 나온 에이 씨는 클럽에서도 콜라에 필로폰을 몰래 넣는 걸 여러 번 봤어요 하고 말했습니다.
examples.translation: mayak jungdokja hoebogeul wihan moime naon ei ssineun keulleobeseodo kollae pilloponeul mollae neonneun geol yeoreo beon bwasseoyo hago malhaetseumnida. — Mr./Ms. A, who came to a gathering for the recovery of drug addicts, said, “I saw them secretly put methamphetamine in cola many times at clubs too.”

examples.text: 필로폰은 한 번만 해도 중독되는데 퐁당 당하고 나면 다 중독돼요 하고 말했습니다.
examples.translation: pilloponeun han beonman haedo jungdokdoeneunde pongdang danghago namyeon da jungdokdwaeyo hago malhaetseumnida. — And said, “Methamphetamine is addictive even if you do it just once, and after being ‘pongdang’-ed everyone gets addicted.”

examples.text: 마약에 빠져서 고통받는 사람이 있다면 가까운 재활센터를 소개해야 합니다.
examples.translation: mayage ppajeoseo gotongbanneun sarami itdamyeon gakkaun jaehwalsenteoreul sogaehaeya hamnida. — If there is a person suffering from falling into drugs, you should introduce a nearby rehabilitation center.

lessons.title: 477. Ch 38 · Grammar A: “in accordance with” and “as”, –는/(으)ㄴ 대로 and ~대로
lessons.subtitle: -는 대로 · -(으)ㄴ 대로 · ~대로 · 약속한 대로 · 선생님 말씀대로 · 의사가 처방한 대로

explanations.title: In accordance with / as
explanations.body: In an earlier chapter, you learned that the conjunctive ending –는 대로 attached to the stem of an action verb can translate to as soon as or immediately after, even though it is used when the time of an action or event is not fixed (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 서울에 도착하는 대로 전화할게요.
examples.translation: seoure dochakaneun daero jeonhwahalgeyo. — I will call you as soon as I arrive in Seoul.

explanations.title: The underlying meaning
explanations.body:
Thus, the underlying meaning of the conjunctive ending is in accordance with or as. Therefore, 서울에 도착하는 대로 전화할게요 essentially says, “I don’t know when I will arrive in Seoul, but I will call you (as soon) as I arrive there. If I arrive there at six, I will call you then. If I arrive there at nine, I will call you then.”

In this lesson, we examine sentences in which the underlying meaning of –는/(으)ㄴ 대로 or ~대로 (in accordance with; as) is used.

explanations.title: 약속한 대로 / 약속대로
explanations.body: Both sentences convey the same message, but note that the conjunctive ending –는/(으)ㄴ 대로 is attached to the attributive form of the verb 약속하다 (to promise), whereas the marker ~대로 is attached to the noun 약속 (promise). In fact, ~대로 frequently works with nouns such as 약속, 말, 말씀, 생각, or 의견. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 약속한 대로 일곱 시에 오겠습니다.
examples.translation: yaksokan daero ilgop sie ogetseumnida. — I will come at 7 as I promised.

examples.text: 약속대로 일곱 시에 오겠습니다.
examples.translation: yaksokdaero ilgop sie ogetseumnida. — I will come at 7 in accordance with my promise.

explanations.title: “In accordance with” / “as”
explanations.body: verb stem + 는/(으)ㄴ 대로; noun + 대로. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 제가 생각했던 대로 이번 시험은 쉬웠습니다.
examples.translation: jega saenggakaetdeon daero ibeon siheomeun swiwotseumnida. — Like I thought, this test was easy.

examples.text: 어제 예상한 대로 지금 비가 옵니다.
examples.translation: eoje yesanghan daero jigeum biga omnida. — (Just) as I expected yesterday, it is raining now.

examples.text: 선생님 말씀대로 한국에 가겠습니다.
examples.translation: seonsaengnim malsseumdaero hanguge gagetseumnida. — I will go to Korea “in accordance with your saying” / as you say.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading and speaking): matching
explanations.body: The book asks you to match each phrase in the left column with its most closely related phrase on the right (answers may vary), then take turns making a sentence with two matched phrases and the pattern –는/(으)ㄴ 대로. The phrases are the book’s; the pairs and the sentences are mine; the book’s model is 의사가 처방하다 / 환자가 약을 먹다.

rows: 의사가 처방한 대로 환자가 약을 먹어요.
친구에게 약속한 대로 콘서트에 같이 가요.

examples.text: 의사가 처방한 대로 환자가 약을 먹어요.
examples.translation: uisaga cheobanghan daero hwanjaga yageul meogeoyo. — As the doctor prescribed, the patient takes the medicine.

examples.text: 교관이 시키는 대로 수류탄을 던져요.
examples.translation: gyogwani sikineun daero suryutaneul deonjeoyo. — I throw the grenade as the instructor tells me.

examples.text: 라디오에서 예보한 대로 비가 와요.

examples.text: 친구에게 약속한 대로 콘서트에 같이 가요.
examples.translation: chinguege yaksokan daero konseoteue gachi gayo. — As I promised my friend, we go to the concert together.

examples.text: 음식을 주문한 대로 비빔밥이 나와요.

lessons.title: 478. Ch 38 · Grammar B: the auxiliary verb –고 말다 (ending up doing)
lessons.subtitle: -고 말다 · -아/어 버리다와 비교 · 사고 말았어요 · 죽고 말았어요 · 꼭 합격하고 말겠어요

explanations.title: Recall –아/어 버리다
explanations.body: Recall the auxiliary verb –아/어 버리다, which you learned about in Chapter 27. It is used to express a completed action and normally implies that the completed action is not reversible or that something/someone is no longer available. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 동생이 내 피자를 다 먹어 버렸어요.
examples.translation: dongsaengi nae pijareul da meogeo beoryeosseoyo. — My younger brother ate all my pizza (and it is no longer available to me).

examples.text: 김 일병이 한국에 가 버렸어요.
examples.translation: gim ilbyeongi hanguge ga beoryeosseoyo. — PFC Kim went to Korea (and he is no longer with us).

explanations.title: –고 말다
explanations.body: The auxiliary verb –고 말다 is also used to express a completed action. However, this auxiliary verb normally implies that the completed action is against one’s intention, wish, or warning. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 컴퓨터를 사고 말았어요.
examples.translation: keompyuteoreul sago marasseoyo. — I ended up buying a computer after all (despite the fact that I couldn’t afford to buy a computer).

examples.text: 김 일병이 한국에 가고 말았어요.
examples.translation: gim ilbyeongi hanguge gago marasseoyo. — (I told PFC Kim not to go to Korea but) he ended up going to Korea after all.

explanations.title: Action completed against one’s intention, wish, or warning
explanations.body: action verb + 고 말다. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 오늘 아침 우리 집 개가 죽고 말았어요.
examples.translation: oneul achim uri jip gaega jukgo marasseoyo. — (I prayed for my sick dog all along, but) my dog ended up dying this morning after all.

examples.text: 여자 친구가 파티에 안 오고 말았어요.
examples.translation: yeoja chinguga patie an ogo marasseoyo. — (I had expected her all along, but) my girlfriend ended up not coming to the party after all.

examples.text: 마침내 컴퓨터가 고장이 나고 말았어요.
examples.translation: machimnae keompyuteoga gojangi nago marasseoyo. — (My computer had acted up in the past, and) finally it broke down after all.

explanations.title: 참고: the future tense
explanations.body: Both –고 말다 and –아/어 버리다 in the future tense are used to express the speaker’s strong intention of doing or accomplishing something (despite obstacles). (The English is the book’s; DLPT is read 디엘피티.)

examples.text: 디엘피티에 꼭 합격하고 말겠어요.
examples.translation: dielpitie kkok hapgyeokago malgesseoyo. — I will surely pass the DLPT.

examples.text: 내년에 한국에 가고 말겠어요.
examples.translation: naenyeone hanguge gago malgesseoyo. — I will definitely go to Korea next year.

examples.text: 다음 주에 그 자동차를 사 버리겠어요.
examples.translation: daeum jue geu jadongchareul sa beorigesseoyo. — I will buy the car next week.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Speaking): 넘어지고 말았어요
explanations.body: In this activity, you share with your classmates something you ended up doing against your will or intention (doing poorly on an exam despite studying, your car breaking down, catching a cold, etc.). You write at least three incidents in a table and share them using –고 말다. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 수영: 명인 씨, 안녕하십니까? 요즘 어때요?
examples.translation: suyeong: myeongin ssi, annyeonghasimnikka? yojeum eottaeyo? — Myeongin, how are you? How have things been lately?

examples.text: 명인: 별로예요.
examples.translation: myeongin: byeolloyeyo. — Not so good.

examples.text: 수영: 무슨 일이 있으세요?
examples.translation: suyeong: museun iri isseuseyo? — Is something the matter?

examples.text: 명인: 어제 제 핸드폰이 고장이 나고 말았어요.
examples.translation: myeongin: eoje je haendeuponi gojangi nago marasseoyo. — Yesterday my cell phone broke down after all.

explanations.title: More sentences (mine)
explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

examples.text: 열심히 공부했는데 시험을 못 보고 말았어요.
examples.translation: yeolsimhi gongbuhaenneunde siheomeul mot bogo marasseoyo. — I studied hard but ended up doing poorly on the exam.

examples.text: 조심했는데 감기에 걸리고 말았어요.
examples.translation: josimhaenneunde gamgie geolligo marasseoyo. — I was careful but ended up catching a cold.

examples.text: 안 가려고 했는데 결국 가고 말았어요.
examples.translation: an garyeogo haenneunde gyeolguk gago marasseoyo. — I didn’t intend to go but ended up going.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): a news article about an online survey
explanations.body: The following news article is about an online survey (Chosun). The book glosses 성추행: sexual harassment; 강제 심부름: forced errands; 합쳐지다: to be combined. The article is the book’s with the numbers and percentages spelled out (the decimal point is read 점 and “·” and brackets are dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 전국 사 년제 대학생 열 명 중 세 명은 대학에서 학교폭력을 목격한 것으로 조사됐다.
examples.translation: jeonguk sa nyeonje daehaksaeng yeol myeong jung se myeongeun daehageseo hakgyopongnyeogeul mokgyeokan geoseuro josadwaetda. — Three out of ten four-year university students nationwide were found to have witnessed school violence at university.

examples.text: 연구진은 칠 개월간 대학생 온라인 커뮤니티 에브리타임을 통해 총 사백육십칠 명의 설문 결과를 수집했다.
examples.translation: yeongujineun chil gaewolgan daehaksaeng ollain keomyuniti ebeuritaimeul tonghae chong sabaegyuksipchil myeongui seolmun gyeolgwareul sujipaetda. — The researchers collected the survey results of a total of 467 people over seven months through the university students’ online community Everytime.

examples.text: 이 조사에 따르면 사 년제 대학생 사백육십칠 명 중 백삼십오 명, 이십팔 점 구 퍼센트가 대학에서 학교폭력을 목격한 적이 있다고 답했다.
examples.translation: i josae ttareumyeon sa nyeonje daehaksaeng sabaegyuksipchil myeong jung baeksamsibo myeong, isippal jeom gu peosenteuga daehageseo hakgyopongnyeogeul mokgyeokan jeogi itdago dapaetda. — According to this survey, 135 of the 467 four-year university students, 28.9 percent, answered that they had witnessed school violence at university.

examples.text: 대학생 사이 폭력은 언어폭력이 육십팔 점 구 퍼센트로 가장 많았으며 그 뒤로 성추행 성폭력, 삼십이 점 육 퍼센트, 신체 폭력, 십칠 점 영 퍼센트 순이었다.
examples.translation: daehaksaeng sai pongnyeogeun eoneopongnyeogi yuksippal jeom gu peosenteuro gajang manasseumyeo geu dwiro seongchuhaeng seongpongnyeok, samsibi jeom yuk peosenteu, sinche pongnyeok, sipchil jeom yeong peosenteu sunieotda. — Among violence between university students, verbal violence was the most common at 68.9 percent, followed by sexual harassment and sexual violence at 32.6 percent and physical violence at 17.0 percent.

examples.text: 강제 심부름, 십육 점 삼 퍼센트, 집단 따돌림과 사이버폭력, 십일 점 구 퍼센트도 목격 비율이 높은 것으로 조사됐다.
examples.translation: gangje simbureum, simnyuk jeom sam peosenteu, jipdan ttadollimgwa saibeopongnyeok, sibil jeom gu peosenteudo mokgyeok biyuri nopeun geoseuro josadwaetda. — Forced errands, 16.3 percent, and group bullying and cyber violence, 11.9 percent, also had high witnessing rates.

examples.text: 학교폭력 목격 장소의 경우 강의실이 칠십팔 점 사 퍼센트로 가장 높은 비율을 보였으며, 강의실 외 교내시설, 사십육 점 사 퍼센트, 교내 건물 밖, 삼십오 점 일 퍼센트의 순으로 나타났다.
examples.translation: hakgyopongnyeok mokgyeok jangsoui gyeongu ganguisiri chilsippal jeom sa peosenteuro gajang nopeun biyureul boyeosseumyeo, ganguisil oe gyonaesiseol, sasimnyuk jeom sa peosenteu, gyonae geonmul bak, samsibo jeom il peosenteuui suneuro natanatda. — As for places where school violence was witnessed, lecture rooms showed the highest rate at 78.4 percent, followed by campus facilities other than lecture rooms, 46.4 percent, and outside campus buildings, 35.1 percent.

examples.text: 응답자의 팔 점 육 퍼센트가 학교폭력 피해를 직접 겪었다고 답했으며, 가해 경험이 있다는 응답자는 없었다.
examples.translation: eungdapjaui pal jeom yuk peosenteuga hakgyopongnyeok pihaereul jikjeop gyeokkeotdago dapaesseumyeo, gahae gyeongheomi itdaneun eungdapjaneun eopseotda. — 8.6 percent of respondents answered that they had directly experienced school violence damage, and no respondent said they had experience as a perpetrator.

examples.text: 학교폭력을 목격한 학생 중 육십육 점 삼 퍼센트는 이후 경찰이나 학교에 신고하지 않았다.
examples.translation: hakgyopongnyeogeul mokgyeokan haksaeng jung yuksimnyuk jeom sam peosenteuneun ihu gyeongcharina hakgyoe singohaji anatda. — Of the students who witnessed school violence, 66.3 percent did not report it to the police or school afterward.

examples.text: 신고했다고 응답한 경우는 이십칠 점 구 퍼센트밖에 되지 않았다.
examples.translation: singohaetdago eungdapan gyeonguneun isipchil jeom gu peosenteubakke doeji anatda. — Those who answered that they had reported it were only 27.9 percent.

examples.text: 연구진은 대학생들의 학교폭력 신고율이 낮게 나타나는 이유를 주위 문제에 무관심한 태도와, 신고를 해도 도움이 되지 못했던 경험이 합쳐져 일어나는 현상이라고 분석했다.
examples.translation: yeongujineun daehaksaengdeurui hakgyopongnyeok singoyuri natge natananeun iyureul juwi munjee mugwansimhan taedowa, singoreul haedo doumi doeji motaetdeon gyeongheomi hapcheojeo ireonaneun hyeonsangirago bunseokaetda. — The researchers analyzed the reason for the low reporting rate of school violence among university students as a phenomenon caused by a combination of an indifferent attitude toward surrounding problems and the experience that reporting did not help.

explanations.title: The questions and my answers
explanations.body: The book asks you to (a) create a Korean headline, (b) tell how the researchers collected the data and over what period, (c) list the three most common types of violence observed, (d) say what 78.4%, 8.6% and 66.3% refer to, and (e) give the reasons for the low reporting rate. My answers:

rows: 대학생 열 명 중 세 명이 대학에서 학교폭력 목격
b. How data were collected and over what period
An online survey of 467 students through the online community Everytime over seven months
c. Three most common types of violence
1. verbal violence; 2. sexual harassment and sexual violence; 3. physical violence
The share of witnesses who saw the violence in a lecture room
The share of respondents who directly experienced school violence
The share of witnesses who did not report it to the police or school
e. Reasons for the low reporting rate
An indifferent attitude toward surrounding problems combined with the experience that reporting did not help

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (a vocabulary card game between two teams), Activity 2 (listening to an EBS news report on a school bullying survey and noting what has decreased and increased, the most common type and reason of bullying) and Activity 4 (two cases of school bullying, one to be listened to on YTN and one read in hani.co.kr, analyzed in groups; the book glosses 유서: last words/note; 동급생: class mates; 후속조치: follow-up measures; 항변하다: to plead; then preventive measures presented on a flip chart) are audio, group and game activities.
