explanations.title: Topic C: Changes in crime with social change (사회변화에 따른 범죄의 변화)
explanations.body: The following text is an excerpt from a TV program in which an anchor is interviewing a detective about the shifts in crime. (The English is mine; the book gives none; “CCTV” is read 씨씨티브이 and the number is spelled out.)

examples.text: 앵커: 형사님, 안녕하세요. 우리 사회가 변화하면서 예전에 비해서 자주 일어나는 범죄에도 많은 변화가 있을 것 같은데요. 어떻습니까?
examples.translation: aengkeo: hyeongsanim, annyeonghaseyo. uri sahoega byeonhwahamyeonseo yejeone bihaeseo jaju ireonaneun beomjoeedo maneun byeonhwaga isseul geot gateundeyo. eotteoseumnikka? — Detective, hello. As our society changes, it seems there have also been many changes in the crimes that happen often compared with the past. How is it?

examples.text: 형사: 네, 우선 살인, 강도, 납치, 방화 같은 전통적인 강력 범죄들은 많이 줄어들었습니다.
examples.translation: hyeongsa: ne, useon sarin, gangdo, napchi, banghwa gateun jeontongjeogin gangnyeok beomjoedeureun mani jureodeureotseumnida. — Yes, first of all, traditional violent crimes such as murder, robbery, kidnapping and arson have decreased a lot.

examples.text: 앵커: 아, 다행이네요. 예전에는 소매치기나 위조지폐 사건도 많았는데 요즘은 어떤가요?
examples.translation: aengkeo: a, dahaengineyo. yejeoneneun somaechigina wijojipye sageondo mananneunde yojeumeun eotteongayo? — Oh, that’s good. In the past there were also many pickpocketing and counterfeit bill cases; how is it these days?

examples.text: 형사: 네, 소매치기 사건은 거의 없고요. 위조지폐 사건도 상당히 줄어서 작년 한 해 동안 위조지폐 발생 건수는 백오십 건 정도밖에 되지 않았습니다.
examples.translation: hyeongsa: ne, somaechigi sageoneun geoui eopgoyo. wijojipye sageondo sangdanghi jureoseo jangnyeon han hae dongan wijojipye balsaeng geonsuneun baegosip geon jeongdobakke doeji anatseumnida. — Yes, there are almost no pickpocketing cases. Counterfeit bill cases have also decreased considerably, so over the past year the number of counterfeit bill cases was only about 150.

examples.text: 앵커: 그렇군요. 그럼 이런 범죄들이 줄어든 원인은 뭐라고 보십니까?
examples.translation: aengkeo: geureokunyo. geureom ireon beomjoedeuri jureodeun wonineun mworago bosimnikka? — I see. Then what do you think is the reason these crimes have decreased?

examples.text: 형사: 무엇보다 현금 대신 신용카드나 스마트폰 결제가 일반화된 이유가 크고요. 씨씨티브이 사용이 늘면서 곳곳에 설치되어 있는 카메라를 피해 범행을 저지르는 것이 거의 불가능해졌습니다. 또 과학 수사의 발달로 우리가 확실한 증거를 빨리 모을 수가 있게 되었고요.
examples.translation: hyeongsa: mueotboda hyeongeum daesin sinyongkadeuna seumateupon gyeoljega ilbanhwadoen iyuga keugoyo. ssissitibeui sayongi neulmyeonseo gotgose seolchidoeeo inneun kamerareul pihae beomhaengeul jeojireuneun geosi geoui bulganeunghaejeotseumnida. tto gwahak susaui baldallo uriga hwaksilhan jeunggeoreul ppalli moeul suga itge doeeotgoyo. — Above all, the generalization of credit card and smartphone payment instead of cash is a big reason. With the increased use of CCTV, it has become almost impossible to commit a crime avoiding the cameras installed everywhere. Also, thanks to the development of scientific investigation, we have become able to collect solid evidence quickly.

examples.text: 앵커: 네. 그렇군요. 그런데 과학의 발달과 함께 늘어난 범죄도 있을 것 같은데요.
examples.translation: aengkeo: ne. geureokunyo. geureonde gwahagui baldalgwa hamkke neureonan beomjoedo isseul geot gateundeyo. — I see. But it seems there are also crimes that have increased along with the development of science.

examples.text: 형사: 그럼요. 인터넷이나 스마트폰을 이용한 디지털 범죄, 특히 보이스피싱 같은 사기 범죄가 크게 늘었습니다. 이와 함께 해킹을 통한 개인정보 유출, 마약 밀수 등의 불법도 크게 늘었고요.
examples.translation: hyeongsa: geureomyo. inteonesina seumateuponeul iyonghan dijiteol beomjoe, teuki boiseupising gateun sagi beomjoega keuge neureotseumnida. iwa hamkke haekingeul tonghan gaeinjeongbo yuchul, mayak milsu deungui bulbeopdo keuge neureotgoyo. — Of course. Digital crimes using the Internet or smartphones, especially fraud crimes such as voice phishing, have increased greatly. Along with this, illegal acts such as leaks of personal information through hacking and drug smuggling have also increased greatly.

examples.text: 앵커: 아, 과학의 발달을 악용해 범죄에 이용하는 경우들이 늘었군요.
examples.translation: aengkeo: a, gwahagui baldareul agyonghae beomjoee iyonghaneun gyeongudeuri neureotgunyo. — Oh, so cases of misusing the development of science and using it for crime have increased.

examples.text: 형사: 네, 그렇습니다. 우리 사회 환경이 변하는 한 그와 함께 범죄도 계속 변화할 겁니다.
examples.translation: hyeongsa: ne, geureoseumnida. uri sahoe hwangyeongi byeonhaneun han geuwa hamkke beomjoedo gyesok byeonhwahal geomnida. — Yes, that’s right. As long as our social environment changes, crime will also keep changing along with it.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): a counterfeit-bill article
explanations.body: Read the news about a crime and fill in the table. The book glosses 소품: prop; 거스름돈: change; 회수하다: to retrieve; 유통하다: to circulate. The article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (the quotation marks are dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 영화 소품으로 사용되는 오만 원권 위조지폐를 실제 돈처럼 사용한 혐의를 받는 삼십 대 외국인 남성이 구속됐다.
examples.translation: yeonghwa sopumeuro sayongdoeneun oman wongwon wijojipyereul silje doncheoreom sayonghan hyeomuireul banneun samsip dae oegugin namseongi gusokdwaetda. — A foreign man in his thirties suspected of using counterfeit 50,000-won bills used as movie props like real money has been arrested.

examples.text: 십육 일 경찰에 따르면 서울 동대문경찰서는 사기 혐의를 받는 외국 국적 남성 에이 씨를 구속해 수사하고 있다.
examples.translation: simnyuk il gyeongchare ttareumyeon seoul dongdaemungyeongchalseoneun sagi hyeomuireul banneun oeguk gukjeok namseong ei ssireul gusokae susahago itda. — According to the police on the 16th, the Dongdaemun Police Station in Seoul has arrested a foreign-national man, Mr. A, suspected of fraud and is investigating.

examples.text: 에이 씨는 지난달부터 이달 초까지 동대문구의 한 시장 등에서 영화 소품용 오만 원권 위조지폐로 오천 원짜리 물건을 구매하고 사만 오천 원을 거스름돈으로 받은 혐의를 받고 있다.
examples.translation: ei ssineun jinandalbuteo idal chokkaji dongdaemunguui han sijang deungeseo yeonghwa sopumyong oman wongwon wijojipyero ocheon wonjjari mulgeoneul gumaehago saman ocheon woneul geoseureumdoneuro badeun hyeomuireul batgo itda. — Mr. A is suspected of buying 5,000-won items with movie-prop counterfeit 50,000-won bills at a market in Dongdaemun-gu and elsewhere from last month to early this month and receiving 45,000 won as change.

examples.text: 에이 씨는 가짜 오만 원권 지폐 열두 장을 사용했다고 진술했는데, 경찰은 이 중 네 장을 증거로 회수했다 한다.
examples.translation: ei ssineun gajja oman wongwon jipye yeoldu jangeul sayonghaetdago jinsulhaenneunde, gyeongchareun i jung ne jangeul jeunggeoro hoesuhaetda handa. — Mr. A stated that he used twelve fake 50,000-won bills, and the police are said to have retrieved four of them as evidence.

examples.text: 경찰 조사 결과 범행에 사용된 가짜 지폐는 실제 지폐에 비해서 크기가 크고 아래쪽에 영화 소품용이므로 사용할 수 없다라는 문구가 적혀 있는 것으로 드러났다.
examples.translation: gyeongchal josa gyeolgwa beomhaenge sayongdoen gajja jipyeneun silje jipyee bihaeseo keugiga keugo araejjoge yeonghwa sopumyongimeuro sayonghal su eopdaraneun munguga jeokyeo inneun geoseuro deureonatda. — As a result of the police investigation, it turned out that the fake bills used in the crime were bigger than real bills and had the phrase “It is for movie props so it cannot be used” written at the bottom.

explanations.title: The table filled in (mine)
explanations.body: The book’s table has the columns allegations, suspect A, distinguishing features of the bills used in the crime and proof of the crime collected by the police. My answers:

rows: Fraud: using movie-prop counterfeit 50,000-won bills like real money (buying 5,000-won items and receiving 45,000 won in change)
A foreign-national man in his thirties, arrested and under investigation by the Dongdaemun Police Station
Bigger than real bills; a phrase at the bottom says they are for movie props and cannot be used
Four of the twelve fake bills he said he used

lessons.title: 481. Ch 38 · Grammar C: the auxiliary verb –아/어 있다 (a state resulting from a completed action)
lessons.subtitle: -아/어 있다 · 앉아 있어요 · 열려 있어요 · 설치되어 있습니다 · -고 있다와 비교

explanations.title: –고 있다 and –아/어 있다
explanations.body: Compare the following two sentences and their meanings (the book shows a picture of Ms. Lee; the English is mine). In the first sentence, –고 있다 indicates that Ms. Lee is in the process of “sitting down” on the floor. In the second sentence, –아/어 있다 indicates that Ms. Lee is in the state of “sitting” on the floor. In other words, –아/어 있다 is used to indicate a condition or state resulting from a completed action.

examples.text: 이 선생님이 바닥에 앉고 있어요.
examples.translation: i seonsaengnimi badage ango isseoyo. — Ms. Lee is sitting down on the floor (in the process).

examples.text: 이 선생님이 바닥에 앉아 있어요.
examples.translation: i seonsaengnimi badage anja isseoyo. — Ms. Lee is sitting on the floor (in the state).

explanations.title: Which verbs take –아/어 있다
explanations.body: However, –아/어 있다 works only with a limited number of intransitive verbs (가다, 오다, 서다, 일어서다, 앉다, 눕다, 잠들다, 취하다, 입원하다, etc.) and with a limited number of transitive verbs in the passive voice (열리다, 닫히다, 잡히다, etc.). Intransitive verbs are those that do not take an object. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 친구가 지금 유럽에 가 있어요.
examples.translation: chinguga jigeum yureobe ga isseoyo. — My friend is (in the state of being) in Europe.

examples.text: 차고 문이 열려 있어요.
examples.translation: chago muni yeollyeo isseoyo. — The garage door is (in the state of being) open.

explanations.title: Expressing a condition/state resulting from a completed action
explanations.body: verb stem + 아/어 있다. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 형이 침대에 누워 있어요.
examples.translation: hyeongi chimdaee nuwo isseoyo. — My older brother is (in the state of) lying on the bed.

examples.text: 창문이 닫혀 있어요.
examples.translation: changmuni dacheo isseoyo. — The window is (in the state of being) closed.

examples.text: 카메라가 설치되어 있습니다.
examples.translation: kameraga seolchidoeeo itseumnida. — The camera is (in the state of being) installed.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading): a student’s website text
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a website in which a student talks about her student life at an English learning center in England. The book asks you to find and circle the –아/어 있다 phrases and to translate those sentences into English (the book glosses 연계되다: to be connected). The text is the book’s with “3개월” spelled out; the English is mine.

examples.text: 브리스톨 영어 학교는 영국의 크고 매력적인 남부 도시에 있어요.
examples.translation: beuriseutol yeongeo hakgyoneun yeonggugui keugo maeryeokjeogin nambu dosie isseoyo. — The Bristol English School is in a big, attractive southern city of England.

examples.text: 이 학교는 명문대 브리스톨대와 연계되어 있어서 브리스톨 대학시설을 이용할 수 있어요.
examples.translation: i hakgyoneun myeongmundae beuriseutoldaewa yeongyedoeeo isseoseo beuriseutol daehaksiseoreul iyonghal su isseoyo. — This school is connected with the prestigious University of Bristol, so you can use the University of Bristol’s facilities.

examples.text: 또, 이 학교는 영어 교육 프로그램뿐만 아니라 다양한 문화 프로그램이 마련되어 있어요.
examples.translation: tto, i hakgyoneun yeongeo gyoyuk peurogeuraemppunman anira dayanghan munhwa peurogeuraemi maryeondoeeo isseoyo. — Also, this school has not only English education programs but also various cultural programs prepared.

examples.text: 특히, 일주일에 두 번 문화행사가 있어서 영국의 문화를 체험할 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: teuki, iljuire du beon munhwahaengsaga isseoseo yeonggugui munhwareul cheheomhal su itseumnida. — In particular, there are cultural events twice a week, so you can experience British culture.

examples.text: 그리고 기숙사 각 방마다 전화 및 최고속 인터넷이 설치되어 있어서 편해요.
examples.translation: geurigo gisuksa gak bangmada jeonhwa mit choegosok inteonesi seolchidoeeo isseoseo pyeonhaeyo. — And every dormitory room has a phone and top-speed Internet installed, so it is convenient.

examples.text: 저는 지금 브리스톨 영어 학교에서 영어를 배운 지 삼 개월이 되었어요.
examples.translation: jeoneun jigeum beuriseutol yeongeo hakgyoeseo yeongeoreul baeun ji sam gaewori doeeosseoyo. — It has been three months since I started learning English at the Bristol English School.

lessons.title: 482. Ch 38 · Grammar D: “as long as”, –(으)ㄴ/는 한 · and self-evaluation
lessons.subtitle: -(으)ㄴ/는 한 · 먹는 한 · 있는 한 · 가능한 한 · 할 수 있는 한 · 자기 평가

explanations.title: Expressing “as long as”
explanations.body: In English, the phrase as long as is used to emphasize a condition, as in “We will win the game as long as we all stay together.” Likewise, in Korean, we use the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄴ/는 한 to emphasize a condition. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 햄버거 같은 음식을 먹는 한 살을 뺄 수 없어요.
examples.translation: haembeogeo gateun eumsigeul meongneun han sareul ppael su eopseoyo. — As long as you eat food like hamburgers, you won’t lose weight.

examples.text: 내가 몬트레이에 있는 한 매일 등산 할 거예요.
examples.translation: naega monteureie inneun han maeil deungsan hal geoyeyo. — I will go hiking every day as long as I live in Monterey.

explanations.title: –는 한 and –(으)ㄴ 한
explanations.body: –는 한 is attached to the stem of an action verb, including 있다 and 없다, whereas –(으)ㄴ 한 is attached to the stem of a stative verb. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 한국에 사는 한 한국말을 배워야 해요.
examples.translation: hanguge saneun han hangungmareul baewoya haeyo. — As long as I live in Korea, I must learn Korean.

examples.text: 친구들이 있는 한 외롭지 않아요.
examples.translation: chingudeuri inneun han oeropji anayo. — As long as there are friends, I am not lonely.

explanations.title: 참고: expressing “as … as possible”
explanations.body: When the expression 할 수 있는 한, 가능한 한, or 될 수 있는 한 is followed by an adverb or adjective, it means “as … as possible”. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 할 수 있는 한 빨리 오세요.
examples.translation: hal su inneun han ppalli oseyo. — Please come as soon as possible.

examples.text: 가능한 한 천천히 운전하세요.
examples.translation: ganeunghan han cheoncheonhi unjeonhaseyo. — Please drive as slowly as possible.

examples.text: 될 수 있는 한 적게 먹습니다.
examples.translation: doel su inneun han jeokge meokseumnida. — I eat as little as possible.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 and 5 (the models)
explanations.body: In Follow-up 4, Partner A reads a sentence strip, Partner B conjugates a verb with –는 한, and Partner A completes the sentence with a main clause. In Follow-up 5, you are given a card describing a concern and give advice with –(으)ㄴ/는 한 to three classmates. The book’s models (the English is mine):

examples.text: 패스트푸드를 많이 먹는 한 체중이 줄지 않을 거예요.
examples.translation: paeseuteupudeureul mani meongneun han chejungi julji aneul geoyeyo. — As long as you eat a lot of fast food, your weight will not decrease.

examples.text: 저녁에 커피를 마시면 잠을 잘 못 자요.
examples.translation: jeonyeoge keopireul masimyeon jameul jal mot jayo. — If I drink coffee in the evening, I can’t sleep well.

examples.text: 가능한 한 커피 대신 주스를 마시세요.
examples.translation: ganeunghan han keopi daesin juseureul masiseyo. — Please drink juice instead of coffee as much as possible.

explanations.title: More sentences (mine)
explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

examples.text: 한국에 있는 한 한국어로 말하겠어요.
examples.translation: hanguge inneun han hangugeoro malhagesseoyo. — As long as I am in Korea, I will speak in Korean.

examples.text: 날씨가 좋은 한 매일 걷겠어요.
examples.translation: nalssiga joeun han maeil geotgesseoyo. — As long as the weather is good, I will walk every day.

examples.text: 가능한 한 일찍 일어나세요.
examples.translation: ganeunghan han iljjik ireonaseyo. — Please get up as early as possible.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with.

Now I am able to: identify and discuss serious crimes such as murder, robbery, theft, sexual assault, violence, etc.; identify and describe physical appearance; identify instances of juvenile delinquency such as bullying and drug addiction; and identify shifting trends of crimes and discuss recent crimes such as ID theft and voice phishing scams.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; –는/(으)ㄴ 대로 and ~대로 (in accordance with; as); the auxiliary verb –고 말다; the auxiliary verb –아/어 있다; expressing “as long as” using –(으)ㄴ/는 한; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 폭력 (暴力), 강력 (强力), and 불법 (不法).

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning, and the book’s parenthesized forms such as ~하다 and ~되다 show how a noun forms a verb. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (3범 → 삼 범; 50명 → 오십 명; 30대 → 삼십 대; 50대 → 오십 대; 7살 → 일곱 살; 5만 원짜리 → 오만 원짜리; 10만 원짜리 → 십만 원짜리; CCTV → 씨씨티브이).

lessons.title: 484. Ch 39 · What the chapter teaches, 예보 (豫報) · 폭우 (暴雨) · 지진 (地震)
lessons.subtitle: 자연재해 · 예보 · 예약 · 예방 · 폭우 · 우산 · 지진 · 여진

explanations.title: What Chapter 39 teaches (자연재해)
explanations.body:
Chapter 39, “Natural Disasters”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: comprehend weather forecasts and talk about suitable activities for varying weather conditions; extract information about natural hazards (flood, earthquake, landslide, etc.) and extreme weather (drought, blizzard), and discuss the disasters caused by them; identify different types of natural disasters and the causes, damages, and casualties associated with them; and report about and describe natural disasters, including the causes, damages, and casualties.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; question words used as indefinite pronouns; a noun clause in an appositive relationship; a question word + (이)나/(이)든지; ~에 관해서/관하여 vs. ~에 관한 (about; regarding; concerning); ~을/를 위해서/위하여 vs. ~을/를 위한 (for the sake of; for); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 예보 (豫報), 폭우 (暴雨), and 지진 (地震).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 예보 (豫報)
explanations.body: The syllable 예 (豫) means beforehand or in advance, as in 예매 (advanced purchase); 보 (報) means report, as in 특보 (special report). Thus, the literal meaning of this Sino-Korean word is “report (on something) in advance”, and the word refers to a (weather) forecast. The book asks you to guess the meaning of 예약, 예매, 예방, 보고서, 보도 and 속보 (my answers are in the table).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 폭우 (暴雨)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means rainstorm or sudden and heavy rain. The first syllable 폭 (暴) means fierce or violent, as in 폭설 (snowstorm; blizzard; “violent snow”), 폭풍 (windstorm; a gust; “violent wind”), and 폭등 (a sudden jump; a sharp rise; “fierce rise”). The second syllable 우 (雨) means rain, as in 우기 (the rainy season; “rainy period”), 우산 (an umbrella), 우비 (a rain outfit; rain gear), 우박 (hail; a hailstone), 강우량 (rainfall; “amount of descending rain”), and 우천 (rainy weather; a rainy day; “rainy sky”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 폭우 is “fierce rain” or “violent rain”, and the word refers to a storm with rain.

rows: a sudden jump; a sharp rise; “fierce rise”
rainy weather; a rainy day; “rainy sky”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 지진 (地震)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means an earthquake. The first syllable 지 (地) means earth or land, as in 지각 (the crust of the earth), 지구 (the earth; the globe; “earth ball”), 지뢰 (a land mine), 천지 (heaven and earth; whole world), 지중해 (the Mediterranean Sea; “sea in the middle of earth”), 지도 (a map; “earth picture”), and 지하도 (an underpass; “land below way”). The second syllable 진 (震) means tremor or shock, as in 강진 (a strong earthquake; a severe earthquake), 여진 (a minor shock following the main shock of an earthquake; “remaining tremor”), 진동 (a shock; a tremor; a quake), and 뇌진탕 (the concussion of the brain). Thus the literal meaning of the word 지진 is “earth tremor” or “earth shock”.

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 주의보 and 경보
explanations.body: The words 주의보 (an advisory) and 경보 (a warning) are often found in a weather report or forecast. 기상청 (Korea Meteorological Administration) issues 주의보 or 경보, depending on the severity of the expected weather condition. For example, if it is expected to snow more than 5 centimeters within 24 hours, a 폭설주의보 is issued; if it is expected to snow more than 20 centimeters, a 폭설경보 is issued. 주의보 or 경보 can be attached to nouns referring to extreme weather conditions, such as 태풍, 폭풍, 폭설, 호우, 황사, etc.; for example 태풍주의보 (a typhoon advisory) and 황사경보 (a yellow dust warning).

examples.text: 지난 겨울부터 올해 봄까지의 강수량이 평년보다 적어 전국적으로 가뭄 현상이 심각한 것으로 나타났습니다.
examples.translation: jinan gyeoulbuteo olhae bomkkajiui gangsuryangi pyeongnyeonboda jeogeo jeongukjeogeuro gamum hyeonsangi simgakan geoseuro natanatseumnida. — It was found that, as the precipitation from last winter to this spring was less than in an average year, the drought phenomenon is serious nationwide.

examples.text: 특히 영동 지방은 예년의 오십 퍼센트만 비가 내려 다른 지역에 비해 가뭄이 심한 것으로 조사됐습니다.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): a weather forecast for South Korea
explanations.body: The following weather forecast is for South Korea. The book asks you to read it and write the weather information for the regions 백령도 (West Sea central sea), 울릉도 (East Sea central sea), 인천 (Gyeonggi-do) and 광주 in English (one is done for you: “Mostly clear”). The forecast is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (the range “8 ~ 17도” is read “8도에서 17도” or “8도 내지 17도”, as the book notes); the English is mine.

examples.text: 이십일 일은 전국이 고기압의 가장자리에 들면서 중부지방은 구름이 많겠다.
examples.translation: isibil ireun jeongugi gogiabui gajangjarie deulmyeonseo jungbujibangeun gureumi manketda. — On the 21st, as the whole country comes under the edge of a high-pressure system, the central region will have many clouds.

examples.text: 서울과 경기도, 강원도 북부에서는 오전이나 낮에 한 때 비, 강수확률 사십 퍼센트, 가 조금 오는 곳이 있겠고 그밖의 지방은 대체로 맑겠다.
examples.translation: seoulgwa gyeonggido, gangwondo bukbueseoneun ojeonina naje han ttae bi, gangsuhwangnyul sasip peosenteu, ga jogeum oneun gosi itgetgo geubakkui jibangeun daechero malgetda. — In Seoul, Gyeonggi-do and northern Gangwon-do, there will be places with a little rain at times in the morning or daytime (40 percent chance of precipitation), and other regions will be mostly clear.

examples.text: 아침 최저기온은 섭씨 팔 도에서 십칠 도, 낮 최고기온은 십구 도에서 이십구 도가 되겠으며 바다의 물결은 서해 중부 바다와 동해 중부 바다에서 오후에 일 점 오 미터에서 이 점 오 미터로 점차 높게 일고 그밖의 해상에서는 영 점 오 미터에서 이 미터로 일겠다.
examples.translation: achim choejeogioneun seopssi pal doeseo sipchil do, nat choegogioneun sipgu doeseo isipgu doga doegesseumyeo badaui mulgyeoreun seohae jungbu badawa donghae jungbu badaeseo ohue il jeom o miteoeseo i jeom o miteoro jeomcha nopge ilgo geubakkui haesangeseoneun yeong jeom o miteoeseo i miteoro ilgetda. — The morning low will be 8 to 17 degrees Celsius and the daytime high 19 to 29 degrees, and the waves at sea will gradually rise to 1.5 to 2.5 m in the afternoon in the central West Sea and central East Sea, and to 0.5 to 2.0 m in other seas.

explanations.title: The regions filled in (mine)
explanations.body: My answers:

rows: Waves rising gradually to 1.5–2.5 m in the afternoon
Waves rising gradually to 1.5–2.5 m in the afternoon
A little rain at times in the morning or daytime (40 percent chance of precipitation)

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Listening and reading): the living index (생활지수)
explanations.body:
The book’s footnote: 생활지수 (“living index”) means the possibility (0–100%) of being able to do a particular activity, given the weather conditions. For example, the possibility of washing a car would be 20% if the 세차지수 indicates 20%. This means the day is not ideal for washing a car. The higher the number, the greater the likelihood of being able to do a particular activity.

The book gives two tables for 오늘의 생활지수 (the 23rd, Tuesday) from Yonhap News, one for 중부 and one for 남부, and asks you to identify which is which (this depends on the audio). The first four rows are the lower-index table and the last four the higher-index table; the English is mine (the book glosses 우산: an umbrella).

rows: Don’t forget to take an umbrella.
오늘은 세차하기에 안 좋은 날이에요. 다음에 하세요.
Today is not a good day to wash the car. Do it next time.
It is not a very good day to go out.
There is no need to take an umbrella.
Today is a good day to wash the car.
Today is a good day to go out.
It is a good day to exercise outside.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading): the four seasons in Korea
explanations.body: The following text is about four seasons in Korea (the book glosses 지구 온난화: global warming). The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (the days in the book’s brackets are set off by commas); the English is mine.

examples.text: 기상청의 발표에 의하면 우리나라의 사계절이 바뀌고 있다.
examples.translation: gisangcheongui balpyoe uihamyeon urinaraui sagyejeori bakkwigo itda. — According to the Korea Meteorological Administration’s announcement, Korea’s four seasons are changing.

examples.text: 백여 년 전에는 겨울이 가장 긴 계절이었지만 최근에는 여름이 가장 길어졌다.
examples.translation: baegyeo nyeon jeoneneun gyeouri gajang gin gyejeorieotjiman choegeuneneun yeoreumi gajang gireojeotda. — More than 100 years ago winter was the longest season, but recently summer has become the longest.

examples.text: 한반도의 연평균 기온은 과거에 비해 최근 일 점 육 도 올랐다.
examples.translation: hanbandoui yeonpyeonggyun gioneun gwageoe bihae choegeun il jeom yuk do ollatda. — The annual average temperature of the Korean peninsula has risen 1.6 degrees recently compared with the past.

examples.text: 기후변화로 인한 지구 온난화 양상이 뚜렷하게 나타나는 것이다.
examples.translation: gihubyeonhwaro inhan jigu onnanhwa yangsangi tturyeotage natananeun geosida. — The pattern of global warming caused by climate change is clearly showing.

examples.text: 기온이 오르면서 계절의 길이가 달라졌다.
examples.translation: gioni oreumyeonseo gyejeorui giriga dallajeotda. — As the temperature rose, the length of the seasons changed.

examples.text: 과거에는 겨울이 백구 일로 가장 길었고, 그 뒤 여름 구십팔 일, 봄 팔십오 일, 가을 칠십삼 일 순이었다.
examples.translation: gwageoeneun gyeouri baekgu illo gajang gireotgo, geu dwi yeoreum gusippal il, bom palsibo il, gaeul chilsipsam il sunieotda. — In the past winter was the longest at 109 days, followed by summer (98 days), spring (85 days) and autumn (73 days).

examples.text: 그러나 최근에는 여름이 백십팔 일로 가장 길고 봄 구십일 일, 겨울 팔십칠 일, 가을 육십구 일 순으로 바뀌었다.
examples.translation: geureona choegeuneneun yeoreumi baeksippal illo gajang gilgo bom gusibil il, gyeoul palsipchil il, gaeul yuksipgu il suneuro bakkwieotda. — But recently summer is the longest at 118 days, followed by spring (91 days), winter (87 days) and autumn (69 days).

examples.text: 여름이 이십 일 길어지고 겨울은 이십이 일 짧아진 것이다.
examples.translation: yeoreumi isip il gireojigo gyeoureun isibi il jjalbajin geosida. — Summer has become 20 days longer and winter 22 days shorter.

explanations.title: The answer (mine)
explanations.body: The book asks: What is said about the four seasons in Korea, and what is behind this? My answers:

rows: Winter was longest (109 days), then summer (98), spring (85), autumn (73)
Summer is longest (118 days), then spring (91), winter (87), autumn (69)
Climate change and global warming: the annual average temperature rose 1.6 degrees

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (SMART Board), the sound parts of Activity 3 (a YTN weather forecast video, a map exercise and translating two sentences heard from the forecast) and Activity 5 (acting as a meteorologist: collecting a three-day forecast and living-index information from a website and presenting a script) need video, a map, a website and a partner.

explanations.title: Topic B: Climate change and natural disasters (기후변화와 자연재해)
explanations.body: The following text is an excerpt from a TV news program in which a news anchor is discussing the abnormal weather with a weather reporter. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the speaker labels 사회자 and 기자 are the book’s.)

examples.text: 사회자: 안녕하세요? 정 기자님, 요즘 세계 여러 곳에서 이상기후가 나타나면서 많은 자연재해가 발생하고 있는데요. 우리나라도 날씨가 점점 이상해지고 있는 것 같죠?
examples.translation: sahoeja: annyeonghaseyo? jeong gijanim, yojeum segye yeoreo goseseo isanggihuga natanamyeonseo maneun jayeonjaehaega balsaenghago inneundeyo. urinarado nalssiga jeomjeom isanghaejigo inneun geot gatjo? — Hello? Reporter Chung, as abnormal weather is appearing in many parts of the world these days, many natural disasters are occurring. It seems Korea’s weather too is getting stranger, doesn’t it?

examples.text: 기자: 네, 맞습니다. 얼마 전까지는 전국적으로 건조한 날씨 때문에 산불이 자주 발생한다는 이야기를 들었는데요. 지난주부터는 갑자기 태풍이 오고 폭우도 쏟아지고 있습니다.
examples.translation: gija: ne, matseumnida. eolma jeonkkajineun jeongukjeogeuro geonjohan nalssi ttaemune sanburi jaju balsaenghandaneun iyagireul deureonneundeyo. jinanjubuteoneun gapjagi taepungi ogo pogudo ssodajigo itseumnida. — Yes, that’s right. Until a while ago I heard that wildfires were occurring often because of the dry weather nationwide, but since last week suddenly a typhoon has come and a heavy rain is pouring.

examples.text: 사회자: 비가 오면서 다행히 가뭄은 해소됐지만, 이제는 반대로 홍수나 침수 걱정을 하게 되었네요. 그리고 올해는 예년보다 집중호우가 더 일찍 내려서 큰 피해를 주고 있다고요? 어떤 피해들이 있나요?
examples.translation: sahoeja: biga omyeonseo dahaenghi gamumeun haesodwaetjiman, ijeneun bandaero hongsuna chimsu geokjeongeul hage doeeonneyo. geurigo olhaeneun yenyeonboda jipjunghouga deo iljjik naeryeoseo keun pihaereul jugo itdagoyo? eotteon pihaedeuri innayo? — Fortunately the drought has been relieved with the rain, but now on the contrary we have come to worry about floods and flooding. And this year the concentrated heavy rain came earlier than usual and is causing great damage? What kind of damage is there?

examples.text: 기자: 네, 경기 지역에서는 도로가 물에 잠기고 자동차가 떠내려가기도 했습니다. 그리고 강원도 산간 지역에서는 산사태로 도로가 폐쇄된 곳도 있습니다.
examples.translation: gija: ne, gyeonggi jiyeogeseoneun doroga mure jamgigo jadongchaga tteonaeryeogagido haetseumnida. geurigo gangwondo sangan jiyeogeseoneun sansataero doroga pyeswaedoen gotdo itseumnida. — Yes, in the Gyeonggi area roads were submerged and cars were even swept away. And in the mountainous area of Gangwon-do there are places where roads were closed because of landslides.

examples.text: 사회자: 기후 변화가 가져오는 재해가 정말 무섭군요. 지금은 비가 그쳤지만 다음 주부터 다시 비가 온다는 일기예보도 있습니다.
examples.translation: sahoeja: gihu byeonhwaga gajeooneun jaehaega jeongmal museopgunyo. jigeumeun biga geucheotjiman daeum jubuteo dasi biga ondaneun ilgiyebodo itseumnida. — The disasters brought by climate change are really frightening. The rain has stopped now, but there is also a forecast that rain will come again from next week.

examples.text: 기자: 네, 그래서 걱정이 많이 됩니다. 지금도 많은 수재민들이 불편을 겪고 계시는데요. 하루빨리 복구 작업이 끝나서 더 큰 피해가 나지 않기를 바랍니다.
examples.translation: gija: ne, geuraeseo geokjeongi mani doemnida. jigeumdo maneun sujaemindeuri bulpyeoneul gyeokgo gyesineundeyo. haruppalli bokgu jageobi kkeunnaseo deo keun pihaega naji ankireul baramnida. — Yes, so I am very worried. Even now many flood victims are going through inconvenience. I hope the restoration work ends as soon as possible so that no greater damage occurs.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: summer in Korea (한국의 여름: 장마, 무더위, 태풍)
explanations.body: Summer falls between June and August in Korea. During this season, the weather is hot and humid, with an average temperature of 78°F. The rainy season, called 장마(철), generally begins in late June and usually lasts until the end of July. During the summer and early fall, typhoons (태풍) frequently occur and bring more rainfall. After 장마 is over, scorching hot days continue until the end of August. Many Koreans take vacations during this time and go to the beaches or mountains to avoid the heat. This summer vacation is called 피서 (“avoiding the heat”), and those who are on 피서 are called 피서객.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): flood damage in North Korea
explanations.body: Read the news article about a natural disaster in North Korea (the book glosses 실종: missing; 가구: a household). The article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (the years are read 이천칠 년 and 이천육 년); the English is mine.

examples.text: 북한지역에도 집중호우가 내려 홍수 피해가 발생했다.
examples.translation: bukanjiyeogedo jipjunghouga naeryeo hongsu pihaega balsaenghaetda. — Concentrated heavy rain fell in the North Korean area too, causing flood damage.

examples.text: 평양방송은 지난 십구 일 평양에 백일 밀리미터에서 삼백이 밀리미터의 폭우가 내렸으며, 평안남북도와 자강도, 함경남도, 강원도 지역에서도 많은 비가 내렸다고 전했다.
examples.translation: pyeongyangbangsongeun jinan sipgu il pyeongyange baegil millimiteoeseo sambaegi millimiteoui poguga naeryeosseumyeo, pyeongannambukdowa jagangdo, hamgyeongnamdo, gangwondo jiyeogeseodo maneun biga naeryeotdago jeonhaetda. — Pyongyang Broadcasting reported that on the 19th a heavy rain of 101 to 302 mm fell in Pyongyang and that much rain also fell in the areas of South and North Pyongan, Jagang, South Hamgyong and Gangwon.

examples.text: 특히 개성 지역에는 팔 월 평균 강우량 이백칠십오 점 칠 밀리미터의 육십오 퍼센트에 달하는 약 사백이십사 밀리미터의 호우가 최근 닷새간 집중적으로 쏟아진 것으로 집계됐다.
examples.translation: teuki gaeseong jiyeogeneun pal wol pyeonggyun ganguryang ibaekchilsibo jeom chil millimiteoui yuksibo peosenteue dalhaneun yak sabaegisipsa millimiteoui houga choegeun datsaegan jipjungjeogeuro ssodajin geoseuro jipgyedwaetda. — In particular, in the Kaesong area a heavy rain of about 424 mm, amounting to 65 percent of the August average rainfall (275.7 mm), was tallied as having poured down intensively over the last five days.

examples.text: 북한은 이천칠 년 팔 월에도 집중호우 때문에 오백여 명이 사망하거나 실종되었으며, 구십만 명의 수재민이 발생했었다.
examples.translation: bukaneun icheonchil nyeon pal woredo jipjunghou ttaemune obaegyeo myeongi samanghageona siljongdoeeosseumyeo, gusimman myeongui sujaemini balsaenghaesseotda. — In August 2007 as well, because of concentrated heavy rain, more than 500 people in North Korea died or went missing, and 900,000 flood victims occurred.

examples.text: 그리고 이천육 년 칠 월에도 홍수 피해 때문에 팔백사십사 명의 사망자와 실종자가 나왔다.
examples.translation: geurigo icheonyuk nyeon chil woredo hongsu pihae ttaemune palbaeksasipsa myeongui samangjawa siljongjaga nawatda. — And in July 2006 too, 844 dead and missing came out because of flood damage.

examples.text: 또한 이만 팔천여 명의 수재민이 발생했으며, 이만 삼천여 가구가 침수됐다.
examples.translation: ttohan iman palcheonyeo myeongui sujaemini balsaenghaesseumyeo, iman samcheonyeo gaguga chimsudwaetda. — In addition, more than 28,000 flood victims occurred, and more than 23,000 households were flooded.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book asks (1) what type of disaster is reported, (2) to check the affected regions on a map, (3) what is said about Kaesong, and (4) to fill in a table of year of flood, casualties and houses flooded. My answers:

rows: A flood caused by concentrated heavy rain
Pyongyang, South and North Pyongan, Jagang, South Hamgyong, Gangwon (and Kaesong)
About 424 mm of heavy rain, 65 percent of the August average rainfall (275.7 mm), poured down over the last five days
More than 500 dead or missing; 900,000 flood victims; houses flooded: N/A
844 dead and missing; more than 28,000 flood victims; more than 23,000 households flooded

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): Text A by an elementary school student
explanations.body: The following texts are about the same natural disaster: Text A was written by an elementary school student and Text B by a newspaper reporter. The book asks you to fill in a table in English from Text A (type of disaster; date and place; cause; casualties; property damage; rescue team’s action), and then to underline the same information in Text B and number it. The texts are the book’s with the numbers spelled out (119 is read 일일구); the English is mine.

examples.text: 칠 일하고 팔 일에 부산에 비가 너무 많이 내렸다.
examples.translation: chil ilhago pal ire busane biga neomu mani naeryeotda. — On the 7th and 8th it rained too much in Busan.

examples.text: 그래서 홍수가 났다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo hongsuga natda. — So a flood occurred.

examples.text: 오늘까지 스물일곱 명이 죽고 스무 명이 다쳤다.
examples.translation: oneulkkaji seumullilgop myeongi jukgo seumu myeongi dacheotda. — As of today 27 people have died and 20 have been injured.

examples.text: 집 이백 채가 물에 잠겼다.
examples.translation: jip ibaek chaega mure jamgyeotda. — Two hundred houses were submerged.

examples.text: 도로도 물에 잠겼다.
examples.translation: dorodo mure jamgyeotda. — Roads were submerged too.

examples.text: 이번 홍수 때문에 삼천 명이 집을 잃어서 우리 학교에서 살고 있다.
examples.translation: ibeon hongsu ttaemune samcheon myeongi jibeul ireoseo uri hakgyoeseo salgo itda. — Because of this flood 3,000 people lost their homes and are living at our school.

examples.text: 아직도 물에 잠긴 집에서 나오지 못한 사람들도 있다.
examples.translation: ajikdo mure jamgin jibeseo naoji motan saramdeuldo itda. — There are still people who could not get out of their submerged houses.

examples.text: 부산 일일구 구조대가 그 사람들을 구조하고 있다.
examples.translation: busan irilgu gujodaega geu saramdeureul gujohago itda. — The Busan 119 rescue team is rescuing those people.

examples.text: 또 경찰은 고속도로도 막았다.
examples.translation: tto gyeongchareun gosokdorodo magatda. — The police also blocked the expressway.

examples.text: 사람이 더 다칠 수도 있다고 한다.

examples.text: 재산 피해가 커질 것이라고 한다.
examples.translation: jaesan pihaega keojil geosirago handa. — They say the property damage will grow.

explanations.title: Text B by a newspaper reporter
explanations.body: The book glosses 주민: a resident; 수용소: a camp. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out; the English is mine.

examples.text: 지난 칠 일, 팔 일 부산 지역에 내린 집중호우로 물난리가 발생해 스물일곱 명이 숨지고 스무 명이 부상을 입었다.
examples.translation: jinan chil il, pal il busan jiyeoge naerin jipjunghouro mullalliga balsaenghae seumullilgop myeongi sumjigo seumu myeongi busangeul ibeotda. — Because of the concentrated heavy rain that fell in the Busan area on the 7th and 8th, a flood occurred and 27 people died and 20 were injured.

examples.text: 또한 주택 이백여 채가 침수되었으며 일부 도로도 물에 잠겼다.
examples.translation: ttohan jutaek ibaegyeo chaega chimsudoeeosseumyeo ilbu dorodo mure jamgyeotda. — In addition, more than 200 houses were flooded and some roads were also submerged.

examples.text: 주택을 잃은 주민 삼천여 명은 수재민 수용소에서 대피 중이다.
examples.translation: jutaegeul ireun jumin samcheonyeo myeongeun sujaemin suyongsoeseo daepi jungida. — More than 3,000 residents who lost their homes are taking shelter at a flood victims’ camp.

examples.text: 부산시는 헬리콥터와 보트를 이용해 구조 작업을 계속하고 있다.

lessons.title: 489. Ch 39 · Grammar A: question words used as indefinite pronouns
lessons.subtitle: 누구 · 무엇 · 언제 · 어디 · 어떻게 · 어느 · 어떤 · 무슨 · 몇 · 누군가 · 어디 가요

explanations.title: Indefinite pronouns
explanations.body: Indefinite pronouns are pronouns that refer to unspecified beings, objects, places, etc. In English, someone, something, anyone, anything, nobody, and nothing are typical examples of indefinite pronouns. In Korean, however, some indefinite pronouns happen to be identical in form with the question words you have learned in earlier chapters (누구, 무엇/뭐, 언제, 어디, etc.). In other words, these words have dual meanings, depending on the context; they can be used as question words (who/whom, what, when, where, etc.) or as indefinite pronouns (someone, something, sometime, somewhere, etc.). The following table lists the words that can be used as question words or indefinite pronouns:

explanations.title: In a non-question sentence
explanations.body: When these words are used in a non-question sentence (statement, command, request, etc.), they always function as indefinite pronouns. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 지금 밖에 누가 있어요.
examples.translation: jigeum bakke nuga isseoyo. — Someone is at the door right now.

examples.text: 우리 언제 같이 점심 먹자.
examples.translation: uri eonje gachi jeomsim meokja. — Let’s have lunch together sometime.

explanations.title: In a question
explanations.body: However, when they are used in a question, depending on the context, they function as either question words or indefinite pronouns. Thus, the following questions can be interpreted in two different ways (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 누가 밖에 왔어요?
examples.translation: nuga bakke wasseoyo? — Who is at the door? or Is someone at the door?

examples.text: 뭐를 먹고 싶으세요?
examples.translation: mworeul meokgo sipeuseyo? — What do you want to eat? or Do you want to eat something?

explanations.title: Stress
explanations.body: In spoken language, however, the speaker’s stress (or lack of stress) helps the listener interpret the meaning of the word. In other words, Koreans tend to stress the word when it is used as a question. The book gives two dialogs (audio) in which 어디 가세요? functions differently (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 가: 김 선생님, 어디 가세요?
examples.translation: ga: gim seonsaengnim, eodi gaseyo? — Mr. Kim, where are you going?

examples.text: 나: 어디 가요.
examples.translation: na: eodi gayo. — I am going somewhere.

examples.text: 가: 김 선생님, 어디 가세요?
examples.translation: ga: gim seonsaengnim, eodi gaseyo? — Are you going somewhere?

examples.text: 나: 네, 어디 가요.
examples.translation: na: ne, eodi gayo. — Yes, I am going somewhere.

explanations.title: More sentences (mine)
explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

examples.translation: nuga jeonhwahaesseoyo. — Somebody called.

examples.text: 무슨 일이 있어요?
examples.translation: museun iri isseoyo? — Is something the matter? / What is the matter?

examples.text: 어떤 지역에서 큰 홍수가 났어요.
examples.translation: eotteon jiyeogeseo keun hongsuga nasseoyo. — A big flood occurred in some region.

lessons.title: 490. Ch 39 · Grammar B: a noun clause in an appositive relationship, –다는 + noun
lessons.subtitle: -다는 소식 · -다는 소문 · -(이)라는 사실 · 산불이 났다는 소식 · 내일 시험 본다는 소식

explanations.title: The appositive
explanations.body: An appositive is a noun, noun phrase, or noun clause that renames or defines another noun. For example, in the following English sentences the phrases in bold are appositives: “Michael Jackson, a famous singer, is no longer with us.” (a noun phrase) and “The rumor that Michael Jackson is still alive is groundless.” (a noun clause). Note that when a noun clause like “Michael Jackson is still alive” becomes an appositive, it begins with that.

explanations.title: In Korean
explanations.body: In Korean, when a noun clause is in an appositive relationship, it ends with the blunt formal form –다, immediately followed by –는. For example (the English is the book’s; the book’s “Big Sur” is a place name):

examples.text: 빅서에 산불이 났다는 소식
examples.translation: bikseoe sanburi natdaneun sosik — the news that a wildfire occurred in Big Sur

examples.text: 김 선생님이 결혼한다는 소문
examples.translation: gim seonsaengnimi gyeolhonhandaneun somun — the rumor that Ms. Kim is getting married

explanations.title: 이다 / 아니다
explanations.body: When the verb of the noun clause is 이다 / 아니다, however, 이다 changes to (이)라 (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 내가 군인이라는 사실
examples.translation: naega guniniraneun sasil — the fact that I am a serviceman

examples.text: 내가 공군이 아니라는 말
examples.translation: naega gongguni aniraneun mal — the talk that I am not an airman

explanations.title: Expressing the noun clause in an appositive relationship
explanations.body: formal blunt form + 는 + noun. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 서울에서 큰 교통사고가 났다는 뉴스를 들었습니까?
examples.translation: seoureseo keun gyotongsagoga natdaneun nyuseureul deureotseumnikka? — Did you hear the news that a big traffic accident occurred in Seoul?

examples.text: 산호세에 한국마켓이 많다는 사실을 알고 있습니까?
examples.translation: sanhosee hangungmakesi mantaneun sasireul algo itseumnikka? — Do you know that there are many Korean markets in San Jose?

lessons.subtitle: 지난주에 강진이 발생했어요 · 튀르키예 지진 · 구조대 · 매몰 생존자 · 여진 · 구호품 · 쓰나미와 해일 · 한국과 쓰나미

explanations.title: Topic C: A strong earthquake occurred last week (지난주에 강진이 발생했어요)
explanations.body: The following text is about the earthquake that occurred in Türkiye. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the numbers are spelled out in Hangul. This is a news report of a disaster with many deaths.)

examples.text: 육 일 새벽 튀르키예 남부와 시리아 북부에서 강진이 발생했다.
examples.translation: yuk il saebyeok twireukiye nambuwa siria bukbueseo gangjini balsaenghaetda. — In the early morning of the 6th, a strong earthquake occurred in southern Türkiye and northern Syria.

examples.text: 지진 발생 후 구 일가량이 지난 현재 두 나라에서 벌써 사망자가 사만 명을 넘었다.
examples.translation: jijin balsaeng hu gu ilgaryangi jinan hyeonjae du naraeseo beolsseo samangjaga saman myeongeul neomeotda. — At present, about nine days after the earthquake, the dead in the two countries have already passed 40,000.

examples.text: 그런데 대피하지 못한 사람들 중에 실종자가 많아 이들을 포함하면 인명피해는 더 늘 것으로 보인다.
examples.translation: geureonde daepihaji motan saramdeul junge siljongjaga mana ideureul pohamhamyeon inmyeongpihaeneun deo neul geoseuro boinda. — But among the people who could not evacuate there are many missing, so including them the human casualties are expected to increase further.

examples.text: 현재 세계 여러 나라의 구조대원들이 무너진 건물 밑에 매몰된 생존자들을 수색하고 있다.
examples.translation: hyeonjae segye yeoreo naraui gujodaewondeuri muneojin geonmul mite maemoldoen saengjonjadeureul susaekago itda. — At present rescue workers from many countries of the world are searching for survivors buried under collapsed buildings.

examples.text: 하지만 주요 피해 지역에서 여진이 계속되고 게다가 기온도 떨어져, 흙더미에 묻힌 사람들의 구조 작업도 쉽지 않다.
examples.translation: hajiman juyo pihae jiyeogeseo yeojini gyesokdoego gedaga giondo tteoreojeo, heukdeomie mutin saramdeurui gujo jageopdo swipji anta. — However, aftershocks continue in the major damaged areas and besides, the temperature has dropped, so the rescue work for the people buried in mud piles is not easy either.

examples.text: 한국 정부도 구조대 예순한 명을 보내서 도움을 주고 있다.
examples.translation: hanguk jeongbudo gujodae yesunhan myeongeul bonaeseo doumeul jugo itda. — The Korean government is also helping by sending a rescue team of 61 people.

examples.text: 한편 적십자사와 같은 구호단체들은 생필품과 성금 등을 모아 이재민들을 지원하고 있다.
examples.translation: hanpyeon jeoksipjasawa gateun guhodanchedeureun saengpilpumgwa seonggeum deungeul moa ijaemindeureul jiwonhago itda. — Meanwhile relief organizations such as the Red Cross are collecting daily necessities and donations and supporting the victims.

examples.text: 비누, 치약 같은 생필품 등은 무엇이든지 많이 필요하다고 한다.
examples.translation: binu, chiyak gateun saengpilpum deungeun mueosideunji mani piryohadago handa. — They say daily necessities such as soap and toothpaste, anything, are needed a lot.

examples.text: 튀르키예 지진에 관한 문의는 튀르키예 지진피해 구호물품 지원 안내에 문의하면 된다.
examples.translation: twireukiye jijine gwanhan munuineun twireukiye jijinpihae guhomulpum jiwon annaee munuihamyeon doenda. — For inquiries about the Türkiye earthquake, you can inquire at the Türkiye Earthquake Relief Supplies Support Information.

explanations.title: 한국어에서는: 쓰나미 (지진해일) and 해일
explanations.body: 쓰나미 (a tsunami) refers to a series of water waves caused by underwater earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or other underwater explosions and mass movements. On the other hand, 해일 (tidal wave) usually refers to a water surge caused by floodwater, a storm surge, or a tsunami.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): an article about tsunamis
explanations.body: The following article is about tsunamis (지진해일). The book asks (1) what makes Korea susceptible to tsunamis and (2) to describe the damages caused by the 1983 tsunami. The article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out; the English is mine.

examples.text: 우리나라는 쓰나미로부터 안전할까요?
examples.translation: urinaraneun sseunamirobuteo anjeonhalkkayo? — Is Korea safe from tsunamis?

examples.text: 삼 면이 바다로 둘러싸여 있고 지진이 자주 일어나는 지역인 일본에 가까운 우리나라는 결코 쓰나미로부터 자유로울 수 없는 곳입니다.
examples.translation: sam myeoni badaro dulleossayeo itgo jijini jaju ireonaneun jiyeogin ilbone gakkaun urinaraneun gyeolko sseunamirobuteo jayuroul su eomneun gosimnida. — Korea, which is surrounded by sea on three sides and close to Japan, an area where earthquakes occur often, is a place that can never be free from tsunamis.

examples.text: 만약 일본의 북서 근해에서 지진이 발생한다면 쓰나미는 한 시간에서 한 시간 삼십 분 후 대한민국 동해에 도착하게 됩니다.
examples.translation: manyak ilbonui bukseo geunhaeeseo jijini balsaenghandamyeon sseunamineun han siganeseo han sigan samsip bun hu daehanminguk donghaee dochakage doemnida. — If an earthquake occurs in the northwest coastal sea of Japan, the tsunami will arrive in the East Sea of the Republic of Korea in one hour to one hour thirty minutes.

examples.text: 실제로 동해안에서도 천구백팔십삼 년과 천구백구십삼 년 일본 근해에서 발생한 지진 해일로 인해 피해를 입은 사례가 있습니다.
examples.translation: siljero donghaeaneseodo cheongubaekpalsipsam nyeongwa cheongubaekgusipsam nyeon ilbon geunhaeeseo balsaenghan jijin haeillo inhae pihaereul ibeun saryega itseumnida. — In fact, there have been cases on the east coast too of suffering damage from tsunamis that occurred in the coastal sea of Japan in 1983 and 1993.

examples.text: 천구백팔십삼 년 쓰나미로 인해 주민 한 명과 어부 두 명이 사망했습니다.
examples.translation: cheongubaekpalsipsam nyeon sseunamiro inhae jumin han myeonggwa eobu du myeongi samanghaetseumnida. — In the 1983 tsunami one resident and two fishermen died.

examples.text: 또한 해일이 항구로부터 칠백 미터 떨어진 인근 초등학교까지 올라와 그 지역 초등학교는 휴교령이 내려지는 등 큰 피해를 주었다고 합니다.
examples.translation: ttohan haeiri hanggurobuteo chilbaek miteo tteoreojin ingeun chodeunghakgyokkaji ollawa geu jiyeok chodeunghakgyoneun hyugyoryeongi naeryeojineun deung keun pihaereul jueotdago hamnida. — Also, the tidal wave came up to a nearby elementary school 700 m away from the port, and they say it caused great damage, such as an order closing the elementary schools in that area.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: My answers:

rows: It is surrounded by sea on three sides and is close to Japan, where earthquakes occur often; a tsunami from northwest Japan would reach the East Sea within about one to one and a half hours
One resident and two fishermen died; the wave rose to an elementary school 700 m from the port, and the schools in the area were ordered closed

lessons.title: 492. Ch 39 · Grammar C: a question word + (이)나/(이)든지 (whoever, whatever, wherever, whenever)
lessons.subtitle: 누구나 · 누구든지 · 무엇이든지 · 어디든지 · 언제든지 · 아무나

explanations.title: A question word + (이)나/(이)든지
explanations.body: In an earlier lesson you learned that the question words like 누구, 언제, 어디, and 무엇 can function as indefinite pronouns. For example, 누구 can be translated as who or someone and 어디 as where or someplace. When the particle ~(이)나 or ~(이)든지 is attached to these question words, they can be translated as follows:

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: (The English is the book’s; the book gives each example with the 나 form; the 든지 forms are mine.)

examples.text: 이 영화는 누구나 볼 수 있어요.
examples.translation: i yeonghwaneun nuguna bol su isseoyo. — Anyone can watch this movie.

examples.text: 우리 형은 무엇이나 잘 먹어요.
examples.translation: uri hyeongeun mueosina jal meogeoyo. — My older brother eats anything well.

examples.text: 주말에는 어디에나 갈 수 있어요.
examples.translation: jumareneun eodiena gal su isseoyo. — I can go anywhere on weekends.

examples.text: 질문 있으면 언제나 전화하세요.
examples.translation: jilmun isseumyeon eonjena jeonhwahaseyo. — Please call me anytime if you have a question.

examples.text: 이 영화는 누구든지 볼 수 있어요.
examples.translation: i yeonghwaneun nugudeunji bol su isseoyo. — Anyone can watch this movie.

examples.text: 우리 형은 무엇이든지 잘 먹어요.
examples.translation: uri hyeongeun mueosideunji jal meogeoyo. — My older brother eats anything well.

examples.text: 주말에는 어디든지 갈 수 있어요.
examples.translation: jumareneun eodideunji gal su isseoyo. — I can go anywhere on weekends.

examples.text: 질문 있으면 언제든지 전화하세요.
examples.translation: jilmun isseumyeon eonjedeunji jeonhwahaseyo. — Please call me anytime if you have a question.

explanations.title: 참고: 아무 + (noun) + (이)나
explanations.body: Without changing the meaning, a question word + (이)나/(이)든지 can be replaced with 아무 + (noun) + (이)나. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 이 책은 쉬워서 누구나 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.translation: i chaegeun swiwoseo nuguna ilgeul su isseoyo. — This book is so easy [that] anyone can read it.

examples.text: 이 책은 쉬워서 누구든지 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.translation: i chaegeun swiwoseo nugudeunji ilgeul su isseoyo. — This book is so easy [that] anyone can read it.

examples.text: 이 책은 쉬워서 아무나 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.translation: i chaegeun swiwoseo amuna ilgeul su isseoyo. — This book is so easy [that] anyone can read it.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): fill in the blanks
explanations.body: Choose the most appropriate phrase from the box 누구나/누구든지, 언제나/언제든지, 어디나/어디든지, 무엇이나/무엇이든지 and complete each sentence. The sentences are the book’s; the completed answers are mine; the English is mine.

rows: 도움이 필요하신 분은 언제든지 저한테 연락주세요.
Anyone who needs help, please contact me anytime.
열심히 노력하면 누구나 성공할 수 있어요.
If you try hard, anyone can succeed.
지진 이재민을 위한 구호물품으로 무엇이든지 환영합니다.

이번 세일 기간 중에는 서울 시내 어디나 무료로 배달해 드립니다.
During this sale period we deliver free anywhere in Seoul.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking and writing): the model
explanations.body: One partner draws a topic card and reads it aloud; the other makes a sentence with a question word + (이)나/(이)든지. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 생일 파티
examples.translation: ga: saengil pati — Birthday party

examples.text: 나: 제 생일 파티에는 누구나 올 수 있어요.
examples.translation: na: je saengil patieneun nuguna ol su isseoyo. — Anyone can come to my birthday party.

examples.text: 나: 제 생일 파티 선물은 무엇이든지 좋아요.
examples.translation: na: je saengil pati seonmureun mueosideunji joayo. — Any present for my birthday party is fine.

explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

examples.translation: eodideunji ttaragalgeyo. — I will follow you anywhere.

lessons.title: 493. Ch 39 · Grammar D: ~에 관해서 vs. ~에 관한 and ~을/를 위해서 vs. ~을/를 위한 · and self-evaluation
lessons.subtitle: ~에 관해서 · ~에 관한 · ~을 위해서 · ~을 위한 · ~에 대해서 · ~에 대한 · 자기 평가

explanations.title: Recall ~에 대해(서) and ~에 대한
explanations.body: You learned in Chapter 19 that the phrases ~에 대해(서), ~에 대하여, and ~에 대한 can be translated as about (or concerning or regarding), as in 김치에 대해서 (about kimchi), 김치에 대하여 (about kimchi), and 김치에 대한 (about kimchi). You also learned that ~에 대해(서) and ~에 대하여 are reserved to modify a verb and ~에 대한 is reserved to modify a noun. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 사회 문제에 대해서 이야기했습니다.
examples.translation: sahoe munjee daehaeseo iyagihaetseumnida. — We talked about social issues.

examples.text: 사회 문제에 대한 의견을 나누었습니다.
examples.translation: sahoe munjee daehan uigyeoneul nanueotseumnida. — We shared the opinion about social issues.

explanations.title: Why they differ
explanations.body:
Note that ~에 대해(서) modifies the verb 이야기했습니다 and ~에 대한 modifies the noun 의견. This occurs because these phrases are derived from the verb 대하다 (to face; to confront). 대한 in ~에 대한 is an attributive form of the verb 대하다; thus the phrase can only modify a noun.

The following phrases are also derived from a verb and show the same pattern: 1. ~에 관해서/관하여/관한 (about; regarding; concerning); 2. ~을/를 위해(서)/위하여/위한 (for the benefit of; for the sake of). ~에 관해서/관하여/관한 are derived from the verb 관하다 (to be related to; to concern; to pertain to) and 위해(서)/위하여/위한 are derived from the verb 위하다 (to do for the greater good; to serve; to honor). ~에 관해서/관하여 and ~을/를 위해서/위하여 modify a verb (or verb phrase), whereas the attributive form ~에 관한 and ~을/를 위한 modify a noun. (The English is the book’s.)

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with.

Now I am able to: comprehend weather forecasts and talk about suitable activities for varying weather conditions; extract factual information about natural hazards (flood, earthquake, landslide, etc.) and extreme weather (drought, blizzard), and discuss the disasters caused by them; identify different types of natural disasters and the causes, damages, and casualties associated with them; and report about and describe natural disasters, including the causes, damages, and casualties.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; question words used as indefinite pronouns; a noun clause in an appositive relationship; a question word + (이)나/(이)든지; ~에 관해서/관하여 vs. ~에 관한 (about; regarding; concerning); ~을/를 위해서/위하여 vs. ~을/를 위한 (for the sake of; for); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 예보 (豫報), 폭우 (暴雨), and 지진 (地震).

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading): a news article about rescue dogs
explanations.body: The following news article (Yonhap News) is about Korean rescue dogs in Türkiye. The book asks you (1) to create a fitting headline, (2) to say what advantage the rescue dogs contribute to the rescue operation and (3) to say what happened to three of the dogs. The article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out; the abbreviation KDRT and the news agency names in Latin letters are dropped (“TRT 하베르” is written 하베르); the English is mine.

examples.text: 튀르키예 강진 피해 현장에서 발에 붕대를 감은 채 수색 작업을 이어가고 있는 한국 구조견이 현지에서도 화제다.
examples.translation: twireukiye gangjin pihae hyeonjangeseo bare bungdaereul gameun chae susaek jageobeul ieogago inneun hanguk gujogyeoni hyeonjieseodo hwajeda. — The Korean rescue dogs continuing search work with bandages wrapped around their feet at the scene of the Türkiye earthquake damage are also a topic of conversation locally.

examples.text: 튀르키예 강진 피해 지역에서 활동 중인 한국 해외긴급구호대는 지난 구 일 구조 활동을 시작한 이래 총 여덟 명의 생존자를 구조했고, 시신 열여덟 구를 찾았다.
examples.translation: twireukiye gangjin pihae jiyeogeseo hwaldong jungin hanguk haeoegingeupguhodaeneun jinan gu il gujo hwaldongeul sijakan irae chong yeodeol myeongui saengjonjareul gujohaetgo, sisin yeollyeodeol gureul chajatda. — The Korea Disaster Relief Team, which is active in the Türkiye earthquake damage area, has rescued a total of eight survivors and found 18 bodies since it began rescue activity on the 9th.

examples.text: 구조 활동에는 특수 인명구조견인 토백이, 티나, 토리, 해태 등 네 마리가 투입됐다.
examples.translation: gujo hwaldongeneun teuksu inmyeonggujogyeonin tobaegi, tina, tori, haetae deung ne mariga tuipdwaetda. — Four dogs, the special life-saving dogs Tobaegi, Tina, Tori and Haetae, were put into the rescue activity.

examples.text: 이들은 모두 이 년간의 훈련 과정을 거쳤다.
examples.translation: ideureun modu i nyeonganui hullyeon gwajeongeul geocheotda. — All of them went through a two-year training course.

examples.text: 구조견들은 무너진 건물 사이에 사람이 들어가기 어려운 좁은 공간에도 접근하고 있다.
examples.translation: gujogyeondeureun muneojin geonmul saie sarami deureogagi eoryeoun jobeun gongganedo jeopgeunhago itda. — The rescue dogs are approaching even narrow spaces between the collapsed buildings where it is hard for people to get in.

examples.text: 위험한 재난 현장을 이리저리 뛰어다닌 탓에 네 마리 가운데 세 마리가 깨진 유리와 부러진 철근에 발에 상처를 입었다.
examples.translation: wiheomhan jaenan hyeonjangeul irijeori ttwieodanin tase ne mari gaunde se mariga kkaejin yuriwa bureojin cheolgeune bare sangcheoreul ibeotda. — Because they ran about the dangerous disaster scene, three of the four dogs were wounded on their feet by broken glass and broken steel bars.

examples.text: 그러나 세 마리 모두 치료를 받은 뒤 다시 현장에 투입됐고, 현재 발에 붕대를 감은 채 계속해서 수색 작업을 이어가고 있다고 하베르는 전했다.
examples.translation: geureona se mari modu chiryoreul badeun dwi dasi hyeonjange tuipdwaetgo, hyeonjae bare bungdaereul gameun chae gyesokaeseo susaek jageobeul ieogago itdago habereuneun jeonhaetda. — However, all three dogs were put back into the scene after receiving treatment, and are now continuing the search work with bandages on their feet, the TRT Haber reported.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: My answers:

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning, and the book’s parenthesized forms such as ~하다 and ~되다 show how a noun forms a verb. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (50 mm → 오십 밀리미터; 1온스 → 한 온스; 980달러 → 구백팔십 달러; 3년 만에 → 삼 년 만에; 7월 → 칠 월; 30도 → 삼십 도; 20cm → 이십 센티미터; 6월 → 유월; 1명 → 한 명; 10명 → 열 명; the English “aurora” and “ounce” are dropped). For the grammar features, the book’s long English labels are used as given.

lessons.title: 496. Ch 40 · What the chapter teaches, 분리 · 재활용 · 온난화 · 식물 · 경차
lessons.subtitle: 환경 · 분리 · 재활용 · 온난화 · 식물 · 경차 · 이식 · 난방 · 활동

explanations.title: What Chapter 40 teaches (환경)
explanations.body:
Chapter 40, “The Environment”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify waste separation and disposal methods; extract factual information about and discuss global warming, its causes, impact, and preventive measures; make suggestions on how to reduce food waste; and talk about the efforts to conserve resources and protect the environment.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the conjunctive ending –자; expressions frequently used in news reports; –(으)ㅁ and –(으)ㄹ 것, abbreviated verb endings used in writing; the conjunctive ending –다면 for a hypothetical condition; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 분리 (分離), 재활용 (再活用), 온난화 (溫暖化), 식물 (植物), and 경차 (輕車).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 분리 (分離)
explanations.body: The syllable 분 (分) means division, section, or fraction, as in 분 (minute; “fraction [of an hour]”), 분대 (squad; “divided group”), and 분수 (fraction; “fractional number”). 리 (離) means detachment, separation, or “off”, as in 이유기 (weaning period; “milk detachment period”). Note that 리 turns into 이 at the beginning of a word. Thus, the literal meaning of the word 분리 is “separation and division” and refers to separation, secession, disunion, split, etc. The book asks you to guess the meaning of 분단, 대부분, 충분, 이탈, 이륙 and 이혼 (my answers are in the table).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 재활용 (再活用)
explanations.body: The syllable 재 (再) means again, twice, or re-, as in 재방송 (rebroadcasting; a re-run) and 재시험 (reexamination; a makeup exam). 활 (活) means life or live(ly), as in 활동 (activity; action), and 용 (用) means use, as in 군사용 (military use) and 일회용 (disposable; “one-time use”). Thus, the literal meaning of the Sino-Korean word 재활용 is “revive and use”, and it means recycling or reuse. The book asks you to guess the meaning of words that contain one of these syllables (the book glosses 화산: a volcano, “fire mountain”; my answers):

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 온난화 (溫暖化)
explanations.body: The syllable 온 (溫) means warm or warmth, as in 온도 (temperature; “degree of warmth”). The syllable 난 (暖) also means warm or heating, as in 난방 (heated room; heating a room). The syllable 화 (化) means change, become, or -ization/-fication, as in 서구화 (Westernization) and 미국화 (Americanization). Thus, the literal meaning of 온난화 is “change of warmth” or “becoming warm”; it generally refers to global warming. The book glosses 유/류 (流): flow; 풍 (風): wind; 노/로 (爐): a fire stove (my answers):

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 경차 (輕車)
explanations.body: The Chinese character of the syllable 경 (輕) depicts a vehicle on wheels crossing a stream and it means light or small, as in 경공업 (light industry). 차 (車) means vehicle on wheels or car. Thus, the literal meaning of the Sino-Korean word 경차 is “light car” or “small car”, and the word refers to a compact car or small car. The book asks you to guess the meaning of words that contain one of these syllables (my answers):

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 식물 (植物)
explanations.body: The Chinese character of the syllable 식 (植) depicts a straight tree, and the syllable means plant (vs. animal) or planting, as in 동식물 (animals and plants; “moving things and planted things”). 물 (物) means thing, object, or material, as in 고물 (an antique; “ancient thing”) and 물가 (price; “prices of things”). Thus, the literal meaning of the Sino-Korean word 식물 is “planted things”, and it refers to a plant, plant life, or vegetation. The book glosses 이 (移): move (my answers):

explanations.title: Activity 1: a handout from an environmental protection seminar
explanations.body: The following handout is from a seminar on environmental protection and is missing some words; the book asks you to complete the sentences with the words in the box 온실가스, 보호, 자제, 배출, 실천, 일회용품. The sentences below are completed with my answers; the English is mine.

rows: 우리 모두 환경을 보호하기 위해 노력해야 합니다.
한 번 쓰고 버리는 나무 젓가락의 사용을 자제합시다.
그리고 온실가스를 줄이기 위해서 냉장고나 에어컨 사용을 줄여야 합니다.
환경 보호를 위해 자기가 할 수 있는 가장 쉬운 것부터 천천히 하나씩 실천하도록 합시다.

examples.text: 우리 모두 환경을 보호하기 위해 노력해야 합니다.
examples.translation: uri modu hwangyeongeul bohohagi wihae noryeokaeya hamnida. — We must all make an effort to protect the environment.

examples.text: 한 번 쓰고 버리는 나무 젓가락의 사용을 자제합시다.
examples.translation: han beon sseugo beorineun namu jeotgaragui sayongeul jajehapsida. — Let’s refrain from using wooden chopsticks that are used once and thrown away.

examples.text: 일회용품은 편리하지만 환경에 좋지 않습니다.
examples.translation: ilhoeyongpumeun pyeollihajiman hwangyeonge jochi anseumnida. — Disposable goods are convenient but not good for the environment.

examples.text: 그리고 온실가스를 줄이기 위해서 냉장고나 에어컨 사용을 줄여야 합니다.
examples.translation: geurigo onsilgaseureul jurigi wihaeseo naengjanggona eeokeon sayongeul juryeoya hamnida. — And in order to reduce greenhouse gas, we must reduce the use of refrigerators and air conditioners.

examples.text: 특히 에어컨은 온실가스를 많이 배출합니다.
examples.translation: teuki eeokeoneun onsilgaseureul mani baechulhamnida. — In particular, air conditioners emit a lot of greenhouse gas.

explanations.title: Topic A: Waste separation and disposal (쓰레기 분리수거)
explanations.body: The following text is a public announcement about the “separation and disposal system” in Korea. The book’s heading is 쓰레기를 줄이고, 재활용을 ___ 늘려 환경을 보호합시다! (one word is blank in the printed text) and “분리 수거 지역: 전국” (the separation area: the whole country). The announcement has four boxes (종이, 유리병, 캔과 페트병, 음식물 쓰레기); the book’s brief notes (some ending in –함, –ㄹ 것) are written below as sentences, with the same meaning; the English is mine. (The book’s footnote: 함 (函) means a box. It is used with another noun as in 우편함 [mailbox], 보관함 [storage box], and 수거함 [collection box].)

examples.text: 쓰레기를 줄이고 재활용을 늘려 환경을 보호합시다.

examples.translation: sinmun, chaek, jongi, sangja, dallyeok deungeun binil koting deungeul jegeohan hu hanaro mukkeo baechulhanda. — Newspapers, books, paper, boxes, calendars, etc.: remove the vinyl coating, etc., then bind them into one and dispose of them.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 쓰레기 분리 수거와 종량제 봉투
explanations.body: In 1995, Korea initiated 쓰레기 분리배출 (waste separation and disposal) for trash and food waste reduction and to help preserve the environment. Koreans sort recyclables into categories such as paper, plastic, and clothes, and must dispose of them properly. For general (unrecyclable) trash and food waste, they must use government-approved plastic bags known as 종량제 봉투 (standard plastic garbage bag; “meter-rate system envelope”). These bags come in different sizes and can be purchased at a market or grocery store. These days newer homes are equipped with a garbage disposal. For the homes without a garbage disposal, people must wring any excess fluid from food waste and then place it in an approved bag for disposal.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): a news report about four cities’ recycling programs
explanations.body: The following news report is about the recycling programs to be run by four major cities (the book glosses 생수: spring water; 가치: value; 청소년: teenagers). The report is the book’s with the numbers spelled out; the book’s English “Ministry of Environment” and “AR-VR” are dropped; the English is mine.

examples.text: 환경부는 전국의 네 개 도시에서 두 달간, 올해 말부터 시작되는 무색 투명 페트병 분리수거를 적극적으로 홍보할 예정이다.
examples.translation: hwangyeongbuneun jeongugui ne gae dosieseo du dalgan, olhae malbuteo sijakdoeneun musaek tumyeong peteubyeong bullisugeoreul jeokgeukjeogeuro hongbohal yejeongida. — The Ministry of Environment plans to actively promote, for two months in four cities nationwide, the separate collection of colorless (transparent) PET bottles that starts at the end of this year.

examples.text: 생수나 음료수를 담는 무색 페트병은 의류나 가방, 신발, 블라인드 등을 만들 수 있어서 재활용 가치가 크다.
examples.translation: saengsuna eumnyosureul damneun musaek peteubyeongeun uiryuna gabang, sinbal, beullaindeu deungeul mandeul su isseoseo jaehwaryong gachiga keuda. — Colorless PET bottles that hold spring water or beverages can be made into clothing, bags, shoes, blinds, etc., so their recycling value is high.

examples.text: 서울특별시는 무색 페트병을 가져오면 현금처럼 쓸 수 있는 포인트를 지급하는데, 작은 페트병 한 개당 백 점, 큰 것은 오백 점을 준다.
examples.translation: seoulteukbyeolsineun musaek peteubyeongeul gajeoomyeon hyeongeumcheoreom sseul su inneun pointeureul jigeupaneunde, jageun peteubyeong han gaedang baek jeom, keun geoseun obaek jeomeul junda. — The Seoul Metropolitan City gives points that can be used like cash if you bring colorless PET bottles: 100 points per small PET bottle and 500 points for a big one.

examples.text: 인천광역시에서는 포인트 대신에 종량제 봉투나 이마트 상품권으로 교환해 줄 예정이다.
examples.translation: incheongwangyeoksieseoneun pointeu daesine jongnyangje bongtuna imateu sangpumgwoneuro gyohwanhae jul yejeongida. — Incheon Metropolitan City plans to exchange them for standard garbage bags or Emart gift certificates instead of points.

examples.text: 광주광역시에서는 청소년을 대상으로 분리배출 가상체험 교육관을 운영할 예정이고, 부산광역시에서는 어린이들을 위해 분리배출의 중요성과 방법에 대한 노래를 만들어 시청 웹사이트와 유튜브에 올릴 예정이다.
examples.translation: gwangjugwangyeoksieseoneun cheongsonyeoneul daesangeuro bullibaechul gasangcheheom gyoyukgwaneul unyeonghal yejeongigo, busangwangyeoksieseoneun eorinideureul wihae bullibaechurui jungyoseonggwa bangbeobe daehan noraereul mandeureo sicheong wepsaiteuwa yutyubeue ollil yejeongida. — Gwangju Metropolitan City plans to operate a virtual-experience education center for separate disposal aimed at teenagers, and Busan Metropolitan City plans to make a song about the importance and method of separate disposal for children and post it on the city hall website and YouTube.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book asks (1) why the Ministry of Environment is actively promoting the recycling of clear PET bottles and (2) to fill in the program of each of four cities. My answers:

rows: They can be made into clothing, bags, shoes, blinds, etc., so their recycling value is high
Points usable like cash for bringing in clear PET bottles: 100 points for a small one, 500 for a big one
Exchange for standard garbage bags or Emart gift certificates instead of points
A virtual-experience education center on separate disposal for teenagers
A song about the importance and method of separate disposal for children, posted on the city hall website and YouTube

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading and listening): reducing food waste
explanations.body: The following sentences describe what can be done to reduce food waste; the book asks you to read them and check whether each applies to a restaurant or a customer (one is done for you: 제공하는 음식의 양을 줄일 것 for the restaurant). The sentences are the book’s; the classification is mine; the English is mine.

rows: 음식 재료를 필요한 만큼만 구입할 것.
Buy only as many food ingredients as needed.
Order only as much food as you will eat.
Reduce the amount of food served.
음식을 남기지 말고 다 먹을 것.
Don’t leave food; eat it all.
Remove the moisture from food waste.
남은 음식은 싸서 집에 가지고 갈 것.
Wrap leftover food and take it home.
Reduce the kinds of side dishes.

explanations.title: Activity 3 b: the Daejeon restaurant report
explanations.body: The book asks you to listen to a report about a restaurant in Daejeon and (1) write three points about the event the restaurant holds and (2) say what the restaurant owner is considering to reduce food waste further. The book glosses 덜어 먹다: to dish up one’s own portion (and eat); ~대 (臺): a stand. This is an audio activity and is left out.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading): a reader’s opinion
explanations.body: The following article is a reader’s opinion published on a newspaper website (the book glosses 용기: a container; 너구리: a raccoon dog; 낭비: waste). The article is the book’s; the English is mine.

examples.text: 우리 아파트에서 쓰레기를 버릴 때 가끔 재활용 쓰레기통 속을 보게 된다.
examples.translation: uri apateueseo sseuregireul beoril ttae gakkeum jaehwaryong sseuregitong sogeul boge doenda. — When throwing out trash at our apartment, I sometimes get to look inside the recycling bin.

examples.text: 예전보다 플라스틱 수거함에 쓰레기가 훨씬 많아졌다.
examples.translation: yejeonboda peullaseutik sugeohame sseuregiga hwolssin manajeotda. — There is much more trash in the plastic collection box than before.

examples.text: 배달음식 주문이 많아지면서 배달음식을 담았던 용기들도 함께 늘어났기 때문이다.
examples.translation: baedareumsik jumuni manajimyeonseo baedareumsigeul damatdeon yonggideuldo hamkke neureonatgi ttaemunida. — This is because as delivery food orders have increased, the containers that held delivery food have also increased.

examples.text: 그런데 용기의 내용물을 비우지 않은 채로 배출하는 사람들이 꽤 많다.
examples.translation: geureonde yonggiui naeyongmureul biuji aneun chaero baechulhaneun saramdeuri kkwae manta. — But quite a lot of people dispose of the containers without emptying the contents.

examples.text: 음식 때문에 밤에는 너구리나 길고양이들이 오기도 하고 여름에는 음식물이 금방 썩어서 냄새가 많이 난다고 들었다.
examples.translation: eumsik ttaemune bameneun neogurina gilgoyangideuri ogido hago yeoreumeneun eumsingmuri geumbang sseogeoseo naemsaega mani nandago deureotda. — I heard that because of the food, raccoon dogs or stray cats come at night, and that in summer the food rots quickly and smells a lot.

examples.text: 재활용 쓰레기 회사의 직원들은 빠른 시간 내에 재활용 쓰레기를 분리해 내야 한다.
examples.translation: jaehwaryong sseuregi hoesaui jigwondeureun ppareun sigan naee jaehwaryong sseuregireul bullihae naeya handa. — The employees of recycling companies have to separate recyclables within a short time.

examples.text: 그렇기 때문에 음식물이 들어 있는 플라스틱은 일반 쓰레기로 처리할 수밖에 없다.

examples.text: 용기를 씻을 시간이 없기 때문이다.

examples.text: 우리가 내용물을 깨끗이 비우고 씻어서 버리면 재활용될 수 있는 것을, 음식물 때문에 재활용이 안 되니까 얼마나 낭비인가?
examples.translation: uriga naeyongmureul kkaekkeusi biugo ssiseoseo beorimyeon jaehwaryongdoel su inneun geoseul, eumsingmul ttaemune jaehwaryongi an doenikka eolmana nangbiinga? — What a waste it is that something that could be recycled if we empty and wash the contents clean is not recycled because of the food!

examples.text: 배달음식 용기를 깨끗이 씻는 데 시간이 그렇게 오래 걸리지 않는다.

examples.text: 피자가 배달된 상자는 기름이나 음식이 묻은 곳을 잘 닦은 후 재활용 종이 수거함에 버린다.
examples.translation: pijaga baedaldoen sangjaneun gireumina eumsigi mudeun goseul jal dakkeun hu jaehwaryong jongi sugeohame beorinda. — For a box in which a pizza was delivered, wipe well the places with oil or food and then throw it in the recycling paper collection box.

examples.text: 우리가 신경을 조금만 더 쓰면 재활용이 안 되는 일반 쓰레기를 줄일 수 있다.
examples.translation: uriga singyeongeul jogeumman deo sseumyeon jaehwaryongi an doeneun ilban sseuregireul juril su itda. — If we pay just a little more attention, we can reduce the general trash that cannot be recycled.

examples.text: 조금 더 환경문제에 관심을 갖자.

explanations.title: The table filled in (mine)
explanations.body: The book’s table has the columns the problem at the author’s apartment building, limitations of recycling companies and the author’s suggestions. My answers:

rows: The problem at the author’s apartment building
Much more trash in the plastic collection box; many people dispose of delivery food containers without emptying them, which attracts raccoon dogs and stray cats at night and smells in summer
Employees must separate recyclables in a short time, so plastic with food in it has to be treated as general trash because there is no time to wash it

Empty and wash containers before disposal; wipe off oil and food from pizza boxes before putting them in the paper collection box; pay a little more attention and take more interest in environmental problems

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (SMART Board), Activity 2 (listening to a radio program about the recycling efforts of Yongin and Jinhae, and the table of what materials are recycled, what is done with them and how the money is used) and Activity 5 (pairs think of ways a local restaurant can reduce food waste, choose three ideas, post and present them) are audio and group activities.
