explanations.title: Topic B: Global warming (지구 온난화)
explanations.body: The following TV news report is about global warming. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the numbers are spelled out in Hangul; the reporter’s name is left out; the printed text has a blank after 지구, which I read as 지구 전역에.)

examples.text: 오늘은 유엔이 지정한 환경의 날입니다.
examples.translation: oneureun yueni jijeonghan hwangyeongui narimnida. — Today is the Environment Day designated by the United Nations.

examples.text: 기자의 보도입니다.
examples.translation: gijaui bodoimnida. — This is the reporter’s report.

examples.text: 남극과 북극의 빙하가 녹아 해수면이 올라가고 있습니다.
examples.translation: namgeukgwa bukgeugui binghaga noga haesumyeoni ollagago itseumnida. — The glaciers of the Antarctic and the Arctic are melting and the sea level is rising.

examples.text: 해수면이 앞으로 백 년간 오십 센티미터에서 일 미터 정도 높아질 것으로 예측되고 있습니다.
examples.translation: haesumyeoni apeuro baek nyeongan osip sentimiteoeseo il miteo jeongdo nopajil geoseuro yecheukdoego itseumnida. — The sea level is predicted to become about 50 cm to 1 m higher over the next 100 years.

examples.text: 이렇게 되면 생태계가 파괴되고 농작물의 수확량이 감소하는 등 지구 전역에 피해가 예상됩니다.
examples.translation: ireoke doemyeon saengtaegyega pagoedoego nongjangmurui suhwangnyangi gamsohaneun deung jigu jeonyeoge pihaega yesangdoemnida. — If this happens, damage is expected across the whole Earth, such as the destruction of ecosystems and a decrease in crop yields.

examples.text: 빙하가 녹는 가장 큰 이유는 지구의 평균기온이 올라가는 지구 온난화 현상 때문입니다.
examples.translation: binghaga nongneun gajang keun iyuneun jiguui pyeonggyungioni ollaganeun jigu onnanhwa hyeonsang ttaemunimnida. — The biggest reason the glaciers are melting is the phenomenon of global warming, in which the Earth’s average temperature rises.

examples.text: 지구 온도는 지난 백 년간 영 점 오 도에서 일 도 정도 상승한 것으로 관측되고 있습니다.
examples.translation: jigu ondoneun jinan baek nyeongan yeong jeom o doeseo il do jeongdo sangseunghan geoseuro gwancheukdoego itseumnida. — The Earth’s temperature has been observed to have risen by about 0.5 to 1 degree over the last 100 years.

explanations.title: Core words and phrases of Topic B
explanations.body: The meanings are the book’s (from the Core Vocabulary of the chapter). The book also lists ~ 등 and ~배.

rows: (減少) decrease; to decrease / to be decreased (~하다/되다)
(觀測) observation; to observe / to be observed (~하다/되다)
(南極) the South Pole; the Antarctic; “south extreme”

explanations.title: 한국어에는: ~ 등
explanations.body: In English, phrases like and so on, and so forth, or etc. indicate that a list continues in a similar manner. Likewise, in Korean, we use ~ 등 to indicate that a list of nouns continues in a similar manner. For instance, 그 한국식품점에는 사과, 배 등 한국과일이 많습니다 (There are many Korean fruits in the Korean grocery store: apples, pears, etc.). However, when indicating a list of verbs, 등 is added to attributive verbal phrases; for example, 지난 주말에 영화도 보고 쇼핑하는 등 여러 가지 일을 했다 (Last weekend, I did various things, like watching a movie, shopping, etc.).

explanations.title: Abbreviated verbs
explanations.body: Bulletin boards, newspaper headlines, titles and subtitles, warnings, notes, memos in a planner, etc., rarely use complete sentences. When they contain sentences, the verbs are often abbreviated. The book shows two texts, Text A (a newspaper ad) and Text B (an online college bulletin board), to see how the verbs are written (the numbers are spelled out; the English is mine).

explanations.title: Two endings
explanations.body: Note that the verbs are abbreviated into either of the following two endings: –(으)ㅁ (우대함, 있음, 바람, 제공함 in Text A) and –(으)ㄹ 것 (들을 것, 확인할 것, 갈 것 in Text B).

explanations.title: –(으)ㅁ
explanations.body: –(으)ㅁ is used to abbreviate a verb when a sentence contains factual information (e.g., a statement, a report, or an observation). Note that –(으)ㅁ can be omitted when the verb is made up of a noun and 하다 (as in 경력자 우대(함), 생활 지원비와 숙소 제공(함)). The book’s examples (the numbers are spelled out; the English is the book’s):

explanations.title: –(으)ㄹ 것
explanations.body: –(으)ㄹ 것 is used to abbreviate a verb when a sentence contains a task (e.g., a request, a command, or an order). Note that in the sentences, non-key words (like noun markers or an honorific infix) can be omitted.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading and writing): abbreviate the verbs

lessons.title: 502. Ch 40 · Grammar B: expressions frequently used in news reports, an attributive form + 것으로
lessons.subtitle: -(으)ㄴ 것으로 나타났다 · -(으)ㄹ 것으로 예측했다 · 밝혀졌다 · 알려졌다 · 조사됐다 · 보도됐다 · 전망했다 · 걸로

explanations.title: Recall –다고 하다
explanations.body: Recall that the grammar feature –다고 하다, which you learned about in Chapter 23, is used when reporting or quoting a statement indirectly, as in the following (the English is the book’s). However, this grammar feature is mainly for conversational language, rather than formal news reports or research papers in which reporting and quoting has to be specific.

examples.text: 김 일병이 지금 비가 온다고 해요.
examples.translation: gim ilbyeongi jigeum biga ondago haeyo. — PFC Kim says that it is raining now.

examples.text: 팀장님이 김 선생님이 아프시다고 합니다.
examples.translation: timjangnimi gim seonsaengnimi apeusidago hamnida. — The team leader says that Ms. Kim is ill.

explanations.title: News report verbs
explanations.body: In news reports, for example, the following verbs are commonly used: 나타나다 (to be revealed; to be shown); 보다/보이다, 조사하다/조사되다, 알려지다, 밝히다/밝혀지다 (to clarify; to be clarified); 전망하다 (to forecast; to expect), etc. When these verbs are used for reporting, the reported information frequently ends in an attributive form + 것으로. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 작년에 기름 값이 십육 퍼센트 오른 것으로 나타났습니다.
examples.translation: jangnyeone gireum gapsi simnyuk peosenteu oreun geoseuro natanatseumnida. — It was revealed / It was shown that oil prices increased by 16% last year.

explanations.title: Note
explanations.body: Note that the attributive form 오른 + 것으로 is immediately followed by 나타나다. In colloquial language, 것으로 is often contracted to 걸로/거로. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 작년에 기름 값이 십육 퍼센트 오른 걸로 나타났어요.
examples.translation: jangnyeone gireum gapsi simnyuk peosenteu oreun geollo natanasseoyo. — It was revealed / It was shown that oil prices increased by 16% last year. (colloquial 걸로)

explanations.title: Expressions frequently used in news reports
explanations.body: Attributive form of a verb + 것으로 + 나타나다/보이다/조사되다/알려지다, etc. More examples (the numbers are spelled out; the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 한 배우가 삼 년간 협박을 당한 것으로 밝혀졌다.
examples.translation: han baeuga sam nyeongan hyeopbageul danghan geoseuro balkyeojeotda. — It was revealed that an actor had been blackmailed for 3 years.

examples.text: 전문가들은 한반도의 기온이 더 올라갈 것으로 예측했다.
examples.translation: jeonmungadeureun hanbandoui gioni deo ollagal geoseuro yecheukaetda. — Experts predicted that the temperatures on the Korean Peninsula would go up.

examples.text: 삼성은 새 휴대폰이 많이 팔릴 것으로 전망했다.
examples.translation: samseongeun sae hyudaeponi mani pallil geoseuro jeonmanghaetda. — Samsung expected that new cell phones would sell well / would be popular.

examples.text: 중학생들의 이십 퍼센트가 담배를 피우는 것으로 조사됐다.
examples.translation: junghaksaengdeurui isip peosenteuga dambaereul piuneun geoseuro josadwaetda. — The survey showed that 20% of middle school students were smokers.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Writing): reporter’s statements
explanations.body: Imagine you are a reporter for a radio news show. Rewrite each statement as if you were going to use it in your news report. Choose an appropriate verb from the box 나타나다, 밝혀지다, 보이다, 보도하다/보도되다, 알려지다, 예보하다/예보되다, 예상하다/예상되다, 예측하다/예측되다, 전망되다, 확인되다 (the verbs may be used more than once). The book’s model is 오만 명의 이재민이 발생했습니다 → 오만 명의 이재민이 발생한 것으로 나타났습니다/밝혀졌습니다/보도됐습니다/알려졌습니다. The statements are the book’s (the numbers are spelled out); the rewrites and the English are mine.

미혼 여성의 삼십 퍼센트가 결혼할 생각이 없는 것으로 나타났습니다.

이 씨는 과속운전을 하지 않은 것으로 밝혀졌습니다.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking and writing): a piece of news about DLI students
explanations.body: Using at least four sentences, write a piece of recent news about DLI students (e.g., what they did last week and what they seem to be going to do this week) and use an attributive form + 것으로 + verb at least twice; present it to your class as if you were a reporter. The book’s model (DLI is read 디엘아이; the number is spelled out; the English is mine):

examples.text: 디엘아이 학생들은 외식을 얼마나 자주 할까요?
examples.translation: dierai haksaengdeureun oesigeul eolmana jaju halkkayo? — How often do DLI students eat out?

examples.text: 지난주에 기숙사에 사는 학생 중 이십 퍼센트가 외식을 한 것으로 나타났습니다.
examples.translation: jinanjue gisuksae saneun haksaeng jung isip peosenteuga oesigeul han geoseuro natanatseumnida. — Last week 20% of the students living in the dormitory were found to have eaten out.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 4 (listening to three news reports about natural hazards and transcribing the segments with an attributive form + 것으로 + verb) is an audio activity.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading): a news report about Earth Day
explanations.body: The following news report is about Earth Day (Kyunghyang). The book glosses 국회의사당: Houses of Parliament; 평균: average; 두께: thickness. The report is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (UN is read 유엔); the English is mine.

examples.text: 이십이 일 로이터 통신에 따르면 유럽의 기후변화 단체들이 지구의 날에 영국 국회의사당 앞에 모여 지구 온난화 문제에 대한 대책을 세워 달라고 요구했다.
examples.translation: isibi il roiteo tongsine ttareumyeon yureobui gihubyeonhwa danchedeuri jiguui nare yeongguk gukoeuisadang ape moyeo jigu onnanhwa munjee daehan daechaegeul sewo dallago yoguhaetda. — According to Reuters on the 22nd, European climate change groups gathered in front of the Houses of Parliament in the UK on Earth Day and demanded that measures be taken on the problem of global warming.

examples.text: 또한 전 세계 봉사자들은 곳곳에서 나무를 심고 쓰레기 청소를 하면서 올해 지구의 날을 기념했다.
examples.translation: ttohan jeon segye bongsajadeureun gotgoseseo namureul simgo sseuregi cheongsoreul hamyeonseo olhae jiguui nareul ginyeomhaetda. — Also, volunteers around the world commemorated this year’s Earth Day by planting trees and cleaning up trash in many places.

examples.text: 서울 광화문 광장에서도 지구의 날 기념행사가 열렸다.
examples.translation: seoul gwanghwamun gwangjangeseodo jiguui nal ginyeomhaengsaga yeollyeotda. — A commemorative event for Earth Day was held at Gwanghwamun Square in Seoul too.

examples.text: 쓰레기를 위한 지구는 없다를 주제로 여러 체험행사와 콘서트가 열렸다.
examples.translation: sseuregireul wihan jiguneun eopdareul jujero yeoreo cheheomhaengsawa konseoteuga yeollyeotda. — With the theme “There is no Earth for trash”, various experience events and a concert were held.

examples.text: 지구의 날은 천구백육십구 년 환경운동가 존 맥코넬이 처음 제안해 시작됐다.
examples.translation: jiguui nareun cheongubaegyuksipgu nyeon hwangyeongundongga jon maekkoneri cheoeum jeanhae sijakdwaetda. — Earth Day started when the environmental activist John McConnell first proposed it in 1969.

examples.text: 천구백칠십 년 사 월 이십이 일 미국에서 지구의 날 행사가 처음 열렸고 지금까지 이어지고 있다.
examples.translation: cheongubaekchilsip nyeon sa wol isibi il migugeseo jiguui nal haengsaga cheoeum yeollyeotgo jigeumkkaji ieojigo itda. — The first Earth Day event was held in the United States on April 22, 1970 and has continued to this day.

examples.text: 지구는 점점 더워지고 있다.
examples.translation: jiguneun jeomjeom deowojigo itda. — The Earth is getting hotter and hotter.

examples.text: 유엔 보고서에 따르면 지난해 지구 평균기온은 천팔백오십 년에서 천구백 년 평균보다 섭씨 일 점 일오 도 가량 높아졌다.
examples.translation: yuen bogoseoe ttareumyeon jinanhae jigu pyeonggyungioneun cheonpalbaegosip nyeoneseo cheongubaek nyeon pyeonggyunboda seopssi il jeom iro do garyang nopajeotda. — According to a UN report, last year’s Earth average temperature rose about 1.15 degrees Celsius above the 1850–1900 average.

examples.text: 빙하 두께는 오십 년간 삼십 미터 가량 줄어들었고, 해수면 상승 속도는 최근 십 년 사이 두 배 빨라진 것으로 나타났다.
examples.translation: bingha dukkeneun osip nyeongan samsip miteo garyang jureodeureotgo, haesumyeon sangseung sokdoneun choegeun sip nyeon sai du bae ppallajin geoseuro natanatda. — Glacier thickness has decreased by about 30 m over 50 years, and the speed of sea level rise was found to have doubled in the last ten years.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: The book asks (1) what the origin of this special day is, (2) how the day was celebrated in Europe, Seoul and around the world, and (3) what findings the UN report presents. My answers:

rows: It was first proposed by the environmental activist John McConnell, and the first event was held in the United States on April 22, 1970
Climate change groups gathered in front of the UK Houses of Parliament and demanded measures on global warming
A commemorative event at Gwanghwamun Square with experience events and a concert on the theme “There is no Earth for trash”
Volunteers planted trees and cleaned up trash in many places
Last year’s average Earth temperature was about 1.15 °C above the 1850–1900 average; glacier thickness decreased by about 30 m in 50 years; the speed of sea level rise doubled in the last ten years

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): a Q and A about the Paris Agreement
explanations.body: The following article is from a Q and A section of a portal site (the question was about homework on the Paris Agreement). The book glosses 목표를 제시하다: to present a goal; 감축: reduction; 탄소중립: carbon neutrality. The answer text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (the English “Paris Agreement” in brackets is dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 파리협정 또는 파리기후변화협정은 이천십육 년에 체결됐습니다.
examples.translation: parihyeopjeong ttoneun parigihubyeonhwahyeopjeongeun icheonsibyuk nyeone chegyeoldwaetseumnida. — The Paris Agreement, or the Paris Climate Change Agreement, was concluded in 2016.

examples.text: 그 목적은 국제사회가 같이 협력해서 지구온난화의 원인인 온실가스를 줄이자는 것입니다.
examples.translation: geu mokjeogeun gukjesahoega gachi hyeomnyeokaeseo jiguonnanhwaui woninin onsilgaseureul jurijaneun geosimnida. — Its purpose is for the international community to cooperate and reduce greenhouse gases, the cause of global warming.

examples.text: 온실가스를 줄여서 지구의 평균 온도 상승을 일 점 오 도로 제한하자는 것이지요.
examples.translation: onsilgaseureul juryeoseo jiguui pyeonggyun ondo sangseungeul il jeom o doro jehanhajaneun geosijiyo. — It is to reduce greenhouse gases and limit the rise in the Earth’s average temperature to 1.5 degrees.

examples.text: 파리협정에 가입한 국가들은 앞으로 온실가스 배출량을 얼마나 줄일 것인지 그 목표를 제시해야 합니다.
examples.translation: parihyeopjeonge gaipan gukgadeureun apeuro onsilgaseu baechullyangeul eolmana juril geosinji geu mokpyoreul jesihaeya hamnida. — Countries that joined the Paris Agreement must present their goals for how much they will reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the future.

examples.text: 예를 들면 이천삼십 년까지 프랑스는 오십오 퍼센트, 브라질은 사십삼 퍼센트, 한국은 이천십칠 년 대비 이십사 점 사 퍼센트를 감축하겠다는 목표를 제시했습니다.
examples.translation: yereul deulmyeon icheonsamsip nyeonkkaji peurangseuneun osibo peosenteu, beurajireun sasipsam peosenteu, hangugeun icheonsipchil nyeon daebi isipsa jeom sa peosenteureul gamchukagetdaneun mokpyoreul jesihaetseumnida. — For example, by 2030 France presented a goal of reducing 55 percent, Brazil 43 percent, and Korea 24.4 percent compared with 2017.

examples.text: 또한, 미국은 이천오십 년까지, 중국은 이천육십 년까지 탄소중립을 하겠다는 목표를 제시했습니다.
examples.translation: ttohan, migugeun icheonosip nyeonkkaji, junggugeun icheonyuksip nyeonkkaji tansojungnibeul hagetdaneun mokpyoreul jesihaetseumnida. — Also, the United States presented a goal of carbon neutrality by 2050 and China by 2060.

examples.text: 그런데 문제는 협정에 가입한 나라들이 국가별 목표를 달성해도 이천삼십 년 온실가스 배출량은 지금보다 일 퍼센트 낮아질 뿐이라고 합니다.
examples.translation: geureonde munjeneun hyeopjeonge gaipan naradeuri gukgabyeol mokpyoreul dalseonghaedo icheonsamsip nyeon onsilgaseu baechullyangeun jigeumboda il peosenteu najajil ppunirago hamnida. — But the problem is that even if the countries that joined the agreement achieve their national goals, they say the 2030 greenhouse gas emissions will be only 1 percent lower than now.

examples.text: 이렇게 되면 이천 년대 말까지 지구의 기온은 이 점 일 도에서 삼 도 상승하게 됩니다.
examples.translation: ireoke doemyeon icheon nyeondae malkkaji jiguui gioneun i jeom il doeseo sam do sangseunghage doemnida. — If this happens, the Earth’s temperature will rise 2.1 to 3 degrees by the end of the 2000s.

examples.text: 이 정도의 상승은 지구의 생태계를 파괴할 만큼 큰 상승입니다.
examples.translation: i jeongdoui sangseungeun jiguui saengtaegyereul pagoehal mankeum keun sangseungimnida. — A rise of this degree is a rise large enough to destroy the Earth’s ecosystem.

explanations.title: The table filled in (mine)
explanations.body: The book’s table has the columns the purpose and the collective goal of the Paris Agreement, each country’s goal (Brazil, Korea, U.S.) and concerns. My answers:

rows: The international community cooperates to reduce greenhouse gases, the cause of global warming, and limit the rise in the Earth’s average temperature to 1.5 degrees
Reduce by 24.4 percent by 2030 compared with 2017

Even if all countries meet their goals, 2030 emissions would be only 1 percent lower than now, and the temperature would rise 2.1 to 3 degrees by the end of the 2000s, enough to destroy the Earth’s ecosystem

explanations.title: Topic C: An interview with the mayor of an eco-friendly city (친환경 도시 시장님과의 인터뷰)
explanations.body: The following text is an excerpt from a radio program in which a reporter is interviewing a mayor about his city’s efforts to protect the environment. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the month and the amount are spelled out in Hangul.)

examples.text: 기자: 시장님, 이번에 울산시가 올해의 친환경 도시로 선정된 것을 축하드립니다.
examples.translation: gija: sijangnim, ibeone ulsansiga olhaeui chinhwangyeong dosiro seonjeongdoen geoseul chukadeurimnida. — Mayor, congratulations on Ulsan City being selected as this year’s environment-friendly city.

examples.text: 시장: 네, 감사합니다.
examples.translation: sijang: ne, gamsahamnida. — Yes, thank you.

examples.text: 기자: 먼저 환경 보호를 위해 울산시는 어떤 노력을 하고 있습니까?
examples.translation: gija: meonjeo hwangyeong bohoreul wihae ulsansineun eotteon noryeogeul hago itseumnikka? — First, what efforts is Ulsan City making for environmental protection?

examples.text: 시장: 네, 저희 시는 매주 수요일을 차 없는 날로 지정해서 시민들이 대중교통을 이용하도록 하고 있습니다. 또 자전거 이용도 적극적으로 권장하고 있습니다.
examples.translation: sijang: ne, jeohui sineun maeju suyoireul cha eomneun nallo jijeonghaeseo simindeuri daejunggyotongeul iyonghadorok hago itseumnida. tto jajeongeo iyongdo jeokgeukjeogeuro gwonjanghago itseumnida. — Yes, our city designates every Wednesday as a car-free day so that citizens use public transportation. We are also actively encouraging the use of bicycles.

examples.text: 기자: 아, 그렇군요. 그리고 칠 월부터는 우리가 전기차를 살 때 보조금을 받을 수 있잖아요? 울산시에선 얼마나 보조해 주게 되나요?
examples.translation: gija: a, geureokunyo. geurigo chil wolbuteoneun uriga jeongichareul sal ttae bojogeumeul badeul su itjanayo? ulsansieseon eolmana bojohae juge doenayo? — Oh, I see. And from July we can receive a subsidy when we buy an electric car, right? How much will Ulsan City subsidize?

examples.text: 시장: 저희 시에선 최대 사백만 원까지 지원해 드릴 예정인데요, 사실 뉴스가 나가자 전기차 구입 문의가 평소보다 많이 늘었다고 합니다. 앞으로 전기차가 많아질 거니까 충전소 설치도 더 늘려갈 계획입니다.
examples.translation: sijang: jeohui sieseon choedae sabaengman wonkkaji jiwonhae deuril yejeongindeyo, sasil nyuseuga nagaja jeongicha guip munuiga pyeongsoboda mani neureotdago hamnida. apeuro jeongichaga manajil geonikka chungjeonso seolchido deo neullyeogal gyehoegimnida. — Our city plans to support up to 4 million won, and in fact they say that as soon as the news went out, inquiries about buying electric cars increased a lot more than usual. Since there will be more electric cars in the future, we also plan to increase the installation of charging stations.

examples.text: 기자: 아, 네. 앞으로 울산시는 자동차의 이산화탄소 배출량이 줄어서 온실가스도 많이 줄어들 것 같네요. 마지막으로 시장님, 환경보존을 위해 저희들이 일상생활에서 무엇을 실천하면 좋을까요?
examples.translation: gija: a, ne. apeuro ulsansineun jadongchaui isanhwatanso baechullyangi jureoseo onsilgaseudo mani jureodeul geot ganneyo. majimageuro sijangnim, hwangyeongbojoneul wihae jeohuideuri ilsangsaenghwareseo mueoseul silcheonhamyeon joeulkkayo? — Oh, yes. In the future, it seems Ulsan’s cars’ carbon dioxide emissions will decrease and greenhouse gases will also decrease a lot. Lastly, Mayor, what would be good for us to put into practice in daily life for environmental preservation?

examples.text: 시장: 일회용품의 지나친 사용을 자제하시고 친환경 제품을 사용하신다면 큰 도움이 될 겁니다.
examples.translation: sijang: ilhoeyongpumui jinachin sayongeul jajehasigo chinhwangyeong jepumeul sayonghasindamyeon keun doumi doel geomnida. — If you refrain from excessive use of disposable goods and use environment-friendly products, it will be a great help.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): an email on resource and energy conservation
explanations.body: The following e-mail is about resource and energy conservation and is from the general affairs department of a company to its employees. The book asks you to read it and fill in the table with the five suggestions and the specific directions in English. The e-mail is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (the five suggestions are written as the lines starting with the topic sentence); the English is mine.

examples.text: 전 사원 자원 보존과 에너지 절약을 실천합시다.
examples.translation: jeon sawon jawon bojongwa eneoji jeoryageul silcheonhapsida. — To all employees: Let’s put resource conservation and energy saving into practice.

examples.text: 사원 여러분, 안녕하십니까?
examples.translation: sawon yeoreobun, annyeonghasimnikka? — Employees, hello.

examples.text: 저희 총무부에서는 오늘부터 팔 월 말까지 여름기간 동안 에너지 절약 및 자원 보존 캠페인을 벌입니다.
examples.translation: jeohui chongmubueseoneun oneulbuteo pal wol malkkaji yeoreumgigan dongan eneoji jeoryak mit jawon bojon kaempeineul beorimnida. — Our general affairs department will run an energy saving and resource conservation campaign during the summer period from today until the end of August.

examples.text: 사원 여러분께서 적극적으로 참여하셔서 이산화탄소 배출을 다같이 줄여 봅시다.
examples.translation: sawon yeoreobunkkeseo jeokgeukjeogeuro chamyeohasyeoseo isanhwatanso baechureul dagachi juryeo bopsida. — Let’s all reduce carbon dioxide emissions together with your active participation.

examples.text: 전기를 아낍시다. 점심시간과 퇴근할 때 컴퓨터와 프린터를 꺼 주세요. 또, 사원 라운지의 커피메이커도 다 사용한 후에는 플러그를 빼 주세요.
examples.translation: jeongireul akkipsida. jeomsimsigangwa toegeunhal ttae keompyuteowa peurinteoreul kkeo juseyo. tto, sawon raunjiui keopimeikeodo da sayonghan hueneun peulleogeureul ppae juseyo. — Let’s save electricity. Please turn off computers and printers at lunchtime and when leaving work. Also, please unplug the coffee maker in the employee lounge after you have finished using it.

examples.text: 기름을 아낍시다. 근처에 사는 동료를 찾아서 카풀 할 수 있는지 알아보세요. 또, 가능한 한 자주 대중교통을 이용해 주세요.
examples.translation: gireumeul akkipsida. geuncheoe saneun dongnyoreul chajaseo kapul hal su inneunji araboseyo. tto, ganeunghan han jaju daejunggyotongeul iyonghae juseyo. — Let’s save fuel. Find a coworker who lives nearby and see if you can carpool. Also, please use public transportation as often as possible.

examples.text: 재활용을 합시다. 종이컵이나 음료수 병, 캔은 잘 헹군 후에 재활용 쓰레기통에 넣어 주세요. 또, 코팅이 되어 있지 않은 종이나 상자도 종이 수거함에 넣어 주세요.
examples.translation: jaehwaryongeul hapsida. jongikeobina eumnyosu byeong, kaeneun jal henggun hue jaehwaryong sseuregitonge neoeo juseyo. tto, kotingi doeeo itji aneun jongina sangjado jongi sugeohame neoeo juseyo. — Let’s recycle. Please rinse paper cups, beverage bottles and cans well and put them in the recycling bin. Also, please put paper or boxes that are not coated in the paper collection box.

examples.text: 종이를 아낍시다. 복사할 때는 중요한 서류가 아니면 이면지를 활용하세요. 또, 가능하면 전자문서를 사용하도록 하세요.
examples.translation: jongireul akkipsida. boksahal ttaeneun jungyohan seoryuga animyeon imyeonjireul hwaryonghaseyo. tto, ganeunghamyeon jeonjamunseoreul sayonghadorok haseyo. — Let’s save paper. When copying, use scratch paper unless it is an important document. Also, try to use electronic documents if possible.

examples.text: 지나친 냉방을 자제합시다. 사무실 온도를 여름철 실내 적정온도인 이십육 도에서 이십팔 도로 맞추세요.
examples.translation: jinachin naengbangeul jajehapsida. samusil ondoreul yeoreumcheol sillae jeokjeongondoin isimnyuk doeseo isippal doro matchuseyo. — Let’s refrain from excessive air conditioning. Set the office temperature to 26 to 28 degrees, the optimal indoor temperature in summer.

explanations.title: The table filled in (mine)
explanations.body: The book glosses 전자문서: electronic document; 적정: optimal. My answers:

rows: Turn off computers and printers at lunchtime and when leaving work; unplug the lounge coffee maker after use
Find a nearby coworker to carpool with; use public transportation as often as possible
Rinse paper cups, bottles and cans and put them in the recycling bin; put uncoated paper and boxes in the paper collection box
Use scratch paper for copies unless the document is important; use electronic documents when possible
Set the office temperature to 26–28 degrees, the optimal summer indoor temperature

lessons.title: 505. Ch 40 · Grammar C: the conjunctive ending –자 (as soon as, when)
lessons.subtitle: -자 · 집을 나서자 · 바람이 불자 · 폭우가 쏟아지자 · 장마가 그치자 · -자마자

explanations.title: Two implications
explanations.body:
The conjunctive ending –자 can be used to indicate either of the following implications:

1. Without-interval-of-time implication. In this case, the conjunctive ending implies that two events or actions occurred without an interval of time. Thus –자 can be translated as as soon as, immediately after, the moment that, or upon, as in 집을 나서자 비가 그쳤다 (As soon as I walked out of the house, it stopped raining). The sentence implies that it stopped raining as soon as (or immediately after) the speaker walked out of the house. Thus, –자 in this sentence can be replaced with –자마자, which you learned about in Chapter 20.

2. Cause-and-Effect implication. In this case, the conjunctive ending implies that two events or actions occurred in sequence and that the speaker suspects the first event/action triggered the second event/action. –자 can be translated as as or when, as in 바람이 불자 전기가 나갔다 (As/When the wind blew, the electricity went out). In this sentence, the speaker suspects that wind blowing (the first event) triggered the blackout (the second event).

examples.text: 집을 나서자 비가 그쳤다.
examples.translation: jibeul naseoja biga geucheotda. — As soon as I walked out of the house, it stopped raining.

examples.text: 바람이 불자 전기가 나갔다.
examples.translation: barami bulja jeongiga nagatda. — As / When the wind blew, the electricity went out.

explanations.title: Both implications
explanations.body: Depending on the context, many of the sentences that use the conjunctive ending –자 can convey either of the implications. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 엄마를 보자 아기가 웃었다.
examples.translation: eommareul boja agiga useotda. — As soon as he saw his mom, the baby smiled. (without-interval-of-time implication) or When he saw his mom, the baby smiled. (cause-and-effect implication)

explanations.title: Only for an action that already took place
explanations.body:
Keep in mind that this conjunctive ending is used solely for an action or event that already took place or started taking place. Thus the following sentences in which an action/event has not yet taken place are ungrammatical (the asterisk * indicates that the marked phrase/sentence is ungrammatical): 엄마를 보자 아기가 *웃겠어요. 집을 나서자 비가 *그치겠어요. 장마가 그치자 *바비큐하자! 선생님이 들어오자 *일어서세요.

Note that the conjunctive ending –자 occurs more often in written language, including news reports, than in colloquial language. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 폭우가 쏟아지자 온 도시가 물에 잠겼습니다.
examples.translation: poguga ssodajija on dosiga mure jamgyeotseumnida. — As heavy rain poured down, the whole town was submerged in water.

examples.text: 장마가 그치자 무더위가 시작되었다.
examples.translation: jangmaga geuchija mudeowiga sijakdoeeotda. — As soon as the rainy season stopped, a sweltering heat began.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): conjugate with –자 and match
explanations.body: For each clause in List A, conjugate the verb with –자, then match it with a clause in List B that can be logically connected (the book gives the first, 불자, as the example). The clauses are the book’s with the number spelled out; my matches are given as complete sentences; the English is mine.

examples.text: 초속 사십 미터의 강풍이 불자 도로 표지판들이 날아갔다.
examples.translation: chosok sasip miteoui gangpungi bulja doro pyojipandeuri naragatda. — As a strong wind of 40 m per second blew, the road signs flew away.

examples.text: 삼 일 동안 계속해서 폭설이 내리자 시내 교통이 마비되었다.
examples.translation: sam il dongan gyesokaeseo pokseori naerija sinae gyotongi mabidoeeotda. — As heavy snow kept falling for three days, traffic in the city was paralyzed.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading): –자 in news excerpts
explanations.body: The following excerpts are from newspaper articles about natural disasters or extreme weather. The book asks you to circle all the verbs with –자, identify the two actions or events in each excerpt and fill in a table in English. The excerpts are the book’s with the numbers spelled out; the table and the English are mine.

rows: An earthquake occurred in Qingdao, China on the night of the 15th
The residents of surrounding areas quickly evacuated out of the buildings
From the morning of the 16th rain of up to 90 mm per hour fell
The Busan weather office issued a heavy rain advisory for the area
A wildfire broke out on Jirisan
Fire engines and 250 firefighters were dispatched and put out the fire
The weather agency issued a heavy rain advisory for Gangwon-do
Residents of this area are preparing measures against floods

examples.text: 십오 일 밤 중국 청도에서 지진이 일어나자 주변지역 주민들은 빨리 건물 밖으로 대피했다.

lessons.title: 506. Ch 40 · Grammar D: the conjunctive ending (만약) … –다면 for a hypothetical condition
lessons.subtitle: -다면 · 만약 · -ㄴ/는다면 · -았/었다면 · -(이)라면 · 백만 불이 있다면

explanations.title: Recall –(으)면
explanations.body: Recall the conjunctive ending –(으)면 that we use to express a conditional. This conjunctive ending is normally used to express either a factual conditional relationship or a future (or predictive) conditional relationship. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 주말에 비가 오면 저는 영화를 봐요.
examples.translation: jumare biga omyeon jeoneun yeonghwareul bwayo. — I watch a movie if (or when) it rains on weekends. (factual conditional)

examples.text: 주말에 비가 오면 저는 영화를 볼 거예요.
examples.translation: jumare biga omyeon jeoneun yeonghwareul bol geoyeyo. — I will watch a movie if it rains this weekend. (future/predictive conditional)

explanations.title: What the two examples show
explanations.body: The first sentence expresses a factual conditional relationship. It can be interpreted as “If (or When) something happens, I do this/that.” The second sentence, however, expresses a future (or predictive) conditional relationship and can be interpreted as “If something happens in the future, I will do this/that.” However, this conjunctive ending is rarely used to express a hypothetical conditional relationship or a counterfactual relationship. For this conditional, Koreans often use the conjunctive ending (만약) … 다면. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 만약 백만 불이 있다면 하와이에 이사갈 거예요.
examples.translation: manyak baengman buri itdamyeon hawaie isagal geoyeyo. — If I had a million dollars (now), I would move to Hawaii. (counterfactual)

examples.text: 만약 백만 불이 생긴다면 무엇을 하겠어요?
examples.translation: manyak baengman buri saenggindamyeon mueoseul hagesseoyo? — If you had a million dollars, what would you do? (hypothetical)

explanations.title: 만약 and 다면
explanations.body: 만약, which begins the clause, is optional but its presence clearly tells us that the following clause is a hypothetical or counterfactual conditional. Note that 다 in 다면 is the formal blunt speech style and the above examples are present hypothetical/counterfactual conditionals. However, the verb 이다 turns into 이라면, not 이다면. (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 만약 내가 한국사람이라면 한국말을 늘 쓰겠지요.
examples.translation: manyak naega hanguksaramiramyeon hangungmareul neul sseugetjiyo. — If I were Korean, I would use Korean every day.

explanations.title: The past
explanations.body: To express past hypothetical/counterfactual conditionals, we add the past tense marker to both clauses. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 그때 제가 백만 불이 있었다면 아마 그 집을 샀을 거예요.
examples.translation: geuttae jega baengman buri isseotdamyeon ama geu jibeul sasseul geoyeyo. — If I had had a million dollars, I would have bought that house.

examples.text: 만약 백만 불이 있었다면 무엇을 했겠어요?
examples.translation: manyak baengman buri isseotdamyeon mueoseul haetgesseoyo? — If you had had a million dollars, what would you have done?

explanations.title: Expressing a hypothetical condition
explanations.body: (만약) … 다면. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 아버지가 이번 크리스마스에 오신다면 같이 하와이에 갈 거예요.
examples.translation: abeojiga ibeon keuriseumaseue osindamyeon gachi hawaie gal geoyeyo. — If my father were to visit this Christmas, we would go to Hawaii together.

examples.text: 아버지가 지난 크리스마스에 오셨다면 같이 하와이에 갔을 거예요.
examples.translation: abeojiga jinan keuriseumaseue osyeotdamyeon gachi hawaie gasseul geoyeyo. — If my father had visited last Christmas, we would have gone to Hawaii together.

examples.text: 내가 너라면 공부를 열심히 하겠다.
examples.translation: naega neoramyeon gongbureul yeolsimhi hagetda. — If I were you, I would study hard.

examples.text: 우리 집이 크다면 집에서 생일파티를 했을 거예요.
examples.translation: uri jibi keudamyeon jibeseo saengilpatireul haesseul geoyeyo. — If my house were bigger, I would have thrown a birthday party at home.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Speaking): the model
explanations.body: Partners take a verbal phrase strip, conjugate the verb with 다면 (using (만약) … –ㄴ/는다면 or (만약) … –았/었다면) and the partner completes the sentence with a logically appropriate clause. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 만약 한국에 간다면
examples.translation: ga: manyak hanguge gandamyeon — If I go to Korea,

examples.text: 나: 만약 한국에 간다면 한국말을 많이 할 거예요.
examples.translation: na: manyak hanguge gandamyeon hangungmareul mani hal geoyeyo. — If I go to Korea, I will speak a lot of Korean.

explanations.title: Follow-up 6 (Reading): guidelines for environmental conservation
explanations.body: The following guidelines for environmental conservation are on the website of an environmental protection group. The book asks you to find and underline the conjunctive ending 다면 and translate those sentences into English. The sentences with 다면 below are the book’s (the numbers are spelled out); the English is mine. The guidelines are: 1. Let’s reduce food waste; 2. Let’s use bicycles and public transportation; 3. Let’s make recycling a habit.

examples.text: 만약 우리가 음식물 쓰레기를 이십 퍼센트 더 줄일 수 있다면 온실가스를 사백만 톤가량 줄일 수 있을 겁니다.
examples.translation: manyak uriga eumsingmul sseuregireul isip peosenteu deo juril su itdamyeon onsilgaseureul sabaengman tongaryang juril su isseul geomnida. — If we could reduce food waste by another 20 percent, we could reduce greenhouse gases by about 4 million tons.

examples.text: 서울 시민이 모두 자가용을 타지 않고 자전거를 탄다면 온실가스 배출을 크게 줄일 수 있을 겁니다.
examples.translation: seoul simini modu jagayongeul taji anko jajeongeoreul tandamyeon onsilgaseu baechureul keuge juril su isseul geomnida. — If all Seoul citizens rode bicycles instead of private cars, greenhouse gas emissions could be greatly reduced.

examples.text: 만약 음료수 캔이나 이면지를 백 퍼센트 재활용할 수 있다면 종이를 구십 퍼센트까지 절약할 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: manyak eumnyosu kaenina imyeonjireul baek peosenteu jaehwaryonghal su itdamyeon jongireul gusip peosenteukkaji jeoryakal su itseumnida. — If beverage cans or scratch paper could be recycled 100 percent, paper could be saved by up to 90 percent.

explanations.title: More sentences (mine)
explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

examples.text: 비가 온다면 집에 있겠어요.
examples.translation: biga ondamyeon jibe itgesseoyo. — If it rains, I will stay home.

examples.text: 만약 시간이 있었다면 같이 갔을 거예요.
examples.translation: manyak sigani isseotdamyeon gachi gasseul geoyeyo. — If I had had time, I would have gone together.

examples.text: 내가 대통령이라면 환경을 먼저 보호하겠어요.
examples.translation: naega daetongnyeongiramyeon hwangyeongeul meonjeo bohohagesseoyo. — If I were president, I would protect the environment first.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 5 (listening to four conversations between two friends and writing the hypothetical condition and the action) is an audio activity.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): a local newspaper article about Ulsan
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a local Korean newspaper article (Yonhap News). The book glosses 공직자: a government employee/official; 수칙: rules. The excerpt is the book’s with the numbers spelled out and the book’s △ marks replaced by commas; the English “Green Day” in brackets is dropped; the English is mine. The book asks you to write the topic in Korean, and then to match Set A phrases with paraphrased sentences from Set B (strips).

examples.text: 울산시가 매주 수요일을 녹색생활 실천의 날로 지정해 운영하는 가운데 공직자가 실천해야 할 열 가지 수칙을 선정했다.
examples.translation: ulsansiga maeju suyoireul noksaeksaenghwal silcheonui nallo jijeonghae unyeonghaneun gaunde gongjikjaga silcheonhaeya hal yeol gaji suchigeul seonjeonghaetda. — While Ulsan City designates and operates every Wednesday as a Green Life Practice Day, it has selected ten rules that public officials must practice.

examples.text: 삼 일 시에 따르면 공직자들은 여름에 넥타이 풀고 겨울에 내복 입기, 걷기, 자전거, 대중교통, 경차, 카풀 적극 이용하기, 청사 내 계단 이용하기, 녹색사무실 가꾸기, 구내식당 이용 시 반찬 남기지 않기 등을 실천할 예정이다.
examples.translation: sam il sie ttareumyeon gongjikjadeureun yeoreume nektai pulgo gyeoure naebok ipgi, geotgi, jajeongeo, daejunggyotong, gyeongcha, kapul jeokgeuk iyonghagi, cheongsa nae gyedan iyonghagi, noksaeksamusil gakkugi, gunaesikdang iyong si banchan namgiji anki deungeul silcheonhal yejeongida. — According to the city on the 3rd, public officials plan to practice taking off neckties in summer and wearing long underwear in winter; actively using walking, bicycles, public transportation, compact cars and carpools; using the stairs inside the government building; tending a green office; and not leaving side dishes when using the cafeteria.

examples.text: 또 이면지 재활용, 자연채광 활용 전기 절약, 부재 시 컴퓨터와 프린터, 복사기 전원 끄기, 일회용품 사용 자제와 재활용품 분리수거 철저, 매주 수요일 자기능력 개발 등을 실천한다.
examples.translation: tto imyeonji jaehwaryong, jayeonchaegwang hwaryong jeongi jeoryak, bujae si keompyuteowa peurinteo, boksagi jeonwon kkeugi, ilhoeyongpum sayong jajewa jaehwaryongpum bullisugeo cheoljeo, maeju suyoil jagineungnyeok gaebal deungeul silcheonhanda. — They will also practice recycling scratch paper; saving electricity by using natural lighting; turning off the power of computers, printers and copiers when absent; refraining from using disposable goods and thorough separation of recyclables; and developing one’s own abilities every Wednesday.

explanations.title: The topic (mine)
explanations.body: A topic for the article: 울산시가 선정한 공직자의 환경 실천 수칙 열 가지 (the ten environmental practice rules that Ulsan City selected for public officials).

explanations.title: Activity 5 (Writing and speaking): save resources!
explanations.body: A contest for the best ideas to conserve resources and protect the environment will be held in your city. You and your partner will enter the competition and submit your ideas: each of you thinks of at least three ideas (written in English), you talk about them in Korean, choose the three best and post them, and rate other teams’ ideas with 1 to 5 stars.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with.

Now I am able to: identify waste separation and disposal methods; extract factual information about and discuss global warming, its causes, impact, and preventive measures; make suggestions on how to reduce food waste; and talk about the efforts to conserve resources and protect the environment.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the conjunctive ending –자; expressions frequently used in news reports; –(으)ㅁ and –(으)ㄹ 것, abbreviated verb endings used in writing; the conjunctive ending –다면 for a hypothetical condition; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 분리 (分離), 재활용 (再活用), 온난화 (溫暖化), 식물 (植物), and 경차 (輕車).

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (SMART Board), Activity 2 (listening to YTN news clips about the government’s efforts to conserve resources and matching them with titles: Developing Alternative Energy; Campaign for Saving Energy/Energy-Saving Measures; Reducing Use of Disposable Products, one does not match; the book glosses 머그잔: a mug; 환경부: Ministry of Environment; 행정안전부/행안부: Ministry of the Interior and Safety) and Activity 4 (listening to MBC news on local government subsidy programs: Chuncheon City’s purpose, who is eligible and the amount, and why more local governments are implementing them; the book glosses 지자체: local government; 사업: program; 이동(하다): movement [to move]; 수단: means; method) are audio, video and computer activities.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning, and the book’s parenthesized forms such as ~하다 and ~되다 show how a noun forms a verb. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank. 팩 is listed also as a loan word.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (2팩 → 두 팩; 영하 50도 → 영하 오십 도; 1.5℃ → 일 점 오 도; 40대 → 사십 대; 10월 → 시월; 2배 → 두 배; TV → 티브이; the English “PET” and “ℓ” notes are in the meaning only). The quotation marks in the example of 주제 are dropped.

explanations.title: What Chapter 41 teaches (한국의 문화 1)
explanations.body:
Chapter 41, “Korean Culture I”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations (clothing, kimchi making, hanok houses) with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and extract information about traditional and modern clothing in Korea, and describe a person’s outfit; discuss food-related culture in Korea, including making kimchi; talk about basic cooking methods; and identify traditional and modern Korean houses, and compare them.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; ~을/를 포함해(서) (including); ~와/과 달리 or ~하고 달리 (unlike); transitive verbs with a causative infix; ~ 중에서/가운데서 (among) and ~에서 (at; on; in) in the superlative form; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 서양 (西洋), 음식 (飮食), and 한옥 (韓屋).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 서양 (西洋)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means the West, Western (world/society), or Occident, as in 서양 문학 (Western literature) and 서양 음악 (Western music). Thus its counterpart is 동양 (the East, Eastern [world/society], or Orient), as in 동양 문학 (Eastern literature) and 동양 음악 (Eastern music). The first syllable 서 (西) means west or western, as in 서부 (western part; the west), 서해 (the West sea; a western sea), and 서풍 (a west wind). The second syllable 양 (洋) means ocean, as in 대양 (the ocean; “big ocean”), 태평양 (the Pacific Ocean), 대서양 (the Atlantic Ocean; “big western ocean”), and 인도양 (the Indian Ocean). Thus the literal meaning of the word 서양 is “west ocean” or “western ocean,” and the word refers to the West or Europe because the West is located west of Korea (or China) across the ocean. Note that the syllable 양 of the word 서양 can mean Western or foreign when it is used as a prefix, as in 양식 (Western food), 양복 (a suit; a dress; Western clothes), 양화점 (a shoe store; “Western shoes”), 양옥 (a Western-style house), and 양담배 (a foreign cigarette; American tobacco; “Western cigarette”). The book asks you to guess the meaning of 동서양, 서양화가, 양배추, 양복점, 서양화(하다) and 오대양 (my answers):

rows: the West Sea; a western sea
East and West; the Orient and the Occident
a tailor shop; a store selling suits

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 음식 (飮食)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means food (and drink) or a meal. The first syllable 음 (飮) means drinking, as in 음주 (drinking; “drinking liquor”) and 음용수 (drinking water; “water for drinking use”). The second syllable 식 (食) means food or eating, as in 식당 (a restaurant) and 한식 (Korean food; Korean dish). Thus the literal meaning of the word 음식 is “drinking and eating,” and the word refers to food (and drink), eatables (and drinkables), or a meal. The book asks you to guess the meaning of 음료수, 음주운전, 음식점, 과식, 과음 and 식품점 (my answers):

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 한옥 (韓屋)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means a traditional Korean-style house. As in words like 한국 and 북한, the first syllable 한 (韓) means Korea(n). The second syllable 옥 (屋) means house or house roof, as in 양옥 (a Western-style house; “Western house”), 옥상 (the rooftop; the housetop), and 옥외 (outside the house; the outdoors; the open [air]). Thus the literal meaning of the word 한옥 is “Korean house.” The book asks you to guess the meaning of 양옥, 한국화, 한반도, 영한사전, 옥외 주차장 and 옥내 주차장 (my answers):

lessons.subtitle: 한복 · 저고리 · 정장과 캐주얼 · 내의 선물 · 북한의 패션 · 한복 체험 행사

explanations.title: Topic A: When do people wear hanbok? (한복은 언제 입을까요?)
explanations.body: The following article is about clothing worn by Koreans in the past and today. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 한국사람들은 옛날에 한복을 입었다.
examples.translation: hanguksaramdeureun yennare hanbogeul ibeotda. — Koreans wore hanbok in the old days.

examples.text: 기본적으로 남자는 바지와 저고리, 여자는 치마와 저고리를 입었다.
examples.translation: gibonjeogeuro namjaneun bajiwa jeogori, yeojaneun chimawa jeogorireul ibeotda. — Basically, men wore trousers and a jeogori, and women wore a skirt and a jeogori.

examples.text: 또, 입는 사람과 목적에 따라 한복의 모양과 색이 다양했다.
examples.translation: tto, imneun saramgwa mokjeoge ttara hanbogui moyanggwa saegi dayanghaetda. — Also, the shape and color of hanbok were varied according to the wearer and the purpose.

examples.text: 계층이 높은 사람들은 색이 화려하거나 장식이 많은 옷을 입었다.
examples.translation: gyecheungi nopeun saramdeureun saegi hwaryeohageona jangsigi maneun oseul ibeotda. — People of high social class wore clothes that were colorful or had many decorations.

examples.text: 계층이 낮은 사람들은 흰 옷을 입었다.
examples.translation: gyecheungi najeun saramdeureun huin oseul ibeotda. — People of low social class wore white clothes.

examples.text: 현대 한국인들은 서양 문화의 영향으로 평상시에는 한복을 잘 입지 않는다.
examples.translation: hyeondae hangugindeureun seoyang munhwaui yeonghyangeuro pyeongsangsieneun hanbogeul jal ipji anneunda. — Modern Koreans, under the influence of Western culture, do not often wear hanbok in ordinary times.

examples.text: 한복은 주로 명절이나 결혼식과 같은 특별한 때에 입는다.
examples.translation: hanbogeun juro myeongjeorina gyeolhonsikgwa gateun teukbyeolhan ttaee imneunda. — Hanbok is mostly worn on special occasions such as holidays or weddings.

explanations.title: Ms. Song Eunji’s clothes
explanations.body: The second text of Topic A (the English is mine; her age is spelled out in Hangul):

examples.text: 송은지 씨는 스물여덟 살의 기혼 직장 여성이다.
examples.translation: songeunji ssineun seumullyeodeol sarui gihon jikjang yeoseongida. — Ms. Song Eunji is a 28-year-old married working woman.

examples.text: 송은지 씨의 직장에서는 보통 정장을 입고 구두를 신어야 한다.
examples.translation: songeunji ssiui jikjangeseoneun botong jeongjangeul ipgo gudureul sineoya handa. — At Ms. Song’s workplace, you usually have to wear a suit and shoes.

examples.text: 그러나 금요일에는 캐주얼한 옷을 입어도 된다.
examples.translation: geureona geumyoireneun kaejueolhan oseul ibeodo doenda. — But on Fridays, you may wear casual clothes.

examples.text: 그래서 그날은 유행하는 스타일의 편안한 옷을 입는다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo geunareun yuhaenghaneun seutairui pyeonanhan oseul imneunda. — So on that day she wears comfortable clothes in a trendy style.

examples.text: 다음 주 화요일은 설날이다.
examples.translation: daeum ju hwayoireun seollarida. — Next Tuesday is Lunar New Year’s Day.

examples.text: 설날에 송은지 씨 부부는 한복을 입고 시댁에 간다.
examples.translation: seollare songeunji ssi bubuneun hanbogeul ipgo sidaege ganda. — On Lunar New Year’s Day, Ms. Song and her husband wear hanbok and go to her husband’s family’s home.

examples.text: 올해는 새로 맞춘 한복을 입고 가려고 한다.
examples.translation: olhaeneun saero matchun hanbogeul ipgo garyeogo handa. — This year they intend to go wearing newly custom-made hanbok.

examples.text: 송은지 씨는 분홍색, 남편은 연한 파란색 한복을 입을 것이다.
examples.translation: songeunji ssineun bunhongsaek, nampyeoneun yeonhan paransaek hanbogeul ibeul geosida. — Ms. Song will wear pink and her husband will wear light blue hanbok.

examples.text: 시부모님께는 따뜻한 내의를 한 벌씩 선물해 드릴 생각이다.
examples.translation: sibumonimkkeneun ttatteutan naeuireul han beolssik seonmulhae deuril saenggagida. — She plans to give her parents-in-law a set of warm underwear each as a present.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 내의 (內衣)
explanations.body: 내의 (內衣), which literally means “inside clothes,” refers to underwear. In certain contexts, 내의 can also refer to thermal underwear known as 내복 (內服). It has been a tradition for grown children to buy parents thermal 내의 or 내복 when they get their first paycheck. Giving 내의 to parents is not limited to that occasion, however. 내의 has been a popular and practical gift item for parents or any elderly relative on birthdays or traditional holidays. Although this tradition is not as common now as in the past, it is still practiced today.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): fashion in North Korea
explanations.body: The following article is about fashion in North Korea; the book asks you to read it and fill in a table in English with North Korean fashion (early 1980s), North Korean fashion (late 1980s), forbidden fashions, and fashion of North Korea’s new generation. The book glosses 대상: a target, an object; 몰래: secretly. The article is the book’s with the years spelled out in Hangul (the book’s quotation marks around the magazine title are dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 팔십 년대 중반까지 북한 여성들은 검정 치마에 흰 저고리를 주로 입었다.
examples.translation: palsip nyeondae jungbankkaji bukan yeoseongdeureun geomjeong chimae huin jeogorireul juro ibeotda. — Until the mid-1980s, North Korean women mostly wore a black skirt with a white jeogori.

examples.text: 그 이후에 원피스, 투피스, 블라우스, 스웨터 등과 같은 다양한 서양식 옷을 입기 시작했다.
examples.translation: geu ihue wonpiseu, tupiseu, beullauseu, seuweteo deunggwa gateun dayanghan seoyangsik oseul ipgi sijakaetda. — After that they began to wear various Western-style clothes such as one-piece dresses, two-piece suits, blouses and sweaters.

examples.text: 천구백구십 년대에도 계속 서양식 옷을 입었다.
examples.translation: cheongubaekgusip nyeondaeedo gyesok seoyangsik oseul ibeotda. — They kept wearing Western-style clothes in the 1990s too.

examples.text: 그러나 짧은 치마와 영어가 쓰여 있는 옷, 청바지는 단속 대상이 되었다.
examples.translation: geureona jjalbeun chimawa yeongeoga sseuyeo inneun ot, cheongbajineun dansok daesangi doeeotda. — But short skirts, clothes with English written on them, and jeans became targets of crackdowns.

examples.text: 북한에도 패션 잡지가 있는데 무역이라고 한다.
examples.translation: bukanedo paesyeon japjiga inneunde muyeogirago handa. — North Korea also has a fashion magazine, called “Trade”.

examples.text: 최근에는 북한 신세대들이 남한의 인기 드라마에 나오는 탤런트들의 패션을 따르고 있다.
examples.translation: choegeuneneun bukan sinsedaedeuri namhanui ingi deuramae naoneun taelleonteudeurui paesyeoneul ttareugo itda. — Recently, the North Korean new generation has been following the fashion of the actors who appear in popular South Korean dramas.

examples.text: 이들은 높은 계층의 자녀들인데 남한 탤런트들의 옷, 머리 스타일, 머리 염색까지 따라 하고 있다.
examples.translation: ideureun nopeun gyecheungui janyeodeurinde namhan taelleonteudeurui ot, meori seutail, meori yeomsaekkaji ttara hago itda. — They are children of the high classes, and they are copying even the South Korean actors’ clothes, hairstyles and hair dyeing.

examples.text: 신세대들은 컴퓨터나 몰래 들여온 남한 드라마를 보고 남한 패션을 배운다.
examples.translation: sinsedaedeureun keompyuteona mollae deuryeoon namhan deuramareul bogo namhan paesyeoneul baeunda. — The new generation learns South Korean fashion by watching computers or South Korean dramas that were secretly brought in.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): a Lunar New Year event
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a Korean newspaper article about an event held on Lunar New Year. The book asks you to skim the title, write in English the type of event that was held, and fill in a table (Participants / What participants did). The book glosses 추억: memory, remembrance. The article is the book’s (the quotation marks are dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 이번 행사에서 외국인들은 한국의 예절과 한복에 대한 설명을 듣고 직접 한복을 입어 보고 세배도 했습니다.

explanations.title: Activity 4: What should I wear? (어떤 옷을 입어야 할까요?)
explanations.body: You will listen to a phone message in which a college graduate asks about suitable clothing for work (audio: the caller’s facts and questions are in the recording and are left out). Three different clothing consultants write back with suggestions. The book asks you to rank the suggestions, write the reasons in English, discuss in Korean with a partner, choose the best, and present it. The three suggestions are the book’s (the labels are spelled out in Hangul: 제안 일, 이, 삼); the English is mine.

examples.text: 제안 일: 보통 회사에서 정장을 많이 하니까 양복을 여러 벌 준비하시면 좋습니다. 양복이 많으면 셔츠나 넥타이를 고르기도 쉽습니다. 유행하는 스타일에 따라서 다양하게 준비하세요. 요즘은 짙은 색깔이 유행하니까 짙은 색깔의 넥타이를 사시면 어떨까요? 그리고 금요일에는 분홍색 셔츠보다는 연한 파랑이나 검은색을 추천합니다.
examples.translation: jean il: botong hoesaeseo jeongjangeul mani hanikka yangbogeul yeoreo beol junbihasimyeon joseumnida. yangbogi maneumyeon syeocheuna nektaireul goreugido swipseumnida. yuhaenghaneun seutaire ttaraseo dayanghage junbihaseyo. yojeumeun jiteun saekkari yuhaenghanikka jiteun saekkarui nektaireul sasimyeon eotteolkkayo? geurigo geumyoireneun bunhongsaek syeocheubodaneun yeonhan parangina geomeunsaegeul chucheonhamnida. — Since people usually wear suits at companies, it is good to prepare several suits. If you have many suits, it is also easy to choose shirts and ties. Prepare a variety according to the trendy style. These days dark colors are trendy, so how about buying a dark-colored tie? And on Fridays, I recommend light blue or black rather than a pink shirt.

examples.text: 제안 이: 우선 정장은 좋은 제품으로 두 벌 정도 사세요. 그리고 셔츠와 넥타이를 여러 색깔로 사세요. 셔츠는 연한 색깔이 넥타이와 맞춰서 입기 쉬워요. 그러니까 연한 색깔로 고르세요. 그리고 신입사원이니까 청바지는 피하세요. 다른 캐주얼 바지가 좋을 것 같습니다.
examples.translation: jean i: useon jeongjangeun joeun jepumeuro du beol jeongdo saseyo. geurigo syeocheuwa nektaireul yeoreo saekkallo saseyo. syeocheuneun yeonhan saekkari nektaiwa matchwoseo ipgi swiwoyo. geureonikka yeonhan saekkallo goreuseyo. geurigo sinipsawoninikka cheongbajineun pihaseyo. dareun kaejueol bajiga joeul geot gatseumnida. — First, buy about two suits of good quality. And buy shirts and ties in various colors. Shirts in light colors are easy to wear matched with ties. So choose light colors. And since you are a new employee, avoid jeans. Other casual trousers seem good.

examples.text: 제안 삼: 양복은 계절에 따라 겨울, 봄과 가을, 여름 양복으로 세 벌 정도 준비하시면 어때요? 색깔은 검정, 파랑, 회색이면 좋을 것 같습니다. 젊으시니까 넥타이는 화려한 색깔이 좋을 것 같습니다. 금요일에는 캐주얼하게 분홍색 셔츠와 청바지가 좋을 것 같아요.
examples.translation: jean sam: yangbogeun gyejeore ttara gyeoul, bomgwa gaeul, yeoreum yangbogeuro se beol jeongdo junbihasimyeon eottaeyo? saekkareun geomjeong, parang, hoesaegimyeon joeul geot gatseumnida. jeolmeusinikka nektaineun hwaryeohan saekkari joeul geot gatseumnida. geumyoireneun kaejueolhage bunhongsaek syeocheuwa cheongbajiga joeul geot gatayo. — How about preparing about three suits, for winter, spring and fall, and summer, according to the season? Black, blue and gray seem good for colors. Since you are young, a colorful tie seems good. On Fridays, a pink shirt and jeans seem good as casual wear.

explanations.title: What each consultant says (mine)
explanations.body: The ranking depends on the caller’s facts in the recording, so I give the points of each suggestion instead:

rows: Several suits; many suits make choosing shirts and ties easy; follow trends, with dark colors and dark ties; on Fridays light blue or black rather than pink
About two good-quality suits; shirts and ties in various colors; light-colored shirts match ties easily; avoid jeans as a new employee; choose other casual trousers
About three suits by season (winter, spring/fall, summer); black, blue or gray; a colorful tie because you are young; a pink shirt and jeans on Fridays

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: The phone message (audio), ranking with reasons, the pair discussion in Korean, writing the choice in the class notebook (MS Teams), presenting in Korean and getting feedback are listening, pair and presentation activities.

lessons.subtitle: 김치 · 김장 · 배추 · 고춧가루 · 이웃 · 절임 배추 · 맞춤 김치 · 요리 방법

explanations.title: Topic B: Korean gimjang culture (한국의 김장 문화)
explanations.body: The following text is about the traditions involved when making kimchi in Korea. (The English is mine; the book gives none; the month is spelled out in Hangul.)

examples.text: 김치는 한국의 대표적인 음식이다.
examples.translation: gimchineun hangugui daepyojeogin eumsigida. — Kimchi is a representative food of Korea.

examples.text: 여러 종류의 김치가 있지만, 그중에서 배추김치가 가장 흔하다.
examples.translation: yeoreo jongnyuui gimchiga itjiman, geujungeseo baechugimchiga gajang heunhada. — There are many kinds of kimchi, but among them napa cabbage kimchi is the most common.

examples.text: 김치 양념에는 고춧가루를 포함해서 여러 가지가 들어간다.
examples.translation: gimchi yangnyeomeneun gochutgarureul pohamhaeseo yeoreo gajiga deureoganda. — Various things go into the kimchi seasoning, including red pepper powder.

examples.text: 보통 십일월에 겨울 동안 먹을 김치를 담근다.
examples.translation: botong sibirwore gyeoul dongan meogeul gimchireul damgeunda. — Usually in November they make the kimchi to eat during the winter.

examples.text: 이것을 김장이라고 한다.
examples.translation: igeoseul gimjangirago handa. — This is called gimjang.

examples.text: 예전과 달리 요즘은 김장을 안 하는 사람도 많다.
examples.translation: yejeongwa dalli yojeumeun gimjangeul an haneun saramdo manta. — Unlike in the past, there are many people these days who do not make gimjang.

examples.text: 그렇지만, 주부 오선희 씨는 전통적인 김장 문화를 지키고 싶어 한다.
examples.translation: geureochiman, jubu oseonhui ssineun jeontongjeogin gimjang munhwareul jikigo sipeo handa. — However, the housewife Ms. Oh Seonhee wants to keep the traditional gimjang culture.

examples.text: 이웃끼리 서로 도우며 김장을 하는 모습이 아름답기 때문이다.
examples.translation: iutkkiri seoro doumyeo gimjangeul haneun moseubi areumdapgi ttaemunida. — This is because the sight of neighbors helping each other and making gimjang is beautiful.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 김장
explanations.body: 김장 refers to making kimchi (for the winter). It was traditionally an important annual event for Koreans because it allowed them to eat vegetables throughout the winter when fresh vegetables were not readily available. In early winter, every household used to make kimchi using various vegetables but mainly napa cabbage and radishes. The kimchi was stored in jars called 김장독/김칫독 and buried in the ground, which functioned much like a refrigerator. Because 김장 is very labor intensive, Koreans used to invite their neighbors to help. These days, with the availability of good-quality commercial 김치 and fresh vegetables throughout the winter, 김장 is not as common as in the past. Today, with 김치 냉장고, which can preserve kimchi for long periods, the practice of burying 김장독 in the ground is no longer common.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Listening): cooking methods
explanations.body: The book asks you to listen to four segments in which a chef talks about a dish (스파게티, 불고기, 김밥, 감자 튀김) and how to make it, and to choose the cooking method(s) from a list: 1. steaming; 2. boiling; 3. frying; 4. cutting; 5. salting; 6. deep-frying; 7. baking; 8. turning over; 9. stirring; 10. mixing/blending (the book glosses 말다: to roll; 얇다: to be thin). This is an audio activity and is left out; the methods match the verbs 찌다, 삶다, 볶다, 썰다, 절이다, 튀기다, 굽다, 뒤집다, 젓다 and 섞다 of the core vocabulary.

lessons.title: 514. Ch 41 · Grammar A: expressing “unlike”, ~와/과 달리 and ~하고 달리
lessons.subtitle: ~와/과 달리 · ~하고 달리 · ~와/과는 달리 · 형과 달리 · 작년과 달리 · 한국과 일본의 음식문화

explanations.title: Recall ~처럼, then “unlike”
explanations.body:
Recall the grammar feature ~처럼 that you learned about in Chapter 34. Its function and use are similar to the English preposition like, as in 우리 형처럼 저는 농구를 잘 해요 (Like my older brother, I am good at basketball). 우리 형처럼 (like my older brother) tells us that the speaker’s older brother is good at basketball and so is the speaker.

How then do we express “unlike my older brother” in Korean? Note the following sentences (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 형과 달리 저는 농구를 잘 합니다.
examples.translation: hyeonggwa dalli jeoneun nonggureul jal hamnida. — Unlike my older brother, I play basketball well.

examples.text: 형하고 달리 저는 농구를 잘 합니다.
examples.translation: hyeonghago dalli jeoneun nonggureul jal hamnida. — Unlike my older brother, I play basketball well. (~하고 달리)

explanations.title: 달리 and the topic marker
explanations.body: Note that 달리 in ~와/과 달리 and ~하고 달리 come from the verb 다르다 (to be different). Note also that 달리 is preceded by ~와/과 or ~하고. The topic marker 은/는 can be added to ~와/과 and ~하고, as shown in the following examples:

examples.text: 형과는 달리 저는 농구를 좋아합니다.
examples.translation: hyeonggwaneun dalli jeoneun nonggureul joahamnida. — Unlike my older brother, I like basketball.

examples.text: 형하고는 달리 저는 농구를 좋아해요.
examples.translation: hyeonghagoneun dalli jeoneun nonggureul joahaeyo. — Unlike my older brother, I like basketball.

explanations.title: Expressing “unlike”: ~와/과 달리, ~하고 달리
explanations.body: More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 한국인들은 미국인들하고 달리 생일날 미역국을 먹습니다.
examples.translation: hangugindeureun migugindeulhago dalli saengillal miyeokgugeul meokseumnida. — Unlike Americans, Koreans eat seaweed soup on their birthdays.

examples.text: 구세대와 달리 신세대는 변화를 좋아합니다.
examples.translation: gusedaewa dalli sinsedaeneun byeonhwareul joahamnida. — Unlike the older generation, the younger generation likes change.

examples.text: 작년과 달리 올해는 장마가 빨리 시작됐습니다.
examples.translation: jangnyeongwa dalli olhaeneun jangmaga ppalli sijakdwaetseumnida. — Unlike last year, the rainy season started earlier this year.

examples.text: 이 의자는 다른 의자와 달리 아주 편합니다.
examples.translation: i uijaneun dareun uijawa dalli aju pyeonhamnida. — Unlike other chairs, this chair is very comfortable.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Speaking): the model
explanations.body: Student A makes a sentence using the grammar feature ~와/과 달리 and the words on the strip. Student B then repeats Student A’s entire sentence, replacing ~와/과 달리 with ~하고 달리. The book’s model (the strip says 몬트레이 vs. 뉴욕; the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 몬트레이는 뉴욕과 달리 겨울에 눈이 안 와요.
examples.translation: ga: monteureineun nyuyokgwa dalli gyeoure nuni an wayo. — Unlike New York, it does not snow in Monterey in winter.

examples.text: 나: 몬트레이는 뉴욕하고 달리 겨울에 눈이 안 와요.
examples.translation: na: monteureineun nyuyokago dalli gyeoure nuni an wayo. — Unlike New York, it does not snow in Monterey in winter.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): food culture in Korea and Japan
explanations.body: The following passage compares food culture in Korea and Japan; the book asks you to read it and fill in a table (Similarity / Difference). The passage is the book’s; the English is mine.

examples.text: 한국과 일본의 음식문화는 비슷한 점도 있고 다른 점도 있습니다.
examples.translation: hangukgwa ilbonui eumsingmunhwaneun biseutan jeomdo itgo dareun jeomdo itseumnida. — The food cultures of Korea and Japan have both similarities and differences.

examples.text: 일본사람들도 한국사람들처럼 야채와 생선을 많이 먹습니다.
examples.translation: ilbonsaramdeuldo hanguksaramdeulcheoreom yachaewa saengseoneul mani meokseumnida. — Japanese people, like Koreans, eat a lot of vegetables and fish.

examples.text: 그렇지만 일본음식은 한국음식과 달리 매운 음식이 별로 없습니다.
examples.translation: geureochiman ilboneumsigeun hangugeumsikgwa dalli maeun eumsigi byeollo eopseumnida. — However, unlike Korean food, Japanese food has few spicy dishes.

examples.text: 또 일본사람들도 한국사람들처럼 식사할 때 젓가락을 씁니다.
examples.translation: tto ilbonsaramdeuldo hanguksaramdeulcheoreom siksahal ttae jeotgarageul sseumnida. — Also, Japanese people, like Koreans, use chopsticks when they eat.

examples.text: 그렇지만 한국사람들은 일본사람들과 다르게 밥을 먹을 때도 젓가락을 잘 사용하지 않습니다.
examples.translation: geureochiman hanguksaramdeureun ilbonsaramdeulgwa dareuge babeul meogeul ttaedo jeotgarageul jal sayonghaji anseumnida. — However, unlike Japanese people, Koreans do not often use chopsticks even when they eat rice.

examples.text: 한국에서는 젓가락으로 밥을 먹는 것은 예의가 아닙니다.
examples.translation: hangugeseoneun jeotgarageuro babeul meongneun geoseun yeuiga animnida. — In Korea, eating rice with chopsticks is not polite.

rows: Both eat a lot of vegetables and fish; both use chopsticks when eating
Japanese food has few spicy dishes, unlike Korean food; Koreans often do not use chopsticks even when eating rice, and eating rice with chopsticks is impolite in Korea

explanations.title: Expressing “including”
explanations.body: Look closely at the underlined phrases in the following sentences to see how Koreans express “including something/somebody.” (The English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 국방외국어대학에서는 한국어를 포함해서 많은 언어를 가르칩니다.

examples.text: 김 일병을 포함해서 많은 학생이 한국에 갑니다.
examples.translation: gim ilbyeongeul pohamhaeseo maneun haksaengi hanguge gamnida. — Many students are going to Korea, including PFC Kim.

explanations.title: Note
explanations.body: Note that ~을/를 포함해서 is preceded by a noun and 서 in ~을/를 포함해서 can be deleted. More examples (the numbers are spelled out; the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 세탁기와 냉장고를 포함해서 다양한 가전제품을 세일합니다.
examples.translation: setakgiwa naengjanggoreul pohamhaeseo dayanghan gajeonjepumeul seilhamnida. — Various home appliances, including washers and refrigerators, are on sale.

examples.text: 팔십팔 년 서울 올림픽에는 미국을 포함해 백오십구 개국이 참가했습니다.
examples.translation: palsippal nyeon seoul ollimpigeneun migugeul pohamhae baegosipgu gaegugi chamgahaetseumnida. — One hundred fifty-nine countries, including the U.S., participated in the Seoul Olympic Games in 1988.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Writing and speaking): countries on a continent
explanations.body: In Korean, write the names of countries that are part of the continent listed in your column (Student A: 아시아, 남아메리카, 오스트레일리아; Student B: 유럽, 북아메리카, 아프리카). Then take turns asking each other what countries are part of the continents, using ~을/를 포함해(서). The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 가: 아시아에는 어떤 나라가 있어요?
examples.translation: ga: asiaeneun eotteon naraga isseoyo? — What countries are there in Asia?

examples.text: 나: 중국, 일본 등을 포함해서 여러 나라가 있어요.
examples.translation: na: jungguk, ilbon deungeul pohamhaeseo yeoreo naraga isseoyo. — There are several countries, including China, Japan, etc.

explanations.title: Some countries on each continent (mine)
explanations.body: My sample answers:

rows: 중국, 일본, 한국, 인도, 베트남, 태국

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Reading): Korean food and foreigners
explanations.body: Read the following passage about Korean food and circle the grammar feature ~을/를 포함해(서); the book asks you to fill in a table in English. The passage is the book’s; the English is mine.

examples.text: 요즘 한국 음식을 먹는 외국인들이 점점 늘어나고 있습니다.
examples.translation: yojeum hanguk eumsigeul meongneun oegugindeuri jeomjeom neureonago itseumnida. — These days the number of foreigners who eat Korean food is gradually increasing.

examples.text: 비빔밥을 포함해 불고기, 김치찌개 등이 특히 인기가 있습니다.
examples.translation: bibimbabeul pohamhae bulgogi, gimchijjigae deungi teuki ingiga itseumnida. — Including bibimbap, bulgogi, kimchi stew, etc. are especially popular.

examples.text: 한국의 대표적인 음식인 김치도 많은 외국인이 좋아합니다.
examples.translation: hangugui daepyojeogin eumsigin gimchido maneun oegugini joahamnida. — Many foreigners also like kimchi, a representative Korean food.

examples.text: 대부분의 외국인들은 처음에는 김치를 잘 못 먹습니다.
examples.translation: daebubunui oegugindeureun cheoeumeneun gimchireul jal mon meokseumnida. — Most foreigners cannot eat kimchi well at first.

examples.text: 하지만, 김치는 먹을수록 맛있다고 합니다.
examples.translation: hajiman, gimchineun meogeulsurok masitdago hamnida. — But they say that the more you eat kimchi, the tastier it is.

examples.text: 김치는 종류가 아주 많습니다.
examples.translation: gimchineun jongnyuga aju manseumnida. — There are very many kinds of kimchi.

examples.text: 배추김치를 포함하여 오이김치, 파김치 등 다양한 종류의 김치가 있습니다.
examples.translation: baechugimchireul pohamhayeo oigimchi, pagimchi deung dayanghan jongnyuui gimchiga itseumnida. — There are various kinds of kimchi, including napa cabbage kimchi, cucumber kimchi, green onion kimchi, etc.

examples.text: 김치를 담글 때 제일 중요한 것은 양념입니다.
examples.translation: gimchireul damgeul ttae jeil jungyohan geoseun yangnyeomimnida. — The most important thing when making kimchi is the seasoning.

examples.text: 김치 양념에는 고춧가루를 포함해서 파, 마늘, 양파 등이 들어갑니다.
examples.translation: gimchi yangnyeomeneun gochutgarureul pohamhaeseo pa, maneul, yangpa deungi deureogamnida. — In the kimchi seasoning, green onion, garlic, onion, etc. go in, including red pepper powder.

rows: Napa cabbage kimchi, cucumber kimchi, green onion kimchi, etc.
Red pepper powder, green onion, garlic, onion, etc.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Writing and speaking): the most memorable birthday party
explanations.body: Recall your most memorable birthday party (who attended, what foods were served, the presents) and fill in the table in English; then write at least five sentences using ~을/를 포함해(서) as many times as you can. The book’s model is the one below (the number of years is missing in the printed text: 살 생일 파티; I have written 열 살; the English is mine). You then present in Korean and get feedback.

examples.text: 제게 가장 기억에 남는 파티는 열 살 생일 파티입니다.
examples.translation: jege gajang gieoge namneun patineun yeol sal saengil patiimnida. — The party that remains most in my memory is my 10th birthday party.

examples.text: 그 파티에는 제 친구 스티브를 포함해서 많은 친구가 왔습니다.
examples.translation: geu patieneun je chingu seutibeureul pohamhaeseo maneun chinguga watseumnida. — Many friends came to that party, including my friend Steve.

examples.text: 친구들이 선물을 많이 주었습니다.
examples.translation: chingudeuri seonmureul mani jueotseumnida. — My friends gave me a lot of presents.

examples.text: 저는 옷을 포함해서 구두, 책, 게임기 등을 선물로 받았습니다.
examples.translation: jeoneun oseul pohamhaeseo gudu, chaek, geimgi deungeul seonmullo badatseumnida. — I received shoes, books, game consoles, etc. as presents, including clothes.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): a personal blog
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a personal blog; the book asks you to read it and fill in a table in English (the dish and its ingredients), and then to write the name of each dish in Korean and number the steps in the order of making (the first step is given). The book glosses 참기름: sesame oil. The blog is the book’s with the numbers of the steps and the minutes spelled out (the steps are numbered 일, 이, 삼, 사, 오 in Hangul; the recipe lines keep their printed numbering as words); the English is mine.

examples.text: 내일은 내 룸메이트의 생일이다.
examples.translation: naeireun nae rummeiteuui saengirida. — Tomorrow is my roommate’s birthday.

examples.text: 그래서 룸메이트를 위해서 미역국과 불고기를 만들기로 했다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo rummeiteureul wihaeseo miyeokgukgwa bulgogireul mandeulgiro haetda. — So I decided to make seaweed soup and bulgogi for my roommate.

examples.text: 처음 만드는 음식이지만 만드는 법이 생각보다 쉬웠다.
examples.translation: cheoeum mandeuneun eumsigijiman mandeuneun beobi saenggakboda swiwotda. — It is the first time I am making these foods, but the way to make them was easier than I thought.

examples.text: 미역국 끓이는 법
examples.translation: miyeokguk kkeurineun beop — How to boil seaweed soup

examples.text: 재료 미역, 소고기, 마늘, 양념 후추, 소금, 간장, 참기름
examples.translation: jaeryo miyeok, sogogi, maneul, yangnyeom huchu, sogeum, ganjang, chamgireum — Ingredients: seaweed, beef, garlic, seasoning (pepper, salt, soy sauce, sesame oil)

examples.text: 일 마른 미역을 물에 넣고 불린다.
examples.translation: il mareun miyeogeul mure neoko bullinda. — 1. Put dry seaweed in water and soak it.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 한옥
explanations.body: 한옥 (韓屋), which literally means “Korean house,” refers to a traditional Korean house. Soil, timber, and rock are the main materials used to construct a 한옥. Usually, the roof of a 한옥 is made of clay tiles called 기와. 온돌 (a heated stone floor) and 대청 (a wooden floor) in 한옥 help residents cope with extreme cold and heat. The living area in a 한옥 is divided into two sections: 안채 and 사랑채. 안채 is the area where women reside and 사랑채 is the area for men and guests (the book shows the floor plan of each area in pictures).

explanations.title: The floor plans (the labels the book gives)
explanations.body: 안채 구조 (floor plan of 안채 [building for women]): 1. 건넌방, 2. 대청, 3. 안방, 4. 마당, 5. 부엌, 6. 방/창고, 7. 대문. 사랑채 구조 (floor plan of 사랑채 [building for men and guests]): 1. 부엌, 2. 사랑방, 3. 대청, 4. 방 (guest room).

lessons.title: 518. Ch 41 · Grammar C: more transitive verbs with causative infixes (끓이다 · 녹이다 · 익히다)
lessons.subtitle: 끓이다 · 녹이다 · 익히다 · 덥히다 · 식히다 · 얼리다 · 절이다 · 튀기다 · 데우다 · 졸이다 · 말리다

explanations.title: Recall the causative infixes
explanations.body: In Chapter 30, you learned that the Korean causative infixes 이, 히, 기, 리, 우, 구, and 추, when added to native Korean verbs (먹다, 입다, etc.), turn the verbs into causative verbs, as in 먹이다 (to feed; to cause someone to eat) and 입히다 (to cause someone to wear/put on). In cooking-related contexts, you will often encounter native verbs with these causative infixes. In these instances, the verbs function as transitive verbs. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 먼저 물을 끓이세요.
examples.translation: meonjeo mureul kkeuriseyo. — Please boil the water first. / “Please cause the water to boil.”

examples.text: 물을 식히세요.
examples.translation: mureul sikiseyo. — Please cool the water. / “Please cause the water to cool down.”

explanations.title: Transitive and intransitive pairs
explanations.body: Note that 끓이다 and 식히다 from the intransitive verbs 끓다 and 식다 respectively function as transitive verbs. The following table lists some of these transitive verbs you will encounter in cooking-related contexts (the book’s table).

rows: to thaw (as in “The ice has thawed.”)
to cool (as in “The water cooled off.”)

explanations.title: Other transitive verbs
explanations.body: Other transitive verbs include the following:

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Listening and speaking): short sentences
explanations.body: Using the words in the table, make short sentences with a noun (object) and a verb; say your sentence aloud; your partner translates it into English. Objects: 찌개, 생선, 고기, 국, 물, 배추, 밥, 감자, 얼음, 차, 야채, 오이, 콩. Verbs: 끓이다, 녹이다, 익히다, 덥히다, 식히다, 얼리다, 절이다, 튀기다, 데우다, 졸이다, 재우다 (the book gives no meaning for 재우다: “to put to sleep”, in cooking “to let meat marinate”; my gloss). The book’s model is 오이를 절입니다 (I pickle cucumbers in salt). My sample sentences (the English is mine; word combinations may vary):

examples.text: 찌개를 끓입니다.
examples.translation: jjigaereul kkeurimnida. — I boil the stew.

examples.text: 생선을 익힙니다.
examples.translation: saengseoneul ikimnida. — I cook the fish.

examples.text: 얼음을 녹입니다.
examples.translation: eoreumeul nogimnida. — I thaw the ice.

examples.text: 국을 데웁니다.
