explanations.title: Topic C: The status and roles of women are changing (여성의 지위와 역할이 변하고 있다)
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a women’s magazine. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 한국 사회에서 여성의 지위와 역할이 변하고 있다.
examples.translation: hanguk sahoeeseo yeoseongui jiwiwa yeokari byeonhago itda. — The status and roles of women in Korean society are changing.

examples.text: 과거에 여성은 주로 가정에서 자녀를 양육하거나 가사 노동을 했다.
examples.translation: gwageoe yeoseongeun juro gajeongeseo janyeoreul yangyukageona gasa nodongeul haetda. — In the past, women mainly raised children at home or did housework.

examples.text: 반면 요즘에는 사회에 진출하는 전문직 여성들이 증가하고 있다.
examples.translation: banmyeon yojeumeneun sahoee jinchulhaneun jeonmunjik yeoseongdeuri jeunggahago itda. — On the other hand, these days the number of professional women entering society is increasing.

examples.text: 엔지니어와 조종사와 같은 전문 분야에도 도전하고 있다.
examples.translation: enjinieowa jojongsawa gateun jeonmun bunyaedo dojeonhago itda. — They are also taking on specialized fields such as engineers and pilots.

examples.text: 이희정 씨는 엔지니어다.
examples.translation: ihuijeong ssineun enjinieoda. — Ms. Lee Heejeong is an engineer.

examples.text: 대학에서 건축공학을 전공했지만, 결혼하고 오랫동안 전업주부로 지냈다.
examples.translation: daehageseo geonchukgonghageul jeongonghaetjiman, gyeolhonhago oraetdongan jeoneopjuburo jinaetda. — She majored in architectural engineering at university, but after marrying she lived as a full-time housewife for a long time.

examples.text: 집에서 희정 씨는 취미로 건물을 디자인해 보곤 했다.
examples.translation: jibeseo huijeong ssineun chwimiro geonmureul dijainhae bogon haetda. — At home, Heejeong used to try designing buildings as a hobby.

examples.text: 건물을 디자인하면서 건축회사에서 일하고 싶어졌다.
examples.translation: geonmureul dijainhamyeonseo geonchukoesaeseo ilhago sipeojeotda. — While designing buildings, she came to want to work at an architecture company.

examples.text: 그래서 엔지니어 교육원에 등록해서 건축 디자인을 공부했다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo enjinieo gyoyugwone deungnokaeseo geonchuk dijaineul gongbuhaetda. — So she enrolled in an engineer academy and studied architectural design.

examples.text: 지금은 건축회사에서 최고의 엔지니어로 인정받고 있다.
examples.translation: jigeumeun geonchukoesaeseo choegoui enjinieoro injeongbatgo itda. — Now she is recognized as the best engineer at an architecture company.

examples.text: 박소민 씨는 비행기 조종사다.
examples.translation: baksomin ssineun bihaenggi jojongsada. — Ms. Park Somin is an airplane pilot.

examples.text: 대학을 졸업한 후 처음에는 교사가 되었다.
examples.translation: daehageul joreopan hu cheoeumeneun gyosaga doeeotda. — After graduating from university, she first became a teacher.

examples.text: 하지만 비행기 조종사가 되기 위해 직장에 사표를 냈다.
examples.translation: hajiman bihaenggi jojongsaga doegi wihae jikjange sapyoreul naetda. — But she resigned from her job in order to become an airplane pilot.

examples.text: 쉬운 결정은 아니었지만, 자기 발전을 위해 사표를 내고 항공대학에 진학했다.
examples.translation: swiun gyeoljeongeun anieotjiman, jagi baljeoneul wihae sapyoreul naego hanggongdaehage jinhakaetda. — It was not an easy decision, but for her own development she resigned and entered an aviation university.

examples.text: 지금은 항공사에서 조종사로 근무하고 있다.
examples.translation: jigeumeun hanggongsaeseo jojongsaro geunmuhago itda. — Now she works as a pilot at an airline.

examples.text: 부모님은 결혼하라고 하지만 소민 씨는 아직 결혼하고 싶은 생각이 없다.
examples.translation: bumonimeun gyeolhonharago hajiman somin ssineun ajik gyeolhonhago sipeun saenggagi eopda. — Her parents tell her to marry, but Somin does not yet have the desire to marry.

examples.text: 현재의 생활에 만족한다.
examples.translation: hyeonjaeui saenghware manjokanda. — She is satisfied with her present life.

explanations.title: 북한에서는
explanations.body: In North Korea, the social status and roles of women radically changed after Korea was liberated from Japanese occupation in 1945. In 1946 North Korea passed a Sex Equality Law, and the 1972 constitution asserts that “women hold equal social status and rights with men.” Women are expected to participate fully in the labor force outside the home because of the country’s labor shortage. Women in North Korea are supposed to devote eight hours a day to work, eight hours to study (presumably, the study of 주체사상 and Kim Il Sung-ism), and eight hours to rest and sleep. Women who have three or more children work only six hours a day but receive a full, eight-hour workday salary.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): Woman of the Year
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a news article about a woman chosen as “Woman of the Year”; the book asks you to fill in a table in English (year mentioned / biographical information; the 1978 row is done for you). The book glosses 이루다: to achieve. The article is the book’s with the years spelled out (the book’s “이리여중·고” is written 이리여중과 이리여고); the English is mine.

examples.text: 올해의 여성 이길여 총장
examples.translation: olhaeui yeoseong igiryeo chongjang — Woman of the Year: President Lee Gilyeo

examples.text: 이길여 경원대 총장은 서울일보가 뽑은 올해의 여성이다.
examples.translation: igiryeo gyeongwondae chongjangeun seourilboga ppobeun olhaeui yeoseongida. — Gyeongwon University President Lee Gilyeo is the Woman of the Year chosen by the Seoul Daily.

examples.text: 이 총장은 천구백삼십이 년 전북 옥구에서 태어났다.
examples.translation: i chongjangeun cheongubaeksamsibi nyeon jeonbuk okgueseo taeeonatda. — President Lee was born in Okgu, Jeonbuk in 1932.

examples.text: 이리여중과 이리여고를 졸업하고 서울대 의대에 진학했다.
examples.translation: iriyeojunggwa iriyeogoreul joreopago seouldae uidaee jinhakaetda. — She graduated from Iri Girls’ Middle and High Schools and entered Seoul National University’s medical school.

examples.text: 그리고 천구백오십육 년 일본 니혼대에서 의학 박사학위를 받았다.
examples.translation: geurigo cheongubaegosibyuk nyeon ilbon nihondaeeseo uihak baksahagwireul badatda. — And in 1956 she received a doctorate in medicine from Nihon University in Japan.

examples.text: 천구백오십팔 년 이길여 산부인과를 열어 생활이 어려운 여성에게 무료 진료를 시작했다.
examples.translation: cheongubaegosippal nyeon igiryeo sanbuingwareul yeoreo saenghwari eoryeoun yeoseongege muryo jillyoreul sijakaetda. — In 1958 she opened the “Lee Gilyeo Obstetrics and Gynecology Clinic” and started free treatment for women in difficult circumstances.

examples.text: 천구백칠십팔 년 모든 재산을 털어 길의료재단을 만들었다.
examples.translation: cheongubaekchilsippal nyeon modeun jaesaneul teoreo giruiryojaedaneul mandeureotda. — In 1978 she gave up all her assets and created the Gil Medical Foundation.

examples.text: 천구백구십팔 년 가천 의대를 열고 이천 년에는 경원대 총장이 되었다.
examples.translation: cheongubaekgusippal nyeon gacheon uidaereul yeolgo icheon nyeoneneun gyeongwondae chongjangi doeeotda. — In 1998 she opened Gachon Medical School and in 2000 became president of Gyeongwon University.

examples.text: 현재 가천대 총장으로 재직중이다.
examples.translation: hyeonjae gacheondae chongjangeuro jaejikjungida. — She is currently serving as president of Gachon University.

rows: Received a doctorate in medicine from Nihon University in Japan
Opened an obstetrics and gynecology clinic and started free treatment for women in difficult circumstances
Donated her assets to found a medical foundation
Became president of Gyeongwon University in 2000 (opened Gachon Medical School in 1998); currently president of Gachon University

lessons.title: 544. Ch 43 · Grammar C: 반면(에), on the other hand
lessons.subtitle: 반면(에) · -(으)ㄴ/는 반면(에) · 백화점은 비싼 반면 품질이 좋다

explanations.title: A sentence connector
explanations.body: 반면(에) is a sentence connector used to connect two contrasting concepts or ideas, and it can be translated as on the other hand. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 백화점은 물건이 비쌉니다. 반면 품질이 좋습니다.
examples.translation: baekwajeomeun mulgeoni bissamnida. banmyeon pumjiri joseumnida. — The department store merchandise is expensive. On the other hand, its quality is good.

examples.text: 고속철도는 비쌉니다. 반면에 빠릅니다.
examples.translation: gosokcheoldoneun bissamnida. banmyeone ppareumnida. — An express train is expensive. On the other hand, it’s fast.

explanations.title: A verb connector too
explanations.body: Note that 반면(에) is placed at the beginning of the second sentence. 반면(에) can also be used as a verb connector (or conjunctive ending). In this case, 반면(에) is preceded by an attributive form. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 백화점은 물건이 비싼 반면 품질이 좋습니다.
examples.translation: baekwajeomeun mulgeoni bissan banmyeon pumjiri joseumnida. — The department store merchandise is expensive. On the other hand, its quality is good.

examples.text: 고속철도는 비싼 반면에 빠릅니다.
examples.translation: gosokcheoldoneun bissan banmyeone ppareumnida. — An express train is expensive. On the other hand, it’s fast.

examples.text: 승화는 수학을 잘하는 반면 영어는 잘 못해요.
examples.translation: seunghwaneun suhageul jalhaneun banmyeon yeongeoneun jal motaeyo. — Seunghwa is good at math. On the other hand, she is not good at English.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Speaking and listening): the model
explanations.body: Student A makes a sentence using –(으)ㄴ/는 반면(에), combines it with a sentence from Table A, and says the completed sentence aloud to Student B; Student B translates it back and then uses the cues from Table B. Table A: 이 아파트는 전망이 좋아요; 저는 고등학교 때 과학을 잘 했어요; 박 일병은 한국 영화를 자주 봐요. Table B: 백화점은 물건이 비싸요; 저는 운동을 잘 합니다; 송 상병은 주말에 늦잠을 자요. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 그 대학교는 좋은 반면 학비가 비싸요.
examples.translation: geu daehakgyoneun joeun banmyeon hakbiga bissayo. — That university is good; on the other hand, the tuition is expensive.

explanations.title: My completed sentences (mine)
explanations.body: My own contrasting halves for the six cues (the English is mine):

examples.text: 이 아파트는 전망이 좋은 반면 교통이 불편해요.
examples.translation: i apateuneun jeonmangi joeun banmyeon gyotongi bulpyeonhaeyo. — This apartment has a good view; on the other hand, the transportation is inconvenient.

examples.text: 저는 고등학교 때 과학을 잘한 반면 수학은 못했어요.
examples.translation: jeoneun godeunghakgyo ttae gwahageul jalhan banmyeon suhageun motaesseoyo. — In high school I was good at science; on the other hand, I was bad at math.

examples.text: 박 일병은 한국 영화를 자주 보는 반면 한국 드라마는 안 봐요.
examples.translation: bak ilbyeongeun hanguk yeonghwareul jaju boneun banmyeon hanguk deuramaneun an bwayo. — PFC Park often watches Korean movies; on the other hand, he does not watch Korean dramas.

examples.text: 백화점은 물건이 비싼 반면 품질이 좋아요.
examples.translation: baekwajeomeun mulgeoni bissan banmyeon pumjiri joayo. — Department stores have expensive goods; on the other hand, the quality is good.

examples.text: 저는 운동을 잘하는 반면 노래는 못해요.
examples.translation: jeoneun undongeul jalhaneun banmyeon noraeneun motaeyo. — I am good at sports; on the other hand, I can’t sing.

examples.text: 송 상병은 주말에 늦잠을 자는 반면 평일에는 일찍 일어나요.
examples.translation: song sangbyeongeun jumare neutjameul janeun banmyeon pyeongireneun iljjik ireonayo. — Cpl. Song sleeps in on weekends; on the other hand, he gets up early on weekdays.

explanations.title: More examples from the Core Vocabulary
explanations.body: The book’s examples for 반면(에) in the Core Vocabulary (the English is mine):

examples.text: 한국의 여름은 덥다. 반면에 겨울은 춥다.
examples.translation: hangugui yeoreumeun deopda. banmyeone gyeoureun chupda. — Korean summers are hot. On the other hand, winters are cold.

examples.text: 남자 농구는 계속 이긴 반면에 여자 농구는 계속 졌다.
examples.translation: namja nongguneun gyesok igin banmyeone yeoja nongguneun gyesok jeotda. — Men’s basketball kept winning, whereas women’s basketball kept losing.

lessons.title: 545. Ch 43 · Grammar D: the auxiliary verb –곤 하다 for common or routine occurrences
lessons.subtitle: -곤 하다 · -곤 했다 · 주말에는 도서관에 가곤 해요 · 어렸을 때 · 습관 · used to

explanations.title: Compare the two sentences
explanations.body: Compare the following two sentences and their English meanings (the English is the book’s).

examples.text: 저는 잠이 올 때 커피를 마셔요.
examples.translation: jeoneun jami ol ttae keopireul masyeoyo. — I drink coffee when I am sleepy.

examples.text: 저는 잠이 올 때 커피를 마시곤 해요.
examples.translation: jeoneun jami ol ttae keopireul masigon haeyo. — I normally drink coffee when I am sleepy.

explanations.title: What the second sentence implies
explanations.body: The first sentence implies that, without exception, the speaker drinks coffee when he is sleepy, whereas the second sentence implies that the speaker routinely (or more often than not) drinks coffee when he is sleepy. This is because of the presence of the auxiliary verb –곤 하다, which is used to express an action/event that commonly or routinely occurs or occurred. Thus, depending on the context, –곤 하다 can be loosely translated as commonly, routinely, regularly, generally, normally, habitually, usually, often, or more often than not. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 추울 때 따뜻한 코코아를 마시곤 해요.
examples.translation: chuul ttae ttatteutan kokoareul masigon haeyo. — I normally drink hot chocolate when it is cold.

examples.text: 주말에는 도서관에 가곤 해요.
examples.translation: jumareneun doseogwane gagon haeyo. — I routinely go to the library on weekends.

explanations.title: The past: –곤 했다
explanations.body: –곤 했다 is used for the past common or regular occurrences of an action or event. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 추울 때 따뜻한 코코아를 마시곤 했어요.
examples.translation: chuul ttae ttatteutan kokoareul masigon haesseoyo. — (In the past) I normally drank hot chocolate when it was cold. / I used to drink hot chocolate when it was cold.

examples.text: 주말에는 도서관에 가곤 했어요.
examples.translation: jumareneun doseogwane gagon haesseoyo. — (In the past) I routinely went to the library on weekends. / I would go to the library on weekends.

explanations.title: Conditions
explanations.body:
Here –곤 했다 can also be translated as used to or would. Note that –곤 하다 involves multiple occurrences of an action/event over a period of time; –곤 하다 does not work with a stative verb or with a one-time action/event.

Expressing an action/event that commonly or routinely occurs or occurred: action verb stem + 곤 하다/했다. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 아침에 구름이 끼면 오후에 비가 오곤 했다.
examples.translation: achime gureumi kkimyeon ohue biga ogon haetda. — When it got cloudy in the morning, it would rain in the afternoon.

examples.text: 방학 때 할아버지 댁에 가곤 했어요.
examples.translation: banghak ttae harabeoji daege gagon haesseoyo. — I used to go to my grandfather’s house during class break.

examples.text: 수미는 주말에 피아노를 치곤 해요.
examples.translation: sumineun jumare pianoreul chigon haeyo. — More often than not, Sumi plays the piano on weekends.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Writing): rewrite with –곤 하다
explanations.body: Rewrite the underlined parts of the following sentences using −곤 하다, and translate the sentence (the first is done for you). The sentences are the book’s; the rewrites and the English are mine.

rows: I used to go to the country farm on weekends.
I often go to the cherry blossom viewing at Jinhae every year.
On New Year’s Day, my grandfather used to give me New Year’s money.
In winter, the temperature often drops below zero.
가끔 인사동에 전통 차를 마시러 가요.
가끔 인사동에 전통 차를 마시러 가곤 해요.
I sometimes go to Insa-dong to drink traditional tea (habitually).
어렸을 때는 감기에 자주 걸리곤 했어요.
When I was young, I used to catch colds often.
제 프랑스 친구는 가끔 한국어로 말해요.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Reading): a college student’s passage
explanations.body: The following passage is written by a college student; the book asks you to write a title in Korean and to translate four underlined parts (a: 조부모님을 뵈러 시골에 가곤 했습니다; b: 낚시를 가곤 했습니다; c: 찌개를 끓여 주시곤 했습니다; d: 조부모님에 대해 이야기하곤 합니다; the book glosses 강가: riverside; 물고기: fish). The passage is the book’s; the English is mine. A title (mine): 시골에 계신 조부모님 (My grandparents in the countryside).

examples.text: 제가 어렸을 때 조부모님은 시골에 사셨습니다.
examples.translation: jega eoryeosseul ttae jobumonimeun sigore sasyeotseumnida. — When I was young, my grandparents lived in the countryside.

examples.text: 그래서 저는 부모님과 함께 주말에 조부모님을 뵈러 시골에 가곤 했습니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo jeoneun bumonimgwa hamkke jumare jobumonimeul boereo sigore gagon haetseumnida. — So I used to go to the countryside with my parents on weekends to see my grandparents.

examples.text: 저는 할아버지를 따라 동네 강가에 낚시를 가곤 했습니다.
examples.translation: jeoneun harabeojireul ttara dongne ganggae naksireul gagon haetseumnida. — I used to go fishing at the riverside in the village, following my grandfather.

examples.text: 집에 오면 할머니는 우리가 잡은 물고기로 맛있는 찌개를 끓여 주시곤 했습니다.
examples.translation: jibe omyeon halmeonineun uriga jabeun mulgogiro masinneun jjigaereul kkeuryeo jusigon haetseumnida. — When we came home, my grandmother used to boil a delicious stew with the fish we had caught.

examples.text: 지금은 두 분 다 돌아가셨습니다.
examples.translation: jigeumeun du bun da doragasyeotseumnida. — Now both of them have passed away.

examples.text: 가끔 부모님과 함께 조부모님에 대해 이야기하곤 합니다.
examples.translation: gakkeum bumonimgwa hamkke jobumonime daehae iyagihagon hamnida. — Sometimes I talk about my grandparents with my parents.

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Writing and reading): guess who it is
explanations.body: Think about three things you did routinely or habitually in the past, write a sentence on each with –곤 했다, give them to the teacher; the teacher mixes them up and the class guesses who wrote each. The book’s examples (the English is mine):

examples.text: 저는 고등학교에 다닐 때 주말마다 암벽등반을 하곤 했어요.
examples.translation: jeoneun godeunghakgyoe danil ttae jumalmada ambyeokdeungbaneul hagon haesseoyo. — When I attended high school, I used to go rock climbing every weekend.

examples.text: 어머니가 저녁 늦게까지 일하셔서 아버지가 요리를 하시곤 했어요.
examples.translation: eomeoniga jeonyeok neutgekkaji ilhasyeoseo abeojiga yorireul hasigon haesseoyo. — My mother worked until late in the evening, so my father used to cook.

examples.text: 형제가 많아서 어렸을 때 자주 싸우곤 했어요.
examples.translation: hyeongjega manaseo eoryeosseul ttae jaju ssaugon haesseoyo. — I had many siblings, so we used to fight often when we were young.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): occupational changes for women
explanations.body: The following news article excerpt is about occupational changes for women; the book asks you to fill in a table in English (causes of changes; jobs now held by women). The excerpt is the book’s; the English is mine.

examples.text: 사회에 진출하는 여성 늘어
examples.translation: sahoee jinchulhaneun yeoseong neureo — More women entering society

examples.text: 현대 사회에서 여성의 지위가 변화되고 있다.
examples.translation: hyeondae sahoeeseo yeoseongui jiwiga byeonhwadoego itda. — The status of women in modern society is changing.

examples.text: 집안일에 대한 부담이 줄어들고 교육을 받을 기회가 많아지면서 많은 여성이 사회활동에 참여하고 있다.
examples.translation: jibanire daehan budami jureodeulgo gyoyugeul badeul gihoega manajimyeonseo maneun yeoseongi sahoehwaldonge chamyeohago itda. — As the burden of housework decreases and opportunities to receive education increase, many women are participating in social activities.

examples.text: 그리고 여성들의 직업이 다양해지고 있다.
examples.translation: geurigo yeoseongdeurui jigeobi dayanghaejigo itda. — And women’s occupations are becoming diverse.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Listening, speaking and writing): Woman of the Year
explanations.body: You are a board member who has been chosen to select the “Woman of the Year”: you listen to the profiles of two women (Woman A: 이영애 씨; Woman B: 전수미 씨; audio), write the biographical information, educational background and volunteer work in English, exchange the information with a student from the other group in Korean, choose a winner and present the reasons. In step c you recommend a candidate for next year and write a short letter of recommendation in Korean. This is an audio and group activity and is left out.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with.

Now I am able to: identify major religions and beliefs in Korea; discuss volunteer work; understand the lives of foreigners in Korea and their typical concerns; discuss the social status and role of women in Korea; and talk about more occupations.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; ~ (도)중에/(–는/던) (도)중에 (in the middle of doing something); the sentence ending –(으)ㄴ/는데(요); 반면(에) (on the other hand; whereas; while); the auxiliary verb −곤 하다 for common or routine occurrences of an action/event; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 천주교 (天主敎), 대륙 (大陸), and 전문직 (專門職).

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (SMART Board) and Activity 2 (listening to three conversations between a man and a woman at a class reunion and noting the woman’s occupation and the reason) are audio and computer activities.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank. 아프리카, 엔지니어 and 유럽 are listed also as loan words; the last section lists the Sino-Korean related words of 대륙, 전문직 and 천주교 as the book gives them.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (100만 원 → 백만 원; 5명의 → 다섯 명의).

explanations.title: What Chapter 44 teaches (한국 사회의 여러 모습)
explanations.body:
Chapter 44, “Various Aspects of Korean Society”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations (traditional holidays, sports events and sports culture, job preferences) with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and describe social customs and trends related to major national holidays; identify and discuss sports events and sports culture; and compare and discuss how job preferences have changed.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; a summary of conjunctive endings related to time reference; an interrogative word followed by –든(지) (no matter what/who/when, etc.); ~까지(도) (even; to a degree that extends); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 최대 (最大), 동계 (冬季), and 안정 (安定).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 최대 (最大)
explanations.body: The first syllable 최 (最) is primarily used as a prefix indicating that the word containing it is in the superlative, as in 최신 (the latest; “the newest”), 최장 (the longest), 최강 (the strongest; the most powerful), 최후 (the last), and 최악 (the worst; “the evilest”). The second syllable 대 (大), which you have seen in 대학교 and 대가족, means big or large. Thus, the Sino-Korean word 최대 is a superlative and means the biggest or the largest. The book asks you to guess the meaning of 최고, 최저, 최상, 최하, 최다 and 최소 (my answers):

rows: the highest; the best; the top
the best; the finest; the top
the lowest; the worst; the bottom
the smallest; the least; the minimum

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 동계 (冬季)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means winter or wintertime and is normally used as an adjective modifying the noun that follows, as in 동계 올림픽 (Winter Olympics), 동계 훈련 (winter training), and 동계 방학 (a winter vacation). The first syllable 동 (冬) means winter, as in 동지 (winter solstice), 춘하추동 (four seasons; “spring, summer, fall, winter”), 동복 (winter clothes; winter wear), and 동면 (hibernation; “winter sleep”). The second syllable 계 (季) means season, as in 사계절 (four seasons). Thus the literal meaning of the word is “winter season,” and the word is followed by a noun indicating an event. To express other seasonal events, Koreans use 춘계 (春季) meaning spring or springtime, 하계 (夏季) meaning summer or summertime, and 추계 (秋季) meaning fall, as in 하계 올림픽 (summer Olympics), 춘계 소풍 (a spring picnic), and 하계 모임 (a summer meet; a summer gathering).

rows: a summer meet; a summer gathering

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 안정 (安定)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means stability or calm, as in 안정감 (sense of stability), 안정시키다 (to stabilize), and 안정되다 (to be stabilized). The first syllable 안 (安) means serene, tranquil, or comfort, as in 안녕하다 (to be fine; “to be serene and comfortable”), 안심하다 (to feel relieved; to feel easy; “to have a serene mind”), 안착 (a safe arrival), and 편안하다 (to be peaceful; to be calm; “to be comfortable and calm”). The second syllable 정 (定) means set, fix(ed), settle(d), or decide(d), as in 정가 (a set price; a fixed price), 정기총회 (a regular general meeting), and 정식 (a meal on a fixed menu). Thus the literal meaning of the word 안정 is “serene and fixed.”

explanations.body: The following article is about two traditional Korean holidays, Lunar New Year and Chuseok. (The English is mine; the book gives none. The book’s footnote: ~화 (化) is much like the English suffix -ization or -fication, as in 간소화 [simplification] and 세계화 [globalization].)

examples.text: 설과 추석은 한국의 최대 민속 명절이다.
examples.translation: seolgwa chuseogeun hangugui choedae minsok myeongjeorida. — Lunar New Year and Chuseok are Korea’s biggest traditional folk holidays.

examples.text: 설과 추석을 맞아서 많은 사람이 부모님이 계시는 고향을 방문한다.
examples.translation: seolgwa chuseogeul majaseo maneun sarami bumonimi gyesineun gohyangeul bangmunhanda. — On the occasion of Lunar New Year and Chuseok, many people visit their hometowns where their parents are.

examples.text: 따라서 고속도로는 긴 귀성 차량 행렬과 밀린 차량 때문에 교통 정체가 심하다.
examples.translation: ttaraseo gosokdoroneun gin gwiseong charyang haengnyeolgwa millin charyang ttaemune gyotong jeongchega simhada. — Therefore, the highways have heavy traffic jams because of the long lines of vehicles of people going home and the backed-up vehicles.

examples.text: 김미진 씨네는 명절 때 시골에 사시는 부모님께서 서울로 올라오신다.

examples.text: 그래서 미진 씨네는 고속도로에서 교통 체증을 겪지 않아도 된다.

examples.text: 또, 미진 씨는 음식을 준비하는 부담을 덜기 위해서 제사 음식을 인터넷으로 주문한다.

explanations.title: 한국에서는
explanations.body:
설날 (Lunar New Year’s Day) is the first day of the lunar calendar, and it generally falls on the day of the second new moon after the winter solstice. 추석 (Harvest Festival; “Autumn Evening”) is the 15th day of the 8th month of the lunar calendar. These two holidays are the most important traditional holidays in Korea, for on these days Koreans have long celebrated the New Year and newly harvested crops (respectively) with their extended family and the spirits of their deceased ancestors. On the mornings of these holidays, Koreans perform ancestral worship rituals. They often visit the tombs of their ancestors to clean the area around the tombs, and they leave offerings of food and drink.

Around these holidays, millions of Koreans are on the move, traveling to and from their hometowns where their parents reside. Thus, the highways become very congested and driving times double or even triple. Radio stations broadcast special traffic updates for motorists during these times of massive exodus from the cities. As part of a new trend, some elderly parents who live in smaller provinces are choosing to travel to their children’s homes in cities instead of their children traveling to see them.

It is increasingly common nowadays for holiday food preparation to be divided among participating siblings, who bring their own dishes to share with the rest of their family. Catering services are gaining more popularity, especially among younger housewives.

examples.translation: chuseok yeonhyue yeohaengeul gagi ttaemune beolsseo i ju jeone seongmyohaetgo keun hyeongnimdaegedo miri gaseo insareul deuryeotda. — “Because I am traveling over the Chuseok holiday, I already visited the ancestral graves two weeks ago and went ahead of time to my eldest brother’s house to pay my respects.”

rows: 1. Translate the title of the article into English.
“Changed Chuseok Scenes” (or “The Changing Face of Chuseok”)
2. What is Mr. Kim Sangjin planning to do during this year’s Chuseok?
Travel to China with his whole family
3. What are the two reasons for his plan?
His youngest son will soon enter the military; his eldest daughter will marry in November (so it is the last overseas trip the family can take together)
4. What two things did Mr. Kim do in advance?
Visited the ancestral graves two weeks earlier; went to his eldest brother’s house early to pay his respects

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): an online news article
explanations.body: The following article is from an online news site. The book asks you to circle the best title and to list three supporting facts. The article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out; the English and the answers are mine.

examples.text: 명절 풍속이 바뀌고 있다.
examples.translation: myeongjeol pungsogi bakkwigo itda. — Holiday customs are changing.

examples.text: 명절 때 직접 음식을 하는 대신 전문업체에 주문하는 가정이 늘고 있다.
examples.translation: myeongjeol ttae jikjeop eumsigeul haneun daesin jeonmuneopchee jumunhaneun gajeongi neulgo itda. — The number of households that, instead of making the food themselves at holidays, order from a specialized company is increasing.

examples.text: 비용이 이십만 원쯤 들기 때문에 큰 부담이 되지는 않는다.
examples.translation: biyongi isimman wonjjeum deulgi ttaemune keun budami doejineun anneunda. — Because the cost is about 200,000 won, it is not a big burden.

examples.text: 인터넷 주문도 가능하다.
examples.translation: inteonet jumundo ganeunghada. — Internet orders are possible too.

examples.text: 또, 고속도로가 복잡해서 귀성을 포기하는 사람도 늘고 있다.
examples.translation: tto, gosokdoroga bokjapaeseo gwiseongeul pogihaneun saramdo neulgo itda. — Also, the number of people who give up going home because the highways are crowded is increasing.

examples.text: 이들은 고향에 가는 대신 해외여행을 가기도 한다.
examples.translation: ideureun gohyange ganeun daesin haeoeyeohaengeul gagido handa. — Instead of going to their hometowns, they sometimes go on overseas trips.

examples.text: 대전시의 한 여행사에 따르면 여름 휴가철 성수기보다 추석 연휴에 해외여행을 떠나는 사람이 더 많다고 한다.
examples.translation: daejeonsiui han yeohaengsae ttareumyeon yeoreum hyugacheol seongsugiboda chuseok yeonhyue haeoeyeohaengeul tteonaneun sarami deo mantago handa. — According to a travel agency in Daejeon City, more people leave on overseas trips during the Chuseok holiday than in the summer vacation peak season.

examples.text: 그리고 인기 해외여행 상품은 한두 달 전에 예약이 다 끝난다고 한다.
examples.translation: geurigo ingi haeoeyeohaeng sangpumeun handu dal jeone yeyagi da kkeunnandago handa. — And they say popular overseas travel packages are fully booked one or two months in advance.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: 1. The best title (of the book’s four choices: Traveling During Traditional Holidays; New Trends in Celebrating Traditional Holidays; Today’s Generation and Unique Lifestyle; Popularity of Virtual Shrines): New Trends in Celebrating Traditional Holidays. 2. Three supporting facts:

rows: More households order holiday food from a specialized company instead of cooking it (about 200,000 won, internet orders possible)
More people give up going to their hometowns because the highways are crowded and go on overseas trips instead
More people leave for overseas trips during Chuseok than in the summer peak season, and popular tour packages are booked one or two months ahead

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 길거리 응원 “대~한민국”
explanations.body: 길거리 응원 (street cheering) has been a prominent feature of Korean cheering culture since the 2002 FIFA World Cup. During that event, when the Korean soccer team advanced to the semifinals, 2.4 million Koreans gathered on the streets of major cities and rooted for the Korean team while watching the game on giant TV screens. They all wore red T-shirts and chanted 대~한민국, immediately followed by rhythmic claps. Since that historic moment, Koreans have been organizing street cheering for big sports events such as 월드컵, 올림픽, and the World Baseball Classic. This phenomenon has become a part of contemporary Korean culture. (The book has a link to a YTN video of 길거리 응원, which is left out.)

explanations.title: 북한에서는: 북한 스포츠
explanations.body: North Korea’s most popular participatory sports are soccer, basketball, and table tennis. North Koreans organize school, factory, and cooperative farm sports teams and enjoy leisure time games. Soccer is the most popular sport for participants and spectators. North Koreans especially remember how in 1966 the North Korean soccer team miraculously advanced to the quarterfinals during the FIFA World Cup in England. However, the women’s soccer team has been more successful on the international stage than the men’s, qualifying for the 1999 and 2003 FIFA Women’s World Cup. In 1999, the team defeated Denmark during the group stage, and in 2003 defeated Nigeria, the champion team from Africa. Boxing and marathon events are also popular spectator sports. There are North Korean professional boxing and wrestling leagues.

rows: Which sports events Koreans are most interested in
2. A short summary of the results

Baseball ranked first (62.0%), followed by soccer (52.6%) and golf (30.9%); then swimming (27%), basketball (26.9%) and eSports (26.3%); volleyball was 10th (21.6%). Among ages 15–29, soccer was first (53.2%), baseball second (50.8%) and eSports third (39.7%)
3. Which age group showed the highest interest in eSports, and why?
The younger generations (thirties and below, especially the Millennials); they are used to using online media, and eSports are easy to take part in and watch

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Listening and reading): a sports news article
explanations.body: In this activity you learn about a sports event through two sources of news. In step a, you read the following excerpt from a newspaper sports section and fill in a table in English (type of event; event result; what fans did). The excerpt is the book’s with the numbers and letters spelled out (the title’s “!” is dropped; “H조” is 에이치 조; the book’s quoted chants are written without the quotation marks and the wave sign); the English is mine.

lessons.title: 554. Ch 44 · Grammar A: interrogative word + –든(지), no matter who/what/when
lessons.subtitle: -든지 · -든 · 누구를 만나든지 · 어디서 살든지 · 무엇을 하든지 · 어떻게 하든지

explanations.title: Expressing “no matter who/whom/what/when,” etc.
explanations.body: Recall the conjunctive ending –든지 you learned about in Chapter 22. This conjunctive ending is used to express an alternative option, as in 주말에 친구를 만나든지 영화를 봅니다 (I see my friends or see a movie on weekends). However, when the conjunctive ending –든지 is preceded by an interrogative word, such as 누구, 무엇, 언제, 어디, and 어떻게, it expresses no matter who/whom/what/when/where/how. For example:

examples.text: 주말에 친구를 만나든지 영화를 봅니다.
examples.translation: jumare chingureul mannadeunji yeonghwareul bomnida. — I see my friends or see a movie on weekends.

examples.text: 무슨 언어를 배우든지 열심히 배우세요.
examples.translation: museun eoneoreul baeudeunji yeolsimhi baeuseyo. — No matter what language you learn, please learn (the language) diligently.

examples.text: 언제 미국에 오시든지 저희 집에 들러주세요.
examples.translation: eonje miguge osideunji jeohui jibe deulleojuseyo. — No matter when you come to the States, please visit my home.

explanations.title: The pattern
explanations.body: 지 in 든지 can be omitted (the book writes 든(지)). “no matter who/whom/what/when/where/how”: interrogative word + … + –든(지). More examples (the English is the book’s; I write 든지 in full):

examples.text: 누구를 만나든지 친절하게 대하세요.
examples.translation: nugureul mannadeunji chinjeolhage daehaseyo. — No matter whom we meet, please treat them kindly.

examples.text: 어디서 살든지 행복하세요.
examples.translation: eodiseo saldeunji haengbokaseyo. — Be happy wherever you live.

examples.text: 무엇을 하든지 열심히 하면 돼.
examples.translation: mueoseul hadeunji yeolsimhi hamyeon dwae. — Work hard, no matter what you do.

examples.text: 어떻게 하든지 이 일을 끝내기만 하세요.
examples.translation: eotteoke hadeunji i ireul kkeunnaegiman haseyo. — Finish this work, no matter how you do it.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Writing): four sentences
explanations.body: Using the words from the table (interrogative words 누구/누가, 무엇, 어디(에/서), 언제, 어떻게, 무슨 ~, 어떤 ~; verbs 읽다, 먹다, 만나다, 운동하다, 근무하다, 일하다), write four sentences in Korean that express “no matter who/whom/what/where,” etc. and translate them into English. The book’s model is 어디서 일하든지 열심히 노력하세요 (Make an effort, no matter where you work). My own sentences (the English is mine):

examples.text: 어디서 일하든지 열심히 노력하세요.
examples.translation: eodiseo ilhadeunji yeolsimhi noryeokaseyo. — Make an effort, no matter where you work.

examples.text: 누가 읽든지 이 책은 재미있을 거예요.
examples.translation: nuga ikdeunji i chaegeun jaemiisseul geoyeyo. — No matter who reads it, this book will be fun.

examples.text: 무엇을 먹든지 건강하게 드세요.
examples.translation: mueoseul meokdeunji geonganghage deuseyo. — No matter what you eat, eat healthily.

examples.text: 어디에서 만나든지 좋아요.
examples.translation: eodieseo mannadeunji joayo. — It’s fine no matter where we meet.

examples.text: 언제 운동하든지 준비 운동을 먼저 하세요.
examples.translation: eonje undonghadeunji junbi undongeul meonjeo haseyo. — No matter when you exercise, do warm-up exercises first.

examples.text: 어떻게 근무하든지 안전이 가장 중요합니다.
examples.translation: eotteoke geunmuhadeunji anjeoni gajang jungyohamnida. — No matter how you work, safety is the most important.

examples.text: 무슨 일을 하든지 최선을 다하세요.
examples.translation: museun ireul hadeunji choeseoneul dahaseyo. — No matter what job you do, do your best.

examples.text: 어떤 사람이든지 처음에는 서투릅니다.
examples.translation: eotteon saramideunji cheoeumeneun seotureumnida. — No matter what kind of person, everyone is clumsy at first.

lessons.title: 555. Ch 44 · Grammar B: ~까지(도), even
lessons.subtitle: ~까지 · ~까지도 · 디저트까지 먹었어요 · 게다가 핸드백까지 샀어요 · 집들이 · 칭찬

explanations.title: Recall ~까지
explanations.body: Recall the meanings of ~까지. When attached to a noun indicating time or place, ~까지 can be translated as until, up to, or by. When attached to a noun indicating place, it can be translated as (up) to or as far as. For example:

examples.text: 어젯밤에 열두 시까지 숙제 했어요.
examples.translation: eojetbame yeoldu sikkaji sukje haesseoyo. — I did homework until 12 o’clock last night.

examples.text: 여기서 학교까지 삼십 분 걸려요.
examples.translation: yeogiseo hakgyokkaji samsip bun geollyeoyo. — It takes 30 minutes (to travel) from here to school.

explanations.title: ~까지 for “even”
explanations.body: However, when ~까지 is attached to a noun other than one indicating time or place, it is used to stress an extreme or highly unlikely condition, and it can be translated as even or to a degree that extends. For example:

examples.text: 배가 너무 고파서 디저트까지 다 먹었어요.
examples.translation: baega neomu gopaseo dijeoteukkaji da meogeosseoyo. — I was so hungry I even ate dessert.

examples.text: 다음 주 숙제까지 했습니다.
examples.translation: daeum ju sukjekkaji haetseumnida. — I even did next week’s homework (not to mention this week’s homework).

explanations.title: ~까지도
explanations.body: In these instances, ~까지 is interchangeable with ~까지도. For example:

examples.text: 배가 너무 고파서 디저트까지도 다 먹었어요.
examples.translation: baega neomu gopaseo dijeoteukkajido da meogeosseoyo. — I was so hungry I even ate dessert.

examples.text: 다음 주 숙제까지도 했습니다.
examples.translation: daeum ju sukjekkajido haetseumnida. — I even did next week’s homework.

explanations.title: More examples (“even”: ~까지(도))
explanations.body: The English is the book’s.

examples.text: 어린 아이들까지도 거리에 나와서 한국 팀을 응원했어요.
examples.translation: eorin aideulkkajido georie nawaseo hanguk timeul eungwonhaesseoyo. — Even young children came out to the street to cheer for the Korean team.

examples.text: 어제 백화점에서 옷이랑 신발을 샀어요. 게다가 핸드백까지 샀어요.
examples.translation: eoje baekwajeomeseo osirang sinbareul sasseoyo. gedaga haendeubaekkaji sasseoyo. — I bought clothes and shoes at the department store yesterday. And I even bought a purse.

examples.text: 하루 종일 요리하고 설거지했어요. 게다가 집 청소까지 했어요.
examples.translation: haru jongil yorihago seolgeojihaesseoyo. gedaga jip cheongsokkaji haesseoyo. — All day long I cooked and washed the dishes. In addition, I even cleaned the house.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading): a journal entry about a housewarming party
explanations.body: The following journal entry is about a housewarming party hosted by So-yeon (소연). The passage is the book’s; the English and the answers are mine.

examples.text: 최근에 새집으로 이사를 해서 어제 집들이를 했다.
examples.translation: choegeune saejibeuro isareul haeseo eoje jipdeurireul haetda. — I recently moved into a new house, so I had a housewarming party yesterday.

examples.text: 친구들을 많이 초대했기 때문에 하루 종일 아주 바빴다.
examples.translation: chingudeureul mani chodaehaetgi ttaemune haru jongil aju bappatda. — Because I invited many friends, I was very busy all day.

examples.text: 아침 일찍부터 집 안 청소를 하고 음식을 준비했다.
examples.translation: achim iljjikbuteo jip an cheongsoreul hago eumsigeul junbihaetda. — From early in the morning I cleaned the house and prepared food.

examples.text: 그리고 예쁘게 집안 장식까지 했다.
examples.translation: geurigo yeppeuge jiban jangsikkaji haetda. — And I even decorated the house prettily.

examples.text: 음식도 여러 가지 떡과 불고기와 잡채 그리고 파전까지도 준비했다.
examples.translation: eumsikdo yeoreo gaji tteokgwa bulgogiwa japchae geurigo pajeonkkajido junbihaetda. — As for food, I prepared various rice cakes, bulgogi, japchae and even green onion pancakes.

examples.text: 힘들었지만 친구들이 음식을 맛있게 먹어서 기분이 좋았다.
examples.translation: himdeureotjiman chingudeuri eumsigeul masitge meogeoseo gibuni joatda. — It was hard, but I felt good because my friends ate the food with relish.

rows: Cleaned the house; decorated the house
Various rice cakes (떡); bulgogi; japchae; green onion pancakes
그리고 예쁘게 집안 장식까지 했다 = “And I even decorated the house prettily.” 파전까지도 준비했다 = “(I prepared …) and even green onion pancakes.”

explanations.title: Follow-up 5 (Speaking): Let’s give compliments!
explanations.body: Each student writes the names of four people both partners know on index cards and thinks of compliments for each. Partner A states a compliment, Partner B states another compliment, and Partner A adds a final compliment using ~까지(도). The book’s model is A: 김 일병은 노래를 잘해요. B: 그리고 춤도 잘 춰요. A: 그리고/게다가 요리까지 잘해요. My own second round (the English is mine):

examples.text: 김 일병은 노래를 잘해요.
examples.translation: gim ilbyeongeun noraereul jalhaeyo. — PFC Kim sings well.

examples.text: 그리고 춤도 잘 춰요.
examples.translation: geurigo chumdo jal chwoyo. — And he dances well too.

examples.text: 그리고 요리까지 잘해요.
examples.translation: geurigo yorikkaji jalhaeyo. — And he even cooks well.

examples.text: 김 일병은 운동을 잘해요.
examples.translation: gim ilbyeongeun undongeul jalhaeyo. — PFC Kim is good at sports.

examples.text: 그리고 공부도 열심히 해요.
examples.translation: geurigo gongbudo yeolsimhi haeyo. — And he studies hard too.

examples.text: 게다가 친구들까지 잘 도와줘요.
examples.translation: gedaga chingudeulkkaji jal dowajwoyo. — On top of that, he even helps his friends well.

explanations.body: Follow-up 4 (listening to four conversations between two friends, transcribing ~까지 and translating the sentences that contain ~까지) is an audio activity; the pair activity of Follow-up 5 is a speaking game.

explanations.title: 한국어에는: ~원, ~가, ~사
explanations.body: The Korean suffixes ~원 (員), ~가 (家), or ~사 (士/師) are commonly used to refer to a person who is working in a certain occupation. When referring to a specific job category, ~원 usually denotes a person who is working as a member of an organization or group. Some examples of this usage are 회사원 (a company employee), 공무원 (a public servant), 연구원 (a researcher), etc. ~가 is often used to describe a person who works as a professional (especially in the arts) or has expert knowledge or skills in a certain field. Examples are 음악가 (a musician), 화가 (a painter), 사업가 (a businessman), etc. ~사 often describes an officially certified professional in a certain field, such as 의사 (a doctor), 교사 (a teacher), 약사 (a pharmacist), or 변호사 (a lawyer).

lessons.title: 557. Ch 44 · Activities C: job preferences, then and now
lessons.subtitle: 직업 선호도 · 교사 · 간호사 · 군인 · 도배사 · 기성세대 · 청년 · 창업

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a survey of high school students
explanations.body: The following news article is about a survey of high school students. In step a the book asks you to choose a fitting title from four (요즘 학생들이 선호하는 직업; 신세대의 연예인 선호 이유; 과거 고등학생들이 선호한 직업; 연봉이 높은 인기 직업), in step b to fill in a table of the top three jobs today and 20 years ago (the first, teacher, is given), and in step c to translate the underlined part. The article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (its slashes between job names are read as 이나); the English and the answers are mine, and I translate every sentence.

examples.text: 교육부와 한국직업연구원이 전국 고등학생 칠천백이십사 명에게 직업 선호도를 조사했다.
examples.translation: gyoyukbuwa hangukjigeobyeonguwoni jeonguk godeunghaksaeng chilcheonbaegisipsa myeongege jigeop seonhodoreul josahaetda. — The Ministry of Education and the Korea Research Institute for Vocational Education and Training surveyed 7,124 high school students nationwide on job preferences.

examples.text: 이 결과에 따르면 학생들이 가장 희망하는 직업은 교사였고, 그다음이 간호사였다.
examples.translation: i gyeolgwae ttareumyeon haksaengdeuri gajang huimanghaneun jigeobeun gyosayeotgo, geudaeumi ganhosayeotda. — According to this result, the job students hoped for most was teacher, followed by nurse.

examples.text: 학생이 희망하는 직업 삼 위는 군인으로, 일 위에서 삼 위는 작년과 변함이 없었다.
examples.translation: haksaengi huimanghaneun jigeop sam wineun gunineuro, il wieseo sam wineun jangnyeongwa byeonhami eopseotda. — Third place among jobs students hope for was soldier, and first to third places were unchanged from last year.

examples.text: 그 밖에 경찰관이나 수사관, 컴퓨터공학자나 소프트웨어개발자, 뷰티디자이너 등이 높은 순위였다.
examples.translation: geu bakke gyeongchalgwanina susagwan, keompyuteogonghakjana sopeuteuweeogaebalja, byutidijaineo deungi nopeun sunwiyeotda. — In addition, police officer or investigator, computer scientist or software developer, and beauty designer ranked high.

examples.text: 이들 직업을 선택한 이유를 묻는 질문에 본인이 하고 싶어하는 일이기 때문이라고 대답했다.
examples.translation: ideul jigeobeul seontaekan iyureul munneun jilmune bonini hago sipeohaneun irigi ttaemunirago daedapaetda. — Asked the reason for choosing these jobs, they answered that it is because it is work they themselves want to do.

examples.text: 이십 년 전에는 학생들이 장래 직업으로 의사를 가장 많이 선택했었고, 이 위와 삼 위는 각각 교수와 변호사였었다.
examples.translation: isip nyeon jeoneneun haksaengdeuri jangnae jigeobeuro uisareul gajang mani seontaekaesseotgo, i wiwa sam wineun gakgak gyosuwa byeonhosayeosseotda. — Twenty years ago, students chose doctor most as a future job, and second and third places were professor and lawyer, respectively.

examples.text: 한편 졸업 후 창업을 희망하는 학생은 꾸준히 늘어나는 것으로 조사됐다.
examples.translation: hanpyeon joreop hu changeobeul huimanghaneun haksaengeun kkujunhi neureonaneun geoseuro josadwaetda. — Meanwhile, the survey found that the number of students hoping to start a business after graduation is steadily increasing.

explanations.title: The answers (mine)
explanations.body: a. Title: 요즘 학생들이 선호하는 직업 (Jobs students prefer these days).

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading and speaking): factors in choosing a job
explanations.body: In this activity you read an article that presents a personal opinion on the current trends and factors young people consider when choosing a job. In step a you rank, from most to least important to you, a list of factors and share your reasons with classmates (my glosses; the ranking is your own):

rows: aptitude and talent for the work
stability such as a guaranteed retirement age

explanations.title: The article written by a wallpaper installer (도배사), paragraph [1]
explanations.body: The book glosses 가치: value; 건설: construction; 기술: skill, technology; 기준: standards; 틀: frame. The article is the book’s with the quotation marks of the loan words ‘클리어(완수)’, ‘미션(과제)’ and ‘옵션(선택)’ read out as 클리어, 곧 완수 and so on; the English is mine.

examples.text: 나는 건설 현장에서 일하는 도배사이다.
examples.translation: naneun geonseol hyeonjangeseo ilhaneun dobaesaida. — I am a wallpaper installer who works at construction sites.

examples.text: 최근 건설 현장에는 나뿐만 아니라 다양한 분야에 다양한 이유로 일을 하는 젊은이들이 많다.
examples.translation: choegeun geonseol hyeonjangeneun nappunman anira dayanghan bunyae dayanghan iyuro ireul haneun jeolmeunideuri manta. — Recently, at construction sites there are many young people, not only me, working in various fields for various reasons.

examples.text: 부모님을 따라 시작한 경우도 있고, 대기업에 다니다가 퇴사하고 마음 편한 일을 하고 싶어 시작한 사람도 있다.
examples.translation: bumonimeul ttara sijakan gyeongudo itgo, daegieobe danidaga toesahago maeum pyeonhan ireul hago sipeo sijakan saramdo itda. — There are cases of starting by following their parents, and there are also people who left a large company and started because they wanted to do work that is easy on the mind.

examples.text: 나의 경우에는 취업할 때 여러 선택지가 있었다.
examples.translation: naui gyeongueneun chwieopal ttae yeoreo seontaekjiga isseotda. — In my case, I had several options when I got a job.

examples.text: 하지만 수량과 품질로 명확하게 인정받을 수 있는, 오로지 기술로만 인정받을 수 있는 직업을 택하고 싶었다.
examples.translation: hajiman suryanggwa pumjillo myeonghwakage injeongbadeul su inneun, oroji gisulloman injeongbadeul su inneun jigeobeul taekago sipeotda. — But I wanted to choose a job in which I could be clearly recognized by quantity and quality, recognized solely by skill.

examples.text: 높은 연봉, 안정성, 사회적 지위 등 많은 사람들이 중요하게 생각하는 기준이 아니라 나만의 기준을 세워서 직업을 선택하고 싶었다.
examples.translation: nopeun yeonbong, anjeongseong, sahoejeok jiwi deung maneun saramdeuri jungyohage saenggakaneun gijuni anira namanui gijuneul sewoseo jigeobeul seontaekago sipeotda. — I wanted to choose a job by setting my own standards, not the standards many people consider important, such as high salary, stability and social status.

examples.text: 그렇게 찾은 직업이 도배사였다.
examples.translation: geureoke chajeun jigeobi dobaesayeotda. — The job I found that way was wallpaper installer.

examples.text: 과거와 다르게 많은 청년들이 다양한 선택을 하는 이유는, 사회가 정해놓은 인생의 틀을 그대로 따라갈지 그러지 않을지의 차이일 것이다.
examples.translation: gwageowa dareuge maneun cheongnyeondeuri dayanghan seontaegeul haneun iyuneun, sahoega jeonghaenoeun insaengui teureul geudaero ttaragalji geureoji aneuljiui chaiil geosida. — The reason many young people make various choices, unlike in the past, is probably the difference in whether they follow the frame of life set by society as it is or not.

examples.text: 대학 졸업, 취업, 결혼, 출산, 육아가 기성세대에게는 클리어, 곧 완수해야 하는 하나의 미션, 곧 과제였다면, 요즘의 청년들에게는 하나의 옵션, 곧 선택일 뿐이다.
examples.translation: daehak joreop, chwieop, gyeolhon, chulsan, yugaga giseongsedaeegeneun keullieo, got wansuhaeya haneun hanaui misyeon, got gwajeyeotdamyeon, yojeumui cheongnyeondeuregeneun hanaui opsyeon, got seontaegil ppunida. — If graduating from university, getting a job, marriage, childbirth and child-rearing were a ‘mission’, something to ‘clear’ (that is, to complete), for the older generation, for young people today they are only an ‘option’ (that is, a choice).

examples.text: 그렇기 때문에 결혼과 출산, 육아하기 좋은 안정적인 직업을 고를 수도 있지만, 그것들을 하지 않을 사람들은 좀 더 자유로운 선택을 하기도 한다.
examples.translation: geureoki ttaemune gyeolhongwa chulsan, yugahagi joeun anjeongjeogin jigeobeul goreul sudo itjiman, geugeotdeureul haji aneul saramdeureun jom deo jayuroun seontaegeul hagido handa. — That is why they may pick a stable job good for marriage, childbirth and child-rearing, but people who will not do those things sometimes make a freer choice.

examples.text: 요즘 청년들은 스스로 중요하게 생각하는 믿음과 가치를 토대로 직업을 선택한다.
examples.translation: yojeum cheongnyeondeureun seuseuro jungyohage saenggakaneun mideumgwa gachireul todaero jigeobeul seontaekanda. — Young people today choose jobs based on the beliefs and values they consider important themselves.

examples.text: 하지만 이런 생각을 이해하지 못하고 본인만의 기준으로 좋은 직업과 안 좋은 직업을 나누는 기성세대가 많다.
examples.translation: hajiman ireon saenggageul ihaehaji motago boninmanui gijuneuro joeun jigeopgwa an joeun jigeobeul nanuneun giseongsedaega manta. — But there are many in the older generation who do not understand this thinking and divide ‘good jobs’ and ‘bad jobs’ by their own standards.

examples.text: 내게도 좋은 대학 나왔으면 공무원을 하지 왜 도배를 하느냐는 얘기를 하는 사람들도 있다.
examples.translation: naegedo joeun daehak nawasseumyeon gongmuwoneul haji wae dobaereul haneunyaneun yaegireul haneun saramdeuldo itda. — There are even people who tell me, “If you graduated from a good university, you should be a public servant; why do wallpapering?”

examples.text: 언젠가는 청년들이 다양한 생각과 판단을 통해 직업을 택한다는 것과, 그 안에서 만족감을 느끼고 있음을 이해 받는 날이 오기를 바란다.
examples.translation: eonjenganeun cheongnyeondeuri dayanghan saenggakgwa pandaneul tonghae jigeobeul taekandaneun geotgwa, geu aneseo manjokgameul neukkigo isseumeul ihae banneun nari ogireul baranda. — I hope the day comes when it is understood that young people choose jobs through various thoughts and judgments and feel satisfaction within them.

rows: 1. Examples of different motivations for working at a construction site
Following their parents into the work; leaving a big company to do work that is easier on the mind
2. The author’s criteria, and how they differed

She wanted a job in which she could be recognized clearly by quantity and quality, solely by skill; she set her own standards instead of the ones many people value, such as high salary, stability and social status
3. Today’s young generation vs. previous generations
Today: marriage, childbirth and child-rearing are just options (a choice); Previous: they were a mission to complete (the life frame set by society)
4. The older generations’ viewpoint the author criticizes
Dividing jobs into “good” and “bad” by their own standards without understanding young people’s thinking (e.g., “you went to a good university, so be a public servant”)
That the day comes when it is understood that young people choose jobs through various thoughts and judgments and feel satisfaction in them

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (SMART Board), Activity 2 (listening to three narrations about the speakers’ desired jobs, the parents’ recommendations and the reasons) and Activity 4 (listening to two narrations about each speaker’s dream job, previous occupation and current occupation, exchanging the information in Korean, and writing and presenting what you want to do after leaving the military or ten years from now) are audio, pair and group activities; the book’s Follow-up 2 on this chapter’s Topic C (listening to three narrations about job preferences of high school students) is audio too.

lessons.title: 558. Ch 44 · Grammar C: summary of conjunctive endings for time reference
lessons.subtitle: –기 전에 · –(으)ㄴ 후에 · –(으)ㄹ 때 · –(으)ㄹ 때마다 · –(으)ㄹ 때부터 · –(으)ㄹ 때까지 · –는 동안 · –(으)면서 · –자마자

explanations.title: The conjunctive endings
explanations.body: You have learned quite a few conjunctive endings that are used for time reference. The book revisits and summarizes them through several activities. First, review the conjunctive endings provided in the table below (“Equivalent Feature Used with Noun” is the noun construction with the same meaning):

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Speaking and listening): saying it one after another
explanations.body: Sit in a circle; the teacher says a sentence about a daily routine, and each student in turn adds a sentence building on the previous one, using a time-reference conjunctive ending each time. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 아침에 여섯 시에 일어납니다.
examples.translation: achime yeoseot sie ireonamnida. — I get up at six in the morning.

examples.text: 일어나자마자 샤워를 합니다.
examples.translation: ireonajamaja syaworeul hamnida. — As soon as I get up, I take a shower.

examples.text: 샤워를 하는 동안에 노래를 부릅니다.
examples.translation: syaworeul haneun dongane noraereul bureumnida. — While I take a shower, I sing.

examples.text: 노래를 부르면서 씻습니다.
examples.translation: noraereul bureumyeonseo ssitseumnida. — I wash while singing.

explanations.title: One example of each ending (mine)
explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

rows: I brush my teeth before going to bed.
I eat lunch after class ends.
I read a book when I am bored.
Whenever it rains, I eat green onion pancakes.
I have liked soccer since I was little.
Please wait until the rain stops.
Please listen to music while I drive.
Don’t talk on the phone while walking.
As soon as I came home, I took a shower.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): a courageous seven-year-old boy
explanations.body: The following is a story about a courageous 7-year-old boy (the Korean text writes the boy as 정호). In step a the book asks you to underline and number the time references that include conjunctive endings (the first, 저녁을 먹기 전에, is done for you); in step b to fill in a table (when / what). The book glosses 잠그다: to lock. The story is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (119 is 일일구); the English is mine.

examples.text: 저녁을 먹기 전에 정호는 여동생과 함께 이 층 방에서 놀고 있었다.
examples.translation: jeonyeogeul meokgi jeone jeonghoneun yeodongsaenggwa hamkke i cheung bangeseo nolgo isseotda. — Before dinner, Jungho was playing with his younger sister in the second-floor room.

examples.text: 엄마는 부엌에서 저녁을 준비하고 아빠는 일 층 거실에서 신문을 읽고 있었다.
examples.translation: eommaneun bueokeseo jeonyeogeul junbihago appaneun il cheung geosireseo sinmuneul ilgo isseotda. — Mom was preparing dinner in the kitchen and Dad was reading the newspaper in the first-floor living room.

examples.text: 엄마가 식구들에게 저녁을 먹으라고 할 때 권총을 든 강도 두 명이 집안으로 들어왔다.
examples.translation: eommaga sikgudeurege jeonyeogeul meogeurago hal ttae gwonchongeul deun gangdo du myeongi jibaneuro deureowatda. — When Mom told the family to eat dinner, two robbers holding pistols came into the house.

examples.text: 강도들이 집으로 들어오자마자 정호는 동생과 함께 화장실로 숨었다.
examples.translation: gangdodeuri jibeuro deureoojamaja jeonghoneun dongsaenggwa hamkke hwajangsillo sumeotda. — As soon as the robbers came into the house, Jungho hid in the bathroom with his sister.

examples.text: 화장실 문을 잠근 후 일일구에 전화를 걸어서 도움을 요청했다.
examples.translation: hwajangsil muneul jamgeun hu irilgue jeonhwareul georeoseo doumeul yocheonghaetda. — After locking the bathroom door, he called 119 and asked for help.

examples.text: 그런데 강도 한 명이 정호와 동생들을 찾아내서 어디에 전화했는지 물었다.
examples.translation: geureonde gangdo han myeongi jeonghowa dongsaengdeureul chajanaeseo eodie jeonhwahaenneunji mureotda. — But one robber found Jungho and his siblings and asked where he had called.

examples.text: 정호는 일일구에 전화했다고 했다.
examples.translation: jeonghoneun irilgue jeonhwahaetdago haetda. — Jungho said he had called 119.

examples.text: 전화를 받고 출동한 경찰이 오는 동안 강도들은 도망쳤다.
examples.translation: jeonhwareul batgo chuldonghan gyeongchari oneun dongan gangdodeureun domangcheotda. — While the police who received the call and were dispatched were coming, the robbers fled.

examples.text: 다행히 다친 사람은 아무도 없었다.
examples.translation: dahaenghi dachin sarameun amudo eopseotda. — Fortunately, no one was hurt.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 3 (listening to ten dialog segments in which a police officer asks a suspect what she did last Saturday, checking the conjunctive ending and writing the two actions) and Follow-up 4 (listening to an incomplete story, writing a few more sentences with time endings in Korean and sharing the story with two classmates) are audio and group activities.

explanations.body: To practice the summary, combine each pair of short sentences with one time-reference ending (the pairs, the answers and the English are mine, in the spirit of the book’s Follow-ups).

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with so that they can provide other activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify and describe social customs and trends related to major national holidays; identify and discuss sports events and sports culture; and compare and discuss how job preferences have changed.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the summary of conjunctive endings related to time reference; an interrogative word followed by –든(지) (no matter what/who/when, etc.); ~까지(도) (even; to a degree that extends); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 최대 (最大), 동계 (冬季), and 안정 (安定).

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: The chapter’s activity sections also contain a SMART Board reading activity, listening activities (Chuseok conversations, international sports events, job positives and negatives), and speaking and writing activities in pairs or groups. They are audio, computer and group activities and are left out; the readings of the activities are in the earlier lessons of this chapter.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning (the book prints 冬系 for 동계 in one place; the Sino-Korean note gives 冬季, which I use). The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank. The book’s Loan Words section repeats words already listed above (디자이너, 메달, 스타, 아마추어, 올림픽, 월드컵, 코치, 프로 and so on); I list each word once. The last section lists the Sino-Korean related words of 최대, 동계 and 안정 as the book gives them.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (4대 → 네 대; 40% → 사십 퍼센트; 24개 → 스물네 개; 32개 → 서른두 개; 4년마다 → 사 년마다; 1988년 → 천구백팔십팔 년).

lessons.title: 561. Ch 45 · What the chapter teaches, 조선업 · 약세 · 하락 · 급감 · 장단점
lessons.subtitle: 경제 · 조선업 · 약세 · 하락 · 급감 · 장단점 · 造船業 · 弱勢 · 下落 · 急減 · 長短點

explanations.title: What Chapter 45 teaches (경제)
explanations.body:
Chapter 45, “Economy”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations (the structure of the Korean economy, Korean trade, investment) with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and discuss sectors of the Korean economy including the gross domestic product (GDP), economic growth rate, trade volume, trading partners, etc.; identify and discuss major types of financial investments and their characteristics; and read and say large numbers in Korean.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; ~에도 (불구하고) or –(으)ㄴ/는데도 (불구하고) (in spite of; despite); –(으)려던 참이다 (I was about to do something); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 조선업 (造船業), 약세 (弱勢), 하락 (下落), 급감 (急減), and 장단점 (長短點).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 조선업 (造船業)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means shipbuilding business or shipbuilding industry. The first syllable 조 (造) means make or build, as in 조어 (coined word; “made word”). The second syllable 선 (船) means a ship or a boat, as in 선장 (skipper; captain; “boat chief”) and 선원 (ship crew member). The last syllable 업 (業) means business, work, or occupation, as in 어업 (fishery; “fishing business”) and 광업 (mining; “mine industry”). The book asks you to guess the meaning of 위조, 모조품, 조화, 어선, 유조선, 선원, 개업, 수산업 and 업소 (the book glosses 모 [模]: imitate, model; 화 [花]: a flower; my answers):

rows: a place of business; an establishment

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 약세 (弱勢)
explanations.body: The first syllable 약 (弱) means weak(ness) or feeble(ness), as in 약자 (a weak person; the weak) and 강약 (loud and soft [in music]; dynamics; “strong and weak”). The second syllable 세 (勢) means power, influence, or force, as in 추세 (tendency; trend; “running force”). Thus, the literal meaning of the word 약세 is “weak force” or “weak influence,” and the word means bearish (falling) trend or weak tendency (in stock, currency exchange rate, price). The book asks you to guess 약화, 강세, 약점, 우세, 노약자 and 세력 (the book glosses 우 [優]: tender, outstanding, sufficient; my answers):

rows: loud and soft (in music); dynamics; “strong and weak”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 하락 (下落)
explanations.body: The syllable 하 (下) means under, below, low, or bottom, as in 지하철 (subway; “underground railroad”) and 하녀 (a female servant; “low woman”). 락/낙 (落) means drop or fall, as in 낙엽 (fallen leaves) or 낙마 (falling from a horse). Keep in mind that 락 changes to 낙 at the beginning of a word. Thus, the literal meaning of the word 하락 is “falling below,” and it means drop or decrease (in number or amount). The book asks you to guess 하수도, 영하, 하반기, 추락, 낙선 and 낙하산 (the book glosses 산 [傘]: umbrella; 선 [選]: election; my answers):

rows: the second half of the year

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 급감 (急減)
explanations.body: The first syllable 급 (急) means urgent, sudden, or rapid, as in 급류 (a rapid; a torrent; “rapid flow”) and 급사 (a sudden death; an untimely death). The second syllable 감 (減) means decrease, reduction, or subtraction, as in 감하다 (to reduce; to subtract) and 감세 (reduction of taxes). Thus, the literal meaning of 급감 is “sudden decrease” or “rapid reduction,” and it means sudden decrease or sharp decrease (in number or amount). The book asks you to guess 급증, 급락, 급성장, 감소, 감원 and 가감 (the book glosses 원 [員]: personnel; 가 [加]: adding; my answers):

rows: a sudden death; an untimely death

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 장단점 (長短點)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means strengths and weaknesses, strong and weak points, pros and cons, merits and demerits, or advantages and disadvantages. The first syllable 장 (長), which was discussed in Chapter 25, means long, big, or chief/head, as in 장거리 (long distance), 장남 (the eldest son; “big man”), 병장 (a sergeant; “head of soldiers”), and 사장 (a company president; “company chief”). The second syllable 단 (短) means short, as in 단거리 (short distance) or 단문 (a short sentence; a short composition; “short letter”). The last syllable 점 (點), discussed in Chapter 33, means point or score, as in 점수 (score; a mark; a grade; “number of points”) and 종점 (the last stop; the end of the route; the terminal; “ending point”). explanations.body: The Sino-Korean syllable 형 (型) means shape, type, model, or style. It is often used as a word suffix: 미래형 자동차 (a futuristic-style car), 최신형 스마트폰 (a newest-style smartphone), and B형/O형 혈액 (Type B/Type O in ABO blood group system).

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 경제개발 5개년 계획
explanations.body:
경제개발 5개년 계획 is a government-led plan that was implemented seven times between the 1960s and 1990s. Each development plan had a different focus. For example, 제1차 경제개발 5개년 계획 (1962–1966) was aimed at securing sources of energy, increasing the income of farmers, and building infrastructure. Manufacturing, production, and exports increased noticeably. During 제3차 (1972–1976) and 제4차 경제개발 5개년 계획 (1977–1981), investment in heavy industries increased, and the development of technology strengthened the nation’s competitiveness in the global economy.

경제개발 5개년 계획 continued until 1996. However, rapid expansion focusing on quantitative growth resulted in many problems: uneven development among different regions, falling participation in agriculture by young people, a growing gap between the rich and poor, etc. Having recognized these issues, the Korean government is now making efforts to improve the quality of life for its people. At the same time, the government is attempting to grow its GDP and make advancements in cutting-edge technologies.

explanations.title: Reading large numbers: 만, 억, 조
explanations.body: One objective of the chapter is to read and say large numbers in Korean. The Korean number system groups digits by units of ten thousand: 만 (10,000), 억 (100,000,000) and 조 (1,000,000,000,000), the last of which the chapter’s core vocabulary lists (조 [兆]: trillion). This table is my own summary of the numbers that appear in the chapter (the sample amounts are the book’s or typical of its examples).

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): forecasts for the Korean economy
explanations.body: The following passage is about forecasts for the Korean economy (the book glosses nothing here). The book asks you to list two forecasts made by the government and two forecasts made by the experts. The passage is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (20–30대 is 이십 대에서 삼십 대); the English and the answers are mine.

examples.text: 정부는 올해 우리 경제가 오 퍼센트 성장해, 오이씨디 국가 중 최고 수준의 성장률을 보일 것으로 예상한다.
examples.translation: jeongbuneun olhae uri gyeongjega o peosenteu seongjanghae, oissidi gukga jung choego sujunui seongjangnyureul boil geoseuro yesanghanda. — The government expects our economy to grow 5 percent this year and show the highest level of growth rate among OECD countries.

examples.text: 반도체와 자동차 등 기존의 주요 산업은 물론 에너지와 녹색산업이 크게 성장할 것으로 전망하고 있다.
examples.translation: bandochewa jadongcha deung gijonui juyo saneobeun mullon eneojiwa noksaeksaneobi keuge seongjanghal geoseuro jeonmanghago itda. — It forecasts that, not to mention the existing major industries such as semiconductors and automobiles, energy and green industries will grow greatly.

examples.text: 그렇지만 경제전문가들은 두 가지 문제점이 계속될 것으로 본다.
examples.translation: geureochiman gyeongjejeonmungadeureun du gaji munjejeomi gyesokdoel geoseuro bonda. — However, economic experts think two problems will continue.

examples.text: 첫째는 일자리 부족 문제이다.
examples.translation: cheotjjaeneun iljari bujok munjeida. — The first is the problem of a shortage of jobs.

examples.text: 특히 이십 대에서 삼십 대 젊은이들의 취업이 계속 어려울 것으로 본다.
examples.translation: teuki isip daeeseo samsip dae jeolmeunideurui chwieobi gyesok eoryeoul geoseuro bonda. — In particular, they think employment for young people in their twenties and thirties will continue to be difficult.

examples.text: 둘째, 전문가들은 대기업 중심의 경제구조가 바뀌지는 않을 것으로 예상한다.
examples.translation: duljjae, jeonmungadeureun daegieop jungsimui gyeongjegujoga bakkwijineun aneul geoseuro yesanghanda. — Second, the experts expect that the big-company-centered economic structure will not change.

examples.text: 대기업 중심의 경제구조는 중소기업의 성장과 발전을 어렵게 하기 때문에 문제가 된다는 것이다.
examples.translation: daegieop jungsimui gyeongjegujoneun jungsogieobui seongjanggwa baljeoneul eoryeopge hagi ttaemune munjega doendaneun geosida. — The point is that the big-company-centered economic structure becomes a problem because it makes the growth and development of small and medium-sized companies difficult.

rows: 1. Two forecasts made by the government

The economy will grow 5% this year, the highest growth rate among OECD countries; energy and green industries will grow greatly, as well as the existing major industries such as semiconductors and automobiles
2. Two forecasts made by the experts

The shortage of jobs will continue, with employment hard especially for people in their 20s and 30s; the big-company-centered economic structure will not change, which makes the growth of small and medium-sized companies difficult

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading) a: which sector?
explanations.body: The following sentences are about various industry sectors in which a person’s family member works. The book asks you to choose the sector from the box (a. 서비스업 b. 농업 c. 조선업 d. 제조업 e. 어업). The sentences are the book’s (the numerals are dropped); the English and the answers are mine.

rows: 제 삼촌은 배를 만드는 회사에서 근무합니다.
우리 큰 형은 올해 쌀 수확량이 줄어들어 속상해합니다.
동생은 전자 제품을 만드는 회사에서 일합니다.
저는 배를 타고 바다에서 물고기를 잡는 일을 합니다.
My uncle works at a company that builds ships.
My eldest brother is upset because this year’s rice harvest has decreased.
My younger sibling works at a company that makes electronic products.
I ride a boat and catch fish at sea.
My older sister works as a section chief at the Daehan Hotel.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading) b: industrialized countries
explanations.body: Read the sentences and check those that describe industrialized countries (the sentences are the book’s; my answers and the English):

rows: The economic structure is mainly agriculture-centered.
Information and communication technology and cutting-edge technology industries are strong.
The per capita national income is very low.
미래형 로봇이나 반도체 산업이 발전되어 있다.
Futuristic robot and semiconductor industries are developed.
국내총생산이 아주 높고 오이씨디에 가입되어 있다.
The gross domestic product is very high and it is a member of the OECD.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 2 (listening to three presentations in which a student reports about a country’s economy, filling in the expected economic growth rate, next year’s GDP and the growing industry; the book glosses 인공지능: AI and 벗어나다: to get out) and Activity 3 (“한국의 경제가 이렇게 달라졌어요”: two partners each read a part of an article about changes in Korea’s economic structure from the 1960s to the present, filling in the major industries and trend and the per capita national income for the 1960s–1980s and the 1990s–2020s, exchanging the information, and presenting; the article itself is not printed in the student book text) are audio and pair activities.

explanations.title: Topic B: Korea’s trade (한국의 무역)
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from Korea’s trade report. (The English is mine; the book gives none. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out [KITA is 케이아이티에이; 1970~1980년대 is 천구백칠십 년대와 팔십 년대]. The book’s footnote: KITA [한국무역협회] stands for the Korea International Trade Association.)

examples.text: 한국의 무역
examples.translation: hangugui muyeok — Korea’s trade

examples.text: 한국무역협회 케이아이티에이의 통계에 따르면, 우리나라의 무역량은 꾸준히 증가해 왔다.
examples.translation: hangungmuyeokyeopoe keiaitieiui tonggyee ttareumyeon, urinaraui muyeongnyangeun kkujunhi jeunggahae watda. — According to the statistics of the Korea International Trade Association (KITA), our country’s trade volume has been increasing steadily.

examples.text: 천구백사십육 년 우리나라의 수출액은 삼백오십사만 달러 수준이었으나 천구백육십사 년 일억 달러로 증가했고, 이천십팔 년에는 처음으로 육천억 달러를 넘었다.
examples.translation: cheongubaeksasibyuk nyeon urinaraui suchuraegeun sambaegosipsaman dalleo sujunieosseuna cheongubaegyuksipsa nyeon ireok dalleoro jeunggahaetgo, icheonsippal nyeoneneun cheoeumeuro yukcheoneok dalleoreul neomeotda. — In 1946 our country’s export amount was at the level of 3.54 million dollars, but it increased to 100 million dollars in 1964 and, in 2018, exceeded 600 billion dollars for the first time.

examples.text: 특히 지난 오 년간 우리나라의 수출 증가율은 연평균 삼 점 육 퍼센트로 세계 수출 순위 육 위에서 칠 위에 오르기도 했다.
examples.translation: teuki jinan o nyeongan urinaraui suchul jeunggayureun yeonpyeonggyun sam jeom yuk peosenteuro segye suchul sunwi yuk wieseo chil wie oreugido haetda. — In particular, over the past five years our country’s export growth rate was 3.6 percent on a yearly average, and it even reached 6th to 7th place in world export rankings.

examples.text: 우리나라의 무역수지는 전 세계적인 경제불황에도 불구하고 전반적으로 흑자를 기록했다.
examples.translation: urinaraui muyeoksujineun jeon segyejeogin gyeongjebulhwangedo bulguhago jeonbanjeogeuro heukjareul girokaetda. — Our country’s trade balance recorded a surplus overall in spite of the worldwide economic recession.

examples.text: 그러나 최근 이상기후나 전쟁 등에 따른 글로벌 경제 환경의 변화는 앞으로 우리나라의 무역수지에 적지 않은 영향을 줄 것으로 예상된다.
examples.translation: geureona choegeun isanggihuna jeonjaeng deunge ttareun geullobeol gyeongje hwangyeongui byeonhwaneun apeuro urinaraui muyeoksujie jeokji aneun yeonghyangeul jul geoseuro yesangdoenda. — However, recent changes in the global economic environment due to abnormal weather, wars and so on are expected to have no small influence on our country’s trade balance in the future.

examples.text: 우리나라의 수출 대상국은 천구백칠십 년대 백삼십칠 개국에서 이천 년대 이백이십팔 개국으로 증가했다.
examples.translation: urinaraui suchul daesanggugeun cheongubaekchilsip nyeondae baeksamsipchil gaegugeseo icheon nyeondae ibaegisippal gaegugeuro jeunggahaetda. — The number of our country’s export destination countries increased from 137 countries in the 1970s to 228 countries in the 2000s.

examples.text: 천구백칠십 년대와 팔십 년대에는 미국과 일본이 전체 수출의 육십 퍼센트 이상을 차지했다.
examples.translation: cheongubaekchilsip nyeondaewa palsip nyeondaeeneun migukgwa ilboni jeonche suchurui yuksip peosenteu isangeul chajihaetda. — In the 1970s and 1980s, the U.S. and Japan accounted for more than 60 percent of total exports.

examples.text: 그러나 천구백구십 년대에는 미국과 일본의 비중이 삼십 퍼센트로 하락했다.
examples.translation: geureona cheongubaekgusip nyeondaeeneun migukgwa ilbonui bijungi samsip peosenteuro harakaetda. — But in the 1990s the share of the U.S. and Japan fell to 30 percent.

examples.text: 이천 년 이후 중남미와 중국 등 새로운 시장을 개척하면서 수출 대상국이 꾸준히 늘어나고 있다.
examples.translation: icheon nyeon ihu jungnammiwa jungguk deung saeroun sijangeul gaecheokamyeonseo suchul daesanggugi kkujunhi neureonago itda. — Since 2000, as new markets such as Central and South America and China have been developed, the number of export destination countries has been steadily increasing.

examples.text: 천구백칠십 년대 우리나라의 주요 수출 품목은 섬유, 신발 등이었다.
examples.translation: cheongubaekchilsip nyeondae urinaraui juyo suchul pummogeun seomyu, sinbal deungieotda. — In the 1970s, our country’s main export items were textiles, shoes and so on.

examples.text: 팔십 년대에는 전기 전자 분야의 수출이 급증했다.
examples.translation: palsip nyeondaeeneun jeongi jeonja bunyaui suchuri geupjeunghaetda. — In the 1980s, exports in the electrical and electronics field increased rapidly.

examples.text: 주요 수출 품목은 반도체와 컴퓨터, 가전제품이었다.
examples.translation: juyo suchul pummogeun bandochewa keompyuteo, gajeonjepumieotda. — The main export items were semiconductors, computers and home appliances.

examples.text: 구십 년대부터 반도체, 기계, 자동차, 선박 등이 꾸준히 주요 수출 품목이 되었다.
examples.translation: gusip nyeondaebuteo bandoche, gigye, jadongcha, seonbak deungi kkujunhi juyo suchul pummogi doeeotda. — From the 1990s, semiconductors, machinery, automobiles, ships and so on steadily became main export items.

examples.text: 현재 우리나라의 주요 수입 품목은 원유 등 원자재와 농산물이다.
examples.translation: hyeonjae urinaraui juyo suip pummogeun wonyu deung wonjajaewa nongsanmurida. — Currently our country’s main import items are raw materials such as crude oil, and agricultural products.
