explanations.title: 한국에서는: A Look at Korea’s Exports
explanations.body: Korea has seen a dramatic shift in its major exports in recent decades. In the 1950s, its primary exports consisted of mining products like tungsten, graphite, and iron. During the 1960s, “light” (labor-intensive) industry products, such as shoes and wigs became leading exports, with textile products accounting for 40% of the total. The Korean government’s promotion of the heavy and chemical industries in the 1970s resulted in products such as steel and plastic goods becoming major export items in the 1980s. Other major export items during that decade included electronics, automobiles, and ships. Semiconductors took the lead in the 1990s, and in the 2000s, Korea expanded into consumer electronics, such as cellular phones and LCD monitors. Today, Korea stands as a major exporter of electrical machinery, equipment, and parts in the world, holding a 5.8% share of global exports in 2020. It also ranked ninth in exports of machinery, mechanical appliances, nuclear reactors, and boilers in the same year.

explanations.title: Presentation step b: the three paragraphs (mine)
explanations.body: The book asks you to read the topic and fill in, in English, a title and the trend or changes for each paragraph. My answers:

rows: Growth of trade volume and the trade balance

Trade has increased steadily: exports rose from 3.54 million dollars (1946) to 100 million (1964) to over 600 billion (2018); export growth averaged 3.6% a year over five years; a surplus overall despite the recession, but global changes may affect it
Destination countries grew from 137 (1970s) to 228 (2000s); the U.S. and Japan took over 60% in the 1970s–80s but 30% in the 1990s; new markets (Central/South America, China) since 2000

1970s textiles, shoes; 1980s electronics surged (semiconductors, computers, home appliances); from the 1990s semiconductors, machinery, cars, ships; imports now crude oil and other raw materials, and farm products

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a news report about Korea’s trade balance
explanations.body: The following news report is about Korea’s trade balance. The book asks you to check whether each quarter’s trade balance was a deficit or a surplus and to fill in the trade items in English. The report is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (1분기 is 일 분기); the English and the answers are mine.

examples.text: 올해 일 분기 무역수지는 적자, 이 분기 무역수지는 흑자를 기록했다.
examples.translation: olhae il bungi muyeoksujineun jeokja, i bungi muyeoksujineun heukjareul girokaetda. — This year’s first-quarter trade balance recorded a deficit, and the second-quarter trade balance recorded a surplus.

examples.text: 일 분기 수출은 기계, 선박 등이 강세를 보였지만, 석유 등 원자재와 농산물 수입이 급증하면서 적자를 기록했다.
examples.translation: il bungi suchureun gigye, seonbak deungi gangsereul boyeotjiman, seogyu deung wonjajaewa nongsanmul suibi geupjeunghamyeonseo jeokjareul girokaetda. — In the first quarter, exports of machinery, ships and so on were strong, but a deficit was recorded as imports of raw materials such as oil and of agricultural products rapidly increased.

examples.text: 지역별로는 중남미 국가에서의 수입이 오십팔 퍼센트나 증가했다.
examples.translation: jiyeokbyeolloneun jungnammi gukgaeseoui suibi osippal peosenteuna jeunggahaetda. — By region, imports from Central and South American countries increased by as much as 58 percent.

examples.text: 이 분기에는 수출이 강세를 보이며 흑자를 기록했다.
examples.translation: i bungieneun suchuri gangsereul boimyeo heukjareul girokaetda. — In the second quarter, exports were strong and a surplus was recorded.

examples.text: 품목별로는 섬유와 기계 수출이 급증했고, 농산물 수입이 증가세를 보였다.
examples.translation: pummokbyeolloneun seomyuwa gigye suchuri geupjeunghaetgo, nongsanmul suibi jeunggasereul boyeotda. — By item, exports of textiles and machinery increased rapidly, and imports of agricultural products showed an upward trend.

examples.text: 국가별로는 미국, 유럽 등 전반적으로 선진국으로의 수출이 강세를 보였다.
examples.translation: gukgabyeolloneun miguk, yureop deung jeonbanjeogeuro seonjingugeuroui suchuri gangsereul boyeotda. — By country, exports to advanced countries overall, such as the U.S. and Europe, were strong.

rows: Raw materials such as oil, and agricultural products (rapid increase; imports from Central and South America up 58%)

lessons.title: 568. Ch 45 · Grammar A: ~에도 (불구하고) and –(으)ㄴ/는데도 (불구하고)
lessons.subtitle: ~에도 불구하고 · -(으)ㄴ/는데도 불구하고 · -(으)ㅁ에도 · 불황에도 · 부상을 입었는데도 · 이달의 학생

explanations.title: In spite of; despite
explanations.body: Both ~에도 (불구하고) and –(으)ㄴ/는데도 (불구하고) can be translated as in spite of or despite. However, ~에도 (불구하고) is preceded by a noun or a gerund form –(으)ㅁ, and –데도 (불구하고) is preceded by an attributive form of a verb. Keep in mind that 불구하고 can be omitted. For example (the English is the book’s; the book writes 불구하고 in parentheses and I write it in full):

examples.text: 불황에도 불구하고 수출은 증가했습니다.
examples.translation: bulhwangedo bulguhago suchureun jeunggahaetseumnida. — In spite of the recession, exports have increased.

examples.text: 매일 열심히 운동함에도 불구하고 체중이 줄지 않아요.
examples.translation: maeil yeolsimhi undonghamedo bulguhago chejungi julji anayo. — In spite of working out diligently every day, I am not losing weight.

examples.text: 매일 열심히 운동하는데도 불구하고 체중이 줄지 않아요.
examples.translation: maeil yeolsimhi undonghaneundedo bulguhago chejungi julji anayo. — In spite of working out diligently every day, I am not losing weight.

explanations.title: The patterns
explanations.body: “In spite of/despite”: noun/–(으)ㅁ + 에도 (불구하고); verb + (으)ㄴ/는데도 (불구하고). More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 주중임에도 불구하고 놀이공원에 사람이 많습니다.
examples.translation: jujungimedo bulguhago norigongwone sarami manseumnida. — Despite its being a weekday, there are many people in the amusement park.

examples.text: 건물이 큰데도 불구하고 짓는 데 시간이 별로 안 걸렸습니다.
examples.translation: geonmuri keundedo bulguhago jinneun de sigani byeollo an geollyeotseumnida. — Despite the fact that the building is big, it did not take long to build.

examples.text: 공부를 열심히 하는데도 불구하고 성적이 별로 안 좋아요.
examples.translation: gongbureul yeolsimhi haneundedo bulguhago seongjeogi byeollo an joayo. — In spite of my studying diligently, my grades are not very good.

examples.text: 여러 번 실패했는데도 불구하고 포기하지 않았다.
examples.translation: yeoreo beon silpaehaenneundedo bulguhago pogihaji anatda. — Despite the fact that he had failed several times, he did not give up.

examples.text: 부상을 입었는데도 불구하고 경기에 나갔습니다.
examples.translation: busangeul ibeonneundedo bulguhago gyeonggie nagatseumnida. — Despite being injured, she went out to compete.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading and speaking): connect the phrases
explanations.body: a. Find two phrases that can be connected with “~에도/–(으)ㄴ/는데도 (불구하고)” and draw a line (there may be more than one correct answer). The book’s left phrases are 감기약을 복용하다, 비가 오다, 물가가 오르다, 휴일이다, 주말에 푹 쉬었다, 불황, 공부를 열심히 하다 and 원유 가격이 하락했다; the right phrases are 비싼 수입품이 잘 팔리다, 성적이 안 오르다, 기름값이 비싸다, 계속 기침하다, 야구 경기를 계속 하다, 월급은 오르지 않는다, 출근해야 하다 and 여전히 피곤하다. My pairings, each as a sentence (the English is mine):

examples.text: 감기약을 복용했는데도 계속 기침해요.
examples.translation: gamgiyageul bogyonghaenneundedo gyesok gichimhaeyo. — I keep coughing even though I took cold medicine.

examples.text: 비가 오는데도 야구 경기를 계속 해요.
examples.translation: biga oneundedo yagu gyeonggireul gyesok haeyo. — They keep playing the baseball game even though it is raining.

examples.text: 물가가 오르는데도 비싼 수입품이 잘 팔려요.
examples.translation: mulgaga oreuneundedo bissan suippumi jal pallyeoyo. — Expensive imported goods sell well even though prices are rising.

examples.text: 휴일인데도 출근해야 해요.
examples.translation: hyuirindedo chulgeunhaeya haeyo. — I have to go to work even though it is a holiday.

examples.text: 주말에 푹 쉬었는데도 여전히 피곤해요.
examples.translation: jumare puk swieonneundedo yeojeonhi pigonhaeyo. — I am still tired even though I rested well on the weekend.

examples.text: 불황에도 월급은 오르지 않아요.
examples.translation: bulhwangedo wolgeubeun oreuji anayo. — Even in a recession, salaries do not go up.

examples.text: 공부를 열심히 하는데도 성적이 안 올라요.
examples.translation: gongbureul yeolsimhi haneundedo seongjeogi an ollayo. — My grades do not go up even though I study hard.

examples.text: 원유 가격이 하락했는데도 기름값이 비싸요.
examples.translation: wonyu gagyeogi harakaenneundedo gireumgapsi bissayo. — Gas is expensive even though the crude oil price has fallen.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading): a figure skater in a competition
explanations.body: The following news article is about a figure skater who participated in a competition. The book asks you to fill in her final performance result, her reaction to the result and the English translation of the underlined sentence. The article is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (130.49점 is 백삼십 점 사구; the quotation marks are dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 김연아는 이십칠 일 한국시간 밤 이탈리아 토리노 팔라벨라 빙상장에서 치러진 대회 여자 싱글 프리스케이팅에서 몇 차례 실수에도 불구하고 백삼십 점 사구를 받아 은메달을 따냈다.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Writing and speaking): a letter of recommendation
explanations.body: You write a letter of five to six sentences recommending a classmate who has overcome many obstacles as “student of the month”, with at least one sentence including ~에도/–(으)ㄴ/는데도 (불구하고), and some background information on the candidate; then you post the letters on the wall, read others’ and choose a student. The book’s model (the English is mine; the quotation marks are dropped):

examples.text: 김 이병을 이달의 학생으로 추천합니다.
examples.translation: gim ibyeongeul idarui haksaengeuro chucheonhamnida. — I recommend Pvt. Kim as the “student of the month.”

examples.text: 김 이병은 얼마 전에 독감에 걸려서 아주 고생했어요.
examples.translation: gim ibyeongeun eolma jeone dokgame geollyeoseo aju gosaenghaesseoyo. — Pvt. Kim recently caught the flu and had a very hard time.

examples.text: 그래서 며칠간 학교에도 못 나왔어요.
examples.translation: geuraeseo myeochilgan hakgyoedo mot nawasseoyo. — So he could not even come to school for a few days.

examples.text: 기숙사에서 공부를 열심히 해서 시험도 잘 봤습니다.
examples.translation: gisuksaeseo gongbureul yeolsimhi haeseo siheomdo jal bwatseumnida. — He studied hard in the dormitory and did well on the exam too.

examples.text: 김 이병은 독감에 걸렸는데도 불구하고 시험 성적이 좋았습니다.
examples.translation: gim ibyeongeun dokgame geollyeonneundedo bulguhago siheom seongjeogi joatseumnida. — Despite having caught the flu, Pvt. Kim’s exam results were good.

examples.text: 그래서 김 이병이 이달의 학생으로 뽑히면 좋겠습니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo gim ibyeongi idarui haksaengeuro ppopimyeon joketseumnida. — So I hope Pvt. Kim is chosen as the “student of the month.”

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 한국의 은행
explanations.body: 한국은행 functions similarly to the Federal Reserve Board in the United States. The primary function of 한국은행 is issuing currency, formulating and implementing monetary and credit policy, and managing foreign exchange reserves. Special banks, such as 농협 (농업협동조합) and 중소기업은행, are set up and owned by the Korean government to provide financial support to specific economic endeavors. In Korea, 우체국 not only provides mail services, but also financial services for the public, such as savings and insurance. (The book’s table of banks, with KB written 케이비:)

rows: 케이비 국민은행, 하나은행, 신한은행, 우리은행, 외환은행

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 예금의 종류
explanations.body: There are three types of bank accounts used in Korea. 보통예금 (regular savings) is similar to a checking account in the United States. Customers can freely deposit and withdraw funds. 정기예금 is a time-deposit account and is similar to a CD (certificate of deposit). Customers have to deposit a specific amount for a specific period of time, based on a contract. 적금 is an installment savings account in which customers deposit a fixed amount each month during a specific contract period. Customers who open 정기예금 and 적금 cannot withdraw funds until the contract expires (만기), unless they close the account earlier, which results in a major loss of interest. In Korean banking, 통장 (a bankbook) is issued when the account is opened. For all banking transactions using 통장, either a stamp or the account holder’s signature is used.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading): types of investment
explanations.body: The following sentences describe the characteristics of different types of investment. The book asks you to write the letter of the type (a. 적금 b. 주식 투자 c. 보통예금 d. 펀드 투자 e. 부동산 투자) before each sentence. The sentences are the book’s; the answers and the English are mine.

rows: 돈을 입금하거나 찾는 것이 자유롭지만 이자율이 낮다. 투자 금액과 기간에도 제한이 없다.
Depositing or withdrawing money is free, but the interest rate is low. There is no limit on the investment amount and period either.
회사의 증권을 개인이 직접 사고 판다. 증권 값이 올라가면 돈을 쉽게 벌 수 있지만 값이 떨어지면 투자한 돈을 잃는다.
Individuals buy and sell company securities directly. If the securities’ price goes up, you can make money easily, but if the price falls, you lose the money you invested.
아파트나 집, 건물, 또는 땅에 투자한다. 많은 돈이 필요하고 투자 기간이 길다.
You invest in an apartment, a house, a building, or land. A lot of money is needed and the investment period is long.
전문가가 개인을 대신해서 주식이나 증권에 투자한다. 개인이 투자하는 것보다 안전한 편이다.
An expert invests in stocks or securities on behalf of an individual. It is on the safer side than an individual investing.
매달 정해진 금액을 계약한 기간 동안 입금한다. 이자율이 높은 편이고 계약 기간이 끝나면 목돈을 찾을 수 있다.
You deposit a set amount every month during the contracted period. The interest rate is on the high side, and when the contract period ends you can withdraw a lump sum.

explanations.title: Activity 3 b (Reading): ways to manage money
explanations.body: The following text from a financial advisor is about ways to manage money (1. 주식 2. 주택적금 3. 펀드 투자 4. 부동산 투자). The book asks you to fill in the characteristics of each investment or type of savings in English. The text is the book’s (the table cells are read as four short paragraphs); the English is mine, and my summary follows.

examples.text: 개인이 직접 주식에 투자한다. 위험성이 따르며 특히 주식에 대해서 잘 모르면 위험성이 더 크다. 경기 추세에 따라 가격이 오르면 짧은 기간 안에 많은 수익을 낼 수 있다. 하지만 주식 값이 떨어지면 손해를 볼 수 있다.
examples.translation: gaeini jikjeop jusige tujahanda. wiheomseongi ttareumyeo teuki jusige daehaeseo jal moreumyeon wiheomseongi deo keuda. gyeonggi chusee ttara gagyeogi oreumyeon jjalbeun gigan ane maneun suigeul nael su itda. hajiman jusik gapsi tteoreojimyeon sonhaereul bol su itda. — An individual invests in stocks directly. It carries risk, and the risk is greater especially if you do not know much about stocks. If the price rises according to the economic trend, you can make a lot of profit in a short period. But if stock prices fall, you may take a loss.

examples.text: 집이 없는 사람이 주택 구입을 위해 저축하는 정기 적금이다. 주택은행에서만 들 수 있다. 정해진 계약 기간 동안 매월 일정 금액을 입금한다. 이자율이 높으며 주택 구입에 필요한 목돈을 마련할 수 있다.
examples.translation: jibi eomneun sarami jutaek guibeul wihae jeochukaneun jeonggi jeokgeumida. jutaegeunhaengeseoman deul su itda. jeonghaejin gyeyak gigan dongan maewol iljeong geumaegeul ipgeumhanda. ijayuri nopeumyeo jutaek guibe piryohan mokdoneul maryeonhal su itda. — This is fixed-term installment savings that a person without a house saves for buying a home. You can open it only at the housing bank. You deposit a fixed amount every month during the set contract period. The interest rate is high and you can make the lump sum needed to buy a home.

examples.text: 개인 대신에 전문가가 주식이나 증권에 투자해 준다. 수수료를 지급해야 한다. 전문가가 투자하기 때문에 위험성이 낮은 편이다. 수익성도 좋은 편이지만 시장의 추세에 따라 손해를 볼 수도 있다.
examples.translation: gaein daesine jeonmungaga jusigina jeunggwone tujahae junda. susuryoreul jigeupaeya handa. jeonmungaga tujahagi ttaemune wiheomseongi najeun pyeonida. suikseongdo joeun pyeonijiman sijangui chusee ttara sonhaereul bol sudo itda. — An expert invests in stocks or securities instead of the individual. You have to pay a fee. Because an expert invests, the risk is on the low side. Profitability is also good, but you may take a loss according to the market trend.

examples.text: 집이나 아파트, 건물, 또는 땅을 구입하는 재산 투자이다. 장기 투자이며 비교적 안정적인 투자이다. 특히 개발가능성이 있는 곳에 땅이나 건물을 사 두면 몇 년 후에 좋은 수익을 올릴 수도 있다.
examples.translation: jibina apateu, geonmul, ttoneun ttangeul guipaneun jaesan tujaida. janggi tujaimyeo bigyojeok anjeongjeogin tujaida. teuki gaebalganeungseongi inneun gose ttangina geonmureul sa dumyeon myeon nyeon hue joeun suigeul ollil sudo itda. — This is a property investment of buying a house, an apartment, a building, or land. It is a long-term and relatively stable investment. In particular, if you buy land or a building in a place with development potential, you may earn a good profit a few years later.

rows: Direct investment by an individual; risky, especially without knowledge; big profit in a short time if prices rise, loss if they fall
Fixed-term installment savings for people without a house; only at the housing bank; fixed monthly deposits; high interest; makes the lump sum for a home purchase
An expert invests for you; a fee must be paid; relatively low risk; good profitability but a loss is possible with market trends
Buying a house, apartment, building or land; long-term and relatively stable; may bring good profit later if the place has development potential

lessons.title: 571. Ch 45 · Grammar B: –(으)려던 참이다, I was just about to do something
lessons.subtitle: -(으)려던 참이다 · -(으)려던 참에 · 아침을 먹으려던 참이었어 · 우체국에 가려던 참에

explanations.title: “I was just about to do something”
explanations.body: In Korean, the grammar pattern –(으)려던 참이다 is used to convey the meaning of “I was just about (to do something).” For example (over the phone; the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 뭐 해?
examples.translation: mwo hae? — What are you doing?

examples.text: 응, 아침을 먹으려던 참이었어.
examples.translation: eung, achimeul meogeuryeodeon chamieosseo. — Uh, I was just about to eat breakfast.

explanations.title: The tenses and the conjunctive ending
explanations.body: –(으)려던 참이다, which comes from –(으)려고 하던 참이다, literally means “(It) is the moment I intended to do (something).” This grammar pattern can be expressed either in the present tense –(으)려던 참이다 or the past tense –(으)려던 참이었다, although the past tense version is used more often. On the other hand, when –(으)려던 참에 is a conjunctive ending, it can be translated as when I was about to do something or at the moment I intended to do something. For example (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 아침을 먹으려던 참에 친구가 방문했다.
examples.translation: achimeul meogeuryeodeon chame chinguga bangmunhaetda. — When I was about to eat breakfast, a friend of mine visited (me).

examples.text: 버스를 타려던 참에 친구를 만났어요.
examples.translation: beoseureul taryeodeon chame chingureul mannasseoyo. — When I was about to get on the bus, I met a friend.

explanations.title: The pattern
explanations.body: Expressing “I was just about to do something”: action verb stem + (으)려던 참이다. More examples (the English is the book’s):

examples.text: 민호야, 같이 점심 먹자.
examples.translation: minhoya, gachi jeomsim meokja. — Minho, let’s have lunch together.

examples.text: 그래. 나도 점심 먹으려던 참이었어.
examples.translation: geurae. nado jeomsim meogeuryeodeon chamieosseo. — OK. I was about to have lunch, too.

examples.text: 김 일병, 이거 공책에 썼어요?
examples.translation: gim ilbyeong, igeo gongchaege sseosseoyo? — PFC Kim, did you write in the notebook?

examples.text: 지금 쓰려던 참이에요.
examples.translation: jigeum sseuryeodeon chamieyo. — I was just about to write.

examples.text: 엄마한테 전화했어?
examples.translation: eommahante jeonhwahaesseo? — Did you call mom?

examples.text: 아니. 막 전화하려는 참이었어.
examples.translation: ani. mak jeonhwaharyeoneun chamieosseo. — No. I was about to call her.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Speaking): on the phone
explanations.body: Partner A asks what Partner B is doing now. Partner B picks up a topic card and answers using the topic and either –(으)려던 참이다 or –(으)려고 하다. The book’s model (the English is mine):

examples.text: 김 일병, 지금 뭐 해요?
examples.translation: gim ilbyeong, jigeum mwo haeyo? — PFC Kim, what are you doing now?

examples.text: 아침을 먹으려던 참이에요.
examples.translation: achimeul meogeuryeodeon chamieyo. — I was just about to eat breakfast.

examples.text: 아침을 먹으려고 해요.
examples.translation: achimeul meogeuryeogo haeyo. — I am about to eat breakfast.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading): Miyoung’s sticky notes
explanations.body: The following messages are sticky notes Miyoung (미영) left for her colleagues; the book asks you to fill in a table in English (note; what she was about to do; what happened). The notes are the book’s (the signatures “이미영” are dropped); the English is mine.

examples.text: 인희 씨, 제가 우체국에 가려던 참에 고향에서 친구가 왔어요.
examples.translation: inhui ssi, jega ucheguge garyeodeon chame gohyangeseo chinguga wasseoyo. — Inhui, just when I was about to go to the post office, a friend came from my hometown.

examples.text: 미안하지만 이 소포 좀 부쳐 주시겠어요?
examples.translation: mianhajiman i sopo jom bucheo jusigesseoyo? — I am sorry, but could you send this package for me?

examples.text: 나중에 커피 살게요.
examples.translation: najunge keopi salgeyo. — I will buy you coffee later.

examples.text: 진호 씨, 핸드폰을 하나 새로 장만하려던 참에 핸드폰을 선물로 주셨네요.
examples.translation: jinho ssi, haendeuponeul hana saero jangmanharyeodeon chame haendeuponeul seonmullo jusyeonneyo. — Jinho, just when I was about to get a new cell phone, you gave me a cell phone as a gift.

examples.text: 고마워요. 잘 쓸게요.
examples.translation: gomawoyo. jal sseulgeyo. — Thank you. I will use it well.

examples.text: 현수 씨, 적금을 들려고 하던 참에 현수 씨가 좋은 투자 상품을 소개해 주었어요.
examples.translation: hyeonsu ssi, jeokgeumeul deullyeogo hadeon chame hyeonsu ssiga joeun tuja sangpumeul sogaehae jueosseoyo. — Hyunsu, just when I was going to open an installment savings account, you introduced me to a good investment product.

examples.text: 고마워요. 다음에도 좋은 조언 부탁 드릴게요.
examples.translation: gomawoyo. daeumedo joeun joeon butak deurilgeyo. — Thank you. I will ask you for good advice next time too.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Speaking): a role-play model
explanations.body: One partner makes a request and the other responds using –(으)려던 참이다 or –(으)려고 하다. The book’s model dialog (the book writes “가려던 참이야/가려고 해” and I use the first; the English is mine):

examples.text: 김 일병, 뭐 해?
examples.translation: gim ilbyeong, mwo hae? — PFC Kim, what are you doing?

examples.text: 지금 우체국에 가려던 참이야.
examples.translation: jigeum ucheguge garyeodeon chamiya. — I was just about to go to the post office.

examples.text: 나도 소포를 부치러 우체국에 가려던 참이었어.
examples.translation: nado soporeul buchireo ucheguge garyeodeon chamieosseo. — I was about to go to the post office to send a package, too.

examples.text: 그래? 내가 대신 부쳐 줄까?
examples.translation: geurae? naega daesin bucheo julkka? — Really? Shall I send it for you?

examples.text: 응. 고마워.
examples.translation: eung. gomawo. — Yes. Thanks.

explanations.title: More sentences (mine)
explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own (the English is mine):

examples.text: 숙제를 하려던 참이에요.
examples.translation: sukjereul haryeodeon chamieyo. — I was just about to do my homework.

examples.text: 지금 막 나가려던 참이었어요.
examples.translation: jigeum mak nagaryeodeon chamieosseoyo. — I was just about to go out right now.

examples.text: 샤워를 하려던 참에 전화가 왔어요.
examples.translation: syaworeul haryeodeon chame jeonhwaga wasseoyo. — Just when I was about to take a shower, a phone call came.

examples.text: 저녁을 준비하려던 참이에요.
examples.translation: jeonyeogeul junbiharyeodeon chamieyo. — I am just about to prepare dinner.

examples.text: 자려던 참에 친구가 찾아왔어요.
examples.translation: jaryeodeon chame chinguga chajawasseoyo. — Just when I was about to go to sleep, a friend came to see me.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with so that they can provide other activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify and discuss sectors of the Korean economy including the gross domestic product (GDP), economic growth rate, trade volume, trading partners, etc.; identify and discuss major types of financial investments and their characteristics; and read and say large numbers in Korean.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; ~에도 (불구하고) or –(으)ㄴ/는데도 (불구하고) (in spite of; despite); –(으)려던 참이다 (I was just about to do something); and the Sino-Korean syllables within 조선업 (造船業), 약세 (弱勢), 하락 (下落), 급감 (急減), and 장단점 (長短點).

explanations.title: Activities left out

They are audio, computer and group activities and are left out.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank. The Loan Words section repeats 로봇 and 펀드, which I list once. The last section lists the Sino-Korean related words of 조선업, 약세, 하락, 급감 and 장단점 as the book gives them.

The example sentences with digits and letters are respelled in Hangul (70년대 → 칠십 년대; 1조 5000억 원 → 일 조 오천억 원; LG전자 → 엘지전자; 16-17세 → 열여섯 살에서 열일곱 살; 1인당 → 일인당; the book’s key 1인당 is written 일인당).

explanations.title: What Chapter 46 teaches (정치)
explanations.body:
Chapter 46, “Politics”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations (the Korean government, the Korean election system, the Korean trial system) with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and write about basic features of the Korean government, such as its organizations, leaders, and their roles; talk about the electoral systems for the president, national assembly members, chiefs of local government, and their procedures; identify and talk about the Korean judicial system; and extract information about the judicial system, such as types of sentences, procedures, and judicial decision(s).

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; a summary of sentence connectors; the conjunctive ending –거든 (if) used in a command/request; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 입법부 (立法府), 장관 (長官), 투표 (投票), 총선 (總選), and 법원 (法院).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 입법부 (立法府)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means the legislative branch (of a government) or a legislature that passes, amends, and repeals laws. The first syllable 입/립 (立) means establish(ed) or erect(ed), as in 주립 대학교 (a state university; “state-established university”) and 시립 도서관 (a municipal library; “library established by city”). The second syllable 법 (法) means law or method, as in 민법 (the civil law), 군법 (military law), 법원 (a court house; “law house”), and 낙법 (defensive way of falling down; “falling-down method”). The last syllable 부 (府) means government office, as in 행정부 (the executive; the administration) and 사법부 (the judicial branch; the judiciary). Thus the literal meaning of the word is “government office that establishes laws.” The book asks you to guess the meaning of 사립 대학교, 도립 병원, 불법 무기, 공립 대학교, 해양법, 국제법, 국립공원 and 국내법 (my answers):

rows: a municipal library; “library established by city”
defensive way of falling down; “falling-down method”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 장관 (長官)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means a Cabinet Minister or Secretary. The first syllable 장 (長) means head or chief (of an organization), as in 사장, 과장, 팀장, 반장, etc. The second syllable 관 (官) means (government) official/officer or government, as in 관용차 (an official vehicle; “car for government use”), 관직 (a government post; a government job), 법관 (a judge; “officer of law”), and 차관 (a vice-minister; a deputy secretary; “next official”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 장관 is “chief official” or “chief officer.” The book asks you to guess 교장, 총장, 시장, 교관, 소방관, 경찰관, 통일부 장관 and 국방부 장관 (the book’s examples 사장, 과장, 팀장 and 반장 are glossed here by me; my answers):

rows: a class president; a squad leader
an official vehicle; “car for government use”
a government post; a government job
a vice-minister; a deputy secretary; “next official”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 투표 (投票)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means vote, voting, or (casting) a ballot. The first syllable 투 (投) means throw or cast, as in 투망 (a cast/thrown net), 투수 (a pitcher; a hurler; “thrower”), 투항 (surrender [to the enemy]; “throwing surrender”), 투자 (investment; “casting capital”), and 투기꾼 (a speculator; “professional who casts opportunity”). The second syllable 표 (票) means ticket as in 버스표, 기차표, and 비행기 [표] (the book prints 비행기), or ballot, as in 찬성표 (a vote in favor of; an assenting vote; “consenting ballot”), 반대표 (a vote against; a dissenting vote; “opposing vote”), and 표심 (hearts [and minds] of voters; “ballot heart”). Thus the literal meaning of the word 투표 is “ticket throwing” or “ballot casting.”

rows: a vote in favor of; an assenting vote; “consenting ballot”
a vote against; a dissenting vote; “opposing vote”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 총선 (總選)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word, which comes from 총선거, means a general election (in which all or most members of a given political body are chosen). The first syllable 총 (總) means whole, total, or general, as in 총사령관 (commander-in-chief; “general commanding officer”), 총장 (president of a university; a chancellor; “general chief”), and 총회 (a general meeting; a general conference). The second syllable 선 (選) means selection, as in 선택하다 (to choose; to select) and 차선 (the second best; the next best; “second selection”). Thus the literal meaning of the word is “general selection” or “general election.” The book asks you to guess 총액, 총수입, 총점, 낙선, 선수 and 재선 (the book glosses 액 [額]: amount [of money]; my answers):

a general meeting; a general conference

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 법원 (法院)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means a court of justice or a courthouse; 법 (法) means law, and 원 (院) means a house or institute. Thus the literal meaning of the word is “law house.” The book asks you to guess 민법, 형법, 불법, 고아원, 학원 and 양로원 (my answers):

explanations.title: Topic A: the Korean government (대한민국 정부)
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a social studies textbook. It describes the organization of the Korean government. (The English is mine; the book gives none. The text is the book’s with 3부 spelled out as 삼 부 and the dots in 행정·입법·사법 written as commas. The book’s footnote: 대통령 중심제 [“president-centered system”] refers to a [full] presidential system.)

explanations.title: The chart of the government (대한민국 정부 조직도)
explanations.body: The book prints an organization chart (a picture, not reproduced here; the book says that on the screen you can click it to see a complete chart of the executive branch). Its structure: 대한민국 정부 is divided into 입법부, 행정부 and 사법부; the 행정부 has the 대통령, the 국무총리, the ministries (행정 각 부, 19 of them) and 19 services (청).

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 부 (府) and 부 (部)
explanations.body: In this chapter you will encounter a number of words that end in 부, as in 입법부, 사법부, 통일부, 국방부, etc. However, depending on the words, the Sino-Korean syllable can be 부 (府), which means a (main) government branch or office, or 부 (部), which means part, department, ministry, or region. Thus, the three branches of government, 입법부 (legislative), 사법부 (judicial), and 행정부 (executive), use the Sino-Korean syllable 부 (府). However, the ministries of government, such as 통일부 (ministry of unification) and 국방부 (ministry of defense), all use the Sino-Korean syllable 부 (部).

explanations.title: 한국에서는: the executive branch of South Korea
explanations.body: The executive branch of South Korea is led by the president, who resides in the Yongsan Presidential Office (용산 대통령실) in Seoul. Prior to its relocation in 2022, the official residence of the president had been Cheong Wa Dae (the Blue House/청와대) since 1948. 청와대 is now a public park. The executive branch consists of the president, the prime minister, and cabinet-level ministers. The South Korean government currently has 19 ministries. Note that the names and numbers of ministries and services can change as part of governmental reforms, such as the 2013 reversion of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (외교통상부) to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (외교부).

explanations.title: 북한에서는: the government of North Korea
explanations.body: The Chairman (국무위원장) of the State Affairs Commission of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea is the head of state in North Korea. The “국무위원장” heads the State Affairs Commission (SAC), which is the highest leadership institution in North Korea, and serves as the commander-in-chief of the North Korean armed forces. The SAC is defined by the 2016 constitution as the supreme policy-oriented leadership body of state power. The Cabinet (내각) can be considered the administrative state body that serves as North Korea’s ‘government’. The Cabinet is headed by the Premier (내각총리), with Vice Premiers (부총리) and Ministers (상) who are in charge of each ministry. The Supreme People’s Assembly (SPA/최고인민회의) is the vehicle through which the Party carries out its decisions. Therefore, the SPA is the highest political body in North Korea. Assembly meetings are held once or twice a year. In reality, the SPA is a rubber-stamp assembly that merely passes laws and decisions handed down by the Workers’ Party of Korea (로동당). During recess periods, the functions of the SPA are carried out by the Standing Committee (최고인민회의 상임위원회). (Source given by the book: DLIFLC/Area Studies.)

explanations.title: Topic B: the Korean election system (한국의 선거 제도)
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from the Korean National Election Commission website. (The English is mine; the book gives none. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out: 5년 is 오 년, 4월과 10월 is 사월과 시월. The book’s footnotes: 3 A mayor and a provincial governor [도지사] are examples of 지방자치단체장; 4 직선제 is the shortened form of 직접선거 제도; 5 중앙 선거관리 위원회 [Central National Election Commission] is an independent government organization that monitors presidential and general elections; 지방 선거관리 위원회 monitors local elections.)

examples.text: 한국의 선거에는 대통령 선거, 국회 의원 총선거, 지방자치 단체장 및 의원 선거가 있다.
examples.translation: hangugui seongeoeneun daetongnyeong seongeo, gukoe uiwon chongseongeo, jibangjachi danchejang mit uiwon seongeoga itda. — Korea’s elections include the presidential election, the National Assembly general election, and the elections of heads of local governments and of (local) assembly members.

examples.text: 원칙적으로 한국의 모든 선거는 직선제이다.
examples.translation: wonchikjeogeuro hangugui modeun seongeoneun jikseonjeida. — In principle, all of Korea’s elections are direct elections.

examples.text: 대통령 선거는 오 년마다 있으며 총선과 지방자치단체장 선거는 사 년마다 있다.
examples.translation: daetongnyeong seongeoneun o nyeonmada isseumyeo chongseongwa jibangjachidanchejang seongeoneun sa nyeonmada itda. — The presidential election is held every five years, and the general election and the elections of heads of local governments are held every four years.

examples.text: 대통령의 임기는 오 년 단임으로 제한되어 있으나 국회의원은 여러 번 재임할 수 있다.
examples.translation: daetongnyeongui imgineun o nyeon danimeuro jehandoeeo isseuna gukoeuiwoneun yeoreo beon jaeimhal su itda. — The president’s term is limited to a single term of five years, but a member of the National Assembly can serve again many times.

examples.text: 하지만, 시장이나 도지사 같은 지방자치단체장은 세 번까지 연임할 수 있다.
examples.translation: hajiman, sijangina dojisa gateun jibangjachidanchejangeun se beonkkaji yeonimhal su itda. — However, heads of local governments such as mayors or provincial governors can serve consecutive terms up to three times.

examples.text: 한국의 선거일은 수요일이고 보궐선거는 매년 사월과 시월에 있다.
examples.translation: hangugui seongeoireun suyoirigo bogwolseongeoneun maenyeon sawolgwa siwore itda. — Election day in Korea is a Wednesday, and by-elections are held every April and October.

examples.text: 선거 운동 기간에는 투명하고 공정한 선거를 위해 중앙 선거관리 위원회와 각 지방 선거관리 위원회가 선거활동을 감시한다.
examples.translation: seongeo undong giganeneun tumyeonghago gongjeonghan seongeoreul wihae jungang seongeogwalli wiwonhoewa gak jibang seongeogwalli wiwonhoega seongeohwaldongeul gamsihanda. — During the election campaign period, the Central Election Commission and each local election commission watch over election activities for a transparent and fair election.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: acronyms and nicknames in politics
explanations.body:
Acronyms are used heavily in Korean politics for proper names and titles. For example, 대선 is a shortened form of 대통령 선거. Other examples include 총선 for 국회의원 총선거, 선관위 for 선거 관리 위원회, 직선제 for 직접 선거제도, and 지자체 for 지방자치단체.

In the political realm, Koreans frequently refer to influential politicians by their Romanized initials. For example, newspapers often refer to 이명박 대통령 as MB, the initials for his given names. In the same manner, 김대중 대통령, a Nobel Peace Prize winner and famous historical figure, is referred to as DJ.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: election culture and the 1987 direct election
explanations.body: Although Korea is a democracy, its election culture and process differ somewhat from that of the United States. In Korea, presidential and general election days are designated as holidays to encourage voter turnout. Also, Korean elections are determined by popular vote and do not involve an electoral college. In 1972, President Park Junghee changed the then-direct presidential election to an indirect election in a maneuver to perpetuate his presidency. This system remained in place until 1987 when the so-called 6.10 민주항쟁 (Democratic Revolt of June 10th) resulted in a return to direct election. This achievement is part of Korea’s modern history. Citizens continually rallied against the military dictators who seized power via coups and manipulated the law to maintain that power. The movement was driven by the middle class, who wanted to change the system and elect the president directly. The movement gained momentum throughout the spring of 1987 and culminated in June of that year, when huge numbers of college students, professors, white and blue collar workers, retirees, and homemakers protested on a daily basis. Finally, the government surrendered to public demand and the Korean people obtained the right to a direct vote. (The book shows a 2022 presidential election poster [대통령 선거 벽보] from 연합뉴스; the picture is left out.)

lessons.title: 580. Ch 46 · Grammar in Focus: revisiting sentence connectors
lessons.subtitle: 문법 탐구 · 그리고 · 게다가 · 또 · 특히 · 예를 들면 · 그렇지만 · 하지만 · 그러나 · 그런데 · 그래서 · 따라서 · 그전에 · 그다음에

explanations.title: Revisiting sentence connectors
explanations.body:
So far you have learned a number of sentence connectors used to join two independent sentences and show a relationship between them, as in 우리 부모님은 키가 커요. 하지만 제 형님은 키가 작아요 (My parents are tall, but my older brother is small). Note that the connector 하지만 is used to join the two sentences in a contrasting/opposing relationship.

Sentence connectors you have learned thus far can be broken into four key categories: addition, contrast, causality, and sequence. Note that some of the connectors can fall into multiple categories. (In the book’s tables, a slash or a bracket joins forms such as 그렇지만/하지만, 그럼/그러면, 반면(에), 또(한), 그뿐(만) 아니라, 그전(에) and 그다음(에)/그 후(에); here each form is listed on its own, and the numbers in the examples are spelled out. The English of the examples is mine.)

explanations.title: Addition
explanations.body: These connectors are used to add more information, to introduce a specific example or topic, or to show similarity.

examples.text: 주말에 바닷가에 갔어요. 그리고 친구랑 영화도 봤어요.
examples.translation: jumare badatgae gasseoyo. geurigo chingurang yeonghwado bwasseoyo. — I went to the beach on the weekend. And I also watched a movie with a friend.

examples.text: 어제 간 식당은 종업원들이 아주 친절했어요. 게다가 값도 싸고 맛있었어요.
examples.translation: eoje gan sikdangeun jongeobwondeuri aju chinjeolhaesseoyo. gedaga gapdo ssago masisseosseoyo. — The waiters at the restaurant I went to yesterday were very kind. What’s more, it was cheap and delicious.

examples.text: 이번 주말에 책을 많이 읽을 거예요. 또 동생이랑 테니스도 칠 거예요.
examples.translation: ibeon jumare chaegeul mani ilgeul geoyeyo. tto dongsaengirang teniseudo chil geoyeyo. — I will read a lot of books this weekend. Also, I will play tennis with my younger sibling.

examples.text: 제 동생은 악기 연주하는 게 취미예요. 특히 피아노를 아주 잘 쳐요.
examples.translation: je dongsaengeun akgi yeonjuhaneun ge chwimiyeyo. teuki pianoreul aju jal cheoyo. — My younger sibling’s hobby is playing instruments. In particular, he/she plays the piano very well.

examples.text: 저는 친환경 운동을 위해 노력해요. 예를 들면 자동차 대신에 자전거를 타고 출퇴근해요.
examples.translation: jeoneun chinhwangyeong undongeul wihae noryeokaeyo. yereul deulmyeon jadongcha daesine jajeongeoreul tago chultoegeunhaeyo. — I make an effort for the eco-friendly movement. For example, I commute by bike instead of by car.

examples.text: 저희 할인점은 스물네 시간 영업을 하고 있습니다. 그뿐만 아니라 이번에 사백여 평의 주차장도 새로 지었습니다.
examples.translation: jeohui harinjeomeun seumulle sigan yeongeobeul hago itseumnida. geuppunman anira ibeone sabaegyeo pyeongui juchajangdo saero jieotseumnida. — Our discount store is open twenty-four hours. Not only that, we have also newly built a parking lot of about 400 pyeong this time.

explanations.title: Contrast
explanations.body: These connectors are used to show contrast between two statements or to express a new statement without invalidating the truth of a previously expressed statement.

examples.text: 어제 친구와 등산을 가기로 했어요. 그렇지만 비가 와서 못 갔어요.
examples.translation: eoje chinguwa deungsaneul gagiro haesseoyo. geureochiman biga waseo mot gasseoyo. — I decided to go hiking with a friend yesterday. But it rained, so I could not go.

examples.text: 오늘까지 일을 끝내야 해요. 그러나 일이 너무 많아서 못 끝낼 것 같아요.
examples.translation: oneulkkaji ireul kkeunnaeya haeyo. geureona iri neomu manaseo mot kkeunnael geot gatayo. — I have to finish the work by today. Yet there is so much work that I don’t think I can finish.

examples.text: 벌써 사월이에요. 그런데 아직도 날씨가 추워요.
examples.translation: beolsseo saworieyo. geureonde ajikdo nalssiga chuwoyo. — It is already April. But the weather is still cold.

examples.text: 지금 바쁘세요? 그럼 제가 나중에 다시 올게요.
examples.translation: jigeum bappeuseyo? geureom jega najunge dasi olgeyo. — Are you busy now? Then I will come again later.

examples.text: 한국어는 너무 어려워요. 그래도 한국어 배우는 건 재미있어요.
examples.translation: hangugeoneun neomu eoryeowoyo. geuraedo hangugeo baeuneun geon jaemiisseoyo. — Korean is too difficult. Still, learning Korean is fun.

examples.text: 제 누나는 일식을 좋아해요. 반면 저는 중식을 좋아해요.
examples.translation: je nunaneun ilsigeul joahaeyo. banmyeon jeoneun jungsigeul joahaeyo. — My older sister likes Japanese food. On the other hand, I like Chinese food.

explanations.title: Causality
explanations.body: These connectors are used to explain cause/effect and reasons or results.

examples.text: 고등학교 때부터 공부를 아주 열심히 했어요. 그 결과 원하는 대학에 들어갔어요.
examples.translation: godeunghakgyo ttaebuteo gongbureul aju yeolsimhi haesseoyo. geu gyeolgwa wonhaneun daehage deureogasseoyo. — I studied very hard from high school. As a result, I got into the university I wanted.

examples.text: 다음 달에 제 딸 돌잔치를 할 거예요. 그러니까 꼭 오셔서 축하해 주세요.
examples.translation: daeum dare je ttal doljanchireul hal geoyeyo. geureonikka kkok osyeoseo chukahae juseyo. — I will hold my daughter’s first-birthday party next month. So please be sure to come and congratulate her.

examples.text: 파티에 가서 너무 많이 먹었어요. 그래서 지금 배불러요.
examples.translation: patie gaseo neomu mani meogeosseoyo. geuraeseo jigeum baebulleoyo. — I went to a party and ate too much. So I am full now.

examples.text: 한국의 서비스업이 급성장하고 있습니다. 따라서 내년에는 경제성장률이 이 퍼센트 오를 것으로 보입니다.
examples.translation: hangugui seobiseueobi geupseongjanghago itseumnida. ttaraseo naenyeoneneun gyeongjeseongjangnyuri i peosenteu oreul geoseuro boimnida. — Korea’s service industry is growing rapidly. Therefore the economic growth rate is expected to rise by 2 percent next year.

explanations.title: Sequence
explanations.body: These connectors are used to express chronological or logical sequence.

examples.text: 지금 나가실 거예요? 그전에 약 드시고 가세요.
examples.translation: jigeum nagasil geoyeyo? geujeone yak deusigo gaseyo. — Are you going out now? Take your medicine before that, and go.

examples.text: 저는 저녁 여섯 시에 집에 돌아옵니다. 그다음에 샤워합니다.
examples.translation: jeoneun jeonyeok yeoseot sie jibe doraomnida. geudaeume syawohamnida. — I return home at six in the evening. After that I take a shower.

exercises.explanation: 예를 들면 means “for example; for instance”.
그뿐만 아니라 means “not only that; additionally”.
그런데 means “but; however; by the way”.
그 결과 means “so that; as a result”.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): two women who ran for local office
explanations.body: The following newspaper article is about two women who became naturalized Korean citizens and are running for public office. The book asks you to fill in a table in English (the candidate’s original country, party affiliation, office sought and life after coming to Korea). The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (2명 is 두 명; 1992년 is 천구백구십이 년; 20세 is 스무 살); the book glosses 귀화: naturalization and 연합회: association. The English is mine.

examples.text: 자유평화당은 일본과 태국에서 귀화한 여성 두 명을 지방의원 후보로 결정했다.
examples.translation: jayupyeonghwadangeun ilbongwa taegugeseo gwihwahan yeoseong du myeongeul jibanguiwon huboro gyeoljeonghaetda. — The Free Peace Party decided on two women naturalized from Japan and Thailand as candidates for local assembly.

examples.text: 자평당 대변인은 일본에서 귀화한 신미자 씨를 경상북도 의원 후보로, 또 태국에서 귀화한 한에리카 씨를 부산시의원 후보로 결정했다고 밝혔다.
examples.translation: japyeongdang daebyeonineun ilboneseo gwihwahan sinmija ssireul gyeongsangbukdo uiwon huboro, tto taegugeseo gwihwahan hanerika ssireul busansiuiwon huboro gyeoljeonghaetdago balkyeotda. — The party’s spokesperson announced that it had decided on Ms. Shin Mi-ja, naturalized from Japan, as a candidate for the Gyeongsangbuk-do assembly, and on Ms. Han Erika, naturalized from Thailand, as a candidate for the Busan city council.

examples.text: 신 씨는 대학교 졸업 후 공무원으로 일하다가 한국인 남편을 만나서 천구백구십이 년에 한국으로 왔다.
examples.translation: sin ssineun daehakgyo joreop hu gongmuwoneuro ilhadaga hangugin nampyeoneul mannaseo cheongubaekgusibi nyeone hangugeuro watda. — Ms. Shin worked as a civil servant after graduating from university, met a Korean husband and came to Korea in 1992.

examples.text: 아들 둘을 낳아 키우고, 현재는 경상북도 다문화 여성연합회에서 일하고 있다.
examples.translation: adeul dureul naa kiugo, hyeonjaeneun gyeongsangbukdo damunhwa yeoseongyeonhapoeeseo ilhago itda. — She bore and raised two sons and now works at the Gyeongsangbuk-do Multicultural Women’s Association.

examples.text: 한에리카 씨는 태국에서 간호대학에 다니던 중 스무 살 때 한국인 남편을 만나 한국에 왔다.
examples.translation: hanerika ssineun taegugeseo ganhodaehage danideon jung seumu sal ttae hangugin nampyeoneul manna hanguge watda. — While attending nursing college in Thailand, Ms. Han Erika met a Korean husband at the age of twenty and came to Korea.

examples.text: 현재 시댁 식구 등과 함께 살고 있으며, 부산시 온라인 다문화 여성 네트워크에서 일하고 있다.
examples.translation: hyeonjae sidaek sikgu deunggwa hamkke salgo isseumyeo, busansi ollain damunhwa yeoseong neteuwokeueseo ilhago itda. — She now lives with her husband’s family and others and works at the Busan Online Multicultural Women’s Network.

examples.text: 두 후보가 당선되면 처음으로 귀화 외국인이 지방의원으로 뽑히는 것이다.
examples.translation: du huboga dangseondoemyeon cheoeumeuro gwihwa oegugini jibanguiwoneuro ppopineun geosida. — If the two candidates are elected, it will be the first time naturalized foreigners are elected as local assembly members.

rows: Came in 1992 after meeting her Korean husband; raised two sons; works at the Gyeongsangbuk-do Multicultural Women’s Association

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 2 (listening to four incomplete comments cut off after the connector, and writing a possible second sentence) and Follow-up 4 (a pair task: building a ten-sentence story with connectors on a sheet of paper that is passed back and forth, then posting the stories on the wall and voting) are audio, writing and pair activities. In the chapter’s Activities pages, Activity 1 (pairs arrange sentence strips into a well-organized story about Mr. Hwang, a candidate for the National Assembly; the strips are not printed in the student text), Activity 2 (listening to audio clips about a local election in 경상북도: the problem identified and the actions to be taken, and four activities planned by an employee of the 경상북도 선거관리위원회) and Activity 4 (pairs create a presidential election system or change an existing one: direct or indirect, term length, possibility of reelection and three qualifications of candidates, then present it in Korean and the class chooses the best) are audio, strip, pair and group activities.

explanations.title: Topic C: the Korean trial system (한국의 재판 제도)
explanations.body: The following information is from a brochure showing the process of a trial and an appeal for civil and criminal cases. (The English is mine; the book gives none.)

examples.text: 개인이나 단체가 다른 사람이나 단체를 상대로 고소할 때 하는 재판을 민사 재판이라고 합니다.
examples.translation: gaeinina danchega dareun saramina danchereul sangdaero gosohal ttae haneun jaepaneul minsa jaepanirago hamnida. — A trial held when an individual or a group files a complaint against another person or group is called a civil trial.

examples.text: 이와 달리 검사에 의해 기소된 피고인을 상대로 하는 재판은 형사 재판이라고 합니다.
examples.translation: iwa dalli geomsae uihae gisodoen pigoineul sangdaero haneun jaepaneun hyeongsa jaepanirago hamnida. — In contrast to this, a trial against a defendant who was indicted by a prosecutor is called a criminal trial.

explanations.title: The process of a trial and an appeal (the brochure’s chart)
explanations.body: The brochure’s chart (a picture, not reproduced here) shows, for both a civil trial (민사 재판) and a criminal trial (형사 재판), these boxes in order; the book’s words are shown with my English, and the dot in 유죄·무죄 is written as a comma. The chart then shows the courts, 지방법원 (District Court), 고등법원 (High Court) and 대법원 (Supreme Court), with an arrow 항소 (appeal) from the first to the second and an arrow 상고 (appeal) from the second to the third.

examples.text: 소송이 제기되면 법원에서 재판이 열린다.
examples.translation: sosongi jegidoemyeon beobwoneseo jaepani yeollinda. — When a lawsuit is filed, a trial is held at a court.

explanations.title: 한국어에는: 형 (刑) and 심 (審)
explanations.body:
1. 형 (刑), which means punishment (for a crime), is usually used in a legal context and can be combined with nouns that describe a type of punishment, as in 벌금형 (fine), 징역형 (imprisonment [with hard labor]), 사형 (capital punishment), etc.

2. 심 (審) is derived from the word 심리 (a trial). It literally means “look into” or “investigate” and can be combined with other nouns. Also frequently used in legal contexts, it means a court, as in 1심 (1st trial; the local court), 2심 (2nd trial; the high court), 3심 (3rd trial; the supreme court), etc. (The numbers are spelled out in the table: 일 심, 이 심, 삼 심.)

explanations.title: 한국에서는: the Korean courts
explanations.body:
The Korean judicial system is based on the three-tier trial system (3심제), composed of district courts (지방법원), the high courts (고등법원), and the Supreme Court (대법원). Other courts exercise specialized functions, with the Patent Court (특허법원) at the same level as the high courts; the family court (가정법원) and the administrative court (행정법원) are at the same level as the district courts.

Unlike U.S. courts where the jury decides a trial’s outcome, almost all court decisions in Korea are made solely by the judge(s). In January 2008, however, 국민참여재판 (People Participating Trial) was introduced and is being implemented in some criminal cases. In this form of trial, the jury relays its verdict to the judge, in the manner of the U.S. judicial system.

explanations.title: 북한에서는: the judiciary of North Korea
explanations.body: In the North Korean judicial process, both adjudicative and prosecuting bodies function as powerful weapons for the proletarian dictatorship. The constitution states that justice is administered by the central court, provincial or special city-level courts, the people’s court, or special courts. The Central Court, the highest court of appeals, stands at the apex of the court system. In the case of special cities directly under central authority, provincial or municipal courts serve as the courts of first instance for civil and criminal cases at the intermediate level. At the lowest level are the people’s courts, established in ordinary cities, counties, and urban districts. Special courts exist for the armed forces and for railroad workers. (Source given by the book: Library of Congress.)

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): read each trial description
explanations.body: Read each trial description and place a check mark next to the type of trial (civil or criminal) and the court (district, high or supreme). The book’s five descriptions are given below with the numbers spelled out (1심 is 일 심; 1년 is 일 년; 5,000만 원 is 오천만 원; 1천500만 원 is 천오백만 원); the English and the answers are mine.

rows: 회사에서 일하다가 다쳤는데 회사가 치료비를 안 주었습니다. 그래서 회사를 법원에 고소했습니다. 어제 처음으로 재판이 열렸는데 이 재판에서 판사가 피고인 회사에 손해배상을 하라고 판결했습니다.
사기 친 사람을 고소해서 재판을 두 번 했습니다. 그런데 두 번 다 판결이 마음에 안 듭니다. 일 심에서는 피고가 징역 일 년 형을 받았고 이 심에서는 집행유예 십 개월을 받았습니다. 그래서 이 법원에 가서 재판을 받으려고 합니다.
어제 오후 사기 혐의로 구속 기소됐던 송 모 씨의 일 심 재판이 열렸습니다. 이동욱 판사는 피고에 대해 오천만 원을 손해 배상하라고 선고했습니다.
이 재판에서 김 모 씨에 대해 징역 오 년의 형이 선고됐습니다. 김 씨는 부모를 폭행한 후 통장을 빼앗아 천오백만 원을 찾아간 혐의로 기소됐었습니다. 김 씨의 변호사에 따르면 김 씨는 이 심에 항소할 것이라고 합니다.
국회의원 조형완 씨는 선거법 위반으로 검거돼서 집행유예 이 년 육 개월을 선고받았습니다. 그래서 항소했지만 여기에서도 일 심에서 받은 형이 확정됐습니다.

I got hurt while working at a company, but the company did not give me treatment costs. So I filed a complaint against the company in court. The first trial was held yesterday, and in this trial the judge ruled that the defendant company must pay compensation for damages.

I filed a complaint against a person who committed fraud, and we had two trials. But I do not like the judgment either time. In the first trial the defendant received a one-year prison sentence, and in the second trial a ten-month suspended sentence. So I intend to go to this court and have a trial.

Yesterday afternoon the first trial of Mr. Song, who had been arrested and indicted on a fraud charge, was held. Judge Lee Dong-wook announced that the defendant must pay 50 million won in compensation for damages.

In this trial, a five-year prison sentence was announced against Mr. Kim. Mr. Kim had been indicted on the charge of assaulting his parents, taking their bankbook and withdrawing 15 million won. According to Mr. Kim’s lawyer, he will appeal to the second trial.

National Assembly member Cho Hyeong-wan was arrested for violating the election law and was sentenced to a two-year-six-month suspended sentence. So he appealed, but here too the sentence he received in the first trial was confirmed.

explanations.title: Notes on my answers (mine)
explanations.body: 1: a lawsuit by the injured worker against the company and an order to pay damages in the first trial: civil, district court. 2: two trials have already been held (a 1-year prison sentence and a suspended sentence), so the next court is the third tier: criminal (징역, 집행유예), Supreme Court. 3: a first trial, so the district court; the description mixes an indictment on a fraud charge (a criminal word) with an order to pay damages, and I mark it civil because the judgment is damages; criminal is arguable. 4: a prison sentence and indictment, so criminal; the lawyer says he will appeal to the second trial, so this is the first trial, district court. 5: criminal (a suspended sentence for violating the election law); he appealed, so this is the second trial at the high court, where the first-trial sentence was upheld.

lessons.title: 584. Ch 46 · Grammar in Focus: –거든, a conditional in a command or request
lessons.subtitle: 문법 탐구 · –거든 · –(으)면 · 명령 · 부탁 · 조건 · –거든요

explanations.title: Expressing a conditional in a command/request
explanations.body: In Chapter 9, you learned that the conjunctive ending –(으)면 (if; when) is used to express a conditional, as in 비가 많이 오면 등산 가지 마세요 (If it rains heavily, do not go hiking). The conjunctive ending –거든, which you will learn in this lesson, is also used to express a conditional. However, –거든 is used primarily in a command or request. For example (the book prints 등산가지; the spacing is mine):

examples.text: 비가 많이 오거든 등산 가지 마세요.
examples.translation: biga mani ogeodeun deungsan gaji maseyo. — If it rains heavily, do not go hiking.

examples.text: 서울에 도착하거든 전화해.
examples.translation: seoure dochakageodeun jeonhwahae. — If you arrive in Seoul, call me.

explanations.title: Note
explanations.body: Note that –거든 in both sentences is followed by a command or request. The pattern is: verb stem + 거든. (The book titles the pattern “Expressing a Conditional in a Command or Request: verb stem + 거든”.)

explanations.title: Examples (the book’s)
explanations.body: Verb stem + 거든:

examples.text: 시간 있거든 이 책 한번 읽어 봐.
examples.translation: sigan itgeodeun i chaek hanbeon ilgeo bwa. — Try to read this book if you have time.

examples.text: 피곤하거든 일찍 자.
examples.translation: pigonhageodeun iljjik ja. — Go to bed early if you are tired.

examples.text: 우체국에 가시거든 이 소포도 부쳐 주세요.
examples.translation: ucheguge gasigeodeun i sopodo bucheo juseyo. — If you go to a post office, send this parcel, too.

examples.text: 바쁘지 않거든 저를 좀 도와주세요.
examples.translation: bappeuji ankeodeun jeoreul jom dowajuseyo. — Please help me if you are not busy.

examples.text: 그 일을 이미 시작하셨거든 계속하세요.
examples.translation: geu ireul imi sijakasyeotgeodeun gyesokaseyo. — If you already started that task, keep doing it.

explanations.title: Do not confuse –거든 with –거든(요)
explanations.body: Be sure not to confuse the conjunctive ending –거든 with the sentence ending –거든(요). The sentence ending –거든요 gives a reason or an explanation; it is not followed by a command:

examples.text: 오늘 저녁때 영화 못 봐요. 숙제가 많거든요.
examples.translation: oneul jeonyeokttae yeonghwa mot bwayo. sukjega mankeodeunyo. — I cannot see a movie tonight; I have a lot of homework.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 1 (Reading, Listening, Speaking: pairs pick verb-phrase strips; Partner A asks Partner B to do something today with –거든, and Partner B declines today but agrees to do it tomorrow with –(으)면; the book’s model is in the next lesson) and Follow-up 2 (video clips from MBC America in which a man makes a request with –거든; the book glosses 무조건: without any reason, unconditionally, 절대로: never and 아가씨: miss, a young lady) are pair and video activities.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with so that they can provide other activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify and write about basic features of the Korean government, such as its organizations, leaders, and their roles; talk about the electoral systems for the president, national assembly members, chiefs of local government, and their procedures; identify and talk about the Korean judicial system; and extract information about the judicial system, such as types of sentences, procedures, and judicial decision(s).

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the summary of sentence connectors; the conjunctive ending –거든 (if) used in a command/request; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 입법부 (立法府), 장관 (長官), 투표 (投票), 총선 (總選), and 법원 (法院).

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank. The last section lists the Sino-Korean related words of 입법부, 장관, 투표, 총선 and 법원 as the book gives them.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (the book’s 2022 and similar numbers; for example 5-year terms and 3-year sentences are read in Korean numbers: 사 년, 삼 년). The book’s 1심, 2심 and 3심 are written 일 심, 이 심, 삼 심.

rows: to point to; to denote; to mean

hanguge inneun miguneun hangugui gukbange daedanhi jungyohan yeokareul handa.

hanbandoreul jungsimeuro miguk, jungguk, ilbon, reosiaui bokjapan oegyo gwangyega balsaenghanda.

이번에 새로 연방대법원 판사로 임명된 사람에 대해서 아세요?

jeongbuga gyehoekaneun ipbeobeul simindanchedeuri bandaehago itseumnida.

행정 각 부 장관들이 모여 비상사태에 대해 논의 중입니다.

explanations.title: What Chapter 47 teaches (사회 문제 1)
explanations.body:
Chapter 47, “Social Issues I”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations (Busan’s measures against the low birthrate, a “goose daddy”, the excessive preference for name brands) with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify and discuss the low birthrate trend in Korea, its causes and effects, and incentives for reversing it; identify and discuss the trend of young Koreans studying abroad; and understand and discuss the trend of people preferring famous name-brand merchandise and how the trend has affected the Korean economy.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; an attributive form + 것처럼/같이 (like; as if); loanwords in Korean; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 저출산 (低出産), 전담 (專擔), and 명품 선호 (名品 選好).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 저출산 (低出産)
explanations.body: The first syllable 저 (低) means low, and when it is placed in front of a word, it functions like the English prefix under- or hypo-, as in 저개발 (underdevelopment; “low development”), 저속(도) (low speed), 저임금 (low wages), 저혈압 (hypotension; “low blood pressure”), etc. Thus the word 저출산 means low birthrate or low delivery rates (of children). The noun 출산 itself means delivery (of a baby) or childbirth; the syllable 출 (出) means (come/go) out or leaving, as in 출국 and 출항. The syllable 산 (産) means produce or give a birth, as in 초산 (one’s first childbirth). Thus, the literal meaning of 저출산 is “low (child) producing” or “low childbirth.” The book asks you to guess 저온, 생산, 저체중, 농산물, 외출, 고저, 산지 and 출구 (my answers; the glosses of the book’s examples 출국, 출항 and 저속 are mine):

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 전담 (專擔)
explanations.body: The syllable 전 (專) means only, exclusive, or specialized, as in 전문가 (a specialist). The syllable 담 (擔) means carrying (a burden) on the shoulder. Thus the literal meaning of the Sino-Korean word is “exclusively carrying (a burden) on the shoulder,” and the word means (being in) exclusive charge or complete charge. The verb 전담하다, which derives from the word 전담, means to be in complete charge or to be in exclusive charge. The book asks you to guess 전용, 전력, 전임, 담임 선생님, 부담 and 담당 (my answers):

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 명품 선호 (名品 選好)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word is made up of the two words, 명품 (name brand) and 선호 (preference). Thus 명품 선호 means a preference for name-brand merchandise. The first syllable 명 (名) means a name, as in 성명 (one’s full name) and 명함 (a business card; “name holder”), 익명 (anonymous; “hidden name”), 무명 (unknown; obscure; “without name”), etc. The syllable 품 (品) means item or goods, as in 식품 (food; “eating item”) and 공산품 (industrial products). 선 (選) means select or selective, as in 선물 (a gift; a present; “selected item”) and 선거 (an election). The last syllable 호 (好), whose Chinese character depicts a woman (女) holding her son (子), means good or like or likable, as in 호의 (goodwill; kindness) and 호감 (an attraction; “favorable feeling”). The book asks you to guess 유명, 호황, 선택, 상품, 기념품, 명소, 호평 and 선발 (the book glosses 평 [評]: evaluation; my answers):

explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a news report (YTN) about efforts by the city of Busan to reverse the low birthrate. (The English is mine; the book gives none. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out: 2008년 is 이천팔 년, 0.98명 is 영 점 구팔 명, 초.중.고 is written with commas. The line with the interviewee’s name is the caption of the interview; the news screenshot overlaps one line of the printed text, so the words around “미혼 남녀들이” are as far as the Korean can be read. The book’s footnotes: 1 기준 means standards, criteria, or basis; the phrase ~을/를 기준으로 means [something] as a basis for or on the basis of [something]. 2 광역시 refers to a city with a population of 1 million or more; 지자체 is an acronym of 지방자치단체, which refers to a local [autonomous] government; thus 광역지자체 refers to local [autonomous] government within 광역시.)

explanations.body: The Sino-Korean syllable 력 (力), which means power or ability, is often attached to other Sino-Korean nouns, as in 노동력 (labor force), 경쟁력 (competitive edge; competitive power), 기억력 (memory; memory power), 생활력 (ability to maintain one’s livelihood), 생산력 (productivity; “production power”), 잠재력 (potentiality; “latent power”), etc.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: Korea’s birthrate and policy changes
explanations.body: In the early 1950s, Korea’s birthrate exceeded six children per woman. In 1962, the Korean government started its national family planning campaign known as 가족계획 to reduce the birthrate. The motto of the campaign was 적게 낳아 잘 기르면 부모 좋고 자식 좋다. (The fewer children, the better for parents and children.) The program aimed to reduce the birthrate to three children per woman. In the 1970s, the campaign for having only three children turned into a campaign for having only two. The motto of the campaign changed to 아들 딸 구별 말고 둘만 낳아 잘 기르자. (Son or daughter, let’s have just two and raise them well.) In the 1980s, a two-child family was considered too big. Because of the continued low birthrate (a historically low rate of 1.08 children per woman in 2005), the Korean government launched a very different campaign. It is now encouraging each household to have more children. The motto of the campaign is 아빠, 혼자는 싫어요. 엄마, 동생을 갖고 싶어요. (Dad, I don’t want to be alone. Mom, I want to have a sibling.) The Korean government has implemented various policies to increase the birthrate, such as providing financial incentives for having more than one child.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a news article without a title
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a news article (연합뉴스) and is missing a title. The book asks you to read the article, underline the sentence that contains the topic, and write a fitting title in English. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (2천만 원 is 이천만 원; 5년간 10회 is 오 년간 열 번); the English is mine. The book glosses 수당: allowance, 장려: encouraging; promotion and 꺼리다: avoid; and its note *첫만남이용권 means a system to support buying the goods needed in the early period after birth. My answers: the topic sentence is the first sentence (the raised incentive); a title could be “Goesan County raises the childbirth incentive for a third child to 50 million won.”

examples.text: 충북 괴산군에서 지난해까지 이천만 원이던 셋째 아이 이상 출산장려금을 올해 오천만 원으로 올렸다.
examples.translation: chungbuk goesanguneseo jinanhaekkaji icheonman wonideon setjjae ai isang chulsanjangnyeogeumeul olhae ocheonman woneuro ollyeotda. — Goesan County in North Chungcheong raised the childbirth incentive for a third child or more, which was 20 million won until last year, to 50 million won this year.

examples.text: 출산장려금은 출산 육아수당 천만 원, 첫만남이용권 이백만 원이 포함된 것으로 오 년간 열 번으로 나눠 지급한다.
examples.translation: chulsanjangnyeogeumeun chulsan yugasudang cheonman won, cheonmannamiyonggwon ibaengman woni pohamdoen geoseuro o nyeongan yeol beoneuro nanwo jigeupanda. — The childbirth incentive includes a 10 million won childbirth and child-rearing allowance and a 2 million won First Meeting Voucher, and is paid in ten installments over five years.

examples.text: 군 관계자는 양육비와 교육비 부담 등이 출산을 꺼리는 가장 큰 이유라며 출산 가정의 경제적 부담을 덜어주고 다산을 유도하기 위해 셋째 아이 이상 출산장려금을 인상한 것이라고 말했다.
examples.translation: gun gwangyejaneun yangyukbiwa gyoyukbi budam deungi chulsaneul kkeorineun gajang keun iyuramyeo chulsan gajeongui gyeongjejeok budameul deoreojugo dasaneul yudohagi wihae setjjae ai isang chulsanjangnyeogeumeul insanghan geosirago malhaetda. — A county official said that the burden of child-rearing and education costs is the biggest reason for avoiding childbirth, and that the incentive for a third child or more was raised to lighten the economic burden of families that give birth and to induce having many children.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading): cause, effect or countermeasure?
explanations.body: Read each sentence and choose, from the phrases a. 저출산의 원인 (cause of the low birthrate), b. 저출산의 영향 (effect of the low birthrate) and c. 저출산의 대책 (countermeasure against the low birthrate), the most appropriate description. The sentences are the book’s; the answers and the English are mine.

rows: 대학에 결혼과 출산에 대한 가치관을 가르치는 교양과목을 개설한다.
보육료, 교육비 등의 경제적인 부담이 많다.
아이를 꼭 낳지 않아도 된다고 생각한다.
인구 감소로 인해 잠재적으로 국가 경쟁력이 약해진다.
정부에서 미혼 남녀들이 짝을 만날 수 있도록 결혼프로그램을 만든다.
The number of children entering school gradually decreases.
Universities open general-education courses that teach values about marriage and childbirth.
The economic burden of childcare fees, education costs and so on is heavy.
It is hard to raise a child while working at a job.
People think they do not have to have a child.
Because of the population decrease, national competitiveness potentially weakens.
The rate of unmarried people keeps increasing.
Education up to high school is made free.
Paid childbirth leave is also given to the spouse.
The government makes marriage programs so that unmarried men and women can meet a partner.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): the survey on married women’s wishes
explanations.body: The following article is about Korea’s low birthrate. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (11일 is 십일 일; 20~44세 is 이십 세에서 사십사 세; 3,585명 is 삼천오백팔십오 명; 55.1% is 오십오 점 일 퍼센트; the dots in 양육·교육비 are commas); the English is mine.

examples.text: 한국보건사회연구원은 십일 일 서울 프라자 호텔에서 열린 전국 결혼 및 출산에 대한 조사 결과 보고 및 학술 세미나에서 기혼여성이 가장 원하는 정부의 저출산 대책은 지속적인 자녀의 양육, 교육비 지원이라고 밝혔다.
examples.translation: hangukbogeonsahoeyeonguwoneun sibil il seoul peuraja hotereseo yeollin jeonguk gyeolhon mit chulsane daehan josa gyeolgwa bogo mit haksul seminaeseo gihonyeoseongi gajang wonhaneun jeongbuui jeochulsan daechaegeun jisokjeogin janyeoui yangyuk, gyoyukbi jiwonirago balkyeotda. — The Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs announced, at the seminar on the results of a nationwide survey on marriage and childbirth held at the Plaza Hotel in Seoul on the 11th, that the low-birthrate measure of the government that married women want most is continued support for child-rearing and education costs.

examples.text: 보사연이 전국의 이십 세에서 사십사 세 기혼여성 삼천오백팔십오 명을 대상으로 조사한 결과 기혼여성이 가장 원하는 정책은 지속적인 양육, 교육비 지원 오십오 점 일 퍼센트, 보육시설 지원 정책 십육 점 칠 퍼센트, 주택 지원 구 점 이 퍼센트 등의 순이었다.
examples.translation: bosayeoni jeongugui isip seeseo sasipsa se gihonyeoseong samcheonobaekpalsibo myeongeul daesangeuro josahan gyeolgwa gihonyeoseongi gajang wonhaneun jeongchaegeun jisokjeogin yangyuk, gyoyukbi jiwon osibo jeom il peosenteu, boyuksiseol jiwon jeongchaek simnyuk jeom chil peosenteu, jutaek jiwon gu jeom i peosenteu deungui sunieotda. — As a result of a survey of 3,585 married women aged 20 to 44 nationwide, the policies that married women want most were, in order, continued child-rearing and education cost support (55.1%), childcare facility support policy (16.7%), housing support (9.2%) and so on.

examples.text: 한편, 제안하고 싶은 정책을 묻는 말에 대해서는 참가자의 대부분이 자녀를 둔 사원에 대한 기업의 배려라고 답했다.
examples.translation: hanpyeon, jeanhago sipeun jeongchaegeul munneun mare daehaeseoneun chamgajaui daebubuni janyeoreul dun sawone daehan gieobui baeryeorago dapaetda. — Meanwhile, to the question asking what policy they would like to propose, most participants answered: companies’ consideration for employees with children.

examples.text: 또 배우자의 출산휴가를 유급으로 바꾸고 기간도 늘릴 것을 제시했다.
examples.translation: tto baeujaui chulsanhyugareul yugeubeuro bakkugo gigando neullil geoseul jesihaetda. — They also suggested changing the spouse’s childbirth leave to paid leave and lengthening the period.

explanations.title: The tasks answered (mine)
explanations.body: a. The title that fits is the third: 저출산 대책 선호도와 제안 정책 (the preference for low-birthrate measures and the proposed policies). b. The table:

rows: 55.1%: continued support for child-rearing and education costs; 16.7%: childcare facility support policy; 9.2%: housing support
Companies’ consideration for employees with children; changing the spouse’s childbirth leave to paid leave and lengthening the period

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 2 (listening to two news clips, YTN and KBS, about Korea’s birthrate: the reasons for not having [more] children), Activity 2 (listening to four YTN news clips and watching the videos: checking whether each is about an effect, a cause or a countermeasure and writing the main idea) and Activity 4 (listening to an interview with a recently married couple: their work, their thoughts on having children and their concerns about raising children; exchanging the information in Korean, discussing incentives for the couple to have children, writing in the class notebook [MS TEAMS], presenting and choosing the best idea) are audio, video and pair activities.

explanations.title: Topic B: “I am a goose daddy” (저는 기러기 아빠입니다)
explanations.body: The following magazine article is about a father whose family lives abroad. (The English is mine; the book gives none. The text is the book’s with 3년째 spelled 삼 년째; the news photo overlaps one line, so the words near “실망입니다” are as far as the Korean can be read. The book’s footnote: the marker ~로(써) in 올해로 specifies a designated time frame as an end point of a certain period; it translates to “as of”, e.g. 수업은 오늘로 끝납니다 [As of today, the instruction ends].)

examples.text: 한도현 씨는 기러기 아빠입니다.
examples.translation: handohyeon ssineun gireogi appaimnida. — Mr. Han Do-hyeon is a goose daddy.

examples.text: 두 자녀가 캐나다 토론토에서 학교에 다닙니다.
examples.translation: du janyeoga kaenada torontoeseo hakgyoe danimnida. — His two children go to school in Toronto, Canada.

examples.translation: buindo geugoseseo aideulgwa hamkke saenghwalhamnida. — His wife also lives there with the children.

examples.text: 가족이 떨어져 지낸 기간이 올해로 벌써 삼 년째입니다.
examples.translation: gajogi tteoreojeo jinaen gigani olhaero beolsseo sam nyeonjjaeimnida. — As of this year the period the family has lived apart is already the third year.

examples.text: 자녀를 조기유학을 보낸 가장 큰 이유는 영어였습니다.
examples.translation: janyeoreul jogiyuhageul bonaen gajang keun iyuneun yeongeoyeotseumnida. — The biggest reason he sent his children for early study abroad was English.

examples.text: 요즘은 학교와 직장마다 영어 열풍이 불고 있습니다.
examples.translation: yojeumeun hakgyowa jikjangmada yeongeo yeolpungi bulgo itseumnida. — These days an English fever is blowing at every school and workplace.

examples.translation: jinhagina chwieobeul hal ttae yeongeoga gajang jungyohan pyeongga gijuni doeeotseumnida. — English has become the most important evaluation standard when advancing to a higher school or getting a job.

examples.text: 그래서 한 씨는 두 자녀를 영어를 쓰는 나라에서 공부시키고 싶었습니다.

examples.text: 또 다른 이유는 한국 교육에 대한 실망입니다.
examples.translation: tto dareun iyuneun hanguk gyoyuge daehan silmangimnida. — Another reason is disappointment in Korean education.

examples.text: 학생들의 개성을 무시하고 입시경쟁만 중시하기 때문입니다.

examples.text: 아이들을 위해 기러기 아빠가 됐지만 견디기 어려울 때가 많습니다.

explanations.title: 한국어에는: the verb 떨어지다
explanations.body: Depending on the context, the verb 떨어지다 can be translated as one of the following: 1) to fall (off) or drop, as in 사과가 나무에서 떨어졌어요 (An apple fell off the tree) and 지난 주에 기름값이 떨어졌어요 (The gas price dropped last week); 2) to run out of (money, gas, food, etc.), as in 기름이 떨어졌어요 (I’ve run out of gas); 3) to be (physically) separated or to be away from (a person), as in 아내와 1년 동안 떨어져 있었어요 (I was away from my wife for a year); 4) to fail (in the exam) as in 시험에 떨어졌어요 (I failed in the exam). (The number is spelled 일 년 below.)

examples.text: 지난 주에 기름값이 떨어졌어요.
examples.translation: jinan jue gireumgapsi tteoreojeosseoyo. — The gas price dropped last week.

examples.text: 기름이 떨어졌어요.
examples.translation: gireumi tteoreojeosseoyo. — I’ve run out of gas.

examples.text: 아내와 일 년 동안 떨어져 있었어요.
examples.translation: anaewa il nyeon dongan tteoreojeo isseosseoyo. — I was away from my wife for a year.

examples.text: 시험에 떨어졌어요.
examples.translation: siheome tteoreojeosseoyo. — I failed in the exam.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: 기러기 아빠
explanations.body: 기러기 아빠, whose literal meaning is “wild goose daddy,” refers to a father who remains in his home country and works while his wife and children live abroad, for the sake of the children’s education. The term likens married couples, who remain loyal to each other despite vast physical distances, to geese, which migrate seasonally and mate for life. To support their families abroad, the “left-behind” fathers work very hard and endure great loneliness and sadness.
