explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): Story A
explanations.body: The following stories are about a father who plans to send his child abroad to study. The book asks you to read them and fill in a table in English (the foreign country, the reason for early study abroad, the concerns). The stories are the book’s with the numbers spelled out (3학년 is 삼 학년; 7월 is 칠 월; 3, 4년 is 삼, 사 년); the English is mine.

examples.text: 제 아들은 초등학교 삼 학년입니다.
examples.translation: je adeureun chodeunghakgyo sam hangnyeonimnida. — My son is in the third grade of elementary school.

examples.text: 오는 칠 월에 캐나다로 삼, 사 년 정도 조기유학을 보내기로 했습니다.
examples.translation: oneun chil wore kaenadaro sam, sa nyeon jeongdo jogiyuhageul bonaegiro haetseumnida. — I decided to send him for early study abroad to Canada for about three or four years this coming July.

examples.text: 어렸을 때부터 영어를 쓰는 나라에서 공부하면 영어를 따로 공부하지 않아도 잘할 수 있지 않을까요?
examples.translation: eoryeosseul ttaebuteo yeongeoreul sseuneun naraeseo gongbuhamyeon yeongeoreul ttaro gongbuhaji anado jalhal su itji aneulkkayo? — If he studies in a country that uses English from an early age, won’t he be able to do well in English without studying it separately?

examples.text: 그러면 나중에 진학할 때나 커서 취직할 때 유리할 거라고 생각합니다.
examples.translation: geureomyeon najunge jinhakal ttaena keoseo chwijikal ttae yurihal georago saenggakamnida. — Then I think it will be advantageous later when he goes on to a higher school or gets a job when grown up.

examples.text: 하지만, 그곳의 학비와 생활비가 비싸서 벌써 걱정입니다.
examples.translation: hajiman, geugosui hakbiwa saenghwalbiga bissaseo beolsseo geokjeongimnida. — But the tuition and living costs there are expensive, so I am already worried.

examples.text: 제가 버는 돈을 거의 모두 송금해야 할 것 같습니다.
examples.translation: jega beoneun doneul geoui modu songgeumhaeya hal geot gatseumnida. — I think I will have to send almost all the money I earn.

examples.text: 제 딸과 아내가 다음 달에 호주로 출국합니다.
examples.translation: je ttalgwa anaega daeum dare hojuro chulgukamnida. — My daughter and wife leave for Australia next month.

examples.text: 중학교에 다니는 딸이 호주에 있는 사립학교에 다닐 예정입니다.
examples.translation: junghakgyoe danineun ttari hojue inneun saripakgyoe danil yejeongimnida. — My daughter, who goes to middle school, is going to attend a private school in Australia.

examples.text: 아이의 개성을 무시하고 경쟁만을 중요시하는 한국 교육에 아이가 너무 힘들어하더군요.
examples.translation: aiui gaeseongeul musihago gyeongjaengmaneul jungyosihaneun hanguk gyoyuge aiga neomu himdeureohadeogunyo. — I noticed that my child was finding Korean education, which ignores a child’s individuality and values only competition, too hard.

examples.text: 그래서 아이를 유학 보내기로 했습니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo aireul yuhak bonaegiro haetseumnida. — So I decided to send her abroad to study.

examples.text: 하지만, 우리 딸이 언어가 다르고 문화가 다른 곳에서 잘 적응할 수 있을지 걱정입니다.
examples.translation: hajiman, uri ttari eoneoga dareugo munhwaga dareun goseseo jal jeogeunghal su isseulji geokjeongimnida. — But I worry whether our daughter can adapt well in a place where the language and culture are different.

examples.text: 조기유학을 하는 아이 중에 적응하지 못해 문제아가 되는 일도 있다고 합니다.
examples.translation: jogiyuhageul haneun ai junge jeogeunghaji motae munjeaga doeneun ildo itdago hamnida. — They say that among children studying abroad early, some fail to adapt and become problem children.

lessons.title: 593. Ch 47 · Grammar in Focus: an attributive form + 것처럼/같이
lessons.subtitle: 문법 탐구 · 것처럼 · 것같이 · 관형형 · like · as · as if · 처럼 · 같이

explanations.title: The conjunctive ending: an attributive form + 것처럼/같이
explanations.body: In an earlier chapter, you learned that ~처럼/같이 (like) is preceded by a noun, as in 마이클 잭슨처럼 (like Michael Jackson) and 한국 사람같이 (like Korean people). 처럼/같이 can also be preceded by a verb or verbal phrase. In this case, however, the verb must be in an attributive form + 것. For example: 손을 씻다 → 손을 씻는 것처럼/손을 씻는 것같이; 한국사람이다 → 한국사람인 것처럼/한국사람인 것같이. An attributive form + 것처럼/같이 can mean like, as, or as if, depending on the context.

rows: as if washing hands (손을 씻는 것같이)
as if (one) is a Korean (한국사람인 것같이)

explanations.title: I. “Like” or “as”
explanations.body: When an attributive form + 것처럼/같이 comes before a clause, the attributive form + 것처럼/같이 translates to like, as, or as much as. (The year 1905년 is spelled out; the English is the book’s.)

examples.text: 조금 전에 안내자가 설명한 것처럼 이 박물관은 천구백오 년에 지어졌습니다.
examples.translation: jogeum jeone annaejaga seolmyeonghan geotcheoreom i bangmulgwaneun cheongubaego nyeone jieojeotseumnida. — As the guide explained just now, this museum was built in 1905.

examples.text: 형이 열심히 공부한 것처럼 너도 열심히 해야 한다.
examples.translation: hyeongi yeolsimhi gongbuhan geotcheoreom neodo yeolsimhi haeya handa. — Just as your brother studied hard, you have to study hard.

examples.text: 아버지가 여행을 좋아하시는 것처럼 저도 여행을 좋아합니다.
examples.translation: abeojiga yeohaengeul joahasineun geotcheoreom jeodo yeohaengeul joahamnida. — I like traveling as much as my father does.

explanations.title: II. “As if”
explanations.body: When an attributive form + 것처럼/같이 comes right before a verb or a short verb phrase, it tends to mean as if. If the verb is 보이다, the whole phrase may be interpreted as look like.

examples.text: 태수가 유학 갈 것처럼 말했어요.
examples.translation: taesuga yuhak gal geotcheoreom malhaesseoyo. — Taesoo talked as if he would go abroad for study.

examples.text: 동생이 일주일 동안 굶은 것처럼 밥을 먹었어요.
examples.translation: dongsaengi iljuil dongan gulmeun geotcheoreom babeul meogeosseoyo. — My younger brother ate as if he hadn’t eaten for a week.

examples.text: 민지는 아픈 것처럼 보였어요.
examples.translation: minjineun apeun geotcheoreom boyeosseoyo. — Minji looked like she was ill.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 1 (a pair task: the teacher gives lists of nouns and verb phrases; Student A reads one from List A, Student B makes a sentence with an attributive form + 것처럼/같이 and a concluding clause; the book’s model is in the next lesson), Follow-up 2 (listening to four short narrations and choosing “like, as” or “as if”, then translating) and Follow-up 4 (the friend Cheolmin who moved away suddenly: writing four things he did or said with 것처럼/같이, and giving clues in a circle) are pair, audio and group activities.

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading): the discussion forum
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a website’s discussion forum about the “fever” for learning English in Korea and studying abroad. The book asks you to underline all the sentences that contain an attributive form + 것처럼/같이, to say what the writer thinks triggers the 영어 열풍 and 조기 유학, to say in detail what is mentioned about the man in his 40s, and to translate 자주 뉴스에 보도되는 것처럼 기러기 아빠가 큰 사회 문제가 되고 있습니다. The text is the book’s with 40대 spelled 사십 대; the English is mine.

examples.text: 주제 영어 열풍과 조기 유학
examples.translation: juje yeongeo yeolpunggwa jogi yuhak — Topic: the English fever and early study abroad

examples.text: 요즘 한국에는 영어 열풍과 조기 유학 때문에 가족과 떨어져 사는 부모들이 상당히 많은 것 같습니다.
examples.translation: yojeum hangugeneun yeongeo yeolpunggwa jogi yuhak ttaemune gajokgwa tteoreojeo saneun bumodeuri sangdanghi maneun geot gatseumnida. — These days in Korea there seem to be quite a lot of parents living apart from their families because of the English fever and early study abroad.

examples.text: 그래서 요즘 자주 뉴스에 보도되는 것처럼 기러기 아빠가 큰 사회 문제가 되고 있습니다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo yojeum jaju nyuseue bododoeneun geotcheoreom gireogi appaga keun sahoe munjega doego itseumnida. — So, as is often reported in the news these days, goose daddies are becoming a big social problem.

examples.text: 이것은 영어가 모든 것인 것처럼 생각하는 우리 사회 때문인 것 같아요.
examples.translation: igeoseun yeongeoga modeun geosin geotcheoreom saenggakaneun uri sahoe ttaemunin geot gatayo. — I think this is because of our society, which thinks as if English were everything.

examples.text: 어제는 회사 직원들하고 같이 회식 후에 술집에 갔어요.
examples.translation: eojeneun hoesa jigwondeulhago gachi hoesik hue suljibe gasseoyo. — Yesterday I went to a bar with the company staff after a company dinner.

examples.text: 거기서 사십 대로 보이는 남자가 혼자 앉아 있었는데 참 외로워 보였어요.
examples.translation: geogiseo sasip daero boineun namjaga honja anja isseonneunde cham oerowo boyeosseoyo. — There a man who looked to be in his forties was sitting alone, and he looked really lonely.

examples.text: 기러기 아빠인 것 같이 보였어요.
examples.translation: gireogi appain geot gachi boyeosseoyo. — He looked like a goose daddy.

examples.text: 아이들과 부인이 조기 유학 때문에 해외에 있는 것처럼 얘기했어요.
examples.translation: aideulgwa buini jogi yuhak ttaemune haeoee inneun geotcheoreom yaegihaesseoyo. — He spoke as if his children and wife were overseas because of early study abroad.

explanations.title: The tasks answered (mine)
explanations.body: 1. The sentences with 것처럼/같이: 그래서 요즘 자주 뉴스에 보도되는 것처럼 …; 이것은 영어가 모든 것인 것처럼 생각하는 우리 사회 때문인 것 같아요; 기러기 아빠인 것 같이 보였어요; 아이들과 부인이 조기 유학 때문에 해외에 있는 것처럼 얘기했어요. 2. The writer thinks it is triggered by a society that thinks as if English were everything. 3. A man who looked to be in his forties was sitting alone in a bar, looked really lonely, looked like a goose daddy and spoke as if his children and wife were overseas because of early study abroad. 4. “As is often reported in the news these days, goose daddies are becoming a big social problem.”

explanations.title: Models of the pair and club tasks
explanations.body: The book’s models for Follow-up 1 (A gives “언니/육군이 되었다”) and Follow-up 4 (what Cheolmin did or said). The English is mine.

examples.text: 제 언니가 육군이 된 것처럼 저도 육군에 입대하고 싶어요.
examples.translation: je eonniga yukguni doen geotcheoreom jeodo yukgune ipdaehago sipeoyo. — Just as my older sister became an army soldier, I want to join the army, too.

examples.text: 철민이가 며칠 전에 뉴욕에 갈 것처럼 말했어요.
examples.translation: cheolminiga myeochil jeone nyuyoge gal geotcheoreom malhaesseoyo. — Cheolmin talked a few days ago as if he would go to New York.

examples.text: 철민이가 여행가는 것처럼 가방을 쌌어요.
examples.translation: cheolminiga yeohaengganeun geotcheoreom gabangeul ssasseoyo. — Cheolmin packed a bag as if he were going on a trip.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): the English-only town
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from a news article about two countermeasures the Korean government will use to solve a social issue related to English-language education. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (1년 is 일 년; 1명 is 한 명); the English is mine. My answers: a. the two policies are constructing an English-only town and having a native English-speaking teacher in every middle school; b. the government emphasizes English education in order to absorb at home the students who would go overseas through early study abroad or overseas training.

examples.text: 조기유학 이렇게 줄인다
examples.translation: jogiyuhak ireoke jurinda — This is how early study abroad is reduced

examples.text: 학교 수업과 생활을 할 때 영어만을 쓰도록 하는 영어 전용타운이 제주도에 만들어진다.
examples.translation: hakgyo sueopgwa saenghwareul hal ttae yeongeomaneul sseudorok haneun yeongeo jeonyongtauni jejudoe mandeureojinda. — An English-only town, where only English is used for school classes and daily life, is being built on Jeju Island.

examples.text: 해외로 빠져나가는 조기유학 수요를 국내로 돌리겠다는 것이다.
examples.translation: haeoero ppajeonaganeun jogiyuhak suyoreul gungnaero dolligetdaneun geosida. — The aim is to turn the demand for early study abroad that flows overseas back to the country.

examples.text: 이번에 제주도 서귀포시에 조성되는 영어 전용타운은 준비 기간이 적어도 일 년 이상이다.
examples.translation: ibeone jejudo seogwiposie joseongdoeneun yeongeo jeonyongtauneun junbi gigani jeogeodo il nyeon isangida. — The English-only town being created this time in Seogwipo, Jeju, needs a preparation period of at least one year.

examples.text: 또한, 원어민 영어 교사도 계속 채용해 모든 중학교에 한 명씩 원어민 교사가 배치되도록 할 예정이다.
examples.translation: ttohan, woneomin yeongeo gyosado gyesok chaeyonghae modeun junghakgyoe han myeongssik woneomin gyosaga baechidoedorok hal yejeongida. — In addition, it plans to keep hiring native English-speaking teachers so that one native teacher is assigned to every middle school.

examples.text: 정부가 이렇게 영어 교육에 중점을 두는 이유는 조기유학이나 해외 연수로 해외로 빠져나가는 학생들을 국내에서 소화하기 위해서이다.
examples.translation: jeongbuga ireoke yeongeo gyoyuge jungjeomeul duneun iyuneun jogiyuhagina haeoe yeonsuro haeoero ppajeonaganeun haksaengdeureul gungnaeeseo sohwahagi wihaeseoida. — The reason the government puts the emphasis on English education like this is to absorb at home the students who flow overseas through early study abroad or overseas training.

explanations.title: Activity 4 (Reading): a column on early English education
explanations.body: In this activity, you share views on early English-language education by reading a text and adding more ideas (Group A finds the positive points and Group B the negative points of the column below, then each adds ideas and presents; each person writes whether they are for or against with one supporting fact, with the model 저는 조기영어교육에 찬성합니다. 왜냐하면 …). The column is the book’s; the English is mine.

examples.text: 한 살이라도 어릴 때 시키자
examples.translation: han sarirado eoril ttae sikija — Let’s start even a year earlier (the column’s title)

examples.text: 최근 조기영어교육 열풍이 불면서 어린 나이에 영어를 가르치는 사례를 많이 볼 수 있다.
examples.translation: choegeun jogiyeongeogyoyuk yeolpungi bulmyeonseo eorin naie yeongeoreul gareuchineun saryereul mani bol su itda. — Recently, as a fever for early English education blows, many cases of teaching English at a young age can be seen.

examples.text: 조기영어교육 열풍은 영어를 잘해야 학교나 직장 등에서 성공할 수 있고, 이러한 외국어 학습은 빠를수록 좋다고 생각하기 때문이다.
examples.translation: jogiyeongeogyoyuk yeolpungeun yeongeoreul jalhaeya hakgyona jikjang deungeseo seonggonghal su itgo, ireohan oegugeo hakseubeun ppareulsurok jotago saenggakagi ttaemunida. — The fever for early English education is because people think that one can succeed at school or a workplace only by being good at English, and that the earlier such foreign-language learning is, the better.

examples.text: 특히, 어린이들은 호기심이 많아 외국어를 쉽게 배울 수 있고, 세계화 시대에 영어를 빨리 가르치면 경쟁력을 키울 수 있다.
examples.translation: teuki, eorinideureun hogisimi mana oegugeoreul swipge baeul su itgo, segyehwa sidaee yeongeoreul ppalli gareuchimyeon gyeongjaengnyeogeul kiul su itda. — In particular, children have much curiosity and can learn a foreign language easily, and teaching English early in the age of globalization can raise competitiveness.

examples.text: 그러나 이러한 조기영어교육으로 인해 여러 가지 문제도 생기고 있다.
examples.translation: geureona ireohan jogiyeongeogyoyugeuro inhae yeoreo gaji munjedo saenggigo itda. — However, various problems are also arising because of such early English education.

examples.text: 모국어가 아직 서투른 아이들에게 외국어를 가르쳐 언어장애가 생기는 예도 있다.
examples.translation: mogugeoga ajik seotureun aideurege oegugeoreul gareucheo eoneojangaega saenggineun yedo itda. — There are also cases in which language disorders arise from teaching a foreign language to children who are still unskilled in their mother tongue.

examples.text: 또한, 영어 교육으로 인해 사교육비가 급등해 가정경제에 어려움을 주고 있기도 하다.
examples.translation: ttohan, yeongeo gyoyugeuro inhae sagyoyukbiga geupdeunghae gajeonggyeongjee eoryeoumeul jugo itgido hada. — In addition, private education costs rise sharply because of English education, causing difficulty for household economies.

rows: One can succeed at school or work with good English; the earlier foreign-language learning is, the better; children are curious and learn easily; teaching English early in the age of globalization raises competitiveness
Language disorders can arise in children still unskilled in their mother tongue; private education costs rise sharply and burden household economies

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 1 (SMART Board) and Activity 2 (listening to two YTN news clips and watching the videos: identifying the social issue [goose family, excessive private education fees or early English-language education] and writing the clue words in Korean) are computer, audio and video activities.

explanations.title: Topic C: the excessive preference for name brands (한국인의 지나친 명품 선호)
explanations.body: The following article, written by a news columnist (YTN), is about the craze in a certain segment of Korean society for famous name-brand merchandise. (The English is mine; the book gives none. The text is the book’s with the ages in brackets written as ages [29 is 스물아홉 살; 23 is 스물세 살] and 2~3개 spelled 두세 개. The book’s footnotes: 4 ~에 관계없이 [regardless of]; 5 적금을 들다 [to open a savings account; “enter into installment savings”].)

examples.text: 서울에서 직장을 다니는 스물아홉 살 최 모 씨는 값비싼 브랜드의 제품을 선호하고 애용한다.
examples.translation: seoureseo jikjangeul danineun seumurahop sal choe mo ssineun gapbissan beuraendeuui jepumeul seonhohago aeyonghanda. — Mr. Choi, 29, who works at a company in Seoul, prefers and habitually uses products of expensive brands.

examples.text: 그래서 최 씨는 월급의 절반 이상을 명품 구입에 낭비하고 있다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo choe ssineun wolgeubui jeolban isangeul myeongpum guibe nangbihago itda. — So Mr. Choi wastes more than half of his salary on buying name-brand goods.

examples.text: 대학생 스물세 살 박 모 씨도 명품을 사기 위해 과외 등 아르바이트를 두세 개씩 하고 있다.
examples.translation: daehaksaeng seumulse sal bak mo ssido myeongpumeul sagi wihae gwaoe deung areubaiteureul duse gaessik hago itda. — Mr. Park, 23, a university student, also does two or three part-time jobs, such as tutoring, in order to buy name-brand goods.

examples.text: 박 씨는 대학에서 편하게 공부만 하고 싶지만 원하는 명품을 갖기 위해서 그 정도는 견딜 수 있다고 말했다.
examples.translation: bak ssineun daehageseo pyeonhage gongbuman hago sipjiman wonhaneun myeongpumeul gatgi wihaeseo geu jeongdoneun gyeondil su itdago malhaetda. — Mr. Park said, “I want to just study comfortably at university, but to have the name-brand goods I want, I can endure that much.”

examples.text: 이 같은 명품 선호 분위기는 이제 나이, 성별, 수입에 관계없이 사회 전체에 만연해 있다.
examples.translation: i gateun myeongpum seonho bunwigineun ije nai, seongbyeol, suibe gwangyeeopsi sahoe jeonchee manyeonhae itda. — This kind of preference for name-brand goods is now rampant throughout the whole of society regardless of age, gender and income.

examples.text: 심지어 명품 구입을 위해 적금을 들거나 범죄를 저지르는 일도 있다.
examples.translation: simjieo myeongpum guibeul wihae jeokgeumeul deulgeona beomjoereul jeojireuneun ildo itda. — There are even cases of opening an installment savings account or committing a crime in order to buy name-brand goods.

examples.text: 이런 명품 선호 현상의 이유 중 하나는 남에게 보이고 싶은 과시욕 때문이다.
examples.translation: ireon myeongpum seonho hyeonsangui iyu jung hananeun namege boigo sipeun gwasiyok ttaemunida. — One of the reasons for this phenomenon of preferring name-brand goods is the desire to show off to others.

examples.text: 무분별한 명품 소비는 가계에 부담을 주고 국가 경쟁력을 약화시킬 수 있다.
examples.translation: mubunbyeolhan myeongpum sobineun gagyee budameul jugo gukga gyeongjaengnyeogeul yakwasikil su itda. — Reckless consumption of name-brand goods can burden households and weaken national competitiveness.

lessons.subtitle: 명품 · 가짜 · 청소년 · 과시욕 · 잡지 · 신용카드 · 신용불량 · 과소비 · 유발 · 부러워하다

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 (Reading): a magazine article on a social trend
explanations.body: The following magazine article is about a recent social trend in Korea. The book asks you to underline the main idea, to write in English the biographical information of the person used as an example and the action she took, and to write two reasons she gives for liking being part of the trend. The text is the book’s with the age and grade written out (1학년 is 일 학년; 17 is 열일곱 살); the quotation marks are removed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 일부 부유층의 명품 선호 분위기는 이제 나이에 관계없이 사회 전체에 만연해 있다.
examples.translation: ilbu buyucheungui myeongpum seonho bunwigineun ije naie gwangyeeopsi sahoe jeonchee manyeonhae itda. — The preference for name-brand goods among some of the rich is now rampant throughout society regardless of age.

examples.text: 이런 분위기 때문에 심지어 청소년들까지 명품 구매에 관심이 많다.
examples.translation: ireon bunwigi ttaemune simjieo cheongsonyeondeulkkaji myeongpum gumaee gwansimi manta. — Because of this atmosphere, even teenagers have a lot of interest in buying name-brand goods.

examples.text: 일부 청소년들은 돈을 모아서 가짜 명품을 사기도 한다.
examples.translation: ilbu cheongsonyeondeureun doneul moaseo gajja myeongpumeul sagido handa. — Some teenagers save money and even buy fake name-brand goods.

examples.text: 이런 현상은 남에게 보여 주기 위한 과시욕 때문으로 생각된다.
examples.translation: ireon hyeonsangeun namege boyeo jugi wihan gwasiyok ttaemuneuro saenggakdoenda. — This phenomenon is thought to be due to the desire to show off to others.

examples.text: 고등학교 일 학년 열일곱 살 송 모 양도 최근에 동대문 시장에서 가짜 샤넬 가방을 샀다.
examples.translation: godeunghakgyo il hangnyeon yeollilgop sal song mo yangdo choegeune dongdaemun sijangeseo gajja syanel gabangeul satda. — Ms. Song, 17, a first-year high school student, also recently bought a fake Chanel bag at the Dongdaemun market.

examples.text: 송 양은 이런 자신의 명품 선호에 대해 다른 친구들과 다르다는 것을 보여 줄 수 있어서 좋다고 말했다.
examples.translation: song yangeun ireon jasinui myeongpum seonhoe daehae dareun chingudeulgwa dareudaneun geoseul boyeo jul su isseoseo jotago malhaetda. — About her own preference for name-brand goods, Ms. Song said, “I like it because I can show I am different from the other friends.”

examples.text: 또한 친구들이 부러워하면 내가 특별해진 것 같아서 좋다고 밝혔다.
examples.translation: ttohan chingudeuri bureowohamyeon naega teukbyeolhaejin geot gataseo jotago balkyeotda. — She also said, “When my friends envy me, I like it because I feel as if I have become special.”

explanations.title: Follow-up 1 answered (mine)
explanations.body: a. The main idea is the first sentence: the preference for name-brand goods is now rampant throughout society regardless of age. b. Ms. Song is a 17-year-old first-year high school student; recently she bought a fake Chanel bag at the Dongdaemun market. c. Two reasons: she can show that she is different from her other friends; when her friends envy her she feels as if she has become special.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): overspending and women’s magazines
explanations.body: The following news article addresses issues associated with purchasing famous name-brand merchandise in Korea. The text is the book’s with 10대 and 20대 spelled 십 대 and 이십 대. The English is mine.

examples.text: 최근 십 대와 이십 대 여성들을 대상으로 하는 여성잡지가 쏟아지면서 여성들의 과소비가 증가하고 있다.
examples.translation: choegeun sip daewa isip dae yeoseongdeureul daesangeuro haneun yeoseongjapjiga ssodajimyeonseo yeoseongdeurui gwasobiga jeunggahago itda. — As magazines aimed at women in their teens and twenties have been pouring out recently, women’s overspending is increasing.

examples.text: 예전에 있던 많은 잡지뿐만 아니라 최근 많은 수의 외국 라이센스 잡지들이 유행처럼 생겨나면서 십 대와 이십 대에게 다양한 광고와 제안을 하고 있다.
examples.translation: yejeone itdeon maneun japjippunman anira choegeun maneun suui oeguk raisenseu japjideuri yuhaengcheoreom saenggyeonamyeonseo sip daewa isip daeege dayanghan gwanggowa jeaneul hago itda. — Not only the many magazines that existed before but also a large number of foreign-licensed magazines recently appearing like a fad are making various advertisements and suggestions to teens and twenty-somethings.

examples.text: 이들 잡지의 내용은 주로 화장법, 옷 코디, 헤어스타일 등의 뷰티와 패션 관련 내용과 화장품이나 옷들의 소비에 집중되어 있다.
examples.translation: ideul japjiui naeyongeun juro hwajangbeop, ot kodi, heeoseutail deungui byutiwa paesyeon gwallyeon naeyonggwa hwajangpumina otdeurui sobie jipjungdoeeo itda. — The content of these magazines is concentrated on beauty and fashion topics such as makeup methods, clothing coordination and hairstyles, and on the consumption of cosmetics and clothes.

examples.text: 이런 잡지를 읽는 십, 이십 대 여성들은 대부분 특별한 소득 없이 부모들로부터 용돈을 받거나 아르바이트로 돈을 벌어서 사용하는 세대들이다.
examples.translation: ireon japjireul ingneun sip, isip dae yeoseongdeureun daebubun teukbyeolhan sodeuk eopsi bumodeullobuteo yongdoneul batgeona areubaiteuro doneul beoreoseo sayonghaneun sedaedeurida. — The women in their teens and twenties who read such magazines are mostly a generation that receives allowances from their parents or earns money from part-time jobs, without special income.

examples.text: 그런데도 잡지들에 나오는 옷들이나 화장품, 액세서리 등이 개당 가격이 수십만 원을 넘는 명품들로 소개되고 있어서 명품 소비를 통한 과소비를 유발하고 있다.
examples.translation: geureondedo japjideure naoneun otdeurina hwajangpum, aekseseori deungi gaedang gagyeogi susimman woneul neomneun myeongpumdeullo sogaedoego isseoseo myeongpum sobireul tonghan gwasobireul yubalhago itda. — Even so, the clothes, cosmetics, accessories and so on that appear in the magazines are introduced as name-brand goods costing over several hundred thousand won each, inducing overspending through name-brand consumption.

examples.text: 또 이 같은 잡지에 소개되는 고가의 상품을 대부분 신용카드로 구입하기 때문에 신용불량 등의 원인으로 지적되고 있다.
examples.translation: tto i gateun japjie sogaedoeneun gogaui sangpumeul daebubun sinyongkadeuro guipagi ttaemune sinyongbullyang deungui wonineuro jijeokdoego itda. — Also, because most of the expensive goods introduced in such magazines are bought with credit cards, they are pointed out as a cause of bad credit and so on.

explanations.title: Activity 3 answered (mine)
explanations.body: a. 1. Women in their teens and twenties are most affected. 2. The cause is the flood of women’s magazines that introduce expensive name-brand goods. b. The order in which the points appear: 1 introduction of new fashions, makeup, coordination of clothes and hairstyles; 2 buying merchandise with a parental allowance or income from part-time jobs; 3 introduction of expensive merchandise over several hundred dollars (the article says several hundred thousand won); 4 bad credit ratings caused by the overuse of credit cards.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 2 (listening to a YTN report about a survey on name-brand merchandise: choosing the title, “mothers with daughters buy more name-brand goods”, “mothers with sons buy more” or “mothers with no children buy more”, and saying what the numbers 103,260 people, 52% and 23 times refer to), Activity 1 (SMART Board), Activity 2 (a YTN news clip on name-brand markets in Korea: the main idea and three true/false statements: the market for name-brand goods has suffered because of the financial crisis; it has been growing rapidly; only department stores sell name-brand goods) and Activity 4 (groups read Text A or Text B about the preference for name-brand goods, noting the people, brands, items and reasons, writing and presenting in Korean; the two texts are not printed in the student text) are audio, video, computer and group activities.

lessons.title: 597. Ch 47 · Grammar in Focus: revisiting English loanwords (외래어)
lessons.subtitle: 문법 탐구 · 외래어 · 콩글리쉬 · 골프 · 컴퓨터 · 가이드 · 미팅 · 핸드폰 · 외래어 표기

explanations.title: Revisiting English loanwords
explanations.body: Loanwords (외래어), words adopted from the West, are one of the three major components of the Korean vocabulary, along with Sino-Korean words and native Korean words. There are over 20,000 loanwords, and the number keeps growing. Although many of these loanwords are technical or scientific, the loanwords are found in almost every aspect of Korean life. Fortunately, a great majority of them are from English, and you can learn them with little difficulty. Loanwords can be categorized into one of the following three groups (the English glosses of the words are mine):

explanations.title: 1. Loanwords with no Korean equivalents
explanations.body: 골프, 테니스, 기타, 피아노, 나이트 클럽, 냅킨, 네트워크, 넥타이, 디자인, 레이저, 로비, 마라톤, 모델, 에어백, 트렁크, 햄버거, 컴퓨터, etc.

explanations.title: 2. Loanwords with Korean equivalents
explanations.body: 가이드 (안내), 그린벨트 (녹지), 디저트 (후식), 랭킹 (순위), 레이스 (경주), 멤버 (회원), 박스 (상자), 빌딩 (건물), 신드롬 (증후군), 와인 (포도주), 타이어 (바퀴), etc.

rows: a green belt; Korean equivalent 녹지

explanations.title: 3. Loanwords whose meanings have been localized
explanations.body: 미팅 (a group blind date; “meeting”), 핫도그 (a corn dog; “hot dog”), 사이다 (clear soda like Sprite™; “cider”), 개런티 (payment to an actor; “guarantee”), 스킨 로션 (toner; “skin lotion”), 비닐 (plastic; “vinyl”), 원피스 (dress; “one piece”), 콘도 (time-shared property; “condo”), 탤런트 (TV actors/actresses; “talent”), 핸드폰 (a cell phone; “hand phone”), etc. The loanwords in the last category are often called 콩글리쉬 (“Konglish”), which means “Korean English.”

explanations.title: Writing loanwords: official and nonofficial transcription
explanations.body: Although Koreans change the pronunciation of loanwords only slightly to make the words easier to speak in Korean, some loanwords are written in Korean uniformly, while others are not. For example, piano is consistently spelled 피아노, whereas agenda is spelled 아젠다, 아젠더, or 어젠다. In order to reduce the confusion and promote consistent transcription, 국립국어연구원 established transcription rules (1986), some of which you learned in the Introductory Unit. You can find Korean transcriptions of frequently used loanwords on the website 한글사랑 서울사랑 기본 외래어 표기. Some examples follow.

explanations.title: English words that are not yet loanwords
explanations.body: Koreans also use many English words which have not yet become part of the Korean language. These English words are readily found in all aspects of daily life. As the use of foreign language spreads rapidly, even Korean native speakers have a hard time keeping up with the changes. After a while, some foreign words will become standard loanwords, while others will fade away.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 1 (searching naver.com or daum.net for two minutes and writing as many loanwords as possible in Korean and English), Follow-up 2 (SMART Board) and Follow-up 3 (listening to a YTN news clip about an event held in Busan and writing the loanwords in Korean with their English meanings) are web, computer and audio activities.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (Reading): skim for loanwords
explanations.body: Skim the following text about an event that Daegu City plans to hold. The book asks you to write in English, as quickly as you can, the loanwords or foreign-language words you recognize (including proper nouns). The text is the book’s (chosun.com) with the numbers spelled out (17일 is 십칠 일; 18일부터 2월15일까지 is 십팔 일부터 이 월 십오 일까지; 14개 is 십사 개; 미션1 is 미션 일; 150명 is 백오십 명); the brackets around 스탬프 투어, 미션 일 and 미션 이 and the dash-like marks are dropped. The book glosses 생태: ecological; eco, 선착순: in the order of arrival; first-come first-served, 지치다: to be exhausted, 추가하다: to add, 획득하다: to obtain and 후기: review. The English is mine.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with so that they can provide other activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify and discuss the low birthrate trend in Korea, its causes and effects, and incentives for reversing it; identify and discuss the trend of young Koreans studying abroad; and understand and discuss the trend of people preferring famous name-brand merchandise and how the trend has affected the Korean economy.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; an attributive form + 것처럼/같이 (like; as if); loanwords in Korean; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 저출산 (低出産), 전담 (專擔), and 명품 선호 (名品 選好).

exercises.prompt: What does 대구시는 설 명절을 맞아 대구를 방문하는 국내외 관광객들이 다양하게 체험하고 즐길 수 있는 대구 관광여행 이벤트를 실시한다고 십칠 일 밝혔다. mean?
options: The city of Daegu announced on the 17th that, for the Lunar New Year holiday, it will hold a Daegu tourist-trip event that domestic and foreign tourists visiting Daegu can experience and enjoy in various ways.

This program, which runs from the 18th to February 15, uses the mobile app “Stamp Tour”: you obtain two or more stamps out of 14 ecological resource courses (Mission 1), then obtain five or more stamps out of 14 general tourist-spot courses (Mission 2), and press the gift application button on each page.
An additional event is also held for city tour passengers.

The first program of this event is the “Natural Daegu Hidden Healing Finding Stamp Tour,” in which you can tour the hidden ecological resources of Daegu, heal a mind tired of daily life and also receive a gift.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank. The Loan Words section repeats 브랜드, which I list once; the Grammar Features section lists the grammar of the chapter; the last section lists the Sino-Korean related words of 저출산, 전담 and 명품 선호 as the book gives them.

The example sentences with digits and letters are respelled in Hangul (20일 → 이십 일; 20대 30대 → 이십 대 삼십 대; 15% → 십오 퍼센트; 1년 → 일 년; the book’s R&D in the example of 경쟁력 is dropped).

lessons.subtitle: 사회 문제 · 성형수술 · 실직 · 안보 · 成形手術 · 失職 · 安保 · 불규칙 동사 · 까 봐

explanations.title: What Chapter 48 teaches (사회 문제 2)
explanations.body:
Chapter 48, “Social Issues II”, has a vocabulary builder, three topic presentations (a survey on cosmetic surgery, a recession and unemployment, the duty of military service) with grammar in focus, activities, a self-evaluation and the core vocabulary.

When you finish the chapter you will be able to: identify, talk about, and express opinions about issues and incidents concerning cosmetic surgery and its popularity in Korea; identify and talk about the issues related to employment, unemployment, layoffs, downsizing, and restructuring; and identify and discuss issues concerning military service in Korea.

You will become familiar with: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ까 봐(서) (being afraid/aware that [something] might …); a summary of irregular verbs; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 성형수술 (成形手術), 실직 (失職), and 안보 (安保).

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 성형수술 (成形手術)
explanations.body: This Sino-Korean word means plastic surgery or cosmetic surgery. The first syllable 성 (成) means achieve, accomplish, or make, as in 성인 (an adult; “achieved person”) and 성적 (a result; a record; “accomplished work”). The second syllable 형 (形) means shape, form, or style, as in 신형 (new style; new model) and 서구형 (Western style). 수 (手) means hand or manual, as in 수공 (handicraft; handwork) and 수족 (limbs: “hands and feet”). The last syllable 술 (術) means skill or artifice, as in 미술 (fine arts; “beautiful skill”). Thus the literal meaning of 성형수술 is “shape-making hand skill.” The book asks you to guess 성장, 악수, 성공, 수건, 완성, 수동, 원형, 기술, 삼각형, 예술 and 화술 (the book prints 원형 twice; it glosses 완 [完]: complete, 원 [圓]: round and 건 [巾]: a towel; my answers):

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 실직 (失職)
explanations.body: The first syllable 실 (失) means lose or loss, as in 실례 (rudeness; impoliteness; “loss of etiquette”) and 실수 (a mistake; an error; loss of control; “loss of a hand/grip”). The second syllable 직 (職) means job or position, as in 이직 (transfer of a job) and 직업 (an occupation; a calling; a vocation; “position work”). Thus, 실직 means unemployment or loss of one’s employment. The book asks you to guess 실업률, 실망, 실점, 직원, 직장 and 취직 (the book glosses 망 [望]: hope, aspiration and 점 [點]: a point; my answers):

rows: a mistake; an error; loss of control; “loss of a hand/grip”
an occupation; a calling; a vocation; “position work”

explanations.title: Sino-Korean in use: 안보 (安保)
explanations.body: The first syllable 안 (安), which you learned in Chapter 44, means serene, tranquil, or comfort, as in 안녕하다 (to be fine; “to be serene and comfortable”). The second syllable 보 (保) means keep or preserve. Thus, the literal meaning of 안보 is “keep serenity” or “preserve tranquility,” and the word means national security. The book asks you to guess 안심, 불안, 편안, 보호, 보온 and 보험 (my answers):

rows: to be fine; “to be serene and comfortable”

explanations.title: Vocabulary Learning Strategy: expand vocabulary using Sino-Korean prefixes and suffixes
explanations.body: Sino-Korean syllables can function as a prefix or suffix when combined with words. They add to or modify the meaning of the words. For example, the Sino-Korean syllable 불/부 (不) can function as a prefix and adds the meaning of not, no, non-, im-, in-, or il-, as in 불가능 (impossibility), 부정확 (inaccuracy), and 부자연 (unnaturalness). When you know the meaning of the prefix, you can easily guess that these words imply something negative, even if you are unsure of the meaning of the words. The following tables list some common Sino-Korean syllables that can function as prefixes or suffixes. You can visit 국립국어원 if you want to learn more about Korean prefixes and suffixes.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: cosmetic surgery in Korea
explanations.body: Cosmetic surgical procedures (성형수술) have witnessed a significant increase in recent years in the United States, with the American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) reporting over 1.5 million such procedures in 2020 alone. Cosmetic surgery is also popular in South Korea. Many Koreans, particularly among young adults, opt for cosmetic surgery as a means to enhance their appearance. In the 1950s and 1960s, when surgical skills and technology were rudimentary, cosmetic surgery in Korea was mainly limited to double eyelid surgery (쌍꺼풀 수술), which helps make the eyes look larger. As surgical skills and technology improved, surgical alteration of the nose and cheekbones became commonplace. These days, various other surgeries for the body and face are popular, partially influenced by entertainers who have enhanced their appearance through cosmetic surgery. In the job market, attractiveness has become an advantage for applicants. This fact accounts for the increase in cosmetic surgery among men, although women still make up the majority of people choosing cosmetic surgery. Korean plastic surgeons are highly skilled and many foreigners, especially Asians, visit Korea to have cosmetic surgery performed. Some well-known clinics have opened branches in China to accommodate the increasing number of Chinese patients.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): surgery during the New Year holiday
explanations.body: The following text is about the New Year’s holiday (한겨레). The book asks you to read it and answer in English: what (new) trend the article is about, and how the medical clinics promote their businesses to take advantage of it (two examples). The text is the book’s with the age written out (26 is 스물여섯 살); the quotation marks are removed. The book glosses ~족 [族]: a tribe, a group, a party; ~생 [生]: a student, an apprentice; 김 아무개 씨 = 김 모 씨; and 지방: a region outside the capital city. The English is mine.

examples.text: 비교적 긴 설 연휴를 이용해 올 상반기 기업 공채 등에 대비해 성형수술을 하려는 취업준비족들이 늘고 있다.
examples.translation: bigyojeok gin seol yeonhyureul iyonghae ol sangbangi gieop gongchae deunge daebihae seonghyeongsusureul haryeoneun chwieopjunbijokdeuri neulgo itda. — Job-preparation “tribes” who want to have cosmetic surgery to prepare for this year’s first-half corporate open recruitment, making use of the relatively long Lunar New Year holiday, are increasing.

examples.text: 취업준비생 김 아무개스물여섯 살, 여 씨는 이번 설에 고향에 가지 않고 쌍꺼풀 수술을 하기로 했다.
examples.translation: chwieopjunbisaeng gim amugaeseumuryeoseot sal, yeo ssineun ibeon seore gohyange gaji anko ssangkkeopul susureul hagiro haetda. — Ms. Kim, 26, a job preparer, decided not to go to her hometown this New Year and to have double eyelid surgery.

examples.text: 김 씨는 다니던 회사 사정이 어려워져 다음 달 퇴사가 결정됐다며 부모님께서도 귀성보다는 취직이 먼저라며 이해해 주셨다고 말했다.
examples.translation: gim ssineun danideon hoesa sajeongi eoryeowojeo daeum dal toesaga gyeoljeongdwaetdamyeo bumonimkkeseodo gwiseongbodaneun chwijigi meonjeoramyeo ihaehae jusyeotdago malhaetda. — Ms. Kim said that, because the situation at the company she had been working for became difficult, her leaving next month has been decided, and that her parents also understood, saying getting a job comes before going home for the holiday.

examples.text: 일부 성형외과들은 취업 사이트 등과 연계해 설맞이 특별 상품을 내놓기도 했다.
examples.translation: ilbu seonghyeongoegwadeureun chwieop saiteu deunggwa yeongyehae seolmaji teukbyeol sangpumeul naenokido haetda. — Some plastic surgery clinics have even come out with special New Year products in connection with job sites and the like.

examples.text: 단체로 수술을 받으면 큰 폭으로 깎아 주거나, 지방에서 올라오는 이들한테 숙소를 제공하는 곳도 있다.
examples.translation: danchero susureul badeumyeon keun pogeuro kkakka jugeona, jibangeseo ollaoneun ideulhante suksoreul jegonghaneun gotdo itda. — Some places give a large discount if you have surgery as a group, or provide lodging to those who come up from the provinces.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 answered (mine)
explanations.body: 1. The trend: job seekers who have cosmetic surgery during the long Lunar New Year holiday to prepare for first-half corporate hiring. 2. Two examples of promotion: special New Year products tied up with job sites, with a large discount for group surgery; and lodging offered to those who come up from the provinces.

explanations.title: Activity 2 (Reading): problems with cosmetic surgery in China
explanations.body: The following news article addresses problems associated with cosmetic surgery in China. The book asks you to fill in a table in English (the issue addressed and the solution to the issue). The text is the book’s with 28일 spelled 이십팔 일; the quotation marks are removed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 중국 여성들 사이에서 해외 성형수술이 유행하면서 중국 당국에 새로운 고민이 생겼다.
examples.translation: jungguk yeoseongdeul saieseo haeoe seonghyeongsusuri yuhaenghamyeonseo jungguk dangguge saeroun gomini saenggyeotda. — As cosmetic surgery abroad has become popular among Chinese women, a new worry has arisen for the Chinese authorities.

examples.text: 여권 사진 속 모습과 입국 때의 실제 얼굴이 너무 다른 여성이 많아서 본인 확인이 어려운 때도 있기 때문이다.
examples.translation: yeogwon sajin sok moseupgwa ipguk ttaeui silje eolguri neomu dareun yeoseongi manaseo bonin hwagini eoryeoun ttaedo itgi ttaemunida. — This is because there are many women whose appearance in the passport photo and actual face at entry are so different that confirming their identity is sometimes difficult.

examples.text: 얼마 전 한국에서 성형 수술한 왕링 씨는 이십팔 일 밤 항공편으로 서울 여행을 마치고 베이징공항을 통해 귀국했다.
examples.translation: eolma jeon hangugeseo seonghyeong susulhan wangning ssineun isippal il bam hanggongpyeoneuro seoul yeohaengeul machigo beijinggonghangeul tonghae gwigukaetda. — Ms. Wang Ling, who had cosmetic surgery in Korea not long ago, finished her trip to Seoul on the night of the 28th by air and returned home through Beijing airport.

examples.text: 이 과정에서 왕 씨는 경찰의 조사를 받아야 했다.
examples.translation: i gwajeongeseo wang ssineun gyeongcharui josareul badaya haetda. — In this process Ms. Wang had to be questioned by the police.

examples.text: 한국에서 성형수술을 한 뒤 여권 사진과 실제 얼굴에 차이가 너무 컸기 때문이었다.
examples.translation: hangugeseo seonghyeongsusureul han dwi yeogwon sajingwa silje eolgure chaiga neomu keotgi ttaemunieotda. — It was because, after having cosmetic surgery in Korea, the difference between her passport photo and her actual face was too big.

examples.text: 이와 관련, 베이징 공항의 한 관계자는 귀를 성형 수술하는 사람은 거의 없어 본인 확인을 위해 최근에는 귀 모양을 비교하는 노하우가 생겼다고 전했다.

explanations.title: Topic B: the recession (불경기)
explanations.body: The following magazine article is about a man in his late 40s who is concerned about losing his job. The picture’s labels are 실직, 이직 and 창업? (The English is mine; the book gives none. The numbers are spelled out: 40대 is 사십 대, 20년 is 이십 년, 50세 이하 is 오십 세 이하.)

examples.text: 최준형 씨는 아내와 딸 하나를 둔 사십 대 가장이다.
examples.translation: choejunhyeong ssineun anaewa ttal hanareul dun sasip dae gajangida. — Mr. Choi Jun-hyeong is a family head in his forties with a wife and one daughter.

examples.text: 대기업에서 이십 년 동안 근무하고 있는데 급여와 사원복지 등의 근무 여건이 좋다.
examples.translation: daegieobeseo isip nyeon dongan geunmuhago inneunde geubyeowa sawonbokji deungui geunmu yeogeoni jota. — He has been working at a large company for twenty years, and the working conditions, such as salary and employee welfare, are good.

examples.text: 몇 달 전에는 해외영업부 부장이 돼서 바빠졌다.
examples.translation: myeot dal jeoneneun haeoeyeongeopbu bujangi dwaeseo bappajeotda. — A few months ago he became the head of the overseas sales department and became busy.

examples.text: 그런데 요즘 불경기 때문에 회사 분위기가 좋지 않다.
examples.translation: geureonde yojeum bulgyeonggi ttaemune hoesa bunwigiga jochi anta. — But these days the atmosphere at the company is not good because of the recession.

examples.text: 경영 사정이 어려워져서 구조조정을 한다는 소문이 있다.
examples.translation: gyeongyeong sajeongi eoryeowojeoseo gujojojeongeul handaneun somuni itda. — There is a rumor that, because the management situation has become difficult, they are going to restructure.

examples.text: 곧 인원 감축을 하면서 직원들을 해고할 거라고 한다.
examples.translation: got inwon gamchugeul hamyeonseo jigwondeureul haegohal georago handa. — They say that soon, as they cut personnel, they will lay off employees.

examples.text: 특히 오십 세 이하의 직원들에게도 조기퇴직이나 명예퇴직을 권유할 거라고 한다.
examples.translation: teuki osip se ihaui jigwondeuregedo jogitoejigina myeongyetoejigeul gwonyuhal georago handa. — In particular, they say they will recommend early retirement or honorary retirement even to employees aged 50 or under.

examples.text: 그래서 최준형 씨는 요즘 출근하기가 싫다.
examples.translation: geuraeseo choejunhyeong ssineun yojeum chulgeunhagiga silta. — So Mr. Choi does not want to go to work these days.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): youth employment rates
explanations.body: The following article is from an online newspaper (YonhapNews). The book asks you to check the topic, say what each number means and underline and translate the topic sentence. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (34세 is 삼십사 세, 15~24세 is 십오 세에서 이십사 세, 23.8% is 이십삼 점 팔 퍼센트, OECD is 오이씨디, 19일 is 십구 일). The book glosses 최하위: lowest in rank. The English is mine.

examples.text: 우리나라의 삼십사 세 이하 청년 고용률이 경제협력개발기구오이씨디 최하위 수준인 것으로 나타났다.
examples.translation: urinaraui samsipsa se iha cheongnyeon goyongnyuri gyeongjehyeomnyeokgaebalgiguoissidi choehawi sujunin geoseuro natanatda. — It turned out that our country’s employment rate for youth aged 34 or under is at the lowest level in the OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development).

examples.text: 한국노동연구원은 지난해 발표된 오이씨디의 고용동향 통계를 분석해 우리나라 십오 세에서 이십사 세, 이십오 세에서 삼십사 세 고용률이 오이씨디 국가 중 각각 꼴찌인 헝가리와 멕시코 다음 순위였다고 십구 일 밝혔다.
examples.translation: hangungnodongyeonguwoneun jinanhae balpyodoen oissidiui goyongdonghyang tonggyereul bunseokae urinara sibo seeseo isipsa se, isibo seeseo samsipsa se goyongnyuri oissidi gukga jung gakgak kkoljjiin heonggariwa meksiko daeum sunwiyeotdago sipgu il balkyeotda. — The Korea Labor Institute analyzed the OECD’s employment trend statistics announced last year and announced on the 19th that our country’s employment rates for ages 15 to 24 and 25 to 34 ranked next after Hungary and Mexico, which were respectively last among the OECD countries.

explanations.title: Activity 1 (Reading): which word is described?
explanations.body: Match each description with the word it describes: a. 명예퇴직 b. 경기침체 c. 고용증가 d. 구직난 e. 실업급여 (one word does not have a match). The descriptions are the book’s with the numbers spelled out (7년 is 칠 년, 3개월 is 삼 개월); the English and answers are mine. The unmatched word is c. 고용증가 (an increase in employment).

rows: 김소정 씨는 지난 칠 년 동안 금융회사에서 근무했다. 그런데 회사 사정이 어려워져서 삼 개월 전에 해고되었다. 실직한 후 정부에서 주는 돈으로 생활하고 있다.
전 세계적인 불황의 영향이 국내 경제에도 미치고 있다. 이에 따라 수출과 수입이 감소하고 소비도 줄어들고 있다. 그래서 폐업하는 회사들이 늘고 있다.
이상호 씨는 중소기업의 해외 영업부장으로 근무해 왔다. 그런데 최근에 회사 전체에 구조조정을 한다는 소문이 있었다. 그래서 해고당하기 전에 미리 회사를 그만두기로 했다.
올해는 새로 인력을 고용하려는 기업들이 많지 않아서 일자리를 구하기가 어렵다. 특히 근무여건이 좋고 연봉이 높은 대기업은 입사 경쟁률이 매우 높다.

Ms. Kim So-jeong worked at a financial company for the last seven years. But the company’s situation became difficult and she was laid off three months ago. After losing her job she is living on money given by the government.

The effect of the worldwide depression is reaching the domestic economy too. Accordingly exports and imports are decreasing and consumption is also declining. So the number of companies going out of business is increasing.

Mr. Lee Sang-ho has worked as the overseas sales manager of a small and medium-sized company. But recently there was a rumor that the whole company would be restructured. So he decided to quit the company in advance, before being fired.

This year there are not many companies trying to hire new personnel, so it is hard to find a job. In particular, large companies with good working conditions and high annual salaries have a very high competition rate for entry.

explanations.title: Activity 3 (Reading): a Q&A on starting a business
explanations.body: The following Q&A exchange is from an online Korean newspaper (Hankyoreh). The answer is headed 지원제도 풍성… 맞는 분야 찾아 도전하길 (Plenty of support systems… I hope you will find a suitable field and take the challenge) and signed by 이랑, chief researcher at the Job Research Center of the Korea Employment Information Service. The text is the book’s with 20, 30대 spelled out (이십 대, 삼십 대), CEO and IT and E-biz spelled in Hangul (씨이오, 아이티, 이비즈); the parenthetical advice to see the Seoul City websites is left out of the passage. The book glosses 정신: spirit; 예비: prospective; 육성하다: to promote, to foster. The English is mine.

examples.text: 요즘 취업이 너무 어려워서 창업을 계획하고 있습니다. 어떻게 준비해야 할까요?
examples.translation: yojeum chwieobi neomu eoryeowoseo changeobeul gyehoekago itseumnida. eotteoke junbihaeya halkkayo? — Getting a job is so difficult these days that I am planning to start a business. How should I prepare?

examples.text: 창업을 희망하는 학생들은 우선 창업에 적합한 기업가 정신과 창업 마인드를 갖추고 있는지 점검해 보기 바랍니다.
examples.translation: changeobeul huimanghaneun haksaengdeureun useon changeobe jeokapan gieopga jeongsingwa changeop maindeureul gatchugo inneunji jeomgeomhae bogi baramnida. — Students who hope to start a business should first check whether they have the entrepreneurial spirit and the start-up mindset suited to starting a business.

examples.text: 또 혼자서 준비하기보다는 창업에 필요한 교육을 받고 창업 동아리에 참가하여 다양한 경험과 경력을 쌓아 보기 바랍니다.
examples.translation: tto honjaseo junbihagibodaneun changeobe piryohan gyoyugeul batgo changeop dongarie chamgahayeo dayanghan gyeongheomgwa gyeongnyeogeul ssaa bogi baramnida. — Also, rather than preparing alone, I hope you will receive the education needed for starting a business, join a start-up club and build up various experiences and careers.

examples.text: 또 최근 서울시에서는 이십 대, 삼십 대 예비창업자들을 대상으로 청년 씨이오를 육성하기 위한 프로젝트를 추진하겠다고 발표한 바 있습니다.
examples.translation: tto choegeun seoulsieseoneun isip dae, samsip dae yebichangeopjadeureul daesangeuro cheongnyeon ssiioreul yukseonghagi wihan peurojekteureul chujinhagetdago balpyohan ba itseumnida. — Also, Seoul City recently announced that it will push ahead with a project to foster young CEOs targeting prospective entrepreneurs in their twenties and thirties.

explanations.body:

lessons.title: 606. Ch 48 · Grammar in Focus: –(으)ㄹ까 봐(서) (being afraid that…)
lessons.subtitle: 접속 어미 · –(으)ㄹ까 봐(서) · 걱정 · 두려움 · 두렵다 · 무섭다 · 겁나다 · 떨리다

explanations.title: Conjunctive Ending –(으)ㄹ까 봐(서)
explanations.body: The conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ까 봐(서), which translates to being afraid that [something/someone] might… or being aware that [something/someone] might …, expresses the subject’s (of a sentence) concern or awareness of future problems. For example:

headers: Written form of the book’s examples
rows: 시험에 떨어질까 봐(서) 공부를 열심히 했어요.
Being afraid that I might fail the exam, I studied hard.
Being aware that I might fail the exam, I am worried / I am worried that I might fail the exam.

examples.text: 시험에 떨어질까 봐서 공부를 열심히 했어요.
examples.translation: siheome tteoreojilkka bwaseo gongbureul yeolsimhi haesseoyo. — Being afraid that I might fail the exam, I studied hard (with the 서 form).

examples.text: 시험에 떨어질까 봐서 걱정이에요.
examples.translation: siheome tteoreojilkka bwaseo geokjeongieyo. — I am worried that I might fail the exam (with the 서 form).

explanations.title: Two kinds of main clause
explanations.body:
Note that the main clause following the conjunctive ending can express one of two ideas: the subject’s proactive action to prevent future problems, as in the first example (공부를 열심히 했어요), or the subject’s feelings or emotion, as in the second example (걱정이에요).

When the main clause expresses the subject’s feelings or emotion, verbs such as 두렵다, 무섭다, 걱정되다/하다, 겁나다, or 떨리다 are commonly used, and the whole sentence can translate to The subject is afraid [worried/scared/nervous, etc.] that something might…. For example:

rows: to be scary; to be afraid

examples.text: 차가 많이 막힐까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.translation: chaga mani makilkka bwa geokjeongieyo. — I am worried that there might be a traffic jam.

examples.text: 비행기가 추락할까 봐 무서웠어요?
examples.translation: bihaenggiga churakalkka bwa museowosseoyo? — Were you scared that the plane might crash?

explanations.title: Conjunctive Ending: verb stem + (으)ㄹ까 봐(서)
explanations.body: Add –ㄹ까 봐(서) to a verb stem that ends in a vowel (or ㄹ) and –을까 봐(서) to a stem that ends in a consonant. More examples:

examples.text: 김 일병은 과속으로 단속에 걸릴까 봐 천천히 운전했습니다.
examples.translation: gim ilbyeongeun gwasogeuro dansoge geollilkka bwa cheoncheonhi unjeonhaetseumnida. — Afraid that he might be caught for speeding, PFC Kim drove slowly.

examples.text: 음식이 부족할까 봐서 음식을 많이 준비했어요.
examples.translation: eumsigi bujokalkka bwaseo eumsigeul mani junbihaesseoyo. — Afraid that there would not be enough, I prepared a lot of food.

examples.text: 수업에 늦을까 봐 불안해요.
examples.translation: sueobe neujeulkka bwa buranhaeyo. — Being aware that I might be late for class, I feel nervous. / I feel nervous that I might be late for class.

explanations.title: Follow-up 4 (the book’s models)
explanations.body: In this activity you share with classmates what you do or will do to prevent something you are afraid might happen to you. The book’s model sentences for the pair work (the English is mine):

explanations.title: Follow-up 3 (Reading): concerns posted on a Q&A site
explanations.body: The following concerns are posted on the Q&A section of a website. The book asks you to fill in a table in English (the writer’s concern/fear and the writer’s feeling or action). The text is the book’s with 3학년 spelled 삼 학년 and 1년 spelled 일 년; the English is mine.

examples.text: 대학교 삼 학년 학생입니다. 요즘은 대학을 졸업해도 취직하기가 어렵다는 말을 많이 듣습니다. 저도 졸업한 후에 취업을 못 할까 봐 걱정이 많이 됩니다. 그래서 일 년 정도 휴학을 할까 생각 중입니다. 휴학하면서 취업 준비를 더 한 후에 졸업하려고 합니다. 어떻게 생각하세요?
examples.translation: daehakgyo sam hangnyeon haksaengimnida. yojeumeun daehageul joreopaedo chwijikagiga eoryeopdaneun mareul mani deutseumnida. jeodo joreopan hue chwieobeul mot halkka bwa geokjeongi mani doemnida. geuraeseo il nyeon jeongdo hyuhageul halkka saenggak jungimnida. hyuhakamyeonseo chwieop junbireul deo han hue joreoparyeogo hamnida. eotteoke saenggakaseyo? — I am a third-year university student. These days I often hear that it is hard to get a job even after graduating from university. I am also very worried that I might not be able to get a job after I graduate. So I am thinking of taking about a year off from school. While on leave I want to prepare more for employment and then graduate. What do you think?

examples.text: 창업을 준비하고 있습니다. 저는 사업 경험이 없어서 걱정이 큽니다. 퇴직금으로 사업을 하려고 하는데, 실패할까 봐 무섭습니다. 창업에 성공하려면 어떻게 해야 합니까?
examples.translation: changeobeul junbihago itseumnida. jeoneun saeop gyeongheomi eopseoseo geokjeongi keumnida. toejikgeumeuro saeobeul haryeogo haneunde, silpaehalkka bwa museopseumnida. changeobe seonggongharyeomyeon eotteoke haeya hamnikka? — I am preparing to start a business. I have no business experience, so I am very worried. I am going to run a business with my retirement pay, but I am scared that I might fail. What should I do to succeed in starting a business?

rows: That after graduating he or she might not be able to get a job
Is very worried; is thinking of taking about a year off to prepare more for employment and then graduate
That the business might fail (no business experience; using retirement pay)
Very worried and scared; asks how to succeed in starting a business

explanations.title: Topic C: the duty of military service (병역의무)
explanations.body: The following excerpt is from an interview about a current social issue. (The English is mine; the book gives none. 작년 3월 is 작년 삼 월; the quotation marks and the underlining of 저지르는, 더, 강화되어야 and the label 징병 in the book are left out.)

examples.text: 기자: 최근 허위 진단서를 제출해서 병역을 면제받은 운동선수가 경찰에 적발됐습니다.
examples.translation: gija: choegeun heowi jindanseoreul jechulhaeseo byeongyeogeul myeonjebadeun undongseonsuga gyeongchare jeokbaldwaetseumnida. — Reporter: Recently an athlete who submitted a false medical certificate and was exempted from military service was caught by the police.

examples.text: 또 얼마 전에는 정신질환이 있는 것처럼 속여 군대에 가지 않은 연예인이 구속된 사건도 있었습니다.
examples.translation: tto eolma jeoneneun jeongsinjilhwani inneun geotcheoreom sogyeo gundaee gaji aneun yeonyeini gusokdoen sageondo isseotseumnida. — Also, not long ago there was an incident in which an entertainer who deceived people as if he had a mental illness and did not go to the army was arrested.

examples.text: 안보가 무엇보다 중요한 한국에서 이와 같은 병역기피는 사회문제가 되고 있는데요.
examples.translation: anboga mueotboda jungyohan hangugeseo iwa gateun byeongyeokgipineun sahoemunjega doego inneundeyo. — In Korea, where security is more important than anything, this kind of draft evasion is becoming a social problem.

examples.text: 이에 대한 시민의 의견을 들어 보겠습니다.
examples.translation: ie daehan siminui uigyeoneul deureo bogetseumnida. — Let us hear citizens’ opinions on this.

examples.text: 남자: 저는 작년 삼 월에 군대에서 제대하고 이번 학기에 복학한 학생입니다.
examples.translation: namja: jeoneun jangnyeon sam wore gundaeeseo jedaehago ibeon hakgie bokakan haksaengimnida. — Man: I am a student who was discharged from the army last March and returned to school this semester.

examples.text: 국방의 의무는 국민이 지켜야 할 가장 기본적인 의무라고 생각합니다.
examples.translation: gukbangui uimuneun gungmini jikyeoya hal gajang gibonjeogin uimurago saenggakamnida. — I think the duty of national defense is the most basic duty that the people must keep.

examples.text: 물론 대부분의 사람은 잘 지키지만 일부 병역 비리를 저지르는 사람들도 있는 것 같아요.
examples.translation: mullon daebubunui sarameun jal jikijiman ilbu byeongyeok birireul jeojireuneun saramdeuldo inneun geot gatayo. — Of course most people keep it well, but it seems there are also some people who commit military service corruption.

examples.text: 이를 막기 위해서 병무청에서는 징병 신체검사를 더 철저히 해야 합니다.
examples.translation: ireul makgi wihaeseo byeongmucheongeseoneun jingbyeong sinchegeomsareul deo cheoljeohi haeya hamnida. — To prevent this, the Military Manpower Administration should do the conscription physical examination more thoroughly.

examples.text: 그리고 비리에 대한 처벌도 더 강화되어야 하고요.
examples.translation: geurigo birie daehan cheobeoldo deo ganghwadoeeoya hagoyo. — And the punishment for corruption should also be strengthened more.

explanations.title: 한국에서는: military service in Korea
explanations.body:
In Korea, military service (군복무) is compulsory for able men. Therefore, all males, after graduating from high school and up to the age of 40, are required to take a physical examination for conscription. Depending on their overall health, men are put in active military service for 18 to 21 months or public service for 36 months. Men with serious health problems are exempt from the draft. Also, men with special circumstances (e.g., studying abroad) must get prior approval from the Military Manpower Administration (병무청) to postpone their service. While military service is considered an important civic duty, high-profile public officials, entertainers, and athletes exempted from the draft are often scrutinized by the media for the possibility of having avoided military service through illegal means.

The book’s useful website is the Military Manpower Administration (병무청).

explanations.title: Presentation Study b: the table (mine)
explanations.body: The book asks you to read Topic Presentation C and fill in the methods for avoiding the military draft and the methods for enforcing it. My answers:

headers: Methods for avoiding the military draft
Methods for enforcing the military draft
rows: Using a false medical certificate (an athlete was exempted from service); pretending to have a mental illness (an entertainer); committing military service corruption

A more thorough conscription physical examination by the Military Manpower Administration; stronger punishment for corruption; a system giving more benefits (tuition support, an advantage in getting a job) to those who completed their service

explanations.title: Follow-up 2 (Reading): the entertainer 유승준
explanations.body: The following article is about a Korean-American entertainer, 유승준 (Yonhap News). The book asks you to fill in a table in English (his biography; the reasons why he was not allowed to enter Korea; what happened after the initial denial of entry). The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (43 is 마흔세 살 in the text, as an age; 20여 년 is 이십여 년; 1997년 4월 is 천구백구십칠 년 사 월; 2002년 1월 is 이천이 년 일 월; 2015년 9월 is 이천십오 년 구 월; F-4 is 에프 사); the quotation marks are removed. The book glosses 취득하다: to acquire; 논란: controversy; 영주권: a green card; 비난: criticism; 거부: refusal. The English is mine.

examples.translation: miguk simingwon chwideuge ttareun byeongyeok gipi uihogeuro ipgugi geumjidoen gasu yuseungjunmigungmyeong seutibeu seungjun yu, maheunse sal ssiga isibyeo nyeon mane hanguge ol su itge doeeotseumnida. — Singer Yoo Seung-jun (American name Steve Seung-jun Yoo, 43), who was banned from entering because of suspicion of draft evasion through acquiring American citizenship, has become able to come to Korea after some twenty years.

examples.translation: ie ttara yu ssiui ipguge daehan chanban nollani keojigo itseumnida. — Accordingly, the pro-and-con controversy over Mr. Yoo’s entry is growing.

examples.text: 한국에서 태어났지만, 미국 영주권이 있던 유승준 씨는 천구백구십칠 년 사 월 한국에서 가수로 데뷔했습니다.
examples.translation: hangugeseo taeeonatjiman, miguk yeongjugwoni itdeon yuseungjun ssineun cheongubaekgusipchil nyeon sa wol hangugeseo gasuro debwihaetseumnida. — Although born in Korea, Mr. Yoo Seung-jun, who had a U.S. green card, debuted as a singer in Korea in April 1997.

examples.text: 유 씨는 가위, 나나나, 열정 등 히트곡을 내며 최고의 댄스 가수로 사랑을 받았습니다.
examples.translation: yu ssineun gawi, nanana, yeoljeong deung hiteugogeul naemyeo choegoui daenseu gasuro sarangeul badatseumnida. — Mr. Yoo had hit songs such as Scissors, Nanana and Passion, and was loved as the best dance singer.

examples.text: 유 씨는 한국의 병역법에 따라 징병 신체검사를 받았고, 검사 결과에 따라 공익근무요원이 될 예정이었습니다.
examples.translation: yu ssineun hangugui byeongyeokbeobe ttara jingbyeong sinchegeomsareul badatgo, geomsa gyeolgwae ttara gongikgeunmuyowoni doel yejeongieotseumnida. — Under Korea’s Military Service Act, Mr. Yoo took the conscription physical examination, and according to the result he was scheduled to become a public service worker.

examples.text: 하지만 이천이 년 일 월, 유 씨는 미국으로 건너가 한국 국적을 갑자기 포기하고 미국 시민권을 취득함으로써 병역을 기피했다는 비난을 받았습니다.
examples.translation: hajiman icheoni nyeon il wol, yu ssineun migugeuro geonneoga hanguk gukjeogeul gapjagi pogihago miguk simingwoneul chwideukameurosseo byeongyeogeul gipihaetdaneun binaneul badatseumnida. — But in January 2002, Mr. Yoo went over to the United States, suddenly gave up his Korean nationality and acquired American citizenship, and so was criticized for having evaded military service.

examples.text: 이천이 년 법무부로부터 한국 입국을 제한당했던 유 씨는 이천십오 년 구 월 재외동포 비자에프 사로 입국하도록 해 달라고 신청했지만 거부당했고, 이후 이를 취소해 달라는 소송을 계속 제기해 왔습니다.
examples.translation: icheoni nyeon beommuburobuteo hanguk ipgugeul jehandanghaetdeon yu ssineun icheonsibo nyeon gu wol jaeoedongpo bijaepeu saro ipgukadorok hae dallago sincheonghaetjiman geobudanghaetgo, ihu ireul chwisohae dallaneun sosongeul gyesok jegihae watseumnida. — Mr. Yoo, whose entry into Korea was restricted by the Ministry of Justice in 2002, applied in September 2015 to be allowed to enter on an overseas Korean visa (F-4) but was refused, and since then has continued to file lawsuits asking for this to be cancelled.

examples.text: 그러다 최근 고등법원이 유 씨에게 승소 판결을 내렸고, 이에 따라 유 씨는 재외동포로 한국에 입국해 가수 활동을 다시 할 수 있는 길이 열리게 되었습니다.
examples.translation: geureoda choegeun godeungbeobwoni yu ssiege seungso pangyeoreul naeryeotgo, ie ttara yu ssineun jaeoedongporo hanguge ipgukae gasu hwaldongeul dasi hal su inneun giri yeollige doeeotseumnida. — Then recently the high court gave Mr. Yoo a winning verdict, and accordingly a way opened for Mr. Yoo to enter Korea as an overseas Korean and resume his activities as a singer.

examples.text: 이번 판결로 유 씨의 한국 입국에 대해 찬반 여론이 뜨거워지고 있습니다.
examples.translation: ibeon pangyeollo yu ssiui hanguk ipguge daehae chanban yeoroni tteugeowojigo itseumnida. — With this ruling, pro-and-con public opinion on Mr. Yoo’s entry into Korea is heating up.

examples.text: 여러분께서는 유승준 씨의 한국 입국에 대해 어떻게 생각하십니까?
examples.translation: yeoreobunkkeseoneun yuseungjun ssiui hanguk ipguge daehae eotteoke saenggakasimnikka? — What do you think about Mr. Yoo Seung-jun’s entry into Korea?

explanations.title: Activity 1 a (Reading): military service terms
explanations.body: The following descriptions are about military service. The book asks you to find, from the word box, what each is about: 병역비리, 모병제, 징병제, 대체복무, 군 가산점제. The sentences are the book’s; the English and the answers are mine.

rows: 군 복무가 의무이기 때문에 일정 기간 군대에서 복무해야 한다.
종교적인 이유 등으로 군 복무를 할 수 없을 때 복무기간 동안 사회봉사 활동 등을 한다.
군 복무가 의무가 아니기 때문에 군대에 입대하고 싶은 사람만 지원한다.
군 복무를 피하려고 불법적인 방법을 사용한다. 돈을 주어서 신체검사 결과를 조작하기도 한다.
군 복무를 마친 남성에게 공무원시험에서 일정한 점수를 추가로 준다.
Because military service is a duty, one must serve in the army for a certain period.
When one cannot do military service for reasons such as religion, one does community service and the like during the service period.
Because military service is not a duty, only people who want to enlist in the army apply.
One uses illegal methods to avoid military service. One even gives money to manipulate the physical examination result.
Men who completed military service are given certain additional points in the civil service exam.

explanations.title: Activity 1 b (Reading): cases
explanations.body: The book asks you to read cases about military service and write which term from the box each is. The cases are the book’s with the numbers spelled out (10,000명 is 만 명, 150명 is 백오십 명, 5퍼센트 is 오 퍼센트, 4학년 is 사 학년); the English and the answers are mine.

rows: 정하나 씨는 어렸을 때부터 여군장교가 되는 것이 꿈이었습니다. 그래서 올해 간호대학을 졸업하면 간호장교로 군대에 지원해서 직업군인으로서 군대에서 계속 근무할 계획입니다.
김수민 씨는 군 복무를 마친 후 몇 년 전에 공무원시험에 합격했어요. 그 시험에는 만 명이 지원했는데 백오십 명만 뽑았기 때문에 경쟁률이 아주 높았습니다. 다행히 그때는 군 복무를 마친 사람에게는 오 퍼센트의 점수를 더 주었기 때문에, 김수민 씨한테는 많은 도움이 되었습니다.
올해 대학교 사 학년인 정재훈 씨는 졸업하기 전에 군 복무를 마치고 싶어합니다. 군 복무는 한국의 모든 남자에게는 의무이기 때문입니다. 게다가 현재 경제사정도 좋지 않기 때문에 올해 가을부터 휴학하고 군에 입대할 계획입니다.

Ms. Jeong Ha-na has dreamed since childhood of becoming a female military officer. So when she graduates from nursing college this year she plans to apply to the army as a nurse officer and continue serving as a career soldier.

Mr. Kim Su-min passed the civil service exam a few years ago after finishing military service. Ten thousand people applied for that exam but only 150 were chosen, so the competition rate was very high. Fortunately, at that time people who had finished military service were given 5 percent more points, so it helped Mr. Kim Su-min a lot.

Mr. Jeong Jae-hun, a fourth-year university student this year, wants to finish military service before graduating. This is because military service is a duty for all men in Korea. Besides, the current economic situation is not good either, so he plans to take leave from school from this fall and enlist in the army.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Activity 2 (a rerecorded YTN news item about crimes, filling in the type of crime, the persons involved and the jail sentence), Activity 3 (a rerecorded radio news report about a survey, summarized in English) and Activity 4 (reading articles about the military draft system and volunteer military system in different countries and exchanging the findings in pairs, writing a summary in the class notebook and presenting; the articles are not printed in the student text) are audio, pair and group activities.

lessons.title: 610. Ch 48 · Grammar in Focus: summary of irregular verbs
lessons.subtitle: 불규칙 동사 · ㄹ 불규칙 · ㅂ 불규칙 · ㄷ 불규칙 · 르 불규칙 · ㅎ 불규칙 · ㅅ 불규칙

explanations.title: Summary of Irregular Verbs
explanations.body: So far you have learned several irregular verbs, such as ㄹ verbs, ㅂ verbs, ㄷ verbs, 르 verbs, ㅅ verbs, and ㅎ verbs. These verbs are called irregular verbs because they go through an extra step in conjugation under certain conditions. For example, ㅅ irregular verbs go through an extra step of dropping ㅅ when the verb stem is followed by a vowel, as in 붓 + 어요 → 부어요. The following cards summarize the irregular verbs you learned in previous chapters. (The verb lists are the book’s; where the book gives an English gloss in parentheses I keep it; a gloss inside a verb is not read aloud in the Hangul lists.)

explanations.title: 1. ㄹ irregular verbs
explanations.body:
Condition/rule: When the verb stem is followed by ㄴ, ㅂ, or ㅅ, ㄹ is dropped.

Verbs: 알다, 살다, 열다, 졸다, 돌다, 말다, 놀다, 떠들다, 만들다, 벌다, 멀다, 길다.

The book’s examples (the English is mine):

examples.text: 지금 사는 집이 넓어요.
examples.translation: jigeum saneun jibi neolbeoyo. — The house I live in now is spacious.

examples.text: 아침에 오면 교실 문을 엽니다.
examples.translation: achime omyeon gyosil muneul yeomnida. — When I come in the morning, I open the classroom door.

examples.text: 돈을 얼마나 버세요?
examples.translation: doneul eolmana beoseyo? — How much money do you earn?

examples.text: 긴 치마를 사고 싶은데 없어요.
examples.translation: gin chimareul sago sipeunde eopseoyo. — I want to buy a long skirt, but there is none.

explanations.title: 2. ㅂ irregular verbs
explanations.body:
Condition/rule: When the verb stem is followed by a vowel, ㅂ is dropped and 우 + 어 is added.

Verbs: 굽다(to bake), 눕다, 춥다, 덥다, 쉽다, 어렵다, 맵다, 싱겁다, 반갑다, 고맙다, 더럽다, 즐겁다, 아쉽다, 아름답다, 곱다, 돕다.

Exceptions (these do not change): 입다, 잡다, 좁다, 굽다(to be bent).

The book’s footnote: For the verbs 돕다 and 곱다, 오 + 아 is added (돕다 → 도와요, 곱다 → 고와요).

The book’s examples (the English is mine):

examples.text: 숙제 좀 도와주세요.
examples.translation: sukje jom dowajuseyo. — Please help me with the homework a little.

examples.text: 피곤해서 누워서 쉬고 있어요.
examples.translation: pigonhaeseo nuwoseo swigo isseoyo. — I am tired, so I am lying down and resting.

examples.text: 공부가 어려워요.
examples.translation: gongbuga eoryeowoyo. — Studying is difficult.

examples.text: 방이 너무 더러워서 청소했어요.
examples.translation: bangi neomu deoreowoseo cheongsohaesseoyo. — The room was so dirty that I cleaned it.

examples.text: 옷을 입으세요.
examples.translation: oseul ibeuseyo. — Please put on clothes.

examples.text: 길이 좁으니까 조심하세요.
examples.translation: giri jobeunikka josimhaseyo. — The road is narrow, so please be careful.

explanations.title: 3. ㄷ irregular verbs
explanations.body:
Condition/rule: When the verb stem is followed by a vowel, ㄷ changes to ㄹ.

Verbs: 걷다, 묻다(to ask), 듣다, 싣다.

Exceptions (these do not change): 믿다, 받다, 닫다, 묻다(to bury).

The book’s examples (the English is mine):

examples.text: 빨리 걸어서 숨이 차요.
examples.translation: ppalli georeoseo sumi chayo. — I walked fast, so I am out of breath.

examples.text: 친구에게 물어봤어요.
examples.translation: chinguege mureobwasseoyo. — I asked a friend.

examples.text: 선물을 받았어요.
examples.translation: seonmureul badasseoyo. — I received a present.

examples.text: 문을 닫으세요.
examples.translation: muneul dadeuseyo. — Please close the door.

explanations.title: 4. 르 irregular verbs
explanations.body:
Condition/rule: When the verb stem is followed by a vowel, ㅡ is dropped from 르, ㄹ moves to the bottom of the preceding syllable, and 라 or 러 is added.

Verbs: 고르다, 모르다, 부르다, 자르다, 누르다, 기르다, 오르다, 바르다, 머무르다, 지르다, 서투르다, 배부르다, 마르다.

Exceptions (these do not change): 따르다.

The book’s examples (the English is mine):

examples.text: 한번 골라 보세요.
examples.translation: hanbeon golla boseyo. — Please try choosing one.

examples.text: 답을 몰라서 못 적었어요.
examples.translation: dabeul mollaseo mot jeogeosseoyo. — I did not know the answer, so I could not write it.

examples.text: 많이 먹어서 배가 불러요.
examples.translation: mani meogeoseo baega bulleoyo. — I ate a lot, so I am full.

examples.text: 목이 말라서 죽겠어요.
examples.translation: mogi mallaseo jukgesseoyo. — I am dying of thirst.

examples.text: 선생님을 따라해 보세요.
examples.translation: seonsaengnimeul ttarahae boseyo. — Please try following the teacher.

explanations.title: 5. ㅎ irregular verbs
explanations.body:
Condition/rule: When the verb stem is followed by a vowel or by the consonant ㄴ or ㄹ, ㅎ is dropped.

Verbs: 빨갛다, 파랗다, 노랗다, 하얗다, 까맣다, 이렇다, 그렇다, 저렇다, 어떻다.

Exceptions (these do not change): 좋다, 많다, 넣다, 낳다, 싫다, 괜찮다, 쌓다.

The book’s examples (the English is mine):

examples.text: 빨간 스웨터가 잘 어울려요.
examples.translation: ppalgan seuweteoga jal eoullyeoyo. — The red sweater suits you well.

examples.text: 가을 하늘이 파래요.
examples.translation: gaeul haneuri paraeyo. — The autumn sky is blue.

examples.text: 이 모자 어때요?
examples.translation: i moja eottaeyo? — How is this hat?

examples.text: 저도 그럴 생각이에요.
examples.translation: jeodo geureol saenggagieyo. — I am thinking so too.

examples.text: 이 책을 가방 안에 넣어 주세요.
examples.translation: i chaegeul gabang ane neoeo juseyo. — Please put this book inside the bag.

examples.text: 아픈 데는 괜찮아요?
examples.translation: apeun deneun gwaenchanayo? — Is the sore spot okay?

explanations.title: 6. ㅅ irregular verbs
explanations.body:
Condition/rule: When the verb stem is followed by a vowel, ㅅ is dropped.

Verbs: 낫다, 붓다, 짓다, 젓다, 잇다(to connect), 긋다(to draw a line).

Exceptions (these do not change): 벗다, 씻다, 웃다, 빗다.

The book’s examples (the English is mine):

examples.text: 쉬니까 병이 다 나았어요.
examples.translation: swinikka byeongi da naasseoyo. — I rested, so the illness is all gone.

examples.text: 손이 자꾸 부어서 큰일이에요.
examples.translation: soni jakku bueoseo keunirieyo. — My hand keeps swelling, so it is a big problem.

examples.text: 밥 먹기 전에 손을 씻으세요.
examples.translation: bap meokgi jeone soneul ssiseuseyo. — Please wash your hands before eating.

examples.text: 사진 찍을 때 웃으세요.
examples.translation: sajin jjigeul ttae useuseyo. — Please smile when you take a photo.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: Follow-up 1 (the teacher’s PowerPoint presentation), Follow-up 2 (six video clips from 옥탑방 고양이 and 호텔리어, transcribing the missing words, writing the verb stem and its meaning), Follow-up 3 (a Hankyoreh cartoon, 비빔툰 알듯 말듯한 즐거움, in which you circle the words conjugated from ㄹ/ㅂ/ㄷ/르/ㅅ/ㅎ verbs; the book’s three examples are 흐르다 [to flow], 듣다 [to listen] and 말다 [to stop, don’t]) and Follow-up 4 (a two-group game: the teacher reads a verb from a card set aloud and points to a student who makes a sentence with it; one point for a correct sentence, and the other group may correct a wrong one) are video, picture, game and group activities.

explanations.title: More practice sentences (mine)
explanations.body: Sample sentences of my own that combine the chapter’s grammar with its vocabulary (the English is mine):

examples.text: 성형수술의 부작용이 있을까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.translation: seonghyeongsusurui bujagyongi isseulkka bwa geokjeongieyo. — I am worried that there might be side effects of cosmetic surgery.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with so that they can provide other activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: identify, talk about, and express opinions about issues and incidents concerning cosmetic surgery and its popularity in Korea; identify and talk about the issues related to employment, unemployment, layoffs, downsizing, and restructuring; and identify and discuss issues concerning military service in Korea.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary section; the conjunctive ending –(으)ㄹ까 봐(서) (being afraid that [something] might …); a summary of irregular verbs; and the Sino-Korean syllables within 성형수술 (成形手術), 실직 (失職), and 안보 (安保).

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: The chapter’s Activities pages (the military-term descriptions and cases, the business Q&A and the word-box descriptions are in the earlier lessons) also hold SMART Board activities, video and listening activities (a campus episode, interviews with people who lost their jobs, a news item about crimes, a radio report about a survey) and pair or group tasks (a debate on cosmetic surgery, a comparison of military systems in different countries). They are audio, video, computer and group activities and are left out.

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning. The book’s related words (synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are left out, and the book’s Additional Vocabulary section is blank. The last section lists the Sino-Korean related words of 성형수술, 실직 and 안보 as the book gives them.

The example sentences with digits and letters are respelled in Hangul where they are spoken.

explanations.title: What Lesson 1 teaches
explanations.body: Unit 15 (Semester III) is titled “Military, Security, and Geography” (군사, 안보 및 지리). Its ten lessons are Accidents, Accidents and Crimes, Crimes, Weather and Natural Disasters, Natural Disasters, Environment, World News, North Korea I, North Korea II and Military. Each lesson has a review of earlier words and Sino-Korean syllables (단어 및 한자어 복습), Part 1 (도입 학습, introduction), Part 2 (본 학습, main study) and Part 3 (심화 학습, advanced study), and each part ends with a list of the words and expressions of its activities (학습활동별 단어 및 표현). Lesson 1 is “Accidents” (사고).
