explanations.title: 학습활동 1 (Reading): natural disasters A–E
explanations.body: Read the following summaries of various natural disasters and, from the box (1. 가뭄, 2. 산사태, 3. 태풍, 4. 폭설, 5. 호우), write the number of the corresponding natural hazard. The summaries, in the book’s words (with 6~7월 spelled out; the English is mine):

examples.text: 많은 비와 강한 바람으로 농작물과 집, 도로, 배 등을 파손시키며 여름철에 남부와 중부 지방에 많이 발생.
examples.translation: maneun biwa ganghan barameuro nongjangmulgwa jip, doro, bae deungeul pasonsikimyeo yeoreumcheore nambuwa jungbu jibange mani balsaeng. — Damages crops, houses, roads, ships and so on with heavy rain and strong wind; occurs often in the southern and central regions in summer. (A)

examples.text: 짧은 시간에 많은 양의 비가 내려 수해 발생. 장마 기간인 유월에서 칠월에 많이 발생한다. 남부와 중부 지방에 많은 피해.
examples.translation: jjalbeun sigane maneun yangui biga naeryeo suhae balsaeng. jangma giganin yuworeseo chirwore mani balsaenghanda. nambuwa jungbu jibange maneun pihae. — A large amount of rain falls in a short time and causes flood damage. Occurs often in June and July, the rainy season. Great damage in the southern and central regions. (B)

examples.text: 오랫동안 비가 내리지 않아 농업용수, 공업용수, 식수 등이 부족해진다. 여름에 주로 발생하며 북부 지방과 산간 지역에 많은 피해.
examples.translation: oraetdongan biga naeriji ana nongeobyongsu, gongeobyongsu, siksu deungi bujokaejinda. yeoreume juro balsaenghamyeo bukbu jibanggwa sangan jiyeoge maneun pihae. — It does not rain for a long time, so water for agriculture, industry, drinking and so on runs short. Occurs mainly in summer; great damage in the northern region and mountain areas. (C)

examples.text: 많은 양의 눈이 내려 교통이 마비되고, 비닐하우스 등이 무너진다. 북부와 산간 지방에 많은 피해. 겨울철에 주로 발생함.
examples.translation: maneun yangui nuni naeryeo gyotongi mabidoego, binilhauseu deungi muneojinda. bukbuwa sangan jibange maneun pihae. gyeoulcheore juro balsaengham. — A large amount of snow falls, traffic is paralyzed and vinyl greenhouses and so on collapse. Great damage in the northern region and mountain regions. Occurs mainly in winter. (D)

examples.text: 많은 비와 지진으로 인해 산의 일부가 무너져 내리는 현상으로, 도로가 끊기고 집이 부서지는 등의 피해. 산간 지역에서 많이 발생.
examples.translation: maneun biwa jijineuro inhae sanui ilbuga muneojeo naerineun hyeonsangeuro, doroga kkeunkigo jibi buseojineun deungui pihae. sangan jiyeogeseo mani balsaeng. — A phenomenon in which part of a mountain collapses because of heavy rain and earthquakes, with damage such as cut roads and broken houses. Occurs often in mountain areas. (E)

explanations.title: 학습활동 3 (Reading): the Sinuiju flood (a Yonhap report quoting the Korean Central News Agency)
explanations.body: The following newspaper article is a report on a weather disaster, quoting North Korea’s Korean Central News Agency (© Yonhapnews). The text is the book’s with the numbers and units spelled out (21일 is 이십일일; 0시부터 9시 is 영 시부터 아홉 시; 300 mm is 삼백 밀리미터; 100% is 백 퍼센트; 19~20일 is 십구 일에서 이십 일; 5천여 명 is 오천여 명; 5천150여 명 is 오천백오십여 명); the quotation marks ‘ ’ around 명령 are removed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 이십일일 압록강이 범람해 북한 평안북도 신의주시와 그 일대가 침수되는 등 홍수피해가 심각한 상황이며, 김정일 국방위원장의 명령으로 수십 대의 비행기와 함정까지 동원해 오천여 명의 주민을 안전하게 구조했다고 조선중앙통신이 전했다.
examples.translation: isibiril amnokgangi beomnamhae bukan pyeonganbukdo sinuijusiwa geu ildaega chimsudoeneun deung hongsupihaega simgakan sanghwangimyeo, gimjeongil gukbangwiwonjangui myeongnyeongeuro susip daeui bihaenggiwa hamjeongkkaji dongwonhae ocheonyeo myeongui jumineul anjeonhage gujohaetdago joseonjungangtongsini jeonhaetda. — On the 21st the Yalu River overflowed and Sinuiju City in North Pyongan Province and its surroundings were flooded; the flood damage is serious, and Korean Central News Agency reported that, by the “order” of the Chairman of the National Defense Commission, Kim Jong-il, dozens of airplanes and even naval vessels were mobilized and about 5,000 residents were rescued safely.

examples.text: 중앙통신은 이십일일 영 시부터 아홉 시 사이에 수풍호 주변지역에 내린 삼백 밀리미터 이상의 강한 폭우와 무더기 비로 인해 압록강물이 넘쳐나 신의주의 살림집과 공공건물, 농경지가 백 퍼센트 침수됐다고 밝혔다.
examples.translation: jungangtongsineun isibiril yeong sibuteo ahop si saie supungho jubyeonjiyeoge naerin sambaek millimiteo isangui ganghan poguwa mudeogi biro inhae amnokgangmuri neomcheona sinuijuui sallimjipgwa gonggonggeonmul, nonggyeongjiga baek peosenteu chimsudwaetdago balkyeotda. — The Central News Agency stated, “Because of the strong downpour of more than 300 millimeters and the concentrated heavy rain that fell on the area around Lake Soopoong between 0:00 and 9:00 on the 21st, the Yalu River overflowed and 100 percent of Sinuiju’s residential houses, public buildings and farmland were flooded.”

examples.text: 통신은 이어 지금 이 지역에서는 신의주시를 비롯한 평안북도의 일꾼과 근로자, 조선인민군 군인들이 동원돼 구조전투가 벌어지고 있다고 덧붙였다.
examples.translation: tongsineun ieo jigeum i jiyeogeseoneun sinuijusireul birotan pyeonganbukdoui ilkkungwa geulloja, joseoninmingun gunindeuri dongwondwae gujojeontuga beoreojigo itdago deotbutyeotda. — The agency went on to add, “In this area now, workers and laborers of North Pyongan Province including Sinuiju City and soldiers of the Korean People’s Army have been mobilized and a rescue battle is under way.”

examples.text: 중앙통신은 이십일일 조선인민군 공군비행기들과 해군함정들이 폭우가 갑자기 들이닥친 평안북도 신의주 지구의 큰물 피해지역으로 긴급출동해 주민들에 대한 구출작전을 성과적으로 벌였다고 보도했다.
examples.translation: jungangtongsineun isibiril joseoninmingun gonggunbihaenggideulgwa haegunhamjeongdeuri poguga gapjagi deuridakchin pyeonganbukdo sinuiju jiguui keunmul pihaejiyeogeuro gingeupchuldonghae jumindeure daehan guchuljakjeoneul seonggwajeogeuro beoryeotdago bodohaetda. — The Central News Agency reported, “On the 21st, Korean People’s Army air force planes and navy vessels were urgently dispatched to the flood-damaged area of the Sinuiju district of North Pyongan Province, where the downpour had suddenly struck, and carried out a successful rescue operation for the residents.”

examples.text: 통신은 십구 일에서 이십 일 사이 중국 동북지방에 폭우가 쏟아져 압록강의 수위가 갑자기 높아지기 시작해 강물은 잠깐 사이에 제방을 넘어 신의주시내에까지 밀려들어 도로운행이 마비되고 많은 대상들이 피해를 입었다며, 신의주시는 완전히 물에 잠겨 단층건물들은 지붕만 보이게 되었다고 밝혔다.
examples.translation: tongsineun sipgu ireseo isip il sai jungguk dongbukjibange poguga ssodajeo amnokgangui suwiga gapjagi nopajigi sijakae gangmureun jamkkan saie jebangeul neomeo sinuijusinaeekkaji millyeodeureo dorounhaengi mabidoego maneun daesangdeuri pihaereul ibeotdamyeo, sinuijusineun wanjeonhi mure jamgyeo dancheunggeonmuldeureun jibungman boige doeeotdago balkyeotda. — The agency stated, “Between the 19th and the 20th a downpour fell in northeastern China, the water level of the Yalu River suddenly began to rise, and in a short time the river water went over the embankment and rushed into the city center of Sinuiju, paralyzing road traffic and damaging many facilities,” and, “Sinuiju was completely submerged and only the roofs of the one-story buildings could be seen.”

examples.text: 중앙통신은 김정일 국방위원장이 이런 사실을 보고받고 북한군을 구조활동에 나서도록 명령했다고 말했다.
examples.translation: jungangtongsineun gimjeongil gukbangwiwonjangi ireon sasireul bogobatgo bukanguneul gujohwaldonge naseodorok myeongnyeonghaetdago malhaetda. — The Central News Agency said that Chairman Kim Jong-il, having been informed of these facts, ordered the North Korean military to take part in the rescue work.

examples.text: 이에 따라 공군부대에서는 수십 대의 비행기를, 해군부대에서는 함정과 각종 장비들을 동원하여 위험에 처했던 오천백오십여 명의 주민들을 안전지대로 무사히 옮겼다고 통신은 밝혀 인명피해는 발생하지 않은 것으로 전했다.
examples.translation: ie ttara gonggunbudaeeseoneun susip daeui bihaenggireul, haegunbudaeeseoneun hamjeonggwa gakjong jangbideureul dongwonhayeo wiheome cheohaetdeon ocheonbaegosibyeo myeongui jumindeureul anjeonjidaero musahi omgyeotdago tongsineun balkyeo inmyeongpihaeneun balsaenghaji aneun geoseuro jeonhaetda. — Accordingly, the agency stated that the air force units mobilized dozens of airplanes and the navy units mobilized vessels and various equipment and safely moved about 5,150 residents who had been in danger to a safe zone, and it reported that no human casualties occurred.

explanations.title: 학습활동 3: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The natural hazard and its effect: the Yalu River overflowed after heavy rain; about 300 mm or more of rain fell in the area around Lake Soopoong in nine hours on the 21st, and heavy rain fell in northeastern China on the 19th and 20th. Sinuiju and the area around it were flooded: 100% of the houses, public buildings and farmland were inundated, road traffic was paralyzed, and the city was so completely under water that only the roofs of one-story buildings could be seen.

2. The rescue efforts: the initiator was Chairman Kim Jong-il, who ordered the military (as the news agency reported) to rescue the people. The participants were air force units (dozens of airplanes), navy units (vessels and equipment), Korean People’s Army soldiers, and the workers and laborers of North Pyongan Province including Sinuiju. The victims rescued were about 5,150 residents, who were moved to a safe zone; no human casualties were reported.

3. The verb(s) associated with the underlined subject: the underline is not visible in the text of the book. The subject of the quoted statements is 중앙통신 (통신), and the verbs associated with it are 전했다, 밝혔다, 덧붙였다, 보도했다 and 말했다.

4. Translation: “Sinuiju was completely submerged, and only the roofs of the one-story buildings could be seen.”

5. North Korean words (below).

explanations.title: 말해 봅시다! (speaking)
explanations.body: The book’s speaking prompts (the English is mine):

examples.text: 최근에 국내 또는 외국에서 발생한 자연재해에 대해서 서로 이야기해 보세요.
examples.translation: choegeune gungnae ttoneun oegugeseo balsaenghan jayeonjaehaee daehaeseo seoro iyagihae boseyo. — Talk to each other about natural disasters that occurred recently in Korea or abroad.

examples.text: 캘리포니아에서는 지진이 자주 발생합니다. 지진이 발생하면 어떻게 대처해야 하는지 서로 이야기해 보세요.
examples.translation: kaelliponiaeseoneun jijini jaju balsaenghamnida. jijini balsaenghamyeon eotteoke daecheohaeya haneunji seoro iyagihae boseyo. — Earthquakes often occur in California. Talk to each other about how to respond when an earthquake occurs.

examples.text: 또, 태풍이 발생할 경우에는 어떻게 대처하는지 서로 이야기해 보세요.
examples.translation: tto, taepungi balsaenghal gyeongueneun eotteoke daecheohaneunji seoro iyagihae boseyo. — Also, talk to each other about how to respond when a typhoon occurs.

explanations.title: Activities left out

lessons.title: 644. U15 L5 · Part 2 (본 학습): an editorial on rice aid to North Korea
lessons.subtitle: 본 학습 · 사설 · 대북 쌀지원 · 머뭇거릴 때 아니다 · 한자 성어 · 삼삼오오 · 일거양득 · 말해 봅시다

explanations.title: 학습활동 3 (Reading): an editorial, “대북 쌀지원 더 이상 머뭇거릴 때 아니다”
explanations.body: The following is a newspaper editorial (Kyunghyang), titled “[사설] 대북 쌀지원 더 이상 머뭇거릴 때 아니다” (Editorial: It is no longer time to hesitate over rice aid to North Korea). The text is the book’s with 100% spelled out (백 퍼센트) and 1석3조 spelled out (일석삼조). The English is mine.

examples.text: 한나라당 지도부가 정부에 대북 쌀지원 문제를 제안했다고 한다.
examples.translation: hannaradang jidobuga jeongbue daebuk ssaljiwon munjereul jeanhaetdago handa. — It is said that the leadership of the Grand National Party proposed the issue of rice aid to North Korea to the government.

examples.text: 북한의 홍수 피해 상황은 언론이 전하는 사진과 화면을 통해 미루어 짐작할 수 있다.
examples.translation: bukanui hongsu pihae sanghwangeun eolloni jeonhaneun sajingwa hwamyeoneul tonghae mirueo jimjakal su itda. — The flood damage situation in North Korea can be inferred through the photos and screens that the press conveys.

examples.text: 압록강의 범람으로 신의주 주변의 들판은 바다로 변했으며 주택들은 지붕만 남았다.
examples.translation: amnokgangui beomnameuro sinuiju jubyeonui deulpaneun badaro byeonhaesseumyeo jutaekdeureun jibungman namatda. — Because of the overflowing of the Yalu River, the fields around Sinuiju turned into a sea, and only the roofs of the houses remained.

examples.text: 북한 조선중앙통신은 지난 주말 내린 폭우로 신의주의 주택과 공공건물, 농경지가 백 퍼센트 침수됐다고 보도했다.
examples.translation: bukan joseonjungangtongsineun jinan jumal naerin poguro sinuijuui jutaekgwa gonggonggeonmul, nonggyeongjiga baek peosenteu chimsudwaetdago bodohaetda. — North Korea’s Korean Central News Agency reported that, because of the downpour that fell last weekend, 100 percent of Sinuiju’s houses, public buildings and farmland were flooded.

examples.text: 북한은 인명 구조를 위해 군 비행기와 함정까지 동원하고 있다.
examples.translation: bukaneun inmyeong gujoreul wihae gun bihaenggiwa hamjeongkkaji dongwonhago itda. — North Korea is mobilizing even military airplanes and vessels for the rescue of lives.

examples.text: 북한에서는 지난달 하순 개성과 흥남 일대에 내린 폭우로 이미 많은 인명 피해와 함께 농경지가 침수된 바 있다.
examples.translation: bukaneseoneun jinandal hasun gaeseonggwa heungnam ildaee naerin poguro imi maneun inmyeong pihaewa hamkke nonggyeongjiga chimsudoen ba itda. — In North Korea, in the last ten days of last month, heavy rain that fell around Kaesong and Hungnam had already flooded farmland along with many human casualties.

examples.text: 그러지 않아도 만성적 식량난을 겪어온 북한 주민들의 생활이 이번 수해로 더욱 어려워질 것은 불 보듯 뻔하다.
examples.translation: geureoji anado manseongjeok singnyangnaneul gyeokkeoon bukan jumindeurui saenghwari ibeon suhaero deouk eoryeowojil geoseun bul bodeut ppeonhada. — It is as plain as fire that the lives of the North Korean residents, who were suffering a chronic food shortage even without this, will become more difficult because of this flood damage.

examples.text: 북한 주민이 수해로 고통을 겪는 것은 시각을 다투는 인도적 문제다.
examples.translation: bukan jumini suhaero gotongeul gyeongneun geoseun sigageul datuneun indojeok munjeda. — The North Korean residents’ suffering from the flood damage is a humanitarian problem that is a race against the clock.

examples.text: 정부가 대북 식량지원을 정치적 문제와 연계시켜 북한에 대한 압박용으로 이용하는 것은 인도주의에 반하는 정략적 자세다.
examples.translation: jeongbuga daebuk singnyangjiwoneul jeongchijeok munjewa yeongyesikyeo bukane daehan apbagyongeuro iyonghaneun geoseun indojuuie banhaneun jeongnyakjeok jaseda. — For the government to link food aid to North Korea with political problems and use it as a means of pressure on North Korea is a politically motivated attitude that goes against humanitarianism.

examples.text: 더욱이 지금은 엄청난 홍수로 북한이 외부세계의 도움을 절실히 필요로 하는 때다.
examples.translation: deougi jigeumeun eomcheongnan hongsuro bukani oebusegyeui doumeul jeolsilhi piryoro haneun ttaeda. — Moreover, now is the time when North Korea acutely needs help from the outside world because of the enormous flood.

examples.text: 정부가 인도적 차원에서 대북 식량지원을 한다면 북한 주민의 긴급한 생활고를 덜 수 있을 뿐 아니라, 결과적으로 넘쳐나는 쌀 재고 관리와 꽉 막힌 남북관계의 변화도 가져올 수 있다.

explanations.title: The questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The writer’s main point: the South Korean government should stop hesitating and send food (rice) aid to flood-stricken North Korea for humanitarian reasons, and should not tie it to politics or use it as pressure.

2. The statement that most accurately reflects the editorial is B: the recent flooding will worsen North Korea’s existing food shortage. (A is wrong: nothing says North Korea rejected aid. C is wrong: the ruling party proposed it, but not as “a donation of rice”; D is wrong: the editorial urges the government, which has not yet acted.)

3. 1석3조 (“one stone, three birds”) is the writer’s version of 일석이조. The 1석 (one stone) is the humanitarian food aid to North Korea. The 3조 (three birds) are: (1) relieving the North Korean residents’ urgent hardship, (2) managing South Korea’s overflowing rice stock, and (3) bringing about a change in the tightly blocked inter-Korean relations.

4. The idioms: the book’s first example is 삼삼오오; the meanings and the example sentences for the others are mine (see the table below).

lessons.title: 646. U15 L5 · Part 3 (심화 학습): 왜 세계의 절반은 굶주리는가?
lessons.subtitle: 심화 학습 · 산불 · 굶주림 · 영양실조 · 사막화 · 결식아동 · 왜 세계의 절반은 굶주리는가 · 말해 봅시다

explanations.title: 학습활동 3 (Reading): a newspaper article, “왜 세계의 절반은 굶주리는가?” (Why is half of the world hungry?)
explanations.body: The following is a text from a newspaper (Kyunghyang). The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (120억 명 is 백이십억 명; 7분의 1 is 칠 분의 일; 8억5000만 명 is 팔억 오천만 명); the book’s title mark < > around the title of Jean Ziegler’s book is dropped and the title is written in plain Hangul (the book’s own title ends with a question mark). The English is mine.

examples.text: 신문, 방송에서 아프리카 어떤 국가에서는 가뭄과 내전으로 많은 사람들이 기아에 허덕인다는 소식을 종종 접한다.
examples.translation: sinmun, bangsongeseo apeurika eotteon gukgaeseoneun gamumgwa naejeoneuro maneun saramdeuri giae heodeogindaneun sosigeul jongjong jeopanda. — In newspapers and on broadcasts, we often hear news that in some African countries many people are struggling with starvation because of drought and civil war.

examples.text: 가끔은 뼈만 앙상하게 남아 눈물마저 마른 어린아이의 사진이 함께 눈에 들어올 때도 있다.
examples.translation: gakkeumeun ppyeoman angsanghage nama nunmulmajeo mareun eorinaiui sajini hamkke nune deureool ttaedo itda. — Sometimes a photo of a small child, with only bones left and even the tears dried up, catches the eye along with it.

examples.text: 마음 한구석이 불편하면서도, 이는 자연재해와도 같은 어쩔 수 없는 일이라고 여긴 적이 있다.
examples.translation: maeum hanguseogi bulpyeonhamyeonseodo, ineun jayeonjaehaewado gateun eojjeol su eomneun irirago yeogin jeogi itda. — Although a corner of my heart felt uneasy, I once regarded this as something unavoidable, like a natural disaster.

examples.text: 심지어 인구과잉을 조절하는 자연현상의 하나일지 모른다는 생각까지 하면서.
examples.translation: simjieo ingugwaingeul jojeolhaneun jayeonhyeonsangui hanailji moreundaneun saenggakkaji hamyeonseo. — I even thought that it might be one of the natural phenomena that regulate overpopulation.

examples.text: 유엔 식량 특별조사관인 장 지글러가 쓴 책 왜 세계의 절반은 굶주리는가를 읽지 않았다면 나의 이런 생각은 변하지 않았을지도 모르겠다.
examples.translation: yuen singnyang teukbyeoljosagwanin jang jigeulleoga sseun chaek wae segyeui jeolbaneun gumjurineungareul ikji anatdamyeon naui ireon saenggageun byeonhaji anasseuljido moreugetda. — If I had not read the book Why Is Half of the World Hungry? by Jean Ziegler, the U.N. special rapporteur on food, my thinking might not have changed.

examples.text: 책에 따르면 지구 전체적으로 현재 전 세계 인구보다 많은 백이십억 명이 먹고도 남을 식량이 생산되고 있다고 한다.
examples.translation: chaege ttareumyeon jigu jeonchejeogeuro hyeonjae jeon segye inguboda maneun baegisibeok myeongi meokgodo nameul singnyangi saengsandoego itdago handa. — According to the book, the Earth as a whole is currently producing food that 12 billion people, more than the world’s population, could eat and still have left over.

examples.text: 그런데도 세계 인구의 칠 분의 일인 팔억 오천만 명 이상이 만성적이고 심각한 영양실조에 시달리고 있다.
examples.translation: geureondedo segye inguui chil bunui irin pareok ocheonman myeong isangi manseongjeogigo simgakan yeongyangsiljoe sidalligo itda. — Even so, more than 850 million people, one seventh of the world’s population, are suffering from chronic and serious malnutrition.

examples.text: 지글러는 이런 불합리한 현실의 원인이 사회구조적 문제에 있음을 조목조목 따져 보여준다.
examples.translation: jigeulleoneun ireon bulhamnihan hyeonsirui wonini sahoegujojeok munjee isseumeul jomokjomok ttajeo boyeojunda. — Ziegler shows, item by item, by examining it closely, that the cause of this irrational reality lies in social-structural problems.

examples.text: 산림파괴로 인한 사막화 등 환경파괴, 전쟁과 정치적 무질서, 신자유주의로 인한 불공정한 분배의 가속화 등이 이런 결과를 초래하는 문제들이다.
examples.translation: sallimpagoero inhan samakwa deung hwangyeongpagoe, jeonjaenggwa jeongchijeok mujilseo, sinjayujuuiro inhan bulgongjeonghan bunbaeui gasokwa deungi ireon gyeolgwareul choraehaneun munjedeurida. — Environmental destruction such as desertification caused by deforestation, war and political disorder, and the acceleration of unfair distribution caused by neoliberalism are the problems that bring about this result.

examples.text: 최근 국내에서도 결식아동이 늘어나고 있는 뉴스를 보면서 비만을 걱정하는 아이들이 있는 한편에서 허기진 배를 움켜쥔 아이가 공존하는 기막힌 현실이 다른 세상의 일만은 아니라는 생각이 든다.
examples.translation: choegeun gungnaeeseodo gyeolsigadongi neureonago inneun nyuseureul bomyeonseo bimaneul geokjeonghaneun aideuri inneun hanpyeoneseo heogijin baereul umkyeojwin aiga gongjonhaneun gimakin hyeonsiri dareun sesangui ilmaneun aniraneun saenggagi deunda. — Watching the news that the number of children skipping meals is increasing in Korea too recently, I come to think that the absurd reality in which children worried about obesity and children clutching their hungry stomachs coexist is not only something of another world.

explanations.title: 학습활동 3: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The article is best described as C, a book review (the writer reflects on how reading Jean Ziegler’s book changed his thinking; it is not a travel journal or a scientific analysis, and it is more a reflective review of a book than a plain editorial).

2. The problem in the African country: many people are struggling with starvation (hunger). The causes: drought and civil war.

3. The causes elaborated in the third paragraph: environmental destruction such as desertification caused by deforestation; war and political disorder; and the acceleration of unfair distribution caused by neoliberalism.

4. The two ironic phenomena: globally, enough food is produced to feed 12 billion people, more than the world’s population, yet more than 850 million people (one seventh) suffer from chronic malnutrition; in Korea, children worried about obesity coexist with children who skip meals and clutch their hungry stomachs.

explanations.title: 말해 봅시다! (speaking)
explanations.body: The book’s speaking prompts (the English is mine):

examples.text: 캘리포니아에서 발생하는 산불에 대해서 이야기해 보세요.
examples.translation: kaelliponiaeseo balsaenghaneun sanbure daehaeseo iyagihae boseyo. — Talk about the wildfires that occur in California.

examples.text: 왜 발생합니까? 어떤 피해가 있습니까?
examples.translation: wae balsaenghamnikka? eotteon pihaega itseumnikka? — Why do they occur? What damage is there?

examples.text: 다른 나라나 자기 나라에서 큰 자연재해로 피해를 입은 사람들을 어떻게 도울 수 있는지 서로 이야기해 보세요.
examples.translation: dareun narana jagi naraeseo keun jayeonjaehaero pihaereul ibeun saramdeureul eotteoke doul su inneunji seoro iyagihae boseyo. — Talk to each other about how you can help people who suffered damage from a big natural disaster in another country or your own country.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: 학습활동 1 (a YTN video about wildfires in Korea, with questions in English: five statistics, such as “93% of wildfires occur in March and April,” the two main causes, and a table of the three research areas — prevention, extinguishing and recovery), 학습활동 2 (a public awareness poster about wildfires caused by humans by KOBACO, whose text is inside the picture; you translate it and make your own poster) and 학습활동 4 (a listening activity from the Seoul Education Research & Information Institute about African farmers’ problem, the speaker’s question to the farmer, a comparison of two African villages and the speaker’s message) are audio, video, picture and drawing activities.

The economic advantages of recycling; C. The number of disposable cups recycled in one year. The picture is not in the text, so the answer cannot be given here.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2 (Reading): news on greenhouse gas emissions
explanations.body: Read the article and the chart and choose the statement that fits the content. The article is the book’s with the numbers and units spelled out (3857 kg is 삼천팔백오십칠 킬로그램; 1인당 is 일 인당; 1일 is 일일; 9시간 51분 is 아홉 시간 오십일 분; 8시간 22분 is 여덟 시간 이십이 분; 25% is 이십오 퍼센트; 46.3% is 사십육 점 삼 퍼센트); the dot in 출·퇴근 is removed. The English is mine. The chart is not in the text.

examples.text: 사무직 직장인의 근무 활동에서 발생하는 연간 온실가스 배출량이 일 인당 삼천팔백오십칠 킬로그램인 것으로 조사됐다.
examples.translation: samujik jikjanginui geunmu hwaldongeseo balsaenghaneun yeongan onsilgaseu baechullyangi il indang samcheonpalbaegosipchil killogeuraemin geoseuro josadwaetda. — It was found that the annual greenhouse gas emissions generated by the work activities of office workers are 3,857 kilograms per person.

examples.text: 조사 대상 직장인들은 일일 근무시간이 평균 아홉 시간 오십일 분이었고 컴퓨터는 여덟 시간 이십이 분 사용했다.
examples.translation: josa daesang jikjangindeureun illil geunmusigani pyeonggyun ahop sigan osibil bunieotgo keompyuteoneun yeodeol sigan isibi bun sayonghaetda. — The surveyed workers’ daily working hours averaged 9 hours 51 minutes, and they used the computer for 8 hours 22 minutes.

examples.text: 이십오 퍼센트가 야근을 했고 출퇴근 교통수단은 자동차가 사십육 점 삼 퍼센트로 가장 많았다.
examples.translation: isibo peosenteuga yageuneul haetgo chultoegeun gyotongsudaneun jadongchaga sasimnyuk jeom sam peosenteuro gajang manatda. — 25 percent worked overtime at night, and as the commuting means of transport, cars were the most common at 46.3 percent.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2: my answer
explanations.body:
The statements are: A. Air conditioning systems produced the greatest amount of greenhouse gas. B. The survey was conducted among blue-collar workers. C. Most interviewees used mass transit for their daily commute. D. The survey is about the amount of greenhouse gas produced by an office worker.

My answer is D. The article is about the yearly greenhouse gas emissions from the work activities of office workers (사무직 직장인). A is not stated in the text (the chart may show it, but the text does not), B is wrong (office workers, not blue-collar workers) and C is wrong (cars, at 46.3%, were the most common commuting means).

explanations.title: 학습활동 4 (Reading · Speaking): the Environmental Crisis Clock (환경위기시계)
explanations.body: The following article is news about an event on the environment (Text and image © Kyunghyang). The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (13일 is 십삼 일; 2010 is 이천십; 3분 is 삼 분; 9시 19분 is 아홉 시 십구 분; 9시 35분 is 아홉 시 삼십오 분; 9시 51분 is 아홉 시 오십일 분; 16분 is 십육 분); the quotation marks ‘ ’ are removed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 십삼 일 오후 서울 소공동에서 환경재단이 주최하는 이천십 대륙별 환경위기시계 발표 행사가 열렸다.
examples.translation: sipsam il ohu seoul sogongdongeseo hwangyeongjaedani juchoehaneun icheonsip daeryukbyeol hwangyeongwigisigye balpyo haengsaga yeollyeotda. — On the afternoon of the 13th, the “2010 Environmental Crisis Clock Announcement by Continent” event, hosted by the Korea Green Foundation, was held in Sogong-dong, Seoul.

examples.text: 환경재단은 환경위기시계의 세계 시각이 지난해보다 삼 분 느린 아홉 시 십구 분이라고 발표했다.
examples.translation: hwangyeongjaedaneun hwangyeongwigisigyeui segye sigagi jinanhaeboda sam bun neurin ahop si sipgu bunirago balpyohaetda. — The foundation announced that the world time of the Environmental Crisis Clock is 9:19, three minutes slower than last year.

examples.text: 한국의 시각은 아홉 시 삼십오 분으로 전 세계 평균시간보다 십육 분 빨랐으나 지난해 아홉 시 오십일 분보다는 십육 분 늦어졌다.
examples.translation: hangugui sigageun ahop si samsibo buneuro jeon segye pyeonggyunsiganboda simnyuk bun ppallasseuna jinanhae ahop si osibil bunbodaneun simnyuk bun neujeojeotda. — Korea’s time is 9:35, 16 minutes faster than the world average time, but it became 16 minutes slower than last year’s 9:51.

examples.text: 환경위기시계는 자정에 가까울수록 환경위기가 심각하다는 것을 의미한다.
examples.translation: hwangyeongwigisigyeneun jajeonge gakkaulsurok hwangyeongwigiga simgakadaneun geoseul uimihanda. — The Environmental Crisis Clock means that the closer it is to midnight, the more serious the environmental crisis is.

explanations.title: 학습활동 4: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. 환경위기시계 is the Environmental Crisis Clock: a clock that shows how serious the environmental crisis is. The closer it is to midnight, the more serious the crisis.

2. 9:19 is the world time of the Environmental Crisis Clock this year (three minutes slower than last year). 9:35 is Korea’s time this year (16 minutes faster than the world average). 9:51 is Korea’s time last year.

3. This question asks for your own opinion about the time in your hometown and on the Monterey Peninsula and why; it has no single answer.

explanations.title: 말해 봅시다! (speaking)
explanations.body: The book’s speaking prompt (the English is mine):

examples.text: 재활용에 대해서 이야기해 봅시다.
examples.translation: jaehwaryonge daehaeseo iyagihae bopsida. — Let us talk about recycling.

examples.text: 재활용할 수 있는 것과 할 수 없는 것에는 어떤 것이 있는지 말해 보세요.
examples.translation: jaehwaryonghal su inneun geotgwa hal su eomneun geoseneun eotteon geosi inneunji malhae boseyo. — Tell what things can be recycled and what things cannot.

examples.text: 각각의 물품 캔, 빈 병, 종이, 플라스틱 등 을 재활용할 때 주의할 점에 대해서도 이야기해 보세요.
examples.translation: gakgagui mulpum kaen, bin byeong, jongi, peullaseutik deung eul jaehwaryonghal ttae juuihal jeome daehaeseodo iyagihae boseyo. — Also talk about the points to be careful about when recycling each item (cans, empty bottles, paper, plastic and so on).

explanations.title: 학습활동 1 (Reading · Speaking): imported farm products and food mileage
explanations.body: The following is an article about farm products (Text and image © Kyunghyang). The text is the book’s with 100년 spelled out (백 년), 1등 (일 등), and 4배 (사 배) and 17배 (십칠 배); the quotation marks ‘ ’ around the words are removed, and the ellipsis after 오렌지 is replaced by a period. The English is mine.

examples.text: 칠레에서 온 포도, 필리핀에서 온 바나나, 미국에서 온 오렌지.
examples.translation: chilleeseo on podo, pillipineseo on banana, migugeseo on orenji. — Grapes from Chile, bananas from the Philippines, oranges from the United States.

examples.text: 마트에는 세계 각지에서 모여든 수입 농산물이 가득하다.
examples.translation: mateueneun segye gakjieseo moyeodeun suip nongsanmuri gadeukada. — The supermarket is full of imported farm products gathered from all over the world.

examples.text: 우리가 바다 건너 먼 길 온 농산물들을 먹는 호사를 누리는 동안 지구의 기온은 더 올라가고 우리 건강은 더욱 위협받는다.
examples.translation: uriga bada geonneo meon gil on nongsanmuldeureul meongneun hosareul nurineun dongan jiguui gioneun deo ollagago uri geongangeun deouk wihyeopbanneunda. — While we enjoy the luxury of eating farm products that came a long way across the sea, the Earth’s temperature rises further and our health is threatened even more.

examples.text: 이제는 로컬 푸드를 먹을 때다.
examples.translation: ijeneun rokeol pudeureul meogeul ttaeda. — Now is the time to eat local food.

examples.text: 음식이 생산지를 떠나 우리 입에 들어오기까지 이동한 총거리를 푸드 마일리지라고 한다.
examples.translation: eumsigi saengsanjireul tteona uri ibe deureoogikkaji idonghan chonggeorireul pudeu maillijirago handa. — The total distance that food travels from leaving its place of production until it enters our mouths is called “food mileage.”

examples.text: 이동 거리가 길면 이동 시간도 길어지고 보관과 품질에 문제가 생기기 쉽다.
examples.translation: idong georiga gilmyeon idong sigando gireojigo bogwangwa pumjire munjega saenggigi swipda. — If the distance traveled is long, the travel time also becomes long, and problems with storage and quality easily arise.

examples.text: 푸드 마일리지가 적은 음식일수록 안전하고 건강한 식품이다.
examples.translation: pudeu maillijiga jeogeun eumsigilsurok anjeonhago geonganghan sikpumida. — The lower the food mileage of a food, the safer and healthier the food is.

examples.text: 만약 백 년 후에 인류가 한 가장 바보 같은 짓이라는 책이 나온다면 우리나라가 지구 반대편에서 포도를 가져와 먹은 것이 일 등을 할 거예요.
examples.translation: manyak baek nyeon hue illyuga han gajang babo gateun jisiraneun chaegi naondamyeon urinaraga jigu bandaepyeoneseo podoreul gajeowa meogeun geosi il deungeul hal geoyeyo. — “If a book called ‘The Most Foolish Thing Humankind Did’ comes out a hundred years from now, our country’s bringing grapes from the other side of the Earth and eating them will win first place.”

examples.text: 에코생협 안병덕 이사장의 뼈 있는 농담이다.
examples.translation: ekosaenghyeop anbyeongdeok isajangui ppyeo inneun nongdamida. — This is a joke with a bone in it (a pointed joke) from An Byeong-deok, the chairman of Eco Consumers’ Cooperative.

examples.text: 부산에 살고 있다면, 미국에서 온 것보다는 아시아에서 온 것, 아시아에서 온 것보다는 서울에서 온 것, 서울에서 온 것보다는 대전에서 온 것이 더 좋다.
examples.translation: busane salgo itdamyeon, migugeseo on geotbodaneun asiaeseo on geot, asiaeseo on geotbodaneun seoureseo on geot, seoureseo on geotbodaneun daejeoneseo on geosi deo jota. — If you live in Busan, what came from Asia is better than what came from the United States, what came from Seoul is better than what came from Asia, and what came from Daejeon is better than what came from Seoul.

examples.text: 식품의 이동 거리가 짧을수록, 즉 내가 사는 지역에서 생산되는 식품을 먹는 것이 가장 좋다.
examples.translation: sikpumui idong georiga jjalbeulsurok, jeuk naega saneun jiyeogeseo saengsandoeneun sikpumeul meongneun geosi gajang jota. — The shorter the food’s travel distance, that is, eating food produced in the region where I live, the better.

examples.text: 먹을거리가 이동할 때는 트럭이나 선박, 비행기 등의 운송 수단을 사용하게 되는데 이때 반드시 배출되는 것이 이산화탄소다.
examples.translation: meogeulgeoriga idonghal ttaeneun teureogina seonbak, bihaenggi deungui unsong sudaneul sayonghage doeneunde ittae bandeusi baechuldoeneun geosi isanhwatansoda. — When food moves, means of transport such as trucks, ships and airplanes are used, and what is always emitted at that time is carbon dioxide.

examples.text: 먹을거리의 이동 거리가 길수록 이산화탄소 배출량이 늘어난다는 말.
examples.translation: meogeulgeoriui idong georiga gilsurok isanhwatanso baechullyangi neureonandaneun mal. — That is, the longer the food’s travel distance, the more the carbon dioxide emissions increase.

examples.text: 결국 멀리서 먹을거리를 옮겨와 먹을수록 지구 온난화를 가속시키는 것이다.
examples.translation: gyeolguk meolliseo meogeulgeorireul omgyeowa meogeulsurok jigu onnanhwareul gasoksikineun geosida. — In the end, the more we bring food from far away and eat it, the more we accelerate global warming.

examples.text: 일반 식품은 로컬 푸드에 비해 온실가스를 적게는 사 배에서 많게는 십칠 배나 배출한다니 날이 덥다고 투정하기 전에 장바구니를 살펴볼 필요가 있다.
examples.translation: ilban sikpumeun rokeol pudeue bihae onsilgaseureul jeokgeneun sa baeeseo mankeneun sipchil baena baechulhandani nari deopdago tujeonghagi jeone jangbagunireul salpyeobol piryoga itda. — Ordinary food emits from as little as 4 times to as much as 17 times the greenhouse gas of local food, so before whining that the weather is hot, we need to look at our shopping baskets.

explanations.title: 학습활동 1: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The sentence that best reflects the main idea: 이제는 로컬 푸드를 먹을 때다. (Now is the time to eat local food.)

2. 푸드 마일리지 (food mileage) is the total distance that food travels from leaving its place of production until it enters our mouths (음식이 생산지를 떠나 우리 입에 들어오기까지 이동한 총거리).

3. 뼈 있는 can be replaced by C. 의미가 있는 (meaningful; with a point): the joke has a serious point behind it.

4. The underlined words in the last sentence are not visible in the text of the book. The last sentence says that, before whining that the weather is hot, we need to look at our shopping baskets; the writer uses it to say that our own food choices (imported food with large greenhouse gas emissions) contribute to the heat we complain about, so we should check what we buy.

5. The book asks you to discuss in Korean, with your classmates, which of the foods you eat every day have the longest and the shortest food mileage.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2 (Reading): reduce the generation of waste itself
explanations.body: The following is an article about the environment (Text and image © Kyunghyang). The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (20년 is 이십 년; 30년 is 삼십 년; 500년 is 오백 년); a stray space after the opening quotation mark of the last quotation is removed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 나무젓가락과 종이컵, 스티로폼 용기가 썩는 데 걸리는 기간은 각각 이십 년, 삼십 년, 오백 년이다.
examples.translation: namujeotgarakgwa jongikeop, seutiropom yonggiga sseongneun de geollineun giganeun gakgak isip nyeon, samsip nyeon, obaek nyeonida. — The periods it takes for wooden chopsticks, paper cups and Styrofoam containers to decompose are 20 years, 30 years and 500 years respectively.

examples.text: 환경운동연합 벌레 먹은 사과팀 이지현 처장은 이제는 재활용을 넘어 발생 자체를 줄여야 한다고 말한다.
examples.translation: hwangyeongundongyeonhap beolle meogeun sagwatim ijihyeon cheojangeun ijeneun jaehwaryongeul neomeo balsaeng jachereul juryeoya handago malhanda. — Lee Ji-hyun, director of the Worm-Eaten Apple team of the Korean Federation for Environmental Movements, says, “Now we must go beyond recycling and reduce the generation of waste itself.”

examples.text: 발생 자체를 줄이라니, 막연하게 느낄 수도 있겠지만 자원을 아끼는 방법은 생각보다 쉽고 간단하다.
examples.translation: balsaeng jachereul jurirani, magyeonhage neukkil sudo itgetjiman jawoneul akkineun bangbeobeun saenggakboda swipgo gandanhada. — “Reduce the generation itself?” You may feel it is vague, but the ways of saving resources are easier and simpler than you think.

examples.text: 현금인출기를 이용할 때 명세서 출력을 생략하거나 사무실에 개인 컵을 하나씩 두고 종이컵 대신 쓰면 굉장히 많은 자원이 절약돼요.
examples.translation: hyeongeuminchulgireul iyonghal ttae myeongseseo chullyeogeul saengnyakageona samusire gaein keobeul hanassik dugo jongikeop daesin sseumyeon goengjanghi maneun jawoni jeoryakdwaeyo. — “If you skip printing the statement when you use an ATM, or keep a personal cup in the office and use it instead of a paper cup, a great deal of resources are saved.”

examples.text: 지로로 받던 고지서를 이메일 명세서로 받으면 지로로 쓰이는 종이와 집까지 배송되며 소비되는 에너지가 절약되죠.
examples.translation: jiroro batdeon gojiseoreul imeil myeongseseoro badeumyeon jiroro sseuineun jongiwa jipkkaji baesongdoemyeo sobidoeneun eneojiga jeoryakdoejo. — “If you receive by e-mail statement the bills you used to receive by giro, the paper used for giro and the energy consumed in delivering it to your home are saved.”

examples.text: 자원 절약이라는 것이 어려운 게 아니에요.
examples.translation: jawon jeoryagiraneun geosi eoryeoun ge anieyo. — “Saving resources is not something difficult.”

examples.text: 아침에 집에서 손수건을 하나 챙기면 하루 종일 핸드 드라이어나 페이퍼 타월로 소비되는 물자를 아낄 수 있다.
examples.translation: achime jibeseo sonsugeoneul hana chaenggimyeon haru jongil haendeu deuraieona peipeo tawollo sobidoeneun muljareul akkil su itda. — If you take one handkerchief from home in the morning, you can save the materials consumed by hand dryers or paper towels all day long.

examples.text: 천으로 된 에코 백을 하나 접어서 가방 안에 넣어두면 쇼핑시 비닐봉투 대신 유용하게 사용할 수 있다.
examples.translation: cheoneuro doen eko baegeul hana jeobeoseo gabang ane neoeodumyeon syopingsi binilbongtu daesin yuyonghage sayonghal su itda. — If you fold one cloth eco bag and keep it in your bag, you can use it usefully instead of a plastic bag when shopping.

examples.text: 아직까지 많은 분들이 환경운동 하면 어렵고 딱딱한 것으로 생각하고 계세요.
examples.translation: ajikkaji maneun bundeuri hwangyeongundong hamyeon eoryeopgo ttakttakan geoseuro saenggakago gyeseyo. — “Even now, many people think of environmental activism as difficult and stiff.”

examples.text: 아침에 나올 때 손수건 하나, 에코 백 하나 챙기는 게 어렵거나 시간이 많이 드는 일은 아니잖아요.
examples.translation: achime naol ttae sonsugeon hana, eko baek hana chaenggineun ge eoryeopgeona sigani mani deuneun ireun anijanayo. — “Taking one handkerchief and one eco bag when you leave in the morning is not difficult or time-consuming, is it?”

examples.text: 조금만 생각을 전환하면 누구나 환경운동가가 될 수 있어요.
examples.translation: jogeumman saenggageul jeonhwanhamyeon nuguna hwangyeongundonggaga doel su isseoyo. — “If you change your thinking just a little, anyone can become an environmental activist.”

explanations.title: 학습활동 2: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The numbers 20, 30 and 500 are the numbers of years it takes for wooden chopsticks, paper cups and Styrofoam containers, respectively, to decompose.

2. The underlined sentences are not visible in the text of the book. The ways of saving resources mentioned include: skipping the printed statement when using an ATM; keeping a personal cup in the office and using it instead of paper cups; and receiving bills as an e-mail statement instead of by giro (the handkerchief and the cloth eco bag are given afterwards).

3. Translation of the sentence “자원 절약이라는 것이 어려운 게 아니에요” (my guess for the underlined sentence, since the underline is not visible): “Saving resources is not something difficult.”

explanations.title: 말해 봅시다! (role-play)
explanations.body: The book’s English instruction: “아래 상황에 맞춰 역할극을 해 봅시다.” (Let us do a role-play to fit the situation below.) You are at a market with your friend who wants to buy inexpensive produce from Chile. Persuade your friend to buy locally grown produce.

explanations.title: Question 5 (speaking)
explanations.body: The book’s speaking prompt of 학습활동 1 (the English is mine):

examples.text: 매일 먹는 음식 중에서 푸드 마일리지가 가장 긴 것과 가장 짧은 것은 무엇입니까?
examples.translation: maeil meongneun eumsik jungeseo pudeu maillijiga gajang gin geotgwa gajang jjalbeun geoseun mueosimnikka? — Of the foods you eat every day, which has the longest and which has the shortest food mileage?

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: 학습활동 3 (a KBS documentary clip on climate change; you answer in English what meteorological and geographic changes are expected and how climate change can be prevented) is an audio activity.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2 (Reading): an interview with an eco-friendly clothing designer
explanations.body: The following is part of an interview with a clothing designer in a magazine (Text and image © Kyunghyang). The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (2년 반 is 이 년 반; 2005년 is 이천오 년; 28쌍 is 스물여덟 쌍); the quotation marks ‘ ’ are removed (the book writes 드레스를 바꿔 보자 in quotation marks and 대지를 위한 바느질 in single quotation marks). The English is mine; the interviewer’s questions are given without quotation marks and the designer’s answers continue across lines.

examples.text: 이경재 씨, 대지를 위한 바느질에 대한 소개를 부탁 드립니다.
examples.translation: igyeongjae ssi, daejireul wihan baneujire daehan sogaereul butak deurimnida. — Mr. Lee Gyeong-jae, please introduce “Sewing for the Earth” (대지를 위한 바느질).

examples.text: 저는 친환경 의류 디자이너입니다.
examples.translation: jeoneun chinhwangyeong uiryu dijaineoimnida. — “I am an environment-friendly clothing designer.

examples.text: 대지를 위한 바느질은 친환경 의류를 주로 만드는 기업으로 설립된 지 이 년 반 정도 되었네요.
examples.translation: daejireul wihan baneujireun chinhwangyeong uiryureul juro mandeuneun gieobeuro seollipdoen ji i nyeon ban jeongdo doeeonneyo. — Sewing for the Earth is a company that mainly makes environment-friendly clothing, and it has been about two and a half years since it was established.

examples.text: 사업은 아직 시작단계라고 봐도 좋아요.
examples.translation: saeobeun ajik sijakdangyerago bwado joayo. — You may regard the business as still being in its starting stage.

examples.text: 파트는 크게 웨딩, 리빙, 단체복 친환경 환자복 등 세 가지로 나뉘어요.
examples.translation: pateuneun keuge weding, ribing, danchebok chinhwangyeong hwanjabok deung se gajiro nanwieoyo. — It is divided broadly into three parts: wedding, living and group clothing (environment-friendly patient gowns and so on).”

examples.text: 친환경 웨딩에 대해 구체적으로 설명해 주세요.
examples.translation: chinhwangyeong wedinge daehae guchejeogeuro seolmyeonghae juseyo. — Please explain environment-friendly weddings in detail.

examples.text: 처음에는 웨딩드레스부터 시작했어요.
examples.translation: cheoeumeneun wedingdeureseubuteo sijakaesseoyo. — “At first I started with wedding dresses.

examples.text: 이천오 년 대학원을 다니며 연예인들이 수천만 원짜리 드레스를 입고 결혼했다는 기사를 보았어요.
examples.translation: icheono nyeon daehagwoneul danimyeo yeonyeindeuri sucheonman wonjjari deureseureul ipgo gyeolhonhaetdaneun gisareul boasseoyo. — In 2005, while attending graduate school, I saw articles saying that celebrities got married wearing dresses worth tens of millions of won.

examples.text: 그렇게 화려하고 값비싼 드레스를 고작 며칠 입고 버리는 것이 아까웠어요.
examples.translation: geureoke hwaryeohago gapbissan deureseureul gojak myeochil ipgo beorineun geosi akkawosseoyo. — It seemed a waste to wear such gorgeous and expensive dresses for barely a few days and throw them away.

examples.text: 폐기처분된 드레스는 결국 환경오염의 주범이 되구요.
examples.translation: pyegicheobundoen deureseuneun gyeolguk hwangyeongoyeomui jubeomi doeguyo. — And the discarded dresses end up becoming a main culprit of environmental pollution.

examples.text: 그래서 드레스를 바꿔 보자라는 생각을 했고 대학원 교수님을 통해 옥수수전분으로 만든 비닐을 알게 되었어요.
examples.translation: geuraeseo deureseureul bakkwo bojaraneun saenggageul haetgo daehagwon gyosunimeul tonghae oksusujeonbuneuro mandeun binireul alge doeeosseoyo. — So I thought, ‘Let’s change the dress,’ and through a graduate school professor I learned about vinyl made from corn starch.

examples.text: 물론 옥수수 비닐은 한 달 정도 만에 다 썩어서 자연으로 돌아가는 무해한 성분이에요.
examples.translation: mullon oksusu binireun han dal jeongdo mane da sseogeoseo jayeoneuro doraganeun muhaehan seongbunieyo. — Of course, corn vinyl is a harmless material that completely decomposes in about a month and returns to nature.

examples.text: 그리고 그걸로 드레스를 만들어 전시를 한 번 했는데 반응이 좋았어요.
examples.translation: geurigo geugeollo deureseureul mandeureo jeonsireul han beon haenneunde baneungi joasseoyo. — And I made a dress with it and held an exhibition once, and the response was good.

examples.text: 그 이후 다른 것은 친환경으로 할 수 없냐는 문의가 들어왔고 친환경 웨딩사업이 시작됐어요.
examples.translation: geu ihu dareun geoseun chinhwangyeongeuro hal su eomnyaneun munuiga deureowatgo chinhwangyeong wedingsaeobi sijakdwaesseoyo. — After that, inquiries came in asking whether other things could not be made environment-friendly too, and the environment-friendly wedding business began.

examples.text: 친구들과 함께 개발한 콩기름 인쇄 청첩장, 뿌리가 살아 있는 부케 결혼식을 하고 난 후 땅에 다시 심는 방식, 친환경 유기농 음식 등을 도입하기 시작했어요.
examples.translation: chingudeulgwa hamkke gaebalhan konggireum inswae cheongcheopjang, ppuriga sara inneun buke gyeolhonsigeul hago nan hu ttange dasi simneun bangsik, chinhwangyeong yuginong eumsik deungeul doipagi sijakaesseoyo. — We began to introduce wedding invitations printed with soybean oil, which I developed with friends, bouquets with living roots (a method of replanting them in the ground after the wedding), environment-friendly organic food and so on.

examples.text: 그렇게 현재까지는 총 스물여덟 쌍의 커플이 결혼했어요.
examples.translation: geureoke hyeonjaekkajineun chong seumullyeodeol ssangui keopeuri gyeolhonhaesseoyo. — In that way, a total of 28 couples have married up to now.”

examples.text: 친환경 결혼식 치룬 부부들의 가정 속에서 이루어진 변화가 있나요?
examples.translation: chinhwangyeong gyeolhonsik chirun bubudeurui gajeong sogeseo irueojin byeonhwaga innayo? — Have there been changes in the homes of the couples who had an environment-friendly wedding?

examples.text: 예비 신랑신부님들이 처음 친환경 결혼을 결정하실 때 환경에 의미를 두고 하시는 분들도 계시지만 꼭 그렇지 않아도 특별한 결혼식을 위해 하시는 분들도 종종 계세요.
examples.translation: yebi sillangsinbunimdeuri cheoeum chinhwangyeong gyeolhoneul gyeoljeonghasil ttae hwangyeonge uimireul dugo hasineun bundeuldo gyesijiman kkok geureochi anado teukbyeolhan gyeolhonsigeul wihae hasineun bundeuldo jongjong gyeseyo. — “When prospective brides and grooms first decide on an environment-friendly wedding, some attach meaning to the environment, but there are also often people who do it for a special wedding even if that is not necessarily the case.

examples.text: 하지만 결혼식을 치룬 후, 그냥 지나치던 작은 일도 환경을 위한 습관으로 변해가고 있다는 얘기를 듣곤 해요.
examples.translation: hajiman gyeolhonsigeul chirun hu, geunyang jinachideon jageun ildo hwangyeongeul wihan seupgwaneuro byeonhaegago itdaneun yaegireul deutgon haeyo. — But after the wedding, I often hear that even small things they used to just pass over are turning into habits for the environment.

examples.text: 그런 이야기를 들으면 정말 흐뭇하고 일의 보람을 느끼죠.
examples.translation: geureon iyagireul deureumyeon jeongmal heumutago irui borameul neukkijo. — When I hear such stories, I feel really pleased and feel the reward of my work.”

explanations.title: 학습활동 2: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The sentence that accurately reflects the passage is D: bouquets and invitation cards were made from environment-friendly materials (the bouquet has living roots to replant after the wedding; the invitation is printed with soybean oil). A is wrong: the corn vinyl dress was made and exhibited; B is wrong: she started the business after the exhibition drew inquiries, not after making her own wedding dress; C is wrong: some of the couples did it simply for a special wedding.

2. 대지를 위한 바느질 (Sewing for the Earth) is a company, set up about two and a half years ago by the interviewee, an environment-friendly clothing designer, that mainly makes environment-friendly clothing. The business is still in its starting stage and is divided broadly into three parts: wedding, living and group clothing (such as environment-friendly patient gowns).

3. The first item she made was a wedding dress. She made it because she was bothered that celebrities wear gorgeous, expensive dresses (worth tens of millions of won) for barely a few days and then throw them away, and the discarded dresses become a main culprit of environmental pollution. She learned about vinyl made from corn starch, which decomposes in about a month, and made the dress from it.

4. What makes her work rewarding: she hears that after their eco-friendly wedding the couples’ small everyday matters that they used to pass over have turned into habits for the environment, and when she hears such stories she feels pleased and feels the reward of her work.

The list is a picture and is not in the text, so the answer cannot be given here.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2 (Reading): overseas news on happiness
explanations.body: Read the article and the chart and choose the statement that fits (© Kyunghyang). The article is the book’s with 15개 국 spelled out (열다섯 개 국). The English is mine.

examples.text: 영국 케임브리지대 연구팀이 유럽 열다섯 개 국의 국민을 대상으로 행복감을 느끼는 정도를 질문한 결과, 덴마크 국민이 자신의 삶에 가장 행복과 만족감을 느끼는 것으로 나타났다.
examples.translation: yeongguk keimbeurijidae yeongutimi yureop yeoldaseot gae gugui gungmineul daesangeuro haengbokgameul neukkineun jeongdoreul jilmunhan gyeolgwa, denmakeu gungmini jasinui salme gajang haengbokgwa manjokgameul neukkineun geoseuro natanatda. — A research team of the University of Cambridge in Britain asked the people of 15 European countries how happy they feel, and the result showed that the Danish people feel the most happiness and satisfaction in their lives.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2: my answer
explanations.body:
The statements are: A. Males and females age 15 and above were surveyed. B. People from countries around the world were asked about their level of satisfaction with life. C. A college in Britain conducted the research. D. Survey results showed that people in Denmark were least satisfied with life.

My answer is C. The text says a research team of the University of Cambridge in Britain conducted it. A cannot be checked in the text (the chart may say), B is wrong (15 European countries, not the world) and D is wrong (the Danes were the most satisfied).

explanations.title: 학습활동 5: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The true statement is C: only seniors 60 or older may enter this park (the association’s playground is “for seniors,” the gardeners stopped young people, and the park side stressed it is not a place for grandchildren). A is wrong (children are not allowed even with seniors), B is wrong (no rides for both generations) and D is wrong (the text only says that such playgrounds exist in China and Europe, not that this one was modeled after one).

2. The underlined sentence is not visible in the text of the book; every sentence of the article is translated above.

explanations.title: 학습활동 1 (Reading): Nepal and Mount Everest
explanations.body: The following article is related to Nepal; the book asks you to read it and do the tasks in English (Text and image © Kyunghyang, © Yonhapnews). The text is the book’s with 8000 m spelled out (팔천 미터). The English is mine.

examples.text: 등반객들이 버린 쓰레기로 오염된 세계 최고봉 에베레스트를 정화하기 위해 정상 등반 경험이 있는 네팔 셰르파들이 나서 팔천 미터 이상 고지대에 있는 쓰레기를 치우기로 했다.
examples.translation: deungbangaekdeuri beorin sseuregiro oyeomdoen segye choegobong ebereseuteureul jeonghwahagi wihae jeongsang deungban gyeongheomi inneun nepal syereupadeuri naseo palcheon miteo isang gojidaee inneun sseuregireul chiugiro haetda. — To purify Everest, the world’s highest peak, polluted by garbage discarded by climbers, Nepalese Sherpas with experience of climbing to the summit have stepped forward and decided to clear the garbage at high altitudes of 8,000 meters and above.

examples.text: 등반객들이 버린 쓰레기는 에베레스트를 오염시키는 주원인이었다.
examples.translation: deungbangaekdeuri beorin sseuregineun ebereseuteureul oyeomsikineun juwoninieotda. — The garbage discarded by climbers was the main cause of polluting Everest.

examples.text: 이 때문에 네팔 정부는 모든 소지품과 쓰레기를 그대로 갖고 돌아오는 등반객들에게만 예치금을 돌려주는 정책을 실시하고 있다.
examples.translation: i ttaemune nepal jeongbuneun modeun sojipumgwa sseuregireul geudaero gatgo doraoneun deungbangaekdeuregeman yechigeumeul dollyeojuneun jeongchaegeul silsihago itda. — For this reason, the Nepalese government is carrying out a policy of returning the deposit only to climbers who bring back all their belongings and garbage just as they are.

examples.text: 에베레스트에 있는 쓰레기의 양은 정확히 알 수 없으나, 과거 청소팀들이 수거해 온 쓰레기는 수 톤에 이른다.
examples.translation: ebereseuteue inneun sseuregiui yangeun jeonghwaki al su eopseuna, gwageo cheongsotimdeuri sugeohae on sseuregineun su tone ireunda. — The amount of garbage on Everest cannot be known exactly, but the garbage that cleaning teams collected in the past amounts to several tons.

explanations.title: 학습활동 1: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The Nepalese government’s policy: it gives the deposit back only to climbers who bring back all their belongings and garbage as they are. The ground for it: the garbage that climbers discard was the main cause of polluting Everest.

2. The Sherpas’ plan: Nepalese Sherpas who have climbed to the summit will step forward to clear the garbage lying at high altitudes of 8,000 meters and above, in order to purify Everest.

explanations.title: 학습활동 3 (Reading): the Salon du Chocolat and Peru
explanations.body: The following newspaper article is news about an event held in France (Text and image © Kyunghyang). The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (10월 is 시월; 10년 is 십 년; 2만 명 is 이만 명); the quotation marks ‘ ’ are removed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 매년 프랑스 파리에서 열리는 살롱 뒤 쇼콜라는 세계 초콜릿 생산농들이 모여 카카오 향을 뽐내는 잔치다.
examples.translation: maenyeon peurangseu parieseo yeollineun sallong dwi syokollaneun segye chokollit saengsannongdeuri moyeo kakao hyangeul ppomnaeneun janchida. — The Salon du Chocolat, held every year in Paris, France, is a feast where the world’s chocolate producers gather and show off the aroma of cacao.

examples.text: 지난해 시월 열린 이 행사에서 최고의 향기의 영예는 페루의 작은 마을에 돌아갔다.
examples.translation: jinanhae siwol yeollin i haengsaeseo choegoui hyanggiui yeongyeneun peruui jageun maeure doragatda. — At this event held last October, the honor of the “best aroma” went to a small village in Peru.

examples.text: 안데스 산맥 줄기가 끝나고 아마존의 열대우림으로 이어지는 경계선에 위치한 페루 북부 산마르틴주의 토카체 마을에서 나온 원두가 대상을 차지한 것이다.
examples.translation: andeseu sanmaek julgiga kkeunnago amajonui yeoldaeurimeuro ieojineun gyeonggyeseone wichihan peru bukbu sanmareutinjuui tokache maeureseo naon wonduga daesangeul chajihan geosida. — The beans from the village of Tocache in San Martín state in northern Peru, located on the boundary line where the Andes mountain range ends and leads into the Amazon tropical rain forest, won the grand prize.

examples.text: 산마르틴은 불과 십 년 전만 해도 코카와 마약 밀매로 유명한 곳이었다.
examples.translation: sanmareutineun bulgwa sip nyeon jeonman haedo kokawa mayak milmaero yumyeonghan gosieotda. — As recently as only ten years ago, San Martín was a place famous for coca and drug trafficking.

examples.text: 주민들은 코카인의 원료인 코카나무를 재배해 마약조직에 넘기며 연명했다.
examples.translation: jumindeureun kokainui wollyoin kokanamureul jaebaehae mayakjojige neomgimyeo yeonmyeonghaetda. — The residents survived by growing coca plants, the raw material of cocaine, and handing them over to drug organizations.

examples.text: 인구 이만 명의 토카체 마을도 마찬가지였다.
examples.translation: ingu iman myeongui tokache maeuldo machangajiyeotda. — The village of Tocache, with a population of 20,000, was the same.

examples.text: 정부는 미국과 유엔 등의 지원을 받아 코카와의 싸움에 들어갔다.
examples.translation: jeongbuneun migukgwa yuen deungui jiwoneul bada kokawaui ssaume deureogatda. — The government, with support from the United States, the United Nations and others, entered a “fight against coca.”

examples.text: 농민들이 먹고 살 길을 열어주는 것이 가장 중요했다.
examples.translation: nongmindeuri meokgo sal gireul yeoreojuneun geosi gajang jungyohaetda. — Opening the way for the farmers to make a living was the most important thing.

examples.text: 코카를 대체할 희망의 싹으로 떠오른 것이 카카오였다.
examples.translation: kokareul daechehal huimangui ssageuro tteooreun geosi kakaoyeotda. — What emerged as the sprout of hope to replace coca was cacao.

examples.text: 산마르틴 주정부는 카카오를 농가수입원으로 삼는 것을 넘어, 세계적인 특산지로 만들기 위해 발벗고 나섰다.
examples.translation: sanmareutin jujeongbuneun kakaoreul nonggasuibwoneuro samneun geoseul neomeo, segyejeogin teuksanjiro mandeulgi wihae balbeotgo naseotda. — The San Martín state government went beyond making cacao a source of farm income and rolled up its sleeves to make the area a world-class specialty-product region.

explanations.title: 학습활동 3: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The town is Tocache (토카체) in San Martín state in northern Peru. Geographically, it lies on the boundary line where the Andes mountain range ends and leads into the Amazon tropical rain forest.

2. Ten years ago the state was famous for coca and drug trafficking, and the residents survived by growing coca plants and handing them to drug organizations. Now it is known for cacao: its beans won the grand prize at the Salon du Chocolat, and the state government is working to make it a world-class specialty-product region.

3. The underlined sentence is not visible in the text of the book; every sentence is translated above (the likely candidate is 코카를 대체할 희망의 싹으로 떠오른 것이 카카오였다: “What emerged as the sprout of hope to replace coca was cacao.”).

lessons.subtitle: 심화 학습 · 히키코모리 · 은둔형 외톨이 · 일본 · 사회현상 · 심심찮게 · 말해 봅시다

explanations.title: 학습활동 1 (Reading): the social phenomenon of 히키코모리 in Japan
explanations.body: The following article is about a social phenomenon that has become a serious problem in Japan (© Kyunghyang). The text is the book’s with the numbers and abbreviations spelled out (TV is 티브이; 2001년 5월 is 이천일 년 오 월; 6개월 is 육 개월; 3~4년 is 삼 년에서 사 년; 10년 is 십 년; 1970년대 is 천구백칠십 년대; 90년대 is 구십 년대; 1백20만 명 is 백이십만 명; 1억 2천만 명 is 일억 이천만 명; 1% is 일 퍼센트; 30대 is 삼십 대; 30% is 삼십 퍼센트); the Japanese ひきこもり after 히키코모리 is dropped, the quotation marks ‘ ’ are removed, the dot in 폭행•살인 and the dots in 광장공포증•햇빛혐오증•우울증•현기증 are replaced by commas. The English is mine.

examples.text: 최근 일본에서 심심찮게 등장하는 단어 중의 하나가 히키코모리이다.
examples.translation: choegeun ilboneseo simsimchanke deungjanghaneun daneo jungui hanaga hikikomoriida. — One of the words that appear quite often in Japan recently is “hikikomori.”

examples.text: 히키코모리는 방안에 틀어박히다라는 뜻인 히키코모루의 명사형이다.
examples.translation: hikikomorineun bangane teureobakidaraneun tteusin hikikomoruui myeongsahyeongida. — Hikikomori is the noun form of “hikikomoru,” which means “to shut oneself up (in a room).”

examples.text: 일체의 사회적인 관계를 거부하고 방안이나 집에서 거의 나오지 않고 지내는 사람들을 지칭한다.
examples.translation: ilcheui sahoejeogin gwangyereul geobuhago banganina jibeseo geoui naoji anko jinaeneun saramdeureul jichinghanda. — It refers to people who refuse all social relationships and live hardly ever coming out of their room or house.

examples.text: 이들은 다른 사람과 대화하지 않고, 낮에는 자고 밤에 일어나 티브이나 비디오를 보며 인터넷에 탐닉하는 행태를 보인다.
examples.translation: ideureun dareun saramgwa daehwahaji anko, najeneun jago bame ireona tibeuina bidioreul bomyeo inteonese tamnikaneun haengtaereul boinda. — They do not talk with other people, sleep during the day, get up at night and show a pattern of watching TV or videos and indulging in the Internet.

examples.text: 누구나 한 번쯤은 해 봤을법한 행동이지만 문제는 지속 기간이다.
examples.translation: nuguna han beonjjeumeun hae bwasseulbeopan haengdongijiman munjeneun jisok giganida. — It is behavior that anyone might have tried once, but the problem is the duration.

examples.text: 일본 후생성은 이천일 년 오 월 그 기준을 육 개월 이상이라고 제시했다.
examples.translation: ilbon husaengseongeun icheonil nyeon o wol geu gijuneul yuk gaewol isangirago jesihaetda. — In May 2001, Japan’s Ministry of Health and Welfare presented the standard as “six months or more.”

examples.text: 길게는 삼 년에서 사 년, 심하면 십 년 이상을 방안에서 지내는 사람들도 있다.
examples.translation: gilgeneun sam nyeoneseo sa nyeon, simhamyeon sip nyeon isangeul banganeseo jinaeneun saramdeuldo itda. — There are people who spend as long as three to four years, or in severe cases more than ten years, in their room.

examples.text: 자청해서 은둔형 외톨이가 된다는 것도 특징이다.
examples.translation: jacheonghaeseo eundunhyeong oetoriga doendaneun geotdo teukjingida. — It is also a characteristic that they become “reclusive loners” of their own accord.

examples.text: 히키코모리는 천구백칠십 년대에 처음 등장했다.
examples.translation: hikikomorineun cheongubaekchilsip nyeondaee cheoeum deungjanghaetda. — Hikikomori first appeared in the 1970s.

examples.text: 당시 입시에 시달리던 학생들이 무단결석하고 낮에는 집안에 있다가 밤이 되면 외출하는 현상이 빈발했다.
examples.translation: dangsi ipsie sidallideon haksaengdeuri mudangyeolseokago najeneun jibane itdaga bami doemyeon oechulhaneun hyeonsangi binbalhaetda. — At that time, the phenomenon of students suffering from entrance exams skipping school without permission, staying at home during the day and going out at night occurred frequently.

examples.text: 대부분의 학자들은 이를 두고 일부 불량청소년들의 단순한 등교거부쯤으로 해석했다.
examples.translation: daebubunui hakjadeureun ireul dugo ilbu bullyangcheongsonyeondeurui dansunhan deunggyogeobujjeumeuro haeseokaetda. — Most scholars interpreted this as the simple “school refusal” of some delinquent youths.

examples.text: 그러다 구십 년대 중반부터는 학생들이 밤에 거리로 나와 행인을 폭행, 살인하는 등 점차 과격한 행동을 보였다.
examples.translation: geureoda gusip nyeondae jungbanbuteoneun haksaengdeuri bame georiro nawa haengineul pokaeng, sarinhaneun deung jeomcha gwagyeokan haengdongeul boyeotda. — Then from the mid-1990s, students came out onto the streets at night and showed increasingly violent behavior, such as assaulting and killing passers-by.

examples.text: 비슷한 시기, 은둔하는 성인들도 나타나면서 히키코모리는 사회문제로 비화했다.
examples.translation: biseutan sigi, eundunhaneun seongindeuldo natanamyeonseo hikikomorineun sahoemunjero bihwahaetda. — At about the same time, reclusive adults also appeared, and hikikomori developed into a social problem.

examples.text: 일본경제가 침체의 늪에 빠져들기 시작한 무렵이다.
examples.translation: ilbongyeongjega chimcheui neupe ppajeodeulgi sijakan muryeobida. — This was around the time Japan’s economy began to sink into the swamp of stagnation.

examples.text: 갑자기 일자리를 잃거나 취업전선에서 낙방한 젊은이들이 자신의 처지를 비관해 사회생활을 거부한 채 아예 집안으로 잠적해 버렸다.
examples.translation: gapjagi iljarireul ilkeona chwieopjeonseoneseo nakbanghan jeolmeunideuri jasinui cheojireul bigwanhae sahoesaenghwareul geobuhan chae aye jibaneuro jamjeokae beoryeotda. — Young people who suddenly lost their jobs or failed in the job-hunting front became pessimistic about their own situation and disappeared altogether into their homes, refusing social life.

examples.text: 히키코모리는 지난해 현재 대략 백이십만 명으로 추산되고 있다.
examples.translation: hikikomorineun jinanhae hyeonjae daeryak baegisimman myeongeuro chusandoego itda. — As of last year, hikikomori are estimated at roughly 1.2 million.

examples.text: 일본 인구 일억 이천만 명 의 일 퍼센트에 해당하는 수치다.
examples.translation: ilbon ingu ireok icheonman myeong ui il peosenteue haedanghaneun suchida. — This is a figure equivalent to 1 percent of Japan’s population (120 million).

examples.text: 일본에서 특히 우려하는 점은 이 중에서 왕성한 사회활동을 해야 할 삼십 대의 비율이 삼십 퍼센트에 이르는 데다 대부분 남성들이라는 것.
examples.translation: ilboneseo teuki uryeohaneun jeomeun i jungeseo wangseonghan sahoehwaldongeul haeya hal samsip daeui biyuri samsip peosenteue ireuneun deda daebubun namseongdeuriraneun geot. — What is especially worrying in Japan is that, among them, those in their thirties, who should be active in society, make up as much as 30 percent, and that most of them are men.

examples.text: 이들은 외부와 단절된 자기만의 공간에서 오래 생활하다 보니 광장공포증, 햇빛혐오증, 우울증, 현기증 등에 시달리는 것으로 알려지고 있다.
examples.translation: ideureun oebuwa danjeoldoen jagimanui gongganeseo orae saenghwalhada boni gwangjanggongpojeung, haetbicheomojeung, uuljeung, hyeongijeung deunge sidallineun geoseuro allyeojigo itda. — Having lived for a long time in a space of their own cut off from the outside, they are known to suffer from agoraphobia, an aversion to sunlight, depression, dizziness and so on.

explanations.title: 학습활동 1: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The sentence that defines 히키코모리: 일체의 사회적인 관계를 거부하고 방안이나 집에서 거의 나오지 않고 지내는 사람들을 지칭한다. (It refers to people who refuse all social relationships and live hardly ever coming out of their room or house.)

2. Comparison of 1970s and after the mid-1990s: see the table below.

3. The concerns in the last paragraph: about 1.2 million people (1% of Japan’s population) are hikikomori; about 30% of them are in their thirties, the age when they should be socially active, and most are men; and because they live a long time in a space cut off from the outside, they suffer from agoraphobia, an aversion to sunlight, depression and dizziness.

4. The word that can replace 심심찮게 is B. 자주 (often).

rows: Students suffering from entrance exams skipped school, stayed at home by day and went out at night; most scholars read it as simple school refusal by some delinquent youths.

Students came out at night and grew more violent (assaulting and killing passers-by); reclusive adults also appeared, and it became a social problem as Japan’s economy stagnated and young people who lost jobs or failed in job hunting shut themselves in.

explanations.title: 말해 봅시다! (speaking)
explanations.body: The book’s speaking prompts (the English is mine):

examples.translation: miguk sinsedaeui teukjinge daehae malhae boseyo. — Tell about the characteristics of the new generation in the United States.

examples.text: 그리고 구세대와 다른 점도 말해 보세요.
examples.translation: geurigo gusedaewa dareun jeomdo malhae boseyo. — And also tell how they differ from the older generation.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: 학습활동 2 (a YTN video on China’s young generation: what the “ant tribe” 개미족 is and why it was given the name, the daily difficulty of Mr. Ryu Jun, a summary of a segment and how the college entrance rate affects them) and 학습활동 3 (a YTN video on a new pension reform policy in France: the policy, the government’s reason, laborers’ reaction, a true statement about the 2006 demonstration and a comparison of older and younger people’s opinions) are audio and video activities.

explanations.title: 알아봅시다 1: inter-Korean relations in the 2000s (남북 관계) — the book’s note
explanations.body: South Korea’s policy toward North Korea in the new millennium has swung from liberalism (pro-NK) to conservatism (anti-NK). 햇볕정책, or the Sunshine Policy, used to be the overarching slogan for South Korea’s administrations under Kim Dae-Jung and Roh Moo-Hyun. The term “sunshine” was adopted from Aesop’s well-known fable (the North Wind and the Sun) in which sunshine proved more effective than a strong wind in ridding a traveler (NK) of a coat. Kim Dae-Jung was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2000 for his initiation of the Sunshine Policy. The two former presidents had historic summit meetings (남북 정상회담) with North Korea’s leader Kim Jung-Il in Pyoungyang, in June 2000 and in October 2007, respectively. In the meantime, tension between the two Koreas relaxed; they discussed economy, culture, sports, the reunion of separated families (남북 이산가족 상봉), etc. The success of 개성공업지구 was a result of combining South Korea’s capital and technology with North Korea’s labor.

explanations.title: 알아봅시다 2: 금강산 관광 — the book’s note
explanations.body: 금강산 is located on the east coast of North Korea, only 30 miles north of the DMZ. 금강산 is well known for its year-round beauty. In 1998, South Korean tourists visited 금강산 via cruise ship for the first time since the partition of the Korean peninsula. This was made possible by Hyundai, a South Korean conglomerate, in cooperation and with support from the South Korean government. In 2003, the land route opened and South Koreans were accommodated with varied tour packages. According to Hyundai’s tally, a million South Koreans visited 금강산 by June 2005. This tourism was not without issues, most of which were caused by inter-Korean politics, and the occasional detention of individual tourists by North Korea. On July 11, 2008, a South Korean tourist was shot to death by North Korean soldiers when she inadvertently crossed over into the military area near a resort beach. This incident, along with the increased tensions on the peninsula, stopped 금강산 관광 for an extended period.

examples.translation: seoureseo charo se sigan namjit dallyeo seoraksan misiryeongeul neomeuni chachang oreunpyeoneuro geompureun badaga pyeolcheojeotda. — After driving a little over three hours from Seoul and crossing Misiryeong in Mount Seorak, the dark blue sea spread out on the right side of the car window.

examples.text: 속초, 간성, 거진을 거치고 남한 최북단 해수욕장인 화진포를 지나 현내면에 도착할 때쯤엔 도로를 달리는 차들이 거의 없었다.
examples.translation: sokcho, ganseong, geojineul geochigo namhan choebukdan haesuyokjangin hwajinporeul jina hyeonnaemyeone dochakal ttaejjeumen dororeul dallineun chadeuri geoui eopseotda. — By the time I passed through Sokcho, Ganseong and Geojin, went by Hwajinpo, the northernmost beach in South Korea, and arrived at Hyeonnae-myeon, there were almost no cars running on the road.

examples.text: 택시 운전사 한진섭 쉰두 살 씨는 여름엔 물놀이를 하러 오는 사람들이라도 있지만 추울 때는 정말 조용한 곳이라며 통일전망대에서 금강산 설경이라도 구경하고 가시라고 권했다.
examples.translation: taeksi unjeonsa hanjinseop swindu sal ssineun yeoreumen mullorireul hareo oneun saramdeurirado itjiman chuul ttaeneun jeongmal joyonghan gosiramyeo tongiljeonmangdaeeseo geumgangsan seolgyeongirado gugyeonghago gasirago gwonhaetda. — Taxi driver Han Jin-seop (52) said, “In summer there are at least people who come to play in the water, but when it is cold it is a really quiet place,” and recommended, “At least look at the snowy scenery of Mount Kumgang from the Unification Observatory before you go.”

examples.text: 통일전망대로 가기 위해 들른 출입 신고소는 한산했다.
examples.translation: tongiljeonmangdaero gagi wihae deulleun churip singosoneun hansanhaetda. — The entry report office I stopped at to go to the Unification Observatory was quiet.

examples.text: 신고소 관계자는 하루 평균 천 명 정도가 전망대를 찾았는데 칠 월 이후로는 육백 명에서 칠백 명대로 줄어들었다고 설명했다.
examples.translation: singoso gwangyejaneun haru pyeonggyun cheon myeong jeongdoga jeonmangdaereul chajanneunde chil wol ihuroneun yukbaek myeongeseo chilbaek myeongdaero jureodeureotdago seolmyeonghaetda. — An official of the report office explained, “On average about 1,000 people visited the observatory a day, but since July it has fallen to the 600 to 700 range.”

examples.text: 출입증을 받고 십여 분 후 전망대에 도착했다.
examples.translation: churipjeungeul batgo sibyeo bun hu jeonmangdaee dochakaetda. — After receiving an entry pass, I arrived at the observatory about ten minutes later.

examples.text: 정상에서 망원경으로 맞은편을 바라보던 고 모 일흔두 살 씨는 금강산 참 아름답다를 되뇌었다.
examples.translation: jeongsangeseo mangwongyeongeuro majeunpyeoneul barabodeon go mo ilheundu sal ssineun geumgangsan cham areumdapdareul doenoeeotda. — Mr. Ko (72), who was looking at the opposite side through a telescope at the top, kept repeating, “Mount Kumgang is truly beautiful.”

examples.text: 고향이 함경도라는 그는 관광 개시 초기에 한 번 금강산에 다녀온 적이 있다고 했다.
examples.translation: gohyangi hamgyeongdoraneun geuneun gwangwang gaesi chogie han beon geumgangsane danyeoon jeogi itdago haetda. — He, whose hometown is Hamgyeong Province, said that he had been to Mount Kumgang once in the early days of the tours.

examples.text: 그때는 부부가 함께였다.
examples.translation: geuttaeneun bubuga hamkkeyeotda. — At that time the couple was together.

examples.text: 그는 아내가 세상을 떠나고 지난 칠 월 다시 금강산 관광을 예약했는데 취소됐다며 아쉬워했다.
examples.translation: geuneun anaega sesangeul tteonago jinan chil wol dasi geumgangsan gwangwangeul yeyakaenneunde chwisodwaetdamyeo aswiwohaetda. — He said regretfully, “After my wife passed away, I booked a Mount Kumgang tour again last July, but it was canceled.”

examples.text: 전망대에서 나와 현내면으로 가는 길.
examples.translation: jeonmangdaeeseo nawa hyeonnaemyeoneuro ganeun gil. — The road from the observatory to Hyeonnae-myeon.

examples.text: 도로변 곳곳에 식당과 상점 십여 곳이 눈에 띄었다.
examples.translation: dorobyeon gotgose sikdanggwa sangjeom sibyeo gosi nune ttuieotda. — About ten restaurants and shops were visible here and there along the road.

examples.text: 모두 휴업했거나 아예 문을 닫은 상태였다.
examples.translation: modu hyueopaetgeona aye muneul dadeun sangtaeyeotda. — All of them were closed temporarily or had shut down altogether.

examples.text: 금강산 콘도 역시 매출의 삼십 퍼센트 이상을 차지하던 금강산 관광객들의 발길이 끊어지면서 이백이십오 개의 객실 중 절반가량이 비었다.
examples.translation: geumgangsan kondo yeoksi maechurui samsip peosenteu isangeul chajihadeon geumgangsan gwangwanggaekdeurui balgiri kkeuneojimyeonseo ibaegisibo gaeui gaeksil jung jeolbangaryangi bieotda. — The Mount Kumgang condominium, too, has about half of its 225 rooms empty, as the footsteps of the Mount Kumgang tourists, who accounted for more than 30 percent of its sales, have stopped.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
3. What can be inferred from the title is A: the tour has been stopped (the title wishes that the road be opened again).

4. The portions that give clues: 신고소는 한산했다; 칠 월 이후로는 육백 명에서 칠백 명대로 줄어들었다; 지난 칠 월 다시 금강산 관광을 예약했는데 취소됐다; 식당과 상점 십여 곳 … 모두 휴업했거나 아예 문을 닫은 상태였다; 금강산 관광객들의 발길이 끊어지면서 … 절반가량이 비었다.

5. The left-out passage (below) fits best at the very beginning of the journal, before the first bulleted paragraph, as the introduction that states the situation (the tours stopped for six months and the residents’ wish), which the bulleted paragraphs then illustrate.

examples.text: 금강산 관광객 피격사건 등으로 금강산 관광이 중단된 지 어느덧 육 개월이다.
examples.translation: geumgangsan gwangwanggaek pigyeoksageon deungeuro geumgangsan gwangwangi jungdandoen ji eoneudeot yuk gaeworida. — It has already been six months since the Mount Kumgang tours were stopped because of incidents such as the shooting of a Mount Kumgang tourist.

examples.text: 강원도 고성군은 이로 인해 지역경제에 적지 않은 타격을 입고 있다.
examples.translation: gangwondo goseongguneun iro inhae jiyeokgyeongjee jeokji aneun tagyeogeul ipgo itda. — Goseong County in Gangwon Province is suffering no small blow to its regional economy because of this.

examples.text: 이곳 주민들의 새해 소원은 막혔던 길이 다시 열려 남북관계가 회복되고 자신들의 삶이 희망을 되찾는 것이다.
examples.translation: igot jumindeurui saehae sowoneun makyeotdeon giri dasi yeollyeo nambukgwangyega hoebokdoego jasindeurui salmi huimangeul doechanneun geosida. — The new-year wish of the residents here is that the blocked road open again, inter-Korean relations recover and their lives regain hope.

explanations.title: 말해 봅시다! (speaking)
explanations.body: The book’s speaking prompts (the English is mine):

examples.text: 한반도가 통일되면 남북한 국민들의 생활에 어떤 변화가 생길지 이야기해 보세요.
examples.translation: hanbandoga tongildoemyeon nambukan gungmindeurui saenghware eotteon byeonhwaga saenggilji iyagihae boseyo. — Talk about what changes will occur in the lives of the people of South and North Korea if the Korean peninsula is unified.

examples.text: 한반도의 통일에 대해 주변 국가들, 특히 중국, 일본, 러시아, 미국은 어떤 입장일지 이야기해 보세요.
examples.translation: hanbandoui tongire daehae jubyeon gukgadeul, teuki jungguk, ilbon, reosia, migugeun eotteon ipjangilji iyagihae boseyo. — Talk about what position the surrounding countries, especially China, Japan, Russia and the United States, would take on the unification of the Korean peninsula.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: 학습활동 1, questions 1 (four spoken descriptions matched with illustrations), 학습활동 2, question 1 (an edunet4u.net audio clip on 금강산 관광: a table of the year tourism began, the specific type of tourists mentioned and who made it possible) and 학습활동 3 (a KBS video on North Korea’s animation industry: an example of cooperation between North and South Korea, North Korea’s animation technology and a unique characteristic of the animation broadcast in North Korea) are audio, video and picture activities.

explanations.title: 알아봅시다: the rules for initial consonant restrictions in North Korean (두음법칙) — the book’s note
explanations.body:
Recall that Sino-Korean syllables beginning with the initial consonants ㄹ or ㄴ have different pronunciations depending on their position; e.g., 력/역 for 力 (power), as in 체력 vs. 역도; 녀/여 for 女 (female), as in 남녀 vs. 여자.

The consonant sound /n/ is not used as the initial sound of a word when it is followed by vowels like ㅕ, ㅑ, ㅛ, and ㅠ. This is known as 두음법칙 (initial consonant restriction; “head sound rule”). The South Korean language is faithful to this restriction, whereas the North Korean language standardized the spelling in accordance with the original Chinese sounds /l, r/, and /n/.

The book lets you click on three Sino-Korean words to hear how North Koreans pronounce them: 노동, 역사 and 여성 (in the North they are said 로동, 력사 and 녀성).

explanations.title: 학습활동 2 (Reading): the June 15 Joint Declaration — the South Korean text
explanations.body: The book gives the declaration of June 15, 2000 (the South Korean text on the left and the North Korean text on the right) and asks you to compare them. The title is 남북 공동 선언. Digits are spelled out here (2000년 6월 13일 is 이천 년 유월 십삼 일; 6월 15일 is 유월 십오 일; 8•15 is 팔 일오). The text ends with the date 2000년 6월 15일 (이천 년 유월 십오 일) and the signatures of 대한민국 대통령 김대중 and 조선민주주의인민공화국 국방위원장 김정일. The English is mine (it is the same for both texts, which differ only in spelling, vocabulary and honorifics).
