examples.text: 남북정상들은 분단 역사상 처음으로 열린 이번 상봉과 회담이 서로 이해를 증진시키고 남북관계를 발전시키며 평화통일을 실현하는 데 중대한 의의를 가진다고 평가하고 다음과 같이 선언한다.
examples.translation: nambukjeongsangdeureun bundan yeoksasang cheoeumeuro yeollin ibeon sangbonggwa hoedami seoro ihaereul jeungjinsikigo nambukgwangyereul baljeonsikimyeo pyeonghwatongireul silhyeonhaneun de jungdaehan uiuireul gajindago pyeonggahago daeumgwa gachi seoneonhanda. — The leaders of the South and the North appraised that this meeting and talks, held for the first time in the history of the division, have great significance in promoting mutual understanding, developing South-North relations and realizing peaceful unification, and declare as follows.

examples.text: 남과 북은 나라의 통일문제를 그 주인인 우리 민족끼리 서로 힘을 합쳐 자주적으로 해결해 나가기로 하였다.
examples.translation: namgwa bugeun naraui tongilmunjereul geu juinin uri minjokkiri seoro himeul hapcheo jajujeogeuro haegyeolhae nagagiro hayeotda. — 1. The South and the North agreed to solve the problem of the country’s unification independently, by joining forces, among our own people, who are its masters.

examples.text: 남과 북은 나라의 통일을 위한 남측의 연합제 안과 북측의 낮은 단계의 연방제 안이 서로 공통성이 있다고 인정하고 앞으로 이 방향에서 통일을 지향시켜 나가기로 하였다.
examples.translation: namgwa bugeun naraui tongireul wihan namcheugui yeonhapje angwa bukcheugui najeun dangyeui yeonbangje ani seoro gongtongseongi itdago injeonghago apeuro i banghyangeseo tongireul jihyangsikyeo nagagiro hayeotda. — 2. The South and the North recognized that the South’s proposal for a union and the North’s proposal for a low-level federation for the country’s unification have elements in common, and agreed to work toward unification in this direction from now on.

examples.text: 남과 북은 올해 팔 일오에 즈음하여 흩어진 가족, 친척방문단을 교환하며 비전향 장기수 문제를 해결하는 등 인도적 문제를 조속히 풀어 나가기로 하였다.
examples.translation: namgwa bugeun olhae pal iroe jeueumhayeo heuteojin gajok, chincheokbangmundaneul gyohwanhamyeo bijeonhyang janggisu munjereul haegyeolhaneun deung indojeok munjereul josoki pureo nagagiro hayeotda. — 3. The South and the North agreed to exchange visiting groups of separated families and relatives on the occasion of this year’s August 15 and to promptly resolve humanitarian issues, such as the problem of unconverted long-term prisoners.

examples.text: 남과 북은 경제협력을 통하여 민족경제를 균형적으로 발전시키고 사회, 문화, 체육, 보건, 환경 등 제반 분야의 협력과 교류를 활성화하여 서로의 신뢰를 다져 나가기로 하였다.
examples.translation: namgwa bugeun gyeongjehyeomnyeogeul tonghayeo minjokgyeongjereul gyunhyeongjeogeuro baljeonsikigo sahoe, munhwa, cheyuk, bogeon, hwangyeong deung jeban bunyaui hyeomnyeokgwa gyoryureul hwalseonghwahayeo seoroui silloereul dajeo nagagiro hayeotda. — 4. The South and the North agreed to develop the national economy in a balanced way through economic cooperation, and to activate cooperation and exchange in various fields such as society, culture, sports, health and the environment, and thereby build mutual trust.

examples.text: 남과 북은 이상과 같은 합의사항을 조속히 실천에 옮기기 위하여 빠른 시일안에 당국 사이의 대화를 개최하기로 하였다.
examples.translation: namgwa bugeun isanggwa gateun habuisahangeul josoki silcheone omgigi wihayeo ppareun siirane dangguk saiui daehwareul gaechoehagiro hayeotda. — 5. The South and the North agreed to hold talks between the authorities in the near future in order to put the above agreements into practice promptly.

examples.text: 김대중 대통령은 김정일 국방위원장이 서울을 방문하도록 정중히 초청하였으며, 김정일 국방위원장은 앞으로 적절한 시기에 서울을 방문하기로 하였다.
examples.translation: gimdaejung daetongnyeongeun gimjeongil gukbangwiwonjangi seoureul bangmunhadorok jeongjunghi chocheonghayeosseumyeo, gimjeongil gukbangwiwonjangeun apeuro jeokjeolhan sigie seoureul bangmunhagiro hayeotda. — President Kim Dae-jung courteously invited Chairman Kim Jong-il to visit Seoul, and Chairman Kim Jong-il agreed to visit Seoul at an appropriate time in the future.

explanations.title: 학습활동 1 (Listening · Reading): a children’s poem, “우리는 본디 하나”
explanations.body: The book gives a children’s poem recorded in audio (© edunet4u.net). You listen and transcribe the missing words (there are fourteen blanks, such as 도 하나 and 을 가르고), then translate the poem. The missing words are heard only in the audio and are not in the text, so I cannot give them. The lines that are printed in full (the English is mine):

examples.text: 우리는 본디 하나
examples.translation: urineun bondi hana — We are originally one.

examples.text: 하지만 지금은
examples.translation: hajiman jigeumeun — But now

examples.text: 인제 다시
examples.translation: inje dasi — Now, again

examples.text: 생각이 하나 되고
examples.translation: saenggagi hana doego — our thoughts become one,

examples.text: 하나의 말을 쓰고
examples.translation: hanaui mareul sseugo — we use one language,

examples.text: 하나 되고 싶은
examples.translation: hana doego sipeun — the one we want to become,

examples.text: 우리의 간절한
examples.translation: uriui ganjeolhan — our earnest

examples.text: 어서 빨리 이루고 싶습니다
examples.translation: eoseo ppalli irugo sipseumnida — we want to achieve it quickly.

explanations.title: 학습활동 1: question 2 (my answer)
explanations.body: In the poem, 우리 refers to the Korean people, North and South together: the Korean nation that was originally one and has been divided.

explanations.title: 학습활동 3 (Reading): a summary of inter-Korean relations in the 2000s
explanations.body: The book gives a chronology (Text and images © Hankyoreh) that includes positive and negative developments and asks you to list the negative incidents with their dates in English (the first, “2002 June 29: 2nd occurrence of exchange of fire in the West Sea (Yeon-pyong warfare),” is done for you). The chronology is a picture and is not in the text, so the list cannot be given here. The three summaries below are in the text, and the book asks you to fill in the dates of the incidents they describe. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (11시 is 열한 시; 9 km is 구 킬로미터; NLL is 엔엘엘; 6.15 is 육일오; 10.4 is 십 사; 7월 1일 is 칠 월 일 일; 2001년 is 이천일 년); the book’s quotation marks are completed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 이날 오전 열한 시경 서해 북방한계선 엔엘엘 부근 대청도 동쪽 약 구 킬로미터 지점에서 한국 해군과 북한 해군 사이에서 전투가 발생했다.
examples.translation: inal ojeon yeolhan sigyeong seohae bukbanghangyeseon enerel bugeun daecheongdo dongjjok yak gu killomiteo jijeomeseo hanguk haegungwa bukan haegun saieseo jeontuga balsaenghaetda. — Around 11 a.m. on this day, a battle occurred between the South Korean navy and the North Korean navy at a point about 9 kilometers east of Daecheong Island, near the Northern Limit Line (NLL) in the West Sea.

examples.text: 발표에 따르면 북한의 경비정 한 척이 한국 해군의 경고방송에도 불구하고 북방한계선을 침범함에 따라 교전으로 이어졌다.
examples.translation: balpyoe ttareumyeon bukanui gyeongbijeong han cheogi hanguk haegunui gyeonggobangsongedo bulguhago bukbanghangyeseoneul chimbeomhame ttara gyojeoneuro ieojeotda. — According to the announcement, one North Korean patrol ship violated the Northern Limit Line despite the South Korean navy’s warning broadcast, which led to an exchange of fire.

examples.text: 한국 해군의 사격으로 북한 경비정은 크게 파손되었고 한국 해군은 함선 외벽에 약간의 파손을 당했다.
examples.translation: hanguk haegunui sagyeogeuro bukan gyeongbijeongeun keuge pasondoeeotgo hanguk haeguneun hamseon oebyeoge yakganui pasoneul danghaetda. — Because of the South Korean navy’s fire, the North Korean patrol ship was badly damaged, and the South Korean navy suffered slight damage to the outer wall of its ship.

examples.text: 이번 서해 교전은 이천 년대에 두 차례의 연평 해전에 이어 세 번째로 발생한 것이다.
examples.translation: ibeon seohae gyojeoneun icheon nyeondaee du charyeui yeonpyeong haejeone ieo se beonjjaero balsaenghan geosida. — This West Sea exchange of fire is the third to occur in the 2000s, following the two Yeonpyeong naval battles.

examples.text: 북한은 육일오 공동선언과 십 사 공동선언에 대한 남조선 당국의 입장과 태도가 확인됐다며 일차적으로 군사분계선을 통한 육로 통행을 제한, 차단한다고 한국에 통보했다.
examples.translation: bukaneun yugiro gongdongseoneongwa sip sa gongdongseoneone daehan namjoseon danggugui ipjanggwa taedoga hwagindwaetdamyeo ilchajeogeuro gunsabungyeseoneul tonghan yungno tonghaengeul jehan, chadanhandago hanguge tongbohaetda. — North Korea notified South Korea, saying, “The position and attitude of the south Korean authorities toward the June 15 and October 4 joint declarations have been confirmed,” and, “As a first step, we restrict and block overland passage through the Military Demarcation Line.”

examples.text: 따라서 판문점을 통한 개성공단의 출입이 불가능하게 되었고, 이는 사실상 개성공단을 폐쇄하겠다는 북한의 의도로 해석된다.
examples.translation: ttaraseo panmunjeomeul tonghan gaeseonggongdanui churibi bulganeunghage doeeotgo, ineun sasilsang gaeseonggongdaneul pyeswaehagetdaneun bukanui uidoro haeseokdoenda. — Accordingly, entry to the Gaesung Industrial Complex through Panmunjom became impossible, which is interpreted as North Korea’s intention to effectively close the Gaesung Industrial Complex.

examples.text: 이로써 지난 칠 월 일 일 북한이 금강산 관광객 박왕자 씨를 사살한 이후 계속 나빠지던 남북관계는 회복이 더욱 어렵게 되었다.
examples.translation: irosseo jinan chil wol il il bukani geumgangsan gwangwanggaek bagwangja ssireul sasalhan ihu gyesok nappajideon nambukgwangyeneun hoebogi deouk eoryeopge doeeotda. — With this, inter-Korean relations, which had been getting worse since North Korea shot to death the Mount Kumgang tourist Park Wang-ja on July 1, became even harder to restore.

examples.text: 이번 핵실험의 목적은 금년 출범한 미국 오바마 정부와 협상을 위한 메시지를 국제사회에 전하려는 의도가 있는 것으로 보인다.

examples.translation: jijinpa josa gyeolgwa ibeon haeksilheom jangsoneun hamgyeongbukdo giljugun bukjjoge inneun mantapsan geuncheoui jihain geoseuro balkyeojeotda. — As a result of examining the seismic waves, the site of this nuclear test turned out to be underground near Mantap Mountain, north of Gilju County in North Hamgyeong Province.

explanations.title: 학습활동 3: the dates (my answers, from my own knowledge)
explanations.body: The dates are not given in the text. From my own knowledge of the events (not from the book), the incidents are: the West Sea clash near Daecheong Island (November 10, 2009); North Korea’s notice restricting overland passage through the Military Demarcation Line (December 1, 2008); and North Korea’s second nuclear test (May 25, 2009). Two details in the book’s text differ from what the book says elsewhere: the book’s note in 알아봅시다 gives July 11, 2008 for the shooting of the tourist (the summary says 7월 1일), and the summary says the earlier underground test was in 2001 (the first North Korean underground nuclear test was in 2006). Please check the dates against your teacher’s key.

explanations.title: A note on the Korean in this list
explanations.body: The book’s examples with digits are spelled in Hangul here: 3일 → 삼 일; 5년 → 오 년; 5명 → 다섯 명; 2차 → 이 차. The North Korean spellings 령도, 리행, 분렬, 위대한 령도자 and 조선로동당 are given with their South Korean equivalents (영도, 이행, 분열, 위대한 영도자, 조선노동당) in the related words. The book lists 침몰(하다;되다) with a semicolon; it is written with a slash here, and the book’s 대량파괴무기 확산방지구상 is the full name of PSI.

explanations.title: 알아봅시다: 황장엽 (Hwang Jang-yop) — the book’s note
explanations.body: Hwang Jang-yop (17 February 1923–10 October 2010) was a major politician in North Korea who defected to South Korea in 1997, making him the highest-ranking defector to date. He was largely responsible for crafting the Juche Idea (주체사상), North Korea’s official state ideology. Hwang was found dead in his home on the morning of 10 October 2010. Initial reports stated that he died of a heart attack. For more information, go to Hwang Jang-yop.

examples.text: 요덕수용소는 북한 정치범수용소이자 인권유린의 현장으로 악명 높다.
examples.translation: yodeoksuyongsoneun bukan jeongchibeomsuyongsoija ingwonyurinui hyeonjangeuro angmyeong nopda. — The Yoduk camp is notorious as a North Korean political prison camp and a scene of human rights abuses.

examples.text: 북한의 인권탄압은 탈북자인 기자 강철환의 체험수기인 수용소의 노래로 국내에 알려진 바 있다.
examples.translation: bukanui ingwontanabeun talbukjain gija gangcheolhwanui cheheomsugiin suyongsoui noraero gungnaee allyeojin ba itda. — North Korea’s suppression of human rights has been made known in Korea through “Song of the Camp,” the memoir of the defector and reporter Kang Chol-hwan.

examples.text: 이번 작품의 제작과 연출을 맡은 정성산 감독은 탈북해 온 영화감독으로 자신의 경험을 바탕으로 요덕수용소 이야기를 뮤지컬로 제작했다.

examples.text: 북한 정치범 수용소 출신 탈북 예술인이 출연하며 국내 최초로 북한 최고 예술 춤인 사계절 춤을 만날 수 있다.

explanations.body:

2. explanations.title: 학습활동 3 (Reading · Speaking): the Walter Judd Freedom Award
explanations.body: The following is an article about the Walter Judd Award (© Yonhapnews), titled 수전 솔티, “월터 저드 자유상” 수상 (VOA). The text is the book’s with the numbers and abbreviations spelled out (VOA is 브이오에이; 13일 is 십삼 일; 1993년 is 천구백구십삼 년; 1996년 is 천구백구십육 년; 2008년 is 이천팔 년; 제9회 is 제구회); the English name “The Fund for American Studies” in parentheses is dropped from the spoken line, and the quotation marks ‘ ’ are removed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 대북인권단체 북한자유연합의 수전 솔티 대표가 북한의 인권개선을 위해 헌신한 공로를 인정받아 월터 저드 자유상을 받게 됐다고 미국의 소리 브이오에이 방송이 십삼 일 전했다.
examples.translation: daebugingwondanche bukanjayuyeonhabui sujeon solti daepyoga bukanui ingwongaeseoneul wihae heonsinhan gongnoreul injeongbada wolteo jeodeu jayusangeul batge dwaetdago migugui sori beuioei bangsongi sipsam il jeonhaetda. — The Voice of America (VOA) broadcast reported on the 13th that Susan Scholte, the head of the North Korea Freedom Coalition, a human rights group for North Korea, will receive the “Walter Judd Freedom Award” in recognition of her contribution in devoting herself to improving North Korea’s human rights.

examples.text: 브이오에이에 따르면 이 상을 수여하는 미국의 비정부기구 미국학기금은 솔티 대표가 북한 인권의 숨은 천사로서 북한 인권의 참상을 미국사회에 알렸고 탈북자들이 북한의 자유와 인권을 위해 일하도록 지원했다고 수상자 선정 이유를 밝혔다.
examples.translation: beuioeie ttareumyeon i sangeul suyeohaneun migugui bijeongbugigu migukakgigeumeun solti daepyoga bukan ingwonui sumeun cheonsaroseo bukan ingwonui chamsangeul miguksahoee allyeotgo talbukjadeuri bukanui jayuwa ingwoneul wihae ilhadorok jiwonhaetdago susangja seonjeong iyureul balkyeotda. — According to VOA, the American NGO that presents this award, The Fund for American Studies, stated as the reason for selecting the recipient that Representative Scholte, as the “hidden angel” of North Korean human rights, informed American society of the horrors of North Korea’s human rights situation and supported defectors in working for freedom and human rights in North Korea.

examples.text: 천구백구십삼 년 제정된 월터 저드 자유상은 폭정과 억압을 폭로하고 자유를 확산시키고자 노력한 개인에게 주어지며, 앞서 로널드 레이건 전 미국 대통령과 프랭크 울프 미 하원의원 등이 이 상을 받았다.
examples.translation: cheongubaekgusipsam nyeon jejeongdoen wolteo jeodeu jayusangeun pokjeonggwa eogabeul pongnohago jayureul hwaksansikigoja noryeokan gaeinege jueojimyeo, apseo roneoldeu reigeon jeon miguk daetongnyeonggwa peuraengkeu ulpeu mi hawonuiwon deungi i sangeul badatda. — The Walter Judd Freedom Award, established in 1993, is given to individuals who worked to expose tyranny and oppression and spread freedom, and earlier recipients include former American President Ronald Reagan and U.S. Representative Frank Wolf.

examples.text: 솔티 대표는 탈북자 강제송환 반대 운동을 시작한 천구백구십육 년 이후 북한의 인권 개선을 위해 노력해 왔으며 이천팔 년에는 제구회 서울평화상을 받기도 했다.
examples.translation: solti daepyoneun talbukja gangjesonghwan bandae undongeul sijakan cheongubaekgusibyuk nyeon ihu bukanui ingwon gaeseoneul wihae noryeokae wasseumyeo icheonpal nyeoneneun jeguhoe seoulpyeonghwasangeul batgido haetda. — Representative Scholte has worked to improve North Korea’s human rights since 1996, when she began the campaign against the forced repatriation of defectors, and in 2008 she also received the 9th Seoul Peace Prize.

explanations.title: 학습활동 3: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1A. Susan Scholte is the head of the North Korea Freedom Coalition (북한자유연합), a human rights group for North Korea, who devoted herself to improving North Korea’s human rights and was recognized with the Walter Judd Freedom Award; she has campaigned against the forced repatriation of defectors since 1996 and received the 9th Seoul Peace Prize in 2008.

1B. The earlier recipients named are former U.S. President Ronald Reagan and U.S. Representative Frank Wolf. What they have in common: both are American politicians, and the award goes to individuals who worked to expose tyranny and oppression and to spread freedom.

2. In the pair activity, taking turns as the Master of Ceremonies, you introduce 수잔 솔티 to each other in Korean.

exercises.prompt: What does 대북인권단체 북한자유연합의 수전 솔티 대표가 북한의 인권개선을 위해 헌신한 공로를 인정받아 월터 저드 자유상을 받게 됐다고 미국의 소리 (브이오에이) 방송이 십삼 일 전했다. mean?
options: The Voice of America (VOA) broadcast reported on the 13th that Susan Scholte, the head of the North Korea Freedom Coalition, a human rights group for North Korea, will receive the “Walter Judd Freedom Award” in recognition of her contribution in devoting herself to improving North Korea’s human rights.

Representative Scholte has worked to improve North Korea’s human rights since 1996, when she began the campaign against the forced repatriation of defectors, and in 2008 she also received the 9th Seoul Peace Prize.

According to VOA, the American NGO that presents this award, The Fund for American Studies, stated as the reason for selecting the recipient that Representative Scholte, as the “hidden angel” of North Korean human rights, informed American society of the horrors of North Korea’s human rights situation and supported defectors in working for freedom and human rights in North Korea.

The Walter Judd Freedom Award, established in 1993, is given to individuals who worked to expose tyranny and oppression and spread freedom, and earlier recipients include former American President Ronald Reagan and U.S. Representative Frank Wolf.

lessons.subtitle: 본 학습 · 북한인권법 · 난민 · 벌목공 · 영주권 · 시민권 · 탈북 여성 · 인신매매 · 말해 봅시다

explanations.title: 알아봅시다: 미국의 북한인권법과 난민 (the U.S. North Korean Human Rights Act and refugees) — the book’s note
explanations.body: The U.S. Senate and House of Representatives passed the 북한인권법 in 2004. At the core of the law is the active involvement of the United States in human right issues of North Korea and the protection of North Korean defectors. By passing this law, the United States acknowledges North Korean defectors as refugees, which allows them to apply for asylum in the United States. Whether or not a country considers a North Korean defector a refugee affects the country’s treatment of the defector. China does not consider North Korean defectors to be refugees, so it sends defectors back to North Korea. Following the example of the United States, Japan established the North Korea Human Rights Law in 2005.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2 (Reading): “난민자격 100번째 탈북자 미국 도착” (the 100th defector with refugee status arrives in the U.S.)
explanations.body: The following is an article about the loggers introduced in 학습활동 1 (© Yonhapnews). The text is the book’s with the numbers and abbreviations spelled out (100번째 is 백 번째; VOA is 브이오에이; 제3국 is 제삼국; 10일 is 십 일; 8일 is 팔 일; 3월 is 삼 월; 2006년 is 이천육 년; 6명 is 여섯 명; 20∼30명 is 이십 명에서 삼십 명; 10여 개 is 십여 개; 3분의 1 is 삼 분의 일; 1년 is 일 년; 5년 is 오 년); the quotation marks are kept as printed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 미국의 북한인권법에 따라 제삼국에서 난민 지위를 부여 받은 백 번째 탈북자가 미국에 입국했다고 미국의 소리 브이오에이 방송이 십 일 밝혔다.
examples.translation: migugui bukaningwonbeobe ttara jesamgugeseo nanmin jiwireul buyeo badeun baek beonjjae talbukjaga miguge ipgukaetdago migugui sori beuioei bangsongi sip il balkyeotda. — The Voice of America (VOA) broadcast stated on the 10th that the 100th defector to be granted refugee status in a third country under the American North Korean Human Rights Act has entered the United States.

examples.text: 이 방송은 미 국무부 고위관리의 말을 인용해 백 번째 탈북 난민이 팔 일 현지시간 미국에 도착했다면서 이 탈북자는 러시아 벌목공 출신인 조 모 씨로 알려졌다고 전했다.
examples.translation: i bangsongeun mi gungmubu gowigwalliui mareul inyonghae baek beonjjae talbuk nanmini pal il hyeonjisigan miguge dochakaetdamyeonseo i talbukjaneun reosia beolmokgong chulsinin jo mo ssiro allyeojeotdago jeonhaetda. — Quoting a senior official of the U.S. State Department, this broadcast reported, “The 100th defector refugee arrived in the United States on the 8th (local time),” and, “This defector is known to be Mr. Cho, who comes from being a logger in Russia.”

examples.text: 조 씨는 북한에서 온 다른 벌목공과 함께 지난 삼 월 러시아 블라디보스토크의 한국 영사관에 진입한 뒤 지난달 난민 판정을 받고 모스크바 주재 미국 대사관의 보호를 받아 왔다.
examples.translation: jo ssineun bukaneseo on dareun beolmokgonggwa hamkke jinan sam wol reosia beulladiboseutokeuui hanguk yeongsagwane jinipan dwi jinandal nanmin panjeongeul batgo moseukeuba jujae miguk daesagwanui bohoreul bada watda. — Mr. Cho, together with another logger from North Korea, entered the South Korean consulate in Vladivostok, Russia, last March, received a refugee determination last month and has been under the protection of the American embassy stationed in Moscow.

examples.text: 조 씨와 함께 탈출한 다른 벌목공도 조만간 미국으로 갈 것으로 알려졌다.
examples.translation: jo ssiwa hamkke talchulhan dareun beolmokgongdo jomangan migugeuro gal geoseuro allyeojeotda. — The other logger who escaped together with Mr. Cho is also known to be going to the United States soon.

examples.text: 브이오에이는 이천육 년 태국에서 탈북자 여섯 명이 처음 미국에 입국한 이후 매년 이십 명에서 삼십 명의 탈북 난민이 태국, 중국, 몽골, 러시아, 필리핀, 라오스 등을 통해 미국에 들어왔다면서 이들 탈북 난민은 미국내 십여 개 중소도시로 보내진 뒤 지역 난민단체의 도움을 받아 정착 과정을 밟는데, 적어도 삼 분의 일 정도는 한인들이 많이 거주하는 대도시로 이동한다고 전했다.
examples.translation: beuioeineun icheonyuk nyeon taegugeseo talbukja yeoseot myeongi cheoeum miguge ipgukan ihu maenyeon isip myeongeseo samsip myeongui talbuk nanmini taeguk, jungguk, monggol, reosia, pillipin, raoseu deungeul tonghae miguge deureowatdamyeonseo ideul talbuk nanmineun migungnae sibyeo gae jungsodosiro bonaejin dwi jiyeok nanmindancheui doumeul bada jeongchak gwajeongeul bamneunde, jeogeodo sam bunui il jeongdoneun hanindeuri mani geojuhaneun daedosiro idonghandago jeonhaetda. — VOA reported, “Since six defectors first entered the United States from Thailand in 2006, 20 to 30 defector refugees have come to the United States every year through Thailand, China, Mongolia, Russia, the Philippines, Laos and others,” and, “After being sent to about ten small and medium-sized cities in the United States, these defector refugees go through a settlement process with the help of local refugee groups, and at least about one third move to large cities where many Koreans live.”

examples.text: 난민 신분으로 미국에 정착한 탈북자들은 일 년 뒤 영주권을 신청할 수 있고, 범죄나 결격 사유가 없으면 영주권 취득 오 년 후 시민권을 신청할 수 있다.
examples.translation: nanmin sinbuneuro miguge jeongchakan talbukjadeureun il nyeon dwi yeongjugwoneul sincheonghal su itgo, beomjoena gyeolgyeok sayuga eopseumyeon yeongjugwon chwideuk o nyeon hu simingwoneul sincheonghal su itda. — Defectors who settled in the United States as refugees can apply for permanent residency after one year, and if they have no crime or reason for disqualification, they can apply for citizenship five years after obtaining permanent residency.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. Mr. Cho is a former logger from Russia and the 100th defector to receive refugee status under the U.S. North Korean Human Rights Act. He entered the South Korean consulate in Vladivostok last March together with another North Korean logger, received a refugee determination last month, was protected by the American embassy in Moscow, and arrived in the United States on the 8th.

2. Since 2006, when six defectors first entered from Thailand, 20 to 30 defector refugees have entered the U.S. every year via Thailand, China, Mongolia, Russia, the Philippines and Laos. They are sent to about ten small and medium-sized cities, go through the settlement process with the help of local refugee groups, and at least a third of them move to large cities where many Koreans live.

3. Yes. Defectors who settled as refugees can apply for permanent residency (a green card) after one year, and, if they have no crime or reason for disqualification, can apply for citizenship five years after getting permanent residency.

explanations.title: 학습활동 4 (Reading): a magazine article on the condition of defector women
explanations.body: The following is part of a magazine article on the condition of defector women (Text and images © Kyunghyang). The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (6명 is 여섯 명; 15가구 가운데 12가구 is 열다섯 가구 가운데 열두 가구; 2006년 is 이천육 년); the quotation marks ‘ ’ are removed. The English is mine. (The article deals with human trafficking.)

examples.text: 미국이 탈북자들에 대해 난민 수용을 허용했다.
examples.translation: migugi talbukjadeure daehae nanmin suyongeul heoyonghaetda. — The United States has allowed the acceptance of defectors as refugees.

examples.text: 그 첫 번째 케이스로 여섯 명의 탈북자가 미국땅을 밟자 전세계인들은 그들의 입을 통해 탈북 여성들의 인권 유린 실태를 듣게 됐다.
examples.translation: geu cheot beonjjae keiseuro yeoseot myeongui talbukjaga migukttangeul bapja jeonsegyeindeureun geudeurui ibeul tonghae talbuk yeoseongdeurui ingwon yurin siltaereul deutge dwaetda. — When six defectors set foot on American soil as the first case, people all over the world came to hear, through their mouths, about the reality of the human rights abuses suffered by defector women.

examples.text: 인신매매로 인해 성적 노리개로 전락하기 일쑤인 탈북 여성들의 인권 유린 실태를 담았다.
examples.translation: insinmaemaero inhae seongjeok norigaero jeollakagi ilssuin talbuk yeoseongdeurui ingwon yurin siltaereul damatda. — It contains the reality of the human rights abuses of defector women, who often fall into becoming sexual playthings through human trafficking.

examples.text: 두리하나선교원 측이 제공한 현지 조선족과의 인터뷰 자료에 따르면 헤이룽장성의 한 시골마을의 경우 열다섯 가구 가운데 열두 가구의 노총각이 탈북 여성을 돈을 주고 사서 살고 있다고 한다.
examples.translation: durihanaseongyowon cheugi jegonghan hyeonji joseonjokgwaui inteobyu jaryoe ttareumyeon heirungjangseongui han sigolmaeurui gyeongu yeoldaseot gagu gaunde yeoldu gaguui nochonggagi talbuk yeoseongeul doneul jugo saseo salgo itdago handa. — According to interview materials with local Korean-Chinese people provided by the Duri Hana Mission, in one rural village in Heilongjiang Province, it is said that unmarried older men in 12 of 15 households are living with defector women whom they bought with money.

examples.text: 탈북자 이 씨의 이야기처럼 탈북 여성들의 상당수가 중국 현지 인신매매 조직에 의해 농촌 지역의 노총각이나 정신질환자 등 정상적으로 결혼하기 어려운 이들에게 팔려가고 있다.
examples.translation: talbukja i ssiui iyagicheoreom talbuk yeoseongdeurui sangdangsuga jungguk hyeonji insinmaemae jojige uihae nongchon jiyeogui nochonggagina jeongsinjilhwanja deung jeongsangjeogeuro gyeolhonhagi eoryeoun ideurege pallyeogago itda. — As in the story of the defector Ms. Lee, a considerable number of defector women are being sold by local Chinese human-trafficking organizations to unmarried older men in rural areas, the mentally ill and others who find it hard to marry normally.

examples.text: 심지어 한족의 성적 노리개나 매춘 시장으로 팔려가는 여성도 있을 정도.
examples.translation: simjieo hanjogui seongjeok norigaena maechun sijangeuro pallyeoganeun yeoseongdo isseul jeongdo. — There are even women who are sold as sexual playthings of Han Chinese or into the prostitution market.

examples.text: 이것이 이천육 년 탈북 여성들의 실상이다.
examples.translation: igeosi icheonyuk nyeon talbuk yeoseongdeurui silsangida. — This is the real condition of defector women in 2006.

examples.text: 두리하나선교원을 비롯해 탈북자동지회 등 여러 탈북 관련 단체에서는 이미 몇 년 전부터 이러한 실상을 한국 사회에 알리며 탈북자 지원에 대한 여론 환기에 앞장섰다.
examples.translation: durihanaseongyowoneul birotae talbukjadongjihoe deung yeoreo talbuk gwallyeon dancheeseoneun imi myeon nyeon jeonbuteo ireohan silsangeul hanguk sahoee allimyeo talbukja jiwone daehan yeoron hwangie apjangseotda. — Several defector-related groups, including the Duri Hana Mission and the Defectors’ Comrades Association, have already for several years informed Korean society of this reality and taken the lead in stirring up public opinion to support defectors.

examples.text: 하지만 한국 사회가 이런 현실을 민감하게 받아들이지 않았다.
examples.translation: hajiman hanguk sahoega ireon hyeonsireul mingamhage badadeuriji anatda. — But Korean society did not take this reality up sensitively.

examples.text: 그런데 최근 미국으로 망명하는 데 성공한 탈북자들의 사연이 알려지면서 탈북 여성의 실상이 조금씩 드러나기 시작했다.
examples.translation: geureonde choegeun migugeuro mangmyeonghaneun de seonggonghan talbukjadeurui sayeoni allyeojimyeonseo talbuk yeoseongui silsangi jogeumssik deureonagi sijakaetda. — However, as the stories of defectors who recently succeeded in seeking asylum in the United States became known, the real condition of defector women began to be revealed little by little.

explanations.title: 학습활동 4: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. According to the first paragraph, the article is about the human rights abuses suffered by North Korean women defectors, which the world came to hear about after the United States allowed defectors to enter as refugees and six of them set foot on American soil.

2. Many of the women defecting to China are likely to be sold by local Chinese human-trafficking organizations to unmarried older men in rural areas or men with mental illness who find it hard to marry normally, and some are even sold as sexual playthings of Han Chinese or into the prostitution market.

3. Their fate became known to the outside world through the stories of the first defectors who succeeded in going to the United States as refugees (the groups helping defectors had told Korean society for years, but it had not taken it up sensitively).

explanations.title: 말해 봅시다! (speaking)
explanations.body: The book’s speaking prompts (the English is mine; each asks you to exchange opinions with a friend and explain the reasons):

examples.text: 중국이나 다른 나라가 탈북자들을 난민으로 인정해야 한다고 생각합니까?
examples.translation: junggugina dareun naraga talbukjadeureul nanmineuro injeonghaeya handago saenggakamnikka? — Do you think China or other countries should recognize defectors as refugees?

examples.text: 친구와 의견을 나누어 보세요.
examples.translation: chinguwa uigyeoneul nanueo boseyo. — Exchange opinions with a friend.

examples.text: 의견에 대한 이유도 설명해 보세요.
examples.translation: uigyeone daehan iyudo seolmyeonghae boseyo. — Also explain the reasons for your opinion.

examples.text: 미국이 더 많은 탈북자들을 받아들여야 한다고 생각합니까?
examples.translation: migugi deo maneun talbukjadeureul badadeuryeoya handago saenggakamnikka? — Do you think the United States should accept more defectors?

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: 학습활동 1 (a YTN news report on two North Korean workers: the EEIs, what happened last January, and where they are likely to live) and 학습활동 3 (a YTN report on a demonstration in the United States, with a table of participants, location, reasons, and requests to China and the United States, and a video check) are audio and video activities.

lessons.title: 674. U15 L9 · Part 3 (심화 학습): Oh Se-hyeok, a settler and student CEO
lessons.subtitle: 심화 학습 · 새터민 · 노동당 · 탈당 · 주민감시제 · 반달이샵 · 적응 · 창업 · 멘토 · 말해 봅시다

explanations.title: 학습활동 1 (Reading • Speaking): a magazine article on a defector (새터민)
explanations.body: The following is a magazine article on a defector (a new settler). The heading is “[새희망 새터민] 캐릭터 ‘반달이’로 쇼핑몰 창업 대학생 오세혁” (New-hope settlers: a university student who started a shopping mall with the character Bandali). The text is the book’s with the age and numbers spelled out (32 → 서른두 살; 1999년 → 천구백구십구 년; 21살 → 스물한 살; CEO → 씨이오), the quotation marks ‘ ’ removed, and the web address of the shop (www.halfmb.com) left out because it cannot be read aloud. The English is mine. (Text and images © Kyunghyang.)

examples.text: 오세혁은 고려대 대학원 시험에 합격했다.
examples.translation: osehyeogeun goryeodae daehagwon siheome hapgyeokaetda. — Oh Se-hyeok passed the entrance exam for the graduate school of Korea University.

examples.text: 사회학 전공이다.
examples.translation: sahoehak jeongongida. — His major is sociology.

examples.text: 사회에 대해 다양한 시각을 갖고 바라볼 수 있는 학문이라는 데 반했다.
examples.translation: sahoee daehae dayanghan sigageul gatgo barabol su inneun hangmuniraneun de banhaetda. — He fell for the fact that it is a field of study through which one can look at society with various perspectives.

examples.text: 북한에서는 접하지 못한 학문이다.
examples.translation: bukaneseoneun jeopaji motan hangmunida. — It is a field of study he could not encounter in North Korea.

examples.text: 그는 공부뿐만 아니라 반달이샵을 창업한 대학생 씨이오이기도 하다.
examples.translation: geuneun gongbuppunman anira bandarisyabeul changeopan daehaksaeng ssiioigido hada. — He is not only studying but also a university student CEO who started up the Bandali Shop.

examples.text: 오세혁서른두 살은 천구백구십구 년 스물한 살의 나이에 북한을 떠나왔다.
examples.translation: osehyeokseoreundu sareun cheongubaekgusipgu nyeon seumulhan sarui naie bukaneul tteonawatda. — Oh Se-hyeok (32) left North Korea in 1999 at the age of 21.

examples.text: 어머니가 심장병으로 돌아가신 후에 집안은 급격히 기울었다.
examples.translation: eomeoniga simjangbyeongeuro doragasin hue jibaneun geupgyeoki giureotda. — After his mother died of heart disease, the family declined rapidly.

examples.text: 설상가상으로 아버지는 노동당에서 쫓겨났다.
examples.translation: seolsanggasangeuro abeojineun nodongdangeseo jjotgyeonatda. — To make matters worse, his father was kicked out of the Workers’ Party.

examples.text: 북한에서는 국민이라면 누구나 의무적으로 노동당에 가입해야 한다.
examples.translation: bukaneseoneun gungminiramyeon nuguna uimujeogeuro nodongdange gaipaeya handa. — In North Korea, every citizen must join the Workers’ Party as an obligation.

examples.text: 그것이 사회생활을 하기 위한 기본 조건이 된다.
examples.translation: geugeosi sahoesaenghwareul hagi wihan gibon jogeoni doenda. — That becomes a basic condition for living a social life.

examples.text: 탈당이라는 것은 아무리 공부를 잘하고 기술이 좋아도 출세할 일, 아니 의식주를 해결할 일마저 막막해진다는 것을 의미한다.
examples.translation: taldangiraneun geoseun amuri gongbureul jalhago gisuri joado chulsehal il, ani uisikjureul haegyeolhal ilmajeo mangmakaejindaneun geoseul uimihanda. — Leaving the party means that no matter how well one studies or how good one’s skills are, getting ahead — no, even solving the matter of food, clothing and shelter — becomes hopeless.

examples.text: 탈당의 원인은 다양하다.
examples.translation: taldangui wonineun dayanghada. — The causes of leaving the party are various.

examples.text: 당비를 제때 내지 못하거나 주민감시제에서 사람들의 신임을 잃었을 경우다.
examples.translation: dangbireul jettae naeji motageona jumingamsijeeseo saramdeurui sinimeul ireosseul gyeonguda. — It is the case when one fails to pay party dues on time or loses people’s trust in the neighbor monitoring system.

examples.text: 아버지의 출당은 아버지 개인뿐 아니라 가족에까지 영향이 있었다.
examples.translation: abeojiui chuldangeun abeoji gaeinppun anira gajogekkaji yeonghyangi isseotda. — His father’s expulsion from the party affected not only his father personally but even the family.

examples.text: 도시의 작은 아파트에서 평범하게 살던 오세혁의 가족들은 생계를 잃고 농촌으로 쫓겨날 판이었다.
examples.translation: dosiui jageun apateueseo pyeongbeomhage saldeon osehyeogui gajokdeureun saenggyereul ilko nongchoneuro jjotgyeonal panieotda. — Oh Se-hyeok’s family, who had lived an ordinary life in a small apartment in the city, were about to lose their livelihood and be driven out to the countryside.

examples.text: 그는 탈북을 결심했다.
examples.translation: geuneun talbugeul gyeolsimhaetda. — He decided to defect from North Korea.

examples.text: 이대로 있을 수 없어 탈출구를 찾다가 중국에 가겠다고 했어요.
examples.translation: idaero isseul su eopseo talchulgureul chatdaga jungguge gagetdago haesseoyo. — “I couldn’t stay as things were, so while looking for a way out, I said I would go to China.

examples.text: 그러나 가족들은 반대했죠.
examples.translation: geureona gajokdeureun bandaehaetjo. — But my family opposed it.

examples.text: 저 혼자 나올 수밖에 없었어요.
examples.translation: jeo honja naol subakke eopseosseoyo. — I had no choice but to come out alone.

examples.text: 누나와 여동생, 그리고 아버지는 아직도 북에 계십니다.
examples.translation: nunawa yeodongsaeng, geurigo abeojineun ajikdo buge gyesimnida. — My older sister, younger sister and father are still in the North.”

examples.text: 북한에서 한국을 오는 데는 상상 이상의 다양한 경로와 방법이 있단다.
examples.translation: bukaneseo hangugeul oneun deneun sangsang isangui dayanghan gyeongnowa bangbeobi itdanda. — They say there are various routes and methods beyond imagination for coming from North Korea to Korea.

examples.text: 브로커들도 판을 친다.
examples.translation: beurokeodeuldo paneul chinda. — Brokers also run rampant.

examples.text: 그는 비교적 쉽게 온 케이스다.
examples.translation: geuneun bigyojeok swipge on keiseuda. — He is a case who came relatively easily.

examples.text: 보호단체의 도움을 받아 기차를 타고 베이징의 독일 대사관을 통해 들어왔다.
examples.translation: bohodancheui doumeul bada gichareul tago beijingui dogil daesagwaneul tonghae deureowatda. — With the help of a protection group, he took a train and came in through the German embassy in Beijing.

examples.text: 힘든 건 혼자 시작하는 서울 생활이었다.
examples.translation: himdeun geon honja sijakaneun seoul saenghwarieotda. — What was hard was the Seoul life he started alone.

examples.text: 복잡한 지하철이나 버스에도 적응이 안 되고 두려웠지만 우선 아파트에 들어오는 순간부터 충격이었어요.
examples.translation: bokjapan jihacheorina beoseuedo jeogeungi an doego duryeowotjiman useon apateue deureooneun sunganbuteo chunggyeogieosseoyo. — “I couldn’t adapt to the complicated subway or buses and was afraid, but first of all it was a shock from the moment I came into the apartment.

examples.text: 이제 나 혼자구나라는 생각 때문이죠.
examples.translation: ije na honjagunaraneun saenggak ttaemunijo. — It was because of the thought, ‘Now I’m all alone.’”

examples.text: 게다가 북에 남겨진 가족들을 생각하면 가슴이 답답해진다.
examples.translation: gedaga buge namgyeojin gajokdeureul saenggakamyeon gaseumi dapdapaejinda. — Besides, thinking of the family left behind in the North makes his chest feel tight.

examples.text: 그는 대사관을 통해 들어왔기 때문에 한국으로 갔다는 정보가 북한 정부에 들어갔을 확률이 크다.
examples.translation: geuneun daesagwaneul tonghae deureowatgi ttaemune hangugeuro gatdaneun jeongboga bukan jeongbue deureogasseul hwangnyuri keuda. — Because he came in through an embassy, there is a high probability that the information that he went to Korea reached the North Korean government.

examples.text: 분명 가족들이 피해를 당했을 것이다.
examples.translation: bunmyeong gajokdeuri pihaereul danghaesseul geosida. — His family surely suffered harm.

examples.text: 가능하다면 가족들을 빨리 데려오고 싶어요.
examples.translation: ganeunghadamyeon gajokdeureul ppalli deryeoogo sipeoyo. — “If possible, I want to bring my family here quickly.

examples.text: 아니 소식만 알고 연락이 된다면 무슨 일이든 할 것 같아요.
examples.translation: ani sosingman algo yeollagi doendamyeon museun irideun hal geot gatayo. — No, if I could just know news and get in touch, I think I would do anything.

examples.text: 제가 최선을 다해 목표를 빨리 이루는 것이 가족을 위한 일이라고 생각해요.
examples.translation: jega choeseoneul dahae mokpyoreul ppalli iruneun geosi gajogeul wihan irirago saenggakaeyo. — I think achieving my goals quickly by doing my best is something I do for my family.”

examples.text: 그는 새터민 친구들 다섯 명과 함께 지난해 한국청년정책연구원의 도움으로 쇼핑몰을 창업했다.

explanations.title: 학습활동 1: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. C — life for his family became more difficult (his mother died, his father was expelled from the Workers’ Party, and the family was about to lose its livelihood and be driven to the countryside).

2. His first life in Seoul was hard: he began it alone and felt lonely (“now I’m all alone”), could not adapt to the complicated subway and buses and was afraid, was shocked from the moment he entered the apartment, and felt his chest tighten thinking of the family left behind, who were probably harmed because he came through an embassy.

3. (a) To develop a story and an animation using the Bandali bear character, take advice from people in the industry and grow the business in earnest with the five founding members. (b) To attend graduate school and act as a mentor for settler youths.

4. (Speaking, mine) His family probably suffered: because he entered through an embassy, the North Korean government likely learned that he had gone to South Korea, so his father and sisters may have been watched, questioned or punished. The article itself says only that they are still in the North and that harm to them is very likely.

Number of weapons operated by the South Korean army
Specifications of North Korean submarines for underwater infiltration
Losses for countries that participated in the Korean War
Military power of countries surrounding Korea
Arms export status among East Asian nations

explanations.title: 학습활동 2 (Reading): news on an Army event
explanations.body: The following is news about an event held by the Army (© Yonhapnews and Kyunghyang). The book asks you to read it and fill in the table. The text is the book’s with the numbers spelled out (제50보병사단 → 제오십 보병사단; 8월 → 팔 월; 27일 → 이십칠 일; 50사단 → 오십 사단; 1시간여 → 한 시간여); the quotation marks ‘ ’ are removed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 육군 제오십 보병사단이 지난 팔 월부터 군인가족 및 면회객을 대상으로 벌이고 있는 강철가족 안보 병영투어가 인기를 끌고 있다.
examples.translation: yukgun jeosip bobyeongsadani jinan pal wolbuteo guningajok mit myeonhoegaegeul daesangeuro beorigo inneun gangcheolgajok anbo byeongyeongtueoga ingireul kkeulgo itda. — The “Iron Family Security Barracks Tour” that the Army’s 50th Infantry Division has been holding since last August for military families and visitors is attracting popularity.

examples.text: 이십칠 일 오십 사단에 따르면 강철가족 안보 병영투어는 매주 주말, 사단에 근무하는 아들을 면회 온 군인가족, 면회객을 대상으로 한 시간여에 걸쳐 막사와 안보교육관을 포함한 병영을 견학하고 안보영상물을 시청하는 형식으로 이뤄진다.
examples.translation: isipchil il osip sadane ttareumyeon gangcheolgajok anbo byeongyeongtueoneun maeju jumal, sadane geunmuhaneun adeureul myeonhoe on guningajok, myeonhoegaegeul daesangeuro han siganyeoe geolcheo maksawa anbogyoyukgwaneul pohamhan byeongyeongeul gyeonhakago anboyeongsangmureul sicheonghaneun hyeongsigeuro irwojinda. — According to the 50th Division on the 27th, the Iron Family Security Barracks Tour is carried out every weekend for military families and visitors who come to see sons serving in the division, in the form of touring the barracks, including the living quarters and the security education hall, and watching security videos over about an hour.

examples.text: 병영투어를 원하는 면회객, 군인 가족은 매주 금요일 사단 정훈공보부에 전화로 신청하거나 주말 면회 당일 사단사령부 남면 면회실에 접수하면 된다.
examples.translation: byeongyeongtueoreul wonhaneun myeonhoegaek, gunin gajogeun maeju geumyoil sadan jeonghungongbobue jeonhwaro sincheonghageona jumal myeonhoe dangil sadansaryeongbu nammyeon myeonhoesire jeopsuhamyeon doenda. — Visitors and military families who want the barracks tour can apply by phone to the division’s Troop Information and Education Department every Friday, or register at the Namyeon visiting room of the division headquarters on the day of the weekend visit.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2: the table filled in (mine)
explanations.body:
Name of event: the “Iron Family Security Barracks Tour” (강철가족 안보 병영투어).

Participants: military families and visitors who come to see sons serving in the 50th Infantry Division (every weekend).

Activities: about an hour of touring the barracks, including the living quarters (막사) and the security education hall, and watching security videos.

Registration: visitors and military families apply by phone to the division’s Troop Information and Education Department (정훈공보부) every Friday, or register at the Namyeon visiting room of the division headquarters on the day of the weekend visit.

explanations.title: Activities left out
explanations.body: 학습활동 3 (Listening · Speaking, track 009): a YTN news report on computer software for boot-camp training (what it is for, who benefits, and what information about boot-camp training you would recommend entering into it). 학습활동 4 (Listening, track 010): a YTN news clip on Army boot camp. explanations.title: 학습활동 1 (Listening): news on weapons developed in Korea
explanations.body: The book plays three YTN news clips (tracks 011 to 013), asks you to fill in a table with the type of weapon and its characteristics (size, function and so on), and then to transcribe the missing words of the last clip (about the helicopter 수리온: it carries soldiers and operates in a tactical area, can fly for more than two hours, can operate over most of the Korean Peninsula, whose terrain is rugged, and is equipped with systems for flight at night and in bad weather). This is audio and is left out.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2 (Reading): a news report from the Joint Chiefs of Staff
explanations.body: The following is news about an incident announced by the Joint Chiefs of Staff (합동참모본부). The book’s note: GP is a Guard Post. The text is the book’s with the numbers and abbreviations spelled out (29일 → 이십구 일; 2발 → 두 발; 5시 26분 → 다섯 시 이십육 분; 15사단 → 십오 사단; 3발 → 세 발; 14.5㎜ → 십사 점 오 밀리미터; 1.3㎞ → 일 점 삼 킬로미터; GP → 지피; K6 → 케이 육); the quotation marks ‘ ’ “ ” are kept as printed. The English is mine. (Text and image © Kyunghyang.)

examples.text: 북한이 이십구 일 오후 강원도 화천군 최전방의 지피 초소에 두 발의 총격을 한 것으로 확인됐다.
examples.translation: bukani isipgu il ohu gangwondo hwacheongun choejeonbangui jipi chosoe du barui chonggyeogeul han geoseuro hwagindwaetda. — It was confirmed that North Korea fired two rounds at a front-line GP (guard post) in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do, on the afternoon of the 29th.

examples.text: 합동참모본부는 이날 오후 다섯 시 이십육 분쯤 강원도 화천군 십오 사단 최전방 지피 초소에 북한군이 두 발의 총격을 가해 왔으며, 우리 군이 즉각 대응 사격 세 발을 했다고 밝혔다.
examples.translation: hapdongchammobonbuneun inal ohu daseot si isimnyuk bunjjeum gangwondo hwacheongun sibo sadan choejeonbang jipi chosoe bukanguni du barui chonggyeogeul gahae wasseumyeo, uri guni jeukgak daeeung sagyeok se bareul haetdago balkyeotda. — The Joint Chiefs of Staff stated that at around 5:26 p.m. that day the North Korean military fired two rounds at the front-line GP of the 15th Division in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do, and that our military immediately fired three rounds in response.

examples.text: 합참 측은 북한군 지피에서 우리 지피로 십사 점 오 밀리미터 기관총으로 추정되는 두 발의 총격이 있어 교전규칙에 따라 즉각 세 발의 대응사격을 했다며 우리측 피격지점은 지피 하단으로 추정되는 가운데 아군 피해는 없었다고 말했다.
examples.translation: hapcham cheugeun bukangun jipieseo uri jipiro sipsa jeom o millimiteo gigwanchongeuro chujeongdoeneun du barui chonggyeogi isseo gyojeongyuchige ttara jeukgak se barui daeeungsagyeogeul haetdamyeo uricheuk pigyeokjijeomeun jipi hadaneuro chujeongdoeneun gaunde agun pihaeneun eopseotdago malhaetda. — The JCS side said, “There were two rounds of fire presumed to be from a 14.5 mm machine gun from the North Korean military GP at our GP, so in accordance with the rules of engagement we immediately fired three rounds in response,” and, “While the point struck on our side is presumed to be the lower part of the GP, there was no damage to friendly forces.”

examples.text: 해당 지역의 북한군 지피와 우리 지피와의 거리는 일 점 삼 킬로미터다.

examples.text: 합참에 따르면 우리 군은 곧장 케이 육 기관총으로 대응 사격을 했으며 귀측의 총격 도발로 인해 아군의 자위권을 발동하여 대응사격을 하였다.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The EEIs (essential elements of information) of the incident: Who: the North Korean military. What: fired two rounds of gunfire at a front-line South Korean GP (guard post). When: the afternoon of the 29th, at around 5:26 p.m. Where: the front-line GP of the 15th Division in Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon-do (the North Korean GP is 1.3 km away). How: presumably with a 14.5 mm machine gun. Result: the point struck is presumed to be the lower part of the GP and there was no damage to friendly forces. Why: not stated in the report (the South treats it as a provocation).

2. The Korean military’s response: (a) It immediately fired three rounds in response, with a K6 machine gun, in accordance with the rules of engagement. (b) It invoked the right of self-defense and broadcast a warning twice, sternly warning the North of its violation of the armistice agreement. (c) It strengthened its alert status (경계태세). (d) It put joint forces that can be dispatched immediately in an emergency on standby.

lessons.title: 681. U15 L10 · Part 3 (심화 학습): the new combat uniform and military culture
lessons.subtitle: 심화 학습 · 전투복 · 위장무늬 · 화강암 · 군복 · 지혈대 · 군대문화 · 상명하복 · 애국심 · 획일성 · 악습 · 말해 봅시다

explanations.title: 학습활동 1 (Reading): an article on combat uniforms
explanations.body:
The following is an article on combat uniforms; the book gives it in two passages (Text and images © Hankyoreh). The text is the book’s with the numbers and abbreviations spelled out (2010년 → 이천십 년; 75% → 칠십오 퍼센트; 5가지 → 다섯 가지; 디지털 5도색 → 디지털 오 도색; 65도 → 육십오 도; IT → 아이티). The English is mine.

Passage 1 (the heading and the first paragraph):

examples.text: 이천십 년 하반기, 군인들의 전투복이 바뀔 예정
examples.translation: icheonsip nyeon habangi, gunindeurui jeontubogi bakkwil yejeong — In the second half of 2010, soldiers’ combat uniforms are scheduled to change. (the heading)

examples.text: 가장 눈에 띄는 변화는 위장 패턴이다.
examples.translation: gajang nune ttuineun byeonhwaneun wijang paeteonida. — The most noticeable change is the camouflage pattern.

examples.text: 신형 전투복은 우리나라 지형의 칠십오 퍼센트가 산지이고 암석이 대부분 화강암이라는 점에 착안해 흙색과 수풀, 나무줄기, 목탄, 침엽수 등 다섯 가지 색을 도입한 디지털 오 도색 화강암 위장무늬로 제작해 위장 효과를 높였다.
examples.translation: sinhyeong jeontubogeun urinara jihyeongui chilsibo peosenteuga sanjiigo amseogi daebubun hwagangamiraneun jeome chaganhae heuksaekgwa supul, namujulgi, moktan, chimyeopsu deung daseot gaji saegeul doipan dijiteol o dosaek hwagangam wijangmunuiro jejakae wijang hyogwareul nopyeotda. — Focusing on the fact that 75 percent of our country’s terrain is mountainous and that most of the rock is granite, the new combat uniform was made with a digital five-color granite camouflage pattern introducing five colors — earth color, bushes, tree trunks, charcoal and conifers — raising the camouflage effect.

examples.text: 현재 다양한 환경에 있는 장병들을 대상으로 시험평가 중인 신형 전투복은 방수와 보온 기능이 고어텍스 수준에 버금가는 첨단 기능성 섬유로 만들어져, 물을 뿌려도 젖지 않는다.
examples.translation: hyeonjae dayanghan hwangyeonge inneun jangbyeongdeureul daesangeuro siheompyeongga jungin sinhyeong jeontubogeun bangsuwa boon gineungi goeotekseu sujune beogeumganeun cheomdan gineungseong seomyuro mandeureojeo, mureul ppuryeodo jeotji anneunda. — The new combat uniform, which is currently being test-evaluated with officers and men in various environments, is made of an advanced functional fabric whose waterproofing and heat-retaining functions are on a par with Gore-Tex, so it does not get wet even when water is sprayed on it.

examples.text: 또한 최전방 장병들에게는 섭씨 육십오 도까지 열을 내는 전자식 발열체를 등에 부착하도록 해 혹한을 견딜 수 있도록 했다.
examples.translation: ttohan choejeonbang jangbyeongdeuregeneun seopssi yuksibo dokkaji yeoreul naeneun jeonjasik baryeolchereul deunge buchakadorok hae hokaneul gyeondil su itdorok haetda. — In addition, the front-line officers and men are made to attach to their backs an electronic heating element that gives off heat up to 65 degrees Celsius, so that they can endure severe cold.

explanations.title: 학습활동 1: Passage 2
explanations.body: Passage 2 of the article (the English is mine):

examples.text: 현대의 전쟁은 온갖 첨단무기들이 동원되고 있다.
examples.translation: hyeondaeui jeonjaengeun ongat cheomdanmugideuri dongwondoego itda. — In modern war all kinds of advanced weapons are being mobilized.

examples.text: 하지만 이제까지 군복의 기능은 잘 찢어지지 않고 열에 잘 견디는 정도가 고작이었다.
examples.translation: hajiman ijekkaji gunbogui gineungeun jal jjijeojiji anko yeore jal gyeondineun jeongdoga gojagieotda. — But up to now the function of a military uniform was at most only not tearing easily and withstanding heat well.

examples.text: 그런데 나노과학기술의 군사적 사용이 늘면서 군복 소재의 궁극적 변화가 예고되고 있다.
examples.translation: geureonde nanogwahakgisurui gunsajeok sayongi neulmyeonseo gunbok sojaeui gunggeukjeok byeonhwaga yegodoego itda. — However, as the military use of nano science and technology increases, an ultimate change in the material of military uniforms is being foretold.

examples.text: 카멜레온처럼 색깔이 변하면서 주인을 보호하는 군복이 등장할 날도 머지않았다.
examples.translation: kamelleoncheoreom saekkari byeonhamyeonseo juineul bohohaneun gunbogi deungjanghal naldo meojianatda. — The day is not far off when a military uniform that protects its owner by changing color like a chameleon will appear.

examples.text: 군복 스스로 환경에 맞게 순간순간 보호색을 나타내는 것이다.
examples.translation: gunbok seuseuro hwangyeonge matge sungansungan bohosaegeul natanaeneun geosida. — The uniform itself shows a protective color suited to the environment moment by moment.

examples.text: 이렇게 자유자재로 자신의 색깔을 바꾼다면 적군의 눈에 쉽게 띄지 않을 것이다.
examples.translation: ireoke jayujajaero jasinui saekkareul bakkundamyeon jeokgunui nune swipge ttuiji aneul geosida. — If it changes its color freely like this, it will not easily catch the eye of enemy troops.

examples.text: 군복 내부에 마이크로 반응기를 설치해 출혈이 있을 경우, 이를 감지하고 상처부위에 압박을 가하는 지혈대로 작용하는 전투복도 연구되고 있다.
examples.translation: gunbok naebue maikeuro baneunggireul seolchihae chulhyeori isseul gyeongu, ireul gamjihago sangcheobuwie apbageul gahaneun jihyeoldaero jagyonghaneun jeontubokdo yeongudoego itda. — A combat uniform is also being researched in which a micro reactor is installed inside, which in the case of bleeding detects it and acts as a tourniquet that applies pressure to the wound.

examples.text: 군복 스스로가 병사의 상태를 진단하고 응급처치까지 할 수 있는 기능을 갖추는 것이다.
examples.translation: gunbok seuseuroga byeongsaui sangtaereul jindanhago eunggeupcheochikkaji hal su inneun gineungeul gatchuneun geosida. — The uniform itself will have the function of diagnosing the soldier’s condition and even giving first aid.

examples.text: 이렇게 되면 전장에서 부상을 당해도 군의관 도움이 없이 일정기간 생존할 수 있는 능력을 갖추게 되는 셈이다.
examples.translation: ireoke doemyeon jeonjangeseo busangeul danghaedo gunuigwan doumi eopsi iljeonggigan saengjonhal su inneun neungnyeogeul gatchuge doeneun semida. — If this happens, it amounts to acquiring the ability to survive for a certain period without a military doctor’s help even if one is wounded on the battlefield.

examples.text: 만약 전투복에 소형 아이티 기기를 부착한다면 지금과는 전혀 새로운 전투복이 등장할 수도 있다.
examples.translation: manyak jeontuboge sohyeong aiti gigireul buchakandamyeon jigeumgwaneun jeonhyeo saeroun jeontubogi deungjanghal sudo itda. — If small IT devices are attached to the combat uniform, a combat uniform completely new from the present might appear.

examples.text: 본부와 무선교신을 할 수 있는 기능은 낙오되거나 고립된 병사를 언제라도 구출할 수 있게 해 준다.
examples.translation: bonbuwa museongyosineul hal su inneun gineungeun nagodoegeona goripdoen byeongsareul eonjerado guchulhal su itge hae junda. — The function of being able to communicate wirelessly with headquarters makes it possible to rescue a soldier who has fallen behind or been isolated at any time.

explanations.title: 학습활동 1: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. The new uniform (Passage 1): it has a new camouflage pattern, a digital five-color granite pattern (earth color, bushes, tree trunks, charcoal and conifers) designed from the fact that 75 percent of Korea’s terrain is mountainous and most of the rock is granite; it is made of an advanced functional fabric whose waterproofing and warmth are on a par with Gore-Tex, so it does not get wet even when water is sprayed on it; and front-line soldiers attach to their backs an electronic heating element that gives off heat up to 65 °C to endure severe cold. It is now being test-evaluated in various environments.

2. The scenarios (Passage 2):

rows: 도시에서 전투를 하다가 수풀이 많은 공원 근처로 이동해서 전투를 해야 한다.
The uniform itself would change its color to suit the environment, showing a protective color moment by moment, so the soldier would not easily catch the enemy’s eye among the bushes of the park.
적의 수류탄 파편에 맞아 팔에 부상을 입었다. 중상은 아니지만 피를 흘리고 있다.

A micro reactor inside the uniform would detect the bleeding and act as a tourniquet, applying pressure to the wound; the uniform could also diagnose his condition and give first aid, so he could survive for a while without a military doctor.
야간에 작전을 하다가 부대와 떨어져 길을 잃었다.
With a small IT device attached, the uniform would let him communicate wirelessly with headquarters, so that he, as an isolated soldier, could be found and rescued.

explanations.title: 학습활동 2 (Listening · Speaking): an editorial on an accident in the military
explanations.body: A KBS editorial on an accident that happened in the military (track 018): the book asks what type of incident occurred and what its cause was, and then asks you, as the commander of the base who wants to avoid such an incident happening again, to give orders to classmates who are under your supervision. This is audio and the speaking is a role-play; both are left out.

explanations.title: 학습활동 3 (Reading · Writing): an editorial on the military
explanations.body: The following is an editorial on the military (Text and image © Kyunghyang). The text is the book’s with the quotation marks ‘ ’ removed. The English is mine.

examples.text: 가정과 학교를 떠나 군대에서 처음으로 느껴 본 집단성과 조직의 효율성은 큰 체험이 아닐 수 없다.
examples.translation: gajeonggwa hakgyoreul tteona gundaeeseo cheoeumeuro neukkyeo bon jipdanseonggwa jojigui hyoyulseongeun keun cheheomi anil su eopda. — The collectivity and organizational efficiency first felt in the military after leaving home and school cannot but be a great experience.

examples.text: 군대의 엄한 군율과 상명하복 시스템, 하면 된다는 불굴의 정신력과 임전태세 등은 사회 생활에서 준법정신, 리더십 및 참여 정신으로 나타났다.
examples.translation: gundaeui eomhan gunyulgwa sangmyeonghabok siseutem, hamyeon doendaneun bulgurui jeongsillyeokgwa imjeontaese deungeun sahoe saenghwareseo junbeopjeongsin, rideosip mit chamyeo jeongsineuro natanatda. — The military’s strict discipline and system of obedience to orders from above, the indomitable spirit of “if you do it, you can,” and the readiness for battle have shown up in social life as a law-abiding spirit, leadership and a spirit of participation.

examples.text: 불가능한 일도 가능하게 만든다는 강인한 실천력은 흔히 군대에 갔다 온 대한민국 남자들에게서 보여지는 특성이다.
examples.translation: bulganeunghan ildo ganeunghage mandeundaneun ganginhan silcheollyeogeun heunhi gundaee gatda on daehanminguk namjadeuregeseo boyeojineun teukseongida. — The strong power of action that makes even impossible things possible is a trait commonly seen in South Korean men who have been to the military.

examples.text: 이 외에도 우리가 간과하기 쉬운 군대문화의 긍정적 측면이 있다.
examples.translation: i oeedo uriga gangwahagi swiun gundaemunhwaui geungjeongjeok cheungmyeoni itda. — Besides this, there is a positive side of military culture that we tend to overlook.

examples.text: 그것은 군생활이 우리 사회의 감정 지수를 키우는 데에 기여한다는 점이다.
examples.translation: geugeoseun gunsaenghwari uri sahoeui gamjeong jisureul kiuneun dee giyeohandaneun jeomida. — It is the point that military life contributes to raising our society’s emotion index.

examples.text: 사실상 부모와 가족, 그리고 애인에 대한 사무치는 그리움과 함께 애국심이 커지는 곳이 군대이다.
examples.translation: sasilsang bumowa gajok, geurigo aeine daehan samuchineun geuriumgwa hamkke aeguksimi keojineun gosi gundaeida. — In fact, the military is a place where patriotism grows together with a deep longing for parents, family and a lover.

examples.text: 동시에 국토를 방위하고 국가를 지킨다는 자긍심을 가져보는 곳도 군대이다.
examples.translation: dongsie guktoreul bangwihago gukgareul jikindaneun jageungsimeul gajeoboneun gotdo gundaeida. — At the same time, the military is also a place to feel pride in defending the national land and protecting the nation.

examples.text: 그러나 군대문화의 특수성과 우월성이 지나쳐 비인격성과 폭력성이 오늘날까지 사회문제가 되기도 한다.
examples.translation: geureona gundaemunhwaui teuksuseonggwa uwolseongi jinacheo biingyeokseonggwa pongnyeokseongi oneullalkkaji sahoemunjega doegido handa. — However, the specialness and superiority of military culture go too far, and impersonality and violence have become social problems up to today.

examples.text: 이는 정상적인 군대 시스템에서 나온 것이 아니다.
examples.translation: ineun jeongsangjeogin gundae siseutemeseo naon geosi anida. — This did not come out of the normal military system.

examples.text: 군사독재 정치부터 우리 사회 조직과 생활에서 발견되는 독선, 획일성, 폭력성, 비민주성 등 부정적 측면들은 상당 부분 일탈된 군대 문화와 관련돼 있다고 보여진다.
examples.translation: gunsadokjae jeongchibuteo uri sahoe jojikgwa saenghwareseo balgyeondoeneun dokseon, hoegilseong, pongnyeokseong, biminjuseong deung bujeongjeok cheungmyeondeureun sangdang bubun iltaldoen gundae munhwawa gwallyeondwae itdago boyeojinda. — From military dictatorship politics on, the negative aspects found in our social organizations and life, such as self-righteousness, uniformity, violence and undemocratic ways, seem to be related in considerable part to a deviated military culture.

examples.text: 이는 하루 빨리 극복해야 할 낙후된 군문화의 악습이자 잔재이다.
examples.translation: ineun haru ppalli geukbokaeya hal nakudoen gunmunhwaui akseubija janjaeida. — This is a bad habit and a remnant of a backward military culture that must be overcome as soon as possible.

examples.text: 군대문화는 부정적인 면을 고치고 긍정적인 면을 잘 관리한다면 앞으로도 한국사회의 성장에 계속 큰 힘이 될 것임에 틀림없다.
examples.translation: gundaemunhwaneun bujeongjeogin myeoneul gochigo geungjeongjeogin myeoneul jal gwallihandamyeon apeurodo hanguksahoeui seongjange gyesok keun himi doel geosime teullimeopda. — If military culture fixes its negative sides and manages its positive sides well, it will undoubtedly continue to be a great force for the growth of Korean society in the future.

examples.text: 젊은이들이 한때 국가를 위해 목숨을 내놓을 수 있는 애국심을 가진 경험을 사회에서 되살린다면 그 사회는 무궁무진하게 발전할 것이다.
examples.translation: jeolmeunideuri hanttae gukgareul wihae moksumeul naenoeul su inneun aeguksimeul gajin gyeongheomeul sahoeeseo doesallindamyeon geu sahoeneun mugungmujinhage baljeonhal geosida. — If the experience of young people once having a patriotism that can give up their lives for the nation is revived in society, that society will develop without limit.

explanations.title: 학습활동 3: the questions answered (mine)
explanations.body:
1. Advantages the military provides: the experience of collectivity and organizational efficiency; strict discipline and a system of obedience to orders, which show up in social life as a law-abiding spirit, leadership and a spirit of participation; an indomitable “if you do it, you can” spirit and a strong power of action; a higher emotion index in society, with a deep longing for parents, family and lover and growing patriotism; and pride in defending the land and the nation.

2. Negative aspects: impersonality and violence (still social problems today); excess specialness and superiority; and, from the military-dictatorship era on, self-righteousness, uniformity, violence and undemocratic ways in social organizations and life — a backward military culture of bad habits and remnants to be overcome as soon as possible.

3. (Your own answer: the question asks about your own military experience. As a sample, mine: discipline and punctuality; teamwork; leadership; physical fitness; patriotism and pride; and endurance in hard conditions.)
